children.translated_text: Homage to <s>Śrīgaṇādhipati</s>.
Homage to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Now the holy <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s> is begun.
There, first, the prior section called the <s>Karmakāṇḍa</s> is begun.

children.text: oṃ nārāyaṇaṃ namaskṛtya naraṃ caiva narottamam
children.translated_text: Having bowed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> and also to <s>Nara</s>, the best of men,
and also to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, one should then utter victory.

children.text: oṃ ajamajaramanantaṃ jñānarūpaṃ mahāntaṃ śivamamalamanādiṃ bhūtadehādihīnam
children.translated_text: The unborn, undecaying, infinite, great one, whose form is knowledge, auspicious, stainless, beginningless, and devoid of elements, body, and the rest,

children.text: sakalakaraṇahīnaṃ sarvabhūtasthitaṃ taṃ harim amalam amāyaṃ sarvagaṃ vanda ekam ||
children.translated_text: that one <s>Hari</s>, stainless, without illusion, all-pervading, dwelling in all beings and without any bodily instruments, I worship.

children.text: namasyāmi hariṃ rudraṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca gaṇādhipam
children.translated_text: I always bow to <s>Hari</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Gaṇādhipa</s>,
and also to the goddess <s>Sarasvatī</s>, with mind, speech, and action.
The greatly blessed sages beginning with <s>Śaunaka</s>, seeing <s>Sūta</s>, the peaceful reciter of Purāṇas, skilled in all śāstras,
a great-souled devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who had come to <s>Naimiṣāraṇya</s>,
and who, in the course of pilgrimage, was seated on an auspicious seat,
meditating on faultless <s>Viṣṇu</s>, honored and praised that wise poet.
Those highly fortunate sages of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, beginning with <s>Śaunaka</s>, rich in austerity,
seers bright as the sun, peaceful and devoted to sacrifice, addressed him.
The seers said:

children.text: sūta jānāsi sarvaṃ tvaṃ pṛcchāmastvāmato vayam
children.translated_text: O <s>Sūta</s>, you know everything; therefore we ask you.

children.text: devatānāṃ hi ko deva īśvaraḥ pūjya eva kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among the deities, who is the god? Who is the Lord, and who alone is worthy of worship?

children.text: ko dhyeyaḥ ko jagatsraṣṭā jagat pāti ca hanti kaḥ
children.translated_text: Who is to be meditated on? Who created the world, and who protects and destroys the world?

children.text: kasmātpravartate dharmo duṣṭahantā ca kaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From whom does <s>dharma</s> (normative order) arise, and who is remembered as the destroyer of the wicked?

children.text: tasya devasya kiṃ rūpaṃ jagatsargaḥ kathaṃ mataḥ
children.translated_text: What is the form of that deity, and how is the creation of the world understood?

children.text: kairvrataiḥ sa tu tuṣṭaḥ syātkena yogena vāpyate ||
children.translated_text: By what vows is he pleased, and by what yoga is he attained?
What are his avatāras (descents), and how did his lineage and the rest arise?
Who protects and who sets in motion the dharmas of the varṇas and āśramas?
Tell all this, and whatever else there is, O wise <s>Sūta</s>.
Relate to us all the excellent stories of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall tell the <s>Garuḍa Purāṇa</s>, the essence resting on the stories of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
which was formerly spoken by <s>Garuḍa</s> to <s>Kaśyapa</s> and which I heard from <s>Vyāsa</s>.
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> alone is the god, the Lord of lords among the gods,

children.text: paramātmā paraṃ brahma janmādyasya yato bhavet ||
children.translated_text: the supreme self, the supreme brahman, from whom the birth and the rest of this world arise.
For the protection of the world, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, undecaying and immortal,
the unborn one, takes avatāras beginning with the form of the <s>Kumāras</s>.

children.text: hariḥ sa prathamaṃ devaḥ kaumāraṃ sargamāsthitaḥ
children.translated_text: That first god, <s>Hari</s>, assuming the creation in the form of the <s>Kumāras</s>,
practiced, O Brahman, a difficult and unbroken brahmacarya.
As the second, for the welfare of this world, wishing to raise up the earth that had gone to <s>Rasātala</s>,
the Lord of sacrifice assumed a boar's body.
As the third, in the creation of the seers, he attained the state of a divine seer,
and taught the <s>Sātvata</s> tantra, from which comes freedom from the binding force of actions.

children.text: naranārāyaṇo bhūtvā turye tepe tapo hariḥ
children.translated_text: As the fourth, <s>Hari</s> became <s>Nara-Nārāyaṇa</s> and performed austerity,
for the protection of <s>dharma</s> (normative order), worshiped by gods and asuras.
As the fifth, named <s>Kapila</s>, lord of siddhas,
he taught <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, the determination of the group of principles, to <s>Sūri</s>, when it had been lost through time.
As the sixth, <s>Datta</s>, obtained by <s>Anasūyā</s>, became the offspring of <s>Atri</s>,
and taught <s>ānvīkṣikī</s> (philosophical inquiry) to <s>Alarka</s>, <s>Prahlāda</s>, and others.
Then, as the seventh, <s>Yajña</s> was born from <s>Ākūti</s> and <s>Ruci</s>,
and, together with the hosts of gods headed by <s>Sutrāman</s>, he performed sacrifice in the interval of <s>Svāyambhuva</s>.
In the eighth, <s>Urukrama</s> was born from <s>Nābhi</s> in <s>Merudevī</s>,
showing the path honored by all āśramas for human beings.
At the request of the seers, he assumed the ninth, royal body.
Through him, O Brahmins, the subjects were revived by milk and great herbs.
He took the fish form during the flood in the <s>Cākṣuṣa</s> interval,
and, placing <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s> on a boat, protected him.
When the gods and asuras were churning the ocean with <s>Mandara</s> mountain,
the all-pervading one, in his eleventh form, bore it on his back in the form of a tortoise.
As the twelfth he became <s>Dhanvantari</s>, and as the thirteenth as well,

children.text: āpyāyat surān anyān mohinyā mohayan striyā ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Mohinī</s>, in female form, he refreshed the gods while deluding the others.
As the fourteenth, in the form of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, he reached the mighty lord of the daityas,
and tore him apart with his fierce claws, as one tears a reed mat.
As the fifteenth, becoming the dwarf <s>Vāmana</s>, he went to the sacrifice of <s>Bali</s>,
asking for three steps of ground and intending to take back <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.
In the sixteenth avatāra, seeing kings hostile to brahman,
he grew angry and made the earth without kṣatriyas twenty-one times.
Then, in the seventeenth, born from <s>Parāśara</s> in <s>Satyavatī</s>,
he made branches of the tree of the Veda, seeing that people had little understanding.
Having assumed divinity among men in order to accomplish the work of the gods,
thereafter he performed deeds such as restraining the ocean.
In the nineteenth and twentieth births, born among the <s>Vṛṣṇis</s>,
the Blessed One, as <s>Rāma</s> and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, removed the burden of the earth.
Then, at the end of the twilight of the Kali age, for the bewilderment of those hostile to the gods,
he will appear among the <s>Kīkaṭas</s> under the name <s>Buddha</s>, son of <s>Jina</s>.
Then, at that eighth twilight, when kings have nearly disappeared,
<s>Kalkī</s>, lord of the world, will arise, named as the son of <s>Viṣṇuyaśas</s>.
The avatāras of <s>Hari</s>, the storehouse of sattva, are indeed countless, O twice-born ones.
The ancient knowers of the Manus and the Vedas, all of them, are remembered as portions of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Therefore creation and the rest have arisen from him, and he is to be worshiped with vows and the like.
<s>Vyāsa</s> formerly told me this <s>Garuḍa Purāṇa</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye karmakāṇḍe etatpurāṇapravṛttihetunirūpaṇaṃ nāma prathamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the first chapter, called 'The Explanation of the Cause for the Promulgation of this <s>purāṇa</s>,' in the karmakāṇḍa called the first section of the first part of the venerable <s>Gāruḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa.
The sages said:

children.text: kathaṃ vyāsena kathitaṃ purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ tava
children.translated_text: How was the <s>Gāruḍa</s> <s>Purāṇa</s> told by <s>Vyāsa</s> to you?
Tell all this in full, for it rests upon the supreme story of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: ahaṃ hi munibhiḥ sārdhaṃ gato badarikāśramam
children.translated_text: Together with the sages I went to <s>Badarikāśrama</s>.

children.text: tatra dṛṣṭo mayā vyāso dhyāyamānaḥ pareśvaram ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Vyāsa</s> was seen by me, meditating on the supreme Lord.
Having bowed to him, I sat down and questioned the lord of sages.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: vyāsa brūhi hare rūpaṃ jagatsargādikaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Vyāsa</s>, tell of the form of <s>Hari</s>, and then of the creation of the world and so forth.

children.text: manye dhyāyasi taṃ yasmāttasmājjānāsi taṃ vibhum
children.translated_text: I think you meditate on him; therefore you know that all-pervading Lord.

children.text: evaṃ pṛṣṭo yathā prāha tathā viprā nibodhata ||
children.translated_text: O brahmins, understand now just as he spoke when questioned in this way.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu sūta pravakṣyāmi purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ tava
children.translated_text: Listen, <s>Sūta</s>; I shall tell you the <s>Gāruḍa</s> <s>Purāṇa</s>,
just as <s>Brahmā</s>, together with <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, and the others, spoke it to me.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
How did <s>Brahmā</s> speak to you, accompanied by <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and the foremost others,
the holy <s>Gāruḍa</s> <s>Purāṇa</s>, which speaks the essence?
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: ahaṃ hi nārado dakṣo bhṛgvādyāḥ praṇipatya tam
children.translated_text: I, <s>Nārada</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and the others bowed down to him,
and asked <s>Brahmā</s>, who had gone to <s>Brahmaloka</s>, 'Tell us the essence.'
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: purāṇaṃ gāruḍaṃ sāraṃ rudraṃ ca māṃ yathā
children.translated_text: The essential <s>Gāruḍa</s> <s>Purāṇa</s>, as also to <s>Rudra</s> and to me,
was spoken by <s>Viṣṇu</s> together with the gods; so, <s>Vyāsa</s>, I tell it to you.
<s>Vyāsa</s> said:

children.text: kathaṃ rudraṃ suraiḥ sārdhamabravīdvai hariḥ purā
children.translated_text: How did <s>Hari</s> formerly speak to <s>Rudra</s> together with the gods?
O <s>Brahmā</s>, tell the essential <s>Gāruḍa</s> <s>Purāṇa</s>, rich in great meaning.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I went to Mount <s>Kailāsa</s> together with <s>Indra</s> and the other deities.

children.text: tatra dṛṣṭo mayā rudro dhyāyamānaḥ paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: There <s>Rudra</s> was seen by me, meditating on the supreme state.

children.text: pṛṣṭo namaskṛtaḥ kiṃ tvaṃ devaṃ dhyāyasi śaṅkara
children.translated_text: After bowing to him, I asked, 'On what god are you meditating, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>?

children.text: tvatto nānyaṃ paraṃ devaṃ jānāmi brūhi māṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: I know no god higher than you; therefore tell me.
Together with the gods I desire to hear the truth that is more essential than the essence.'
<s>Rudra</s> said:
I meditate on that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme Self and Lord,
the giver of all, present everywhere, all things, dwelling in the hearts of all beings.
With my body smeared with ash and adorned with a mass of matted locks,
my observance of vows, O Grandfather, is for the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: tameva gatvā pṛcchāmaḥ sāraṃ yaṃ cintayāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: Let us go to him alone and ask for the essence, the one whom I contemplate.
I meditate on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the victorious one, <s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Hari</s>, free from a body,
pure, dwelling in purity, the swan, that supreme state, the highest Lord.
United with my whole self, I meditate on that god, the self of the self,

children.text: yasminviśvāni bhūtāni tiṣṭhanti ca viśanti ca ||
children.translated_text: in whom all beings stand, and into whom they enter.
They exist as attributes in the Lord of beings, like clusters of jewels on a thread.
He is thousand-eyed, thousand-footed, thousand-thighed, with excellent face.
He is subtler than the subtle, and the most massive of the massive.

children.text: garīyasāṃ gariṣṭhaṃ ca śreṣṭhaṃ ca śreyasāmapi ||
children.translated_text: He is the weightiest of the weighty, and the best even of what is best.
In sentences and repeated recitations, in the <s>Niṣads</s> and <s>Upaniṣads</s>,
they praise him as true in action, truth among the true, in the <s>Sāmans</s>.
Among the twice-born he is called the ancient Person; he is called <s>Brahmā</s>.
At dissolution he is called <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>; we worship him as the one to be worshipped.
In him these worlds tremble or gleam, like birds in water.
He is <s>ṛta</s> (cosmic truth), the single syllable, <s>brahman</s>, that which is beyond being and non-being.
The gods, yakṣas, rākṣasas, and serpents worship him.
Fire is his mouth, heaven his head, space his navel, and earth his feet.

children.text: candrādityau ca nayane taṃ devaṃ cintayāmyaham
children.translated_text: The moon and sun are his eyes; I meditate on that god.

children.text: yasya trilokī jaṭhare masya kāṣṭhāśca bāhavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The three worlds are in his belly, and the quarters and intermediate quarters are his arms.
His exhalation is the wind; I meditate on that god.
In his hair are the rain-clouds, and in the joints of all his limbs are the rivers.
In his belly are the four oceans; I meditate on that god.

children.text: paraḥ kālātparo yajñātparaḥ sadasataś ca yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is beyond time, beyond sacrifice, and beyond being and non-being.
He is beginningless and the beginning of the universe; I meditate on that god.
From his mind came the moon, and from his two eyes the sun.
From his mouth fire was born; I meditate on that god.

children.text: padbhyāṃ yasya kṣitirjātā śrotrābhyāṃ ca tathā diśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From his two feet the earth was born, and likewise from his two ears the directions.
From the upper part of his head came heaven; I meditate on that god.
Creation, secondary creation, lineage, and the manvantaras,
and the accounts of lineages arise from him; I meditate on that god.
Because of this one whom I meditate upon, let us worship him in order to behold the essence.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Having been addressed thus in former times, I and <s>Rudra</s> approached the inhabitant of <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>.

children.text: stutvā praṇamya taṃ viṣṇuṃ śrotukāma sthitaḥ suraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having praised and bowed to that <s>Viṣṇu</s>, I stood with the gods, desiring to hear.
From among us <s>Rudra</s> spoke to the supreme Lord.

children.text: sārāt sārataraṃ viṣṇuṃ pṛṣṭavāṃstaṃ praṇamya vai ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed, he questioned <s>Viṣṇu</s>, who is more essential than the essence.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: yathā papraccha māṃ vyāsas tathāsau bhagavān bhavaḥ
children.translated_text: Just as <s>Vyāsa</s> questioned me, so that blessed <s>Bhava</s>
questioned <s>Viṣṇu</s> together with the chief gods, while the immortals listened.
<s>Rudra</s> said:

children.text: hare kathaya deveśa devadevaḥ ka īśvaraḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Hari</s>, tell us, O Lord of gods: who is the god of gods, the Lord?

children.text: ko dhyeyaḥ kaśca vai pūjyaḥ kairvratais tuṣyate paraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who is to be meditated upon, who indeed is to be worshipped, and by what vows is the Supreme pleased?

children.text: kairdharmaiḥ kaiśca niyamaiḥ kayā vā dharmapūjayā
children.translated_text: By what dharmas, by what restraints, or by what worship according to dharma,

children.text: kenācāreṇa tuṣṭaḥ syātkiṃ tadrūpaṃ ca tasya vai ||
children.translated_text: by what conduct would he be pleased, and what is his form?
From what god was the world born, and who protects the world?
And by what kinds of avatāras, and into what, does the world dissolve?
Creation and secondary creation, lineage, and the manvantaras:
from what deity do they proceed, and in what is this established?
Tell all this, O <s>Hari</s>, and whatever else there may be,
the greatness of the supreme lord, and also yoga together with its disciplines.
And likewise the eighteen sciences. Then <s>Hari</s> spoke to <s>Rudra</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu rudra pravakṣyāmi brahmaṇā ca suraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Rudra</s>; I shall proclaim it, together with <s>Brahmā</s> and the gods.
For I am the god of the gods, the lord of all lords of the worlds.

children.text: ahaṃ dhyeyaśca pūjyaśca stutyo 'haṃ stutibhiḥ suraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am to be meditated on, I am to be worshipped, and I am to be praised with hymns by the gods.

children.text: ahaṃ hi pūjito rudra dadāmi paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: For when I am worshipped, O <s>Rudra</s>, I grant the supreme goal,
being pleased by restraints, vows, and proper conduct among human beings.
I am the seed of the world's continuance; I indeed am the maker of the world, O <s>Śiva</s>.
I am the restrainer of the wicked and the protector of dharma, O <s>Hara</s>.
By my avatāras, beginning with <s>Matsya</s>, I protect the whole world.
I am the mantras and the meaning of the mantras; I am also the object of worship and meditation.
I am the maker of heaven and the other realms, and I myself am heaven and the other realms.
I am the yogin, I am yoga, I am the primordial one; I myself am the purāṇas.

children.text: jñātā śrotā tathā mantā vaktā vaktavyameva ca
children.translated_text: I am the knower, the hearer, the thinker, the speaker, and the thing to be spoken.
I am the supreme god who is all and whose self is all, the giver of enjoyment and liberation.
I am meditation, worship, and offering; I myself am the maṇḍalas.
I am the itihāsas, O <s>Rudra</s>; I am all the Vedas, O <s>Śiva</s>.
I am all forms of knowledge, O <s>Śambhu</s>; I am the self of <s>Brahmā</s>; I am <s>Śiva</s>.
I am <s>Brahmā</s>; I am all the worlds; indeed I am the self of all the gods.
I am manifest good conduct; I am dharma; indeed I am the Vaiṣṇava one.
I am the varṇas and āśramas, and I am their ancient dharma.

children.text: yamo 'haṃ niyamo rudra vratāni vividhāni ca
children.translated_text: I am yama and niyama, O <s>Rudra</s>, and the various vows.
I am the sun and the moon, and likewise Mars and the other planets.
Long ago the bird <s>Garuḍa</s> propitiated me on earth with austerity.

children.text: tuṣṭa ūce varaṃ brūhi matto vavre varaṃ sa tu ||
children.translated_text: Pleased, I said, "Choose a boon from me," and he chose a boon.
<s>Garuḍa</s> said:

children.text: mama mātā ca vinatā nāgairdāsīkṛtā hare
children.translated_text: My mother <s>Vinatā</s>, O <s>Hari</s>, has been made a slave by the serpents.

children.text: yathāhaṃ deva tāñjitvā cāmṛtaṃ hyānayāmi tat ||
children.translated_text: Grant that, after conquering them, O god, I may bring that nectar,
that I may free her from slavery, and that I may become your vehicle.
Make me very strong, very heroic, all-knowing, and a tearer of serpents.
And make it so that I may be the maker of the Purāṇa-saṃhitā.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> said:

children.text: yathā tvayoktaṃ garuḍa tathā sarvaṃ bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: As you have said, O <s>Garuḍa</s>, so all of it shall be.
You will free your mother <s>Vinatā</s> from servitude to the serpents.
After conquering all the gods and the others, you will indeed bring the nectar.
You will be very strong, my vehicle, and a destroyer of poison.
And through my grace there will be a Purāṇa that proclaims my greatness.
The form of mine that has been described will also become manifest in you.

children.text: gāruḍaṃ tava nāmnā talloke khyātiṃ gamiṣyati ||
children.translated_text: That text, named <s>Gāruḍa</s> after you, will become famous in the world.
As I am famed as the glory of the gods, O son of <s>Vinatā</s>,
so the <s>Gāruḍa</s> will attain fame among the purāṇas through <s>Garuḍa</s>.
Just as I am to be praised, so too are you, in the form of <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: māṃ dhyātvā pakṣimukhyedaṃ purāṇaṃ gada gāruḍam ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on me, O best of birds, speak this <s>Gāruḍa</s> Purāṇa.
Thus addressed, <s>Garuḍa</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, told it to <s>Kaśyapa</s> when he asked.
<s>Kaśyapa</s>, having heard the <s>Gāruḍa</s>, revived a tree that had been burned.
And he himself, becoming intent on another matter, revived others by means of the vidyā.
The supreme <s>Gāruḍī</s> vidyā is recited with the mantra-like formula "yakṣi oṃ uṃ svāhā."

children.text: garuḍoktaṃ gāruḍaṃ hi śṛṇu rudra madātmakam ||
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Rudra</s>, to the <s>Gāruḍa</s>, spoken by <s>Garuḍa</s> and of my own nature.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śrīgaruḍamahāpurāṇotpattinirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvitīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the Śrī <s>Gāruḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the second chapter, named "The Explanation of the Origin of the Śrī <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa," is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: iti rudrābjajo viṣṇoḥ śuśrāva brahmaṇo muniḥ
children.translated_text: Thus <s>Rudra</s> and the lotus-born one heard it from <s>Viṣṇu</s>; the sage heard it from <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: vyāso vyāsādahaṃ vakṣye 'haṃ te śaunaka naimiṣe ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vyāsa</s> heard it, and from <s>Vyāsa</s> I shall tell it to you, O <s>Śaunaka</s>, at <s>Naimiṣa</s>.
Among the sages as they listen, creation and the rest, and the worship of the gods,
tīrthas, the arrangement of the worlds, and manvantaras are taught here.
The dharmas beginning with those of varṇa and āśrama, and the dharmas concerning gifts and kings,
legal procedure, vows, lineages, and medicine together with diagnosis,
the ancillary sciences, dissolution, and the highest knowledge of dharma, kāma, and artha,
both with manifestation and beyond manifestation, are said to belong to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
In the <s>Gāruḍa</s> Purāṇa all this is taught; and the blessed <s>Garuḍa</s>,
endowed with extraordinary powers through the grace of <s>Vāsudeva</s>,

children.text: bhūtvā harervāhanaṃ ca sargādīnāṃ ca kāraṇam
children.translated_text: became <s>Hari</s>'s vehicle and is connected with the causes beginning with creation.
<s>Garuḍa</s> conquered the gods and also performed the bringing of the nectar.

children.text: cakre kṣudhā hṛtaṃ yasya brahmāṇḍamudare hareḥ
children.translated_text: For his hunger's sake, even the cosmic egg was taken into the belly of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: yaṃ dṛṣṭvā smṛtamātreṇa nāgāndīnāṃ ca saṃkṣayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: On seeing him, and even merely remembering him, serpents and the like are destroyed.
Because <s>Kaśyapa</s>, through the <s>Gāruḍa</s>, revived the tree that had been burned,

children.text: garuḍaḥ sa haristena proktaṃ śrīkaśyapāya ca ||
children.translated_text: that <s>Garuḍa</s> is <s>Hari</s>; by him it was spoken to holy <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
That blessed <s>Gāruḍa</s>, holy and granting everything to one who recites it,

children.text: vakṣye vyāsaṃ namaskṛtya śṛṇu śaunaka tadyathā ||
children.translated_text: I shall tell after bowing to <s>Vyāsa</s>; listen, O <s>Śaunaka</s>, just as it is.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣayanirūpaṇaṃ nāma tṛtīyo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the Śrī <s>Gāruḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the third chapter, named "The Explanation of the Topics," is completed.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
Creation and secondary creation, lineage, and the manvantaras,
and also the accounts of the lineages: tell this, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Listen, O <s>Rudra</s>; I shall proclaim creation and the rest, which destroy sin.
That ancient play of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, extending to creation, maintenance, and dissolution.
The god <s>Naranārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, stainless,
the supreme self, the supreme brahman, the maker of the world's birth, dissolution, and the rest.
All this indeed, all this, has the nature of the manifest and the unmanifest,
and likewise stands in the form of <s>Puruṣa</s> and in the form of Time.

children.text: vyaktaṃ viṣṇustathāvyaktaṃ puruṣaḥ kāla eva ca
children.translated_text: The manifest is <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and so too the unmanifest, <s>Puruṣa</s>, and Time itself.
Hear his actions as he plays, like those of a child.
The creator is without beginning or end, infinite, the highest person.
From him arises the unmanifest, and from him the self too is born.
From him comes intellect; from him mind; from that, space; from that, wind.
From that comes fire; from that, the waters; from that, earth then came to be.

children.text: aṇḍo hiraṇmayo rudra tasyāntaḥ svayameva hi
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, there was a golden egg; within it, he himself indeed,
the Lord, first undertakes the taking on of a body for the sake of creation.
Becoming four-faced <s>Brahmā</s>, always predominating in the measure of rajas,
having taken on a body, he created this moving and unmoving world.
Within the egg was the whole world, together with gods, demons, and humans.

children.text: sraṣṭā sṛjati cātmānaṃ viṣṇuḥ pālyaṃ ca pāti ca ||
children.translated_text: As creator he creates himself, and <s>Viṣṇu</s> protects what is to be protected.

children.text: apasaṃhriyate cānte saṃhartā ca svayaṃ hara
children.translated_text: At the end it is withdrawn, and he himself is the destroyer, O <s>Hara</s>.
Having become <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s> created; <s>Hari</s> himself protects the world.
And in the form of <s>Rudra</s>, at the end of the kalpa, he destroys the entire world.
But <s>Brahmā</s>, at this time of creation, [saw] the earth situated in the midst of the waters.
Knowing this, he raises it up with his tusk, having assumed the boar body.
I shall briefly tell the creations beginning with the gods; listen, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: prathamo mahataḥ sargo virūpo brahmaṇastu saḥ
children.translated_text: The first creation was from the great principle; that was the irregular creation of Brahmā.

children.text: nanmātrāṇāṃ dvitīyastu bhūtasargo hi sa smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The second was that of the subtle elements; it is remembered as the elemental creation.
The third was the vaikhārika creation, remembered as the creation of the senses.
Thus this natural creation arose, preceded by intelligence.
The fourth is the primary creation; stationary beings are remembered as the primary ones.
The one called the oblique-streamed creation is said to be the birth of animals.
The sixth, of those whose current is upward, is remembered as the creation of the gods.

children.text: tato 'rvāksrotasāṃ sargaḥ saptamaḥ sa tu mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the creation of those whose current is downward is the seventh, namely the human creation.
The eighth creation is grace; it is both sattvic and tamasic.

children.text: pañcaite vaikṛtāḥ sargāḥ prākṛtāstu trayaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: These five are the modified creations, while the natural creations are remembered as three.
The ninth is remembered as the Kaumāra creation, both natural and modified.
O <s>Rudra</s>, creatures, from the gods down to the stationary beings, are fourfold.

children.text: brahmaṇaḥ kurvataḥ sṛṣṭiṃ jajñire mānasāḥ sutāḥ
children.translated_text: As <s>Brahmā</s> was performing creation, mind-born sons were born.
Then, wishing to create the fourfold set of gods, demons, ancestors, and humans,
he joined these waters, his own self, with himself.
From the manifest self of that <s>Prajāpati</s>, in whom tamas alone was predominant,
as he desired to create, the demons were first born from his loins.
Then he cast off that body whose nature was tamas alone.
That body of tamas, once abandoned, became night, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
In that body the yakṣas and attendant beings found delight; thereafter the gods did so.
O <s>Hara</s>, they arose from the mouth of <s>Brahmā</s>, with sattva predominant.
That body, being mostly sattva, was also abandoned by him and became day.

children.text: tato hi balino rātrāvasurā devatā divā
children.translated_text: Therefore the demons are strong at night, and the gods by day.
Then, taking on a body consisting of sattva alone, the ancestors came into being.
When that too was cast off, it became twilight, situated between day and night.
Then, taking on a body consisting of rajas alone, humans came into being.
When that was abandoned, it became moonlight, which is called the earlier twilight.

children.text: jyotsnā rātryahanī sandhyā śarīrāṇi tu tasya vai ||
children.translated_text: Moonlight, night, day, and twilight are indeed his bodies.

children.text: rajomātrāṃ tanuṃ gṛhya kṣudabhūtkopa eva ca
children.translated_text: Taking on a body consisting of rajas alone, hunger and anger came into being.
The rākṣasas, wasted by hunger and thirst, are eaters of raw flesh; they are so called from guarding.
The yakṣas are to be known from eating, and serpents from the creeping of his hair.

children.text: jātāḥ kopena bhūtāste gandharvā jajñire tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those beings were born from anger; thereafter the gandharvas were born.
Singing, they brought forth speech: those gandharvas and apsarases.
He made heaven, the sky, from his breast; from pleasure he created goats, according to the corrupt reading.

children.text: sṛṣṭavānudarād rāś ca pārśvābhyāṃ ca prajāpatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Prajāpati</s> also created [beings] from his belly and from his two sides.
And from his feet came the lowest creatures: elephants, buffaloes, camels, and sheep.
From the plants, those bearing fruits and roots were born; from his body-hairs they arose.
The cow, the goat, the sacrificial human, and horses, mules, and donkeys were born.
These they call domestic animals; now learn from me the wild ones.
Wild beasts, two-hoofed animals, elephants, monkeys, and birds as the fifth class,
aquatic animals as the sixth, and creeping creatures as the seventh.
From his mouths, beginning with the eastern one, the <s>Ṛgveda</s> and the other Vedas were born.

children.text: āsyādvai brāhmaṇā jātā bāhubhyāṃ kṣattriyāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: From his mouth the brāhmaṇas were born; from his arms the kṣatriyas are remembered.

children.text: ūrubhyāṃ tu viśaḥ sṛṣṭāḥ śūdraḥ padbhyām ajāyata ||
children.translated_text: From his thighs the vaiśyas were created; the śūdra was born from his feet.
The world of <s>Brahmā</s> belongs to the brāhmaṇas; the realm of <s>Śakra</s> belongs to those born as kṣatriyas.

children.text: mārutaṃ ca viśāṃ sthānaṃ gāndharvaṃ śūdrajanmanām ||
children.translated_text: The realm of the <s>Maruts</s> is the place of the vaiśyas, and the gandharva realm of those born as śūdras.
The world of <s>Brahmā</s> arises for those who stand in the vow of brahmacarya.
The realm of <s>Prajāpati</s> belongs to householders who act according to prescription.
Likewise, the place of the Seven Sages belongs to those who dwell in the forest.
For ascetics there is always an imperishable place, where they go at will.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sṛṣṭivarṇanaṃ nāma caturtho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the fourth chapter, named "Description of Creation," is completed.
The speaker said:
Having established the arrangement both here and hereafter, and the mental creation of beings,
then the lord brought forth the makers of creatures, his mind-born sons.

children.text: dharmaṃ rudraṃ manuṃ caiva sanakaṃ ca sanātanam
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Manu</s>, and also <s>Sanaka</s> and <s>Sanātana</s>,

children.text: bhṛguṃ sanatkumāraṃ ca ruciṃ śraddhāṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Sanatkumāra</s>, <s>Ruci</s>, and likewise <s>Śraddhā</s>,
<s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, the two <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s> and <s>Nārada</s> too, and the <s>Barhiṣad</s> Pitṛs as well,
the <s>Agniṣvātta</s>, the <s>Kavyāda</s>, the <s>Ājyapa</s>, and the <s>Sukālin</s>,
and likewise the <s>Upahūta</s> and the shining ones, three without embodied form,
and four endowed with form; from his thumb he created the lord <s>Dakṣa</s>,
and from his left thumb the lotus-born one created <s>Dakṣa</s>'s wife.

children.text: tasyāṃ tu janayāmāsa dakṣo duhitaraḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: In her <s>Dakṣa</s> begot auspicious daughters,

children.text: dadau tā brahmaputrebhyaḥ satīṃ rudrāya dattavān ||
children.translated_text: and he gave them to the sons of <s>Brahmā</s>; he gave <s>Satī</s> to <s>Rudra</s>.
The sons of <s>Rudra</s> became innumerable and very powerful.

children.text: bhṛgave ca dadau khyātiṃ rūpeṇāpratimāṃ śubhām ||
children.translated_text: To <s>Bhṛgu</s> he gave <s>Khyāti</s>, auspicious and incomparable in beauty.
That auspicious woman bore to <s>Bhṛgu</s> <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>,

children.text: śriyaṃ ca janayāmāsa patnī nārāyaṇasya yā ||
children.translated_text: and she also bore <s>Śrī</s>, who became the wife of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: tasyāṃ vai janayāmāsa balonmādau hariḥ svayam
children.translated_text: In her <s>Hari</s> himself begot <s>Bala</s> and <s>Unmāda</s>.
<s>Āyati</s> and <s>Niyati</s> were daughters of the great-souled <s>Manu</s>.
They were the wives of <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>; from them two sons were born,
<s>Prāṇa</s> and <s>Mṛkaṇḍu</s>; and from <s>Mṛkaṇḍu</s> came <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.
<s>Sambhūti</s>, the wife of <s>Marīci</s>, gave birth to <s>Paurṇamāsa</s>.
<s>Virajas</s> and <s>Sarvaga</s> were that great-souled one's two sons.
From <s>Smṛti</s>, wife of <s>Aṅgiras</s>, daughters were likewise born,
<s>Sinīvālī</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, <s>Rākā</s>, and also <s>Anumati</s>.
Likewise <s>Anasūyā</s>, wife of <s>Atri</s>, bore sinless sons:

children.text: somaṃ durvāsasaṃ caiva dattātreyaṃ ca yoginam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s>, <s>Durvāsas</s>, and the yogin <s>Dattātreya</s>.
In <s>Prīti</s>, the wife of <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Dattoli</s> was born as his son,
and <s>Karmaśa</s>, <s>Arthavīra</s>, and <s>Sahiṣṇu</s> were the three sons.

children.text: kṣamā tu suṣuve bhāryā pulahasya prajāpateḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Kṣamā</s>, wife of the Prajāpati <s>Pulaha</s>, gave birth,
and <s>Sumati</s>, wife of <s>Kratu</s>, bore the <s>Vālakhilya</s>s,
sixty thousand sages who kept their seed drawn upward,
no larger than the joint of a thumb and blazing with the brilliance of the sun.

children.text: ūrjāyāṃ tu vasiṣṭhasya saptājāyanta vai sutāḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Ūrjā</s>, wife of <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, seven sons were born:
<s>Rajogātra</s>, <s>Ūrdhvabāhu</s>, <s>Śaraṇa</s>, and likewise <s>Anagha</s>,
<s>Sutapas</s> and <s>Śukra</s>; these all were the stainless seven seers.
That <s>Dakṣa</s> also gave <s>Svāhā</s> to embodied Fire as his wife.
From him <s>Svāhā</s> obtained three sons of lofty power, O <s>Hara</s>:

children.text: phāvakaṃ pavamānaṃ ca śuciṃ cāpi jalāśinaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pāvaka</s>, <s>Pavamāna</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>, who consume the waters.

children.text: pitṛbhyaśca svadhā jajñe menāṃ vaitaraṇīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: And <s>Svadhā</s> was born for the Pitṛs, as were <s>Menā</s> and <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>.

children.text: te ubhe brahmavādinyau menāyāṃ tu himācalaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those two were expounders of brahman; in <s>Menā</s>, <s>Himācala</s>

children.text: mainākaṃ janayāmāsa gaurīṃ pūrvaṃ tu yā satī
children.translated_text: begot <s>Maināka</s> and <s>Gaurī</s>, who had formerly been <s>Satī</s>.
Then first the lord made from himself, born of <s>Brahmā</s>,
his own self as <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>, guardian of creatures, O <s>Hara</s>,
and that woman <s>Śatarūpā</s>, whose sin had been destroyed by austerity.
The mighty god <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s> took her as his wife.
From that male the goddess <s>Śatarūpā</s> came forth.
<s>Priyavrata</s> and <s>Uttānapāda</s>, and the three named <s>Prasūti</s>, <s>Ākūti</s>,
and <s>Devahūti</s> were <s>Manu</s>'s children; among them he gave <s>Ākūti</s> to <s>Ruci</s>,

children.text: prasūtiṃ caiva dakṣāya devahūtiṃ ca kardame
children.translated_text: <s>Prasūti</s> to <s>Dakṣa</s>, and <s>Devahūti</s> to <s>Kardama</s>.
From <s>Ruci</s>, <s>Yajña</s> was born, and <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> was born; from <s>Dakṣiṇā</s> and <s>Yajña</s>
there arose twelve very powerful sons named <s>Yāma</s>.
And excellent <s>Dakṣa</s> created twenty-four daughters.

children.text: śraddhā calā dhṛtistuṣṭiḥ puṣṭirmedhā kriyā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Calā</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, and <s>Kriyā</s>,
<s>Buddhi</s>, <s>Lajjā</s>, <s>Vapus</s>, <s>Śānti</s>, <s>Ṛddhi</s>, and <s>Kīrti</s> as the thirteenth,
the lord <s>Dharma</s> accepted as wives the daughters of <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: khyātiḥ satyatha sambhūtiḥ smṛtiḥ prītiḥ kṣamā tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Khyāti</s>, <s>Satī</s>, <s>Sambhūti</s>, <s>Smṛti</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, and <s>Kṣamā</s>,

children.text: sannatiścānasūyā ca ūrjā svāhā svadhā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Sannati</s>, <s>Anasūyā</s>, <s>Ūrjā</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>, and <s>Svadhā</s> likewise,
were taken in due order by <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Bhava</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, and also the sage <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
by <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, the best of seers,
by <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, Fire, and the Pitṛs, in that order.
Those foremost sages took the daughters beginning with <s>Khyāti</s> as wives.

children.text: śraddhā kāmaṃ calā darpaṃ niyamaṃ dhṛtirātmajam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s> bore <s>Kāma</s>, <s>Calā</s> bore <s>Darpa</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s> bore her son <s>Niyama</s>.
<s>Tuṣṭi</s> bore <s>Santoṣa</s>, and <s>Puṣṭi</s> bore <s>Lobha</s>.

children.text: medhā śrutaṃ kriyā daṇḍaṃ layaṃ vinayameva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Medhā</s> bore <s>Śruta</s>, and <s>Kriyā</s> bore <s>Daṇḍa</s>, <s>Laya</s>, and <s>Vinaya</s>.
<s>Buddhi</s> bore <s>Bodha</s>; likewise <s>Lajjā</s> bore <s>Vinaya</s> as her son.
<s>Vapus</s> gave birth to <s>Vyavasāya</s>, and <s>Śānti</s> bore <s>Kṣema</s>.
<s>Ṛddhi</s> bore <s>Sukha</s>, and <s>Kīrti</s> bore <s>Yaśas</s>; these were the sons of <s>Dharma</s>.

children.text: kāmasya ca ratirbhāryā tatputro harṣa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rati</s> was the wife of <s>Kāma</s>, and their son is called <s>Harṣa</s>.
Once <s>Dakṣa</s> performed a sacrifice, a horse sacrifice.
All his sons-in-law, invited, went to that sacrifice,

children.text: bhāryābhiḥ sahitāḥ sarve rudraṃ devīṃ satīṃ vinā
children.translated_text: all accompanied by their wives, except <s>Rudra</s> and the goddess <s>Satī</s>.
Uninvited, <s>Satī</s> arrived and was insulted by <s>Dakṣa</s> himself.

children.text: tyaktā dehaṃ punarjātā menāyāṃ tu himālayāt
children.translated_text: She abandoned her body and was born again from <s>Menā</s> through <s>Himālaya</s>.

children.text: śambhor bhāryābhavad raurī tasyāṃ jajñe vināyakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: As <s>Gaurī</s> she became the wife of <s>Śambhu</s>; in her <s>Vināyaka</s> was born,
and also <s>Kumāra</s> and <s>Bhṛṅgīśa</s>. Mighty <s>Rudra</s>, enraged,

children.text: vidhvaṃsya yajñaṃ dakṣaṃ tu taṃ śaśāpa pinākadhṛk
children.translated_text: destroyed the sacrifice, and the bearer of <s>Pināka</s> cursed that <s>Dakṣa</s>.
You will be born as a human being, sprung from the lineage of <s>Dhruva</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe prajākartrādisṛṣṭir nāma pañcamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the Śrī <s>Gāruḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the fifth chapter, named "The Creation Beginning with the Makers of Creatures," is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
From <s>Uttānapāda</s>, by <s>Suruci</s>, a son named <s>Uttama</s> was born.

children.text: sunītyāṃ tu dhruvaḥ putraḥ sa lebhe sthānamuttamam ||
children.translated_text: But by <s>Sunīti</s> there was a son, <s>Dhruva</s>; he obtained the highest station.
Through the grace of the sage, having worshiped <s>Janārdana</s>, the god of gods,
<s>Dhruva</s>'s son was <s>Śliṣṭi</s>, mighty and of great valor.
His son was <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, and his son too was noble-minded.
<s>Divaṃjaya</s> was his son; his son is remembered as <s>Ripu</s>.
The glorious <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s> is proclaimed as the son of <s>Ripu</s>.
His son was the glorious <s>Ruru</s>, and <s>Aṅga</s> was his son.
But <s>Aṅga</s>'s son was <s>Veṇa</s>, an atheist and devoid of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order).
<s>Veṇa</s>, a doer of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), was killed by the sages with blades of <s>kuśa</s> grass.
For the sake of obtaining a son they churned his thigh; then his offspring came forth.
He was short, extremely small, and black-limbed; then they said, "Sit down."
Thus the <s>Niṣāda</s> was born, dwelling on <s>Vindhya</s> mountain.

children.text: tato 'sya dakṣiṇaṃ pāṇiṃ mamanthuḥ sahasā dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then the twice-born ones quickly churned his right hand.
From that a son of his was born, bearing a mind-born form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
He was called precisely <s>Pṛthu</s> by name; that son of <s>Veṇa</s> went to heaven.

children.text: dudoha pṛthivīṃ rājā prajānāṃ jīvanāya hi
children.translated_text: The king milked the earth for the livelihood of his subjects.
<s>Antardhāna</s> was <s>Pṛthu</s>'s son, and <s>Havirdhāna</s> was his son.
<s>Prācīnabarhis</s>, his son, shone on earth as sole ruler.

children.text: upayeme samudrasya lavaṇasya sa vai sutām ||
children.translated_text: He married the daughter of the salt ocean.
From him <s>Sāmudrī</s> bore ten sons of <s>Prācīnabarhis</s>.
All were named <s>Pracetas</s>, and they were masters of the science of archery.
United in the practice of <s>dharma</s>, they performed great austerity.
For ten thousand years they lay in the waters of the ocean.

children.text: prajāpatitvaṃ samprāpya bhāryā teṣāṃ ca māriṣa
children.translated_text: Having obtained the status of <s>prajāpati</s> (lord of creatures), their wife was <s>Māriṣā</s>.
Through <s>Dhava</s>'s curse, <s>Dakṣa</s> was then born in her.
At first <s>Dakṣa</s> created four kinds of creatures by his mind.

children.text: nāvardhanta ca tāstasya apadhyātā hareṇa tu ||
children.translated_text: But those creatures of his did not increase, having been obstructed by <s>Hara</s>.
Then the <s>Prajāpati</s> desired to bring forth creation through sexual union.
He took <s>Asiknī</s>, daughter of the <s>Prajāpati Vīraṇa</s>, as his wife.
A thousand sons were born to him by <s>Vairaṇī</s>.

children.text: nāradoktā bhuvaścāntaṃ gatā jñātuṃ ca nāgatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Instructed by <s>Nārada</s>, they went to learn the end of the earth, and they did not return.
When they were lost, <s>Dakṣa</s> created another thousand sons.
Those <s>Śabalāśvas</s> too went along the path of their brothers, O <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: dakṣaḥ kruddhaḥ śaśāpātha nāradaṃ janma cāpsyasi
children.translated_text: <s>Dakṣa</s>, angered, then cursed <s>Nārada</s>: "You shall undergo birth."
Thus <s>Nārada</s> again became the son of the sage <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
Then, when the sacrifice had been destroyed, <s>Dakṣa</s> also cursed fierce <s>Maheśvara</s>.
"Having praised you with offerings, they will worship you, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Even in another birth, those who are hostile to you perish, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>."
Therefore enmity should never be made by anyone at any time.
Then <s>Dakṣa</s> begot daughters in <s>Asiknī</s>.

children.text: ṣaṣṭiṃ kanyā rūpayutā dve caivāṅgirase dadau
children.translated_text: He had sixty beautiful maidens, and he gave two to <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: dve prādātsa kṛśāśvāya daśa dharmāya cāpyatha ||
children.translated_text: He gave two to <s>Kṛśāśva</s>, and then ten to <s>Dharma</s>.
He gave fourteen to <s>Kaśyapa</s> and twenty-eight to <s>Indu</s>.
He gave <s>Suprabhā</s> and also <s>Bhāminī</s> to <s>Bahuputra</s>.
<s>Manoramā</s>, <s>Bhānumatī</s>, <s>Viśālā</s>, and then <s>Bahudāmā</s>,
these four, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s> gave to <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s>.

children.text: sa kṛśāśvāya ca prādāt suprajāṃ ca tathā jayām
children.translated_text: And he gave <s>Suprajā</s> and <s>Jayā</s> to <s>Kṛśāśva</s>.
<s>Arundhatī</s>, <s>Vasu</s>, <s>Yāmī</s>, <s>Lambā</s>, <s>Bhānu</s>, and <s>Marudvatī</s>,

children.text: saṃkalpā ca muhūrtā ca sādhyā viśvā ca tā daśa
children.translated_text: and <s>Saṃkalpā</s>, <s>Muhūrtā</s>, <s>Sādhyā</s>, and <s>Viśvā</s>: these ten
are declared to be the wives of <s>Dharma</s>; I shall tell of <s>Kaśyapa</s>'s wives.
<s>Aditi</s>, <s>Diti</s>, <s>Danu</s>, <s>Kālā</s>, <s>Anāyu</s>, <s>Siṃhikā</s>, <s>Muni</s>,

children.text: kadrūḥ sādhyā harā krodhā vinatā surabhiḥ khagā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kadrū</s>, <s>Sādhyā</s>, <s>Harā</s>, <s>Krodhā</s>, <s>Vinatā</s>, <s>Surabhi</s>, and <s>Khagā</s>.
From <s>Viśvā</s> came the <s>Viśvedevas</s>; <s>Sādhyā</s> gave birth to the <s>Sādhyas</s>.
In <s>Marutvatī</s> were born the <s>Marutvants</s>, and from <s>Vasu</s> the <s>Vasus</s>.
From <s>Bhānu</s> came the <s>Bhānus</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, and from <s>Muhūrtā</s> the <s>Muhūrtajas</s>.
From <s>Lambā</s> came <s>Ghoṣa</s>, and from <s>Yāmī</s> came <s>Nāgavīthi</s>.
In <s>Marutvatī</s> was born everything belonging to the sphere of the earth.

children.text: saṃkalpāyāstu sarvātmā jajñe saṃkalpa eva hi ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Saṃkalpā</s> was born <s>Saṃkalpa</s> himself, the soul of all.
<s>Āpa</s>, <s>Dhruva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Dhara</s>, <s>Anila</s>, and <s>Anala</s>,
and <s>Pratyūṣa</s> and <s>Prabhāsa</s> are remembered by name as the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: āpasya putro vetuṇḍiḥ śramaḥ śrānto dhvanistathā
children.translated_text: <s>Āpa</s>'s sons were <s>Vetuṇḍi</s>, <s>Śrama</s>, <s>Śrānta</s>, and <s>Dhvani</s>.
<s>Dhruva</s>'s son was the blessed <s>Kāla</s>, cleanser of the worlds.
<s>Soma</s>'s son was the blessed <s>Varcā</s>, through whom splendor is born.
<s>Dhara</s>'s sons were <s>Druhiṇa</s> and <s>Hutahavyavaha</s>.
In <s>Manoharā</s> were born <s>Śiśira</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s>, and then <s>Ramaṇa</s>.

children.text: anilasya śivā bhāryā tasyāḥ putraḥ pulomajaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śivā</s> was the wife of <s>Anila</s>; her son was <s>Pulomaja</s>.
And <s>Avijñātagati</s> too: these were the two sons of <s>Anila</s>.
<s>Kumāra</s>, the son of <s>Agni</s>, was born in a clump of reeds.
His sons <s>Śākha</s>, <s>Viśākha</s>, and <s>Naigameya</s> were born from his back.

children.text: apatyaṃ kṛttikānāṃ tu kārtikeya iti smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The offspring of the <s>Kṛttikās</s> is remembered as <s>Kārtikeya</s>.

children.text: pratyuṣasya viduḥ putramṛṣiṃ nāmnā tu devalam
children.translated_text: They know the son of <s>Pratyuṣa</s> as the seer named <s>Devala</s>.
<s>Viśvakarmā</s>, the son of <s>Prabhāsa</s>, is famed as the builder of the gods.
<s>Ajaikapād</s>, <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and the powerful <s>Rudra</s>,
and also <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>'s own son, <s>Viśvarūpa</s>, great in austerity;
and <s>Hara</s>, <s>Bahurūpa</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>;
<s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, <s>Kapardin</s>, and likewise <s>Raivata</s>;
<s>Mṛgavyādha</s>, <s>Śarva</s>, and <s>Kapālī</s>, O great sage:
these eleven <s>Rudras</s>, lords of the three worlds, have been declared.
From <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Kaśyapa</s> were born the twelve suns;

children.text: viṣṇuḥ śakro 'ryamā dhātā tvaṣṭā pūṣā tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Śakra</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, and likewise <s>Pūṣan</s>;

children.text: vivasvānsavitā caiva mitro varuṇa eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>;
<s>Aṃśumān</s> and <s>Bhaga</s> too are remembered as the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>.
The Moon had twenty-seven wives, known by the name of the <s>nakṣatras</s>.
<s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> were then born to <s>Diti</s>.
And a daughter, <s>Siṃhikā</s>, became the wife of <s>Vipracitti</s>.
The sons of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>, of broad power, were four:
<s>Anuhrāda</s>, <s>Hrāda</s>, and the valiant <s>Prahrāda</s>,
and <s>Saṃhrāda</s>, the youngest of them; <s>Prahrāda</s> was devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
The son of <s>Saṃhrāda</s> was the long-lived <s>Śibi</s>, and also <s>Bāṣkala</s>.
<s>Virocana</s> was born from <s>Prahrāda</s>, and <s>Bali</s> was born from <s>Virocana</s>.
<s>Bali</s> had a hundred sons, with <s>Bāṇa</s> as the eldest, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
And the sons of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> were all very strong.
<s>Utkura</s>, <s>Śakuni</s>, and <s>Bhūtasaṃtāpana</s>,
the great serpent <s>Mahānāga</s>, mighty-armed, and another, <s>Kālanābha</s>.
The sons of <s>Danu</s> were <s>Dvimūrdhā</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s>;
<s>Ayomukha</s>, <s>Śaṅkuśiras</s>, <s>Kapila</s>, and <s>Śambara</s>;
the mighty-armed <s>Ekacakra</s>, and <s>Tāraka</s>, very strong;
<s>Svarbhānu</s>, <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, and <s>Puloman</s>, the great Asura.

children.text: ete danoḥ sutāḥ khyātā vipracittiśca vīryavān
children.translated_text: These are famed as the sons of <s>Danu</s>, along with the powerful <s>Vipracitti</s>.
The daughter of <s>Svarbhānu</s> was <s>Suprabhā</s>; <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s> was the daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>.
<s>Upadānavī</s> and <s>Hayaśiras</s> were renowned excellent maidens.
Both daughters of <s>Vaiśvānara</s> were <s>Pulomā</s> and <s>Kālakā</s>.

children.text: ubhe te tu mahābhāge mārīcestu parigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: Those two greatly fortunate ones were the wives of <s>Mārīci</s>.
By them were born sixty thousand foremost <s>Dānavas</s>.
The <s>Paulomas</s> and <s>Kālakañjas</s> are remembered as the sons of <s>Mārīci</s>.
Likewise, the sons of <s>Vipracitti</s> were born from <s>Siṃhikā</s>.

children.text: vyaṃśaḥ śalyaśca balavān nabhaś caiva mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vyaṃśa</s>, <s>Śalya</s> the strong, and <s>Nabhas</s>, very powerful,
<s>Vātāpi</s>, <s>Namuci</s>, <s>Ilvala</s>, and <s>Khasṛmān</s>;
<s>Añjaka</s>, <s>Naraka</s>, and likewise <s>Kālanābha</s>;
the <s>Daityas</s> called the <s>Nivātakavacas</s> arose in the family of <s>Prahrāda</s>.
Six mighty daughters of <s>Tāmrā</s> are proclaimed:

children.text: śukī śyenī ca bhāsī ca sugrīvī śucigṛdhrike ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śukī</s>, <s>Śyenī</s>, <s>Bhāsī</s>, <s>Sugrīvī</s>, <s>Śuci</s>, and <s>Gṛdhrikā</s>.
<s>Śukī</s> gave birth to parrots, and <s>Ulūkī</s> to owls.

children.text: śyenī śyenāṃstathā bhāsī bhāsān gṛdhrāṃśca gṛdhryapi ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śyenī</s> produced hawks, while <s>Bhāsī</s> produced bhāsas, and <s>Gṛdhrī</s> vultures.
<s>Śuci</s> produced groups of water-birds; <s>Sugrīvī</s>, however, gave birth
to horses, camels, and donkeys; this is proclaimed as <s>Tāmrā</s>'s lineage.
The two famous sons of <s>Vinatā</s> were <s>Garuḍa</s> and <s>Aruṇa</s>.
From <s>Surasā</s> came a thousand serpents of boundless vigor.
The sons of <s>Kadrū</s> too were a thousand hooded serpents of boundless vigor.
Chief among them were <s>Bhūteśa</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, and <s>Takṣaka</s>;
<s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, and also <s>Kambala</s> and <s>Aśvatara</s>;
likewise the serpent <s>Elāpatra</s>, and <s>Karkoṭaka</s> and <s>Dhanañjaya</s>.

children.text: gaṇaṃ krodhavaśaṃ viddhi te ca sarve ca daṃṣṭriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Know the <s>Krodhavaśa</s> group; they too are all fanged.
<s>Krodhā</s> gave birth to very strong <s>Piśācas</s>.
<s>Surabhī</s> gave birth to cows and also buffaloes.
<s>Irā</s> gave birth to trees, creepers, vines, and every kind of grass.
<s>Khagā</s> gave birth to <s>Yakṣas</s> and <s>Rākṣasas</s>, and <s>Muni</s> to <s>Apsarases</s>.
<s>Ariṣṭā</s> produced the mighty <s>Gandharvas</s>.
The gods, the <s>Maruts</s>, were forty-nine in number.
<s>Ekajyotis</s>, <s>Dvirjyotis</s>, and likewise <s>Caturjyotis</s>;
<s>Ekaśukra</s>, <s>Dviśukra</s>, and <s>Triśukra</s>, very powerful;

children.text: īdṛk sadṛk tathānyādṛk tataḥ pratisadṛk tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Īdṛk</s>, <s>Sadṛk</s>, then <s>Anyādṛk</s>, and next <s>Pratisadṛk</s>;
<s>Mita</s>, <s>Samita</s>, and <s>Sumita</s>, very powerful;
<s>Ṛtajit</s>, <s>Satyajit</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Senajit</s>;
<s>Atimitra</s>, <s>Amitra</s>, <s>Dūramitra</s>, and <s>Ajita</s>;

children.text: ṛtaśca ṛtadharmā ca vihartā varuṇo dhruvaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ṛta</s>, <s>Ṛtadharman</s>, <s>Vihartṛ</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Dhruva</s>;
<s>Vidhāraṇa</s> and <s>Durmedhā</s>: this is remembered as one troop.
<s>Īdṛśa</s>, <s>Sadṛkṣa</s>, <s>Etādṛkṣa</s>, and <s>Mitāśana</s>;
<s>Etena</s>, <s>Prasadṛkṣa</s>, and <s>Surata</s>, great in austerity;
<s>Hetumān</s>, <s>Prasava</s>, and likewise <s>Surabha</s>, greatly renowned;

children.text: nādir ugro dhvanirbhāso vimukto vikṣipaḥ sahaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nādi</s>, <s>Ugra</s>, <s>Dhvani</s>, <s>Bhāsa</s>, <s>Vimukta</s>, <s>Vikṣipa</s>, and <s>Saha</s>;
<s>Dyuti</s>, <s>Vasura</s>, <s>Anādhṛṣya</s>, <s>Lābhakāma</s>, <s>Jayī</s>, and <s>Virāṭ</s>;

children.text: udveṣaṇo gaṇo nāma vāyuskandhe tu saptame
children.translated_text: this troop, named <s>Udveṣaṇa</s>, belongs to the seventh wind-region.

children.text: etatsarvaṃ hare rūpaṃ rājāno dānavāḥ surāḥ ||
children.translated_text: All this is <s>Hari</s>'s form: kings, <s>Dānavas</s>, and gods.
With the retinue beginning with the Sun, the <s>Manus</s> and others worshipped <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe uttānapādavaṃśādivarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭho 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the sixth chapter, named 'Description of the Lineage of <s>Uttānapāda</s> and Others,' is completed.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
Tell me about the worship of the Sun and the others, as performed by <s>Svāyambhuva</s> and the rest;
the highest essence, briefly, that grants enjoyment and liberation, O <s>Vyāsa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall explain the worship of the Sun and the others, which brings <s>dharma</s>, desire, and the other aims.
Oṃ, homage to the seat of <s>Sūrya</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the form of <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sūryāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, homage to <s>Sūrya</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Soma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Maṅgala</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Budha</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Śukra</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Śanaiścara</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Rāhu</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ketu</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Tejaścaṇḍa</s>.
A seat, invocation, water for the feet, arghya, and also sipping water,

children.text: snānaṃ vastropavītaṃ ca gandhapuṣpaṃ ca dhūpakam ||
children.translated_text: bathing, clothing and sacred thread, fragrance and flowers, and incense,
a lamp, obeisance, circumambulation, and dismissal:
one should always perform these for <s>Sūrya</s> and the others with these mantras, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to <s>Śiva</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to <s>Śiva</s> as the form of <s>Śiva</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ hrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ hrūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the topknot.
Oṃ hrai, huṃ to the armor.
Oṃ hrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Oṃ hraḥ, homage to the weapon.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>.
Oṃ hrūṃ, homage to <s>Aghora</s>.
Oṃ hraiṃ, homage to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
Oṃ hrauṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Gaurī</s>.
Oṃ hrauṃ, homage to the gurus.
Oṃ hrauṃ, homage to <s>Indra</s>.
Oṃ hrauṃ, homage to <s>Caṇḍa</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to <s>Aghora</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the seat of <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: oṃ aṃ oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ aṃ, oṃ, homage to the Blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>; homage.

children.text: oṃ āṃ oṃ namo bhagavate saṃkarṣaṇāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ āṃ, oṃ, homage to the Blessed <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>; homage.

children.text: oṃ aṃ oṃ namo bhagavate pradyumnāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ aṃ, oṃ, homage to the Blessed <s>Pradyumna</s>; homage.

children.text: oṃ aḥ oṃ namo bhagavate aniruddhāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ aḥ, oṃ, homage to the Blessed <s>Aniruddha</s>; homage.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Tat-sad-brahman</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: oṃ kṣauṃ namo bhagavate narasiṃhāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣauṃ, homage to the Blessed <s>Narasiṃha</s>; homage.

children.text: oṃ bhūḥ oṃ namo bhagavate varāhāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ bhūḥ, oṃ, homage to the Blessed <s>Varāha</s>; homage.

children.text: oṃ kaṃ ṭaṃ paṃ śaṃ vainateyāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ kaṃ ṭaṃ paṃ śaṃ, homage to <s>Vainateya</s>.

children.text: oṃ jaṃ khaṃ raṃ sudarśanāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ jaṃ khaṃ raṃ, homage to <s>Sudarśana</s>.

children.text: oṃ khaṃ ṭhaṃ phaṃ ṣaṃ gadaiyau namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ khaṃ ṭhaṃ phaṃ ṣaṃ, homage to the mace.

children.text: oṃ vaṃ laṃ maṃ kṣaṃ pāñcajanyāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ vaṃ laṃ maṃ kṣaṃ, homage to <s>Pāñcajanya</s>.

children.text: oṃ ghaṃ ḍhaṃ bhaṃ haṃ śriyai namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ ghaṃ ḍhaṃ bhaṃ haṃ, homage to <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: oṃ gaṃ ḍaṃ vaṃ saṃ puṣṭyai namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ gaṃ ḍaṃ vaṃ saṃ, homage to <s>Puṣṭi</s>.

children.text: oṃ dhaṃ ṣaṃ vaṃ saṃ vanamālāyai namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ dhaṃ ṣaṃ vaṃ saṃ, homage to the forest garland.

children.text: oṃ saṃ daṃ laṃ śrīvatsāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ saṃ daṃ laṃ, homage to the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.

children.text: oṃ ṭhaṃ caṃ bhaṃ yaṃ kaustubhāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ ṭhaṃ caṃ bhaṃ yaṃ, homage to the <s>Kaustubha</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the gurus.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Indra</s> and the other guardians of the directions.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.

children.text: āsanādīn harer atair mantrair mantrair dadyād vṛṣadhvaja
children.translated_text: One should offer the seat and the rest to <s>Hari</s> with these mantras, with the mantras, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
Hear the auspicious worship of <s>Sarasvatī</s>, the power of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to the head.
Oṃ hrūṃ, homage to the topknot.
Oṃ hraiṃ, homage to the armor.
Oṃ hrauṃ, homage to the three eyes.
Oṃ hraḥ, homage to the weapon.

children.text: śraddhā ṛddhiḥ kalā medhā tuṣṭiḥ puṣṭiḥ prabhā matiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śraddhā</s>, <s>Ṛddhi</s>, <s>Kalā</s>, <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Tuṣṭi</s>, <s>Puṣṭi</s>, <s>Prabhā</s>, and <s>Mati</s>:
with hrīṃ at the beginning and namaḥ at the end, these are the powers of <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Homage to the guardian of the field.
Oṃ, homage to the gurus.
Oṃ, homage to the supreme gurus.
One should prepare the seat and the other offerings for <s>Sarasvatī</s>, who is seated on a lotus,
and likewise the mounting of the sacred thread for <s>Sūrya</s> and the others, each with their own mantras.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sūryādīnāṃ sarasvatyāśca pūjanaṃ nāma saptamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first part called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the seventh chapter, named "The Worship of <s>Sūrya</s> and the Others and of <s>Sarasvatī</s>," is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Having bathed in a pavilion set on the ground, one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> in a maṇḍala.
With five-colored powder, the maṇḍala should have a vajra-navel.
There, O <s>Rudra</s>, one should make it measured out with sixteen compartments,
and one should lay the cords at the fourth and fifth angles.
The angles that are situated there on both sides of the angle-cord:
at those too the skilled person should lay the cord.
At the immediately following angles he should do exactly the same.
The first navel is specified at the meeting of the lines in the middle.

children.text: antareṣu ca sarveṣu aṣṭau caiva tu nābhayaḥ
children.translated_text: And in all the intervening spaces there are indeed eight navels.
Then he should turn the cord from the eastern and middle navels.
Between them, O best of twice-born men, O <s>Hara</s>, he should turn it short by one quarter.
By this means, O <s>Śiva</s>, he should turn the pericarp of the navel-cord.
With two parts of the pericarp, the skilled person should mark out the filaments.
With its tip the learned person should always draw the petals.
In all the navel-spaces, by this measure, O well-vowed one,
the teacher who knows the highest truth should make those lotuses.
He should arrange the gateways according to the division of the original cord.

children.text: dvāraśobhāṃ tathā tatra tadardhena tu kalpayet ||
children.translated_text: There he should also arrange the ornament of the gateway as half of that.
He should make the pericarp yellow, with filaments white, red, and so on.
The interior should be blue, and the petals black.
He should fill the square with black-colored powder.

children.text: dvārāṇi śuklavarṇena rekhāḥ pañca ca maṇḍale ||
children.translated_text: The gateways should be white, and there should be five lines in the maṇḍala.

children.text: sitā raktā tathā pītā kṛṣṇā caiva yathākramam
children.translated_text: They are white, red, yellow, and black, in that order.
Having first made the maṇḍala and performed the nyāsa, he should worship <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: hṛnmadhye tu nyasedviṣṇuṃ kaṇṭhe saṅkarṣaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He should place <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the center of the heart, and <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> at the throat.
Having placed <s>Pradyumna</s> on the head, he should place <s>Aniruddha</s> on the topknot.
He should place <s>Brahmā</s> on all the limbs, and <s>Śrīdhara</s> on the hands.
Having meditated, "I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>," he should place <s>Hari</s> in the pericarp.
One should place <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> in the east, and <s>Pradyumna</s> in the south,

children.text: aniruddhaṃ paścime ca brahmāṇaṃ cottare nyaset ||
children.translated_text: and one should place <s>Aniruddha</s> in the west and <s>Brahmā</s> in the north.
One should place <s>Śrīdhara</s> in the corners beginning with <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Indra</s> and the others in the directions.
Then, after worshiping with perfumes and the like, one obtains the supreme state.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣṇupūjopayogivajranābhamaṇḍalanirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighth chapter, named "Description of the Vajranābha Maṇḍala Used for the Worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>," is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
At the proper time, the initiated disciple, with his eyes bound by a cloth,
should have eight hundred oblations offered for him with the root mantra.

children.text: dviguṇaṃ putrake homaṃ triguṇaṃ sādhake matam
children.translated_text: For a putraka initiation the oblation is considered double, and for a sādhaka initiation triple;
for the teacher of nirvāṇa, O <s>Rudra</s>, it is declared to be fourfold.
One who kills a guru, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, a brahmin, or a woman is liable to be slain even by the uninitiated.
Now I shall explain initiation, which brings about the destruction of both merit and demerit.
Having seated the disciples outside, he should cause concentration to be performed in them.
O <s>Rudra</s>, he should contemplate them as being dried up by the windy kalā.
He should contemplate them as being burned by the fiery kalā and then flooded again with water.
Having united that living self, fire with fire, he should draw it in completely.
He should meditate on the praṇava in space, and on the other cause in the body.
There, whoever conquers each one should separate the knower of the field from the cause of the body.
Having produced each one, he should then join it, O <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.
But if he is unable to do this in maṇḍalas and the like, he should fashion a substitute and worship <s>Hari</s>.
That should have four doors, in sequence beginning from the Brahma-tīrtha.
The hand is called a lotus, and the fingers are remembered as its petals.

children.text: karṇikā talahastaṃ tu nakhānyasya tu kesarāḥ
children.translated_text: The hollow of the palm is its pericarp, and its nails are its filaments.
There he should worship <s>Hari</s>, meditating on the sun between the two fires.

children.text: taṃ hastaṃ pātayenmūrdhni śiṣyasya tu samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Concentrated, he should place that hand on the head of the disciple.
Since <s>Viṣṇu</s> is present in the hand, this is therefore the hand of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
By its touch all sins are destroyed.

children.text: guruḥ śiṣyaṃ samabhyarcya netre baddhe tu vāsasā
children.translated_text: The guru, after worshiping the disciple while his eyes are bound with a cloth,
should turn him to face the deity and then offer a flower.

children.text: puṣpaṃ nipatitaṃ yatra mūrdhno devasya śārṅgiṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Where the flower has fallen from the head of the deity, the bearer of the Śārṅga bow,
he should have that name given to him; for women, he himself should make it marked with a name.
For śūdras, the wise man should make it joined with the word dāsa.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣṇudīkṣānidṛ nāma navamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the ninth chapter, named "Viṣṇu Initiation," is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall explain the worship of the ṛṣi and the others, on the ritual altar and so forth, for success.
Śrīṃ, hrīṃ, obeisance to <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>.

children.text: śrāṃ śrīṃ śrūṃ śraiṃ śrauṃ śraḥ kramāddhṛdayaṃ ca śiraḥ śikhām
children.translated_text: Śrāṃ, śrīṃ, śrūṃ, śraiṃ, śrauṃ, śraḥ: in order, the heart, the head, and the topknot,
the armor, the eye, the missile, the seat, and the image should be worshiped.
In a maṇḍala with a lotus-womb, four doors, and colored powder,
the maṇḍala extends from eight up to sixty-four, with the obscure khākṣa and khākṣī sequences.
All of it, connected with khākṣī, moon, and sun, proceeds according to the khādi and the Veda-moon sequence.
One should place <s>Lakṣmī</s> and her limbs in one corner, and <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Gaṇa</s>, and the guru.
Then, beginning with <s>Agni</s>, he should offer oblations to <s>Kṣetrapāla</s> and the others, desiring the wished-for result.

children.text: oṃ ghaṃ ṭaṃ ḍaṃ haṃ śrīmahālakṣmyai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ ghaṃ ṭaṃ ḍaṃ haṃ, obeisance to revered <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>.
With this he should worship <s>Lakṣmī</s> together with the retinues mentioned before.
Oṃ saiṃ, obeisance to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Oṃ hrīṃ saiṃ, obeisance to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ vadavadavāgvādinisvāhā oṃ hrīṃ sarasvatyai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ, speak, speak, O speaker of speech, svāhā; oṃ hrīṃ, obeisance to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe lakṣmyarcananirūpaṇaṃ nāma daśamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the tenth chapter, named "Description of the Worship of <s>Lakṣmī</s>," is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall teach the worship of the nine vyūhas, just as it was taught to <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
Having raised the living self to the head, he should place it from the navel into space.
Then, with the seed syllable ram, he should burn the body made of the elements.
With the seed syllable yam, he should destroy all of that.
With the seed syllable lam, he should flood the moving and unmoving world.
Then, with the seed syllable vam, he should meditate on nectar.
Then, within the bubble, he should contemplate himself as wearing yellow garments and having four arms;
thus he should contemplate himself in meditation, thinking, "I am that."
Then he should perform the threefold mantra-nyāsa on the hands and body,
with the twelve-syllabled seed and then with the seed syllables already stated.
Then he should perform it with the six limbs, by which one becomes <s>Hari</s> directly.
Beginning with the right thumb, he should place the middle thumb on the petal.

children.text: madhye bījadvayaṃ nyasya nyasedaṅge tataḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: Having placed the two seed syllables in the middle, he should then again place them on the limbs:
on the heart, head, topknot, armor, mouth, eyes, chest, and back.
He should place them on the arms, hands, knees, and also on the feet.
Making the two hands lotus-shaped, he should insert the thumb in the middle.
There he should meditate on the Lord of all, the supreme principle, free from affliction.
Then in sequence he should place these seed syllables on the index fingers and the rest.

children.text: tato mūrdhākṣivaktreṣu kaṇṭhe ca hṛdaye tathā
children.translated_text: Then he should place them in order on the head, eyes, mouth, throat, and also the heart,
on the navel, the secret part, the knees, and the feet.

children.text: pāṇyoḥ ṣaḍaṅgabījāni nyasya kāye tato nyaset
children.translated_text: Having placed the six-limbed seed syllables on the hands, he should then place them on the body.
He should place the five seed syllables from the thumb through to the little finger.
The eye seed is placed in the middle of the hand; this too is the order for aṅganyāsa.

children.text: hṛdaye hṛdayaṃ nyasya śiraḥ śirasi vinyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having placed the heart on the heart, he should place the head on the head.

children.text: śikhāyāṃ tu śikhāṃ nyasya kavacaṃ sarvatastanau
children.translated_text: On the topknot he should place the topknot-mantra, and the armor-mantra everywhere on the body.

children.text: netraṃ netre vidhātavyam astraṃ ca karayordvayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The eye-mantra should be assigned to the eyes, and the weapon-mantra to the two hands.
Having bound the directions with that very same one, he should then perform the procedure of worship.
First, composed in mind, he should meditate in the heart on the <s>yogapīṭha</s> (yogic seat).
He should place <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), knowledge, detachment, and sovereignty in due order,
beginning from the southeast and so on, and he should place non-dharma and the others beginning from the east and so on.
With these his body is enclosed; it has become the seat and is of their nature.
After that he should place <s>Ananta</s>, standing with the forepart of his body raised.
Then he should know a lotus to have arisen, with eight petals equal to the eight directions,
a white lotus, rich with a hundred petals, with its pericarp spread upward.
Having meditated afterward with the mantra beginning with the Veda,
he should contemplate, in sequence, the maṇḍalas whose nature is sun, moon, and fire, one above another.
Then he should place the powers, situated in the directions beginning with the east and belonging to the sphere of <s>Keśava</s>,
the eight beginning with <s>Vimalā</s>, and the ninth set in the pericarp.
Having meditated in this way and duly worshipped the <s>yogapīṭha</s>,
he should mentally invite there <s>Hari</s>, the lord bearing <s>Śārṅga</s>, and place him again.
He should place the heart-mantra and the others in connection with the petals in the four directions beginning with the east.

children.text: madhye netraṃ tu koṇeṣu astramantraṃ nyasettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he should place the eye-mantra in the middle, and the weapon-mantra in the corners.
He should place the seed-syllables beginning with <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> in the order beginning with the east.

children.text: dvāri pūrve pare caiva vainateyaṃ tu vinyaset ||
children.translated_text: At the eastern gate and the opposite one he should place <s>Vainateya</s>.
At the southern gate he should place <s>Sudarśana</s>, thousand-spoked.
He should place <s>Śrī</s> to the south, and likewise <s>Lakṣmī</s> to the north.

children.text: dvāryuttare gadāṃ nyasya śaṅkhaṃ koṇeṣu vinyaset
children.translated_text: At the northern gate he should place the mace, and in the corners he should place the conch.
The wise one should place <s>Śārṅga</s> to the god's right side, and likewise on the left.
In the same way he should place the sword and the discus, a pair on the two flanks.
Then he should place the inner guardians of the worlds according to the division of their own directions.
He should likewise set in place the weapons beginning with the thunderbolt.
Above he should contemplate <s>Brahmā</s>, and below, <s>Ananta</s>.
Having meditated on all this and worshipped accordingly, he should then display the <s>mudrās</s> (ritual gestures).
The first mudrā is the añjali, which quickly wins the god's favor.
The salutation mudrā is joined to the heart and raised together toward the right.
The left fist has its thumb raised; the right thumb is bound around it.

children.text: savyasya tasya cāṅguṣṭho yaḥ sa uddhaḥ prakīrtitaḥ
children.translated_text: The thumb of that left hand is what is proclaimed as the raised one.
These three are common mudrās, devised according to the distinction of forms.
By releasing from the little finger onward, there are eight mudrās in due order.
Understand them as corresponding, one by one, to the eight previous seed-syllables.
Having bent the three fingers down to the little finger with the thumb,
this is the mudrā of <s>Narasiṃha</s>, after both hands have been turned downward.
Likewise, having made the left hand turned upward, he should slowly rotate it upward.
This ninth mudrā is remembered as always dear to <s>Varāha</s>.
Then he should turn both fists upward and release each one straight, one by one.
He should draw them upward; when all are released, this is called the limb-mudrā.
Then, when both fists have been bound in just this way, successively,
there are the mudrās of the ten guardians of the worlds in their proper order.

children.text: suramādyaṃ dvitīyaṃ ca upāntyaṃ cāntyameva ca
children.translated_text: The first, the second, the penultimate, and the last are headed by the gods.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Bala</s>, <s>Kāma</s>, and <s>Aniruddha</s> come in that order.
The mantras are the praṇava, then tat, sat, huṃ, kṣaiṃ, and bhūr.
There are also <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Man-Lion, and King <s>Varāha</s>.
White, reddish, yellow, blue, dark, and red,
and cloud-colored, fire-colored, and honey-brown: these are the nine names by color.

children.text: kaṃ ṭaṃ paṃ śaṃ garutmānsyājjaṃ khaṃ vaṃ ca sudarśanam
children.translated_text: Kaṃ, ṭaṃ, paṃ, and śaṃ are for <s>Garutmān</s>; jaṃ, khaṃ, and vaṃ are for <s>Sudarśana</s>.

children.text: ṣaṃ caṃ phaṃ ṣaṃ gadādevī vaṃ laṃ maṃ kṣaṃ ca śaṅkhakam ||
children.translated_text: Ṣaṃ, caṃ, phaṃ, and ṣaṃ are for the goddess <s>Gadā</s>; vaṃ, laṃ, maṃ, kṣaṃ, and śaṃ are for the conch.

children.text: ghaṃ ḍhaṃ bhaṃ haṃ bhavecchrīśca gaṃ jaṃ vaṃ śaṃ ca puṣṭikā
children.translated_text: Ghaṃ, ḍhaṃ, bhaṃ, and haṃ are for <s>Śrī</s>; gaṃ, jaṃ, vaṃ, and śaṃ are for <s>Puṣṭikā</s>.

children.text: ghaṃ vaṃ ca vanamālā syācchrī vatsaṃ daṃ saṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Ghaṃ and vaṃ are for the forest-garland; daṃ and saṃ are for <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.

children.text: chaṃ ḍaṃ paṃ yaṃ kaustubhaḥ proktaścānanto hyahameva ca
children.translated_text: Chaṃ, ḍaṃ, paṃ, and yaṃ are taught for <s>Kaustubha</s>; and there is <s>Ananta</s>, and also myself.
Thus these are the ten limbs of the god of gods, according to their proper application.
<s>Garuḍa</s> is like a lotus, and the mace is dark in form.
<s>Puṣṭi</s> has the appearance of a śirīṣa flower, and <s>Lakṣmī</s> is like gold.
The conch is like the full moon, and <s>Kaustubha</s> has the radiance of dawn.
The discus shines like a thousand suns, and <s>Śrīvatsa</s> is like jasmine.
The garland has the appearance of five colors, and <s>Ananta</s> is like a cloud.
The weapons whose colors have not been stated have the form of lightning.
He should offer arghya, pādya, and the rest with the <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s> vidyā.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe navavyūhārcanaṃ nāmaikādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eleventh chapter, named "The Worship of the Nine Vyūhas," is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
For the accomplishment of the sequence of worship, the sequence of worship is now stated.
At the beginning, with "oṃ namaḥ," there is recollection of the supreme self.
With yaṃ, raṃ, vaṃ, and laṃ, there is purification of the body.
With "oṃ namaḥ," there is the construction of oneself as four-armed.
Then comes the threefold nyāsa of hand and body.
Then comes worship of the <s>yogapīṭha</s> established in the heart.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Dharma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Jñāna</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vairāgya</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Aiśvarya</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Adharma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ajñāna</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Avairāgya</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Anaiśvarya</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ, homage to the solar maṇḍala.
Oṃ, homage to the lunar maṇḍala.
Oṃ, homage to the fire maṇḍala.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vimalā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Jñānā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kriyā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yogā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Prahvī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Satyā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Īśānā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the one whose face is everywhere.
Oṃ, homage to the seat of <s>Hari</s>, together with its subsidiary limbs.
Then, in the pericarp: homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Āṃ, homage to the heart.
Īṃ, homage to the head.
Ūṃ, homage to the topknot.
Aiṃ, homage to the armor.
Auṃ, homage to the three eyes.
Aḥ phaṭ, homage to the weapon.
Āṃ, homage to <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>.
Aṃ, homage to <s>Pradyumna</s>.
Aḥ, homage to <s>Aniruddha</s>.
Oṃ aḥ, homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the Brahman denoted by the word tat.
Oṃ huṃ, homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: kṣaiṃ narasiṃhāya bhūr varāhya kaṃ vainateyāya jaṃ khaṃ vaṃ sudarśanāya khaṃ caṃ phaṃ ṣaṃ gadāyai vaṃ laṃ maṃ kṣaṃ pāñcajanyāya ghaṃ ḍhaṃ bhaṃ haṃ śriyai gaṃ ḍaṃ vaṃ śaṃ puṣṭyai dhaṃ vaṃ vanamālāyai daṃ śaṃ śrīvatsāya chaṃ ḍaṃ yaṃ kaustubhāya śaṃ śārṅgāya iṃ iṣudhibhyāṃ caṃ carmaṇe khaṃ khaḍgāya indrāya surāya partaye agnaye tejo'dhipataye yamāya dharmādhipataye kṣaṃ nairṛtāya rakṣo'dhipataye varuṇāya jalādhipataye yoṃ vāyave prāṇādhipataye dhāṃ dhanadāya dhanādhipataye hāṃ īśānāya vidyādhipataye oṃ vajrāya śaktyai oṃ daṇḍāya khaḍgāya oṃ pāśāya dhvajāya gadāyai triśūlāya laṃ anantāya pātālādhipataye khaṃ brahmaṇe sarvalokādhipataye oṃ namo bhagavate vāsudevāya namaḥ
