children.translated_text: Kṣaiṃ, to <s>Narasiṃha</s>; bhūr, to <s>Varāha</s>; kaṃ, to <s>Vainateya</s>; jaṃ khaṃ vaṃ, to the <s>Sudarśana</s>; khaṃ caṃ phaṃ ṣaṃ, to the mace; vaṃ laṃ maṃ kṣaṃ, to <s>Pāñcajanya</s>; ghaṃ ḍhaṃ bhaṃ haṃ, to <s>Śrī</s>; gaṃ ḍaṃ vaṃ śaṃ, to <s>Puṣṭi</s>; dhaṃ vaṃ, to the garland of forest flowers; daṃ śaṃ, to the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>; chaṃ ḍaṃ yaṃ, to the <s>Kaustubha</s>; śaṃ, to <s>Śārṅga</s>; iṃ, to the two quivers; caṃ, to the shield; khaṃ, to the sword; to <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods; to <s>Agni</s>, lord of brilliance; to <s>Yama</s>, lord of dharma; kṣaṃ, to <s>Nairṛta</s>, lord of the rākṣasas; to <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of the waters; yoṃ, to <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of the vital breath; dhāṃ, to <s>Dhanada</s>, lord of wealth; hāṃ, to <s>Īśāna</s>, lord of knowledge; oṃ, to the thunderbolt and the spear; oṃ, to the staff and sword; oṃ, to the noose, banner, mace, and trident; laṃ, to <s>Ananta</s>, lord of the netherworld; khaṃ, to <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of all worlds; oṃ, homage, homage to the blessed <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Oṃ oṃ, homage.
Oṃ naṃ, homage.
Oṃ moṃ, homage.
Oṃ oṃ bhaṃ, homage.
Oṃ gaṃ, homage.
Oṃ vaṃ, homage.
Oṃ teṃ, homage.
Oṃ vāṃ, homage.
Oṃ suṃ, homage.
Oṃ deṃ, homage.
Oṃ vāṃ, homage.
Oṃ yaṃ, homage.
Oṃ oṃ, homage.
Oṃ naṃ, homage.
Oṃ moṃ, homage.
Oṃ nāṃ, homage.
Oṃ rāṃ, homage.
Oṃ ṇāṃ, homage.
Oṃ yaṃ, homage.

children.text: oṃ naṃ noṃ bhagavateṃ vāṃsuṃdevāyaṃ oṃ namo nārāyaṇāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ naṃ noṃ bhagavateṃ vāṃsuṃdevāyaṃ; oṃ, homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
Salutation to you, lotus-eyed one; salutation to you, creator of the universe.
Salutation to you, most holy great person, first-born one.
In the rite of homa one should arrange these with svāhā at the end.
Having recited thus according to rule, likewise one hundred and eight times,

children.text: arghaṃ dattvā jitaṃ tena praṇāmaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: and having given the argha, thereby he has conquered; then he should make obeisance again and again.
Then, having worshipped him also in the fire, he should sacrifice to him according to rule.
He should worship the god of gods, <s>Acyuta</s>, with his own bīja and with the limbs and the rest.
Having first drawn it out and sprinkled it, the knower of mantra should use the praṇava.
Having caused the fire to move around in the pit, he should worship with auspicious fruits.

children.text: pūrvaṃ tatsakalaṃ dhyātvā maṇḍale manasā nyaset ||
children.translated_text: Having first meditated on all of that, he should place it mentally in the maṇḍala.
Having offered one hundred and eight oblations with the principle called <s>Vāsudeva</s>,
he should similarly worship the set of six with the bīja of <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s> and the others.
Likewise, three by three, for the limbs, and each of the lords of the directions,
and at the end, standing properly, he should give the full oblation in the same way.

children.text: vāgatīte pare tattve ātmānaṃ ca layaṃ nayet
children.translated_text: He should bring the self to dissolution in the supreme principle beyond speech.
Sitting down again, having displayed the mudrā, he should bow once more.
Such a homa is daily; on an occasional rite it should be doubled.

children.text: gaccha gaccha paraṃ sthānaṃ yatra devo nirañjanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Go, go to the supreme place where the stainless god abides.
Let all the deities go, for the sake of remaining in their own places."
<s>Sudarśana</s>, <s>Śrīhari</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, and he who is <s>Trivikrama</s>,

children.text: caturbhujo vāsudevaḥ ṣaṣṭhaḥ pradyumna eva ca
children.translated_text: the four-armed <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and the sixth is <s>Pradyumna</s>;
<s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, then <s>Puruṣa</s>, the ninth emanation, and the tenfold one;
<s>Aniruddha</s>, the twelvefold one, and above them <s>Ananta</s>:
these gods should be known as marked by wheels beginning with one and so on.
When worshipped by men with wheel-marked rites, he should always protect the house.

children.text: oṃ cakrāya svāhā oṃ vicakrāya svāhā oṃ sucakrāya svāhā oṃ mahācakrāya svāhā oṃ mahācakrāya asurāntakṛt huṃ phaṭ oṃ huṃ sahasrāra huṃ phaṭ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ, to the wheel, svāhā; oṃ, to the special wheel, svāhā; oṃ, to the good wheel, svāhā; oṃ, to the great wheel, svāhā; oṃ, to the great wheel, destroyer of demons, huṃ phaṭ; oṃ huṃ, thousand-spoked one, huṃ phaṭ.
This worship of the <s>Dvārakā</s> wheel is auspicious and brings protection in the house.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe pūjānukramanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first part called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the twelfth chapter, named "Description of the Order of Worship," is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Now I shall teach this auspicious Vaiṣṇava armor-cage.
Homage, homage to you; taking up the <s>Sudarśana</s> wheel,

children.text: prācyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: protect me in the east, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I have gone to you for refuge.

children.text: gadāṃ kaumodakīṃ gṛhṇa padmanābha namo 'sta te ||
children.translated_text: Take up the mace <s>Kaumodakī</s>, O <s>Padmanābha</s>; salutation be to you.

children.text: yāmyāṃ rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Protect me in the south, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I have gone to you for refuge.
Taking up the plough, O wielder of <s>Saunanda</s>, salutation to you, <s>Puruṣottama</s>.

children.text: pratīcyāṃ rakṣa māṃ viṣṇo tvāmahaṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: Protect me in the west, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I have gone to you for refuge.

children.text: musalaṃ śātanaṃ gṛhya puṇḍarīkākṣa rakṣa mām ||
children.translated_text: Taking up the crushing pestle, O lotus-eyed one, protect me.
In the north, O lord of the world, I have gone to you for refuge.
Taking up the sword, and then the shield, and weapons and missiles, O <s>Hari</s>,

children.text: namaste rakṣa rakṣoghna aiśānyāṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: salutation to you; protect, O destroyer of hostile beings; I have gone for refuge in the northeast.
The great conch <s>Pāñcajanya</s>, and the resounding lotus,

children.text: pragṛhya rakṣa māṃ viṣṇo āgneyyāṃ rakṣa sūkara
children.translated_text: Having taken hold of it, protect me, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; in the southeast protect me, O <s>Sūkara</s>.
Taking up the moon and sun, and likewise the lunar sword,

children.text: nairṛtyāṃ māṃ ca rakṣasva divyamūrte nṛkesarin
children.translated_text: protect me in the southwest, O divine-formed <s>Nṛkeśarin</s>.
Taking up the <s>Vaijayantī</s> garland and the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, the ornament of the throat,

children.text: vāyavyāṃ rakṣa māṃ deva hayagrīva namo 'stu te
children.translated_text: protect me in the northwest, O god <s>Hayagrīva</s>; obeisance to you.
Mounting <s>Vainateya</s>, O <s>Janārdana</s>, in the midair,
protect me always, O unconquered one; obeisance to you, O undefeated one.

children.text: viśālākṣaṃ samāruhya rakṣa māṃ tvaṃ rasātale ||
children.translated_text: Mounting <s>Viśālākṣa</s>, protect me in the netherworld.
Obeisance to you, O <s>Akūpāra</s>; obeisance to you, O great fish.
In the fingers, beginning with the tips of the hands, O true one, make an arm-cage,

children.text: kṛtvā rakṣasva māṃ viṣṇo namaste puruṣottama
children.translated_text: and protect me, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>; obeisance to you, O <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
This great Vaiṣṇava cage of protection was spoken to <s>Śaṅkara</s>
long ago, for the protection of <s>Īśānī</s>, O bull-bannered one, and of <s>Kātyāyanī</s>.
By it she destroyed the Cāmaras and <s>Mahiṣāsura</s>,
the demon <s>Raktabīja</s>, and the other tormentors of the gods.
A man who recites this with devotion always conquers his enemies.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣṇupañjarastotraṃ nāma trayodaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa called the first section, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the thirteenth chapter, named the <s>Viṣṇupañjara</s> hymn, is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Now I shall teach yoga, the supreme means that grants enjoyment and liberation.
By those who meditate, <s>Hari</s>, the Lord, is called the object to be meditated upon through meditation.
Listen to this, O <s>Maheśāna</s>, destroyer of all sin.
<s>Viṣṇu</s> is the Lord of all, endless, devoid of the six worldly conditions.
He is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, lord of the world, the self of <s>Brahmā</s>; indeed, I myself am he.
He abides eternally in the embodied person and in the body, yet is free from every body.
He is without the properties of the body and is free from the perishable and the imperishable.

children.text: ṣaḍvidheṣu sthito draṣṭā śrotā ghrātā hyatīndriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Situated in the six kinds of objects, he is the seer, hearer, and smeller, yet beyond the senses.
He is free from their properties, the creator, devoid of name and lineage.
The god is the thinker, abiding in the mind, yet separate from the mind.
He is without the properties of the mind, and is discernment and knowledge itself.
He is the knower, abiding in the intellect, the witness, omniscient, yet free from intellect.
He is without the properties of intellect; he is all, all-pervading mind,
released from all living beings and devoid of the properties of breath.
He is the breath of breath, greatly peaceful, free from fear,
without egoism and the rest, and devoid of their properties.
He is their witness and their controller, having the form of supreme bliss.
He abides in waking, dream, and deep sleep; he is their witness and free from them.
He is the fourth state, the supreme supporter, whose form is sight, free from the qualities.

children.text: mukto buddho 'jaro vyāpī satya ātmāsmyahaṃ śivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: I am the liberated, awakened, ageless, all-pervading, true, auspicious self.

children.text: evaṃ ye mānavā vijñā dhyāyantīśaṃ paraṃ padam
children.translated_text: Those wise human beings who thus meditate on the Lord, the supreme abode,

children.text: prāpnuyuste ca tadrūpaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā ||
children.translated_text: attain his form; there is no deliberation to be made about this.

children.text: iti dhyānaṃ samākhyātaṃ tava śaṅkara suvrata
children.translated_text: Thus meditation has been explained to you, O well-vowed <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Whoever constantly recites this goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe dhyānayogo nāma caturdaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa called the first section, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the fourteenth chapter, named Dhyānayoga, is completed.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
By reciting what, O Lord, is a man released from the terrible ocean of saṃsāra?

children.text: narastanme paraṃ japyaṃ pathaya tvaṃ janārdana ||
children.translated_text: Teach me that supreme recitation, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
A man who praises <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the supreme Lord, the supreme brahman, the imperishable supreme self,
with the thousand names becomes liberated.

children.text: yat pavitraṃ paraṃ japyaṃ kathayāmi vṛṣadhvaja
children.translated_text: I shall teach what is supremely purifying and the highest recitation, O bull-bannered one.
Listen with attention to that which destroys all sin.
Oṃ. He is <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Vāsava</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>;
he is like the young moon, youthful, <s>Balabhadra</s>, and lord of strength.
He bound <s>Bali</s>; he is the ordainer, the excellent one, the knower of the Veda, the seer-poet.
He is maker of the Veda, form of the Veda, to be known through the Veda, and filled with the Veda.
He knows the limbs of the Veda, is lord of the Veda, support of strength, and destroyer of strength.
He is changeless, lord of boons, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and lord of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
He slays heroes, is a great hero, honored, the supreme Lord.

children.text: ātmā ca paramātmā ca pratyagātmā viyatparaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is the self, the supreme self, the inner self, and beyond space.
He is lotus-naveled, treasure of lotuses, lotus-handed, and mace-bearing.
He is supreme, beyond all beings, <s>Puruṣottama</s>, and Lord.
His shanks are lotuses; he is a lotus, wearer of a lotus garland, beloved.
He is lotus-eyed, lotus-wombed, rain-cloud, and seated on a lotus.

children.text: apāraḥ paramārthaśca parāṇāṃ ca paraḥ prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: He is boundless, the highest truth, higher than the highest, the Lord.
He is learned, praised by the learned, purifying, and crusher of sin.
He is pure, whose form is light, purifying, and protector on every side.
He is free from thirst, worthy of foot-water, the person, and also <s>prakṛti</s> (primordial nature).
He is <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter), earth, lotus, lotus-naveled, and giver of what is dear.
He is lord of all, all-pervading, all, all-knowing, all-giving, and divine.

children.text: sarvasya jagato dhāma sarvadarśo ca sarvabhṛt
children.translated_text: He is the abode of the whole world, all-seeing, and bearer of all.
The god grants favor to all and dwells in the heart of every being.
He is worshiped by all, first of all, and honored by all the gods.
He is the root of the whole world, with parts and without parts, fire.
He is protector of all, the ground of all, and the cause of every cause.
He is to be meditated on by all, friend of all, and bearer of every form in every place.
He is overseer of all, overseer of the gods, and honored by gods and asuras.

children.text: duṣṭānāṃ ca surāṇāṃ ca sarvadā ghātako 'ntakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is at all times the destroyer and ender of both the wicked and the gods.
He is <s>Satyapāla</s>, well-formed, lord of the siddhas, honored by the siddhas.
He is accomplished by the siddhas and sādhyas, perfected among the perfected, fulfiller of what is to be accomplished, the lord within the heart.
He is the refuge of the world, and also prosperity and security.
He is the doer of good, auspicious, gentle, true, and of true valor.
He stands in truth, has true resolve, knows truth, and likewise gives truth.

children.text: dharmo dharmo ca karmo ca sarvakarmavivarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is <s>Dharma</s>, dharma, and action, yet free from all action.

children.text: karmakartā ca karmaiva kriyā kāryaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: He is the doer of action, action itself, the rite, and likewise the thing to be done.
He is the lord of <s>Śrī</s>, lord of kings, glorious, and the mighty lord of all.
He is indeed the lord of the gods and the praised lord of the Vṛṣṇis.
He is the lord of <s>Hiraṇyagarbha</s>, and likewise the lord of <s>Tripurānta</s>.

children.text: paśūnāṃ ca patiḥ prāyo vasūnāṃ patireva ca
children.translated_text: He is the lord of beasts, generally, and indeed the lord of the Vasus.
He is the lord of <s>Ākhaṇḍala</s> himself, and likewise the lord of <s>Varuṇa</s>.
He is the lord of forest trees, and likewise the lord of wind.
He is indeed the lord of fire, and likewise the lord of <s>Yama</s>.
He is indeed the lord of <s>Kubera</s>, and likewise the lord of the lunar mansions.
He is indeed the lord of herbs, and likewise the lord of trees.
He is the lord of serpents, of the sun, and indeed the lord of <s>Dakṣa</s>.

children.text: suhṛdāṃ ca patiścaiva nṛpāṇāṃ ca patistathā ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the lord of friends, and likewise the lord of kings.
He is indeed the lord of gandharvas and the supreme lord of vital breaths.
He is indeed the lord of mountains, and likewise the lord of rivers.

children.text: surāṇāṃ ca patiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ kapilasya patistathā
children.translated_text: He is the best lord of the gods, and likewise the lord of <s>Kapila</s>.

children.text: latānāṃ ca patiścaiva vīrudhāṃ ca patistathā ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the lord of creepers, and likewise the lord of plants.
He is indeed the lord of sages and the supreme lord of the sun.
He is the best lord of the moon, and indeed the lord of <s>Śukra</s>.
He is indeed the lord of planets, and likewise the lord of rākṣasas.
He is indeed the lord of kinnaras and the supreme lord of twice-born men.
He is indeed the lord of rivers, and likewise the lord of oceans.

children.text: sarasāṃ ca patiścaiva bhūtānāṃ ca patistathā ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the lord of lakes, and likewise the lord of beings.
He is indeed the lord of vetālas, and likewise the lord of kūṣmāṇḍas.

children.text: pakṣiṇāṃ ca patiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ paśūnāṃ patireva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is the best lord of birds, and indeed the lord of beasts.
He is the great-souled one, auspicious, measurable, <s>Mandara</s>, and lord of <s>Mandara</s>.
He is <s>Meru</s>, mother, measure, <s>Mādhava</s>, and free from impurity.
He wears a garland, is the great god, and is worshipped by <s>Mahādeva</s>.
He is greatly peaceful, greatly fortunate, and indeed <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
He has great heroism and great breath, and is honored by the sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s>.

children.text: māyātmā māyayā baddho māyayā tu vivarjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His nature is māyā; he is bound by māyā, yet free from māyā.
He is praised by sages; he is a sage, friendly, great-nosed, and great-jawed.
He is great-armed, great-toothed, and free from death.
He has a great mouth, is great-souled, great-bodied, and great-bellied.
He has great feet, a great neck, great pride, and a great mind.
He has a great course, great fame, a great form, and is a great asura.
He is <s>Madhu</s> and <s>Mādhava</s>, and indeed <s>Mahādeva</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
He is worshipped in sacrifice, has sacrifice as his form, is worthy of honor, and is lord of sacrifice.
He is the great wind, greatly fortunate, the great lord, and beyond human measure.
He is human and <s>Manu</s> himself, the maker of welfare for human beings.
He is the deer, worshipped by deer, and likewise the lord of deer.
He is indeed the lord of <s>Budha</s>, and indeed the lord of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
He is the lord of <s>Śanaiścara</s> himself, and likewise the lord of <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Ketu</s>.
He is <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, the mark, long-lipped, and graceful.
He is adorned with many ornaments and anointed with many sandal pastes.
His face shines with many essences and is beautified with many flowers.
He is <s>Rāma</s>, the lord of <s>Ramā</s>, together with his wife, the supreme lord.
He gives jewels and takes jewels; he has form and is without form.
He has a great form, a terrible form, and likewise a gentle form.
He resembles a dark cloud, is pure, and likewise resembles a sāla cloud.
He is smoke-colored, lord-colored, of many forms, and indeed colorless.
He is deformed and also giver of form, and likewise white in color.
He is of every color, a great yogin, sacrifice, and indeed the maker of sacrifice.
He possesses a golden color and likewise bears the name golden.
His limbs are golden; he is golden and has a golden girdle.
He is the giver of gold and likewise the lord of gold.
He is fond of gold and likewise rich in gold.

children.text: suparṇaś ca mahāparṇaḥ suparṇasya ca kāraṇ
children.translated_text: He is <s>Suparṇa</s>, great-winged, and the cause of <s>Suparṇa</s>.
He is <s>Vainateya</s>, likewise <s>Āditya</s>, the beginning, maker of beginnings, and <s>Śiva</s>.
He is the cause of the great principle and indeed the cause of primordial matter.
He is indeed the cause of intellects, and likewise the cause of the mind.
He is indeed the cause of consciousness and the cause of egoity.
He is likewise the cause of beings and the cause of fire.
He is likewise the cause of space and the supreme cause of earth.

children.text: aṇḍasya kāraṇaṃ caiva prakṛteḥ kāraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the cause of the cosmic egg, and likewise the cause of prakṛti.
He is indeed the cause of the body and the cause of the eye.
He is likewise the cause of the ear and likewise the cause of the skin.

children.text: jihvāyāḥ kāraṇaṃ caiva prāṇasyaiva ca kāraṇam
children.translated_text: He is indeed the cause of the tongue and indeed the cause of breath.
He is likewise the cause of the hands and likewise the cause of the feet.
He is likewise the cause of speech and indeed the cause of the anus.

children.text: indrasya kāraṇaṃ caiva kuberasya ca kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the cause of <s>Indra</s> and the cause of <s>Kubera</s>.

children.text: yamasya kāraṇaṃ caiva īśānasya ca kāraṇam
children.translated_text: He is indeed the cause of <s>Yama</s> and the cause of <s>Īśāna</s>.

children.text: yakṣāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ caiva rakṣasāṃ kāraṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the cause of yakṣas and the supreme cause of rākṣasas.

children.text: nṛpāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ śreṣṭhaṃ dharmasyaiva tu kāraṇam
children.translated_text: He is the best cause of kings, and indeed the cause of dharma.

children.text: jantūnāṃ kāraṇaṃ caiva vasūnāṃ kāraṇaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: And he is the cause of living creatures, the supreme cause of the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: manūnāṃ kāraṇaṃ caiva pakṣiṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: And he is the cause of the <s>Manus</s>, the supreme cause of birds.
He is the cause of sages, the supreme cause of the best yogins.

children.text: siddhānāṃ kāraṇaṃ caiva yakṣāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: And he is the cause of the perfected beings, the supreme cause of the <s>Yakṣas</s>.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ kinnarāṇāṃ ca gandharvāṇāṃ ca kāraṇam ||
children.translated_text: He is the cause of the <s>Kinnaras</s>, and the cause of the <s>Gandharvas</s>.

children.text: nadānāṃ kāraṇaṃ caiva nadīnāṃ kāraṇaṃ param
children.translated_text: And he is the cause of rivers and streams, the supreme cause of rivers.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ ca samudrāṇāṃ vṛkṣāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He is the cause of the oceans, and likewise the cause of trees.

children.text: kāraṇaṃ vīrudhāṃ caiva lokānāṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: And he is the cause of plants, and likewise the cause of the worlds.
And he is the cause of <s>Pātāla</s>, and likewise the cause of the gods.

children.text: sarpāṇāṃ kāraṇaṃ caiva śreyasāṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: And he is the cause of serpents, and likewise the cause of blessings.

children.text: pūśanāṃ kāraṇaṃ caiva sarveṣāṃ kāraṇaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: And he is the cause of the nourisher <s>Pūṣan</s>, and likewise the cause of all things.

children.text: dehātmā cendriyātmā ca ātmā buddhistathaiva ca
children.translated_text: He is the self of the body and the self of the senses; he is the self, and likewise intelligence.
Likewise he is the self of the mind, and the self of the ego-consciousness.
He is the self of the waking and the sleeping one; he is the self of the great principle and beyond it.

children.text: pradhānasya parātmā ca ākāśātmā hy apāṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He is the supreme self of primordial matter, and the self of space and of the waters.

children.text: pṛthivyāḥ paramātmā ca rasasyātmā tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: He is the supreme self of the earth, and likewise the self of taste.
He is the supreme self of smell, and likewise the higher self of form.
He is the self of sound, the self of speech, the self of touch, and likewise the <s>Puruṣa</s>.

children.text: śrotrātmā ca tvagātmā ca jihvāyāḥ paramastathā ||
children.translated_text: He is the self of hearing, the self of skin, and the supreme self of the tongue.
He is the self of smell, the self of the hands, and likewise the supreme self of the feet.
Likewise he is the self of the generative organ, and likewise the supreme self of the anus.

children.text: indrātmā caiva brahmātmā rudrātmā ca manostathā
children.translated_text: He is the self of <s>Indra</s>, the self of <s>Brahmā</s>, the self of <s>Rudra</s>, and likewise of <s>Manu</s>.
He is the self of <s>Dakṣa Prajāpati</s>, the self of truth, and likewise the supreme one.
He is the self of the lord, the supreme self, the fierce self, and the attainment of liberating knowledge.

children.text: yatnavāṃśca tathā yatnaś carmo khaḍgī murāntakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is effortful, and he is effort; he is armor, sword-bearing, and the destroyer of <s>Mura</s>.
He has the nature of setting modesty in motion, and he is devoted to the welfare of ascetics.

children.text: yatirūpī ca yogī ca yogidhyeyo hariḥ śitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: He has the form of an ascetic, is a yogin, is to be meditated on by yogins; he is <s>Hari</s>, the white one.

children.text: saṃvinmedhā ca kālaśca ūṣmā varṣā matistathā
children.translated_text: He is consciousness, wisdom, time, heat, rain, and likewise thought.
He is the year, the maker of liberation, and likewise the destroyer of delusion.
He is the maker of delusion for the wicked, <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, and the submarine fire-mouth.
He is <s>Saṃvarta</s>, the maker of time, <s>Gautama</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s>.

children.text: atrir vasiṣṭhaḥ pulahaḥ pulastyaḥ kutsa eva ca
children.translated_text: He is <s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, and also <s>Kutsa</s>.
He is <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, <s>Devala</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, and <s>Parāśara</s>.
He is the giver of happiness, <s>Gāṅgeya</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, and the one of great fame.
He is <s>Keśava</s>, destroyer of affliction, fair-eared, and without ears.
He is <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, greatly fortunate, and indeed the lord of the vital breath <s>prāṇa</s>.
He is the lord of <s>apāna</s>, and the lord of <s>vyāna</s>.
He is the best lord of <s>udāna</s>, and likewise the lord of <s>samāna</s>.

children.text: śabdasya ca patiḥ śreṣṭhaḥ sparśasya patireva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is the best lord of sound, and indeed the lord of touch.
He is the first lord of forms, sword in hand and armed with the plough.
He bears the discus in his hand, wears earrings, and is marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.
He is nature, has the <s>Kaustubha</s> on his neck, and wears yellow garments.
He is fair-faced and grim-faced, and is without ugly nails.
He is endless, of endless forms, fair-nailed, and the mountain of the gods.
He is fair-cheeked, all-pervading, victorious, shining, and likewise armed with arrows.
He is the slayer of <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s> and crusher of <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
He is the killer of <s>Pūtanā</s> and destroyer of the end of the sun.
He is the crusher of <s>Keśin</s> and the pulverizer of <s>Muṣṭika</s>.
He is the splitter of the demon <s>Kaṃsa</s> and the crusher of <s>Cāṇūra</s>.

children.text: ariṣṭasya nihantā ca akrūrapriya eva ca
children.translated_text: He is the killer of <s>Ariṣṭa</s>, and dear to <s>Akrūra</s>.
He is <s>Akrūra</s>, has a fierce form, and is worshipped by dear <s>Akrūra</s>.

children.text: bhagahā bhagavān bhānustathā bhāgavataḥ svagavataḥ svayam
children.translated_text: He is the taker of fortune, the blessed lord, the sun, and likewise the devotee himself; the text here is corrupt.
He is <s>Uddhava</s>, the lord of <s>Uddhava</s>, and contemplated by <s>Uddhava</s>.
He bears the discus, is mobile, and is free from both moving and unmoving things.
He is ego, likeness, mind, sky, earth, and water.

children.text: vāyuścakṣustathā śrotraṃ jihvā ca ghrāṇameva ca
children.translated_text: He is wind, sight, hearing, tongue, and smell.
He is speech, hand, foot, swiftness, anus, and generative organ.
He is <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the all, giver of patience, maker of patience, and man.
He is dear to devotees, father, supporter, devoted, and increaser of devotion.
He is praised by devotees, devoted to devotees, giver of fame, and increaser of fame.

children.text: kīrtirdeptiḥ kṣamā kāntir bhaktaścaiva dayā parā ||
children.translated_text: He is fame, splendor, forbearance, beauty, a devotee, and supreme compassion.

children.text: dānaṃ dātā ca kartā ca devadevapriyaḥ śuciḥ
children.translated_text: He is gift, giver, maker, beloved of the gods' god, and pure.
He is pure, giver of happiness, liberation, desire, wealth, and thousand-footed.
He is thousand-headed, a physician, and likewise the door to liberation.
He is the door of creatures, thousand-eyed, and thousand-handed.
He is <s>Śukra</s>, well-crowned, fair-necked, and likewise <s>Kaustubha</s>.
He is <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, <s>Hayagrīva</s>, and the Boar.
He is the Fish, <s>Paraśurāma</s>, <s>Prahrāda</s>, and <s>Bali</s>.
He is a refuge, eternal, awakened, liberated, and embodied.
He is the slayer of <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>, and the crusher of <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.
He is the husband of <s>Sītā</s>, ever-growing, and likewise <s>Bharata</s>.
He is the killer of <s>Kumbha</s> and <s>Indrajit</s>, and the crusher of <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
He is the ender of <s>Narāntaka</s> and destroyer of <s>Devāntaka</s>.
He is the killer of wicked demons and likewise the enemy of <s>Śambara</s>.
He is the killer of <s>Naraka</s> and the destroyer of <s>Triśīrṣa</s>.
He is the breaker of the twin <s>Yamala-Arjuna</s> trees and the doer of good for asceticism.

children.text: vāditraṃ caiva vādyaṃ ca buddhaścaiva varapradaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is instrumental music itself and that which is played; he is <s>Buddha</s> and the bestower of boons.
He is the essence, lover of the essence, solar, the cutter down of the destroyer Time.
He is <s>Agastya</s> and <s>Devala</s>, and <s>Nārada</s>, dear to <s>Nārada</s>.

children.text: prāṇo 'pānastathā vyāno rajaḥ sattvaṃ tamaḥ śarat
children.translated_text: He is <s>prāṇa</s> (the vital breath), <s>apāna</s>, and <s>vyāna</s>; he is <s>rajas</s>, <s>sattva</s>, <s>tamas</s>, and autumn.

children.text: udānaśca samānaśca bheṣajaṃ ca bhiṣak tathā ||
children.translated_text: He is <s>udāna</s> and <s>samāna</s>; he is medicine and also the physician.
He is changeless, of clear and pure form, and devoid of every body.
He is without the faculty of sight and devoid of the faculty of speech.
He is without the faculty of the hands and is also devoid of the two feet.
He is without anus and generative organ, and free from wind and water.
He is without conscious awakening and is also devoid of intellect.
He is gone beyond mind itself and devoid of vital breath.
He is without <s>apāna</s> and also devoid of <s>vyāna</s>.
He is without <s>udāna</s> and devoid of <s>samāna</s>.
He is without ether and free from wind.
He is without fire and devoid of water.

children.text: pṛthivyā ca vihīnaśca śabdena ca vivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: He is without earth and devoid of sound.
He is without touch and devoid of every form.
He is free from passion and entirely free from sin.
He is without sorrow and free from speech.
He is devoid of <s>rajas</s> and of the six transformations.
He is free from desire and entirely free from anger.
He is gone beyond greed and devoid of hypocrisy.
He is subtle and very subtle, and grosser than the gross.
He is expert, superintendent of power, and agitator of everything.
He is the agitator of <s>prakṛti</s> and also the agitator of <s>mahat</s>.
He is the agitator of the beings and also the agitator of the intellect.
He is the agitator of the senses and likewise the agitator of the sense-objects.
He is the agitator of <s>Brahmā</s> and also the agitator of <s>Rudra</s>.
He is inaccessible to the eye and the other senses, and likewise inaccessible to the ear.

children.text: tvacā na gamyaḥ kūrmaśca jihvāgrāhyastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: He is not reached by the skin; he is <s>Kūrma</s>, and likewise not grasped by the tongue.
He is inaccessible to the faculty of smell and likewise ungraspable by speech.
He is not reached by the hands and likewise not reached by the feet.
He is ungraspable by the mind, ungraspable by the intellect; such is <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: ahaṃ buddhyā tathā grāhyaścetasā grāhyā eva ca
children.translated_text: As the 'I' he is apprehensible by understanding, and likewise apprehensible by the mind.
He holds the conch in his hand, is imperishable, and likewise holds the mace in his hand.
He holds the <s>Śārṅga</s> bow in his hand; he is <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, the embodiment of knowledge, scorcher of foes.

children.text: tapasvī jñānagamyo hi jñānī jñānavideva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is an ascetic, indeed accessible through knowledge, a knower, and a knower of knowledge.
He is what is to be known and beyond what is to be known; he is cognition, having the form of consciousness.
He is being, what is to be brought into being, the maker of existence, the creator, and the destroyer of becoming.
He is <s>Govinda</s>, lord of cows, cowherd, and giver of happiness to all the cowherd-women.
He is protector of cows, the way of cows, possessed of cows, and likewise bearer of cows.
He is <s>Upendra</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, <s>Śauri</s>, and <s>Janārdana</s>.
He is fire-born, great-rayed, and likewise of great brilliance.
He is <s>Dāmodara</s>, the three times, knower of time, and free from time.
He is the three junctions of the day, <s>Dvāpara</s> and <s>Tretā</s>, the gate of creatures, and <s>Trivikrama</s>.
He is stride and valor, staff in hand, the single-staff ascetic, and the bearer of the triple staff.
He is conciliation and division, likewise strategy; he has the form of the Sāman and sings the Sāman.
He is the <s>Sāmaveda</s> and the <s>Atharvaveda</s>; he is well-made and beautifully formed.
He is the knower of the <s>Atharvaveda</s> and also the teacher of the Atharvan tradition.
He has the form of the Ṛc; he is the <s>Ṛgveda</s>, established in the Ṛgveda hymns.
He is the <s>Yajurveda</s>, the knower of the Yajurveda, and the one-footed one.
He is many-footed, well-footed, and likewise thousand-footed.
He is four-footed and two-footed; he is <s>smṛti</s>, logic, <s>Yama</s>, and the strong one.
He is the renouncer and non-renunciation, and the four <s>āśramas</s>.
He is the celibate student, the householder, the forest-dweller, and the mendicant.

children.text: brāhmaṇaḥ kṣatriyo vaiśyaḥ śūdro varṇastathaiva ca
children.translated_text: He is the Brahmin, the Kṣatriya, the Vaiśya, the Śūdra, and likewise the social class.
He gives good conduct, is endowed with good conduct, and is free from bad conduct.
He is liberation, absorbed in the inner self; he is praise, the praiser, and the worshipper.

children.text: pūjyo vāk karaṇaṃ caiva vācyaṃ caiva tu vācakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is worshipful; he is speech, the instrument, what is to be expressed, and the expresser.

children.text: vettā vyākaraṇaṃ caiva vākyaṃ caiva ca vākyavit
children.translated_text: He is the knower, grammar, the sentence, and the knower of sentences.
He is reached through the sentence, dwelling at a sacred ford; he is the sacred ford and the knower of sacred fords.
He is the primal source of sacred fords; he is <s>Sāṃkhya</s>, <s>Nirukta</s>, and the divine referent.
He is the <s>praṇava</s>, lord of the praṇava, and deeply praised by the praṇava.

children.text: praṇavena ca lakṣyo vai gāyatrī ca gadādharaḥ
children.translated_text: He is indeed indicated by the praṇava; he is the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the mace-bearer.
He dwells in the <s>Śālagrāma</s>, and likewise is the Śālagrāma itself.
He reclines on the waters, reclines in yoga, reclines on <s>Śeṣa</s>, and rests on the lotus.

children.text: mahībhartā ca kāryaṃ ca kāraṇaṃ pṛthivīdharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is bearer of the earth, the effect, the cause, and holder of the earth.
He is <s>Prajāpati</s>, eternal, desirable, the desirer, and <s>Virāṭ</s>.

children.text: samrāṭ pūṣā tathā svargo rathasthaḥ sārathirbalam ||
children.translated_text: He is emperor, <s>Pūṣan</s>, heaven, chariot-mounted, charioteer, and strength.

children.text: dhanī dhanaprado dhanyo yādavānāṃ hite rataḥ
children.translated_text: He is wealthy, giver of wealth, blessed, and intent on the welfare of the <s>Yādavas</s>.

children.text: arjunasya priyaścaiva hyarjuno bhīma eva ca ||
children.translated_text: He is dear to <s>Arjuna</s>; he is also <s>Arjuna</s> and <s>Bhīma</s>.
He is valor, hard to withstand, and expert in all śāstras.
He is Sārasvata, greatly awesome, and likewise the remover of the <s>Pārijāta</s>.

children.text: amṛtasya pradātā ca kṣīrodaḥ kṣīrameva ca
children.translated_text: He is the giver of nectar, the ocean of milk, and milk itself.
He is the son of <s>Indra</s>, his protector, and likewise the lifter of <s>Govardhana</s>.
He is the destroyer of <s>Kaṃsa</s>, and likewise protector of elephants and destroyer of elephants.
He is <s>Śipiviṣṭa</s>, gracious, and remover of the affliction of all worlds.
He is the seal, maker of seals, and free from all seals.
He is the embodied one, abiding in the body, and the controller of the body.

children.text: śrotrā śrotraniyantā ca śrotavyaḥ śravaṇaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He is the ear, the controller of the ear, what is to be heard, and hearing itself.

children.text: tvaksthitaśca sparśayitvā spṛśyaṃ ca sparśanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He abides in the skin; he makes contact; he is what is touched and touch itself.
He is the seer of form, abiding in the eye, and the controller of the eye.

children.text: dṛśyaṃ caiva tu jihvāstho rasajñaśca niyāmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He is indeed the visible object; abiding in the tongue, he knows taste and is its controller.
He abides in the nose, makes smelling, is the smeller, and controls the organ of smell.

children.text: vākstho vaktā ca vaktavyo vacanaṃ vāṅniyāmakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He abides in speech, is the speaker, what is to be spoken, speech itself, and the controller of speech.
He abides in living beings; he is the maker of craft, craft itself, and the controller of the hands.

children.text: padavyaścaiva gantā ca gantavyaṃ gamanaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He is the paths, the goer, what is to be reached, and going itself.
He is also the controller of the feet, the recipient of foot-water, and the maker of excretion.

children.text: visargasya niyantā ca hyupasthasthaḥ sukhaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: He is the controller of excretion, and, abiding in the generative organ, is pleasure itself.
He is the controller of the generative organ and the giver of that bliss.
He is <s>Śatrughna</s>, <s>Kārtavīrya</s>, and likewise <s>Dattātreya</s>.
He is the benefactor of <s>Alarka</s> and the cutter down of <s>Kārtavīrya</s>.
He is <s>Kālanemi</s>, the great-rimmed one, cloud, and lord of clouds.
He gives food, has the form of food, eats food, and sets food in motion.
He makes smoke, has the form of smoke, and is the excellent son of <s>Devakī</s>.

children.text: devakyānandano nando rohiṇyāḥ priya eva ca
children.translated_text: He is the joy of <s>Devakī</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, and dear to <s>Rohiṇī</s>.
He is dear to <s>Vasudeva</s> and likewise the son of <s>Vasudeva</s>.
He is the kettledrum, laughter in form, and flower-like laughter.
He loves loud laughter; he is overseer of all, the perishable and the imperishable.
He is <s>Acyuta</s>, lord of truth, and the excellent beloved of <s>Satyā</s>.
He is the husband of <s>Rukmiṇī</s> and likewise the beloved of <s>Rukmiṇī</s>.
He is the beloved of the cowherd women, and renowned as one whose verse is meritorious.
He is <s>Vṛṣākapi</s>, <s>Yama</s>, the secret one, <s>Makula</s>, and <s>Budha</s>.
He is <s>Rāhu</s>, <s>Ketu</s>, a planet, a seizer, and the one joined with the elephant-lord's face.
He is the destroyer of the seizer, the villager, and the protector.

children.text: kinnaraścaiva siddhaśca chandaḥ svacchanda eva ca
children.translated_text: He is a <s>kinnara</s>, a perfected being, meter, and the self-willed one.
He is universal in form, broad-eyed, and destroyer of demons.
He has endless forms, abides in beings, and is established among gods and dānavas.

children.text: suṣuptisthaḥ suṣuptiśca sthānaṃ sthānānta eva ca ||
children.translated_text: He abides in deep sleep; he is deep sleep, the state, and the end of states.
He abides in the world, is the waker, the state, and waking.
He abides in his own dream, knows his own dream, and is the dream-state and dream itself.
He is the fourth, indeed, free from waking, dream, and deep sleep.

children.text: vijñānaṃ vedyarūpaṃ ca jīvo jīvayitā tathā ||
children.translated_text: He is cognition, the form of what is to be known, the living soul, and the giver of life.
He is lord of the worlds and controller of the worlds.
He dwells in <s>Pātāla</s>, is <s>Pātāla</s> itself, and destroys every fever.
He has the form of supreme bliss and sets the dharmas in motion.
He is easy to obtain and difficult to obtain, and he is devoted to breath-control.
He is withdrawal of the senses, the supporter, and the maker of withdrawal.
He is splendor, beauty, and flame, resembling pure crystal.
He is ungraspable, fair, all, pure, and praised.

children.text: vaṣaṭkāro vaṣaḍ vauṣaṭ svadhā svāhā ratistathā ||
children.translated_text: He is the vaṣaṭ-call, vaṣaḍ, vauṣaṭ, svadhā, svāhā, and delight.

children.text: paktā nandayitā bhoktā boddhā bhāvayitā tathā
children.translated_text: He is the cook, the delighter, the enjoyer, the knower, and the one who brings into being.
He is the self of knowledge, the self of the body, vastness, and the Lord of all lords.

children.text: nadī nandī ca nandīśo bhāratas tarunāśanaḥ
children.translated_text: He is river, <s>Nandī</s>, lord of <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Bhārata</s>, and destroyer of the tree.
He bears the discus, is lord of <s>Śrī</s>, and is lord of kings who are universal emperors.
He is lord of all the gods and is established in <s>Dvārakā</s>.
He is <s>Puṣkara</s>, overseer of <s>Puṣkara</s>, and <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s> itself.
He is <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Janaka</s>, what is produced, and devoid of every form.
He is formless, without cause, free from distress, and without support.
Thus, O bull-bannered one, the thousand names have been proclaimed to you
of the god <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord, which destroy all sin.
A twice-born man who recites them attains the state of <s>Viṣṇu</s>; a kṣatriya obtains victory.
A vaiśya obtains wealth and happiness; a śūdra becomes endowed with devotion to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śrīviṣṇusahasranāmastotranirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa called the first section, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the fifteenth chapter, named the exposition of the hymn of the thousand names of revered <s>Viṣṇu</s>, is completed.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
Again explain meditation, O bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the Lord, the god, the pure supreme self.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Listen, O <s>Rudra</s>, to meditation on <s>Hari</s>, which destroys the tree of saṃsāra,
who is endless in the form of sight, all-pervading, unborn, and undecaying.
He is imperishable, omnipresent, eternal; he is the great brahman alone.
He is the root of the whole world, all-pervading, the supreme Lord.
He indeed abides in the heart of every being and is the great Lord of all beings.
He is the support of all, without support, and the cause of every cause.
He is unstained, and liberated, contemplated by liberated yogins.
He is without a gross body and devoid of eyes.
He is without the organ of speech and devoid of the properties of living beings.
He is without the organ of feet and devoid of the properties of speech.
He is without anus or generative organ, and devoid of all sense-organs.
He is without mind, likewise devoid of the properties of mind.
He is the lord of gods, without intellect and devoid of thought.
He is indeed without ego and devoid of the properties of intellect.
He is without breath and devoid of downward breath.
He is without the wind called vyāna and devoid of the properties of breath.
<s>Hari</s> said:

children.text: punaḥ sūryarcanaṃ vakṣye yaduktaṃ bhṛgave purā ||
children.translated_text: Again I shall teach the worship of <s>Sūrya</s>, which was formerly taught to <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Khakholka</s>.
This is the root mantra of <s>Sūrya</s>, bestowing enjoyment and liberation.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Khakholka</s>, the god.
Oṃ vici ṭhaṭha. Homage to the head.
Oṃ. Homage to the knowing one, ṭhaṭha, to the topknot.
Oṃ. Homage to the thousand-rayed one, ṭhaṭha, to the armor.
Oṃ. Homage to the lord of all brilliance, ṭhaṭha, to the missile.

children.text: oṃ jvala jvala prajvala prajvala ṭhaṭha namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Blaze, blaze; flame forth, flame forth; ṭhaṭha. Homage.
This is <s>Sūrya</s>'s fire-rampart mantra, destroyer of sin.

children.text: oṃ ādityāya vidmahe viśvabhāvāya dhīmahi tannaḥ sūrya pracodayāt ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. We know <s>Āditya</s>; we meditate on the maker of the universe. May that <s>Sūrya</s> impel us.
He should perform the <s>sakalīkaraṇa</s> (integration rite) with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> of <s>Bhāskara</s>.
In the east, to <s>Dharmātman</s>; and in the south, with the formula 'to <s>Yama</s>'.
Then to <s>Daṇḍanāyaka</s>; and in the north, with the formula 'to the deity'.
In the northeast he should worship <s>Śyāma</s> and <s>Piṅgala</s>, and in the southeast <s>Dīkṣita</s>.

children.text: vajrapāṇiṃ ca nairṛtyāṃ bhūr bhuvaḥ svaśca vāyave
children.translated_text: And in the southwest <s>Vajrapāṇi</s>; in the northwest, <s>Bhūr</s>, <s>Bhuvaḥ</s>, and <s>Svaḥ</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Candra</s>, lord of the lunar mansions.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Aṅgāraka</s>, son of the earth.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Budha</s>, son of <s>Soma</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Vāgīśvara</s>, lord of all knowledge.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Śukra</s>, the great seer, son of <s>Bhṛgu</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Śanaiścara</s>, son of <s>Sūrya</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Rāhu</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Ketu</s>.
These are to be worshiped from the east up to the northeast, O bull-bannered one.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Anūka</s>.
Oṃ. Homage to the first lord.
Oṃ. Homage to <s>Buddha</s>.

children.text: oṃ bhagavannaparimitamayūkhamālin sakalajagatpate saptāśvavāhana caturbhuja paramasiddhiprada visphuliṅgapiṅgala tata ehyehi idamarghyaṃ mama śirasi gataṃ gṛhṇa gṛhṇa tejograrūpam anagna jvala jvala ṭhaṭha namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. O Blessed One, garlanded with immeasurable rays, lord of the whole world, borne by seven horses, four-armed, giver of supreme accomplishment, tawny like sparks, come, come here. Receive, receive this arghya of mine, placed upon my head, O one of fierce radiant form, unburned one. Blaze, blaze. ṭhaṭha. Homage.
Having invoked <s>Sūrya</s> with this invocation mantra, he should then dismiss him.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate ādityāya sahasrakiraṇāya gaccha sukhaṃ punarāgamanāyeti ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ. Homage to the Blessed <s>Āditya</s> of a thousand rays. Go happily, and return again.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe haridhyānasūryārcanayornirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa called the first section, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the sixteenth chapter, named the exposition of meditation on <s>Hari</s> and worship of <s>Sūrya</s>, is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:

children.text: punaḥ sūryārcanaṃ vakṣye yaduktaṃ dhanadāya hi
children.translated_text: Again I shall teach the worship of <s>Sūrya</s>, which was taught to <s>Dhanada</s>.
In a pure place he should draw an eight-petaled lotus with a pericarp.
Then, after forming the invocation mudrā, he should invoke <s>Ravi</s>.
Having established <s>Khakholka</s>, he should establish the mudrā in the form of a mantra.
In the southeast direction of the god he should establish the heart, O <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: aiśānyāṃ tu śiraḥ sthāpyaṃ nairṛtyāṃ vinyasecchikhām ||
children.translated_text: The head should be established in the northeast, and the topknot should be placed in the southwest.
In the eastern quarter he should place <s>Dharma</s>, with his mind fixed in concentration.

children.text: vāyavyāṃ caiva netraṃ tu vāruṇyāmastrameva ca ||
children.translated_text: In the northwest he should place the eye, and in the western quarter the missile.
In the northeast he should establish <s>Soma</s>, and in the eastern quarter <s>Lohita</s>.
In the southeast, the son of <s>Soma</s>; and in the southern quarter, <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
In the southwest, the guru of the Dānavas; and in the western quarter, <s>Śanaiścara</s>.

children.text: vāyavyāṃ ca tathā ketuṃ kauberyāṃ rāhumeva ca ||
children.translated_text: Likewise in the northwest, <s>Ketu</s>; and in the northern quarter, <s>Rāhu</s>.
In the second enclosure he should worship the twelve suns.

children.text: bhagaḥ sūryo 'ryamā caiva mitro vai varuṇastathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhaga</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Mitra</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>,

children.text: savitā caiva dhātā ca vivasvāṃśca mahābalaḥ
children.translated_text: and <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Dhātṛ</s>, and mighty <s>Vivasvant</s>,

children.text: tvaṣṭā pūṣā tathā cendro dvādaśo viṣṇurucyate ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>, <s>Pūṣan</s>, and <s>Indra</s>; <s>Viṣṇu</s> is called the twelfth.
Beginning in the east, a man should worship the gods, <s>Indra</s> and the others, with faith.

children.text: jayā ca vijayā caiva jayanti cāparājitā
children.translated_text: <s>Jayā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Jayantī</s>, and <s>Aparājitā</s>,
and <s>Śeṣa</s> and <s>Vāsuki</s>, and the Nāgas and the rest, he should worship.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sūryārcanavidhir nāma saptadaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa called the first section, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the seventeenth chapter, named the procedure for worship of <s>Sūrya</s>, is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall teach the worship of <s>Mṛtyuñjaya</s>, spoken by <s>Garuḍa</s> to <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
auspicious, preceded by the ritual extraction of syllables, and regarded as consisting of all the gods.
First one should utter the syllable oṃ, and after that the syllable juṃ.
The third should have the visarga; it crushes death and poverty.
The armor of <s>Īśa</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Arka</s>, the Goddess, and the others accomplishes everything.
The worship of <s>Amṛteśa</s>, the great three-syllabled mantra, is equivalent to it.
By recitation, people become free from death and devoid of all sin.
From a hundred recitations one obtains the fruit of the Veda, of sacrifice, and of pilgrimage.
By reciting it one hundred and eight times at the three twilights, one conquers death, the enemy.
He should meditate on <s>Amṛteśvara</s> seated on a white lotus, granting boons and making the gesture of fearlessness,
and with two hands holding a pot of nectar; thus he should contemplate <s>Amṛteśvara</s>.
He should also contemplate the goddess <s>Amṛtā</s>, abiding in his limbs and speaking nectar,
with a pot in her right hand and a lotus in her left hand.
He should recite eight thousand times at the three twilights for one month.
It grants auspicious peace from old age, death, great disease, and enemies.
Invocation, establishment, restraint, bringing near, installation,
water for the feet, sipping water, bathing, arghya, garland, and unguent,
lamp, garment, ornament, food offering, drink, and fanning,
mātrā, mudrā, recitation, meditation, donation, oblation, and praise,

children.text: vādyaṃ gatiṃ ca nṛtyaṃ ca nyāsayogaṃ pradakṣiṇam
children.translated_text: music, procession, dance, nyāsa-yoga, and circumambulation,
bowing, the mantra-bed, salutation, and dismissal,
worship is set forth in sequence by the method beginning with the six limbs.
Whoever knows what was uttered from the mouth of <s>Parameśa</s> is a true worshipper.
First comes the worship of the arghya-vessel, and then the striking with the cloth.
Purification is done with the kavaca, and after that the making into nectar.
Then there is worship beginning with the foundational power, and prāṇāyāma on the seat.
Then he should perform the purification of the pīṭha, and after the drying and the other acts he should meditate.
He should contemplate himself in the form of the deity and perform the nyāsa on the hands and limbs.
Afterward he should worship himself as a form of light arising from the lotus of the heart.

children.text: mūrtau vā sthaṇḍile vāpi kṣipetpuṣpaṃ tu bhāsvaram
children.translated_text: On an image or on a ritual ground he should place a radiant flower.
For the worship at the gate of invocation, the worship begins with the foundational power.
He should establish the presence of the deity and worship the attendant retinue.

children.text: aṅgaṣaṭkasya pūjā vai kartavyā ca vipaścitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The wise should also perform the worship of the six limbs.
<s>Dharma</s> and the others, <s>Śakra</s> and the rest, together with their weapons, are the attendants.
The yugas, the Vedas, and the muhūrtas are to be worshipped; this worship brings enjoyment and liberation.
At the beginning he should worship the <s>Mātṛkās</s>, the <s>Gaṇas</s>, <s>Nandin</s>, and <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Formerly he should worship <s>Mahākāla</s> and <s>Yamunā</s> at the threshold.
Oṃ, <s>Amṛteśvara</s>; oṃ, homage to <s>Bhairava</s>.

children.text: evaṃ oṃ juṃ haṃsaḥ sūryāya namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise: oṃ juṃ haṃsaḥ, homage to <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: evaṃ śivāya kṛṣṇāya brahmaṇe ca gaṇāya ca
children.translated_text: Likewise he should worship <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the <s>Gaṇa</s>,
and <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, and the others.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe 'mṛteśamṛtyuñjayapūjanaṃ nāmāṣṭādaśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the eighteenth chapter, named The Worship of <s>Amṛteśa Mṛtyuñjaya</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall declare the <s>Prāṇeśvara</s> and the <s>Gāruḍa</s> teaching, spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.
First I shall state the places; one bitten by a serpent in them does not live.
At a funeral pyre, an anthill, a rock, and the like, or in a hollow of a tree,

children.text: daṃśe rekhātrayaṃ yasya pracchannaṃ sa na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: if, at the bite, a person has three concealed lines, he does not live.
On the sixth lunar day, and in <s>Cancer</s> or <s>Aries</s>, or in <s>Mūla</s>, <s>Āśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, and the like,
or when bitten at the armpit, hip, throat, joint, temple, ear, belly, and so on,
a staff-bearer, a weapon-holder, a mendicant, a naked person, and others are messengers of death.

children.text: bāhau ca vaktre grīvāyāṃ daṣṭāyāṃ na hi jīvati ||
children.translated_text: If one is bitten on the arm, face, or neck, he certainly does not live.
First the lord of the day, the sun, takes possession for half a yāma, and after that the others do so.
The remaining planets, day by day, proceed through sixfold rotations.
The serpent's possession at night is to be known in order, through fivefold rotations.

children.text: śeṣo 'rkaḥ phaṇipaś candras takṣako bhauma īritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śeṣa</s> is the sun, the lord of serpents is the moon, and <s>Takṣaka</s> is declared to be Mars.

children.text: karkoṭo jño guruḥ padmo mahāpadmaśca bhārgavaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Karkoṭa</s> is Mercury, <s>Padma</s> is Jupiter, and <s>Mahāpadma</s> is Venus.
<s>Śaṅkha</s> is Saturn; <s>Rāhu</s> and <s>Kulika</s> are the serpent-planets.
By night or by day, in the portion of the preceptor of the gods, there is <s>Amarāntaka</s>.

children.text: paṅgoḥ kāle divā rāhuḥ kulikena saha sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the time of the lame one, by day, <s>Rāhu</s> stands together with <s>Kulika</s>.
He should observe the time called <s>Kālavatī</s>, situated at the junction of half-yāmas.
The numbers are reckoned by one portion as arrow, two, six, fire, horse, yuga, and earth.
By day the human portions are six, one, eye, mountain, five, and three.

children.text: pādāṅguṣṭhe pādapṛṣṭhe pādapṛṣṭhe gulphe jānuni liṅgake ||
children.translated_text: In order, on the big toe, on the top of the foot, on the top of the foot, on the ankle, on the knee, and on the liṅga,
at the navel, heart, side of the breast, throat, nostril, and eye,
and at the ears, brows, temples, and head, the moon stands from the first lunar day onward.
If the moon stands on the right side of a man's body, he lives,
and likewise for a woman when it is on the left side of the body, because of the movement of the vital air.
The nectar produced by that and the stupor would cease through rubbing.
One should give the supreme seed of the self, called haṃsa, stainless like crystal.
That poison- and sin-destroying seed is fourfold.
The first is said to be joined with bindu and the fifth vowel; the second is another form.
The third is mounted on the sixth, and the fourth has visarga.
Oṃ kuru kule svāhā.
This vidyā was formerly held by <s>Garuḍa</s> for the protection of the three worlds.
Desiring the killing of serpents and great serpents, one should then place the praṇava in the mouth.

children.text: gale kuru nyaseddhīmānkule ca gulphayoḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The wise man should place 'kuru' in the throat, and 'kule' is remembered at the ankles.

children.text: svāhā pādayuge caiva yugahā nyāsa īritaḥ ||
children.translated_text: 'Svāhā' is placed on the pair of feet; this is declared to be the nyāsa that removes the pair.

children.text: gṛhe vivikhitā yatra tannāgāḥ saṃtyajanti ca
children.translated_text: Where it is written in a house, the serpents abandon that place.

children.text: sahasramantraṃ japtvā tu karṇe sūtraṃ dhṛtaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: After reciting the mantra a thousand times, a thread worn on the ear has the same effect.

children.text: yadgṛhe śarkarā japtā kṣiptā nāgāstyajanti tat
children.translated_text: If consecrated sugar is thrown in a house, the serpents leave it.
By seven hundred thousand recitations, perfection was attained by gods and asuras.
Oṃ suvarṇarekhe kukkuṭavigraharūpiṇi svāhā.
In this way one should write the pair of syllables on the petals of an eight-petalled lotus.
A bitten person, bathed with streams of water over this name, casts off the poison.
Oṃ pakṣi svāhā.
Then, on the hand, he should place it from the thumb through to the little finger, and on the body.

children.text: ke vaktre hṛdi liṅge ca pādayorgaruḍasya hi ||
children.translated_text: On the face, heart, liṅga, and feet, it is indeed the nyāsa of <s>Garuḍa</s>.
Poisonous serpents do not cross his shadow, even in a dream.

children.text: yastu lakṣaṃ japeccāsyāḥ sa dṛṣṭvā nāśayedviṣam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever recites this a hundred thousand times destroys poison by merely seeing it.

children.text: oṃ hrī hrau hrīṃ bhiruṇḍāyai svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrī hrau hrīṃ, svāhā to <s>Bhiruṇḍā</s>.

children.text: karṇe japtā tviyaṃ vidyā daṣṭakasya viṣaṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: This vidyā, recited in the ear, removes the poison of one who has been bitten.

children.text: a ā nyasettu pādāgre i ī gulphe 'tha jānuni
children.translated_text: He should place a and ā at the tips of the feet, i and ī at the ankles and then at the knees.

children.text: u ū e ai kaṭitaṭe o nābhau hṛdi au nyaset ||
children.translated_text: He should place u, ū, e, and ai at the region of the waist, o at the navel, and au at the heart.
He should place aṃ at the mouth and aḥ at the crown of the head, each joined with haṃsa.

children.text: haṃso viṣādi ca harejjapto dhyāto 'tha pūjitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Haṃsa, when recited, meditated upon, and worshipped, removes poison and the rest.
Meditating, 'I am <s>Garuḍa</s>,' he should perform the poison-removing rite.
The haṃ-mantra, placed upon the limbs, is declared to remove poison and the like.
Having placed haṃsa on the left hand, he should perform the blocking of the nose and mouth.
The mantra removes the poison of the bitten person that has entered the skin, flesh, and the other tissues.

children.text: sa vāyunā samākṛṣya daṣṭānāṃ garalaṃ haret
children.translated_text: Having drawn out the poison of those who have been bitten by means of breath, he should remove it.
He should apply it to the body of the bitten person and call to mind <s>Nīlakaṇṭha</s> and the others.
The root of <s>Pratyaṅgirā</s>, drunk with grains of rice, removes poison.
So too are the roots of <s>Punarnavā</s> and <s>Phalinī</s>, and this root called vakkraja.
The root of white <s>Bṛhatī</s>, together with <s>Karkoṭī</s> and gairikarṇikā,
rubbed with water and mixed with ghee, is this paste that crushes poison.

children.text: viṣamṛddhiṃ na vrajecca uṣṇaṃ pibati yo ghṛtam
children.translated_text: Poison does not increase for one who drinks warm ghee.

children.text: pañcāṅgaṃ tu śirīṣasya mūlaṃ gṛñjanajaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: The five parts of <s>Śirīṣa</s>, and also the root produced from gṛñjana,
by being smeared over the whole body, or by being drunk, becomes a remover of poison.
Hrīṃ: it removes poisons such as that of the goṇasa snake.
Meditated upon as extending from the heart to the forehead and ending in the visarga, it brings subjugation and the like.
Placed in the vulva, it brings a maiden under control and makes her wet with the fluid of passion.
After reciting it seven or eight thousand times, one becomes all-ranging like <s>Garutmān</s>.
He becomes a poet, one who retains what he has heard, gains women under control, and obtains long life.
It becomes poison-removing; likewise the account, the jewel, and <s>Vyāsa</s> are certainly remembered.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sarpaviṣaharopāyanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikonaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the nineteenth chapter, called 'Description of the Means for Removing Snake Poison,' in the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain that supreme secret, the group of mantras spoken by <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: pāśaṃ dhanuśca cakraṃ ca mudraraṃ śūlapaṭṭiśam ||
children.translated_text: The noose, bow, discus, club, trident, and paṭṭiśa spear:
with these very weapons and mantras a king should conquer enemies in battle.
For the extraction of the mantra, he should write on a lotus petal, beginning with the first and so on.
The eight groups and the eighth are known on the <s>Īśāna</s> petal.
Oṃ is the seed of <s>Brahmā</s>, and hrīṃ is indeed <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: hrīṅkāraśca śivaḥ śūle triśākhe tu kramānnyaset
children.translated_text: Hrīṃ is also <s>Śiva</s>; on the three-branched trident he should place them in order.
Oṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ.
Taking the trident in his hand, he should whirl it while facing the sky.
By the sight of it, hostile serpents perish when they see it.

children.text: dhūmārakte karaṃ madhye dhyātvā khe cintayennaraḥ
children.translated_text: Meditating on the smoky-red hand in the middle, a man should contemplate it in the sky.

children.text: duṣṭā nāgā grahā meghā vinaśyanti ca rākṣasāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Evil serpents, grahas, clouds, and rākṣasas are destroyed.
The mantra protects the three worlds; what need is there to speak of the mortal world?
Oṃ jūṃ sūṃ hūṃ phaṭ.
He should consecrate eight pegs of khadira wood and set them in the field.
There is no danger there from a lightning strike, thunderclap, or the like.
With the great mantras taught by <s>Garuḍa</s>, he should consecrate eight pegs.
He should bury them in the field at night twenty-one times.
Then there is the destruction of troubles such as lightning, mice, and thunderbolts.
The syllable-series ha-ra-kṣa-ma-la-va-ra-yū, furnished with a bindu, is <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
With the index finger he should place the piṇḍa, bright like a pomegranate blossom.
At the mere sight of it, evil clouds, lightning, flames, and the like,
rākṣasas, bhūtas, and ḍākinīs flee in the ten directions.
Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
Homage to the wheel of stambhana and the other rites.
Oṃ aiṃ, homage to the corrupted formula brahayaintrai lokyaḍāmarāya.
The <s>Bhairava</s> piṇḍa has been described as removing poison, sin, and grahas.
It protects the field and crushes bhūtas, rākṣasas, and the like.
Oṃ, homage.
Meditating on <s>Indra</s>'s thunderbolt in the hand wards off evil clouds and the like.
Poison, enemy hosts, and bhūtas are destroyed by the thunderbolt mudrā.
Oṃ kṣuṃ, homage.
He should visualize a noose in the left hand; poison, bhūtas, and the like are destroyed.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage.
By its utterance, the mantra removes poison, clouds, grahas, and the like.

children.text: dhyātvā kṛtāntaṃ ca dahecchedakāstreṇa vai jagat
children.translated_text: Meditating on <s>Kṛtānta</s>, he should burn the world with the cutting weapon.
Oṃ kṣṇaṃ, homage.
Having meditated on <s>Bhairava</s>, he should perform a rite that removes grahas, bhūtas, and poison.
Oṃ lasaddijihvākṣa svāhā.
In fields and similar places it prevents grahas, bhūtas, poison, and harmful birds.
Oṃ kṣva, homage.
When it is written in blood on a drum, grahas and the like tremble at the sound.

children.text: oṃ mara mara māraya māraya svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, kill, kill; slay, slay; svāhā.
Oṃ huṃ phaṭ svāhā.
After consecrating the trident with eight hundred recitations, by whirling it one removes the host of enemies.
By the descent of the upward power, he should contract the downward power.
The mantras are filled by inhalation and well consecrated by breath-retention.
Nourished also by the praṇava, those mantras, when uttered,
being thus nourished, grant results like servants.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣādiharamantravṛndanirūpaṇaṃ nāma viṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twentieth chapter, called 'Description of the Group of Mantras that Remove Poison and the Like,' in the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain separately the worship of the five-faced one, which grants enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: oṃ bhūrviṣṇave ādibhūtāya sarvādhārāya mūrtaye svāhā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ, bhūḥ, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the primordial being, the form that supports all, svāhā.
With this he should first perform the invocation of <s>Sadyojāta</s>.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ sadyojātāyaiva kalā hyaṣṭau prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ, to <s>Sadyojāta</s>; his eight kalās are proclaimed.
They are Siddhi, Ṛddhi, Dhṛti, Lakṣmī, Medhā, Kānti, Svadhā, and Sthiti.
Oṃ hīṃ, to <s>Vāmadeva</s>; his kalās are thirteen.

children.text: rajā rakṣā ratiḥ pālyā kāntis tṛṣṇā matiḥ kriyā
children.translated_text: Rajā, Rakṣā, Rati, Pālyā, Kānti, Tṛṣṇā, Mati, and Kriyā,

children.text: kāmā buddhiśca rātriśca trāsanī mohinī tathā ||
children.translated_text: Kāmā, Buddhi, Rātri, Trāsanī, and Mohinī as well.

children.text: manonmanī aghorā ca tathā mohā kṣudhā kalāḥ
children.translated_text: Manonmanī and Aghorā, and likewise Mohā and Kṣudhā are kalās.

children.text: nidrā mṛtyuśca māyā ca aṣṭasaṃkhyā bhayaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: Nidrā, Mṛtyu, and Māyā make eight in number, terrifying ones.

children.text: oṃ haiṃ tatpuruṣāyaiva nivṛttiśca pratiṣṭhā ca vidyā śāntirna kevalā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ haiṃ, to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; there are Nivṛtti, Pratiṣṭhā, Vidyā, Śānti, and Kevalā.

children.text: oṃ hauṃ īśānāya namo niścalā ca nirañjanā
children.translated_text: Oṃ hauṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>; there are Niścalā and Nirañjanā,
and also Śaśinī, Aṅganā, Marīci, and Jvālinī.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍaṃ pañcavaktrapūjanaṃ nāmaikaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa called the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, the twenty-first chapter, named the worship of <s>Pañcavaktra</s>, is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, the supreme rite that grants enjoyment and liberation.
He is peaceful, all-pervading, void, and established in the set of twelve mātrās.
The five faces are the short syllables, the limbs are the long syllables, together with the bindu.

children.text: savisargaṃ vadedastraṃ śiva ūrdhvaṃ tathā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With the visarga one should utter the astra-mantra; then again <s>Śiva</s> is placed above.
With the sixth below, the great mantra, namely hauṃ, grants every aim.
With both hands he should touch the feet, moving upward from the feet to the head.
For this is the great mudrā of all; he should perform the nyāsa of the hands and limbs.
With the flat palm he should purify the back by means of the astra-mantra.
Beginning with the little finger, he should assign the limbs up to the index finger.
I shall explain the worship in the pericarp, in the heart-lotus.
With the heart-mantra he should worship <s>Dharma</s>, knowledge, dispassion, sovereignty, and the rest.
With the heart-mantra he should offer invocation, establishment, water for the feet, and arghya.
He should offer water for sipping, bathing, and worship, in a manner equal to a single support.
I shall explain the procedure for the fire rite: he should make the marking with the astra-mantra.
Sprinkling should be performed with the armor-mantra, and the placing of the śakti should be done with the heart-mantra.
In the heart, or in the hollow of the śakti, he should cast <s>Jātavedas</s>, the fire.
Having performed the rites beginning with garbhādhāna, and then the final expiation for the caru offering,

children.text: hṛdā kṛtvā sarvakarma śivaṃ sāṅgaṃ tu homayet ||
children.translated_text: having performed every rite with the heart-mantra, he should offer <s>Śiva</s> together with his limbs into the fire.
He should worship <s>Śambhu</s> in the maṇḍala, in the womb of the lotus, marked with the syllable ga.
The maṇḍala begins with eight and extends to sixty-four, with the kha-syllable and eye, and with the kha-class and the rest.
It proceeds with kha, the eye, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Sūrya</s>, and with all the kha-series, the Vedas, and the moon.
In the southeast he should make a fine fire-pit shaped like a half-moon.
The group beginning with the heart is said to be established according to the fire-ritual teaching.
The astra is assigned to the direction of the good lotus; <s>Sadāśiva</s> is in the pericarp.

children.text: dīkṣāṃ vakṣye pañcatattve sthitāṃ bhūmyādikāṃ pare
children.translated_text: I shall explain initiation, established in the five tattvas, beginning with earth, O supreme one.
<s>Nivṛtti</s> is connected with earth and <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>; <s>Vidyā</s> is fire, and <s>Śānti</s> is one's own principle.
<s>Śāntyatīta</s> is ether; that is supreme, peaceful, and undecaying.

children.text: ekaikasya śataṃ homā hatyevaṃ pañca homayet ||
children.translated_text: For each of these he should offer a hundred oblations; thus he should make the fivefold oblation.
After giving the final oblation, he should remember <s>Śiva</s> for appeasement.
For purification through expiation, he should offer eight oblations for each, in order.
He should make the oblation with the astra seed-syllable; thus he should complete the initiation.
Except in the context of worship, this highest consecration is to be kept secret.
For one whose consecration has been purified in this way, <s>Śivahood</s> surely arises.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śivārcanaprakāro nāma dvāviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa called the first section, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the twenty-second chapter, named the procedure for worship of <s>Śiva</s>, is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain the worship of <s>Śiva</s>, which accomplishes <s>dharma</s>, desire, and the other aims.
He should sip water with three mantras ending in svāhā and beginning with the praṇava.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ ātmatattvāya vidyātattvāya hīṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ, to the principle of self; to the principle of knowledge, hīṃ likewise.

children.text: oṃ hūṃ śivatattvāya svāhā hṛdā syācchrotravandanam ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hūṃ, to the principle of <s>Śiva</s>, svāhā; with the heart-mantra there should be reverence to the ears.

children.text: bhasmasnānaṃ tarpaṇaṃ ca oṃ hāṃ svāhā sarvamantrakāḥ
children.translated_text: The bath with ashes and the tarpaṇa are performed with oṃ hāṃ svāhā; all mantras are used.
All gods and all sages are addressed with formulas ending in namaḥ and ending in vauṣaṭ.
All the ancestors are addressed with formulas ending in svadhā, and the grandfathers also with formulas ending in svadhā.
Oṃ hāṃ, to the great-grandfathers; likewise to the maternal grandfathers and the others.
Hāṃ, homage to all the mothers; after that there should be restraint of the breath.

children.text: ācāmaṃ mārjanaṃ cātho gāyatrīṃ ca japettataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he should perform sipping and sprinkling, and after that recite the Gāyatrī.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ tanmaheśāya vidmahe vāgviśuddhāya dhīmahi tanno rudraḥ pracodayāt ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ, may we know that <s>Maheśa</s>; may we meditate on the one whose speech is purified; may that <s>Rudra</s> impel us.
Having performed the attendance upon the sun, he should worship with the solar mantras.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ śivasūryāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ haḥ, homage to <s>Śivasūrya</s>.
Oṃ haṃ, homage to <s>Khakholka</s>, the solar form.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sūryāya namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, homage to <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: daṇḍine piṅgale tvātibhūtāni ca tataḥ smaret
children.translated_text: Then he should remember <s>Daṇḍin</s>, <s>Piṅgala</s>, and the beings beyond the elements.
Beginning in the southeast, having worshipped <s>Vimaleśāna</s>, he obtains supreme happiness.

children.text: yajetpadmāṃ ca rāṃ dīptāṃ rīṃ sūkṣmāṃ rūṃ jayāṃ ca reṃ
children.translated_text: He should worship <s>Padmā</s> with rāṃ, <s>Dīptā</s> with rīṃ, <s>Sūkṣmā</s> with rūṃ, and <s>Jayā</s> with reṃ,

children.text: bhadrāṃ ca raiṃ vibhūtiṃ roṃ vimalāṃ raum amoghikām ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhadrā</s> with raiṃ, <s>Vibhūti</s> with roṃ, <s>Vimalā</s> with raum, and <s>Amoghikā</s> with raṃ.

children.text: raṃ vidyutāṃ ca pūrvādau rā madhye sarvatomukhīm
children.translated_text: He should worship <s>Vidyutā</s> in the east and the other directions, and <s>Sarvatomukhī</s> with rā in the middle.

children.text: arkāsanaṃ sūryamūrteṃ hrāṃ hrūṃ saḥ sūryamarcayet ||
children.translated_text: He should worship the seat of <s>Arka</s>, the form of <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Sūrya</s> himself with hrāṃ hrūṃ saḥ.

children.text: oṃ āṃ hṛdarkāya ca śiraḥ śikhā ca bhūrbhuvaḥ svarom
children.translated_text: Oṃ āṃ, for the heart-sun; then the head and topknot, with bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ oṃ.

children.text: jvālinīṃ hraṃ kavacasya cāstraṃ rājñāṃ ca dīkṣitām ||
children.translated_text: He should assign <s>Jvālinī</s>, hraṃ for the armor and the astra, and the consecrated royal powers.

children.text: yajetsūryahṛdā sarvān soṃ somaṃ maṃ ca maṅgalam
children.translated_text: With the solar heart-mantra he should worship all of them: soṃ for <s>Soma</s>, maṃ for <s>Maṅgala</s>,

children.text: baṃ budhaṃ bṛṃ bṛhaspatiṃ bhaṃ bhārgavaṃ śaṃ śanaiścaram ||
children.translated_text: baṃ for <s>Budha</s>, bṛṃ for <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, bhaṃ for <s>Bhārgava</s>, and śaṃ for <s>Śanaiścara</s>.

children.text: raṃ rāhuṃ kaṃ yajetketuṃ oṃ tejaścaṇḍamarcayet
children.translated_text: He should worship <s>Rāhu</s> with raṃ, <s>Ketu</s> with kaṃ, and <s>Tejaścaṇḍa</s> with oṃ.
Having worshipped <s>Sūrya</s> and sipped water, he should place the limb-mantras beginning with the little finger.

children.text: hāṃ hṛcchiro hūṃ śikhā haiṃ varma hauṃ caiva netrakam
children.translated_text: Hāṃ is for the heart and head, hūṃ for the topknot, haiṃ for the armor, and hauṃ for the eye.
Hoṃ is the astra; after establishing the śakti, he should again perform purification of the elements and nyāsa.
Then, having prepared the arghya vessel, he should sprinkle with its waters and worship.

children.text: ātmānaṃ padmasaṃsthaṃ ca hauṃ śivāya tato bahiḥ
children.translated_text: He should worship himself as seated in a lotus; then outside he should use hauṃ, homage to <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: dvāre nandimahākālau gaṅgā ca yamunātha gauḥ ||
children.translated_text: At the doorway he should worship <s>Nandin</s> and <s>Mahākāla</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, and the cow.

children.text: śrīrastraṃ vāstvadhipatiṃ brahmāṇaṃ ca gaṇaṃ gurum
children.translated_text: He should worship <s>Śrī</s>, the astra, the lord of the site, <s>Brahmā</s>, the gaṇa, and the guru.
In the middle he should worship <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Ananta</s>; beginning in the east, <s>Dharma</s> and the rest.

children.text: adharmādyaṃ ca vahnyādau madhye padmasya karṇike
children.translated_text: Beginning in the southeast he should worship <s>Adharma</s> and the others, in the middle, in the lotus pericarp.

children.text: vāmā jyeṣṭhā ca pūrvādau raudrī kālī ca pūrṣadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmā</s> and <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, beginning in the east, and <s>Raudrī</s> and <s>Kālī</s>, the attendants,
Oṃ hauṃ: to <s>Kalavikariṇī</s>; then to <s>Balavikariṇī</s>;
then to <s>Balapramathinī</s>, and then to <s>Damanī</s>, subduer of all beings.
One should worship <s>Manonmanī</s> and these goddesses in the middle of the path, before <s>Śiva</s>.
One should worship the seat of <s>Śiva</s>, the great form, and <s>Śiva</s> within the image.
Invocation, installation, bringing near, and restraint,
the rite of making whole, the showing of mudrās (ritual gestures), and arghya and pādya offerings,
sipping-water, anointing, rubbing with fragrant powder, bathing, and churning should be performed.

children.text: vastraṃ vilepanaṃ puṣpaṃ dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ caruṃ dadet ||
children.translated_text: One should give garments, unguent, flowers, incense, lamp, and caru (food offering).
Sipping-water, mouth-fragrance, betel, and cleansing of the hands,
parasol, chowrie, purifier, and the rite of making supreme should be performed.
There should also be the one-day recitation according to form and the dedication of what has been recited.
Praise, bowing, and worship of the name and limbs, beginning with the heart, are to be understood.
In the fiery, lordly, rākṣasa, and vāyu quarters, and in the middle, the procedure begins with the east.
He should worship <s>Indra</s> and the others, and <s>Caṇḍa</s>, and should offer the used worship-material to him.
You are the protector of the cave, of the very secret place; accept the japa performed by us.
May accomplishment be mine, O god; through that grace, may there be steadfastness in you.

children.text: yat kiṃcit kriyate karma sadā sukṛtaduṣkṛtam
children.translated_text: Whatever action is done, whether always meritorious or sinful,
that, for me who stand at the feet of <s>Śiva</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, destroy.

children.text: śivo dātā śivo bhoktā śivaḥ sarvamidaṃ jagat
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> is the giver, <s>Śiva</s> is the enjoyer, <s>Śiva</s> is this whole universe.
