children.text: śivo jayati sarvatra yaḥ śivaḥ so 'hameva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śiva</s> triumphs everywhere; whatever is <s>Śiva</s>, that indeed am I.
Whatever I have done and whatever I shall do, all that merit is yours.

children.text: tvaṃ trātā viśvanetā ca nānyo nātho 'sti me śiva ||
children.translated_text: You are the protector and guide of the universe; there is no other lord for me, O <s>Śiva</s>.
Now I shall describe worship of <s>Śiva</s> in another manner.
The gaṇa, <s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Nandī</s>, <s>Mahākāla</s>, and then <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
the wind-missile and the lord of the dwelling should be placed at the door; beginning in the east are these.
<s>Indra</s> and the others should be worshipped, as well as the tattvas (principles): earth and water,

children.text: tejo vāyurvyoma gandho rasarūpe ca śabdakaḥ
children.translated_text: fire, wind, ether, smell, taste, form, and sound,

children.text: sparśo vāk pāṇipādaṃ ca pāyūpasthaṃ śrutitvacam ||
children.translated_text: touch, speech, hand, foot, anus, generative organ, hearing, and skin,
eye, tongue, nose, mind, intellect, ego, and prakṛti (primordial nature),
puruṣa (person), rāga (attachment), buddhi and vidyā, kalā, time, and destiny,

children.text: māyā ca śuddhavidyā ca īśvaraśca sadāśivaḥ
children.translated_text: māyā, pure knowledge, <s>Īśvara</s>, <s>Sadāśiva</s>,

children.text: śaktiḥ śivaśca tāñjñātvā mukto jñānī śivo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śakti</s> and <s>Śiva</s>; knowing these, the liberated knower becomes <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: yaḥ śivaḥ sa harirbrahmā so 'haṃ brahmāsmi śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: He who is <s>Śiva</s> is <s>Hari</s> and <s>Brahmā</s>; I am he, I am brahman, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: bhūtaśuddhiṃ pravakṣyāmi yayā śuddhaḥ śivo bhavet
children.translated_text: I shall teach bhūtaśuddhi (purification of the elements), by which, being purified, one becomes <s>Śiva</s>.
In the heart-lotus is the <s>Sadya</s> mantra, and there are <s>Nivṛtti</s> as kalā and <s>Iḍā</s>.

children.text: piṅgalā dve ca nāḍyau tu prāṇo 'pānaśca mārutau
children.translated_text: <s>Piṅgalā</s> is the second nāḍī (channel), and the winds are prāṇa and apāna.
<s>Indra</s>, the body, the cause <s>Brahmā</s>, and a square maṇḍala are to be contemplated.
One should contemplate the wind marked by the mouth, with one upward impulse, its qualities, and the arrows.
It has a sound resembling the heart-place and extends for a hundred crores.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ pratiṣṭhāyai hrūṃ hraḥ phaṭ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ, to <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>; hrūṃ hraḥ phaṭ.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ vidyāyai hraṃ hraḥ phaṭ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ hrūṃ, to <s>Vidyā</s>; hraṃ hraḥ phaṭ.
The earth-procedure has an elevation of eighty-four crores.

children.text: tanmadhye bhavavṛkṣaṃ ca ātmānaṃ ca vicintayet
children.translated_text: In its middle one should contemplate the tree of becoming and oneself.
Then one should contemplate the earth facing downward; each becomes purified, certainly.

children.text: vāmā devī pratiṣṭhā ca suṣumnā dhārikā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vāmā</s>, the goddess <s>Pratiṣṭhā</s>, <s>Suṣumṇā</s>, and likewise <s>Dhārikā</s>,
<s>Samāna</s>, <s>Udāna</s>, and <s>Varuṇa</s>, the deity, with <s>Viṣṇu</s> as cause,

children.text: addhātāśca guṇā vedāḥ śvetaṃ dhyānaṃ tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: the stated elements, the qualities, the Vedas, and the white meditation likewise,
in this way one should form the throat-lotus and the maṇḍala called the half-moon.
One should remember it marked with a lotus and extending twenty-two crores.
It has an elevation of ninety-four crores, and one should contemplate oneself facing downward.

children.text: tālusthānaṃ ca padmaṃ ca aghoro vidyayānvitaḥ
children.translated_text: The palate-place and the lotus are joined with the <s>Aghora</s> vidyā.
At the navel and lips, the elephant-tongued meditation, <s>Nāga</s>, and the fire deity are contemplated.
Its cause is <s>Rudra</s>; it has three impulses, three qualities, and a red color.
One should contemplate a triangle in the form of flame, measuring four hundred crores,
in breadth and elevation, as the <s>Rudra</s>-tattva (principle).

children.text: lalāṭe vai tatpuruṣaḥ śāntiryaḥ śādvalaṃ budhāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the forehead is <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>; <s>Śānti</s>, grass-green in color, is known by the wise.
<s>Kūrma</s> and <s>Kṛkara</s> are the winds, and the deity is <s>Īśvara</s> as cause.
It has two impulses and two qualities, and it is a smoky six-cornered maṇḍala.
It is marked with a bindu, extends eight crores, and has an elevation likewise.
One should contemplate the vāyu-tattva (wind principle), fourteen crores and more in measure.
In the twelve-petaled lotus are <s>Śāntyatītā</s> and the <s>Īśvaras</s>.
<s>Kuhū</s> and <s>Śaṅkhinī</s> are the nāḍīs, and <s>Devadatta</s> and <s>Dhanañjaya</s> are the winds.
The topknot and <s>Īśāna</s> are the cause; this is remembered as <s>Sadāśiva</s>.
It has one quality and one upward impulse; one should remember it as like pure crystal.
It extends sixteen crores and has an elevation of twenty-five crores.
One should contemplate ether as circular; this is called bhūtaśuddhi.
The guru of the qualities, the teacher of enjoyment, the two powers, <s>Ananta</s>, and dharma are to be contemplated.
Then, with knowledge, dispassion, and lordship, on the petals beginning in the east,
with two faces below and above, one should contemplate the lotus pericarp and filaments.
One should always meditate on the principle called <s>Śiva</s>, together with <s>Vāmā</s> and the others and with <s>Ātmavidyā</s>.

children.text: tattvaṃ śivāsane mūrtirhe hauṃ vidyādehāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: The tattva, the image on <s>Śiva</s>'s seat, is worshipped with: he hauṃ, homage to the body of vidyā.
Seated in bound lotus posture, white, sixteen years old,
five-faced, the Lord holds with the tips of his ten hands
fearlessness, grace, a spear, a trident, and a khaṭvāṅga in his right hands,
and, with his right and left hands, a serpent and a rosary.
a ḍamaru drum, a blue lotus, and an excellent citron.
For <s>Sadāśiva</s> is three-eyed and possesses the powers of will, knowledge, and action.
Thus one who meditates in the worship of <s>Śiva</s> is always free from the power of time and death.
Here, by the course of one day and night, he lives for three years.
By the course of two days a man lives for two years.
By the course of three days he lives for one year.

children.text: nākāle śītale mṛtyuruṣṇe caiva tu kārake ||
children.translated_text: Death does not come untimely when it is cold, nor when heat is the operative cause.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śivārcananirūpaṇaṃ nāma trayoviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-third chapter, called 'Description of the Worship of Śiva,' in the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: vakṣye gaṇādikāḥ pūjāḥ sarvadā svargadāḥ parāḥ
children.translated_text: I shall explain the worships beginning with <s>Gaṇa</s>, supreme rites that always bestow heaven.
One should worship the seat of <s>Gaṇa</s>, the image of <s>Gaṇa</s>, and <s>Gaṇādhipati</s>.
One should worship the heart and other limbs beginning with the syllable gām, the pādukās of <s>Durgā</s>, and the guru's pādukās.

children.text: durgāsanaṃ ca tanmūrtiṃ hrīṃ durge rakṣaṇīti ca ||
children.translated_text: One should worship the seat of <s>Durgā</s> and her image, and the formula, 'hrīṃ, O <s>Durgā</s>, protect.'
After the heart and the other limbs come the nine powers: <s>Rudracaṇḍā</s>, together with <s>Pracaṇḍā</s>,
<s>Caṇḍogrā</s>, <s>Caṇḍanāyikā</s>, <s>Caṇḍā</s>, and <s>Caṇḍavatī</s>, in order.
<s>Caṇārūpā</s> and the one called <s>Caṇḍikā</s>; then the formula, 'O <s>Durgā</s>, O <s>Durgā</s>, O Protectress.'
There are the mudrās of the thunderbolt, sword, and the like, beginning with <s>Śiva</s>, from the fiery quarter.
Alternatively, there is the lotus-seat of <s>Sadāśiva</s>, the great corpse.
Aiṃ klīṃ sauḥ, homage to <s>Tripurā</s>.

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ kṣeṃ kṣaiṃ strīṃ skīṃ roṃ spheṃ sphīṃ śāṃ padmāsanaṃ ca mūrtiṃ ca tripurāhṛdayādikam ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ kṣeṃ kṣaiṃ strīṃ skīṃ roṃ spheṃ sphīṃ śāṃ; one should worship the lotus-seat, the image, and the heart and other rites of <s>Tripurā</s>.

children.text: pīṭhāmbuje tu brāhayādīr brahmāṇī ca maheśvarī
children.translated_text: In the lotus of the pīṭha, one should worship the goddesses beginning with <s>Brahmāṇī</s>: <s>Brahmāṇī</s> and <s>Maheśvarī</s>,
<s>Kaumārī</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, <s>Vārāhī</s>, and the goddess of <s>Indra</s>.
<s>Cāmuṇḍā</s> and <s>Caṇḍikā</s> are to be worshipped; after that one should worship those called <s>Bhairavas</s>.
<s>Asitāṅga</s>, <s>Ruru</s>, <s>Caṇḍa</s>, <s>Krodha</s>, and <s>Unmattabhairava</s>,
<s>Kapālī</s>, <s>Bhīṣaṇa</s>, and <s>Saṃhāra</s>: these are the eight <s>Bhairavas</s>.

children.text: ratiḥ prītiḥ kāmadevaḥ pañca bāṇāśca yoginī ||
children.translated_text: There are <s>Rati</s>, <s>Prīti</s>, <s>Kāmadeva</s>, the five arrows, and the <s>Yoginī</s>.
One should contemplate <s>Vaṭuka</s> with <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Vighnarāja</s>, the guru, and <s>Kṣetrapa</s>,
in the lotus womb, in the maṇḍala, and in the triangle, within the heart.
She is white and furnished with the boon-granting gesture, rosary, book, and gesture of fearlessness.
Through one hundred thousand recitations and through oblation, <s>Tripurā</s> becomes the giver of siddhi.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe tripurādipūjānirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fourth chapter, called 'Description of the Worship of Tripurā and the Others,' in the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: aiṃ krīṃ śrīṃ spheṃ kṣaiṃ anantaśaktipādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Aiṃ krīṃ śrīṃ spheṃ kṣaiṃ: I worship the pādukā of <s>Anantaśakti</s>; homage.

children.text: aiṃ śrīṃ phraiṃ kṣaiṃ ādhāraśaktipādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ
children.translated_text: Aiṃ śrīṃ phraiṃ kṣaiṃ: I worship the pādukā of <s>Ādhāraśakti</s>; homage.
Oṃ hraṃ: I worship the pādukā of <s>Kālāgnirudra</s>; homage.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ huṃ hāṭakeśvaradevapādukāṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ huṃ: I worship the pādukā of the god <s>Hāṭakeśvara</s>; homage.
Oṃ hrīṃ: I worship the pādukā of <s>Śeṣabhaṭṭāraka</s>; homage.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ pūthivītatsavarṇabhuvanadvīpasamudradiśām anantākhyam āsanaṃ padmāsanaṃ pūjayāmi namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ: I worship the seat called <s>Ananta</s>, the lotus-seat, of the earth, the worlds of the same color, the islands, oceans, and directions; homage.
Hrīṃ śrīṃ: the earth and other tattvas with the kalās beginning with <s>Nivṛtti</s>, the worlds beginning with <s>Ananta</s>, and the letters beginning with oṃ,
the ninefold word beginning with ha, the mantra beginning with <s>Sadyojāta</s>, and the limbs beginning with the heart, hrāṃ:

children.text: evaṃ mantramaheśvarasiddhavidyātmakaḥ parāmṛtārṇavaḥ sarvabhūto diksamastaṣaḍaṅgaḥ sadāśivārṇavapayaḥpūrṇodadhipakṣaśrīmān āspadātmakaḥ vidyomāpūrṇajñatvakartṛtvalakṣaṇajyeṣṭhācakrarudraśaktyātmakakarṇikaḥ
children.translated_text: thus it has the nature of <s>Mantramaheśvara</s> and <s>Siddhavidyā</s>, is an ocean of supreme nectar, consists of all beings, all directions, and all six limbs, is glorious as a seat whose sides are an ocean filled with the waters of the <s>Sadāśiva</s> ocean, and has as its pericarp the <s>Rudraśakti</s> of the <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> wheel, characterized by full knowledge and agency with <s>Vidyā</s> and <s>Umā</s>.
I worship the lotus-seat pādukā that has arisen from the three root maṇḍalas and their inner constituents, together with the nine powers and <s>Śiva</s> and the others; homage.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe āsanapūjānirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-fifth chapter, called 'Description of the Worship of the Seat,' in the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Next comes the hand nyāsa.
The purification that produces the vidyā is to be performed.
Having bound the lotus mudrā, one should perform mantra nyāsa.
Kaiṃ, homage to the little finger.
Naiṃ, homage to the ring finger.
Maiṃ, homage to the middle finger.
Taiṃ, homage to the index finger.
Aṃ, homage to the thumb.
Lāṃ, homage to the palm.
Vāṃ, homage to the back of the hand.
Now the body nyāsa.
Smaṃ smaṃ, homage to the wrist.
Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the striking of the hands.
Having the form of great radiance, one should strike the hands with huṃ, with the huṃ utterance.

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ sphaiṃ namo bhagavate sphaiṃ kubjīkāyai namaḥ
children.translated_text: Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ sphaiṃ, homage to the Blessed One; sphaiṃ, homage to <s>Kubjikā</s>.

children.text: hraṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ ṅa ña ṇa name aghorāmukhi hrāṃ hrīṃ kilikili vicce sthaulyakrośī hrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ namo bhagavate ūrdhvavaktrāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Hraṃ hrīṃ hrauṃ ṅa ña ṇa name, O <s>Aghorāmukhī</s>; hrāṃ hrīṃ kilikili vicce, O <s>Sthaulyakrośī</s>; hrīṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ aiṃ, homage to the Blessed One, homage to the upward-facing one.
Sphaiṃ, homage to <s>Kubjikā</s> as the eastern face.

children.text: hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ ṅa ā ña ṇa name dakṣiṇavaktrāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Hrīṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ ṅa ā ña ṇa name, homage to the southern face.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kilikili paścimavaktrāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ kilikili, homage to the western face.
Oṃ akhoramukhi, homage to the northern face.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavate hṛdayāya namaḥ kṣaiṃ kubjikāyai śirase svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the Blessed One; homage to the heart. Kṣaiṃ, svāhā to <s>Kubjikā</s> for the head.

children.text: hrīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ āṃ ṅa ña ṇa name śikhāyai vaṣaṭ
children.translated_text: Hrīṃ krīṃ hrīṃ āṃ ṅa ña ṇa name, vaṣaṭ to the topknot.
<s>Aghorāmukhī</s>, huṃ to the armor.
Haiṃ haiṃ īṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Kilikili vicce, phaṭ to the weapon.

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ akhaṇḍamaṇḍalākāramahāśūlamaṇḍalamāya namaḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ vāyumaṇḍalāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the great trident maṇḍala, shaped like an unbroken circle; aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the wind maṇḍala.
Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the moon maṇḍala.

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ mahākulabodhāvalimaṇḍalāya namaḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ mahākaulamaṇḍalāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the maṇḍala of the great lineage of awakening; aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the great Kaula maṇḍala.

children.text: aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ gurumaṇḍalāya namaḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ sāmamaṇḍalāya namaḥ aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ samagrasiddhayoginīpīṭhāpapīṭhakṣetrepakṣetramahāsaṃtānamaṇḍalāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the guru-maṇḍala; aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the sāma-maṇḍala; aiṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ, homage to the great lineage-maṇḍala comprising all seats, subsidiary seats, fields, and subsidiary fields of perfected yoginīs.
Thus the set of twelve maṇḍalas should be worshiped in order.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe ācārakāṇḍe karanyāsādinirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaḍviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-sixth chapter, called 'Description of Kara-nyāsa and the Like,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: oṃ kaṇicikīṇikakrāṇī carvāṇī bhūtahāriṇi phaṇiviṣiṇi virathanārāyayaṇi ume daha daha haste caṇḍe raudre māheśvari mahāmukhi jvālāmukhi śaṅkukarṇi śukamuṇḍe śatruṃ hana hana sarvanāśini svedaya sarvāṅgaśoṇitaṃ tannirīkṣāsi manasā devi saṃmohaya saṃmohaya rudrasya hṛdaye jātā rudrasya hṛdaye sthitā
children.translated_text: Oṃ kaṇicikīṇikakrāṇī, carvāṇī, remover of beings, phaṇiviṣiṇi, virathanārāyayaṇi, <s>Umā</s>, burn, burn; in the hand, fierce one, terrible one, <s>Māheśvarī</s>, great-mouthed one, flame-mouthed one, conch-eared one, parrot-headed one, strike the enemy, strike; destroyer of all, make the blood of every limb sweat forth. Observing that with the mind, O goddess, bewilder, bewilder; born in <s>Rudra</s>'s heart, abiding in <s>Rudra</s>'s heart,

children.text: rudro raudreṇa rūpeṇa tvaṃ devi rakṣa rakṣa māṃ hrūṃ māṃ hrūṃ pha pha pha ṭhaṭhaḥ skandamekhalābālagrahaśatruviṣahārī oṃ śāle māle hara hara viṣoṅkārarahiviṣavege hāṃ hāṃ śavari huṃ śavari ā kaulavegeśe sarve viñcameghamāle sarvanāgādiviṣaharaṇam ||
children.translated_text: O goddess, as <s>Rudra</s> in his terrible form, protect, protect me. Hrūṃ, me; hrūṃ, pha pha pha ṭhaṭhaḥ. Remover of <s>Skanda</s>, girdles, child-seizing demons, enemies, and poison. Oṃ śāle māle, remove, remove the poison; at the speed of poison with the sound viṣoṃkāra. Hāṃ hāṃ, Śavarī; huṃ, Śavarī; ā, mistress of Kaula-speed, in every cloud-garland of poison: removal of every poison from serpents and the like.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe nāgādivividhaviṣaharamantranirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptaviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-seventh chapter, called 'Description of Mantras that Remove Various Poisons from Serpents and the Like,' in the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain the worship of <s>Gopāla</s>, which grants enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: dvāre dhātā vidhātā ca gaṅgāyamunayā saha ||
children.translated_text: At the doorway are <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, together with <s>Gaṅgā</s> and <s>Yamunā</s>.
And the treasures <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s>, <s>Sāraṅga</s> and <s>Śarabha</s>, together with <s>Śrī</s>.

children.text: pūrve bhadraḥ subhadro dvau dakṣe caṇḍapracaṇḍakau ||
children.translated_text: In the east are the two, <s>Bhadra</s> and <s>Subhadra</s>; on the right are <s>Caṇḍa</s> and <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>.
In the west he should worship <s>Bala</s> and <s>Prabala</s>, and <s>Jaya</s> and <s>Vijaya</s>.
In the north, at the fourth door, are <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Gaṇa</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
In the fire-corner and the other corners of the sacred field, and in the directions, beginning with <s>Nārada</s>,
he should worship the siddha, the guru, <s>Nalakūbara</s>, and the blessed one in the corner.
In the east he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Viṣṇutapas</s>, and <s>Viṣṇuśakti</s>.

children.text: tato viṣṇuparīvāraṃ madhye śaktiṃ ca kūrmakam ||
children.translated_text: Then he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s retinue, the śakti in the middle, and the tortoise.
<s>Ananta</s>, the earth, dharma, knowledge, and detachment are to be worshiped beginning from the southeast.
And sovereignty, beginning from the northwest, and the self of light in the north.
He should worship sattva, the self of prakṛti, rajas whose form is delusion,
tamas, the bulb and lotus, and the syllable ka as the crow-principle.
The principle of vidyā, the supreme principle, and the maṇḍalas of sun, moon, and fire,

children.text: vimalādyā āsanaṃ ca prācyāṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ prapūjayet ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vimalā</s> and the others as the seat; in the east he should worship śrīṃ and hrīṃ.
The mantra ending in svāhā to 'the beloved of the cowherd women' is taught.

children.text: aṅgāni yathā cakraṃ ca sucakraṃ ca vicakraṃ ca tathaica ||
children.translated_text: The limbs are as follows: the cakra, sucakra, and vicakra as well.
The cakra that protects the three worlds, the <s>Sudarśana</s> that is the enemy of demons,
the missile in the corners beginning with the heart and the others, and the śakti in the east.
<s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, <s>Sunandā</s>, and <s>Nāgnajitī</s> too,
<s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, <s>Mitravindā</s>, <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, and <s>Suśīlā</s>.
He should worship the conch, discus, mace, lotus, pestle, and <s>Śārṅga</s> bow.

children.text: khaḍgaṃ pāśāṅkuśaṃ prācyāṃ śrīvatsaṃ kaustubhaṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: In the east he should worship the sword, noose, and goad, and also <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s>.
He should worship the crown and the garland, and the standards and chief emblems beginning with that of <s>Indra</s>.
He should worship <s>Kumuda</s> and the others, <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, and <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> together with <s>Śrī</s>.
By recitation, meditation, and worship he obtains all desires.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śrīgopālapūjānirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭāviṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-eighth chapter, called 'Description of the Worship of Śrī <s>Gopāla</s>,' in the first section, the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall explain the Trailokyamohinī, foremost among rites of <s>Puruṣottama</s>,
the worship-mantras of <s>Śrīdhara</s> and the others, which grant dharma, desire, and the other aims.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hrūṃ oṃ namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ śrīṃ klīṃ hrūṃ oṃ, homage.

children.text: puruṣottama apratirūpa lakṣmīnivāsa jagatkṣobhaṇa sarvastrīhṛdayadāraṇa tribhuvanamadonmādanakara surāsuramanujasundarī janamanāṃsi tāpaya tāpaya śoṣaya śoṣaya māraya māraya stambhaya stambhaya drāvaya drāvaya ākarṣaya ākarṣaya paramasubhaga sarvasaubhāgyakara sarvakāmaprada amukaṃ hana hana cakreṇa gadayā khaḍgena sarvabāṇair bhinddhi bhinddhi pāśena kuṭṭa kuṭṭa aṅkuśena tāḍaya tāḍaya turu turu kiṃ tiṣṭhasi tāraya tāraya yāvatsamīhitaṃ me siddhaṃ bhavati hrīṃ phaṭ namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Puruṣottama</s>, incomparable one, abode of <s>Lakṣmī</s>, shaker of the world, splitter of the hearts of all women, maker of the three worlds mad with intoxication, heat, heat the minds of beautiful women among gods, asuras, and humans; dry them up, dry them up; kill, kill; paralyze, paralyze; drive away, drive away; attract, attract. Supremely fortunate one, maker of every fortune, giver of every desire, strike such-and-such a person, strike; with the discus, mace, sword, and all arrows, split, split; with the noose, crush, crush; with the goad, beat, beat. Hurry, hurry. Why do you stand still? Carry across, carry across, until my intended aim is accomplished. Hrīṃ phaṭ, homage.
Oṃ śrīṃ, homage to <s>Śrīdhara</s>, the enchanter of the three worlds.
Klīṃ, homage to <s>Puruṣottama</s>, the enchanter of the three worlds.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the enchanter of the three worlds.

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ klīṃ trailokyamohanāya viṣṇave namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ śrīṃ klīṃ, homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the enchanter of the three worlds.
The Trailokyamohana mantras all accomplish every purpose.
They may all be contemplated separately, either at length or in brief.
The seat, the image-mantra, the homa and other auxiliaries, the six limbs,

children.text: cakraṃ gadāṃ ca khaḍgaṃ ca musalaṃ śaṃmakhaśarṅgakam ||
children.translated_text: the discus, mace, sword, pestle, and the conch-faced Śārṅga,
the arrow, noose, and goad, together with <s>Lakṣmī</s> and <s>Garuḍa</s>,
and <s>Viṣvaksena</s>: whether at length or in brief, a person obtains everything.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe trailokyamohinīpūjanavidhir nāmaikonatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the twenty-ninth chapter, called 'The Procedure for the Worship of <s>Trailokyamohinī</s>,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall explain in detail the auspicious worship of <s>Śrīdhara</s>.

children.text: parivāraśca sarveṣāṃ samo jñeyo hi paṇḍitaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: The retinue of all of them is to be understood by the learned as the same.
Oṃ śrāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ śrīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ śrūṃ, vauṣaṭ to the crest-lock.
Oṃ śraiṃ, huṃ to the armor.
Oṃ śrauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Oṃ śraḥ, phaṭ to the weapon: thus.
He should display his own mudrā, such as the conch, discus, mace, and the like,
after meditating on himself as one named <s>Śrīdhara</s>, holding conch, discus, and mace.
Then he should worship that god in a maṇḍala such as a svastika.
First he should worship the seat of the god of gods, the bearer of <s>Śārṅga</s>.
With these mantras, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; hear those mantras, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Oṃ, deities of <s>Śrīdhara</s>'s seat, come.
Oṃ, homage to the seat of <s>Acyuta</s> together with the entire retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Dhātṛ</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vidhātṛ</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yamunā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the support-power.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kūrma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Pṛthivī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Dharma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to knowledge.
Oṃ, homage to detachment.
Oṃ, homage to sovereignty.
Oṃ, homage to adharma.
Oṃ, homage to ignorance.
Oṃ, homage to non-detachment.
Oṃ, homage to lack of sovereignty.
Oṃ, homage to the bulb.
Oṃ, homage to the stalk.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vimalā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Jñānā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kriyā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yogā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Prahvī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Satyā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Īśānā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Anugrahā</s>.
Having worshiped <s>Rudra</s> in the same way, the very wise man should invoke and worship <s>Hari</s>
with these mantras, which destroy all sins.

children.text: oṃ hrīṃ śrīdharāya trailokyamohanāya viṣṇave namaḥ āgaccha ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Śrīdhara</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the enchanter of the three worlds; come.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Śrī</s>.
Oṃ śrāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ śrīṃ, homage to the head.
Oṃ śrūṃ, homage to the crest-lock.
Oṃ śraiṃ, homage to the armor.
Oṃ śrauṃ, homage to the three eyes.
Oṃ śraḥ, homage to the weapon.
Oṃ, homage to the conch.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ, homage to the discus.
Oṃ, homage to the mace.
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> mark.
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Kaustubha</s> jewel.
Oṃ, homage to the forest garland.
Oṃ, homage to the yellow garment.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Nārada</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the gurus.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Indra</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Agni</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yama</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Nirṛti</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāyu</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Soma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to sattva.
Oṃ, homage to rajas.
Oṃ, homage to tamas.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.
Then, with these great mantras, he should offer the ablution, the garment, and then the sacred thread,

children.text: gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā dhūpaṃ dīpamannaṃ pradakṣiṇam ||
children.translated_text: sandal paste, flowers, incense, a lamp, food, and circumambulation.
Having made the offerings, he should then recite the mantra.
After reciting it one hundred and eight times, he should then offer it up.

children.text: tato muhūrtamekaṃ tu dhyāyeddevaṃ hṛdi sthitam
children.translated_text: Then for one muhūrta he should meditate on the god established in his heart,
shining like pure crystal and equal in radiance to ten million suns,
with a gracious face, gentle, with flashing makara earrings,
wearing a crown, noble in body, and adorned with a forest garland.
The wise man should contemplate <s>Śrīdhara</s> as the form of the supreme brahman,
and with this very hymn he should praise the supreme lord.
Homage to the god <s>Śrīnivāsa</s>; homage to <s>Śrīpati</s>.
Repeated homage to <s>Śrīdhara</s>, who bears <s>Śārṅga</s>, the giver of prosperity.
Repeated homage to the peaceful beloved of <s>Śrī</s>, the glorious one.
Homage to the dweller on <s>Śrīparvata</s>, and to the maker of welfare.
Repeated homage to the lord of all excellences and to the refuge.
Repeated homage to him whose form is welfare and who brings prosperity.
Homage to the one who gives refuge and is most excellent; again and again, homage.
Having made the hymn and bowed, he should dismiss the god of gods.
Thus, O <s>Rudra</s>, the worship of the great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been fully described.

children.text: yaḥ karoti mahābhaktyā sa yāti paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: He who performs it with great devotion goes to the supreme abode.
He who recites this chapter, which reveals the worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>,

children.text: sa vidhūyeha pāpāni yāti viṣṇoḥ paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: shakes off sins here and goes to the supreme abode of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śrīdharārcanavidhir nāma triṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirtieth chapter, called 'The Procedure for the Worship of <s>Śrīdhara</s>,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Rudra</s> said:

children.text: bhūya evaṃ jagannātha pūjāṃ kathaya me prabho
children.translated_text: Again, in this way, O lord of the world, tell me the worship, O lord,
by which I may cross the ocean of saṃsāra, so very hard to cross.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall teach the worship of the god <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.
Listen to that auspicious rite, O greatly fortunate one, which grants enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: kṛtvā snānaṃ tataḥ sandhyāṃ tato yāgagṛhaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Having bathed, then performed the twilight rite, he should go to the sacrificial house.

children.text: prakṣālya pāṇī pādau ca ācamya ca viśeṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having washed his hands and feet, he should sip water carefully.
He should install the entire root mantra pervasively on his two hands.

children.text: mūlamantraṃ ca devasya śṛṇu rudra vadāmi te ||
children.translated_text: And hear the root mantra of the god; I shall tell it to you, O <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ śrīdharāya viṣṇave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ śrīṃ hrīṃ, homage to <s>Śrīdhara</s>, to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
This mantra denotes the lord of the gods, the sovereign <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
It removes all diseases and likewise removes all grahas.
and it removes all sins and grants both enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: aṅganyāsaṃ tataḥ kuryād ebhir mantrair vicakṣaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Then the discerning man should perform aṅganyāsa (installation on the limbs) with these mantras:
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ hīṃ, svāhā to the head.
Oṃ hūṃ, vaṣaṭ to the topknot.
Oṃ haiṃ, huṃ to the armor.
Oṃ hauṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes.
Oṃ haḥ, phaṭ to the missile.

children.text: iti mantraḥ samākhyāto mayā te prabhaviṣṇunā
children.translated_text: Thus the mantra has been explained to you by me, powerful <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Having performed nyāsa (ritual installation), the self-controlled man should display his mudrā (ritual seal).
Then he should meditate on supreme <s>Viṣṇu</s>, dwelling in the cavity of the heart,
on <s>Hari</s>, furnished with conch and discus, white as jasmine and the moon,
bearing the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s>, adorned with a forest-garland,
the supreme lord, furnished with a jeweled necklace and crown.

children.text: ahaṃ viṣṇuriti dhyātvā kṛtvā vai śodhanādikam
children.translated_text: Having meditated, "I am <s>Viṣṇu</s>," and having performed purification and the rest,

children.text: yaṃ kṣaiṃ ramiti bījaiśca kaṭhinīkṛtya nāmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: with the seed-syllables yaṃ, kṣaiṃ, and raṃ, and with the names, he should make it firm.
Then, having produced an egg, he should split it by means of the praṇava (oṃ) alone.
There, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>, having visualized the form described before,
he should then perform self-worship with auspicious fragrances, flowers, and the like.
Having invoked them, he should worship all the deities that belong to the seat.
With these mantras, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; hear that mantra, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
May the deities of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s seat come.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Acyuta</s> together with his whole retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Dhātṛ</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vidhātṛ</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yamunā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Śaṅkhanidhi</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Padmanidhi</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Caṇḍa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Pracaṇḍa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the fortune of the doorway.
Oṃ, homage to the supporting power.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kūrma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Śrī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>dharma</s> (normative order).
Oṃ, homage to knowledge.
Oṃ, homage to dispassion.
Oṃ, homage to lordly power.
Oṃ, homage to <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness).
Oṃ, homage to ignorance.
Oṃ, homage to non-dispassion.
Oṃ, homage to absence of lordly power.
Oṃ saṃ, homage to <s>sattva</s> (lucidity).
Oṃ raṃ, homage to <s>rajas</s> (activity).
Oṃ taṃ, homage to <s>tamas</s> (darkness).
Oṃ kaṃ, homage to the root-stock.
Oṃ naṃ, homage to the stalk.
Oṃ lāṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to the solar disk.
Oṃ soṃ, homage to the lunar disk.
Oṃ vaṃ, homage to the fire disk.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vimalā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Jñānā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kriyā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yogā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Prahvī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Satyā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Īśānā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Anugrahā</s>.
With these fragrances and flowers, and with these mantras, he should worship them.
Having worshipped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the maker of creation and dissolution,
and having invoked him in the maṇḍala (ritual diagram), O <s>Rudra</s>, he should worship the supreme lord.
By this procedure, O <s>Rudra</s>, it is supreme and removes all sins.

children.text: yathātmani tathā deve nyāsaṃ kurvīta cāditaḥ
children.translated_text: As in oneself, so also in the deity, he should perform nyāsa first.
After that he should display the mudrā, and then offer the arghya and other offerings.
Then he should perform the bath, give clothing, and then water for sipping.

children.text: gandhapuṣpaṃ tathā dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ dadyāccaruṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he should give fragrance and flowers, incense, a lamp, and the oblation.
Then circumambulation, then recitation; after that he should offer it to him.
With their own mantras, the sādhaka (practitioner) should worship the limbs and the rest.
Know that this is done with the deity's root-mantra, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
Hear now, O three-eyed one, the mantras as they are being spoken by me.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ hīṃ, homage to the head.
Oṃ hūṃ, homage to the topknot.
Oṃ haiṃ, homage to the armor.
Oṃ hauṃ, homage to the three eyes.
Oṃ haḥ, homage to the missile.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Śrī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the conch.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ, homage to the discus.
Oṃ, homage to the mace.
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Kaustubha</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the forest-garland.
Oṃ, homage to the yellow garment.
Oṃ, homage to the sword.
Oṃ, homage to the pestle.
Oṃ, homage to the noose.
Oṃ, homage to the goad.
Homage to <s>Śārṅga</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the arrow.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Nārada</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the former siddhas.
Oṃ, homage to the <s>Bhāgavatas</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the gurus.
Oṃ, homage to the supreme gurus.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Agni</s>, lord of fiery splendor, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yama</s>, lord of the departed, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Nirṛti</s>, lord of the rākṣasas, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of the waters, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of vital breath, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Soma</s>, lord of the lunar mansions, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>, lord of knowledge, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>, lord of the nāgas, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the worlds, together with his vehicle and retinue.
Oṃ, homage to the thunderbolt: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the spear-power: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the staff: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the sword: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the noose: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the banner: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the mace: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the trident: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the discus: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus: huṃ phaṭ.
Oṃ vaiṃ, homage to <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.
With these mantras, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, the limbs and the rest are to be worshipped by men.
Having worshipped the great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose nature is <s>Brahman</s>,
one should praise the imperishable <s>Paramātman</s> with this hymn:
Homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the god of gods; homage indeed to the mighty <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Homage to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and also to the maintainer.
Homage likewise to the devourer; homage to him who lies down at the dissolution.

children.text: devānāṃ prabhave caiva yajñānāṃ prabhave namaḥ
children.translated_text: Homage to the source of the gods, and homage to the source of sacrifices.
Homage always to the source of the sages, and to the powerful <s>Viṣṇu</s> of the <s>Yakṣas</s>.
Homage to <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, lord of all the gods, to the all-pervading great-souled one,
to him honored by <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Indra</s>, and <s>Rudra</s>; homage again and again to the lord of all.
Homage indeed to him who acts for the welfare of all worlds, to the overseer of the worlds,
to the protector of all, the maker of all, the destroyer of all the wicked.
Homage again and again to the giver of boons, the peaceful one, the most excellent one,
to the refuge, the beautiful one, the giver of <s>dharma</s>, desire, and wealth.
Having praised him, one should meditate in one's own heart on the imperishable one whose form is <s>Brahman</s>.
Thus, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the root mantra.

children.text: mūlamantraṃ japedvāpi yaḥ sa yāti naro harim
children.translated_text: Or the man who recites the root mantra goes to <s>Hari</s>.
This supreme worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s> has been taught to you, O <s>Rudra</s>,
the highest secret, deeply hidden, supreme, granting enjoyment and liberation.
And the learned man devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s> who reads this, O <s>Hara</s>,
or who hears it or causes it to be heard, goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣṇupūjāvidhir nāmaikatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part called the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the thirty-first chapter, named "The Procedure for Worship of <s>Viṣṇu</s>," is completed.
<s>Maheśvara</s> said:
Teach me the worship of the five tattvas (principles), O bearer of conch, discus, and mace,

children.text: yena vijñānamātreṇa naro yāti paraṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: by the knowledge of which alone a man goes to the supreme state.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall teach you the worship of the five tattvas, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, excellent in vows,

children.text: maṅgalyaṃ maṅgalaṃ divyaṃ rahasyaṃ kāmadaṃ param ||
children.translated_text: auspicious, blessed, divine, secret, supreme, and granting desires.
Listen to that, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, holy and destructive of the Kali age.
The eternal <s>Paramātman</s> is one alone, imperishable and peaceful.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> is fixed, pure, all-pervading, and stainless.

children.text: sa eva māyāyā deva pañcadhā saṃsthito hariḥ ||
children.translated_text: By <s>māyā</s> (cosmic power), O god, that same <s>Hari</s> stands in a fivefold form.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, who benefits the worlds and destroys all the wicked,
exists in the form of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and likewise as <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>,
likewise in the form of <s>Pradyumna</s>, and as the one called <s>Aniruddha</s>.
In the form of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the non-dual one indeed stands fivefold.
Hear these mantras that denote them, O bull-bannered one.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Oṃ āṃ, homage to <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Pradyumna</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Aniruddha</s>.
Oṃ oṃ, homage to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
The five mantras have been declared to you as denoting the deities.
They remove all sins, are meritorious, and destroy all diseases.
Now I shall fully teach the auspicious worship of the five tattvas,

children.text: vidhinā yena kartavyaṃ yairvā mantraiśca śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: the rule by which it is to be performed and the mantras with which, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: ādau snānaṃ prakurvīta snātvā sandhyāṃ samācaret
children.translated_text: First one should bathe; having bathed, one should perform the twilight rite.
Having reached the worship room, one should wash the arghya and the other vessels as well.
Having sipped water, the wise man should sit down, assuming the desired posture.

children.text: śoṣaṇādi tataḥ kuryād aṃ kṣaiṃ ramiti mantrakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then he should perform drying and the other rites with the mantras "aṃ," "kṣaiṃ," and "raṃ."
Having made the ordinary substance firm, he should then produce the cosmic egg.
After splitting the egg, he should then visualize <s>Parameśvara</s> within the egg:
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, lord of the world, clothed in yellow silk,
shining like a thousand suns, with glittering makara earrings.

children.text: ātmano hṛdi padme tu dhyāyettu parameśvaram
children.translated_text: In the lotus of his own heart he should meditate on <s>Parameśvara</s>.
Then he should contemplate the god <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> as himself, the lord,
then <s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, and glorious <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
He should contemplate <s>Indra</s> and the other gods as arisen from that god of gods.
Then he should contemplate nyāsa (ritual placement), to be performed on both hands.
Then comes the pervading nyāsa with the root mantra, and after that the limb-nyāsa.
With the limb mantras, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; hear those mantras, O excellent in vows.
Oṃ āṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ īṃ, homage to the head.
Oṃ ūṃ, homage to the topknot.
Oṃ aiṃ, homage to the armor.
Oṃ auṃ, homage to the three eyes.
Oṃ aḥ, homage to the missile; phaṭ.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Acyuta</s> together with his entire retinue.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Dhātṛ</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vidhātṛ</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the supporting power.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kūrma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the earth.
Oṃ, homage to <s>dharma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>dharma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to knowledge.
Oṃ, homage to dispassion.
Oṃ, homage to lordly power.
Oṃ, homage to ignorance.
Oṃ, homage to lack of lordly power.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to the solar orb.
Oṃ soṃ, homage to the lunar orb.
Oṃ vaṃ, homage to the fire orb.

children.text: oṃ vaṃ vāsudevāya parabrahmaṇe śivāya tejorūpāya vyāpine sarvadevādhidevāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ vaṃ, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, auspicious, formed of radiance, all-pervading, the god above all gods.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Pāñcajanya</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Sudarśana</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the mace.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Śrī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Hrī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Puṣṭi</s>.
Oṃ, homage to song.
Oṃ, homage to power.
Oṃ, homage to affection.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Indra</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Agni</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Yama</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Nirṛti</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāyu</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Soma</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Viṣvaksena</s>.
These mantras have been set forth for you briefly, O <s>Rudra</s>.
And the worship should indeed be performed on a maṇḍala such as one marked with a svastika.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus.

children.text: aṅganyāsaṃ ca kṛtvā tu mudrāḥ sarvāḥ pradarśayet
children.translated_text: Having performed the aṅganyāsa, he should display all the mudrās.

children.text: ātmānaṃ vāsudevaṃ ca dhyātvā caiva pareśvaram ||
children.translated_text: He should meditate on himself as <s>Vāsudeva</s> and on the supreme lord.
After that, having duly invoked him, a man should worship the seat.
At the doorway the worship of <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s> should be performed, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
First he should worship <s>Garuḍa</s> before <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
In the middle region he should fully worship the series beginning with the conch and ending with the lotus.
Beginning in the eastern quarter, he should worship <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), knowledge, detachment, and sovereignty.
In the southeast and the other quarters he should worship the four beginning with unrighteousness.
In the middle of the three maṇḍalas the placement of the seat has been stated.
On the lotus petals beginning in the east, <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s> and the others are to be worshiped.
In the pericarp he should worship <s>Vāsudeva</s>, the supreme lord.
<s>Pāñcajanya</s> and the others are to be worshiped, stationed in the northeast and the other quarters.
And the powers of the god of gods are to be worshiped beginning in the east, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
The guardians of the worlds beginning with <s>Indra</s> are to be worshiped, stationed in the east and the other quarters.

children.text: adho nāgaṃ tadūrdhvaṃ tu brahmāṇaṃ pūjayetsudhīḥ
children.translated_text: Below he should worship the serpent, and above that <s>Brahmā</s>; so should the wise man do.

children.text: iti sthānakramo jñeyo maṇḍale śaṅkara tvayā ||
children.translated_text: Thus the sequence of places in the maṇḍala should be known by you, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: āvāhya maṇḍale devaṃ kṛtvā nyāsaṃ tu tasya ca
children.translated_text: Having invoked the god in the maṇḍala and performed his nyāsa,

children.text: mudrāṃ pradarśya pādyādīn dadyān mūlena śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: he should display the mudrā and, with the root mantra, offer water for the feet and the other offerings, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: snānaṃ vastraṃ tathācāmaṃ gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ ca dhūpakam
children.translated_text: Bathing water, a garment, water for sipping, fragrance, flowers, and incense,
a lamp, food offering, water for sipping, obeisance, and circumambulation
he should perform with the root mantra, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and he should also offer his japa.
Then he should recite this hymn, remembering <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: oṃ namo vāsudevāya namaḥ saṃkarṣaṇāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, and homage to <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>.
Repeated homage to <s>Pradyumna</s>, the primordial god, and to <s>Aniruddha</s>.
Homage indeed to <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; homage to the lord of <s>Nara</s> and <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Homage to him who is worshiped by men, renowned, praised, and boon-granting,
to the beginningless and endless one, the ancient one; repeated homage.
Homage to the maker of creation and destruction, and to the lord of <s>Brahmā</s>.
Homage to him who is to be known through the Veda, and to him who bears the conch and discus.
Repeated homage to the remover of the stain of the Kali age and to the lord of the gods.
Repeated homage to the cutter of the tree of saṃsāra and to the cleaver of māyā.
Homage to the many-formed one, the sacred ford, the one with the three guṇas and beyond the guṇas,
to him whose forms are <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Īśa</s>, the giver of liberation; repeated homage.
Repeated homage to the gateway of liberation, to <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), and to the maker of creation.
Homage to the giver of all desires, whose own nature is the supreme brahman.
Lift me up, sunk in the terrible ocean of saṃsāra.

children.text: tvadanyo nāsti deveśa nāsti trātā jagatprabho ||
children.translated_text: There is no lord of gods other than you; there is no rescuer, O lord of the world.

children.text: tvāmava sarvagaṃ viṣṇuṃ gato 'haṃ śaraṇaṃ gataḥ
children.translated_text: I have gone for refuge to you alone, the all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>; I have taken refuge.
By giving the lamp of knowledge, make me free from darkness and illumined.
Thus he should praise the lord of gods, the destroyer of all afflictions.

children.text: anyaiśca vādakeḥ stotraiḥ stutvā vai nīlalohita ||
children.translated_text: Having praised him also with other hymns, O <s>Nīlalohita</s>,
a man should meditate in his heart on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, endowed with the five principles.
Then he should dismiss the god. Thus the worship has been proclaimed.
It is the best worship of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and grants all desires.
By this worship alone a man becomes one whose purpose is accomplished.

children.text: idaṃ ca yaḥ paṭhedrudra pañcatattvārcanaṃ naraḥ
children.translated_text: And the man who recites this worship of the five principles, O <s>Rudra</s>,
or hears it or causes it to be heard, goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe pañcatattvārcanavidhir nāma dvātriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-second chapter, called 'The Procedure for the Worship of the Five Principles,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
Tell me the worship of <s>Sudarśana</s>, O bearer of conch and mace,
by performing which all planetary afflictions, diseases, and the like indeed come to destruction.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Hear the worship of the discus <s>Sudarśana</s>, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
First one should perform bathing, and then one should worship <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: mūlamantreṇa vai nyāsaṃ mūlamantraṃ śṛṇuṣva ca
children.translated_text: With the root mantra one should perform nyāsa; and hear the root mantra.

children.text: sahasrāraṃ huṃ phaṭ namo mantraḥ praṇavapūrvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Preceded by the praṇava, the mantra is: 'sahasrāraṃ huṃ phaṭ namaḥ.'
It has been taught as the destroyer of all evil beings and as the breaker of mantras.

children.text: dhyāyet sudarśanaṃ devaṃ hṛdi padme 'male śubhe ||
children.translated_text: One should meditate on the god <s>Sudarśana</s> in the stainless, auspicious lotus of the heart,
gentle, crowned, and bearing conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
Having invoked the god in the maṇḍala by the previously stated method, O <s>Hara</s>,
he should worship him with fragrant flowers and other services, O <s>Maheśvara</s>.
After worshiping, a man should recite the mantra one hundred and eight times.
O <s>Rudra</s>, whoever performs in this way the excellent worship of the discus
becomes free from all diseases and attains the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Afterward he should recite this hymn, which destroys all diseases.
Homage indeed to <s>Sudarśana</s>, whose radiance is that of a thousand suns,
who blazes with garlands of flames, who is thousand-spoked, who is an eye,
who destroys all evil beings and crushes every sin.
Homage to the good discus, the varied discus, the breaker of all mantras,
to the progenitor, the bearer of the world, and the destroyer of the world.
Homage to him who exists for the protection of the worlds and for the destruction of wicked asuras,

children.text: ugrāya caiva saumyāya caṇḍāya ca namonamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to the fierce one, the gentle one, and the terrible one; repeated homage.
Homage to him whose form is an eye, the splitter of the fear of saṃsāra,
and to the breaker of the cage of māyā, the auspicious one; repeated homage.
Homage to him whose form is graha and atigraha, to the lord of the grahas,

children.text: kālāya mṛtyave caiva bhīmāya ca namonamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: to Time, to Death, and indeed to the terrifying one; repeated homage.
Repeated homage to the giver of grace to devotees and the protector of devotees,
to the peaceful one in the form of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and to the bearer of weapons.
Homage again and again to the disc, <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s weapon.

children.text: iti stotraṃ mahāpuṇyaṃ cakrasya tava kīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Thus this greatly meritorious hymn of your disc has been proclaimed.

children.text: yaḥ paṭhetparayā bhaktyā viṣṇulokaṃ sa gacchati
children.translated_text: Whoever recites it with supreme devotion goes to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
And whoever, O <s>Rudra</s>, self-controlled, recites the procedure for worship of the disc,
after reducing sin to ashes, becomes fit for the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sudarśanapūjāvidhir nāma trayastriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the venerable <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the eastern part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the thirty-third chapter, called The Procedure for the Worship of <s>Sudarśana</s>.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
Tell me again, O <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, O <s>Gadādhara</s>, about worship of the gods.
As I listen, I have no satiety for the worship that you describe.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall tell you the worship of the god <s>Hayagrīva</s>;
listen to that, O lord of the world, by which <s>Viṣṇu</s> is pleased.
O <s>Mahādeva</s>, the root mantra that names <s>Hayagrīva</s>

children.text: pravakṣyāmi paraṃ puṇyaṃ tadādau śṛṇu śaṅkara ||
children.translated_text: I shall declare, most holy; first hear that, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: oṃ saiṃ kṣaiṃ śirase namaḥ iti praṇavasaṃyutaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ saiṃ kṣaiṃ, homage to the head: this is joined with the praṇava;
this nine-syllabled mantra bestows all knowledge.
O <s>Mahādeva</s>, hear its limbs, O bull-bannered one.
Oṃ kṣāṃ, homage to the heart.

children.text: oṃ kṣīṃ śirase svāhā śiraḥ proktaṃ kṣūṃ vaṣaṭ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣīṃ, svāhā to the head; the head is declared, and likewise kṣūṃ vaṣaṭ.

children.text: oṃ kārayuktā devasya śikhā jñeyā vṛṣadhvaja
children.translated_text: Joined with oṃ, it is to be known as the god's topknot, O bull-bannered one.

children.text: oṃ kṣaiṃ kavacāya huṃ vai kavacaṃ parikīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣaiṃ, huṃ to the armor; thus the armor has been proclaimed.

children.text: oṃ kṣaiṃ netratrayāya vauṣaṭ netraṃ devasya kīrtitam
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣaiṃ, vauṣaṭ to the three eyes: the eye of the god has been declared.

children.text: oṃ haḥ astrāya phaṭ astraṃ devasya kīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ haḥ, phaṭ to the missile: the god's missile has been proclaimed.
I shall explain the procedure of worship; hear it as I tell it.

children.text: ādau snātvā tathācamya tato yāgagṛhaṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: First, after bathing and then sipping water, he should go to the sacrificial house.

children.text: tataḥ praviśya vidhivat kuryād vaṃ śoṣaṇādikam
children.translated_text: Then, having entered properly, he should perform drying with vaṃ and the rest.

children.text: yaṃ kṣaiṃ ramiti bījaiśca kaṭhinīkṛtya lamiti ||
children.translated_text: With the seed-syllables yaṃ, kṣaiṃ, and raṃ, and having made it firm with laṃ,

children.text: aṇḍamutpādya ca tataḥ oṃ kāreṇaiva bhedayet
children.translated_text: he should produce the cosmic egg, and then split it by means of oṃ.
Within the egg he should contemplate himself as <s>Hayagrīva</s>.
He is white like a conch, jasmine, and the moon, with the radiance of lotus fiber and silver,
like cow's milk, and likewise equal in splendor to ten million suns,

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ cakraṃ gadāṃ padmaṃ dhārayantaṃ caturbhujam ||
children.translated_text: four-armed, holding conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
He wears a crown and earrings and is adorned with a forest garland,
with a beautiful discus and fine cheeks, the all-pervading lord wearing yellow garments.
Having visualized the great-souled one, accompanied by all the gods,
he should then perform nyāsa (ritual placement) with the limb-mantras and likewise with the root mantra.
Then he should display the auspicious mudrās (ritual gestures), beginning with the conch and lotus.
Having meditated, he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the root mantra, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Then, O <s>Rudra</s>, he should invoke the deities who belong to the seat.
Oṃ, deities of <s>Hayagrīva</s>'s seat, come.
Having invoked them in the maṇḍala (ritual diagram), he should worship them in the svastika and other diagrams.
At the doorway worship should be performed for <s>Dhātṛ</s> and <s>Vidhātṛ</s>, O bull-bannered one.
'Homage to <s>Acyuta</s> together with his entire retinue':

children.text: asya madhye 'rcanaṃ kāryaṃ dvāre gaṅgāṃ ca pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: with this, worship should be performed in its center; at the doorway he should worship <s>Gaṅgā</s>,
and the great goddess <s>Yamunā</s>, and also the treasures <s>Śaṅkha</s> and <s>Padma</s>.

children.text: garuḍaṃ pūjayedagre madhye śaktiṃ ca pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: He should worship <s>Garuḍa</s> in front, and in the middle he should worship the power,
called Support, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; then he should worship <s>Kūrma</s>.
After that, <s>Ananta</s> and the earth; then he should worship <s>dharma</s> and knowledge,
and then dispassion and lordly power in the southeast and the other directions.
But in the east and the other directions he should worship adharma, ignorance, lack of dispassion, and lack of lordly power.
Then he should worship sattva, rajas, and tamas in the central region,

children.text: kandaṃ nālaṃ ca padmaṃ ca madhye caiva prapūjayet ||
children.translated_text: and in the middle he should worship the stalk, the stem, and the lotus.
The worship of the maṇḍalas (ritual circles) called sun, moon, and fire
is to be performed in the central region; thus it has been proclaimed, O <s>Rudra</s>.
O bull-bannered one, <s>Vimalā</s>, <s>Utkarṣiṇī</s>, <s>Jñānā</s>, <s>Kriyā</s>, <s>Yogā</s>,
<s>Prahvī</s>, <s>Satyā</s>, and also <s>Īśānā</s> and <s>Anugrahā</s>: these are the powers.
On the petals beginning in the east, <s>Vimalā</s> and the others are to be worshiped;
<s>Anugrahā</s> is to be worshiped in the pericarp by men who desire welfare.
With mantras beginning with the praṇava and ending with namaḥ, and with names in the dative case,
with these mantras, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, he should worship the seat fully.
By offering bathing-water and fragrance, and by offering flowers and incense,
by offering a lamp and food, the auspicious worship of the seat

children.text: kartavyaṃ vidhinānena iti te hara kīrtitam
children.translated_text: should be performed according to this rule; this has been declared to you, O <s>Hara</s>.
Then he should invoke the god, <s>Hayagrīva</s>, lord of the gods.
He should imagine him coming through the left nostril.
With the ritual expression 'come' and with the root mantra, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
the invocation of the god of gods, the bearer of the conch, should be performed.
Having invoked him in his maṇḍala (ritual diagram), he should diligently perform nyāsa (ritual placement).
Having performed nyāsa (ritual placement), he should contemplate the supreme lord established there,
<s>Hayagrīva</s>, the great god, honored by gods and asuras,
imperishable <s>Viṣṇu</s>, accompanied by <s>Indra</s> and the other guardians of the worlds.
Having meditated, he should display the auspicious mudrās (ritual gestures), beginning with conch and discus.
Then he should give foot-water, arghya (honor-offering), and water for sipping to <s>Viṣṇu</s>;
then he should bathe the god, <s>Padmanābha</s>, free from illness.
Having installed the god according to rule, he should offer clothing, O bull-bannered one.
Then he should offer water for sipping, and after that the auspicious sacred thread.
Then, in the maṇḍala, O <s>Rudra</s>, he should meditate on the god, the supreme lord.
Having meditated, he should again offer water for the feet and the other services to the god <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
He should make an offering to the god <s>Bhairava</s> with the root mantra, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: oṃ kṣāṃ hṛdayāya namaḥ anena hṛdayaṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣāṃ, homage to the heart: with this he should worship the heart.

children.text: oṃ kṣīṃ śirase namaśca śirasaḥ pūjanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣīṃ, homage to the head: thus the worship of the head is to be performed.

children.text: oṃ kṣūṃ śikhāyai namaśca śikhāmetena pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣūṃ, homage to the topknot: with this he should worship the topknot.

children.text: oṃ kṣaiṃ kavacāya namaḥ kavacaṃ paripūjayet
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣaiṃ, homage to the armor: he should fully worship the armor.

children.text: oṃ kṣaiṃ netrāya namaśca netraṃ cānena pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣaiṃ, homage to the eye: and with this he should worship the eye.

children.text: oṃ kṣaḥ astrāya nama iti astraṃ cānena pūjayet
children.translated_text: Oṃ kṣaḥ, homage to the missile: and with this he should worship the missile.

children.text: hṛdayaṃ ca śiraścaiva śikhāṃ ca kavacaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: The heart, the head, the topknot, and likewise the armor
he should worship completely in the places beginning with the east.
In the corners, O <s>Rudra</s>, he should worship the missile; in the center he should worship the eye.
He should worship the supreme goddess <s>Lakṣmī</s>, auspicious and bestowing <s>Lakṣmī</s>.

children.text: śaṅkhaṃ padmaṃ tathā cakraṃ gadāṃ pūrvādito 'rcayet ||
children.translated_text: He should worship the conch, lotus, discus, and mace, beginning from the east.

children.text: khaḍgaṃ ca musalaṃ pāśamaṅkuśaṃ saśaraṃ dhanuḥ
children.translated_text: The sword, pestle, noose, goad, bow together with its arrow
he should worship from the east, O <s>Rudra</s>, with these mantras bearing their own names.

children.text: śrīvatsaṃ kaustubhaṃ mālāṃ tathā pītāmbaraṃ śubham
children.translated_text: The <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, the <s>Kaustubha</s>, the garland, and the auspicious yellow garment
he should worship from the east, O <s>Rudra</s>, together with the bearer of conch, discus, and mace.

children.text: brahmāṇaṃ nāradaṃ siddhaṃ guruṃ paraguruṃ tathā
children.translated_text: He should worship <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, the siddha, the guru, and likewise the supreme guru.
And in the same way he should worship the sandals of the guru and of the supreme guru.
Then he should worship <s>Indra</s> with his vehicle and with his surrounding retinue.

children.text: agniṃ yamaṃ nirṛtiṃ ca varuṇaṃ vāyumeva ca ||
children.translated_text: Also <s>Agni</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Nirṛti</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s>,
and in this way he should fully worship <s>Soma</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and <s>Brahmā</s>.
He should worship from the east onward up to the upper direction, O bull-bannered one.

children.text: vajraṃ śaktiṃ tathā daṇḍaṃ khaḍgaṃ pāśaṃ dhvajaṃ gadām
children.translated_text: The thunderbolt, spear, staff, sword, noose, banner, and mace,
then the trident, discus, and lotus: he should worship these weapons.
Then he should worship the god <s>Viṣvaksena</s> in the northeastern direction.
With these mantras, ending in 'namaḥ' and beginning with the praṇava, O bull-bannered one,
the worship of <s>Ananta</s> is to be performed, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, O bull-bannered one.
The worship of the god is to be performed with the root mantra, O bull-bannered one.

children.text: gandhaṃ puṣpaṃ tathā dhūpaṃ dīpaṃ naivedyameva ca
children.translated_text: Fragrance, flowers, incense, lamp, and food offering,
circumambulation, homage, and recitation: he should present these to him.
He should also praise him with another hymn of praise beginning with the praṇava, O bull-bannered one:

children.text: oṃ namo hayaśirase vidyādhyakṣāya vai namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the horse-headed one, homage indeed to the superintendent of knowledge.
Homage to the one whose nature is knowledge; homage again and again to the giver of knowledge.
Homage to the peaceful god; homage to the self endowed with the three guṇas.
And homage to the destroyer of gods and demons, to the destroyer of all the wicked,
homage indeed to the lord of all worlds, whose form is <s>Brahman</s>.
Homage to the one revered by lords, and to the bearer of conch and discus.
Homage to the primordial one, the restrained one, and the benefactor of all beings.
Homage to the one with the three guṇas and also without guṇas, whose form is <s>Brahmā</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>,
to the creator, the destroyer, the lord of gods, the all-pervading one: homage again and again.
Having made a praise in this way, he should contemplate the god of gods,
in the spotless lotus of the heart, O <s>Rudra</s>, as holding conch, discus, and mace,
shining like ten million suns and beautiful in every limb,
as <s>Hayagrīva</s>, lord of the earth, the supreme self, imperishable.

children.text: iti te kathitā pūjā hayagrīvasya śaṅkara
children.translated_text: Thus, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, the worship of <s>Hayagrīva</s> has been told to you.

children.text: yaḥ paṭhet parayā bhaktyā sa gacchetparamaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever recites it with supreme devotion goes to the highest state.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe hayagrīvapūjāvidhir nāma catustriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part of the early section, in the section on conduct, the thirty-fourth chapter, named 'The Procedure for the Worship of <s>Hayagrīva</s>'.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall explain the nyāsa and related rites of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>; listen, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
<s>Viśvāmitra</s> is its seer, and <s>Savitṛ</s> is its deity.
It has <s>Brahmā</s> as its head, <s>Rudra</s> as its topknot, and it rests in the heart of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Its application is its single eye, and it is born in the lineage of <s>Kātyāyana</s>.
It should be known as having the three worlds for its feet and as abiding in the womb of the earth.
Knowing <s>Gāyatrī</s> in this way, one should recite it twelve hundred thousand times.
It is to be known as three-footed with eight syllables; as four-footed, it has six syllables.

children.text: jape ca tripadā proktā arcane ca catuṣpadā ||
children.translated_text: In recitation it is said to be three-footed, and in worship four-footed.

children.text: nyāse jape tathā dhyāne agnikārye tathārcane
children.translated_text: In nyāsa, recitation, meditation, the fire rite, and worship,
one should always install <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the destroyer of all sin.
On the big toes, at the middle of the ankles, on the shanks, know it on the knees,

children.text: ūrvorguhye ca vṛṣaṇe nāḍyāṃ nābhau tanūdare ||
children.translated_text: on the thighs, in the private part and testicles, in the channel, at the navel, and in the body's belly,
on the breasts, heart, throat, lips, mouth, palate, and shoulders,

children.text: netre bhuvār lalāṭe ca pūrvasyāṃ dakṣiṇottare ||
children.translated_text: on the eyes, on the brow, on the forehead, and in the east, south, and north,
in the west and on the head: he should place the syllable a. I shall state the colors of the syllables.

children.text: indranīlaṃ ca vahniṃ ca pītaṃ śyāmaṃ ca kāpilam ||
children.translated_text: Indra-blue, fiery, yellow, dark, and tawny,

children.text: śvetaṃ vidyutprabhaṃ tāraṃ kṛṣṇaṃ raktaṃ krameṇa tat
children.translated_text: white, lightning-bright, star-like, black, and red, in that order,

children.text: śyāmaṃ śuklaṃ tathā pītaṃ śvetaṃ vai padmarāgavat ||
children.translated_text: dark, white, then yellow, white, and like ruby,
conch-colored, pale, red, and resembling liquor,
equal to the color of the sun, gentle, conch-like, and white indeed.
Whatever he touches with his hand and whatever he sees with his eye,

children.text: pūtaṃ bhavati tatsarvaṃ gāyattryā na paraṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: all that becomes purified; they know nothing higher than <s>Gāyatrī</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe gāyatrīnyāsanirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part of the early section, in the section on conduct, the thirty-fifth chapter, named 'Explanation of the Nyāsa of <s>Gāyatrī</s>'.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall teach the procedure of <s>sandhyā</s> (twilight worship), O <s>Rudra</s>; listen, for it destroys sin.
Having performed three prāṇāyāmas, one should begin the sandhyā bath.
Together with the praṇava and the vyāhṛtis, with the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and its head,

children.text: triḥ paṭhed āyatapraṇaḥ prāṇāyāmaḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: one should recite it three times with breath extended; that is called prāṇāyāma.
A twice-born man should burn away faults born of mind, speech, and body by prāṇāyāmas.
Therefore at all times he should be devoted to prāṇāyāma.
In the evening he should sip water with the formula 'Agniś ca me'; in the morning, with 'Sūryaś ca me.'
At midday, saying 'May the waters purify,' he should touch water according to rule.
With the ṛc beginning 'Āpo hi ṣṭhā' he should perform sprinkling with kuśa-water.

children.text: praṇavena tu saṃyuktaṃ kṣipedvāri pade pade ||
children.translated_text: Joined with the praṇava, he should cast water at each step.
The faults arising from rajas, tamas, and one's own delusion, and those born in waking, dream, and deep sleep,
and those born of speech, mind, and action: these nine he should burn away with nine [recitations].

children.text: samuddhṛtyodakaṃ pāṇau japtvā ca drupadāṃ kṣipet
children.translated_text: Having lifted water in his hand and recited the Drupadā verse, he should throw it away.
He should perform the offering-away of sin in three, eight, or twelve turns.
With the two verses beginning 'Ud u tyaṃ' and 'Citram,' he should attend upon the sun.

children.text: divā rātrau ca yatpāpaṃ sarvaṃ naśyati tatkṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: Whatever sin there is by day or by night is all destroyed at that very moment.
At the morning sandhyā one should stand while reciting; at the western one one should sit.
He should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, joined with the great vyāhṛtis and furnished with the praṇava.
With ten [recitations] <s>Gāyatrī</s> destroys sin produced from birth; with a hundred, what was done before.

children.text: triyugaṃ tu sahasreṇa gāyattrī hanti duṣkṛtam ||
children.translated_text: With a thousand, <s>Gāyatrī</s> destroys wrongdoing of three ages.
<s>Gāyatrī</s> is red; <s>Sāvitrī</s> is white in color.
<s>Sarasvatī</s> is to be known as black; thus the three sandhyās are declared.

children.text: oṃ bhūrvinyasya hṛdaye oṃ bhuvaḥ śirasi nyaset
children.translated_text: He should place 'oṃ bhūḥ' in the heart and place 'oṃ bhuvaḥ' on the head.

children.text: oṃ svariti śikhāyāṃ ca gāyattryāḥ prathamaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: And 'oṃ svaḥ' on the crest; then the first foot of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>,
the learned man should place on the armor, and the second he should place on the two eyes.
With the third he should make the limb-nyāsa, and the fourth he should place on all sides.
Having made the placement at sandhyā time, he should recite the Mother of the Veda.
May there be auspiciousness for him through the whole day; after prāṇāyāma he should perform the placement.
The three-footed <s>Gāyatrī</s> is <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
Having learned the application, seer, and meter, he should begin the recitation.
Freed from all sin, he attains <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
'Paro rajasi sāvad oṃ' is declared to be the fourth foot.

children.text: taṃ hanti sūryaḥ sandhyāyāṃ nopāstiṃ kurute tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: The sun destroys the one who does not perform attendance upon the sandhyā.
And the seer of the fourth foot is indeed <s>Nirmala</s>.

children.text: chandastu devī gāyattrī paramātmā ca devatā ||
children.translated_text: Its meter is the goddess <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and its deity is the supreme self.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe saṃdhyāvidhirnāma ṣaṭtriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-sixth chapter, called 'The Procedure of Sandhyā,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:

children.text: gāyattrī paramā devī bhuktimuktipradā ca tām
children.translated_text: <s>Gāyatrī</s> is the supreme goddess, and she grants enjoyment and liberation.
For the one who recites her, even great sins perish.
I shall explain the Gāyatrī rite, which grants enjoyment and liberation.
One should recite one thousand and eight times, or else eight hundred times.

children.text: trisandhyaṃ brahmalokī syācchataṃ japtvā jalaṃ pibet
children.translated_text: By reciting at the three sandhyās he becomes one whose world is <s>Brahmaloka</s>; having recited a hundred times, he should drink water.
At sandhyā one should invoke and worship the goddess who destroys all sins.

children.text: bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ svamantreṇa yutāṃ dvādaśanāmabhiḥ
children.translated_text: With 'bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ' and her own mantra, together with the twelve names,
'Homage to <s>Gāyatrī</s>.'
'Repeated homage to <s>Sāvitrī</s> and to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.'

children.text: vedamātre ca sāṃkṛtyai brahmāṇī kauśikī kramāt
children.translated_text: Then, in order, to the Mother of the Veda, to <s>Sāṃkṛtī</s>, to <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, and to <s>Kauśikī</s>,
to <s>Sādhvī</s>, to <s>Sarvārthasādhinī</s>, and to <s>Sahasrākṣī</s>, with 'bhūr bhuvaḥ'
and 'svaḥ'; in this way he should offer into the fire fuel, ghee, and sacrificial food.
He should offer ghee one thousand and eight times, or else eight hundred times.
For the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), desire, and the other aims, he should make offerings in all rites.
Having properly worshiped an image made of sandalwood or gold,
one should recite a hundred thousand times, living on milk, roots, and fruits.
By a homa of twenty thousand offerings, one obtains all desires.
Born on the northern peak, dwelling on the mountain on earth,
permitted by <s>Brahmā</s>, go, O goddess, as you please.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe gāyatrīkalpanirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-seventh chapter, called 'Explanation of the Gāyatrī Rite,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section, of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:

children.text: navamyādau yajeddurgāṃ hrīṃ durge rakṣiṇīti ca
children.translated_text: Beginning with the ninth day, one should worship <s>Durgā</s> with 'hrīṃ, O <s>Durgā</s>, protectress.'
O mother, mother, excellent <s>Durgā</s>, accomplisher of every desired aim,
by this offering of bali, grant me all desires.

children.text: gaurī kālī umā durgā bhadrā kāntiḥ sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Umā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: maṅgalā vijayā lakṣmīḥ śivā nārāyaṇī kramāt
children.translated_text: <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Vijayā</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, in order.
Beginning with the third day in Mārgaśīrṣa, one should worship, and he will not suffer separation.
One should visualize her as eighteen-armed, with shield, bell, mirror, and threatening finger,
with bow, banner, drum, axe, and noose,
with spear, club, tridents, skull, arrows, and goads,

children.text: vajraṃ cakraṃ śalākāṃ ca aṣṭādaśabhujāṃ smaret ||
children.translated_text: and with thunderbolt, discus, and rod; one should remember her as eighteen-armed.
I shall teach the mantra of the glorious <s>Bhagavatī</s>, along with recitation and the rest.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavati cāmuṇḍe śmaśānavāsini kapālahaste mahāpretasamārūḍhe mahāvimānamālākule kālarātri bahugaṇaparivṛte mahāmukhe bahubhuje sughaṇṭāḍamarukiṅkiṇīke aṭṭāṭṭahāse kilikili huṃ sarvanādaśabdabahule gajacarmaprāvṛtaśarīre rudhiramāṃsadigdhe lolagrajihve mahārākṣasi raudradaṃṣṭrākarāle bhīmāṭṭāṭṭahāse sphuritavidyutsamaprabhe cala cala karālanetre hilihili lalajjihve hraiṃ hrīṃ bhṛkuṭimukhi oṃ kārabhadrāsane kapālamālāveṣṭite jaṭāmukuṭaśaśāṅkadhāriṇi aṭṭāṭṭahāse kilikili huṃhuṃ daṃṣṭrāghorāndhakāriṇi sarvavighnavināśini idaṃ karma sādhaya sādhaya śīghraṃ kuru kuru kaha kaha aṅkuśe samanupraveśaya vargaṃ vargaṃ kampaya kampaya cala cala cālaya cālaya rudhiramāṃsamadyapriye hana hana kuṭṭa kuṭṭa chinda chinda māraya māraya anubūma anubūma vajraśarīraṃ sādhaya sādhaya trailokyagatamapi duṣṭamaduṣṭaṃ vā gṛhītamagṛhītam āveśaya āveśaya krāmaya krāmaya nṛtya nṛtya bandha bandha valga valga koṭarākṣi ūrdhvakeśi ulūkavadane karakiṅkiṇi karaṅkamālādhāriṇi daha daha paca paca gṛhṇa gṛhṇa maṇḍalamadhye praveśaya praveśaya kiṃ vilambasi brahmasatyena viṣṇusatyena ṛṣisatyena rudrasatyena āveśaya āveśaya kilikili khili khili mili mili cili cili vikṛtarūpadhāriṇi kṛṣṇabhujaṅga veṣṭitaśarīra sarvagrahāveśini pralambhoṣṭhi bhrūmagnanāsike vikaṭamukhi kapilajaṭe brāhmi bhañja bhañja jvala jvala kālamukhi khala khala kharakharaḥ pātaya pātaya raktākṣi dhūrṇāpaya dhūrṇāpaya bhūmiṃ pātaya pātaya śiro gṛhṇa gṛhṇa cakṣur mīlaya mīlaya bhañja bhañja pādau gṛhṇa gṛhṇa mudrāṃ sphoṭaya sphoṭaya huṃ hūṃ phaṭ vidāraya vidāraya triśūlena bhedaya bhedaya vajreṇa
children.translated_text: Om. Homage to the blessed <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>: O dweller in the cremation ground, skull in hand, mounted on a great corpse, thronged by garlands of great aerial cars; O <s>Kālarātri</s>, surrounded by many hosts, great-mouthed, many-armed, with fine bells, ḍamarus, and tinkling ornaments; O you of repeated loud laughter, kilikili, huṃ, rich in every roar and sound, your body covered with elephant-hide, smeared with blood and flesh, with a lolling tongue, great rākṣasī, terrible with fierce fangs, frightening with repeated loud laughter, flashing like quivering lightning: move, move; O you of dreadful eyes, hili hili, with dangling tongue, hraiṃ hrīṃ, frowning-faced one; Om, seated on the auspicious seat of kāra, encircled by a garland of skulls, bearing matted hair, crown, and moon, laughing aṭṭāṭṭa, kilikili, huṃ huṃ; O you whose fangs make a dreadful darkness, destroyer of all obstacles, accomplish this rite, accomplish it; do it quickly, do it; kaha kaha. O goad, cause the group to enter completely; shake group after group; move, move; impel, impel. O lover of blood, flesh, and liquor, strike, strike; pound, pound; cut, cut; kill, kill; anubūma, anubūma. Accomplish the adamantine body, accomplish it. Whether the evil one or the non-evil one, whether seized or not seized, even if he has gone through the three worlds, possess him, possess him; make him advance, make him advance; dance, dance; bind, bind; leap, leap. O hollow-eyed one, upward-haired one, owl-faced one, with tinkling hands, wearing a garland of skeletons, burn, burn; cook, cook; seize, seize; make him enter the middle of the maṇḍala, make him enter. Why do you delay? By the truth of <s>Brahmā</s>, by the truth of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, by the truth of the seers, by the truth of <s>Rudra</s>, possess him, possess him. Kilikili, khili khili, mili mili, cili cili. O bearer of a distorted form, your body encircled by black serpents, possessor of all grahas, long-lipped one, with nose sunk between the brows, misshapen-faced one, tawny-matted one, O <s>Brāhmī</s>, break, break; blaze, blaze; black-faced one, khala khala kharakharaḥ.
