Cast down, cast down; red-eyed one, make him reel, make him reel; cast him to the ground, cast him down; seize the head, seize it; close the eyes, close them; break, break; seize the feet, seize them; burst the seal, burst it. Huṃ hūṃ phaṭ. Split, split; pierce with the trident, pierce; with the thunderbolt

children.text: hana hana daṇḍena tāḍaya tāḍaya cakreṇa chedaya chedaya śaktinā bhedaya bhedaya daṃṣṭrayā daṃśaya daṃśaya kīlakena kīlaya kīlaya kartārikayā pāṭaya pāṭaya aṅkuśena gṛhṇa gṛhṇa brahmāṇi ehi ehi māheśvari ehi ehi kaumāri ehi ehi vārāhi ehi ehi
children.translated_text: strike, strike; beat with the staff, beat; cut with the discus, cut; pierce with the spear, pierce; bite with the fang, bite; fasten with the peg, fasten; split with the knife, split; seize with the goad, seize. O <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, come, come; O <s>Māheśvarī</s>, come, come; O <s>Kaumārī</s>, come, come; O <s>Vārāhī</s>, come, come;

children.text: aindri ehi ehi cāmuṇḍe ehi ehi vaiṣṇavi ehi ehi himavantacāriṇi ehi ehi kailāsavāriṇi ehi ehi paramantraṃ chinddhi chinddhi kilikili bimbe aghore ghorarūpiṇi cāmuṇḍe rurukrodhāndhaviniḥsṛte asurakṣayaṅkari ākāśagāmini pāśena bandha bandha samaye tiṣṭha tiṣṭha maṇḍalaṃ praveśaya praveśaya pātaya pātaya gṛhṇa gṛhṇa mukhaṃ bandha bandha cakṣur bandhaya bandhaya hṛdayaṃ bandha bandha hastapādau ca bandha bandha duṣṭagrahān sarvān bandha bandha diśāṃ bandha bandha vidiśāṃ bandha bandha ūrdhvaṃ bandha bandha adhastād bandha bandha bhasmanā pānīyena mṛttikayā sarṣapairvā āveśaya āveśaya pātaya pātaya cāmuṇḍe kilikili vicche hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Aindrī</s>, come, come; O <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, come, come; O <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, come, come; O wanderer on <s>Himavant</s>, come, come; O wanderer on <s>Kailāsa</s>, come, come. Cut the hostile mantra, cut it. Kilikili, O image, O non-terrible one, terrible-formed one, O <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, issued forth from the blind rage of <s>Ruru</s>, destroyer of asuras, sky-goer: bind with the noose, bind; stand at the appointed time, stand; make him enter the maṇḍala, make him enter; cast him down, cast him down; seize, seize; bind the mouth, bind; bind the eye, bind; bind the heart, bind; bind the hands and feet, bind; bind all evil grahas, bind; bind the directions, bind; bind the intermediate directions, bind; bind above, bind; bind below. With ash, water, earth, or mustard seeds, possess, possess; cast down, cast down. O <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, kilikili vicche hrīṃ phaṭ svāhā.
Indeed, the sequence of one hundred and eight words is a mantra-made japa.
For each individual word there should be eight thousand repetitions; for the homa, eight thousand sesame seeds smeared with the three sweets are offered.

children.text: mahāmāṃsena trimadhurāktena aṣṭottarasahasraṃ ca ekaikaṃ ca padaṃ yajet
children.translated_text: With great meat smeared with the three sweets, he should also sacrifice each individual word one thousand and eight times.
And he should offer in homa one thousand and eight sesame seeds smeared with the three sweets.
Or, with great meat and the three sweets, it is effective for every ritual act.
By scattering water, mustard seeds, ash, and the like, there is victory in battle and similar undertakings.
She should be meditated upon as twenty-eight-armed, or else as eighteen-armed;
or she may be meditated upon as twelve-armed, eight-armed, or even four-armed.
Two hands are furnished with sword and shield; another pair with mace and staff;
another pair with arrow and bow; another pair furnished with sword and mudgara;
another pair with khaṅkha and bell; another pair with banner and staff;
another pair rich with axe and discus; another furnished with ḍamaru and mirror;
another pair holding a spear; another furnished with raṭoṇī and pestle;
another pair joined with noose and tomara; another joined with ḍhakkā and paṇava drums;
with one further hand she threatens, and with another she makes a tumultuous sound;
and there are hands showing fearlessness, svastika, and the like. She is the slayer of <s>Mahiṣa</s> and rides a lion.
Victory to you, indeed, O mistress of beings, surrounded by all beings.

children.text: rakṣa māṃ nijabhūtebhyo baliṃ gṛhṇa namo 'stu te ||
children.translated_text: Protect me from your own beings; accept the bali. Homage to you.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe durgājapapūjābalimantranirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭatriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the thirty-eighth chapter, called 'The Exposition of the Mantras for Durgā-japa, Worship, and Bali,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
Tell me again, in brief, the worship of the gods, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
bestowing enjoyment and liberation through <s>Sūrya</s>, whose form is <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> said:

children.text: śṛṇu sūryasya rudra tvaṃ punarvakṣyāmi pūjanam
children.translated_text: Listen, O <s>Rudra</s>; I shall again explain the worship of <s>Sūrya</s>.

children.text: oṃ uccaiḥśravase namaḥ oṃ aruṇāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to <s>Uccaiḥśravas</s>. Oṃ, homage to <s>Aruṇa</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the staff-bearing one.
Oṃ, homage to the tawny one.

children.text: ete dvāre prapūjyā vai ebhir mantrair vṛṣadhvaja ||
children.translated_text: These are indeed to be worshipped at the doorway with these mantras, O bull-bannered one.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Prabhūta</s>.
In the middle he should worship this one called <s>Prabhūta</s> and <s>Amala</s>.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Vimalā</s>.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Sārā</s>.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Ādhārā</s>.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Paramamukhā</s>.
Thus <s>Vimalā</s> and the others are indeed to be worshipped in the corners beginning with the southeast.
Oṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ, homage to the pericarp.

children.text: madhye tu pūjayedrudra pūrvādiṣu tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: In the middle he should worship, O <s>Rudra</s>, and likewise in the eastern and other directions.
He should worship <s>Dīptā</s> and the others in the middle, and should worship those facing everywhere.
Oṃ vāṃ, homage to <s>Dīptā</s>.
Oṃ vīṃ, homage to <s>Sūkṣmā</s>.
Oṃ vūṃ aurūṃ, homage to <s>Bhadrā</s>.
Oṃ vaiṃ, homage to <s>Jayā</s>.
Oṃ vauṃ, homage to <s>Vibhūti</s>.
Oṃ vaṃ, homage to <s>Aghorā</s>.
Oṃ vaṃ, homage to <s>Vaidyutā</s>.
Oṃ vaḥ, homage to <s>Vijayā</s>.
Oṃ ro, homage to <s>Sarvatomukhī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to the seat of <s>Arka</s>.
Oṃ hrāṃ, homage to the image of <s>Sūrya</s>.
He should worship these in the middle; now listen to the heart-mantras, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.

children.text: oṃ haṃ saṃ khaṃ khakholkāya krāṃ krīṃ saḥ svāhā sūryamūrtaye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ haṃ saṃ khaṃ, to <s>Khakholka</s>, krāṃ krīṃ saḥ svāhā; homage to the image of <s>Sūrya</s>.
With this he should perform the invocation, the installation, and the making-present.
And with the mantra of close establishment he should perform the making-whole.

children.text: mudrāyā darśanaṃ rudra mūlamantreṇa vā hara
children.translated_text: The display of the mudrā, O <s>Rudra</s>, may be done with the root mantra, O <s>Hara</s>.
He should meditate on him as having the form of splendor, red in color, standing upon a white lotus,
mounted on a chariot with one wheel, two-armed, and holding a lotus.

children.text: evaṃ dhyāyetsadā sūryaṃ mūlamantraṃ śṛṇuṣva ca
children.translated_text: Thus he should always meditate on <s>Sūrya</s>; now listen to the root mantra:

children.text: oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ sūryāya namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Oṃ hrāṃ hrīṃ saḥ, homage to <s>Sūrya</s>.
Three times he should display the lotus mudrā and the disk mudrā.
Oṃ āṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ, svāhā to the head as <s>Arka</s>.

children.text: oṃ aḥ bhūrbhuvaḥ svaḥ jvālini śikhāyai vaṣaṭ
children.translated_text: Oṃ aḥ, bhūr bhuvaḥ svaḥ, jvālini, vaṣaṭ to the topknot.
Oṃ huṃ, huṃ to the armor.
Oṃ bhāṃ, vauṣaṭ to the two eyes.
Oṃ vaḥ, phaṭ to the weapon.
He should worship in the southeast, or in the northeast, or in the southwest, O <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: hṛdayādi hi vāyavyāṃ netraṃ cāntaḥ prapūjayet ||
children.translated_text: The heart and the rest are to be worshipped in the northwest, and the eye within.
He should worship the weapon of the directions, O <s>Rudra</s>, and <s>Soma</s>, white in color.
On the eastern petal he should worship <s>Budha</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, shining like gold.
To the south he should worship, O <s>Rudra</s>; he should honor <s>Guru</s> with a yellow color.

children.text: paścime caiva bhūteśaṃ uttare bhārgavaṃ sitam ||
children.translated_text: In the west he should worship <s>Bhūteśa</s>, and in the north the white <s>Bhārgava</s>.
He should also worship the red <s>Aṅgāraka</s> in the southeast, O <s>Hara</s>.
He should worship black-colored <s>Śanaiścara</s> in the southwestern direction.
He should worship <s>Rāhu</s> in the northwestern region, O <s>Hara</s>, resembling the nandyāvarta.
And in the northeast he should fully worship smoke-colored <s>Ketu</s>.
With these mantras, O <s>Mahādeva</s>; listen to them, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Oṃ soṃ, homage to <s>Soma</s>.
Oṃ buṃ, homage to <s>Budha</s>.
Oṃ bṛṃ, homage to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.
Oṃ bhaṃ, homage to <s>Bhārgava</s>.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to <s>Aṅgāraka</s>.
Oṃ śaṃ, homage to <s>Śanaiścara</s>.
Oṃ raṃ, homage to <s>Rāhu</s>.
Oṃ kaṃ, homage to <s>Ketu</s>.
Having given the pādya and other offerings to <s>Sūrya</s> with the root mantra, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
at the end of the food offering the best of practitioners should display the cow mudrā.

children.text: japtvā cāṣṭasahasraṃ tu tacca tasmai samarpayet
children.translated_text: Having recited eight thousand times, he should offer that to him.

children.text: aiśānyāṃ diśi bhūteśa tejaścaṇḍaṃ tu pūjayet ||
children.translated_text: In the northeastern direction, O <s>Bhūteśa</s>, he should worship fierce splendor.

children.text: oṃ tejaścaṇḍāya huṃ phaṭ svadhā svāhā pauṣaṭ
children.translated_text: Oṃ, to <s>Tejaścaṇḍa</s>, huṃ phaṭ svadhā svāhā pauṣaṭ.
He should offer the remainder of the worship to him, and then give the arghya, O <s>Hara</s>.
It should be mixed with sesame and rice, smeared with red sandalwood,
combined with fragrant water, and accompanied by flowers and incense.
Having placed that vessel on his head, he should go down to the ground on his knees.
He should give the arghya to <s>Sūrya</s> with the heart-mantra, O bull-bannered one.
Then, having worshipped the gaṇa and the gurus, he should worship all the gods.
Oṃ gaṃ, homage to <s>Gaṇapati</s>.
Oṃ aṃ, homage to the gurus.
The worship of <s>Sūrya</s> has been told; having performed it, one becomes a partaker of the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sūryārcanaprakāro nāmaikonacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part of the early section, in the section on conduct, the thirty-ninth chapter, named 'The Procedure for the Worship of <s>Sūrya</s>'.
<s>Śaṅkara</s> said:

children.text: māheśvarīṃ ca me pūjāṃ vada śaṅkhagadādhara
children.translated_text: Tell me also the Māheśvarī worship, O bearer of conch and mace,

children.text: yāṃ jñātvā mānavāḥ siddhiṃ gacchanti parameśvara ||
children.translated_text: knowing which human beings attain accomplishment, O supreme lord.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Listen to the Māheśvarī worship as it is being taught, O bull-bannered one.

children.text: ādau snātvā tathācamya hyāsane copaviśya ca ||
children.translated_text: At first, having bathed and then sipped water, he should sit upon the seat.

children.text: nyāsaṃ kṛtvā maṇḍale vai pūjayecca maheśvaram
children.translated_text: Having performed nyāsa in the maṇḍala, he should worship <s>Maheśvara</s>,
<s>Hara</s>, accompanied by his retinue, with these mantras, O <s>Maheśāna</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ; let the deities of <s>Śiva</s>'s seat come.
With this, O <s>Rudra</s>, he should invoke the deities who belong to the seat.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Gaṇapati</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Nandin</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Mahākāla</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Mahākalā</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the weapon.
These are indeed to be worshipped at the doorway with bathing, fragrance, and the other offerings, O <s>Hara</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of the dwelling-place.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the gurus.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Ādhāraśakti</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Dharma</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to knowledge.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to dispassion.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to lordly power.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to adharma.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to ignorance.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to lack of dispassion.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to lack of lordly power.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Ūrdhvacchanda</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Adhaśchanda</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the lotus.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the pericarp.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Vāmā</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Raudrī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Kālī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Kalavikaraṇī</s>.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Balapramathinī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Sarvabhūtadamanī</s>, subduer of all beings.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Manonmanī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the triad of maṇḍalas.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ hauṃ haṃ śivamūrtaye namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ hauṃ haṃ, homage to <s>Śivamūrti</s>, the form of <s>Śiva</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the lord of knowledge.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hauṃ śivāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hauṃ, homage to <s>Śiva</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the heart.
Oṃ, homage to the head.
Oṃ hūṃ, homage to the topknot.
Oṃ haiṃ, homage to the armor.
Oṃ hauṃ, homage to the three eyes.
Oṃ haḥ, homage to the weapon.
Oṃ, homage to <s>Sadyojāta</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to accomplishment.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to prosperity.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Vidyutā</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Lakṣmī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to awakening.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Kālī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Svadhā</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to radiance.

children.text: satyasyāṣṭau kalā jñeyāḥ pūjyāḥ pūrvādiṣu sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The eight kalās of <s>Satya</s> should be known; they should be worshipped as stationed in the east and the other directions.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Vāmadeva</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to rajas.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to protection.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to delight.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the maiden.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to desire.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the mother.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to ritual action.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to increase.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to what is to be done.
Oṃ, homage to night.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the roaming one.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the enchantress.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the perishable one.
The kalās of <s>Vāmadeva</s> should be known as thirteen, O bull-bannered one.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to withdrawal.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to establishment.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to knowledge.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to peace.
These four should be known as belonging to <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> himself, O bull-bannered one.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to thirst.
The set of six kalās of <s>Aghora</s>, terrible in form, should indeed be known, O <s>Hara</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Samiti</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Aṅgadā</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the dark one.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Marīcī</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the flame.
Know the five kalās of <s>Īśāna</s>, O bull-bannered one.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to the retinue of <s>Śiva</s>.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Indra</s>, lord of the gods.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Agni</s>, lord of brilliance.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Yama</s>, lord of the departed.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Nirṛti</s>, lord of the rākṣasas.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Varuṇa</s>, lord of the waters.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Vāyu</s>, lord of breath.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Soma</s>, lord of the eyes.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Īśāna</s>, lord of all knowledge.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Ananta</s>, lord of the nāgas.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Brahmā</s>, lord of all worlds.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to <s>Dhūlicaṇḍeśvara</s>.
Invocation, installation, and bringing into presence, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>,
and likewise he should perform confinement and making-whole.

children.text: tattvanyāsaṃ ca mudrāyā darśanaṃ dyānameva ca
children.translated_text: Also the <s>tattvanyāsa</s> (installation of principles), the showing of <s>mudrā</s> gestures, and meditation,
water for the feet, sipping water, arghya, flowers, and the gift of anointing,
then rubbing, bathing, perfume, and fragrant unguent,
garments, ornaments, and enjoyments, and also <s>aṅganyāsa</s> and incense,
a lamp and the giving of food offering, and the rubbing of the hands,
water for the feet, arghya, sipping water, fragrance, betel, singing, and instrumental music,
dance, the provision of a parasol and the like, and the showing of <s>mudrā</s> gestures,

children.text: rūpaṃ dhyānaṃ japaṃ cātha ekavadbhāva eva ca ||
children.translated_text: form, meditation, recitation, and then the state of becoming one,
with the root mantra he should indeed make the offering of recitation and worship.
The <s>Māheśī</s> worship has been taught, O <s>Rudra</s>, destroying sin.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe maheśvarapūjāvidhirnāma catvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part called the earlier section, in the section on conduct, the fortieth chapter, named 'The Procedure for the Worship of <s>Maheśvara</s>'.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> said:

children.text: oṃ viśvāvasurnāma gandharvaḥ kanyānāmadhipatirlabhāmi te kanyāṃ samutpādya tasmai viśvāvasave svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ: the gandharva named <s>Viśvāvasu</s> is the lord of maidens. I obtain your maiden; having brought forth a maiden for him, svāhā to that <s>Viśvāvasu</s>.
The obtaining of a woman comes from mantra-recitation; now I shall teach <s>Kālarātrī</s>.

children.text: oṃ namo bhagavati ṛkṣakarṇi caturbhuje ūrdhvakeśi trinayane kālarātri mānuṣāṇāṃ vasārudhirabhojane amukasya prāptakālasya mṛtyuprade huṃ phaṭ hana hana daha daha māṃsarudhiraṃ paca paca ṛkṣapatni svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage to the blessed <s>Ṛkṣakarṇī</s>, four-armed, with hair raised upward, three-eyed, O <s>Kālarātrī</s>, eater of human fat and blood, giver of death to so-and-so whose time has come: huṃ phaṭ, strike, strike, burn, burn, cook flesh and blood, O wife of <s>Ṛkṣa</s>, svāhā.

children.text: na tithirna ca nakṣatraṃ nopavāso vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: No lunar day, no asterism, and no fasting is prescribed.

children.text: kruddho raktena saṃmārjya karau tābhyāṃ pragṛhya ca
children.translated_text: When angry, having smeared both hands with blood and then grasped with them,
at twilight he should recite at the liṅga, and he should destroy the unbaked vessel.

children.text: oṃ namaḥ sarvatoyantrāṇyetadyathā jambhani mohani sarvaśatruvidāriṇi rakṣa rakṣa māmamukaṃ sarvabhayopadravebhyaḥ svāhā
children.translated_text: Oṃ, homage. On every side are these yantras: thus, O Stupefier, O Bewilderer, O splitter of all enemies, protect, protect me, so-and-so, from all fears and calamities, svāhā.
When Śukra is lost, O <s>Mahādeva</s>, I shall explain it here, O twice-born one.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vaśyādisādhikamantranirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-first chapter, called 'The Explanation of Mantras Accomplishing Subjugation and the Like,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall explain the offering of the pavitra for <s>Śiva</s>, which destroys what is inauspicious.
The ācārya, the sādhaka, the putraka, or the samayin should perform it, O <s>Hara</s>.
Otherwise <s>Vighneśa</s> takes away the worship performed over the year.
One should do it in Āṣāḍha, Śrāvaṇa, Māgha, or also in Bhādrapada.
The thread should be known, in order, as made of gold, silver, copper, or cotton.

children.text: jñeyaṃ kujādau saṃgrāhyaṃ kanyayā kartitaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: It is to be gathered beginning on Tuesday and cut by a maiden.
Having made it threefold and tripled, he should then make the pavitra.
The knots are made with the <s>Vāmadeva</s> mantra; with the Satya mantra one should wash it, O <s>Śiva</s>.
It should be purified with the Aghora mantra, and bound with the <s>Tatpuruṣa</s> mantra.
He should fumigate it with the Īśa mantra; these are remembered as the deities of the threads.
The syllable oṃ, the Moon, Fire, <s>Brahmā</s>, the serpent, <s>Śikhidhvaja</s>,
the Sun, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> are said to be the deities in the threads, in order.
One should make one hundred and eight, fifty, or twenty-five.

children.text: rudro 'ttamādi vijñeyaṃ mānaṃ ca granthayo daśa ||
children.translated_text: The Rudra and the excellent and other measures are to be known; the knots are ten.
The knots should be four fingers apart, and their names, in order, are these:
Prakṛti, Pauruṣī, Vīrā, and fourth Aparājitā,

children.text: jayā ca vijayā rudrā ajitā ca sadāśivā
children.translated_text: Jayā, Vijayā, Rudrā, Ajitā, and Sadāśivā,
Manonmanī and Sarvamukhī; or the spacing may be two fingers or one finger.
He should color it with saffron and the like, and make the pavitra with fragrant substances.
On the seventh or thirteenth lunar day, in the bright fortnight or likewise in the other one,
he should bathe the liṅga with milk and the like and worship it with perfumes and other offerings.
He should offer the fragrant pavitra to himself and to <s>Brahmā</s>, O <s>Hara</s>.
With the root mantra, he should offer a flower together with perfume in the region of Īśāna.

children.text: pūrve ca daṇḍakāṣṭhaṃ tu uttare cāmalakīphalam ||
children.translated_text: In the east he should place a tooth-stick, and in the north an āmalakī fruit.
In the west he should place clay; in the south, ash for the beings.
In the southwest he should place aguru with the śikhā mantra, being one who knows the mantra.
In the northwest he should place mustard seed with the kavaca mantra, O Bull-bannered one.
Having encircled the house with thread, he should offer the fragrant pavitra.

children.text: homaṃ kṛtvā gneya dattvā dadyādbhūtabaliṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Having performed the homa and given the fire-offering, he should likewise offer bali to the beings.
'You have been invited, O lord of gods, O <s>Maheśvara</s>, together with your hosts.
In the morning I shall worship you; remain present here.'
Having invited him with this, he should stay there at night, performing singing and the like.
He should place the consecrated pavitras beside the deity.
Having bathed, on the fourteenth day he should first worship the Sun and then <s>Rudra</s>.
Having meditated on the universal form situated on the forehead, he should worship himself.
When they have thus been sprinkled with the astra mantra and then worshiped with the hṛdaya mantra,
he should offer them, consecrated with the saṃhitā mantra and fumigated.
First he should worship that which consists of Śiva-tattva, then that which consists of Vidyā-tattva,
afterwards that which consists of Ātma-tattva, and then that called Devaka.
Oṃ hauṃ hauṃ, homage to Śiva-tattva.
Oṃ hīṃ, homage to Vidyā-tattva.
Oṃ hāṃ, homage to Ātma-tattva.

children.text: oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ kṣaiṃ sarvatattvāya namaḥ
children.translated_text: Oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ kṣaiṃ, homage to Sarva-tattva.

children.text: kālātmanā tvayā deva yaddṛṣṭaṃ māmake vidhau ||
children.translated_text: 'O god, whatever has been observed by you, whose nature is Time, in my rite,

children.text: kṛtaṃ kliṣṭaṃ samutsṛṣṭaṃ hutaṃ guptaṃ ca yatkṛtam
children.translated_text: whatever has been done, done with difficulty, abandoned, offered, protected, or otherwise performed,
O <s>Śambhu</s>, by yourself as the Self of all, through the pavitra and by your will,

children.text: pūraya pūraya makhavrataṃ tanniyameśvarāya sarvatattvātmakāya sarvakāraṇapālitāya oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ śivāya namaḥ ||
children.translated_text: fill, fill that sacrificial observance for the lord of its rules, for the one whose nature is all tattvas, for the protector of all causes. Oṃ hāṃ hīṃ hūṃ haiṃ hauṃ, homage to <s>Śiva</s>.'
With this preceding formula one should offer the set of four pavitras.

children.text: dattvā vahneḥ pavitraṃ ca gurave dakṣiṇāṃ diśet ||
children.translated_text: Having offered a pavitra to the fire, he should assign a fee to the guru.

children.text: baliṃ dattvā dvijān bhojya caṇḍaṃ prācyai visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: Having given bali and fed the Brahmins, he should dismiss <s>Caṇḍa</s> toward the east.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śivapavitrāropaṇaṃ nāma dvicatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-second chapter, called 'The Offering of the Pavitra for Śiva,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall explain the offering of the pavitra for <s>Hari</s>, which grants enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: purā devāsure yuddhe brahmādyāḥ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Long ago, in the war between the gods and the asuras, <s>Brahmā</s> and the others sought refuge.

children.text: viṣṇuśca teṣāṃ devānāṃ dhvajaṃ graiveyakaṃ dadau
children.translated_text: Then <s>Viṣṇu</s> gave those gods a banner in the form of a neck-ornament.
'On seeing these two, the Dānavas will perish,' <s>Hari</s> said.
When <s>Viṣṇu</s> had spoken, the serpent who was <s>Vāsuki</s>'s younger brother then said,

children.text: vṛṇīta ca pavitrākhyaṃ varaṃ cedaṃ vṛṣadhvaja ||
children.translated_text: 'Choose the boon called pavitra, if this is a boon, O Bull-bannered one.
The neck-ornament given by <s>Hari</s> will become famous by my name.'

children.text: ityukte tena te devāstannāmnā tadvaraṃ viduḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he had spoken thus, the gods understood that boon by that name.

children.text: prāvṛṭkāle tu ye martyā nārciṣyanti pavitrakaiḥ
children.translated_text: Those mortals who do not worship with pavitras in the rainy season

children.text: teṣāṃ sāṃvatsarī pūjā viphalā ca bhaviṣyati ||
children.translated_text: will have their yearly worship become fruitless.
Therefore, for all the gods, the offering of the pavitra should be done in order,
from the first lunar day through the full moon, on whatever lunar day is prescribed for each.

children.text: dvādaśyāṃ viṣṇave kāryaṃ śukle kṛṣṇe 'thavā hara
children.translated_text: For <s>Viṣṇu</s> it should be performed on the twelfth day, in either the bright or dark fortnight, O <s>Hara</s>,
at the vyatīpāta, at a solstice, and at an eclipse of the moon or sun, O <s>Śiva</s>.
It is also prescribed for <s>Viṣṇu</s> in rites for increase and when the guru arrives.
The pavitra is prescribed always, but in the rainy season it is obligatory.

children.text: kauśeyaṃ paṭṭasūtraṃ vā kārpāsaṃ kṣaumameva vā
children.translated_text: It may be of silk, paṭṭa-thread, cotton, linen, or kuśa-thread.
For Brahmins it should be kuśa-thread; for kings, silk and paṭṭa.
For Vaiśyas it should be cīraṇa cloth or linen; for Śūdras, fiber made from hemp bark.
Cotton and lotus-born fiber too are praised for all, O Lord.
The thread should be spun by a Brahmin woman, made of three strands and tripled.

children.text: oṃkāro 'tha śivaḥ somo hyagnir brahmā phaṇī raviḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Oṃkāra</s>, then <s>Śiva</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Agni</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, the serpent, and the sun,
<s>Vighneśa</s> and <s>Viṣṇu</s>: these are the deities stationed in the threads.

children.text: brahmā viṣṇuśca rudraśca trisūtre devatāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, and <s>Rudra</s> are remembered as the deities in the three-threaded cord.

children.text: sauvarṇe rājate tāmre vaiṇave mṛnmaye nyaset
children.translated_text: One should set it in a gold, silver, copper, bamboo, or earthen vessel.
Measured by the thumb, sixty-four is the best; half of that is the middle measure.

children.text: tadardhā tu kaniṣṭhā syāt sūtram aṣṭottaraṃ śatam
children.translated_text: Half of that again is the lowest; the thread may also be one hundred and eight.
The superior, middle, and inferior forms should be understood in that order, as before.
The superior is by the measure of the thumb, while the middle is by the middle finger.

children.text: kanyase ca kaniṣṭhena aṅgulyā granthayaḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For the inferior form the knots are remembered as being measured by the little finger.
For a shrine and for an altar this is the general characteristic.

children.text: śivoddhṛtaṃ pavitraṃ tu pratimāyāṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: For an image one should make the <s>pavitra</s> thread as taken up for <s>Śiva</s>.
It should hang according to the measures of the heart, navel, and thigh, down to the knees.
With one thousand and eight, four knots are prescribed.
Or there may be thirty-six, twenty-four, or twelve knots.
They should be understood for the superior and the other grades, or the small <s>pavitra</s> may be made by sections.
It should be rubbed with saffron, or with turmeric and sandalwood.
Fasting, one should consecrate the <s>pavitra</s> while it is placed in a vessel.
It is set in packets of aśvattha leaves in the eight directions.

children.text: daṇḍakāṣṭhaṃ kuśāgraṃ ca pūrve saṅkarṣaṇena tu ||
children.translated_text: In the east, with <s>Saṅkarṣaṇa</s>, one should place the staff-wood and the tips of kuśa grass.
In the south, with <s>Pradyumna</s>, one should place yellow pigment and saffron.
In the west, with <s>Aniruddha</s>, it is for the sake of battle and for accomplishing the desired fruit.
Sandalwood mixed with blue pigment, and sesame, ash, and unbroken rice likewise,
should be placed in the corners beginning with the southeast, in the order of the seers and the rest.
One should consecrate the <s>pavitra</s> again and again with <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
Having looked upon it, worshiped it again, and carefully covered it with a cloth,
it should be placed before the deity, or before the image and maṇḍala.
In the west, south, north, and east, one should proceed in the same order as before.
One should also install <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, and worship the water jar.

children.text: astreṇa maṇḍalaṃ kṛtvā naivedyaṃ ca samarpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having made the maṇḍala with the weapon-mantra, one should offer the food offering.

children.text: adhivāsya pavitraṃ tu trisūtreṇa navena vā
children.translated_text: Having consecrated the <s>pavitra</s> with three threads or with nine,

children.text: vedikāṃ veṣṭayitvā tu ātmānaṃ kalaśaṃ ghṛtam ||
children.translated_text: one should encircle the altar, oneself, the jar, and the ghee,

children.text: agnikuṇḍaṃ vimānaṃ ca maṇḍapaṃ gṛhameva ca
children.translated_text: the fire-pit, the shrine, the pavilion, and the house itself.
Taking a single thread, one should place it on the head of the deity.
After placing it there, having worshiped <s>Maheśvara</s>, one should recite this mantra:
"You have been invoked, O lord of gods, O supreme Lord, for the sake of worship.
Tomorrow morning I shall worship you; be present together with the ritual materials."
After consecrating the <s>pavitraka</s> for one night or for three nights,

children.text: rātrau jāgaraṇaṃ kṛtvā prātaḥ sampūjya keśavam
children.translated_text: having kept vigil at night and worshiped <s>Keśava</s> in the morning,
one should place them on in order: the senior, the middle, and the lesser.
Having fumigated the <s>pavitra</s>, one should consecrate it with the mantra itself.
One should worship the knot empowered by recitation with flowers and the like.

children.text: gāyattryā cārcitaṃ tena devaṃ sampūjya dāpayet
children.translated_text: Having honored it with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, one should worship the deity and cause it to be given.
Together with sons, wife, and the others, one should hold the tail of the thread.
"Pure-knotted, beautiful, destroyer of great sins,
destroyer of all sin, O god, I wear you before you.
Having worshiped in this way with incense and the rest, one should offer the middle and the other ones.
"O <s>pavitra</s> of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, splendor that destroys every grave sin,
for the accomplishment of dharma, desire, and wealth, I wear you on my own neck."
Having worshiped the forest-garland, one should cause it to be given with its own mantra.
After offering various food offerings, one should present the bali with flowers and the like.
Having satisfied the fire there too, according to a measure of twelve aṅgulas,
one should give a single <s>pavitraka</s> with the one hundred and eight.
First, after giving arghya to the sun, one should give one <s>pavitraka</s> there.

children.text: viṣvaksenaṃ tataḥ prārcya surum arghyādibhir hara
children.translated_text: Then, having worshiped <s>Viṣvaksena</s>, and the god with arghya and the like, O <s>Hara</s>,
standing before the deity with cupped joined hands, one should recite the mantra:
"Whether knowingly or unknowingly, the worship and other rites have been performed by me.
May all that be complete through your favor, O lord of gods.
With garlands of jewels and coral, and with mandāra flowers and the like,
may this annual worship be yours, O <s>Garuḍadhvaja</s>.

children.text: vanamālā yathā deva kaustubhaṃ satataṃ hṛdi
children.translated_text: As the forest-garland, O god, and the <s>Kaustubha</s> are always on your heart,

children.text: tadvatpavitraṃ tantūnāṃ mālāṃ tvaṃ hṛdaye dhara ||
children.translated_text: so may you bear at your heart this <s>pavitra</s>, a garland of threads."

children.text: evaṃ prārthya dvijān bhojya dattvā tebhyaśca dakṣiṇām
children.translated_text: Having prayed thus, he should feed the Brahmins and give them a fee.
Then he should dismiss it that very evening, or on the following day.
"This annual worship has been properly accomplished by me.
Now, O <s>pavitraka</s>, having been dismissed, go to the world of <s>Viṣṇu</s>."

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣṇupavitrāropaṇaṃ nāma tricatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part called the earlier section, in the section on conduct, the forty-third chapter, named "The Installation of the <s>Viṣṇu-pavitra</s>."
<s>Hari</s> said:
Having worshiped Brahman with <s>pavitras</s> and the rest, and having meditated on Brahman, one becomes <s>Hari</s>.
I shall teach meditation on Brahman, which crushes the mechanism of māyā.
The wise man should restrain speech in the mind; he should worship that knowledge in the Self.
He should restrain knowledge in the Great one, if he desires knowledge in the Self.
It is free from body, senses, mind, intellect, vital breath, and ego-maker,
free from the elements and subtle elements, and from the guṇas, birth, eating, and the like.
That which is self-luminous, formless, and marked by giving, restraint, and the like,
eternal, pure, awakened, abundant, true, blissful, and nondual,
the fourth, imperishable <s>Brahman</s>, the supreme state: that am I.
Abiding in the thought, "I am <s>Brahman</s>," is also called <s>samādhi</s>.

children.text: ātmānaṃ rathinaṃ viddhi śarīraṃ rathameva tu
children.translated_text: Know the self as the rider in the chariot, and the body as the chariot itself.

children.text: buddhiṃ ca sārathiṃ viddhi manaḥ pragrahameva ca
children.translated_text: Know the intellect as the charioteer, and the mind as the reins.
They call the senses the horses, and the sense-objects their fields of movement.
Joined with self, senses, and mind, it is the enjoyer, so the wise say.
But he who is always joined with a mind guided by discriminating knowledge,

children.text: sa tu tatpadamāpnoti sa hi bhūyo na jāyate
children.translated_text: he reaches that state, and he is not born again.
But the man whose charioteer is knowledge and who has the mind as reins,
reaches the far shore of the heavenly stream, the supreme place of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
<s>Yama</s> is said to be non-violence and the rest; <s>niyama</s> is remembered as purity and the rest.
<s>Āsana</s> is connected with the lotus posture and so on; <s>prāṇāyāma</s> is the conquest of the winds.
<s>Pratyāhāra</s> is said to be mastery, and meditation is contemplation of the Lord.
Steadiness of mind is <s>dhāraṇā</s>, and <s>samādhi</s> is abiding in <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: pūrvaṃ cetaḥ sthiraṃ na syāttatomūrtiṃ vicintayet ||
children.translated_text: If at first the mind is not steady, then one should contemplate the image.
In the middle of the pericarp of the lotus of the heart, he bears conch, discus, mace, and lotus.
He is adorned with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s> and <s>Kaustubha</s>, and endowed with the beauty of the forest garland.
He is eternal, pure, endowed with power, called truth and bliss, supreme.

children.text: ātmāhaṃ paramaṃ brahma paramaṃ jyotireva tu ||
children.translated_text: I am the self, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, and also the supreme light.
He has twenty-four forms and abides in the <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone.
Established in stones such as those of <s>Dvārakā</s>, he is to be meditated on and worshiped; I too am he.
Having obtained what the mind desires, one becomes a god who travels in a celestial vehicle.
Free from desire, one obtains liberation while meditating on the image, praising it, and reciting.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe brahmamūrtidhyānanirūpaṇaṃ nāma catuścatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section called the first part, in the section on conduct, the forty-fourth chapter, named "Description of Meditation on the Form of <s>Brahman</s>."
<s>Hari</s> said:
In passing, I shall describe the characteristics of the <s>Śālagrāma</s>.
From touching a <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone comes the destruction of sins from ten million births.
Bearing conch, discus, mace, and lotus, he is <s>Gadādhara</s>.
The all-pervading one has lotus, <s>Kaumodakī</s> mace, discus, and conch.
With discus, conch, lotus, and mace, he is glorious <s>Gadādhara</s>.
Or, bearing mace, lotus, conch, and discus, <s>Gadādhara</s> is to be worshiped.
Homage to him whose emblems are lotus, conch, discus, and mace.
With conch, lotus, mace, and discus.
Homage also to the one joined with mace, discus, conch, and lotus.
The one with discus, <s>Kaumodakī</s>, lotus, and conch.
Homage to the one whose emblems are discus, lotus, conch, and mace.
Homage to the discus-bearer with lotus, mace, and conch.
With lotus, discus, mace, and conch,
O lotus-bearing one with conch, discus, and mace, homage in my mind.
Homage indeed to the one with discus, conch, mace, and lotus.
And homage to the one whose emblems are conch, lotus, discus, and mace.
To the holder of fine conch, fine mace, lotus, and discus,
homage to the bearer of mace, conch, lotus, and discus.
With lotus, conch, mace, and discus,
homage to the lotus-bearing one with mace, conch, and discus.
To the bearer of lotus, mace, conch, and discus,
homage to the one whose emblems are lotus, discus, conch, and mace.
To the one here with conch, discus, lotus, and mace,
homage in mind to the one with mace and discus, with lotus and conch.
To the one joined with fine discus, lotus, mace, and conch,
homage to the one with mace, lotus, discus, and conch.
A <s>Śālagrāma</s> stone bearing two joined discus-marks attached at the opening
and white in appearance: may that glorious <s>Gadādhara</s> protect you.
With two joined discus-marks, red in appearance, and full in the front part,
it is <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>; then the one with a subtle discus-mark is yellowish.
It is long, with an aperture like a head; the one that is round
is blue, with three lines at the opening, and then black.
With a line in the middle shaped like a mace and a very raised navel-disc,
broad-chested, tawny, and having three spots, may it protect you.
Or else it has five spots; its worship belongs to brahmacārins.
The power-marked <s>liṅga</s>, with two unequal discus-marks, may protect.
Blue, three-lined, and large; then the tortoise-form, marked with a spot,
round and spiral, with bowed back, may it protect you.
The five-lined one, marked with a mace, may protect.
Round or short, the <s>Rāmacakra</s>, lord of the gods.
Of many colors and many forms, serpent-hooded, it is <s>Anantaka</s>.
Thick and blue, <s>Dāmodara</s> is curved in the middle and very dark blue.
With a narrow opening, may he protect; then <s>Brahmā</s> is very red,
with a long line, hollow, broad, and having one discus and lotus.
With a broad opening and a large discus, black <s>Viṣṇu</s> is like a bilva fruit.
<s>Hayagrīva</s> is hook-shaped, five-lined, and marked with the <s>Kaustubha</s>.
<s>Vaikuṇṭha</s> has the appearance of jewels and gems, with one discus and lotus, and is black.
<s>Matsya</s> is long, lotus-shaped, and has a line at the opening; may he protect you.
The <s>Rāmacakra</s>, with a line on the right, is dark; may <s>Trivikrama</s> protect you.
Homage to the mace-bearer dwelling in the <s>Śālagrāma</s> at <s>Dvārakā</s>.
With one opening and four discus-marks, adorned with a forest garland,
endowed with golden lines and shining with a cow's-foot mark,
shaped like a kadamba flower, may <s>Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa</s> protect.
The one distinguished by a single mark, bearing mace and discus, may protect.
With two marks he is <s>Lakṣmīnārāyaṇa</s>; with three, the form <s>Trivikrama</s>.
With four he is <s>Caturvyūha</s>; with five, <s>Vāsudeva</s>.

children.text: pradyumnaḥ ṣaḍbhir eva syāt saṃkarṣaṇa itastataḥ
children.translated_text: With six he is <s>Pradyumna</s>; thereafter, <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>.
With eight he is <s>Puruṣottama</s>; with nine marks, <s>Navavyūha</s>.
With ten he is <s>Daśāvatāra</s>; then may <s>Aniruddha</s> protect.
The twelve-formed one is accompanied by the twelve; above that is <s>Anantaka</s>.

children.text: viṣṇormūrtimayaṃ stotraṃ yaḥ paṭhetsa divaṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Whoever recites this hymn made of the forms of <s>Viṣṇu</s> goes to heaven.
<s>Brahmā</s> is four-faced, bearing a staff and furnished with a pair of water-pots.
<s>Maheśvara</s> is five-faced, ten-armed, and has the bull as his banner.
He is furnished with his proper weapons; so too are <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Caṇḍikā</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>.
<s>Mahālakṣmī</s>, the Mothers, and <s>Divākara</s> with a lotus in his hand are also to be represented.
So too are the elephant-faced lord of hosts and <s>Skanda</s>, six-faced; their qualities are manifold.
When these have been worshipped and installed in a temple after the vāstu rite,
a man obtains <s>dharma</s> (religious merit), wealth, desire, liberation, and the other aims.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śālagrāmamūrtilakṣaṇaṃ nāma pañcacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section called the first part, in the section on conduct, the forty-fifth chapter, named 'The Characteristics of the <s>Śālagrāma</s> Images'.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall briefly explain vāstu, which removes obstacles in houses and the like.
Beginning from the northeast corner, one should worship in the eighty-one-square layout.

children.text: īśāne ca śiraḥ pādau nairṛte 'gnyanile karau
children.translated_text: The head is in the northeast, the feet in the southwest, and the hands in the quarters of <s>Agni</s> and <s>Anila</s>.
In dwellings, residences, houses, cities, villages, and merchants' streets,
and in temples, gardens, forts, shrines, and monasteries,
there are twenty-two gods outside, and inside those there are thirteen.
They are <s>Īśa</s>, then <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Jayanta</s>, and <s>Kuliśāyudha</s>.

children.text: sūryaḥ satyo bhṛguścaiva ākāśo vāyureva ca ||
children.translated_text: Then come <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Satya</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, <s>Ākāśa</s>, and <s>Vāyu</s>.
Then <s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Vitatha</s>, and both <s>Grahakṣetra</s> and <s>Yama</s>.
Then <s>Gandharva</s>, <s>Bhṛgurāja</s>, <s>Mṛga</s>, and the group of ancestors.
Then <s>Dauvārika</s>, <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Puṣpadanta</s>, and <s>Gaṇādhipa</s>.

children.text: asuraḥ śeṣapāpau ca rogo ḍahimukha eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Asura</s>, <s>Śeṣa</s>, <s>Pāpa</s>, <s>Roga</s>, and <s>Ḍahimukha</s>.
Then <s>Bhallāṭa</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Sarpa</s>, and likewise <s>Aditi</s> and <s>Diti</s>.
These thirty-two are outside; now hear the four who are within them.
A wise man should worship those placed in the four corners beginning with the northeast.
They are <s>Āpas</s>, <s>Sāvitrī</s>, <s>Jaya</s>, and likewise <s>Rudra</s>.

children.text: madhye navapade brahmā tasyāṣṭhau ca samīpagān
children.translated_text: In the nine squares at the center is <s>Brahmā</s>, and there are eight deities near him.
Hear these additional gods by name, beginning from the east.
They are <s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Savitṛ</s>, <s>Vivasvant</s>, and <s>Vibudhādhipa</s>.

children.text: mitro 'tha rājayakṣmā ca tathā pṛthvīdharaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: Then come <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Rājayakṣmā</s>, and <s>Pṛthvīdhara</s>, in sequence.

children.text: aṣṭamaś cāpavatsaś ca parito brahmaṇaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The eighth, <s>Apavatsa</s>, is remembered as standing around <s>Brahmā</s>.
Beginning from the northeast corner, the vaṃśa-line in a fort is described.
Beginning from the southeast corner, the vaṃśa-line becomes <s>Durdhara</s>.

children.text: aditiṃ himavantaṃ ca jayantaṃ ca idaṃ trayam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aditi</s>, <s>Himavant</s>, and <s>Jayanta</s>: these are the three.
The presiding female is named <s>Kālikā</s>; again, the reading concerning the line from <s>Śakra</s> to <s>Gandharva</s> is uncertain.
After worshipping the vāstu deities, one may become a builder of houses and temples.
A place for worship of the gods should be made in front, and the kitchen should be in the southeast.
At the passage called kapinirgamana, the sacrificial pavilion should be to the east.
The room for perfumes and flowers should be in the northeast and furnished with cloth or seats.

children.text: bhāṇḍāgāraṃ ca kauberyāṃ goṣṭhāgāraṃ ca vāyave ||
children.translated_text: The treasury should be in the quarter of <s>Kubera</s>, and the cow-house in the quarter of <s>Vāyu</s>.
The water reservoir should be in the quarter of <s>Varuṇa</s> and furnished with windows.
The place for kindling sticks, kuśa grass, fuel, and weapons should be in the southwest.
A guest house, pleasant and supplied with beds, seats, and sandals,
with water, fire, lamps, and good servants, should be on the southern side.
All the inner apartments should be arranged with water and plantain bowers,
and should be adorned with five-colored flowers.
Outside that, one should place an enclosure wall measuring five hastas.
In this way one should make an āśrama of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, furnished with woods and groves.
For a temple and the like, the vāstu of sixty-four squares is to be worshipped.
In the center <s>Brahmā</s> occupies four squares, while <s>Aryaman</s> and the others occupy two squares each.
In the corners, <s>Śikhī</s> and the other deities are likewise proclaimed.
On both sides of them there are also other gods occupying two-square places.
Thus the deities of the sixty-four-square layout have been proclaimed.

children.text: carakī ca vidārī ca pūtanā pāparākṣasī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Carakī</s>, <s>Vidārī</s>, <s>Pūtanā</s>, and the evil rākṣasī <s>Pāparākṣasī</s>,
beginning with the northeast, are outside; after them are deities such as <s>Hetuka</s>.
They are <s>Haituka</s>, <s>Tripurānta</s>, <s>Agni</s>, the two <s>Vetālas</s>, and <s>Yama</s>.
Then come <s>Agnijihva</s>, <s>Kālaka</s>, <s>Karāla</s>, and <s>Akapādaka</s>.
In the northeast is <s>Bhīmarūpa</s>; in the underworld is <s>Pretanāyaka</s>.
In the sky is <s>Gandhamālī</s>; after that one should worship the <s>Kṣetrapālas</s>.
One should multiply the width by the length and compute the rāśi of the vāstu.

children.text: kṛtvā ca vasubhir bhāgaṃ śeṣaṃ baddhāyam ādiśet
children.translated_text: Having divided it by the Vasus, that is, by eight, one should assign the remainder as the āya.
Again, having multiplied it by eight, one should divide the resulting portion.
Whatever the remainder is, that becomes the ṛkṣa; after division by the portions, it becomes the vyaya.
Having multiplied the ṛkṣa by four, it should be divided by nine.
The remainder should be known as the aṃśa, according to the opinion of <s>Devala</s>.
The total should be multiplied by eight and divided by sixty.
Whatever the remainder is, that becomes the life-span; the calculation of death is in the corrupt remainder of the verse.

children.text: vāstukroḍe gṛhaṃ kuryānna pṛṣṭhe mānavaḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: A man should always build the house in the lap of the vāstu, not on its back.
It sleeps on its left side; there is no need for deliberation about this.
In <s>Siṃha</s>, <s>Kanyā</s>, and <s>Tulā</s>, a doorway is purified when it faces north.
In the same way, beginning with <s>Vṛścika</s>, the directions are east, south, and west.
The doorway should have a width equal to half its length; eight kinds of doorways are remembered.
They concern progeny, servants, low status, one's own vehicle, and gold ornaments.

children.text: sutahīnaṃ tu raudreṇa vīryaghnaṃ dakṣiṇe tathā ||
children.translated_text: With the <s>Raudra</s> doorway there is sonlessness, and in the southern one there is loss of virility.
In the fiery one there is death; another gives increase of life, gain of sons, and full satisfaction.
In the quarter of <s>Dhanada</s> there is oppression by the king, loss of wealth, and in the water quarter disease.
There is fear from rulers, dead offspring, and indeed childlessness, but it does not produce enmity.
It gives wealth and also leads to loss of wealth; it gives faults and brings the death of a son.
Now I shall describe the doors known as northern, and the eastern doors.
Fear of fire, many daughters, wealth, honor, and anger arise from them.
In the east, the door has been declared, according to its result, to kill a king and to produce anger.
Beginning with the northeast there should be the east; beginning with the southeast, the south.
Beginning with the southwest there should be the west, and beginning with the northwest, the north.

children.text: aṣṭabhāge kṛte bhāge dvārāṇāṃ ca phalāphalam ||
children.translated_text: When the section is divided into eight parts, the good and bad effects of the doors are determined.
The aśvattha, plakṣa, nyagrodha, and udumbara trees should stand beginning from the east.

children.text: gṛhasya śobhanaḥ prokta īśāne caiva śālmaliḥ
children.translated_text: They are declared auspicious for a house; and in the northeast, the śālmali tree,
when worshiped, removes obstacles for both a prāsāda and a house.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vāstumānalakṣaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-sixth chapter, called 'The Characteristics of Vāstu Measurements,' in the Ācārakāṇḍa, known as the first section of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: prāsādānāṃ lakṣaṇaṃ ca vakṣye śaunaka tacchṛṇu
children.translated_text: I shall describe the characteristics of prāsādas, O <s>Śaunaka</s>; listen to that.
Having made a sixty-four-square plan, marked by the cardinal and intermediate directions,
it should be square, with four sides, and with doors according to the number of the suns.
The arrangement of the walls should consist of forty-eight parts.
The jaṅghā is equal to the upper field, and it should be twice half the jaṅghā.
The śukāṅghri is prescribed as extending across the breadth of the garbha.
It should be made as one third of that, or again as one fifth.
The projection of the śukāṅghri has a height reaching half the śikhara.
Having divided the śikhara into four parts, the vedibandha is set at the third part,
and in its fourth part its neck is established down to the base.
Or else, having made an equal vāstu and divided it into sixteen parts,

children.text: tasya madhye caturbhāgamādau garbhaṃ tu kārayet ||
children.translated_text: in its middle he should first make the garbha with four parts.
The height of the walls should measure four parts.
The height of the śikhara is measured as twice the height of the wall,
and the circumambulatory passages should be made from half of half the śikhara.

children.text: caturdikṣu tathā jñeyo nirgamastuḥ tathā budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: Likewise, the wise should understand the projection in the four directions.
The skilled man, dividing the measure of the garbha into five parts,

children.text: bhāgamekaṃ gṛhītvā tu nirgamaṃ kalpayet punaḥ
children.translated_text: should take one part and then arrange the projection.
In front, the mukha-maṇḍapa should be a part equal to the garbha-sūtra.
This has been stated as the general characteristic of a prāsāda.
Now I shall state the measure of the liṅga: the pīṭha should be equal to the liṅga.
The garbha should certainly be twice that on every side, O <s>Śaunaka</s>.

children.text: taddvidhā ca bhaved bhītir jaṅghā tadvistarārdhagā ||
children.translated_text: The wall should be twofold, and the jaṅghā should extend to half of its breadth.
The śikhara is said to be twice the jaṅghā, O <s>Śaunaka</s>.
The work enclosing the pīṭha and garbha is according to that measure, and so is the śukāṅghri.
The projection has been explained; the rest is just as before.
This is remembered as the measure of the liṅga; now the measure of the doorway is stated.
Having made the forepart like the Veda, the doorway should be one eighth part.
Its breadth has been stated; its height may be twice that, as desired.
As with the doorway, the remaining space in the middle of the pīṭha should be hollow.
The remaining wall is a quarter, since it is reckoned by half the doorway.
The jaṅghā is equal to that breadth, and the śikhara should be twice it.
The śukāṅghri should be understood as before, and the projection should have its proper height.
This is the measure for a maṇḍapa; I shall tell another form.
He should make a three-Veda field where the deities stand.
With the measure made in this way, extending out from the outer part,
the nemi, one quarter in breadth, surrounds the prāsāda on all sides.

children.text: garbhaṃ tu dviguṇaṃ kuryānnemyā mānaṃ bhavediha
children.translated_text: One should make the garbha twice that; here the measure is that of the nemi.

children.text: sa eva bhitter utsedhaḥ śikharo dviguṇo mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: That same measure is the height of the wall, and the śikhara is considered twice it.

children.text: prāsādānāṃ ca vakṣyāmi mānaṃ yoniṃ ca mānataḥ
children.translated_text: I shall now state the measurement and yoni, according to measure, of prāsādas.
<s>Vairāja</s>, the one called <s>Puṣpaka</s>, <s>Kailāsa</s>, and the one named <s>Mālikā</s>,
and <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>: these five prāsādas are the sources of all yonis.
The first is square; the second is elongated from that.
One is round, another is oblong-round, and the fifth here is octagonal.
From these very forms arise very beautiful prāsādas.
From all those primary forms, forty types arise in just this way.
<s>Meru</s>, <s>Mandara</s>, and also <s>Vimāna</s>, and another,
<s>Bhadraka</s>, <s>Sarvatobhadra</s>, <s>Rucaka</s>, and likewise <s>Nandana</s>,
the one named <s>Nandivardhana</s>, and <s>Śrīvatsa</s>: these are the nine.
They are understood to be square forms arising from <s>Vairāja</s>.
<s>Valabhī</s>, <s>Gṛharāja</s>, <s>Śālāgṛha</s>, and <s>Mandira</s>,

children.text: vimānaṃ ca tathā brahmamandiraṃ bhavanaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: and also <s>Vimāna</s>, <s>Brahmamandira</s>, and <s>Bhavana</s>,
<s>Uttambha</s>, <s>Śibikā</s>, and <s>Veśma</s>: these nine arise from <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
<s>Valaya</s>, <s>Dundubhi</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and also <s>Mahāpadma</s>,
<s>Mukulī</s>, its <s>Uṣṇīṣī</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, and <s>Kalaśa</s>,
and another, <s>Guvāvṛkṣa</s>: these round forms arise from <s>Kailāsa</s>.
<s>Gaja</s>, then <s>Vṛṣabha</s>, <s>Haṃsa</s>, <s>Garuḍa</s>, and the one named <s>Siṃha</s>,
<s>Bhūmukha</s>, <s>Bhūdhara</s>, <s>Śrījaya</s>, and <s>Pṛthivīdhara</s>,
these nine oblong-round forms arise from the one called <s>Maṇikā</s>.
<s>Vajra</s>, <s>Cakra</s>, and another named <s>Muṣṭika</s> and <s>Babhru</s>,

children.text: vakraḥ svastikakhaḍgau ca gadā śrīvṛkṣa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vakra</s>, <s>Svastika</s>, <s>Khaḍga</s>, <s>Gadā</s>, and <s>Śrīvṛkṣa</s> as well.
The ones called <s>Vijaya</s> are white and are born from <s>Triviṣṭapa</s>.
A triangle, a lotus, a half-moon, a quadrangle, and sixteenfold forms

children.text: yatra tatra vidhātavyaṃ saṃsthānaṃ maṇḍapasya tu
children.translated_text: should be made here and there as the arrangement of the pavilion.

children.text: rājyaṃ ca vibhavaś caivaḥ hyāyurvardhanameva ca ||
children.translated_text: Kingship, prosperity, and indeed increase of lifespan as well,
the gain of sons, women, and nourishment arise in order from the triangular form and the others.
One should make the banner and the rest at the well-known doorway, and likewise the sanctum.
The pavilion, as well as the measuring cord, should be multiplied by even numbers.
By one who knows, the <s>bhadra</s> projection should be made from a quarter of the pavilion.
It may be furnished with projecting windows and lattice openings, or it may be without lattice windows.
It may be according to the measure of a wall and a half, or again according to the measure of the wall,
or in some cases pavilions should be made with twice the wall's measure.
On the temple a <s>mañcarī</s> should be made, variegated and with uneven stories,
adorned with irregular lines because of a difference in measurement.
The base should have four supports and be adorned with four pavilions.
The excellent temple called <s>Meru</s> is furnished with a hundred peaks.
Its pavilions should be made adorned with three <s>bhadras</s>.
According to the forms and measures of their construction, these are both distinct and not distinct.
In some of them there are several supports, and some are without supports.
Those temples arise according to differences of model and covering.
There is no mutual confusion among those arrangements, because their constructions are not identical.
Many temples are taught for the particular distinction of the deities.
There is no fixed rule in a temple for self-manifest deities.
For those very deities too, one should have them made according to the earlier measure.
There, square and oblong forms, furnished with four corners,
should be made with moon-windows and equipped with drum-shaped spires.

children.text: purato vāhanānāṃ ca kartavyā lagna maṇḍapāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Attached pavilions should be made in front of the vehicles.
A theatre hall should also be made, situated near the doorway.

children.text: prasāde devatānāṃ ca kāryā dikṣu vidikṣvapi ||
children.translated_text: In the temple of the deities, they should be made in the cardinal and intermediate directions as well.
Door guardians too should be made, the chief ones having gone separately.
A little way off, monasteries should be made there for those who live from the temple.
A covered platform should be made, provided with fruits, flowers, and water.
Having installed the gods in the temples, a man should worship them with acts of worship.
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, the god of all, becomes the one who receives every share for the maker of that house and the rest.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśe ācārakāṇḍe prāsādaliṅgamaṇḍapādilakṣaṇanirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section, in the first part, in the section on conduct, the forty-seventh chapter, named "The Explanation of the Characteristics of Temples, Liṅgas, Pavilions, and the Like."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall briefly describe the consecration of all the gods.
On an auspicious lunar day and the like, the guru should perform the consecration in a very pleasing place.
Together with the officiating priests, he should choose an ācārya from the middle country.
He should do so according to the rule taught in his own Vedic branch, or else with the <s>praṇava</s>.
With five or with many, he should perform the offering of water for the feet and the arghya,
and likewise with rings, garments, perfumes, garlands, and ointments.

children.text: mantranyāsaṃ guruḥ kṛtvā tataḥ karma samārabhet
children.translated_text: After the guru has performed the placement of mantras, he should then begin the rite.
In front of the temple he should make a pavilion measuring ten hands,
or he should make one measuring twelve hands, furnished with sixteen pillars.

children.text: dhvajāṣṭakaiś caturhastāṃ madhye vediṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: With eight banners, he should have an altar of four hands made in the middle.
He should have sand brought there from a tīrtha at the confluence of rivers.
Square, bow-shaped, circular, and lotus-shaped,
a set of five fire-pits should be made, beginning from the east.
Or else he should have all these made square.
According to the procedure of the rite of appeasement, it is for the accomplishment of every desired object.
At the place of the deity's head, the ācārya should perform the oblation.
Some prefer it in the northeast, after smearing the auspicious ground.

children.text: dvārāṇi caiva catvāri kṛtvā vai toraṇāntike ||
children.translated_text: Having made four doors near the gateways,
banyan, udumbara, aśvattha, bilva, palāśa, and khadira
arches, five hands high and adorned with cloth, flowers, and the like, should be made.
He should bury them one hand deep, four of them in the four directions.

children.text: pūrvadvāre mṛgendraṃ tu hayarājaṃ tu dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: At the eastern door he should place <s>Mṛgendra</s>; at the southern, <s>Hayarāja</s>;
in the west, the one named <s>Gopati</s>; and in the north, <s>Suraśārdūla</s>.

children.text: agnim īleti hi mantreṇa prathamaṃ pūrvato nyaset ||
children.translated_text: With the mantra "Agnim īḷe," he should first set down the eastern one.
With the mantra "Iṣe tve," he should set down the second one in the south.
With the mantra "Agnā ā yāhi," he should set down the third one in the west.

children.text: śaṃ no devīti mantreṇa uttarasyāṃ caturthakam
children.translated_text: With the mantra "Śaṃ no devī," he should set down the fourth one in the north.
In the east it should be made like a raincloud; in the southeast it is smoke-colored.

children.text: yāmyāṃ vai kṛṣṇarūpā tu nairṛtyā śyāmalā bhavet
children.translated_text: In the south it is black in form, and in the southwest it should be dark.
In the west it is to be known as pale, and in the northwest yellow-colored.

children.text: uttare raktavarṇā tu śukleśī ca patākikā
children.translated_text: In the north it is red, and in the white northeast it is furnished with a banner.
In the middle it is many-colored; in the east it is called <s>Indravidyā</s>.
In the south, with the mantra of <s>Agni</s> and "saṃsupti," and with "Yamo na āgaḥ,"
it should be worshiped with "Rakṣohaṇa" in the west, and also in the north.
Then, having sprinkled it with "Vāta," and in the north with "Āpyāyasva,"
and after that with "Tam īśānam," in the middle with "Viṣṇor nu ka."

children.text: kalaśau tu tato dvau dvau niveśyau toraṇāntike
children.translated_text: Then two jars each should be set near the gateway,
provided with pairs of garments and well adorned with sandalwood and the like.
They should be consecrated with many flowers and canopies and with the initial syllables.
Then the guardians of the directions should be worshiped by the rite seen in the śāstra.
With the mantra "Trātāram Indram," and others with "Agnir mūrdhā,"

children.text: asmin vṛkṣa itaṃ caiva pracārīti parā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: and another is taught with "Asmin vṛkṣe" and "Itaṃ caiva pracāri," respectively.
And, with the formula beginning somewhat indistinctly, "ācatvābhitvā" and so on: this is the seventh.
Having worshiped the guardians of the directions with "imā rudrā" and related formulas, the discerning man should proceed.
He should place the materials for the homa in the northwestern quarter, together with their implements.
The guru should place white conches, as prescribed by the śāstra, at the two eyes.

children.text: ālokanena dravyāṇi śuddhiṃ yānti na saṃśayaḥ
children.translated_text: By the act of looking, the materials attain purity; there is no doubt about this.
The heart and the other limbs are to be assigned with the vyāhṛtis and the praṇava.
And the astra is for all of them; this nyāsa fulfills every desire.
He should consecrate the unbroken grains and the viṣṭara with the astra alone.
With the viṣṭara he should touch the materials gathered for the sacrificial pavilion.
Afterwards he should scatter the unbroken grains, purified by the astra, all around.
Beginning with the direction of <s>Śakra</s>, and extending as far as the region of <s>Īśāna</s>,
having scattered the unbroken grains everywhere, he should then smear the pavilion.
With perfumes and the like, the guru should install the group of mantras in the arghya vessel.
With that water from the arghya vessel he should sprinkle the sacrificial pavilion.

children.text: pratiṣṭhā yasya devasya tadākhyaṃ kalaśaṃ nyaset
children.translated_text: He should set down a kalaśa bearing the name of the deity whose installation is being performed.
In the northeastern quarter he should worship, and in the southern quarter the vardhanī with the astra itself.

children.text: kalaśaṃ vardhanīṃ caiva grahān vāstoṣpatiṃ tathā
children.translated_text: The kalaśa, the vardhanī, the planets, and likewise <s>Vāstoṣpati</s>,
having placed all these on their seats, the guru should recite what is called the praṇava.
The guru should worship the kalaśa, with a thread around its neck, containing jewels, wrapped in a pair of cloths,
and anointed with all herbs and perfumes.
The deity is to be worshiped in the kalaśa, and an excellent cloth is to be placed on the vardhanī.
He should then turn the kalaśa together with the vardhanī.
Sprinkling with the stream from the vardhanī, he should then carry it in front.
Having worshiped the vardhanī vessel, he should worship the deity on the altar-ground.

children.text: ghaṭaṃ cāvāhya vāyavyāṃ gaṇānāṃ tveti sadgaṇam
children.translated_text: Having invoked the pot in the northwestern quarter, he should invoke the good host of gaṇas with the formula "gaṇānāṃ tvā."
The wise man should recite to <s>Vāstoṣpati</s> in the northeastern corner for the deity.
With the mantra "vāstoṣpati," this is done for the appeasement of faults in the site.

children.text: kumbhasya pūrvato bhūtaṃ gaṇadevaṃ baliṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: To the east of the kumbha he should offer bali to the being who is the deity of the gaṇas.
The wise man should recite the vidyās and perform the ālambana.
With the mantra "yoge yoge," he should make a covering with green kuśa grasses.
Then the guru, as ācārya, together with the officiating priests, should stand at the bathing seat.
With various Brahmanical chants, and with cries of "puṇyāha," victory, and auspiciousness,

children.text: kṛtvā brahmarathe devaṃ pratiṣṭhanti tato dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: the Brahmins then install the deity after placing it on the <s>Brahma</s>-chariot.
The guru should bring the seat into the northeastern part and set it in the pavilion.
After bathing with the formula "bhadraṃ karṇe" and with what is made of thread and bark,
he should bathe it fully and perform the revealing of the marks, accompanied by the playing of musical instruments.
In a bronze or copper vessel, with honey and ghee mixed together,
he should anoint its eyes with a golden rod.
With the mantra "agnir jyotiḥ," he should perform the opening of the eyes.

children.text: lakṣaṇe kriyamāṇe tu nāmaikaṃ sthāpako vadet ||
children.translated_text: While the marks are being made, the installer should pronounce one name.

children.text: imaṃ me gaṅge mantreṇa netrayoḥ śītalakriyā
children.translated_text: With the mantra "imaṃ me gaṅge," the cooling rite for the two eyes is performed.
With the mantra "agnir mūrdhā," he should apply earth from an anthill.
Bilva, udumbara, aśvattha, vaṭa, and pālāśa:
with the mantra "yajñā yajñā," he should apply the fivefold astringent decoction.
He should bathe it with pañcagavya and then with sahadevī and the other herbs.
Sahadevī, balā, śatamūlī, and śatāvarī,

children.text: kumārī ca guḍūcī ca siṃhī vyāghrī tathaiva ca
children.translated_text: kumārī, guḍūcī, siṃhī, and likewise vyāghrī:
with the mantra "yā oṣadhi," the bath with water infused with herbs is prescribed.
With the mantra "yāḥ phalinī," the fruit bath is prescribed.
With the mantra "drupadādiva," the wise should perform the rubbing with unguents.
Having placed them in the kalaśas successively, beginning with the north,
jewels, grains, herbs, and śatapuṣpikā,
and having also placed the oceans, four by four, in the four directions,

children.text: kṣīraṃ dadhi kṣīrodasya ghṛtodasyeti vā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should place milk, curd, the ocean of milk, or again the ocean of ghee.
With the mantras "āpyāyasva," "dadhikrāvṇo," and "yā oṣadhīḥ,"
and with the mantra "tejo 'si," he should consecrate the kumbha.
Then he should bathe it with the kalaśas named after the four oceans.
After it has been bathed and well adorned, incense of guggulu should be offered.
For the consecration he should place the corresponding tīrthas in the kumbhas.
All the tīrthas that are on the earth, and the rivers and oceans likewise,
with the mantra "yā oṣadhi," he should consecrate the kumbha.
Whoever bathes with that water is freed from all sins.
Having consecrated it with the oceans, he should then again give arghya.

children.text: gandhadvāreti gandhaṃ ca nyāsaṃ vai vedamantrakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: With "gandhadvāra" he should offer perfume, and perform nyāsa with Vedic mantras.
With the proper mantras prescribed by his own śāstra, including "yuvaṃ vastrā," he should offer the garment.
With the mantra "kavihā," he should bring it into the auspicious pavilion.
With the mantra "śambhavāya," he should place it on the bed.
With the mantra "viśvataś cakṣus," he should make it both manifest and unmanifest, with parts and without parts.

children.text: sthitvā caiva pare tattve mantranyāsaṃ tu kārayet
children.translated_text: Standing in the supreme principle, he should perform the mantra-nyāsa.
The mantra prescribed by his own śāstra, and the nyāsa, are stated there in that same way.
Having covered it with a cloth, it is to be worshiped in its proper manner.
According to the śāstra, he should have the offerings set at the base of its feet.
Then he should take a kalaśa joined with the praṇava and wrapped in a pair of cloths,
and offer the kalaśa, together with gold, at the place of the head.
Then, standing near the fire-pit, he should perform the establishment of the fire.
The guru should do so with mantras prescribed by his own śāstra, or else with those taught in the Veda.
The Bahvṛc should recite on the eastern side the <s>Śrīsūkta</s>, the <s>Pāvamānī</s> hymns, and the <s>Vāsadāmya</s> and <s>Savājina</s>,

children.text: vṛṣākapiṃ ca mitraṃ bahvacaḥ pūrvato japet ||
children.translated_text: and also the <s>Vṛṣākapi</s> and <s>Mitra</s> hymns.

children.text: rudraṃ puruṣasūktaṃ ca ślokādhyāyaṃ ca śukriyam
children.translated_text: The Adhvaryu should recite on the southern side the <s>Rudra</s>, the <s>Puruṣasūkta</s>, the chapter of verses, the <s>Śukriya</s>,
the <s>Brahman</s> hymn, and the <s>Pitṛmaitra</s>.
The Chāndoga should recite on the western side the <s>Vedavrata</s>, the <s>Vāmadevya</s>, the <s>Jyeṣṭhasāman</s>, the <s>Rathantara</s>,

children.text: bheruṇḍāni ca sāmāni chandogaḥ paścime japet ||
children.translated_text: and the <s>Bheruṇḍa</s> sāman hymns.
The Atharvan should recite on the northern side the <s>Atharvaśiras</s>, the <s>Kumbhasūkta</s> of the Atharvan,
the <s>Nīlarudra</s> hymns, and the <s>Maitra</s>.
The ācārya, in particular, should sprinkle the fire-pit with the astra-mantra,
and, according to his means, use a copper vessel, a bowl, or whatever is available.
Having brought <s>Jātavedas</s>, he should set him down in front.
He should kindle the fire with the astra-mantra and enclose it with the kavaca-mantra.
Afterward the deśika should make it amṛta-like with all the mantras.

children.text: pātraṃ gṛhya karābhyāṃ ca kuṇḍaṃ bhrāmya tataḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Taking the vessel with both hands, he should then move it around the fire-pit once more.

children.text: vaiṣṇavena tu yogena paraṃ tejastu niḥkṣipet
children.translated_text: By the Vaiṣṇava yoga he should place the supreme radiance there.
He should place <s>Brahmā</s> on the southern side and the praṇīta waters on the northern side.
With a common mantra, or with one prescribed in his own sūtra,

children.text: dikṣu dikṣu tato dadyātparidhiṃ viṣṭaraiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: he should then place the enclosing sticks in each of the directions, together with the spread darbha seats.
<s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Hara</s>, and <s>Īśāna</s> are to be worshipped with the common mantra.
He should set the fire upon darbha grass, encircled with darbha grass.
Even if it lacks mantra, what has been touched with darbha-water becomes pure.
When the fire is surrounded with unbroken darbha grasses spread out with their tips eastward, northward, and westward,
it itself comes into sacred presence.
The mantra-knower should perform the rite that has been prescribed for the protection of the fire.
Some ācāryas desire it after the rites beginning with <s>jātakarman</s>.

children.text: pavitraṃ tu tataḥ kṛtvā kuryādājyasya saṃskṛtim ||
children.translated_text: Then, having made the pavitra, he should perform the consecration of the ghee.
The ācārya should inspect the consecrated nīrājya, after looking at it,
up to the ājyabhāga and the abhighāra, in order to ensure the readiness of the ghee.
After that, he should offer twenty-five oblations with ghee.
From <s>garbhādhāna</s> onward, up to the rite of hair-cutting,
he should sacrifice with the mantras prescribed in his own śāstra, or else with the praṇava.

children.text: tataḥ pūrṇāhutiṃ dattvā pūrṇāt pūrṇam anārethaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then, having given the full oblation, he should recite the formula beginning, “From fullness, fullness.”
The fire produced in this way grants success in all rites.
Then, after worshipping the fire, he should proceed with it in the fire-pits in the same manner.
With the proper mantras of <s>Indra</s> and the others, he should offer one hundred oblations for each,
and at the end of the hundred he should offer the full oblation for all of them.
Then the hotṛ should place his own oblation among the ghee-offerings in that kalaśa.
Having made the deities, the mantras, <s>Jātavedas</s>,
and himself into a single unity, he should then cause the full oblation to be offered.
The ācārya should go outside and present bali-offerings to the guardians of the directions,

children.text: bhūtānāṃ caiva devānāṃ nāgānāṃ ca prayogataḥ
children.translated_text: and also to beings, gods, and nāgas, according to the procedure.
Sesame seeds and fuel-sticks are remembered as the two substances for homa.

children.text: ājyaṃ tayoḥ sahakāri tatpradhānaṃ yad aṅkayoḥ
children.translated_text: Ghee is auxiliary to those two, while what is principal depends on the particular limbs of the rite.

children.text: paruṣasuktaṃ pūrveṇaiva rudraś caiva tu dakṣiṇe ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Puruṣasūkta</s> is to the east, and the <s>Rudra</s> is to the south.
The <s>Jyeṣṭhasāman</s>, the <s>Bhāruṇḍa</s>, and the formula <s>tan nayāmi</s> are to the west.
The <s>Nīlarudra</s>, the great mantra, and the <s>Kumbhasūkta</s> of the Atharvan are to the north.
After offering a thousand oblations to each deity, he should assign that deity to the head.

children.text: evaṃ madhye tathā pāde pūrṇāhutyā tathā punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Likewise in the middle and at the feet, and again with the full oblation,
he should sacrifice at the places of the head and make the entry in due order.
Or, with the first mantras of the Vedas, or with mantras made of the gods' names,
or with those prescribed in his own śāstra, or with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, O twice-born ones,
or the ācārya may do it with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, the vyāhṛtis, and the praṇava.
Having performed the homa rite in this way, the deśika should place the mantras.

children.text: caraṇāv agnim īḍe tu iṣe tvo gulphayoḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: On the two feet he should place <s>agnim īḍe</s>; <s>iṣe tvā</s> is stationed on the ankles.

children.text: agna āyāhi jaṅghe dve śaṃ no devīti jānunī
children.translated_text: On the two shanks he should place <s>agna āyāhi</s>, and on the knees <s>śaṃ no devī</s>.

children.text: bṛhadrathantare ūrū udareṣv ātilo svātino nyaset ||
children.translated_text: On the thighs he should place the <s>Bṛhat</s> and <s>Rathantara</s>; on the belly he should place the uncertain formula transmitted here.
At the heart he should place <s>dīrghāyuṣṭvāya</s>, and at the throat he should place <s>śrīś ca te</s>.
On the chest he should place <s>trātāram indram</s>, and on the two eyes <s>tryambakam</s>.
On the head he should place <s>mūrdhā bhava</s>; after the attachment he should perform the homa.
Then he should raise the deity with the mantra <s>uttiṣṭha brahmaṇaspate</s>.
With Vedic and puṇyāha sounds he should circumambulate the temples.
Having made contact with the pedestal, the mantra-knower should use the formula <s>devasya tvā</s>.
The guardians of the directions, along with jewels, metals, and herbs,
and prepared iron seeds are to be arranged; afterward he should install the deity.

children.text: na garbhe sthāpayeddevaṃ na garbhaṃ tu parityajet
children.translated_text: He should not set the deity directly in the garbha, yet he should not abandon the garbha.

children.text: īṣanmadhyaṃ parityajya tato doṣāpahaṃ tu tat ||
children.translated_text: Leaving the exact middle slightly aside, that becomes a remover of faults.

children.text: tilasya tuṣamātraṃ tu uttaraṃ kiṃcid ānayet
children.translated_text: He should bring it a little to the north, by the measure of a sesame husk.

children.text: oṃ sthiro bhava śivo bhava prajābhyaśca namonamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: With “oṃ, become firm, become auspicious; repeated homage to the creatures,”

children.text: devasya tvā saviturvaḥ ṣaḍbhyo vai vinyasedguruḥ
children.translated_text: the guru should install it for the six, using the mantra <s>devasya tvā savituḥ</s>.
He should use the transmitted formula concerning tattva, syllable, kalā, measure, progeny, and the daughter of the world.
Having installed it for the six and for the siddhārtha, he should consecrate it with mantras for firmness.
With the sampāta-kalaśa he should bathe the well-established deity.
He should worship it fully with lamp, incense, perfumes, and food offerings.

children.text: arghyaṃ dattvā namaskṛtya tato devaṃ kṣamāpayet ||
