children.translated_text: After giving arghya and bowing, he should then ask the deity for forgiveness.
A vessel, a pair of garments, an umbrella, and likewise a divine ring
And dakṣiṇā (ritual fees) should be given to the priests according to one's ability.
Afterwards the yajamāna (sacrificing patron), composed in mind, should offer oblations for the fourfold ones.

children.text: āhutīnāṃ śataṃ hutvā tataḥ pūrṇāṃ pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Having offered one hundred oblations, he should then have the full oblation presented.
The ācārya should go outside and offer bali (food-offering) to the guardians of the directions.
Then the ācārya, with flowers in his hand, should dismiss them, saying, "Forgive me."
At the end of the sacrifice he should give a tawny cow to the ācārya, and also a yak-tail fan,
a crown, earrings, a parasol, armlets, and a waist-cord,
a fan, village garments, and the like, together with accessories, and a fine pavilion.
He should arrange a great meal, and he becomes one who has accomplished what had to be done.
The yajamāna is freed through the favor of the installer.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe devapratiṣṭhādinirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the forty-eighth chapter, named "Description of Deity Consecration and Related Matters," is complete.
Thus the section on consecration is complete.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
<s>Hari</s>, the maker of creation and the rest, is to be worshipped by <s>Svāyambhuva</s> and the others,

children.text: viprādyaiḥ svena dharmeṇa taddharmaṃ vyāsa vai śṛṇu ||
children.translated_text: and by Brahmins and the rest according to their own dharma (normative duty). Listen, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, to that dharma.
Sacrificing, officiating at sacrifice, giving, and receiving gifts are for a Brahmin,
as are teaching and study: these are the six acts, O best of the twice-born.
Giving, study, and sacrifice are the dharma of Kṣatriyas and Vaiśyas;
punitive rule is his, while agriculture is prescribed for the Vaiśya.
Service to the twice-born alone is the means of dharma for Śūdras;
craft-work is also their livelihood, and the simple cooked offering too is in accordance with dharma.

children.text: bhikṣācaryātha śuśrūṣā guroḥ svādhyāya eva ca
children.translated_text: Begging, service to the guru, and self-recitation of scripture,
the twilight rite and the fire rite: this is the dharma of a brahmacārin (celibate student).
Of all the āśramas (life-stages) there is a twofold division, and also a fourfold one.
The brahmacārin is either temporary, or lifelong, intent on brahman.
One who has studied the Vedas according to rule and then enters the householder āśrama
is to be known as a temporary student; the lifelong one remains so until death.
Sacred fires, service to guests, sacrifice, giving, and worship of the gods:
in brief, this is the dharma of a householder, O best of the twice-born.
A householder may be of two kinds, indifferent or active;
one engaged in supporting his family is that active householder.
But one who has discharged the three debts and abandoned wife, wealth, and the rest,
and wanders alone, is indifferent and directed toward liberation.
Living on roots and fruits on the ground, self-recitation of scripture, and austerity:
this, along with proper sharing, is the dharma of the forest-dweller.
One who practices austerity in the forest, sacrifices to the gods, and offers oblations,
and is devoted to self-recitation, is a forest-dweller, the best of ascetics.
But one who is greatly emaciated by austerity and intent on meditation

children.text: saṃnyāsī sa hi vijñeyo vānaprasthāśrame sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: is to be known as a saṃnyāsin (renunciant), though situated in the vānaprastha āśrama.
A bhikṣu (mendicant), always devoted to the practice of yoga, wishing to ascend, and with senses conquered,
acts for the sake of knowledge and is called pārameṣṭhika.
But the great sage whose delight is in the self alone and who is always satisfied,

children.text: samyak ca damasampannaḥ sa yogī bhikṣurucyate ||
children.translated_text: and who is fully endowed with restraint, is called a yogin and a bhikṣu.

children.text: bhaikṣyaṃ śrutaṃ ca maunitvaṃ tapo dhyānaṃ viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Begging, sacred learning, silence, austerity, and especially meditation,

children.text: samyak ca jñānavairāgyaṃ dharmo 'yaṃ bhikṣuke mataḥ ||
children.translated_text: together with true knowledge and detachment: this is regarded as the dharma of a mendicant.
Some are renouncers through knowledge, others are renouncers of the Veda,
and some are renouncers of rites: the pārameṣṭhika is threefold.

children.text: yogī ca trividho jñeyo bhautikaḥ kṣatra evaca
children.translated_text: The yogin too should be known as threefold: the bhautika, the kṣatra,
and the third, called the one in the final āśrama, established in the form of yoga.
The first bhāvanā (contemplative disposition) belongs to the former; in liberation there is the bhāvanā of the imperishable.
In the third case the final bhāvanā is declared to be supreme and lordly.
From dharma arises liberation, while from wealth desire is born.
Vedic action is twofold: engagement and withdrawal.
Knowledge is prior and belongs to withdrawal; engagement is performed for Agni and the gods.

children.text: kṣamā damo dayā dānamalobhābhyāsa eva ca ||
children.translated_text: Forbearance, self-control, compassion, giving, and the repeated practice of non-greed,
uprightness, freedom from envy, and likewise resorting to sacred fords,
truth, contentment, belief in sacred authority, and control of the senses,
honoring deities and especially worship of Brahmins,
nonviolence, pleasant speech, absence of slander, and lack of harshness:
these are the dharmas of those in the āśramas. Now I shall speak of the four varṇas.
The prājāpatya place is remembered for Brahmins who perform ritual acts.
The place of <s>Indra</s> is for Kṣatriyas who do not flee in battles.
The place of the <s>Maruts</s> is for Vaiśyas who follow their own dharma.
The gāndharva place is for people born as Śūdras who engage in service.
For the eighty-eight thousand sages whose seed flows upward,

children.text: smṛtaṃ teṣāṃ tu yatsthānaṃ tadeva vanavāsinām
children.translated_text: the place remembered as theirs is also the very place for forest-dwellers.

children.text: saptarṣīṇāṃ tu yatsthānaṃ sthānaṃ tadvai vanaukasām ||
children.translated_text: The place that belongs to the Seven Sages is indeed the place of forest inhabitants.
For ascetics with restrained minds, renouncers whose seed flows upward,
their place is bliss, brahman, from which a sage does not return.
For yogins there is the immortal place, called the ether, the supreme imperishable.
It is the blissful, lordly state from which, once freed, a man does not return.
Liberation comes from knowledge of the eight limbs; listen as I tell it briefly.
The five yamas begin with nonviolence; nonviolence is not harming living beings.
Truth is speech beneficial to beings; non-stealing is the supreme non-grasping of what belongs to oneself alone.
Celibacy is non-intercourse; non-possession is complete renunciation.

children.text: niyamāḥ pañca satyādyā brāhmam ābhyantaraṃ dvidhā
children.translated_text: The five niyamas, beginning with truth, are declared; cleanliness is twofold, external and internal.
Cleanliness, satisfaction and contentment, austerity, and restraint of the senses are taught.
Svādhyāya is the recitation of mantras; praṇidhāna is the worship of <s>Hari</s>.
Āsana is posture, such as the lotus posture; prāṇāyāma is mastery over the breath.
When it is accompanied by mantra-meditation it is called 'with seed'; the opposite is indeed 'seedless.'

children.text: evaṃ dvidhā tridhāpyuktaṃ puraṇāt pūrakaḥ sa ca ||
children.translated_text: Thus it has been taught as twofold and also as threefold; because of filling, it is called pūraka.
Because of stillness it is kumbhaka, and because of exhaling it is recaka; it is threefold.
The light form is of twelve mātrās, the next is of twenty-four.
The best is measured by thirty-six mātrās; pratyāhāra is restraint.
Meditation is reflection on <s>Brahman</s> as the self; dhāraṇā is the steadiness of the mind.
Abiding in the thought 'I am <s>Brahman</s>' is samādhi, the state of being established in <s>Brahman</s>.
I am the self, the supreme <s>Brahman</s>, truth, knowledge, and the infinite.
<s>Brahman</s> is knowledge and bliss; you are that reality alone.
I am <s>Brahman</s>; I am <s>Brahman</s>, without body and without senses.
I am free from mind, intellect, the great principle, ego, and the rest.
I am that light connected with waking, dream, deep sleep, and the other states.
I am eternal, pure, awakened, liberated, true, blissful, and non-dual.
That person who is in the sun, he am I, unbroken and indivisible.
Meditating in this way, a brāhmaṇa is released from the bondage of worldly existence.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe varṇāśramadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikonapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the forty-ninth chapter, named 'The Explanation of the Dharmas of the Varṇas and Āśramas,' in the section on conduct, in the first part called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
One who performs the rite day after day obtains knowledge.

children.text: brāhme muhūrte cotthāya dharmamarthaṃ ca cintayet ||
children.translated_text: Having risen in the brāhma muhūrta, he should reflect on dharma and artha.
He should contemplate in his heart <s>Hari</s>, seated on a lotus, blissful and undecaying.

children.text: uṣaḥkāle tu samprāpte kṛtvā cāvaśyakaṃ budhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the time of dawn has arrived, the wise man should first perform what is necessary.
Having cleansed himself according to rule, he should bathe in pure rivers.
By the morning bath even people who have committed sins are purified.
Therefore, with every effort, one should practice the morning bath.

children.text: prātaḥ snānaṃ praśaṃsanti dṛṣṭādṛṣṭaṣṭakaraṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: They praise the morning bath, for it brings both visible and invisible benefit.
From one who has slept comfortably, saliva and other discharges continually flow.
Therefore one should not perform rites without first taking a bath.
Misfortune, Kālakarṇī, bad dreams, bad thoughts,

children.text: prātaḥ snānena pāpāni dhūyante nātra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and sins are washed away by the morning bath; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: na ca snānaṃ vinā puṃsāṃ prāśastyaṃ karma saṃsmṛtam
children.translated_text: For men, no rite is remembered as praiseworthy without bathing.
Especially for homa and japa, therefore one should bathe.
If one is unable, a bath without wetting the head is prescribed for him.

children.text: ārdreṇa vāsasā vāpi mārjanaṃ kāyikaṃ smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: Or wiping the body with a wet garment is remembered as a bodily purification.
The brāhma, āgneya, vāyavya, divya,
vāruṇa, and likewise yaugika forms make up the sixfold bath that one should perform.

children.text: brāhmaṃ tu mārjanaṃ mantraiḥ kuśaiḥ sodakabindubhiḥ
children.translated_text: The brāhma bath is sprinkling with mantras, with kuśa grass and drops of water.
The āgneya bath is shaking or rubbing the body with ash from foot to head.

children.text: gavāṃ hi rajasā proktaṃ vāyavyaṃ snānamuttamam
children.translated_text: The vāyavya bath is said to be with the dust of cows, and it is excellent.
The bath that occurs through rain while the sun shines is called the divya bath.
The vāruṇa bath is immersion in water; the mental bath is knowledge of the self.
The yaugika bath is declared to be contemplation of <s>Hari</s> through yoga.
This is known as the tīrtha of the self, resorted to by speakers of <s>Brahman</s>.
Auspicious tooth-cleaning sticks may come from milk-bearing trees or from mālatī.

children.text: apāmārgaṃ ca bilvaṃ ca karavīraṃ ca dhāvane
children.translated_text: Apāmārga, bilva, and karavīra may also be used for cleaning the teeth.
Facing north or facing east, one should chew the tooth-cleaning stick.
After rinsing and using it, he should discard it in a clean place, composed in mind.
After bathing, he should satisfy the gods, the seers, and the hosts of ancestors.
Having sipped water according to rule each day, and having sipped again, restrained in speech,
he should sprinkle himself with mantras, using kuśa grass and drops of water.
He should use the Āpo hi ṣṭhā verses, the vyāhṛtis, the Sāvitrī, and auspicious Varuṇa mantras.
Having recited the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, mother of the Veda, joined with oṃ and the vyāhṛtis,

children.text: japtvā jalāñjaliṃ dadyād bhāskaraṃ prati tanmanāḥ
children.translated_text: he should offer a handful of water toward <s>Bhāskara</s>, with his mind fixed on him.
Then, standing on darbha grass by the eastern bank, well composed,
he should perform prāṇāyāma and then meditate on <s>Sandhyā</s>; so says śruti.

children.text: yā sandhyā sā jagatsūtirmāyātītā hi niṣkalā ||
children.translated_text: That <s>Sandhyā</s> is the source of the world, beyond māyā, and without parts.
She is the sovereign, solitary power, arisen from the three principles.

children.text: dhyātvā raktāṃ sitāṃ kṛṣṇāṃ gāyattrīṃ vai japedbudhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on the <s>Gāyatrī</s> as red, white, and black, the wise man should recite it.
The brāhmaṇa should always perform <s>sandhyā</s> worship facing east.
One who lacks <s>sandhyā</s> is always impure and unfit for all rites.
Whatever else he does, he does not become a sharer in its fruit.
Holy brāhmaṇas, whose minds are fixed on no other object and who have mastered the Vedas,
having worshiped <s>Sandhyā</s> according to rule, have attained the former and the latter goal.
The best of twice-born men who strives elsewhere in works of dharma,
after abandoning reverence to <s>Sandhyā</s>, goes to ten thousand hells.
Therefore, with every effort, one should practice <s>sandhyā</s> worship.
Through it the supreme god, whose body is yoga, becomes worshiped by him.
The highest recitation is one thousand repetitions, the middle is one hundred, and the lowest is ten.
A learned man, facing east, controlled and pure, should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
Then, composed in mind, he should attend upon the rising sun,
with various solar mantras known as Ṛg, Yajus, and Sāman.
Having approached the great yogin, the god of gods, the maker of day,
he should make a prostration on the ground, having consecrated his head with mantra.
"Oṃ, to <s>Khakholka</s>, the peaceful one, the cause of the three causes,
I offer myself; homage to you, whose form is knowledge.
You alone are supreme <s>Brahman</s>, the waters, light, essence, and immortality.
You are bhūr, bhuvaḥ, and svaḥ; you are oṃkāra, all, the ancient <s>Rudra</s>."
Having recited this <s>Sūryahṛdaya</s>, the excellent hymn,
one should bow to the maker of day in the morning and at midday.
Then, having come home, the Brahmin should sip water according to rule,
kindle the fire according to rule, and offer oblations to <s>Jātavedas</s>.

children.text: ṛtvik putro 'tha patnī vā śiṣyo vāpi sahodaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: An officiating priest, son, wife, pupil, or brother,
after especially obtaining permission, may offer oblations according to rule.
Any rite performed without mantra gives no fruit in the next world or in this one.
He should bow to the deities and present offerings.
He should also attend upon the guru and do what is beneficial for him.
Then the twice-born man should diligently undertake Vedic recitation, as far as he is able.
He may recite, teach pupils, retain the texts, and examine them.
The best of twice-born men should inspect the śāstras, those concerning <s>dharma</s> and the rest,
and also the Vedic scriptures and all the Vedāṅgas.
He should approach the Lord for the attainment of welfare and security.
Then the twice-born man should accomplish various aims for the sake of his family.
Then, at midday, he should bring clay for the bath,
as well as flowers, unbroken grains, sesame, kuśa grass, and pure cow-dung.
In rivers, divine reservoirs, ponds, and lakes,
he should perform bathing, but never in one belonging to another.

children.text: pañca piṇḍān anuddhṛtya snānaṃ duṣyanti nityaśaḥ
children.translated_text: Bathing is always spoiled if five lumps have not been taken out.
With one portion of clay the head is to be washed, and with two the area above the navel;

children.text: adhaśca tisṛbhiḥ kṣālyaṃ pādau ṣaḍbhistathaiva ca
children.translated_text: with three the lower part is to be washed, and likewise the feet with six.
The prescribed amount of clay is said to be about the size of an old āmalaka fruit.
The measure of cow-dung is the same; then he should smear his body with it.
Having washed and sipped water according to rule, he should then bathe with collected mind.
Standing on the bank after smearing himself, he should do so with those very signs and with mantra.
He should consecrate the water with auspicious mantras connected with the waters and with <s>Varuṇa</s>.

children.text: snānakāle smared viṣṇam āpo nārāyaṇo yataḥ
children.translated_text: At the time of bathing he should remember <s>Viṣṇu</s>, since the waters are <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>.
Looking toward oṃkāra and the sun, he should plunge three times into the water.
Having sipped, the knower of mantra should sip again with this mantra:
"You move within beings, in the cave, facing all directions.

children.text: tvaṃ yajñastvaṃ vaṣaṭkāra āpo jyotī raso 'mṛtam
children.translated_text: You are sacrifice; you are the vaṣaṭ-call, the waters, light, essence, and immortality."
Or he should recite the <s>Drupadā</s> three times, joined with the vyāhṛtis and the praṇava,
or the learned man should recite the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, and likewise the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>.
Then he should perform the sprinkling with the verse <s>Āpo hi ṣṭhā mayobhuvaḥ</s>,
and likewise with <s>Idam āpaḥ pravahata</s> and the vyāhṛtis.
Then, with water consecrated by mantras beginning with <s>Āpo hi ṣṭhā</s>,
immersed in the water with his face downward, he should recite the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s> three times.

children.text: drupadāṃ vātha sāvitrīṃ tadviṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam ||
children.translated_text: Or he should repeat the <s>Drupadā</s>, the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, or <s>Tad Viṣṇoḥ paramaṃ padam</s>,
or he may repeat the praṇava and remember <s>Hari</s>, the god of gods.

children.text: apaḥ pāṇau samādāya japtvā vai mārjane kṛte ||
children.translated_text: Taking water in his hand, having recited, and after performing the sprinkling,
he should place that water on his head; he is freed from all sins.
Having performed the sandhyā and sipped water, he should remember the Lord every day.
Then he should attend upon <s>Āditya</s>, with his joined palms holding upward-pointing flowers.
Having cast them, he should look at the god rising, though it is not possible to gaze directly.
He should do so with the mantras <s>Ud u tyaṃ citram</s> and <s>Tac cakṣus</s>.
With <s>Haṃsaḥ śuciṣat</s> and especially with the <s>Sāvitrī</s>,

children.text: anyaiḥ saurairvaidikaiśca gāyattrīṃ ca tato japet
children.translated_text: and with other Vedic solar mantras, he should then recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
Afterward, he should recite various mantras on the eastern bank and on a seat of kuśa grass.
Standing and looking at the sun, he should perform japa with collected mind.
With crystal, lotus-seed, rudrākṣa, or beads produced from putrajīva,

children.text: kartavyā tvakṣālā syādantarā tatra sā smṛtā
children.translated_text: a rosary should be used; there it is remembered as an intermediate one.
If his garment is wet, he should remain situated in the midst of the water;

children.text: anyathā ca śucau bhūmyāṃ darbheṣu ca samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: otherwise, he should sit collected on clean ground and on darbha grass.
Having turned around clockwise and then bowed down on the ground,
and having sipped water according to scripture, he should perform self-recitation according to his ability.
Then he should satisfy the gods, the seers, and the hosts of ancestors.
First uttering oṃkāra, he should say 'namaḥ' at the end and 'I satisfy.'
He should satisfy the gods and brahmarṣis with water mixed with unbroken grains.
With devotion he should satisfy the ancestors, gods, and sages according to the rule stated in his own sūtra.
The wise man should satisfy the divine seers, and the ancestors with handfuls of water.
For the gods he wears the sacred thread over the left shoulder; for libations to seers it is worn as a garland,

children.text: prācīnāvītī pitrye tu tena tīrthena bhārata
children.translated_text: but for the ancestral rite it is over the right shoulder, with that tīrtha of the hand, O <s>Bhārata</s>.

children.text: niṣpīḍya snānavastraṃ vai samācamya ca vāgyataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having wrung out his bathing cloth, sipped water, and restrained his speech,
he should worship the gods with their own mantras, with flowers, leaves, and water.
He should worship <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Śaṅkara</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and likewise <s>Madhusūdana</s>,
and other chosen deities, with devotion and free from anger, O <s>Hara</s>.
Or he should offer flowers and the like with the <s>Puruṣa</s> hymn.

children.text: āpo vā devatāḥ sarvāstena samyak samarcitāḥ
children.translated_text: All the deities are the waters; through that they are properly worshiped.
Having meditated on the deity, preceded by the praṇava, he should be composed in the water.
With reverence he should arrange the flowers separately.
For without worship there is no merit in a Vedic rite.
Therefore there, at the beginning, middle, and end, he should hold <s>Hari</s> in his mind,
with the mantra beginning "That of <s>Viṣṇu</s>" and also with the <s>Puruṣa</s> hymn.
And he should offer himself to <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whose splendor is stainless,
then, inwardly intent on him and peaceful, by means of the mantra "That of <s>Viṣṇu</s>."
With the unclear formula, he should worship <s>Hari</s> in the flower offering.
He should perform the sacrifice to the gods, the sacrifice to the ancestors, and likewise
the human sacrifice and the brahma-sacrifice: he should carry out the five sacrifices.

children.text: yadi syāttarpaṇād arvāg brayajñaṃ kuto bhavet
children.translated_text: If the brahma-sacrifice were after the tarpaṇa, how could it be the brahma-sacrifice?
Having performed the human sacrifice, he should then carry out svādhyāya, recitation of sacred learning.

children.text: vaiśvadevastu kartavyo devayajñaḥ sa tu smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The Vaiśvadeva is to be performed; that is remembered as the sacrifice to the gods.

children.text: bhūtayajñaḥ sa vai jñeyo bhūtebhyo yastvayaṃ baliḥ ||
children.translated_text: That bali offering which is for beings should be known as the bhūta-sacrifice.
To dogs, to dog-cook outcastes, and to fallen persons and the like,
the best of the twice-born should give food on the ground outside, and also to birds.
O excellent ones, one should feed a single Brahmin with the ancestors in view;
that daily śrāddha performed for them is the ancestor-sacrifice, bestowing onward passage.

children.text: uddhṛtya vā yathāśakti kiṃcid annaṃ samāhitaḥ
children.translated_text: Or, having set aside some food according to one's ability, with collected mind,
one should provide it to a twice-born man who knows the true meaning of the Veda.
One should honor a guest daily and bow to and worship a Brahmin
who is peaceful in mind, speech, and action, then welcoming him into one's own house.
A bhikṣā is said to be a single mouthful; that amount of food is four times as much.
The full portion, called hantakāra, is said to be four times that.
An atithi should be awaited for the length of time needed to milk a cow;
and an arriving guest should likewise be honored as an atithi according to one's ability.

children.text: bhikṣāṃ vai bhikṣave dadyād vidhivad brahmacāriṇe
children.translated_text: One should give alms according to rule to a bhikṣu and to a brahmacārin;
free from greed, one should give food according to one's ability to those who ask.
Restrained in speech and not disparaging the food, he eats together with his relatives.

children.text: akṛtvā tu dvijaḥ pañca mahāyajñān dvijottamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But if a twice-born man, O best of the twice-born, has not performed the five great sacrifices

children.text: bhuñjate cetsa mūḍhātmā tiryagyoniṃ ca gacchati
children.translated_text: and then eats, that deluded soul goes to an animal womb.
Daily study of the Veda according to ability, and fitness for the rites of the great sacrifices,
quickly destroy sins, as does worship of the gods.
He who, through delusion or laziness, does not perform worship of the deities

children.text: bhuṅkte sa yāti narakān sūkareṣveva jāyate
children.translated_text: and eats goes to hells and is born among pigs.
I shall explain impurity: one who is impure is always sinful.
Impurity comes from contact, and purity from avoiding contact.
All wise Brahmins declare impurity to last ten days
when there is death or birth among Brahmins, O best of the twice-born.
Until the cutting of teeth it is immediate; until the cūḍā tonsure it lasts one night.
After the initiation it is three nights; after that it is ten nights.
A Kṣatriya is purified after twelve days, and a Vaiśya after fifteen.

children.text: śudhyenmāsena vai śūdro yatīnāṃ nāsti pātakam
children.translated_text: A Śūdra is purified after a month; for ascetics there is no defilement.
In miscarriages the impurity is for as many nights as there were months of pregnancy.

children.text: iti gāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe nityakarmāśaucayornirūpaṇaṃ nāma pañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part of the eastern section, in the ācāra division, the fiftieth chapter, called "The Explanation of Daily Rite and Impurity."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Now then I shall explain the unsurpassed <s>dāna-dharma</s>, the religious law of giving:
the handing over of wealth to a proper recipient with faith.
Giving is described by those who know as granting the fruits of enjoyment and liberation.
One should acquire wealth lawfully, and its fruit is giving and enjoyment.
Teaching, officiating at sacrifice, and accepting gifts are said to be the livelihood;
usury, agriculture, trade, and the Kṣatriya livelihood he should avoid.
What is given to worthy recipients is called giving.
Giving is said to be fourfold: daily, occasional, desire-prompted, and pure.
Whatever is given day by day to one who cannot return a favor,
without aiming at a result, and regularly to a Brahmin,

children.text: yattu pāpopaśāntyai ca dīyate vidupāṃ kare
children.translated_text: and what is given into the hands of knowers for the pacification of sin,
that is designated occasional giving, practiced by good people.
What is given for offspring, victory, sovereignty, or heaven
is called desire-prompted giving by sages who reflect on <s>dharma</s>.
What is given to knowers of brahman for the pleasure of the Lord,
with a mind endowed with sattva, that giving is pure and auspicious.
He who gives land covered with sugarcane and rich in barley, wheat, and rice
to a knower of the Veda is not born again.

children.text: bhūmidānātparaṃ dānaṃ na bhūtaṃ na bhaviṣyati
children.translated_text: There has never been, nor will there be, a gift higher than the gift of land.
Having given knowledge to a Brahmin, one is honored in the world of <s>Brahmā</s>.
One should give day by day, with faith, to a brahmacārin;
freed from all sins, one would attain the station of brahman.

children.text: vaiśākhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ tu brāhmaṇānsapta pañca ca
children.translated_text: On the Vaiśākha full-moon day, seven or five Brahmins
the learned man should worship after fasting, with honey, sesame, and ghee.
Having honored them fully with fragrances and the like, he should have this recited, or say it himself:
"May <s>Dharmarāja</s> be pleased," according to what is present in his mind.
Whatever sin has been committed throughout life perishes at that very moment.
Placing sesame seeds on a black antelope skin, together with gold, honey, and ghee,

children.text: dadāti yastu viprāya sarvaṃ tarati duṣkṛtam
children.translated_text: the man who gives them to a Brahmin crosses over all evil.
Ghee-food and water, especially in Vaiśākha,
when assigned to <s>Dharmarāja</s> and given to Brahmins, free one from fear.
On the twelfth lunar day one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, fasting, as the destroyer of sins.
A man certainly becomes freed from all sins.
Whatever deity a man wishes to propitiate,
he should carefully honor brahmins and feed women and gods.
One who desires offspring should constantly worship <s>Purandara</s>.
But one who desires brahmanical splendor should honor brahmins with firm devotion to <s>Brahman</s>.
One desiring health should worship the sun; one desiring wealth should worship the fire.
But one desiring success in undertakings should worship <s>Vināyaka</s>.
One desiring enjoyments should worship the moon; one desiring strength should worship the wind.
One seeking liberation from all worldly existence should carefully worship <s>Hari</s>.
Whether without desire or filled with all desires, one should worship <s>Gadādhara</s>.
The giver of water obtains satisfaction; the giver of food obtains imperishable happiness.
The giver of sesame obtains desired offspring; the giver of a lamp obtains excellent sight.
The giver of land obtains everything; the giver of gold obtains long life.
The giver of a house obtains excellent dwellings; the giver of silver obtains excellent beauty.
The giver of clothing obtains residence in the world of <s>Candra</s>; the giver of a horse obtains residence in the world of the <s>Aśvins</s>.

children.text: anaḍuddaḥ śriyaṃ puṣṭāṃ godo bradhnasya viṣṭapam ||
children.translated_text: The giver of an ox obtains abundant prosperity; the giver of a cow obtains the heaven of <s>Bradhna</s>.
The giver of a vehicle and bed obtains a wife, and the giver of fearlessness obtains sovereignty.

children.text: dhānyadaḥ śāśvataṃ saukhyaṃ brahmado brahma śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: The giver of grain obtains lasting happiness; the giver of sacred knowledge obtains eternal <s>Brahman</s>.
A knower of the Veda, giving knowledge, is honored in heaven.
By giving fodder to cows one is released from all sins.
By giving fuel a man is born with a blazing fire.
Giving medicine, oil, and food for the relief of a sick person's disease,
he becomes free from disease, happy, and long-lived.
The path through the forest of sword-leaves, furnished with razor-edges,
and fierce heat, is crossed by a man who gives umbrellas and shoes.
Whatever is most desired in the world, and whatever is dear to him in his house,
that very thing should be given to a worthy person by one who wishes it to become imperishable.
At the solstitial passages, at the equinox, and at lunar and solar eclipses,
and at times such as saṃkrānti, what is given becomes imperishable.
At sacred fords such as <s>Prayāga</s>, and especially at <s>Gayā</s>,
there is no dharma here for beings higher than the dharma of giving.
For one who desires heaven, long life, and prosperity, giving is for the calming of sin.
But the sinful man who, through delusion, obstructs a gift being given to cows, brahmins, fire, or gods,
goes to an animal womb.
And he who does not give food and eatables in a time of famine,

children.text: mriyamāṇeṣu vipreṣu brahmahā sa tu garhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: while brahmins are dying, is reviled as a killer of <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe dānadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the fifty-first chapter, named the exposition of the dharma of giving.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Next I shall teach the rule of expiation, O twice-born ones.

children.text: brahmahā ca surāpaśca steyī ca gurutalpagaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The killer of a brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, and the violator of a guru's bed:
these are the sinners guilty of the five grave sins, and the fifth is one who associates with them.
The gods have declared secondary sins, beginning with the killing of a cow.

children.text: brahmahā dvādaśābdāni kuṭīṃ kṛtvā vane vaset
children.translated_text: The killer of a brahmin should make a hut and live in the forest for twelve years.
Or he should undertake fasting unto death, or else a fall from <s>Bhṛgu</s>.

children.text: jvalantaṃ vā viśedagniṃ jalaṃ vā praviśetsvayam
children.translated_text: Or he should enter a blazing fire, or enter water by himself.
Or, for the sake of a brahmin or for the sake of a cow, he should properly abandon his life.

children.text: dattvā cānnaṃ ca viduṣe brahmahatyāṃ vyapohati
children.translated_text: By giving food to a learned man, he removes the sin of killing a brahmin.
Or a twice-born man is released by bathing at the avabhṛtha bath of a horse sacrifice.
Or he should cause all his property to be given to a brahmin who knows the Veda.
At the world-renowned confluence of the flowing <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
a twice-born man, pure, bathing three times a day and fasting for three nights,
or a man bathing at <s>Setubandha</s>, is released from the sin of killing a brahmin.
Likewise, by bathing at <s>Kapālamocana</s> and at <s>Vārāṇasī</s>.
But the drinker of liquor, having drunk liquor heated to the color of fire, O best of the twice-born,
or milk, ghee, or cow urine, is released from that sin.
One who has stolen gold becomes released when struck down by kings with a club.
A twice-born man wearing rags should dwell in the wilderness, observing the vow of a brahmin-killer.
A brahmin who, deluded by desire, has mounted the wife of his guru,
should embrace a woman made of black iron, heated and blazing.
Those who go to a guru's wife should observe the vow of a brahmin-killer.

children.text: cāndrāyaṇāni vā kuryātpañca catvāri vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Or he should perform five <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vows, or again four.

children.text: patitena ca saṃsargaṃ kurute yastu vai dvijaḥ ||
children.translated_text: But whatever twice-born man associates with a fallen person,
for the removal of that sin, he should practice that person's very vow.
Or he should practice the heated kṛcchra penance for a year without negligence.
The gift of all one's property, according to rule, purifies all sins.
And a <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> performed according to rule, and also the atikṛcchra penance,
and going to a holy field such as <s>Gayā</s>, destroy sin.
He who, on reaching the new-moon lunar day, worships <s>Bhava</s>,
and feeds brahmins, is released from all sins.
Fasting on the fourteenth day in the dark fortnight, with collected mind,
to <s>Yama</s>, <s>Dharmarāja</s>, <s>Mṛtyu</s>, and <s>Antaka</s>,
and to <s>Vaivasvata</s>, <s>Kāla</s>, and the destroyer of all beings,
he should give seven handfuls of water, each mixed with sesame.

children.text: snātvā nadyāṃ tu pūrvāhne mucyate sarvapātakaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed in a river in the forenoon, he is released from all grave sins.
Celibacy, sleeping on the ground, fasting, and honoring twice-born men:
he should perform these during these vows, calm and self-controlled in mind.
Having fasted on the sixth lunar day in the bright fortnight, collected in mind,
he should worship the god <s>Bhānu</s> on the seventh; he is freed from all sins.
On the eleventh, fasting without food, after fully worshiping <s>Janārdana</s>,
on the twelfth of the bright fortnight he is released from great sins.
Austerity, recitation, service at <s>tīrthas</s>, and worship of gods and brahmins,
at times such as eclipses, destroy even great transgressions.
Even if a man is burdened with every sin, if at holy <s>tīrthas</s>
he gives up his life under a vow, he is freed from all sins.
A woman who enters the fire together with her husband raises up that husband,
even if he is a brahmin-killer, an ingrate, or stained by great transgression.

children.text: pativratā tu yā nārī bhartuḥ śuśrūṣaṇotsukā
children.translated_text: But a woman who is devoted to her husband and eager to serve him

children.text: na tasyā vidyate pāpamiha loke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: has no sin, either in this world or in the next.
So too the fortunate <s>Sītā</s>, famed through the three worlds, belonged to <s>Rāma</s>;
the goddess, wife of <s>Dāśarathi</s>, conquered the lord of the rākṣasas.
Having bathed at <s>Phalgu-tīrtha</s> and the other sacred places, one obtains the fruit of all observances;
so the blessed <s>Viṣṇu</s> said to me of old, O you whose vows are restrained.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe prāyaścittanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvipañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-second chapter, called 'The Explanation of Expiation,' in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s> of the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s> in the blessed great <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Thus <s>Brahmā</s> spoke, after hearing also of <s>Hari</s>'s eight treasures:
among them are <s>Padma</s> and <s>Mahāpadma</s>, and likewise <s>Makara</s> and <s>Kacchapa</s>;
<s>Mukunda</s>, <s>Kunda</s>, <s>Nīla</s>, and <s>Śaṅkha</s> are the other treasure.
These arise when prosperity is true; I shall tell their nature.
A man marked by <s>Padma</s> is born sāttvic;
that gracious-natured person gathers gold and the like.
He should collect silver and other things, and should give to ascetics, deities, and sacrificers.
One marked by <s>Mahāpadma</s> should give wealth and the like to a righteous person.
The two treasures, <s>Padma</s> and <s>Mahāpadma</s>, are remembered as sāttvic persons.
One marked by <s>Makara</s> stores up swords, arrows, spears, and the like.

children.text: dadyācchrutāya maitrīṃ ca yāti nityaṃ ca rājabhiḥ
children.translated_text: He gives to learned men and makes friendship, and he constantly moves among kings.

children.text: dravyārthaṃ śatruṇā nāśaṃ saṃgrāme cāpi saṃvrajet ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of wealth he may meet destruction from an enemy, even in battle.

children.text: makaraḥ kacchapaścaiva tāmasau tu nidhī smṛtau
children.translated_text: <s>Makara</s> and <s>Kacchapa</s> are remembered as the two tāmasic treasures.

children.text: kacchapī viśvasennaiva na bhuṅkena dadāti ca ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Kacchapa</s> man trusts no one; he neither enjoys his wealth nor gives it away.
He makes a deposit in the earth; that treasure too belongs to only one person.
One marked by the rajasic <s>Mukunda</s> gathers royal power.
Having enjoyed pleasures, he gives to singers and to courtesans and the like.
The <s>Nandī</s> treasure, made of rajas and tamas, becomes the support of a family.

children.text: stutaḥ prīto bhavati vai bahubhāryā bhavanti ca
children.translated_text: When praised, he is pleased, and he has many wives.
He grows slack toward former friends and forms affection for others.
One marked by <s>Nīla</s> is endowed with sattva and brilliance.
He gathers garments, grain, and the like, and makes tanks and similar works.
That treasure lasts for three generations, and he has mango groves and parks made.

children.text: ekasya syānnidhiḥ śaṅkhaḥ svayaṃ bhuṅkte dhanādikam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Śaṅkha</s> treasure is for one person alone; he himself enjoys wealth and the like.
His household eats bad food and does not wear fine clothes.
The <s>Śaṅkha</s> man is intent on supporting himself, and gives uselessly to another man.
When the marks are mixed in appearance, the treasures give mixed natures and results.
The form of the treasures has thus been stated by <s>Hari</s> also, to <s>Hara</s> and the others;
as <s>Hari</s> spoke of the treasury of the worlds and the rest, so I shall tell it.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe navanidhivarṇanaṃ nāma tripañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-third chapter, called 'Description of the Nine Treasures,' in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s> of the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s> in the blessed great <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
<s>Agnīdhra</s>, <s>Agnibāhu</s>, <s>Vapuṣmān</s>, and likewise <s>Dyutimān</s>,
<s>Medhā</s>, <s>Medhātithi</s>, <s>Bhavya</s>, <s>Śabala</s>, and <s>Putra</s>,
and <s>Jyotiṣmān</s> was born as the tenth; these were the sons of <s>Priyavrata</s>.
But <s>Medhā</s>, <s>Agnibāhu</s>, and <s>Putra</s>, the three sons, were devoted to yoga.
Greatly fortunate and remembering their former births, they rejoiced in freedom from kingship.

children.text: vibhajya sapta dvīpāni saptānāṃ pradadau nṛpaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Dividing the seven <s>dvīpas</s>, the king gave them to seven of his sons.
The earth, measured at fifty crores of <s>yojanas</s>, is spread out
over water; resting above the water, it is like a boat in river-water.
The islands called <s>Jambū</s> and <s>Plakṣa</s>, and another, <s>Śālmala</s>, O <s>Hara</s>,
<s>Kuśa</s>, <s>Krauñca</s>, <s>Śāka</s>, and <s>Puṣkara</s> as the seventh: these are the seven <s>dvīpas</s>.
These <s>dvīpas</s> are surrounded by seven oceans, each by its own seven seas,
of salt, sugarcane juice, wine, ghee, curds, milk, and water respectively.
Each <s>dvīpa</s> is twice the preceding <s>dvīpa</s>, and so is each ocean, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
In <s>Jambūdvīpa</s> stands <s>Meru</s>, extending a hundred thousand <s>yojanas</s>.
Its height is eighty-four thousand <s>yojanas</s>,
it penetrates sixteen thousand below, and is thirty-two thousand wide at the summit.
Below it is sixteen thousand, and it stands shaped like a pericarp.
<s>Himavān</s>, <s>Hemakūṭa</s>, and <s>Niṣadha</s> are to its south;

children.text: nīlaḥ śvetaśca śṛṅgī ca uttare varṣaparvatāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Śveta</s>, and <s>Śṛṅgī</s> are the northern mountains of the regions.

children.text: plakṣādiṣu narā rudra ye vasanti sanātanāḥ ||
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, the eternal men who dwell in <s>Plakṣa</s> and the other <s>dvīpas</s>,
O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, have no condition of yugas at all.
From <s>Agnīdhra</s>, lord of <s>Jambūdvīpa</s>, nine sons were born:
<s>Nābhi</s>, <s>Kimpuruṣa</s>, <s>Harivarṣa</s>, and <s>Ilāvṛta</s>,
<s>Ramya</s>, the one called <s>Hiraṇmaya</s>, <s>Kuru</s>, and <s>Bhadrāśva</s>,
and <s>Ketumāla</s>; the king gave to them regions bearing those names.
From <s>Nābhi</s>, through <s>Merudevī</s>, a son named <s>Ṛṣabha</s> was born, O <s>Hara</s>.

children.text: tatputro bharato nāma śālagrāme sthito vratī
children.translated_text: His son was named <s>Bharata</s>, a vow-holder dwelling at <s>Śālagrāma</s>.
<s>Sumati</s> was born from <s>Bharata</s>; his son was <s>Taijasa</s>.
And <s>Indradyumna</s> was his son; after him <s>Parameṣṭhin</s> is remembered.
<s>Pratīhāra</s> was his son, and <s>Pratihartṛ</s> was his son.
From him a son was then born, <s>Prastāra</s>; his son was mighty <s>Vibhu</s>.

children.text: pṛthuśca tatsuto nakto naktasyāpi gayaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: And <s>Pṛthu</s> was his son; <s>Nakta</s> was his son, and <s>Gaya</s> is remembered as <s>Nakta</s>'s son.
<s>Nara</s> was <s>Gaya</s>'s son; his son became <s>Virāḍ</s>.
Then the wise and very splendid <s>Bhauvana</s> was his son.
<s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> was born; from <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> came <s>Virajā</s>, and <s>Rajas</s> too was his son.
From <s>Rajas</s> came <s>Śatajit</s>; his son is remembered as <s>Viṣvagjyotis</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhuvanakośavarṇanopayogipriyavratavaṃśanirūpaṇaṃ nāma catuḥpañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the eastern section called the first part, in the ācāra division, the fifty-fourth chapter, called "The Explanation of <s>Priyavrata</s>'s Lineage Useful for the Description of the World-Cosmos."
<s>Hari</s> said:
In the middle is <s>Ilāvṛta</s> varṣa; to the east is the wondrous <s>Bhadrāśva</s>.
To the southeast is the varṣa <s>Hiraṇvān</s>, O <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.
Then <s>Kimpuruṣa</s> varṣa is remembered as lying south of <s>Meru</s>.
<s>Bhārata</s> is said to be to the south, and <s>Hari</s> to the southwest.
To the west is <s>Ketumāla</s>, and <s>Ramyaka</s> is to the northwest.
And to the north is the varṣa of <s>Kuru</s>, covered with wish-fulfilling trees.

children.text: siddhiḥ svābhāvikī rudra varjayitvā tu bhāratam
children.translated_text: O <s>Rudra</s>, natural perfection exists there, except in <s>Bhārata</s>.
<s>Indradvīpa</s>, <s>Kaśerumat</s>, <s>Tāmravarṇa</s>, and <s>Gabhastimat</s>,
<s>Nāgadvīpa</s>, <s>Kaṭāha</s>, <s>Siṃhala</s>, and also <s>Vāruṇa</s>:
this, surrounded by the ocean, is the ninth dvīpa (island-continent) among them.
To its east stand the <s>Kirātas</s>; to the west are the <s>Yavanas</s>.

children.text: andhrā dakṣiṇato rudra turaṣkās tvapi cottare ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Andhras</s> are to the south, O <s>Rudra</s>, and the <s>Turuṣkas</s> also to the north.
<s>Brāhmaṇas</s>, <s>Kṣatriyas</s>, <s>Vaiśyas</s>, and <s>Śūdras</s> dwell in the interior.
<s>Mahendra</s>, <s>Malaya</s>, <s>Sahya</s>, <s>Śuktimat</s>, and <s>Ṛkṣa</s> mountain,
together with <s>Vindhya</s> and <s>Pāriyātra</s>: these are the seven family-mountains here.

children.text: vedasmṛtir narmadā ca varadā surasā śivā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vedasmṛti</s>, <s>Narmadā</s>, <s>Varadā</s>, <s>Surasā</s>, and <s>Śivā</s>,

children.text: tāpī payoṣṇī sarayūḥ kāverī gomatī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Tāpī</s>, <s>Payoṣṇī</s>, <s>Sarayū</s>, <s>Kāverī</s>, and also <s>Gomatī</s>,
<s>Godāvarī</s>, <s>Bhīmarathī</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇī</s>, the great river,
<s>Ketumālā</s>, <s>Tāmraparṇī</s>, <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
<s>Ṛṣikulyā</s>, <s>Kāverī</s>, <s>Mattagaṅgā</s>, and <s>Payasvinī</s>,

children.text: vidarbhā ca śatadrūśca nadyaḥ pāpaharāḥ śubhāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Vidarbhā</s> and <s>Śatadrū</s> are auspicious rivers that remove sin.
The people beginning with those of <s>Madhyadeśa</s> drink the waters of these rivers.
The <s>Pāñcālas</s>, <s>Kurus</s>, <s>Matsyas</s>, <s>Yaudheyas</s>, together with the <s>Paṭaccaras</s>,
the <s>Kuntis</s> and <s>Śūrasenas</s> are remembered as peoples of <s>Madhyadeśa</s>.
O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>, the peoples called <s>Pādmas</s>, <s>Sūtas</s>, <s>Māgadhas</s>, and <s>Cedis</s>,
the <s>Kāśis</s>, the <s>Videhas</s>, and also the <s>Kosalas</s> are in the eastern quarter.
The <s>Kaliṅgas</s>, <s>Vaṅgas</s>, <s>Puṇḍras</s>, <s>Aṅgas</s>, <s>Vaidarbhas</s>, and also the <s>Mūlakas</s>
are remembered as the countries dwelling within the <s>Vindhya</s> region, to the southeast.
The inhabitants of <s>Pulanda</s>, <s>Aśmaka</s>, <s>Jīmūta</s>, and <s>Naya</s> territory,
and the <s>Karṇāṭas</s>, <s>Kambojas</s>, and <s>Ghaṇas</s>, dwell in the southern region.
The <s>Ambaṣṭhas</s>, <s>Draviḍas</s>, <s>Lāṭas</s>, <s>Kāmbojas</s>, <s>Strīmukhas</s>, and <s>Śakas</s>,
and likewise the inhabitants of <s>Ānarta</s>, should be known as being in the southwest.
The <s>Strīrājyas</s>, <s>Saindhavas</s>, <s>Mlecchas</s>, <s>Nāstikas</s>, and also the <s>Yavanas</s>

children.text: paścimena ca vijñeyā māthurā naiṣadhaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: should be known as western, together with the <s>Māthuras</s> and <s>Naiṣadhas</s>.
The <s>Māṇḍavyas</s>, <s>Tuṣāras</s>, <s>Mūlikas</s>, <s>Aśvamukhas</s>, and <s>Khaśas</s>,
the <s>Mahākeśas</s> and <s>Mahānāsas</s> are countries in the northwest.
The <s>Lambakas</s>, <s>Stananāgas</s>, <s>Mādras</s>, <s>Gāndhāras</s>, and <s>Bāhlikas</s>,
and the <s>Mlecchas</s> dwelling in the <s>Himācala</s> resort to the northern direction.
The <s>Trigartas</s>, <s>Nīlas</s>, <s>Kolātas</s>, <s>Brahmaputras</s>, and <s>Saṭaṅkaṇas</s>,
the <s>Abhīṣāhas</s>, together with the <s>Kāśmīras</s>, are spoken of in the northern division.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhuvanakośavarṇanaṃ nāma pañcapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the eastern section called the first part, in the ācāra division, the fifty-fifth chapter, called "The Description of the World-Cosmos."
<s>Hari</s> said:
There were seven sons of <s>Medhātithi</s>, the lord of <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>.
The eldest was named <s>Śāntabhava</s>; next after him was <s>Śiśira</s>.

children.text: sukhodayastathā nandaḥ śivaḥ kṣemaka eva ca
children.translated_text: Then came <s>Sukhodaya</s>, <s>Nanda</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Kṣemaka</s>.
And <s>Dhruva</s> was the seventh of them; they were the lords of <s>Plakṣadvīpa</s>.
<s>Gomeda</s>, <s>Candra</s>, <s>Nārada</s>, and likewise <s>Dundubhi</s>,
<s>Somaka</s>, <s>Sumanas</s>, and <s>Vaibhrāja</s> as the seventh are the mountains there.

children.text: anutaptā śikhī caiva vipāśā tridivā kramuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Anutaptā</s>, <s>Śikhī</s>, <s>Vipāśā</s>, <s>Tridivā</s>, <s>Kramu</s>,
<s>Amṛtā</s>, and <s>Sukṛtā</s>: these seven are the rivers there.
<s>Vapuṣmat</s> was lord of <s>Śālmaladvīpa</s>; his sons gave their names to the varṣas.
<s>Śveta</s>, then <s>Harita</s>, <s>Jīmūta</s>, and <s>Rohita</s>,
<s>Vaidyuta</s>, <s>Mānasa</s>, and <s>Suprabha</s> as the seventh:
<s>Kumuda</s>, <s>Unnata</s>, <s>Droṇa</s>, then <s>Mahiṣa</s> and <s>Balāhaka</s>,
<s>Krauñca</s> and <s>Kakudmat</s>: these indeed are the mountains; and the rivers are these:

children.text: yonitoyā vitṛṣṇā ca candrā śuklā vimocanī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Yonitoyā</s>, <s>Vitṛṣṇā</s>, <s>Candrā</s>, <s>Śuklā</s>, and <s>Vimocanī</s>,
with <s>Vidhṛti</s> as their seventh; they are remembered as givers of the pacification of sin.
Now listen to the seven sons of <s>Jyotiṣmat</s> in <s>Kuśadvīpa</s>.
<s>Udbhida</s>, <s>Veṇumat</s>, <s>Dvairatha</s>, <s>Lambana</s>, and <s>Dhṛti</s>,
then <s>Prabhākara</s> and <s>Kapila</s>: the order of the varṣas bears their names.
<s>Vidruma</s>, <s>Hemaśaila</s>, <s>Dyutimat</s>, and <s>Puṣpavat</s>,
<s>Kuśeśaya</s>, <s>Hari</s>, and <s>Mandarācala</s> as the seventh are there.
<s>Dhūtapāpā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Pavitrā</s>, and <s>Saṃmati</s>,
<s>Vidyudabhrā</s> and another, <s>Mahī</s>: these rivers remove all sins.
In <s>Krauñcadvīpa</s> there were seven noble sons of the great-souled <s>Dyutimat</s>:
<s>Kuśala</s>, <s>Mandaga</s>, <s>Uṣṇa</s>, <s>Pīvara</s>, and then <s>Andhakāraka</s>;
and <s>Muni</s> and <s>Dundubhi</s>; these seven were his sons, O <s>Hara</s>.
<s>Krauñca</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and the third, <s>Andhakāraka</s>;
the fifth was <s>Divāvṛt</s>; another was <s>Dundubhi</s>, and <s>Puṇḍarīkavān</s>.
<s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Kumudvatī</s>, <s>Sandhyā</s>, <s>Rātrī</s>, and <s>Manojavā</s>,
<s>Khyāti</s> and <s>Puṇḍarīkā</s>: these seven are rivers flowing through the <s>varṣas</s> (regions).
From <s>Bhavya</s>, lord of <s>Śākadvīpa</s>, seven sons were born:
<s>Jalada</s>, <s>Kumāra</s>, <s>Sukumāra</s>, <s>Uruṇī</s>, and <s>Baka</s>,
<s>Kusumoda</s>, <s>Samodārki</s>, and the seventh, <s>Mahādruma</s>.

children.text: sukumārī kumārī ca nalinī dhenukā ca yā
children.translated_text: <s>Sukumārī</s>, <s>Kumārī</s>, <s>Nalinī</s>, and <s>Dhenukā</s>,

children.text: ikṣuśca veṇukā caiva gabhastī saptamī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ikṣu</s>, <s>Veṇukā</s>, and likewise <s>Gabhastī</s> as the seventh.
From <s>Śabala</s>, lord of <s>Puṣkara</s>, came <s>Mahāvīra</s> and <s>Dhātaki</s>,
and there were just two <s>varṣas</s> (regions), with Mount <s>Mānasottara</s>.
It rises upward fifty thousand yojanas,
and is just as broad, circular on every side.
<s>Puṣkara</s> is encircled by the ocean of sweet water;
beyond the sweet-water ocean the arrangement of the worlds is seen.
There is a golden land twice as large, devoid of all living beings.
Then comes Mount <s>Lokāloka</s>, ten thousand yojanas broad,
the mountain is covered by darkness, and the darkness too by the shell of the cosmic egg.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhuvanakośavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣaṭpañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the eastern section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the fifty-sixth chapter, named "The Description of the Arrangement of the Worlds."
<s>Hari</s> said:
The height of the earth too is said to be seventy thousand yojanas;
each <s>pātāla</s> is ten thousand, O <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.

children.text: atalaṃ vitalaṃ caiva nitalaṃ ca gabhastimat
children.translated_text: They are <s>Atala</s>, <s>Vitala</s>, <s>Nitala</s>, and <s>Gabhastimat</s>,

children.text: mahākhyaṃ sutalaṃ cāgryaṃ pātālaṃ cāpi saptamam ||
children.translated_text: the one called <s>Mahā</s>, excellent <s>Sutala</s>, and <s>Pātāla</s> as the seventh.
They are black, white, red, yellow, gravelly, rocky, and golden;
and there especially the <s>Daityas</s> and serpents dwell.

children.text: raudre tu puṣkaradvīpe narakāḥ santi tāñchṛṇu
children.translated_text: But in dreadful <s>Puṣkaradvīpa</s> there are hells; hear of them:
<s>Raurava</s>, <s>Sūkara</s>, <s>Rodha</s>, <s>Tāla</s>, and likewise <s>Vinaśana</s>;
<s>Mahājvāla</s>, <s>Taptakumbha</s>, <s>Lavaṇa</s>, and <s>Vimohita</s>;
the one called <s>Rudhira</s>, <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, <s>Kṛmiśa</s>, and <s>Kṛmibhojana</s>;
<s>Asipattravana</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, and <s>Nānābhakṣa</s>, terrible indeed;
likewise <s>Pūyavaha</s>, <s>Pāpa</s>, <s>Vahnijvāla</s>, and <s>Adhaḥśiras</s>;
<s>Saṃdaṃśa</s>, <s>Kṛṣṇasūtra</s>, <s>Tamas</s>, and <s>Avīci</s>;
<s>Śvabhojana</s>, then <s>Apratiṣṭha</s>, and <s>Uṣṇavīci</s> are remembered as hells.
In them sinners are cooked: poisoners, assailants with weapons, and arsonists.

children.text: uparyupari vai lokā rudra bhūtādayaḥ sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Above and above are worlds, O <s>Rudra</s>, where the elements and the rest are established.
That cosmic egg is enclosed by water, fire, wind, ether, and also by <s>bhūtādi</s> (the elemental source).

children.text: tadaṇḍaṃ mahatā rudra pradhānena ca veṣṭitam ||
children.translated_text: That egg, O <s>Rudra</s>, is enveloped by <s>mahat</s> (cosmic intelligence) and by <s>pradhāna</s> (primordial matter).
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s> stands pervading the egg tenfold.

children.text: iti gāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhuvanakośagatāpātalanarakādinirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the eastern section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the fifty-seventh chapter, named "The Explanation of the <s>Pātālas</s>, Hells, and Other Things in the Arrangement of the Worlds."
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall describe the measured arrangement of the sun and the others; listen to me.
The chariot of <s>Bhāskara</s> is nine thousand yojanas,
and its pole is twice that, O <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.
Its axle is seven and a half <s>koṭis</s> of yojanas, with additional <s>niyutas</s>,
and on that the wheel is fixed.
With three hubs, five spokes, and six rims, it is of the nature of an imperishable axle;
the whole wheel of time, consisting of the year, is established there.
The second axle of <s>Vivasvat</s> is forty thousand,
plus another five and a half thousand, for the chariot, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.
The measure of the two axles is the measure of the two half-yokes.
The short axle, equal to half that yoke, is at the support of <s>Dhruva</s> for the chariot,
while on the second axle that wheel is set upon Mount <s>Mānasa</s>.
The <s>Gāyatrī</s>, together with <s>Bṛhatī</s>, <s>Uṣṇih</s>, <s>Jagatī</s>, and <s>Triṣṭubh</s>,
and <s>Anuṣṭubh</s> and <s>Paṅkti</s> are said to be the meters that are the horses of the sun.
<s>Dhātā</s>, <s>Kratu</s>, <s>Sthalā</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, and <s>Vāsuki</s>,
<s>Rathakṛt</s>, <s>Grāmaṇī</s>, <s>Heti</s>, and <s>Tumburu</s> are in the month of <s>Caitra</s>.
<s>Aryaman</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, <s>Rathaujā</s>, and <s>Puñjikasthalā</s>,
<s>Praheti</s>, <s>Kacchanīra</s>, and <s>Nārada</s> are likewise in <s>Mādhava</s>.
<s>Mitra</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, the <s>rakṣas</s> <s>Pauruṣeya</s>, and <s>Menakā</s>,

children.text: hāhā rathasvanaścaiva jyeṣṭhe bhāno rathe sthitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hāhā</s> and <s>Rathasvana</s> are stationed in <s>Bhānu</s>'s chariot in <s>Jyeṣṭha</s>.
<s>Varuṇa</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Sahajanyā</s>, <s>Kuhū</s>, and <s>Budha</s>,
with <s>Rathacitra</s> and <s>Śukra</s>, dwell in the month called <s>Āṣāḍha</s>.
<s>Indra</s>, <s>Viśvāvasu</s>, <s>Srotas</s>, <s>Ailāpatra</s>, and <s>Aṅgiras</s>,

children.text: pramlocā ca nabhasyete sarpāścārke tu santi vai ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Pramlocā</s>; in <s>Nabhasya</s> these, including the serpents, are present in the sun.
<s>Vivasvān</s>, <s>Ugrasena</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Āpūraṇa</s>,
<s>Anumlocā</s>, <s>Śaṅkhapāla</s>, and <s>Vyāghra</s> are likewise in <s>Bhādrapada</s>.
<s>Pūṣan</s>, <s>Suruci</s>, <s>Dhātā</s>, <s>Gautama</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s>,
another, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Ghṛtācī</s> dwell in the sun in <s>Āśvayuja</s>.
<s>Viśvāvasu</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, and <s>Airāvata</s> then,
<s>Viśvācī</s>, <s>Senajit</s>, and <s>Āpa</s> are the presiding ones in <s>Kārtika</s>.
And <s>Aṃśu</s>, <s>Kāśyapa</s>, <s>Tārkṣya</s>, <s>Mahāpadma</s>, and <s>Urvaśī</s>...
<s>Citrasena</s> and likewise <s>Vidyut</s> are the presiding ones for <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>.
<s>Kratu</s>, <s>Bharga</s>, likewise <s>Ūrṇāyu</s>, <s>Sphūrja</s>, and <s>Karkoṭaka</s>,
and <s>Ariṣṭanemi</s> too, and the other, <s>Pūrvacitti</s>, an excellent apsaras,
these seven dwell in the solar orb in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>.
Then <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s> and <s>Jamadagni</s>, <s>Kambala</s>, and <s>Tilottamā</s>,
then <s>Brahmāpeta</s>, <s>Ṛtajit</s>, and <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> as the seventh,
these seven dwell in the solar orb in the month of <s>Māgha</s>.
<s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Aśvatara</s>, <s>Rambhā</s>, <s>Sūryavarcā</s>, and <s>Satyajit</s>,
and <s>Viśvāmitra</s>, the rakṣas, and <s>Yajñāpeta</s> are indeed in <s>Phālguna</s>.
In the orb of <s>Savitṛ</s>, O <s>Brahman</s>, they are strengthened by the power of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: stuvanti munayaḥ sūryaṃ gandharvair gīyate puraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The sages praise <s>Sūrya</s>, and he is sung before him by the gandharvas.
The apsarases go dancing as attendants of the Sun through the night.
The serpents bear him, and the gathering of the reins is done by the yakṣas.
The <s>Vālakhilyas</s> too sit around him, surrounding him on every side.
The chariot of <s>Soma</s> has three wheels; its horses are white as jasmine.
Ten are yoked on the left and right, and by that chariot he moves.
The chariot of the son of the Moon is formed from water, fire, and material substance.
It is yoked with eight tawny horses, swift as the wind.
With its guard-rail and rear-frame, it is yoked with horses born from the earth.
The great chariot of <s>Śukra</s> also has side-fittings and a banner.
The chariot of the earth-born one too is like heated gold.

children.text: aṣṭāśvaḥ kāñcanaḥ śrīmān bhaumasyāpi ratho mahān ||
children.translated_text: The great chariot of <s>Bhauma</s> is golden, splendid, and drawn by eight horses.
It is joined to ruby-red horses born from fire.
In a golden chariot yoked with eight pale steeds,

children.text: tiṣṭhaṃstiṣṭhati varṣaṃ vai rāśau rāśau bṛhaspatiḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Bṛhaspati</s> remains, staying for a year in each zodiacal sign.
The chariot is yoked with dappled horses born from the sky.
Mounting it, slow-moving <s>Śanaiścara</s> goes slowly.
The horses of <s>Svarbhānu</s> are eight, bee-colored, and his chariot is smoky.
Once yoked, O lord of beings, O <s>Śiva</s>, they carry it without ceasing.
Likewise the horses of <s>Ketu</s>'s chariot are eight, swift as the wind.
They have the color of chaff-smoke and are red like lac-dye.
The islands, rivers, mountains, oceans, and worlds are the body of <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhuvanakośanirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭapañcāśattamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-eighth chapter, called 'Description of the World-System,' in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s> of the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s> in the blessed great <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Having stated the stellar wheel and the measure of the earth, <s>Keśava</s> spoke
the four-lakh essence of jyotiṣa to <s>Rudra</s> for all time.
<s>Hari</s> said:
The <s>Kṛttikās</s> have <s>Agni</s> as deity; the <s>Rohiṇīs</s> are remembered as belonging to <s>Brahmā</s>.
The <s>Ilvalās</s> have <s>Soma</s> as deity, and <s>Ārdrā</s> is declared to be <s>Raudra</s>.
<s>Punarvasu</s> has <s>Aditi</s>, and <s>Tiṣya</s> has <s>Guru</s> as deity.
The <s>Aśleṣās</s> have the serpents as deity, and the <s>Maghās</s> have the ancestors as deity.
The <s>Pūrvaphalgunīs</s> belong to <s>Bhaga</s>, and the latter one likewise to <s>Aryaman</s>.

children.text: sāvitraśca tathā hastā citrā tvaṣṭā prakīrtitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Hasta</s> belongs to <s>Savitṛ</s>, and <s>Citrā</s> is proclaimed to belong to <s>Tvaṣṭṛ</s>.
<s>Svātī</s> is proclaimed as the asterism whose deity is <s>Vāyu</s>.
<s>Viśākhā</s> is said to have <s>Indra</s> and <s>Agni</s> as deities, O <s>Vṛṣabhadhvaja</s>.
<s>Anurādhā</s> is the asterism of <s>Mitra</s>; <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> is proclaimed as belonging to <s>Śakra</s>.
Likewise <s>Mūla</s> is said by those who know to have <s>Nirṛti</s> as deity.
The former <s>Āṣāḍhās</s> belong to the waters, while the latter have the <s>Viśvedevas</s> as deities.
<s>Abhijit</s> is said to belong to <s>Brahmā</s>, and <s>Śravaṇa</s> is remembered as belonging to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: vāsavastu tathā ṛkṣaṃ dhaniṣṭhā procyate budhaiḥ
children.translated_text: The asterism <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> is said by the wise to belong to the <s>Vasus</s>.

children.text: tathā śatabhiṣā proktaṃ nakṣatraṃ vāruṇaṃ śiva ||
children.translated_text: Likewise the asterism <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> is said to belong to <s>Varuṇa</s>, O <s>Śiva</s>.
The former <s>Bhādrapadā</s> is <s>Āja</s>, and the latter likewise belongs to <s>Ahirbudhnya</s>.
<s>Revatī</s> is the asterism of <s>Pūṣan</s>, and <s>Aśvayuj</s> has the <s>Aśvins</s> as deity.
The asterism <s>Bharaṇī</s> is likewise said to belong to <s>Yama</s>; these are the deities of the asterisms.
<s>Brahmāṇī</s> stands in the east on the lunar days of the first and ninth.
<s>Māheśvarī</s> is in the north on the second and tenth lunar days.

children.text: pañcamyāṃ ca trayodaśyāṃ vārāhī dakṣiṇe sthitā ||
children.translated_text: On the fifth and thirteenth, <s>Vārāhī</s> stands in the south.
On the sixth and fourteenth, <s>Indrāṇī</s> stands in the west.
On the seventh and on the full-moon day, <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s> is in the region of the wind.
At the conjunction of the eighth and the new-moon day, <s>Mahālakṣmī</s> is in the region of <s>Īśa</s>.
On the eleventh and third lunar days, <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s> is in the fire-corner.

children.text: dvādaśyāṃ ca caturthyāṃ tu kaumārī nairṛte tathā
children.translated_text: On the twelfth and fourth lunar days, <s>Kaumārī</s> is likewise in the southwest.
When the <s>Yoginī</s> is facing one directly, one should not undertake departure and the like.
<s>Aśvinī</s>, the asterism of <s>Mitra</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, and <s>Punarvasu</s>,

children.text: puṣyā hastā tathā jyeṣṭhā prasthāne śreṣṭhamucyate ||
children.translated_text: with <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, and <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s>, are said to be best for setting out.
The five asterisms beginning with <s>Hasta</s>, and the three <s>Uttarās</s> as well,

children.text: aśvinī rohiṇī puṣyā dhaniṣṭhā ca punarvasū ||
children.translated_text: <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, and <s>Punarvasu</s>,
are remembered as the best group of asterisms for clothing and outer garments.
<s>Kṛttikā</s>, <s>Bharaṇī</s>, <s>Aśleṣā</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Mūla</s>, and <s>Viśākhā</s>,

children.text: trīṇi pūrvā tathā caiva adhovakrāḥ prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: and likewise the three <s>Pūrvās</s>, are proclaimed to be downward-facing.
Under these, wells, tanks and the like, pits, fields, grasses,
the digging for a temple, and also the digging for treasure,
calculation, the commencement of astrology, and entrance into mines and caves
should be done as downward-going acts, along with other such things, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>.

children.text: revatī cāśvinī citrā svātī hastā punarvasū ||
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, <s>Svātī</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, and <s>Punarvasu</s>,

children.text: anurādhā mṛgo jyeṣṭhā ete pārśvamukhāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Anurādhā</s>, <s>Mṛgaśiras</s>, and <s>Jyeṣṭhā</s> are remembered as side-facing.
The taming of elephants, camels, horses, bulls, and buffaloes,
One should sow seeds, undertake going and coming, and similar acts,
and set in motion wheels, machines, carts, boats, and the like.
Whatever works are to be done at the sides should also be done in these.
<s>Rohiṇī</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, and the three <s>Uttarās</s>,

children.text: vāruṇaṃ śravaṇaṃ caiva nava cordhvamukhāḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: the <s>Vāruṇa</s> star and <s>Śravaṇa</s>: these nine are remembered as upward-facing.

children.text: eṣu rājyābhiṣekaṃ ca paṭṭabandhaṃ ca kārayet ||
children.translated_text: Under these one should have a royal consecration and the binding of the diadem performed.
All elevated, upward-facing undertakings should be performed under these upward-facing stars.

children.text: caturthī cāśubhā ṣaṣṭhī aṣṭamī navamī tathā ||
children.translated_text: The fourth lunar day is inauspicious, and so are the sixth, eighth, and ninth,

children.text: amāvāsyā pūrṇimā ca tadvādaśī ca caturdaśī
children.translated_text: as well as new moon, full moon, the twelfth, and the fourteenth.
The first lunar day, when not in the bright fortnight, is best; the second is best with <s>Candrasūnu</s>.
The third is best with <s>Bhūmiputra</s>, and the fourth with <s>Śanaiścara</s>.

children.text: gurau śubhā pañcamī syāt ṣaṣṭhī maṅgalaśukrayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: The fifth is auspicious on the day of <s>Guru</s>; the sixth is so on the days of <s>Maṅgala</s> and <s>Śukra</s>.
The seventh is auspicious with <s>Somaputra</s>; the eighth with <s>Kuja</s> or <s>Bhāskara</s>.

children.text: navamī candravāreṇa daśamī tu gurau śubhā ||
children.translated_text: The ninth is auspicious on the lunar weekday, and the tenth on the day of <s>Guru</s>.
For the eleventh, <s>Guru</s> and <s>Śukra</s> are auspicious; for the twelfth, again <s>Budha</s> is auspicious.
For the thirteenth, <s>Śukra</s> and <s>Bhauma</s> are auspicious; the fourteenth is best on the day of <s>Śani</s>.
Full moon and also new moon are best when they fall on the day of <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: dvādaśīṃ dahate bhānuḥ śaśī caikādaśīṃ dahet ||
children.translated_text: The sun burns the twelfth lunar day, and the moon burns the eleventh.

children.text: kujo dahecca daśamīṃ navamīṃ ca budho dahet
children.translated_text: <s>Kuja</s> burns the tenth, and <s>Budha</s> burns the ninth.

children.text: aṣṭamīṃ dahate jīvaḥ saptamīṃ bhārgavo dahet ||
children.translated_text: <s>Jīva</s> burns the eighth, and <s>Bhārgava</s> burns the seventh.
The son of the sun burns the sixth; in matters such as travel, there is indeed no favorable result.
On the first and ninth lunar days, and on the fourteenth and eighth,
one should completely avoid departure on a Wednesday.
In <s>Meṣa</s> and <s>Karkaṭaka</s> the sixth is burnt; in <s>Kanyā</s> and <s>Mithuna</s>, the eighth.

children.text: vṛṣe kumbhe caturthī ca dvādaśī makare tule
children.translated_text: In <s>Vṛṣa</s> and <s>Kumbha</s> the fourth is burnt; the twelfth is burnt in <s>Makara</s> and <s>Tulā</s>.
The tenth is burnt in <s>Vṛścika</s> and <s>Siṃha</s>; the fourteenth in <s>Dhanuḥ</s> and <s>Mīna</s>.

children.text: etā dagdhā na gantavyaṃ pīḍādiḥ kila mānavaiḥ
children.translated_text: These are burnt; people should not travel under them, for affliction and the like arise.
The triad beginning with <s>Viśākhā</s> on Sunday, and the triad beginning with <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> on Monday,
the triad beginning with <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> on Tuesday, and, on Wednesday, the triad beginning with <s>Revatī</s>,
the triad beginning with <s>Rohiṇī</s> on the day of <s>Jīva</s>, and the triad beginning with <s>Puṣya</s> on Friday, O <s>Śiva</s>,
and on Saturday one should avoid the triad beginning with <s>Uttarāphālgunī</s>.
In these yogas there will be portents, death, disease, and the like.
The sun in <s>Mūla</s>, the moon in <s>Śravaṇa</s>, and <s>Kuja</s> in <s>Uttaraproṣṭhapadā</s>,
<s>Budha</s> in the <s>Kṛttikās</s>, and, under <s>Guru</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>,
<s>Pūrvaphalgunī</s> on Friday, and <s>Svātī</s> on the day of <s>Śanaiścara</s>:
these are amṛta-yogas, accomplishing all undertakings.
A time that brings weakness and is undesirable and dull
is to be recognized, beginning with parvan-days and the like, by those expert in time.
After combining the syllables and measures of the names of woman and man, and dividing by three,
if the remainder is two there is destruction for the woman; for the man it occurs when the remainder is one or zero.

children.text: viṣkambhe ghaṭikāḥ pañca śūle sapta prakīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Viṣkambha</s> there are five ghaṭikās; in <s>Śūla</s>, seven are proclaimed.
Six are proclaimed in <s>Gaṇḍa</s> and <s>Atigaṇḍa</s>, and nine in <s>Vyāghāta</s> and <s>Vajra</s>.

children.text: vyatīpāte ca parighe vaidhṛte ca dine dine
children.translated_text: In <s>Vyatīpāta</s>, <s>Parigha</s>, and <s>Vaidhṛti</s>, day by day,
these are joined with death; therefore one should avoid all acts during them.

children.text: haste 'rkaśca guruḥ puṣye anurādhā budhe śubhā
children.translated_text: The sun in <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Guru</s> in <s>Puṣya</s>, and <s>Anurādhā</s> on Wednesday are auspicious.

children.text: rohiṇī ca śanau śreṣṭhā saumaṃ somena vai śubham ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rohiṇī</s> on Saturday is excellent, and the lunar star with Monday is auspicious.

children.text: śukre ca revatī śreṣṭhā aśvinī maṅgale śubhā
children.translated_text: <s>Revatī</s> is excellent on Friday, and <s>Aśvinī</s> is auspicious on Tuesday.
These are siddhi-yogas, destroyers of all faults.

children.text: bhārgave bhaparaṇī caiva some citrā vṛṣadhvaja
children.translated_text: <s>Bharaṇī</s> on Friday, and <s>Citrā</s> on Monday, O <s>Vṛṣadhvaja</s>,

children.text: bhaume caivottarāṣāḍhā dhaniṣṭhā ca budhe hara ||
children.translated_text: <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s> on Tuesday, and <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> on Wednesday, O <s>Hara</s>,

children.text: garau śatabhiṣā rudra śukre vai rohiṇī tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> under <s>Guru</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, and likewise <s>Rohiṇī</s> on Friday,

children.text: śanau ca revatī śambho viṣayogāḥ prakīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Revatī</s> on Saturday, O <s>Śambhu</s>, are proclaimed as viṣa-yogas.
<s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Punarvasu</s>, and <s>Revatī</s> together with <s>Citrā</s>,

children.text: śravaṇaṃ ca dhaniṣṭhā ca hastāśvanīmṛgās tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śravaṇa</s>, <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s>, <s>Hasta</s>, <s>Aśvinī</s>, and <s>Mṛgaśiras</s> likewise:
under <s>Śatabhiṣā</s> too a man should perform birth rites and the like.
<s>Viśākhā</s>, the three <s>Uttarās</s>, <s>Maghā</s>, <s>Ārdrā</s>, and <s>Bharaṇī</s>,
<s>Āśleṣā</s> and <s>Kṛttikā</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>, are death-giving for departure.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe jyotiḥśāstre nakṣatrataddevatādagdhayogādinirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikonaṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the fifty-ninth chapter, called 'Description of the Lunar Mansions, Their Deities, Burnt Yogas, and So On,' in the <s>Jyotiḥśāstra</s> section of the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, named the first part of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the blessed great <s>Garuḍapurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:

children.text: ṣaḍāditye daśā jñeyā some pañcadaśa smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: The period of <s>Āditya</s> should be known as six years; that of <s>Soma</s> is remembered as fifteen.
That of <s>Aṅgāraka</s> is eight, and that of <s>Budha</s> is remembered as seventeen.
That of <s>Śanaiścara</s> should be known as ten; that of <s>Guru</s> is nineteen.
That of <s>Rāhu</s> is twelve years, and that of <s>Bhārgava</s> is twenty-one.
The daśā of the sun gives suffering and causes anxiety and the destruction of kings.
The daśā of <s>Soma</s> gives prosperity, happiness, and desired food.
The daśā of <s>Kuja</s> gives suffering and destroys kingdoms and the like.
The daśā of <s>Budha</s> gives celestial women, gives kingdom, and increases the treasury.
The daśā of <s>Śani</s> causes loss of kingdom and grief from kinsmen.
The daśā of <s>Guru</s> gives kingdom and bestows happiness, dharma, and the like.
The daśā of <s>Rāhu</s> gives loss of kingdom, disease, and suffering.
The daśā of <s>Śukra</s> gives elephants and horses, and brings kingdom and the gain of women.
<s>Meṣa</s> is the field of <s>Aṅgāraka</s>; <s>Vṛṣa</s> is said to belong to <s>Śukra</s>.

children.text: mithunasya budho jñeyaḥ somaḥ karkaṭakasya ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Budha</s> should be known as the lord of <s>Mithuna</s>, and <s>Soma</s> of <s>Karkaṭaka</s>.

children.text: sūryakṣetraṃ bhavetsiṃhaḥ kanyā kṣetraṃ budhasya ca
children.translated_text: <s>Siṃha</s> is the field of the sun, and <s>Kanyā</s> is the field of <s>Budha</s>.
<s>Tulā</s> is the field of <s>Bhārgava</s>, and <s>Vṛścika</s> of <s>Aṅgāraka</s>.
<s>Dhanuḥ</s> belongs to the preceptor of the gods, and <s>Makara</s> and <s>Kumbha</s> to <s>Śani</s>.
<s>Mīna</s>, Pisces, is declared to be the planetary domain of the preceptor of the gods.
There, when there are two full-moon days, there should also be two <s>Pūrvāṣāḍhā</s> days.

children.text: dvirāṣāḍhaḥ sa vijñeyo viṣṇuḥ svapiti karkaṭe ||
children.translated_text: That should be known as the double <s>Āṣāḍha</s>; <s>Viṣṇu</s> sleeps when the Sun is in <s>Karkaṭa</s>.
<s>Aśvinī</s>, <s>Revatī</s>, <s>Citrā</s>, and <s>Dhaniṣṭhā</s> are said to be auspiciously adorned.
Deer, snakes, monkeys, cats, dogs, boars, and birds,
as well as mongooses and mice, are auspicious on the right side during a journey.
A Brahmin maiden, an auspicious woman, conches, kettledrums, and earth or grain,
bamboo, women, and full jars are auspicious sights during a journey.
Jackals, camels, asses, and the like are auspicious on the left side during a journey.
Cotton, medicines, oil, cooked food, embers, and snakes,
and also a woman with loosened hair, a red garland, nakedness, and the like, are inauspicious when seen.
I shall describe the sign for a hiccup: if it occurs in the east, it brings a great result.
In the southeast there are grief and burning distress; in the south one incurs loss.
In the southwest there are grief and burning distress; in the west there is sweet food.
In the northwest one obtains wealth; in the north there will be quarrel.
In the northeast death is declared; such is the good and bad fruit of hiccups.
Having drawn the solar diagram, one should represent <s>Bhāskara</s>, the Sun, in human form.
In whatever nakṣatra <s>Bhānu</s>, the Sun, is staying, one should place that and the next three on the head.
Three should be assigned to the face, and one each should be set on the two shoulders.
One each should be placed on the pair of arms, and one each on the two hands.

children.text: hṛdaye pañca ṛkṣāṇi ekaṃ nābhau pradāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Five nakṣatras should be assigned to the heart, and one should be placed on the navel.
One nakṣatra should be placed on the private parts, and one each on the knees.
The remaining nakṣatras should be assigned to the feet of the Sun.
By a nakṣatra of the feet a man becomes short-lived.
When it is on the knees there is travel abroad; when it is on the private parts one is attached to others' wives.
When it is on the navel one is easily satisfied; when it is on the heart one becomes a great lord.
When it is on the hand one becomes a thief; when it is on the arm one falls from one's station.
When it is on the shoulder one becomes wealthy; when it is on the face one obtains sweet food.
If the nakṣatra is located on the head, there will be fine cloth.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍaṃ prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe jyotiḥśāstre grahadaśādinirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the eastern section called the first part, in the ācāra division, the sixtieth chapter, called "The Description of Planetary Periods and Related Matters" in the science of jyotiṣa.
<s>Hari</s> said:
The Moon situated in the seventh or in an upacaya house is auspicious everywhere.
In the bright fortnight, the second, fifth, and ninth lunar days are likewise auspicious.
Being honored by people, the Moon is seen like a guru.

children.text: candrasya dvādaśāvasthā bhavanti śṛṇu tā api ||
children.translated_text: There are twelve states of the Moon; listen to them also.

children.text: triṣu triṣu ca ṛkṣeṣu aśvinyādi vadāmyaham
children.translated_text: I shall state them in groups of three nakṣatras each, beginning with <s>Aśvinī</s>.
They are the state of being abroad, being seen again, the state of death, and the one that brings victory,
the state of laughter, the bowed state, and the state of delight,
the state of despondency, the state of enjoyment, and the state of fever,
the state of trembling and the state of happiness: thus there are twelve states.

children.text: pravāso hānimṛnyṛ ca jayo hāse 'ratiḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: Travel, loss, death, victory, laughter, aversion, and happiness,

children.text: śoko bhogo jvaraḥ kampaḥ sukhaṃ ceti kramātphalam
children.translated_text: grief, enjoyment, fever, trembling, and happiness are the fruits in order.

children.text: janmasthaḥ kurute tuṣṭiṃ dvitīye nāsti nirvṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the Moon is in the natal sign it produces satisfaction; in the second there is no contentment.
In the third there is royal honor; in the fourth, the coming of quarrel.

children.text: pañcamena mṛgāṅkena strīlābho vai tathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: With the Moon in the fifth, there is also gain of a woman.

children.text: ghanadhānyāgamaḥ ṣaṣṭhe ratiḥ pūjā ca saptame
children.translated_text: In the sixth there is acquisition of abundant grain; in the seventh, pleasure and honor.
In the eighth there is danger to life; in the ninth, accumulation of treasure.
In the tenth there is accomplishment of the undertaking; in the eleventh, certain victory.
With the Moon in the twelfth there is surely death, without doubt.

children.text: kṛttikādau ca pūrveṇa saptarkṣāṇi ca vai vrajet
children.translated_text: Beginning with <s>Kṛttikā</s>, one should go eastward for seven nakṣatras.
