children.translated_text: whether diamond or <s>kuruvinda</s>, except by this one thing,
it is impossible to make a scratch on <s>padmarāga</s> and sapphire.

children.text: jātyasya sarve 'pi maṇerna jātu vijātayaḥ santi samānavarṇāḥ
children.translated_text: All stones of a genuine gem are never of the same color as stones of a different class.
Even so, precisely for the sake of distinguishing them, the supreme method of classification has been taught.

children.text: guṇopapannena sahāvabaddho maṇir na dhāryo viguṇo hi jātyā
children.translated_text: A gem defective by nature should not be worn together with one endowed with virtues.
A learned man should never wear a gem of another class bound together even with the <s>Kaustubha</s>.

children.text: cāṇḍāla eko 'pi yathā dvijātīnsametya bhūrīnapi hantyayatnāt
children.translated_text: Just as even one <s>cāṇḍāla</s>, when mixed among many twice-born men, destroys them effortlessly,
so a gem of a different class can spoil many gems endowed with virtues.
Even when it dwells among rivals, even when it is involved in negligent handling,
no misfortune here touches the possessor of a <s>padmarāga</s> of great virtue.
Those afflictions that arise from the onset of defects do not assail him,

children.text: guṇaiḥ samuttejitacārurāgaṃ yaḥ padmarāgaṃ prayato bibharti ||
children.translated_text: who, purified and careful, wears a <s>padmarāga</s> whose lovely color is heightened by its virtues.
The price that has been stated for a diamond by the number of rice-grains, when its weight has been determined,
that is the price of a <s>padmarāga</s> of great virtue when reckoned by the standard of the <s>māṣa</s>.
A jewel-gem endowed with color and brilliance is praised.
A gem that falls away even slightly from those two is reduced from the value of a gem.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe padmarāgaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāma saptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Gāruḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section called the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the seventieth chapter, named the examination of <s>padmarāga</s>, is complete.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Taking the bile of the lord of the demons, the lord of serpents,
<s>Vāsuki</s>, as though splitting the sky in two, went swiftly.
Then, in the ocean of the sky made bright by the radiance of the jewel on his own head,
that great one shone alone like a fragment of a silver bridge.
Then, as though drawing the two worlds together by the beat of his wings,
<s>Garuḍa</s> began to strike the king of serpents.
Suddenly that serpent-lord dropped it on the slopes of the excellent mountain of rubies,
which were anointed with fragrant turuṣka trees and perfumed with the thick scent of buds.
Immediately after its fall, having passed beyond that excellent abode and near <s>Ramā</s>,
it reached a place on the earth, a line on the shore of the ocean, on the slopes of the excellent mountain of rubies.

children.text: tatraiva kiṃcit patatastu pittādupetya jagrāha tato garutmān
children.translated_text: Then <s>Garuḍa</s> came there and seized some of the bile as it was falling.
Overcome by stupor, he suddenly released all of it through the two openings of his nostrils.
There emeralds, having acquired the luster of tender parrot-throats, śirīṣa flowers, fireflies' backs, fresh grass, moss,

children.text: kalhāraśaṣpakabhujaṅgabhujāṃ ca patraprāptatviṣo marakatāḥ śubhadā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: water-lilies, young shoots, snakes' arms, and leaves, become auspicious.
Where the bile of the lord of the Daityas fell, associated with the arm of the king of serpents,

children.text: tasyākarasyātitarāṃ sa deśo duḥkhopalabhyaśca guṇaiśca yuktaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the region of that mine is extremely hard to obtain and endowed with virtues.
Whatever is produced in that place of emeralds,
all of it is proclaimed to pacify poison-diseases.
That poison produced from the fang of a great serpent, which cannot be treated
by all groups of mantras and medicines, is pacified by it.
Whatever else is produced in that mine, free from defects,
is proclaimed to be the best among purifying things.
That which is intensely green in color, soft, with rays divided and intricate,
and which appears as though filled within with gold dust,

children.text: yuktaṃ saṃsthānaguṇaiḥ samarāgaṃ gauraveṇa na vihīnam
children.translated_text: endowed with qualities of shape, evenly colored, and not lacking in weight,
brightens every support with its brilliance from the touch of the sun's rays.
And that whose brilliance is lodged inside after leaving behind mere greenness,
shines like fresh grass struck by the radiance of lightning-flashes.
And that which, when looked at intensely, produces clarity of mind,
that, according to the judgment of gem-knowers, is an emerald of great quality.
Because of the great abundance of its color, within it is a garment of clear rays,
dense, smooth, pure, and equal in luster to the radiance of a soft peacock-feather.
By its color-bright splendor it appears with a dense form, shining forth;
that too receives the designation 'possessing qualities,' just as the one described before.
An emerald that is variegated, hard, dirty, rough, and containing bits of stone and gravel,
and that looks as though smeared with mineral pitch, is defective in this way.
A jewel other than emerald that has dried at the joints
should never be worn or bought by those who desire welfare.
The <s>bhallātakī</s> and the <s>putrikā</s> are similar to it in color.
These are to be recognized as the alien varieties of the <s>marakata</s> jewel.

children.text: kṣaumeṇa vāsasā mṛṣṭā dīptiṃ tyajati putrikā
children.translated_text: When rubbed with a linen cloth, a <s>putrikā</s> gives up its brilliance.
Glass can be distinguished simply by its lightness.
Even when something follows emerald through manifold forms and through qualities and colors,
from the sound of bhallātaka it acquires an unevenness of color.

children.text: vajrāṇi muktāḥ santyanye ye ca kecid vijātayaḥ
children.translated_text: Diamonds, pearls, and other such things are also alien varieties.
When they are unobstructed, their radiance rises upward.
And because of straightness, in some cases it somehow arises,
but when they are viewed sideways it disappears at once.
In bathing, sipping water, recitation, and the procedure of protective mantras,
when giving cows and gold and when performing rites of accomplishment,
in rites for gods, ancestors, and guests, and in honoring teachers,
and when one is afflicted by various faults born of region, birth, or poison,
one that is free from defects, endowed with qualities, and set in gold
should be worn by the wise, and also by those moving about in battle.
Whatever value is obtained for a <s>padmarāga</s> when weighed on the balance,
an emerald endowed with qualities obtains more than that.
And just as the value of <s>padmarāga</s> gems is diminished by defects,
so, in the case of this emerald too, there would be an even greater loss through defects.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe marakataparīkṣaṇaṃ nāmaikasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section, in the first division called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-first chapter, named "The Examination of Emeralds."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
There itself, in a region where the coral-like young lavalī blossoms had been torn by the tips of the sprout-like hands of <s>Siṃhala</s> women,

children.text: deśe papāta ditijasya nitāntakāntaṃ protphullanīrajasamadyuti netrayugmam ||
children.translated_text: there fell the demon's pair of eyes, exceedingly lovely and possessing the radiance of fully opened, intoxicated lotuses.
By reason of that, with the shining of waves lovely in both ways, the shoreland of the ocean spread out,
and it appears as if filled with dense <s>indranīla</s> jewels, marked by lines of blossoming ketaka groves.
There, from dark lotuses, the garment of <s>Halabhṛt</s>, swords, bees, the body of <s>Śārṅgāyudha</s>, the throat of <s>Hara</s>, and tawny flowers,

children.text: śuṣketaraiśca kusumair girikarṇikāyās tasmādbhavanti maṇayaḥ sadṛśāvabhāsaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and from other flowers of the mountain karnikā that are not dried up, gems arise with a similar appearance.
Some have the hue of the clear water of the ocean; others are like flocks of peacocks.
Some have the gleam of bubbles produced from the juice of nīlī dye, and some shine like the throat of an intoxicated cuckoo.
Uniform, manifestly shining with the beauty of clear color,
there are born in that place <s>indranīla</s> jewels of great virtue.
Those joined with earth, stone, rock-cavities, roughness, and cracks,
and those spoiled by defects of color and shade like a layer of mica or cloud,

children.text: tata eva hi jāyante maṇayastatra bhūrayaḥ
children.translated_text: many such jewels too are born there from that very source.
Sages whose understanding has been awakened by śāstra praise them.
Whatever qualities have been seen in wearing a <s>padmarāga</s> jewel,
a person obtains those very qualities by wearing an <s>indranīla</s>.
And just as there may be a threefold class among <s>padmarāga</s> gems,
so too it should be recognized without distinction among <s>indranīla</s> gems.
And by whatever evidential tests a <s>padmarāga</s> is examined,
those same tests are seen also for an <s>indranīla</s> jewel.
And however far fire may pass by the use of a <s>padmarāga</s>,
an <s>indranīla</s> jewel would pass much farther than that.
Even so, for the sake of testing or for increasing its qualities,
no jewel whatsoever should ever be placed in fire.
If the measure of fire is not understood and it is spoiled by the faults of burning,
it would bring harm to its owner, to the one who acts, and likewise to the one who causes the act to be done.
Glass, blue lotus, oleander, crystal, and the like, together with <s>vaidūrya</s>, are here
declared by the wise to be these alien varieties similar to the <s>indranīla</s> jewel.
The heaviness and hardness of these should always be known
as increasing in due order from glass onward, especially.
Just as some <s>indranīla</s> bears a reddish color,
so too the karavīra and the utpala, both reddish, are to be specially guarded.
The one in whose blue interior the brilliance of a rainbow shines
they call <s>indranīla</s>; it is very valuable and rare on earth.
When, through the great abundance of its color, it has been placed in milk one hundred times its quantity
and makes all of that blue, it is called <s>mahānīla</s>.
The price that belongs to a greatly excellent <s>padmarāga</s> weighed at one māṣa
is the price of a greatly excellent <s>indranīla</s> weighed according to the count of suvarṇas.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe indranīlaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāma dvisaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section, in the first division called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-second chapter, named "The Examination of <s>Indranīla</s>."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall tell the examination of <s>vaidūrya</s> and <s>puṣparāga</s>, in regard to the karketa and bhīṣmaka varieties,

children.text: parīkṣāṃ brahmaṇā proktāṃ vyāsena kathitāṃ dvijāḥ ||
children.translated_text: taught by <s>Brahmā</s> and related by <s>Vyāsa</s>, O twice-born ones.
From the demon's roar, like the roar of the ocean agitated at the time of the end of an age,
there arose <s>vaidūrya</s>, many-colored, the seed of beautiful radiance and color.
Not far from the mountain <s>Vidūra</s>, with its lofty banks,
along the border of <s>Kāmabhūtika</s>, its mine came into being.
Because that mine arose from his roar, it was of very great quality,
and became, in the world, a surpassing ornament of the three worlds.
Corresponding to the roar of that very lord of <s>Dānavas</s>, and showing lovely forms like excellent rain-clouds,
the <s>vaidūrya</s> jewels, with varied brilliance, arose from him like masses of sparks.
Taking <s>padmarāga</s> as a point of comparison, whatever jewel-colors exist on earth,
the <s>vaidūrya</s> follows all of them with the beauties of its colors.
Among them the best is blue like a peacock's neck, or else one that has the gleam of a bamboo leaf;

children.text: cāṣāgrapakṣapratimaśriyo ye na te praśastā maṇiśāstravidbhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: those whose beauty resembles the tip of a cāṣa bird's wing are not praised by experts in gem-science.
A good <s>vaidūrya</s> jewel joins its owner to supreme good fortune;
one joined with flaws brings flaws; therefore one should examine it carefully.
<s>Girikāca</s>, <s>śiśupāla</s>, glass, and crystals split by smoke
are inferior kinds of the <s>vaidūrya</s> jewel; they are similar in appearance.
One should know glass by the absence of streaks, and <s>śaiśupālaka</s> by its lightness;
<s>girikāca</s> by its mountain-glass-like brilliance, and crystal by its brightness of color.
The price of an <s>indranīla</s> of great quality, reckoned by the number of <s>suvarṇas</s>,
that same price is prescribed for a <s>vaidūrya</s> jewel whose weight has been measured at two <s>palas</s>.

children.text: jātyasya sarve 'pi maṇestu yādṛgvijātayaḥ santi samānavarṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Although all the inferior kinds of a genuine jewel may have the same color,
nevertheless a highest classification is prescribed, with distinctions inferred from various causes.

children.text: sukhopalakṣyaśca sadā vicāryo hyayaṃ prabhedo viduṣā nareṇa
children.translated_text: This distinction should always be considered by a learned man, for it is easy to observe;

children.text: snehaprabhedo laghutā mṛdutvaṃ vijātiliṅgaṃ khalu sārvajanyam ||
children.translated_text: differences of gloss, lightness, and softness are indeed the common marks of an inferior kind.
Filled by skilled and unskilled persons and set through applications of proper treatment,
gems acquire a different value, arising from their qualities and faults.
When gems, whether from former or present sources, are carefully mounted by a jeweler in due order,

children.text: yadi nāma bhavanti doṣahīnā maṇayaḥ ṣaḍguṇamāpnuvanti mūlyam ||
children.translated_text: if indeed they are free from faults, they obtain six times their value.
For those that have passed beyond their mines, near the shore of the ocean,
this value of gems does not apply everywhere on earth.
The <s>suvarṇa</s> that was declared by <s>Manu</s> to be sixteen <s>māṣakas</s>,
the seventieth part of it will serve as the unit so named.
A <s>śāṇa</s> is measured as four <s>māṣas</s>; a <s>māṣaka</s> is five <s>kṛṣṇalas</s>;
a <s>dharaṇa</s> is said to be a tenth part of a <s>pala</s>.
Thus the rule for gems has been stated for determining the value of jewels.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vaidūryaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāma trisaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-third chapter, named 'Examination of <s>Vaidūrya</s>,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
When the skin of that enemy of the gods had fallen on <s>Himādri</s>,
from those pieces there arise <s>puṣparāgas</s> of great quality.
A stone that is yellowish-white and pleasant is called <s>padmarāga</s>;
if it is red-yellow, that same one is named <s>kaukaṇṭaka</s>.

children.text: ālohitastu pītaḥ svacchaḥ kāṣāyakaḥ sa ekoktaḥ
children.translated_text: But the one called <s>eka</s> is reddish, yellow, clear, and tawny;
one blue-white in color and glossy is the good <s>somālaka</s>.

children.text: atyantalohito yaḥ sa eva khalu padmarāgasaṃjñaḥ syāt
children.translated_text: That which is extremely red is indeed called <s>padmarāga</s>;

children.text: api cendranīlasaṃjñaḥ sa eva kathitaḥ sunīlaḥ san ||
children.translated_text: and the same, when very blue, is said to bear the name <s>indranīla</s>.
Its value has been stated by the knower of the essence of jewels to be like that of the <s>vaidūrya</s> jewel,

children.text: dhāraṇaphalaṃ ca tadvat kiṃtu strīṇāṃ sutaprado bhavati ||
children.translated_text: and the fruit of wearing it is the same; but for women it becomes a giver of sons.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe puṣparāgaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāma catuḥsaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-fourth chapter, named 'Examination of <s>Puṣparāga</s>,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The wind, taking the nails of the lord of demons, joyfully cast them into good lotus-groves;

children.text: tataḥ prasūtaṃ pavanopapannaṃ karketanaṃ pūjyatamaṃ pṛthivyām ||
children.translated_text: from them was born, produced by the wind, the <s>karketana</s>, most worthy of honor on earth.
In color it shines with the appearance of blood, soma, and honey, glowing coppery-yellow like fire;

children.text: nīlaṃ punaḥ khalu sitaṃ paruṣaṃ vibhinnaṃ vyādhyādidoṣakaraṇena ca tadvibhāti ||
children.translated_text: but when blue, white, rough, or cracked, it appears as a cause of diseases and other faults.

children.text: snigdhā viśuddhāḥ samarāgiṇaśca āpītavarṇā guravo vicitrāḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>karketanas</s> that are glossy, pure, even-colored, yellowish, heavy, and variegated,
and free from fissures, wounds, and serpent-like marks are supremely purifying.

children.text: patreṇa kāñcanamayena tu veṣṭayitvā taptaṃ yadā hutavahe bhavati prakāśam
children.translated_text: When, wrapped with a golden sheet, it becomes radiant while heated in fire,

children.text: rogapraṇāśanakaraṃ kalināśanaṃ tadāyuṣkaraṃ kulakaraṃ ca sukhapradaṃ ca ||
children.translated_text: then it destroys disease, removes <s>Kali</s>, gives long life, continues the family, and gives happiness.

children.text: evaṃvidhaṃ bahuguṇaṃ maṇimāvahanti karketanaṃ śubhālaṅkṛtaye narā ye
children.translated_text: Those men who carry such a many-quality <s>karketana</s> jewel as an auspicious adornment,

children.text: te pūjitā bahudhanā bahubāndhavāśca nityojjvalāḥ pramuditā apite bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: are honored, wealthy, rich in relatives, ever bright, and joyful as well.
Some, however, when tied on, have a distorted and confused blue sheen; their red is faded and disturbed, turbid and ugly.
With color devoid of power, great brilliance, and the strengthening of the family, they bear only a body similar to <s>karketana</s>.
If a <s>karketana</s> has been examined and found proper in color and form, shining brightly like the fresh sun,

children.text: tasyottamasya maṇiśāstravidāṃ mahimnā tulyaṃ tu mūlyamuditaṃ tulitasya kāryam ||
children.translated_text: then, by the authority of those who know gem-science, the price of the best one should be set equal to that of one of the same weight.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe karketanaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāma pañcasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-fifth chapter, named 'Examination of <s>Karketana</s>,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In the northern region of <s>Himavat</s>, the semen of that enemy of the gods fell;
it came to be the source-mines of the finest <s>bhīṣmaratnas</s>.
White, resembling conches and lotuses, similar to <s>syonāka</s>, and possessing power,
from them arise, while still young, <s>bhīṣma</s> stones resembling vajra.
He who, with faith, sets a pure <s>bhīṣma</s> jewel bound with gold and the like,

children.text: bhīṣmamaṇiṃ grīvādiṣu susampadaṃ sa sarvadā labhate ||
children.translated_text: and wears the <s>bhīṣma</s> jewel on his neck and so forth, always obtains excellent prosperity.
Wild-dwelling violent beasts flee when they see him, even nearby:
leopards, wolves, śarabhas, elephants, lions, tigers, and the like.
For him there is no fear from that sharply cut tree of <s>Utkala</s>; nor do they mock the Lord.
The <s>bhīṣma</s> jewel, when endowed with qualities and properly obtained for the finger or for a woman, has this power.
At an offering to the fathers, the satisfaction of the ancestors lasts for many years.
Even strange afflictions are pacified, as are the poisons of snakes, birds, mice, and scorpions;
terrible fears from water, fire, enemies, and thieves disappear.
A wise man should avoid from afar one that has the appearance of moss or a cloud, yellowish in lustre, devoid of brilliance,

children.text: malinadyuti ca vivarṇaṃ dūrāt parivarjayet prājñaḥ ||
children.translated_text: dirty in radiance and discolored.
Their value should be fixed by excellent learned men through knowledge of place and time:
much for those produced far away, something little for those born nearby.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vaidūryaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṭsaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-sixth chapter, called 'The Examination of <s>Vaidūrya</s>,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: puṇyeṣu parvatavareṣu ca nimnagāsu sthānāntareṣu ca tathottaradeśagatvāt
children.translated_text: In holy places, on the best mountains and in rivers, and likewise in other places, because they had gone to the northern region,

children.text: saṃsthāpitāḥ svanakhabāhugateḥ prakāśaṃ sampūjya dānavapatiṃ prathite pradeśe ||
children.translated_text: they were established in a famous district, after worshipping the lord of demons, displaying the mark of his own nails and arms.
In <s>Dāśārṇa</s>, <s>Vāgada</s>, <s>Mekala</s>, <s>Kālagāda</s>, and other places, they have the colors of guñjā berries, collyrium, honey, and lotus fiber.
Those <s>pulaka</s> gems are praised when they arise with an appearance like a <s>gandharva</s>, fire, or plantain.
Variegated with patterns like conches, lotuses, bees, and the sun, and furnished with threads, they are supreme and pure.
Those <s>pulaka</s> gems, auspicious and variegated with many colors, become givers of increase.
Those marked with fierce forms of crows, horses, donkeys, jackals, wolves, and vultures, and with mouths wet with flesh and blood,

children.text: mṛtyupradāśca viduṣā parivarjanīyā mūlyaṃ palasya kathitaṃ ca śatāni pañca ||
children.translated_text: give death and should be avoided by the learned; the value of a pala has been stated as five hundred.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe pulakaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāma saptasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-seventh chapter, called 'The Examination of <s>Pulaka</s>,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Taking on the form of fire, according to the demon's wish,
he cast it into the <s>Narmadā</s>, in lands somewhat deficient and the like.
There, the <s>rudhirākṣa</s> jewel, speckled with indragopa insects, parrot-beaked in color, and in shape about the size of a visible pīlu fruit,
having been fashioned in various forms and drawn out, is indeed entirely equal to that.

children.text: madhyendupāṇḍuramatīva viśuddhavarṇaṃ taccendranīlasadṛśaṃ paṭalaṃ tule syāt
children.translated_text: If its plate is very pure in color, pale like the middle of the moon, and resembling sapphire in the balance,

children.text: saiśvaryabhṛtyajananaṃ kathitaṃ tadaiva pakvaṃ ca tatkila bhavetsuravajravarṇam ||
children.translated_text: then it is said to produce sovereignty and servants; when mature, it is said to have the color of the gods' vajra.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe rudhirākṣaratnaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭasaptatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-eighth chapter, called 'The Examination of the <s>Rudhirākṣa</s> Jewel,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
In the lands of <s>Kāvera</s>, <s>Vindhya</s>, the <s>Yavanas</s>, <s>Cīna</s>, and <s>Nepāla</s>,
<s>Lāṅgalī</s> carefully scattered the demon's fat.
From that arose crystal, clear as the sky and called oily,
white like lotus fiber and conch, with some slight difference of color.
It is not equal to the jewels; nevertheless it destroys sin.

children.text: saṃskṛtaṃ śilpinā sadyo mūlyaṃ kiṃcillabhet tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Once worked by an artisan, it may thereby acquire some value.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sphaṭikaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāmaikonāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the seventy-ninth chapter, called 'The Examination of Crystal,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Śeṣa</s> took the entrail of that <s>Bala</s> and, among the plantain groves and other places,
threw it down; there corals arise, having very auspicious qualities.
There the best is taught to be red like a hare's blood, like a guñjā berry or a hibiscus flower.

children.text: sunīlakaṃ devakaromakaṃ ca sthānāni teṣu prabhavaṃ surāgam ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Sunīlaka</s> and the <s>Devakaromaka</s> are also places where deep-red ones arise among them.

children.text: anyatra jātaṃ ca na tatpradhānaṃ mūlyaṃ bhavecchilpiviśeṣayogāt
children.translated_text: What is born elsewhere is not excellent; its value depends on the particular skill of the artisan.

children.text: prasannaṃ komalaṃ snigdhaṃ surāgaṃ vidrumaṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: That coral is clear, soft, smooth, and deeply red.
In the world it brings wealth and grain, and destroys suffering, poison, and fear.
The examination of <s>pulaka</s>, of the <s>rudhirākṣa</s> jewel,
and of crystal and coral has been stated for the knowledge of jewels, O <s>Śaunaka</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vidrumaparīkṣaṇaṃ nāmāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the eightieth chapter, called 'The Examination of Coral,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall describe all the sacred bathing places. <s>Gaṅgā</s> is the best of the best tīrthas.

children.text: sarvatra sulabhā gaṅgā triṣu sthāneṣu durlabhā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaṅgā</s> is easy to reach everywhere, but difficult to reach in three places:
at <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, at <s>Prayāga</s>, and at the confluence of <s>Gaṅgā</s> with the ocean.
<s>Prayāga</s> is the supreme tīrtha, granting enjoyment and liberation to the dead.
Through its service it conquers sin for those who have made piṇḍa offerings, and grants people's desires.

children.text: vārāṇasī paraṃ tīrthaṃ viśveśo yatra keśavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Vārāṇasī</s> is the supreme tīrtha, where <s>Viśveśa</s> and <s>Keśava</s> are present.
<s>Kurukṣetra</s> is the supreme tīrtha, granting enjoyment and liberation through gifts and other acts.

children.text: prabhāsaṃ paraṃ tīrthaṃ somanātho hi tatra ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Prabhāsa</s> is the supreme tīrtha, for <s>Somanātha</s> is there.
And <s>Dvārakā</s> is a lovely city, granting enjoyment and liberation.
The eastern <s>Sarasvatī</s> is holy, and <s>Saptasārasvata</s> is supreme.
<s>Kedāra</s>, destroyer of all sins, and the excellent village <s>Sambhala</s>,
the tīrtha of <s>Nara-Nārāyaṇa</s>, and <s>Badarikāśrama</s>, which leads to liberation;

children.text: śvetadvīpaṃ purī māyā naimiṣaṃ puṣkaraṃ param
children.translated_text: <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>, the city <s>Māyā</s>, <s>Naimiṣa</s>, and supreme <s>Puṣkara</s>,

children.text: ayodhyā cārghyatīrthaṃ tu citrakūṭaṃ ca gomatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the <s>Arghyatīrtha</s>, <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, and the <s>Gomatī</s>;
<s>Vaināyaka</s>, the great tīrtha, and the supreme hermitage at <s>Rāmagiri</s>,
<s>Kāñcīpurī</s>, the <s>Tuṅgabhadrā</s>, <s>Śrīśaila</s>, and <s>Setubandhana</s>;
<s>Rāmeśvara</s>, the supreme tīrtha, and likewise the excellent place of <s>Kārttikeya</s>,
<s>Bhṛgutuṅga</s>, <s>Kāmatīrtha</s>, and the tīrtha <s>Amarakaṇṭaka</s>;
at <s>Ujjayinī</s> there is <s>Mahākāla</s>; at <s>Kubjaka</s> there is <s>Śrīdhara Hari</s>;
<s>Kubjāmraka</s>, the great tīrtha, and <s>Kālasarpi</s>, which grants desires;
<s>Mahākeśī</s>, the <s>Kāverī</s>, the <s>Candrabhāgā</s>, and the <s>Vipāśā</s>,

children.text: ekāmraṃ ca tathā tīrthaṃ brahmeśaṃ devakoṭakam ||
children.translated_text: and likewise the tīrtha <s>Ekāmra</s>, <s>Brahmeśa</s>, and <s>Devakoṭaka</s>;

children.text: mathurā ca purī ramyā śoṇaścaiva mahānadaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mathurā</s>, the lovely city, and the great river <s>Śoṇa</s>,

children.text: jambūsaro mahātīrthaṃ tāni tīrthāni viddhi ca ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Jambūsara</s>, the great tīrtha: know these to be tīrthas.

children.text: sūryaḥ śivo gaṇo devī hariryatra ca tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: Where <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, the <s>Gaṇas</s>, the Goddess, and <s>Hari</s> abide,

children.text: eteṣu ca yathānyeṣu snānaṃ dānaṃ japastapaḥ ||
children.translated_text: in these places, and in others like them, bathing, giving, recitation, and austerity,

children.text: pūjā śrāddhaṃ piṇḍadānaṃ sarvaṃ bhavati cākṣayam
children.translated_text: worship, śrāddha, and the offering of piṇḍas all become inexhaustible.
<s>Śālagrāma</s> is said to be all-giving, the supreme tīrtha of <s>Paśupati</s>.
<s>Kokāmukha</s>, <s>Vārāha</s>, <s>Bhāṇḍīra</s>, called <s>Svāmin</s>,
at <s>Lohadaṇḍa</s> there is <s>Mahāviṣṇu</s>; on <s>Mandāra</s> there is <s>Madhusūdana</s>.
<s>Kāmarūpa</s> is a great tīrtha, where <s>Kāmākhyā</s> abides;
and <s>Puṇḍravardhana</s> is a tīrtha where <s>Kārttikeya</s> also is.
<s>Viraja</s> is a great tīrtha, and the tīrtha <s>Śrīpuruṣottama</s>;
<s>Mahendraparvata</s> is a tīrtha, and the <s>Kāverī</s> is the supreme river.
The <s>Godāvarī</s> is a great tīrtha, and <s>Payoṣṇī</s> is a boon-granting river;
the <s>Vindhya</s> is a sin-removing tīrtha, and the excellent <s>Narmadābheda</s>.

children.text: gokarṇaṃ paramaṃ tīrthaṃ tīrthaṃ māhiṣmatī purī
children.translated_text: <s>Gokarṇa</s> is the highest tīrtha, and the city <s>Māhiṣmatī</s> is a tīrtha;
<s>Kālañjara</s> is a great tīrtha on earth, and <s>Śuklatīrtha</s> is unsurpassed.

children.text: kṛte śauce muktidaṃ ca śārṅgadhārī tadantike
children.translated_text: When purification has been performed, it grants liberation, and <s>Śārṅgadhārī</s> is nearby.
<s>Viraja</s> is an all-giving tīrtha, and <s>Svarṇākṣa</s> is an excellent tīrtha.
<s>Nanditīrtha</s> grants liberation and bestows the fruit of ten million tīrthas.
<s>Nāsikya</s> too is a great tīrtha, and after that <s>Govardhana</s> is supreme.
The <s>Kṛṣṇaveṇī</s>, <s>Bhīmarathī</s>, <s>Gaṇḍakī</s>, and the <s>Irāvatī</s>,
the holy tīrtha <s>Bindusaras</s>, and the supreme water from <s>Viṣṇu's</s> feet;
meditation on <s>Brahman</s> is the supreme tīrtha, and restraint of the senses is a tīrtha.

children.text: damastīrthaṃ tu paramaṃ bhavaśuddhiḥ paraṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Self-control is indeed the highest tīrtha, and so too is purity of becoming.
In the lake of knowledge, in the water of meditation, which removes the dirt of passion and hatred,

children.text: yaḥ snāti mānase tīrthe sa yāti paramāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: whoever bathes in the mental tīrtha goes to the supreme goal.

children.text: idaṃ tīrthamidaṃ neti ye narā bhedadarśinaḥ
children.translated_text: Those men who see distinctions, saying, 'This is a tīrtha, this is not,'

children.text: teṣāṃ vidhīyate tīrthagamanaṃ tatphalaṃ ca yat ||
children.translated_text: for them pilgrimage to tīrthas is prescribed, together with whatever fruit it has.
But one who knows, 'All this is <s>Brahman</s>,' has nothing at all that is not a tīrtha.
In these places, bathing, gifts, śrāddha, and the piṇḍa-offering are inexhaustible.
All rivers and all mountains are tīrthas, served by gods and others.

children.text: śrīraṅgaṃ ca harestīrthaṃ tāpī śreṣṭhā mahānadī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīraṅga</s> is the tīrtha of <s>Hari</s>, and the <s>Tāpī</s> is the best of great rivers.
<s>Saptagodāvara</s> is a tīrtha, and <s>Koṇagiri</s> is the supreme tīrtha;
there the goddess <s>Mahālakṣmī</s> is present, and <s>Praṇītā</s> is a supreme river.
On the <s>Sahyādri</s> is <s>Devadeveśa</s>, and <s>Ekavīrā</s> is the sovereign goddess.
At <s>Gaṅgādvāra</s>, at <s>Kuśāvarta</s>, on the <s>Vindhya</s>, and on <s>Nīlaparvata</s>,

children.text: snātvā kanakhale tīrthe sa bhavenna punarbhave
children.translated_text: having bathed at the tīrtha <s>Kanakhala</s>, one does not come into rebirth.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
These and other tīrthas are always fruitful through bathing and the like.
Having heard this from <s>Hari</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, together with <s>Dakṣa</s> and the others, spoke to <s>Vyāsa</s>.
After telling of these tīrthas, he again described the very best among excellent tīrthas,
called <s>Gayā</s>, inexhaustible for all and bestowing <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sarvatīrthamāhātmyaṃ nāmaikāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighty-first chapter, named 'The Greatness of All Tīrthas,' is completed.
Homage to venerable <s>Gaṇeśa</s>.
Now the Greatness of <s>Gayā</s> begins.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
O <s>Vyāsa</s>, I shall briefly proclaim the excellent greatness of <s>Gayā</s>,
the essence of what is still more essential, granting enjoyment and liberation; listen.
Formerly there was <s>Gayāsura</s>, powerful and exceedingly mighty,
who performed a terribly severe austerity that afflicted all beings.
Burned by that austerity, the gods went to <s>Hari</s> for the purpose of killing him.
They took refuge, and <s>Hari</s> said to them, 'You must become of the nature of <s>Śiva</s>.'
'His great body is to be cast down.' The gods said to <s>Hari</s>, 'So be it.'
Once, for the sake of worshiping <s>Śiva</s>, the powerful one brought lotuses

children.text: ānīya kīkaṭe deśe śayanaṃ cākarod balī
children.translated_text: from the Milk Ocean and lay down in the region of <s>Kīkaṭa</s>.
Bewildered by <s>Viṣṇu's</s> māyā, he was struck down by <s>Viṣṇu</s> with the mace.
Therefore <s>Viṣṇu Gadādhara</s>, giver of liberation, remains at <s>Gayā</s>.

children.text: tasya deho liṅgarūpī sthitaḥ śuddhe pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His body, in the form of a liṅga, remained pure; there is <s>Pitāmaha</s>,
and <s>Janārdana</s>, <s>Kāleśa</s>, and also another called <s>Prapitāmaha</s>.
Then <s>Viṣṇu</s> declared the boundary: 'This will be a holy field.

children.text: yajñaṃ śrāddhaṃ piṇḍadānaṃ snānādi kurute naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who performs sacrifice, śrāddha, piṇḍa-offering, bathing, and the rest here

children.text: sa svargaṃ brahmalokaṃ ca gacchenna narakaṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: will go to heaven and to <s>Brahmaloka</s>; that man will not go to hell.'

children.text: gayātīrthaṃ paraṃ jñātvā yāgaṃ cakre pitāmahaḥ
children.translated_text: Knowing the <s>Gayā</s> tīrtha to be supreme, <s>Pitāmaha</s> performed a sacrifice.
He honored the Brahmins who had come for the office of priests,
and created the great river <s>Rasavahā</s>, as well as reservoirs and the like.
and he created edible and chewable foods, fruits, and the like, and likewise <s>Kāmadhenu</s>.
The Lord gave the five-krośa field of <s>Gayā</s> to the Brahmins.
Out of greed, at the sacrifices of <s>dharma</s> they accepted wealth and other gifts.
Then, after they had settled there, the Brahmins of <s>Gayā</s> were cursed.

children.text: mā bhūt traipuruṣī vidyā mā bhūttraipuruṣaṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: 'May there be no learning through three generations; may there be no wealth through three generations.
For you there shall be a water-bearing river, stones, and mountains.'
But when the cursed ones entreated <s>Brahmā</s>, the Lord granted them a favor.

children.text: lokāḥ puṇyā gayāyāṃ hi śrāddhino brahmalokagāḥ
children.translated_text: 'There are holy worlds at <s>Gayā</s>; performers of <s>śrāddha</s> go to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Those who will honor you will always have honored me thereby.
Knowledge of <s>Brahman</s>, <s>Gayā-śrāddha</s>, and death in a cow-house,
and residence by men in <s>Kurukṣetra</s>: this liberation is fourfold.
All oceans, rivers, reservoirs, wells, and ponds,

children.text: snātukāmā gayātīrthaṃ vyāsa yāsa yānti na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: desiring to bathe, go to <s>Gayā-tīrtha</s>, O <s>Vyāsa</s>; there is no doubt.
Brahmin-murder, drinking liquor, theft, and going to the guru's wife,
and every sin born from association with those, are destroyed by <s>Gayā-śrāddha</s>.

children.text: asaṃskṛtā mṛtā ye ca paśucorahatāśca ye
children.translated_text: Those who died unconsecrated, and those who were killed by beasts or thieves,
and those bitten by snakes: freed by <s>Gayā-śrāddha</s>, they go to heaven.
The fruit that a man obtains by giving <s>piṇḍas</s> at <s>Gayā</s>
I cannot describe even in hundreds of crores of years.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe gayāmāhātmyaṃ nāma dvyaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first section called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the eighty-second chapter, named 'The Greatness of <s>Gayā</s>,' is completed.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: kīkaṭeṣu gayā puṇyā puṇyaṃ rājagṛhaṃ vanam
children.translated_text: Among the <s>Kīkaṭas</s>, <s>Gayā</s> is holy; holy too is the forest of <s>Rājagṛha</s>.

children.text: viṣayaścāraṇaḥ puṇyo nadīnāṃ ca punaḥ punā ||
children.translated_text: The region called <s>Cāraṇa</s> is holy, and the rivers too are again and again holy.
On <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, to the east, west, south, and north,
the measure at <s>Gayā</s> is declared to be two and a half krośas.
The field of <s>Gayā</s> is five krośas, and <s>Gayāśiras</s> is one krośa.
There, by giving <s>piṇḍas</s>, everlasting satisfaction arises.
From <s>Naga</s>, <s>Janārdana</s>, and the well called <s>Uttaramānasa</s>,
this is called <s>Gayāśiras</s>; that is called <s>Phalgu-tīrtha</s>.
There, by giving <s>piṇḍas</s>, the ancestors obtain the highest state.
By merely going to <s>Gayā</s>, one becomes free from debt to the ancestors.
At <s>Gayā</s>, the God of gods, <s>Janārdana</s>, is present in the form of the ancestors.

children.text: taṃ dṛṣṭvā puṇḍarīkākṣaṃ mucyate vai ṛṇatrayāt ||
children.translated_text: Having seen that lotus-eyed one, a man is freed from the three debts.
Having seen the chariot-road at <s>Gayā-tīrtha</s>, at <s>Rudrapada</s> and the other places,
and <s>Kāleśvara</s> and <s>Kedāra</s>, he becomes free from debt to the ancestors.
Having seen the god <s>Pitāmaha</s>, he is released from all sins.

children.text: lokaṃ tvanāmayaṃ yāti dṛṣṭvā ca prapitāmaham ||
children.translated_text: And having seen <s>Prapitāmaha</s>, he goes to a world free from disease.
Likewise, having seen the god <s>Gadādhara</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>,

children.text: taṃ praṇamya prayatnena na bhūyo jāyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: and having reverently bowed to him with care, a man is not born again.
Having seen the great-souled <s>Maunāditya</s>, and especially <s>Kanakārka</s>,
in silence, O Brahmin sage, he becomes free from debt to the ancestors.
Having worshipped <s>Brahmā</s>, he obtains <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
The man who rises in the morning and sees <s>Gāyatrī</s>,
after carefully performing the twilight rite, obtains the fruit of all the Vedas.

children.text: sāvitrīṃ caiva madhyāhne dṛṣṭvā yajñaphalaṃ labhet ||
children.translated_text: And having seen <s>Sāvitrī</s> at midday, he obtains the fruit of sacrifice.

children.text: sarasvatīṃ ca sāyāhne dṛṣṭvā dānaphalaṃ labhet
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Sarasvatī</s> in the evening, he obtains the fruit of giving.
Having seen the Lord stationed on the mountain, he becomes free from debt to the ancestors.
Having seen <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> and <s>Dharmeśa</s>, there is destruction of debt.

children.text: devaṃ gṛdhreśvaraṃ dṛṣṭvā ko na mucyeta bandhanāt ||
children.translated_text: Having seen the god <s>Gṛdhreśvara</s>, who would not be released from bondage?
Having seen the cow in <s>Dhenuvana</s>, one leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: prabhāseśaṃ prabhāse ca dṛṣṭvā yāti parāṃ gatim ||
children.translated_text: And having seen <s>Prabhāseśa</s> at <s>Prabhāsa</s>, one goes to the supreme state.
Having seen <s>Koṭīśvara</s> and <s>Aśvamedha</s>, there is destruction of debt.
Having seen <s>Svargadvāreśvara</s>, one is released from the bondage of existence.
Having seen <s>Rāmeśvara</s> and <s>Gayālola</s>, one obtains heaven.
And having seen <s>Brahmeśvara</s>, one is released from the sin of Brahmin-murder.
Having seen great <s>Caṇḍī</s> on <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, one obtains one's desires.

children.text: phalgvīśaṃ phalgucaṇḍīṃ ca gaurīṃ dṛṣṭvā ca maṅgalām ||
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Phalgvīśa</s>, <s>Phalgucaṇḍī</s>, <s>Gaurī</s>, and <s>Maṅgalā</s>,
and the god <s>Gomaka</s>, <s>Gopati</s>, one becomes free from debt to the ancestors.

children.text: aṅgāreśaṃ ca siddheśaṃ gayādityaṃ gajaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Having seen <s>Aṅgāreśa</s>, <s>Siddheśa</s>, <s>Gayāditya</s>, and likewise <s>Gaja</s>,
and <s>Mārkaṇḍeyeśvara</s>, one becomes free from debt to the ancestors.

children.text: phalgutīrthe naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā devaṃ gadādharam ||
children.translated_text: When a man has bathed at <s>Phalgu-tīrtha</s> and seen the god <s>Gadādhara</s>,

children.text: etena kiṃ na paryāptaṃ nṝṇāṃ sukṛtakāriṇām
children.translated_text: what is not made sufficient by this for men who do meritorious deeds?
Here twenty-one generations of men go to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ yāni tīrthāni ye samudrāḥ sarāṃsi ca
children.translated_text: All the <s>tīrthas</s> that are on earth, and the oceans and lakes,
will go to <s>Phalgu-tīrtha</s> once, day by day.

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ ca gayā puṇyā gayāyāṃ ca gayāśiraḥ
children.translated_text: On earth <s>Gayā</s> is holy; in <s>Gayā</s>, <s>Gayāśiras</s> is holy.

children.text: śreṣṭhaṃ tathā phalgutīrthaṃ tanmukhaṃ ca surasya hi ||
children.translated_text: Likewise <s>Phalgu-tīrtha</s> is the best, for it is the very mouth of the god.
To the north are the <s>Kanakā</s> rivers; in the middle is <s>Nābhi-tīrtha</s>.
Holy is <s>Brahmasadas-tīrtha</s>; by bathing there it grants <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Having performed <s>piṇḍa</s>-giving and the like at the well, one becomes free from debt to the ancestors.
Likewise, at <s>Akṣayavaṭa</s>, a performer of <s>śrāddha</s> leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Having bathed at <s>Haṃsa-tīrtha</s>, a man is released from all sins.
At <s>Koṭi-tīrtha</s>, at <s>Gayālola</s>, at <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, and at <s>Gomaka</s>,
a performer of <s>śrāddha</s> leads twenty-one generations of men to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
At <s>Brahma-tīrtha</s>, <s>Rāma-tīrtha</s>, the southeastern <s>Āgneya</s>, and <s>Soma-tīrtha</s>,
One who performs <s>śrāddha</s> (an ancestral rite) at <s>Rāmahrada</s> leads his ancestral family to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: uttare mānase śrāddhī na bhūyo jāyate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man who performs <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Uttara Mānasa</s> is not born again.
One who performs <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Dakṣiṇa Mānasa</s> leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
At <s>Svargadvāra</s>, a man who performs <s>śrāddha</s> leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
One who performs the <s>tarpaṇa</s> (libation) for <s>Bhīṣma</s>, at that peak, carries the ancestors across.
Likewise, one who performs <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Gṛdhreśvara</s> becomes free of debt to the ancestors.
And one who performs <s>śrāddha</s> in <s>Dhenukāraṇya</s> leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: tiladhenupradaḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā dhenuṃ na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: After bathing and seeing the cow, the giver of a sesame-cow obtains this, without doubt.

children.text: aindre vā naratīrthe ca vāsave vaiṣṇave tathā
children.translated_text: At the <s>Aindra</s> tīrtha, at <s>Naratīrtha</s>, and likewise at the <s>Vāsava</s> and <s>Vaiṣṇava</s> tīrthas,
one who has performed <s>śrāddha</s> on the <s>Mahānadī</s> leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: gāyatre caiva sāvitre tīrthe sārasvate tathā
children.translated_text: At the <s>Gāyatra</s>, <s>Sāvitra</s>, and <s>Sārasvata</s> tīrthas too,
one who bathes, performs twilight worship and <s>tarpaṇa</s>, and performs <s>śrāddha</s>

children.text: pitṝṇāṃ tu kulaṃ brahmalokaṃ nayati mānavaḥ
children.translated_text: leads one hundred and one ancestral families to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
The restrained man, intent on the ancestors, should come forth from <s>Brahmayoni</s>.
Having satisfied the ancestors and the gods, he does not enter the distress of the womb.
At the <s>tarpaṇa</s> at <s>Kākajaṅghāri</s>, the satisfaction of the ancestors is inexhaustible.
By <s>śrāddha</s> in <s>Dharmāraṇya</s>, at <s>Mataṅga</s>'s well, one goes to heaven.

children.text: dharmayūpe ca kūpe ca pitṝṇāmanṛṇo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: And at <s>Dharmayūpa</s> and the well, one becomes free of debt to the ancestors.
Let the deities be authority; let the guardians of the worlds be witnesses:
'Having come here to <s>Mataṅga</s>, I have performed release from debt for the ancestors.'

children.text: rāmatīrthe narāḥ snātvā śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā prabhāsake
children.translated_text: After men bathe at <s>Rāmatīrtha</s> and perform <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Prabhāsaka</s>,
the hosts of ancestors, it is said, are freed from the state of ghosts upon the stone.

children.text: śrāddhakṛcca svapuṣṭāyāṃ triḥ saphta kulam uddharet
children.translated_text: One who performs <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Svapuṣṭā</s> raises up three times seven families.
One who performs <s>śrāddha</s> at <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s> and the other places leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: gayāyāṃ na hi tatsthānaṃ yatra tīrthaṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: In <s>Gayā</s> there is no place where a sacred tīrtha is not found.

children.text: pañcakrośe gayākṣetre yatra tatra tu piṇḍadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Within the five-krośa field of <s>Gayā</s>, wherever one offers a <s>piṇḍa</s> (ancestral food-ball),
he obtains imperishable fruit and leads the ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>.

children.text: janārdanasya haste tu piṇḍaṃ dadyātsvakaṃ naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man should place his own <s>piṇḍa</s> in the hand of <s>Janārdana</s>.

children.text: eṣa piṇḍe mayā dattastava haste janārdana
children.translated_text: 'This <s>piṇḍa</s> has been given by me in your hand, <s>Janārdana</s>;
when I have gone to the other world, may imperishable liberation attend me.'
He surely obtains <s>Brahmaloka</s> together with the ancestors.
In <s>Gayā</s>, at <s>Dharmapṛṣṭha</s>, and likewise at the lake of <s>Brahmā</s>,
at <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s> and <s>Akṣayavaṭa</s>, what is given to the ancestors is imperishable.
<s>Dharmāraṇya</s>, <s>Dharmapṛṣṭha</s>, and <s>Dhenukāraṇya</s> too:
having seen these, one raises up the ancestors and twenty members of one's noble lineage.
The western part of the <s>Mahānadī</s> is called <s>Brahmāraṇya</s>.
The eastern part is the region of <s>Brahmasada</s>, <s>Nāgādri</s>, and <s>Bharatāśrama</s>.
In <s>Bharata</s>'s hermitage, the performer of <s>śrāddha</s> should be at the foot-place of <s>Mataṅga</s>.
South of <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s> and west of the <s>Mahānadī</s>,
that is remembered as <s>Campakavana</s>; there indeed is <s>Pāṇḍuśilā</s>.
The performer of <s>śrāddha</s> there, at <s>Tṛtīyā</s> and in the district of <s>Niścirā</s>,
and at <s>Mahāhrada</s> and <s>Kauśikī</s>, obtains imperishable fruit.
North of the <s>Vaitaraṇī</s> is the body of water called <s>Tṛtīyā</s>.

children.text: padāni tatra krauñcasya śrāddhī svargaṃ nayetpitṝn ||
children.translated_text: There are the footprints of <s>Krauñca</s>; the performer of <s>śrāddha</s> leads the ancestors to heaven.
North of <s>Krauñcapāda</s> is the body of water called <s>Niścirā</s>.
Even a single visit there and a single dropping of a <s>piṇḍa</s>

children.text: durlabhaṃ kiṃ punarnityam asmin eva vyavasthitiḥ
children.translated_text: is hard to obtain; how much more so constant residence in this very place?
Having touched the water of the <s>Mahānadī</s>, one should satisfy the ancestral deities.
He obtains imperishable worlds and also raises up his family.

children.text: sāvitre paṭhyate sandhyā kṛtā syād dvādaśābdikī ||
children.translated_text: When the twilight prayer is recited at <s>Sāvitra</s>, it is as though a twelve-year observance had been performed.
The man who stays at <s>Gayā</s> through both fortnights, bright and dark,

children.text: punāty ā saptamaṃ caiva kulaṃ nāstyatra saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: purifies his family up to the seventh generation; there is no doubt about this.

children.text: gayāyāṃ muṇḍapṛṣṭhaṃ ca aravindaṃ ca parvatam
children.translated_text: At <s>Gayā</s>, <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, <s>Aravinda</s>, and the mountain,

children.text: tṛtīyaṃ krauñcapādaṃ ca dṛṣṭvā pāpaiḥ pramucyate ||
children.translated_text: and after seeing the third place, <s>Krauñcapāda</s>, one is released from sins.
When the sun is in <s>Makara</s>, and at eclipses of the moon and sun,
the dropping of a <s>piṇḍa</s> at <s>Gayā</s> is rare in the three worlds.
At <s>Mahāhrada</s> and <s>Kauśikī</s>, and especially at <s>Mūlakṣetra</s>,
and in the cave of <s>Gṛdhrakūṭa</s>, a <s>śrāddha</s> that is given has great fruit.

children.text: yatra māheśvarī dhārā śrāddhī tatrānṛṇo bhavet
children.translated_text: Where the <s>Māheśvarī</s> stream flows, the performer of <s>śrāddha</s> there becomes free from ancestral debt.
Having reached the holy, broad river famed throughout the three worlds,
the performer of <s>śrāddha</s> obtains the fruit of an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and goes to heaven.
After bathing at <s>Māsapada</s>, the performer of <s>śrāddha</s> gains the fruit of a <s>Vājapeya</s>.
By giving a <s>piṇḍa</s> at <s>Ravipāda</s>, there is the raising up of the fallen.
Whoever, standing in <s>Gayā</s>, gives food, by him the ancestors possess a son.
The ancestors, trembling with fear of hell, long for sons:
'Whoever will go to <s>Gayā</s> will carry us across.'
When the ancestors see a son who has reached <s>Gayā</s>, there is rejoicing among them.

children.text: padbhyāmapi jalaṃ spṛṣṭvā asmabhyaṃ kila dāsyati ||
children.translated_text: 'Even after touching the water with his feet, he will surely give it to us.'

children.text: ātmajo vā tathānyo vā gayākūpe yadā tadā
children.translated_text: Whether one's own son or another, whenever he is at <s>Gayākūpa</s>,
in whatever name he drops a <s>piṇḍa</s>, he leads that person to the eternal <s>Brahman</s>.
One who goes to <s>Koṭitīrtha</s> obtains <s>Puṇḍarīka</s> and <s>Viṣṇuloka</s>.

children.text: yā sā vaitaraṇī nāma triṣu lokeṣu viśrutā ||
children.translated_text: That which is named <s>Vaitaraṇī</s>, famed in the three worlds,
has descended into the field of <s>Gayā</s> for the sake of carrying the ancestors across.
One who gives <s>śrāddha</s>, gives <s>piṇḍas</s> there, and makes a gift of a cow,
saves twenty-one lineages; there is no doubt about this.
If a son should go to <s>Gayā</s> at some time in the course of time...
One should feed those very Brahmins who were appointed by <s>Brahmā</s>;

children.text: teṣāṃ brahmasadaḥ sthānaṃ somapānaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: for them there is residence in <s>Brahmā's</s> assembly and likewise the drinking of soma.
The place was prepared by <s>Brahmā</s>, and the Brahmins were appointed by <s>Brahmā</s>.

children.text: pūjitaiḥ pūjitāḥ sarve pitṛbhiḥ saha devatāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When they are honored, all the deities together with the ancestors are honored.
Therefore one should satisfy the Brahmins of <s>Gayā</s> with offerings for gods and ancestors according to rule;
when the body is abandoned, residence in <s>Gayā</s> is prescribed.
A man who performs the release of a bull in the unsurpassed field of <s>Gayā</s>
obtains the merit of a hundred <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> sacrifices; there is no doubt about this.
Even for himself, a very wise man at <s>Gayā</s>, even without sesame seeds,
should perform the offering of piṇḍas, and for others also, O man.
As many paternal kinsmen, relatives, and friends as there are,
to them a piṇḍa should be given according to rule on the ground of <s>Vyāsagayā</s>.
After bathing at <s>Rāmatīrtha</s>, a man obtains the fruit of a hundred cows;
and after bathing in <s>Mataṅga's</s> reservoir, he gains the fruit of a thousand cows.
After bathing at the confluence of <s>Niścirā</s>, he leads his ancestors to <s>Brahmaloka</s>;
after bathing in <s>Vasiṣṭha's</s> hermitage, he also obtains the <s>Vājapeya</s>.
By dwelling at <s>Mahākauśī</s>, he gains the fruit of an <s>Aśvamedha</s>;
from the lake of <s>Pitāmaha</s> issued forth a purifier of the worlds.

children.text: samīpe tvagnidhāreti viśrutā kapilā hi sā
children.translated_text: Nearby, as <s>Agnidhārā</s>, she is renowned; she indeed is <s>Kapilā</s>.
A performer of śrāddha, having bathed here, gains the fruit of an <s>Agniṣṭoma</s> and has fulfilled his purpose.
A performer of śrāddha at <s>Kumāradhārā</s> obtains the fruit of an <s>Aśvamedha</s>;
then, having approached <s>Kumāra</s> and bowed, he obtains liberation.

children.text: somakuṇḍe naraḥ snātvā somalokaṃ ca gacchati
children.translated_text: A man, having bathed in <s>Somakuṇḍa</s>, goes to <s>Somaloka</s>;

children.text: saṃvartasya naro vāpyāṃ subhagaḥ syāttu piṇḍadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the man who gives piṇḍas in <s>Saṃvarta's</s> reservoir becomes fortunate.

children.text: dhautapāpo naro yāti pretakuṇḍe ca piṇḍadaḥ
children.translated_text: At <s>Pretakuṇḍa</s> too, the man who gives piṇḍas goes forth with his sins washed away.
At <s>Devanadī</s>, <s>Lelihāna</s>, <s>Mathana</s>, and <s>Jānugartaka</s>,
at such tīrthas and others, the giver of piṇḍas saves his ancestors.
Having bowed to the gods beginning with <s>Vasiṣṭheśa</s>, he brings about the extinction of debt.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe gayāmāhātmyaṃ nāma tryaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighty-third chapter, named 'The Greatness of <s>Gayā</s>,' is completed.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: udyatastu gayāṃ gantuṃ śrāddhaṃ kṛtvā vidhānataḥ
children.translated_text: One who has set out to go to <s>Gayā</s>, having performed śrāddha according to rule,
and having put on the kārpaṭī garb and circumambulated even the village,
then, after going to another village, should eat the remainder of the śrāddha food;
having done so and having circumambulated, he should go on, abstaining from accepting gifts.
From the very moment he has set out from home to go to <s>Gayā</s>,
there is, at every step, a stairway for the ancestors' ascent to heaven.
Shaving the head and fasting: this is the rule at all tīrthas,
except for <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, <s>Viśālā</s>, <s>Virajā</s>, and <s>Gayā</s>.

children.text: divā ca sarvadā rātrau gayāyāṃ śrāddhakṛdbhavet
children.translated_text: At <s>Gayā</s> one may always perform śrāddha, by day or by night;

children.text: vārāṇasyāṃ kṛtaṃ śrāddhaṃ tīrthe śoṇanade tathā ||
children.translated_text: the śrāddha performed at <s>Vārāṇasī</s> and likewise at the tīrtha on the <s>Śoṇa</s> river,

children.text: punaḥ punā mahānadyāṃ śrāddhī svargaṃ pitṝnnayet
children.translated_text: and again and again on the <s>Mahānadī</s>, leads the ancestors of the śrāddha-performer to heaven.
Having gone to <s>Uttara Mānasa</s>, he attains unsurpassed perfection.
There he should carry out śrāddha, and he should also carry out bathing.
He obtains divine desires and, in every way, the means to liberation.

children.text: dakṣiṇaṃ mānasaṃ gatvā maunī piṇḍādi kārayet
children.translated_text: Having gone to <s>Dakṣiṇa Mānasa</s>, keeping silence, he should have piṇḍa-offerings and the like performed.
At <s>Dakṣiṇa Mānasa</s> he obtains the removal of the three debts.
It brings delight to the siddhas and is terrifying to sins,
blazing, very fearsome, unharmed, and associated with the foremost serpents.

children.text: nāmnā kanakhalaṃ tīrthaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
children.translated_text: The tīrtha named <s>Kanakhala</s> is renowned in the three worlds,
north of <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, served by hosts of divine seers.

children.text: tatra snātvā divaṃ yāti śrāddhaṃ dattamathākṣayam
children.translated_text: Having bathed there, one goes to heaven, and śrāddha given there is inexhaustible.
Having bowed to the Sun, the man who has completed the proper rites beginning with piṇḍa-offering should say this:
May <s>Kavyavāha</s>, <s>Soma</s>, <s>Yama</s>, and likewise <s>Aryaman</s>,
the <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, <s>Barhiṣads</s>, <s>Somapās</s>, and the ancestral deities,
come here, O greatly fortunate ones, protected here by you;

children.text: madīyāḥ pitaro ye ca kule jātāḥ sanābhayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and may those ancestors of mine who were born in the family, my close kinsmen,
come here. I have come to this <s>Gayā</s> for the purpose of giving piṇḍas to them.
Having made the piṇḍa-offering at <s>Phalgutīrtha</s>, he should behold the god <s>Pitāmaha</s>.
Then he should behold <s>Gadādhara</s> and become free from debt to the ancestors.

children.text: phalgutīrthe naraḥ snātvā dṛṣṭvā devaṃ gadādharam ||
children.translated_text: A man, having bathed at <s>Phalgutīrtha</s> and seen the god <s>Gadādhara</s>,
immediately saves himself, ten ancestors before him and ten descendants after him.
The rule for the first day has been stated; on the second day he should go
to <s>Dharmāraṇya</s> and perform piṇḍa-offerings and the like in <s>Mataṅga's</s> reservoir.
Having reached <s>Dharmāraṇya</s>, he obtains the fruit of a <s>Vājapeya</s>.
At <s>Brahmatīrthaka</s> there is the fruit of the <s>Rājasūya</s> and <s>Aśvamedha</s> sacrifices.

children.text: śrāddhaṃ piṇḍodakaṃ kāryaṃ madhye vai kūpayūpayoḥ ||
children.translated_text: Śrāddha and piṇḍa-water offerings should be made between the well and the sacrificial post.
That should be done with water from the well; what is given to the ancestors is inexhaustible.
On the third day, having gone to <s>Brahmasadas</s> and bathed, he should then perform tarpaṇa,

children.text: kṛtvā śrāddhādikaṃ piṇḍaṃ madhye vai yūpakūpayoḥ
children.translated_text: and, having performed śrāddha and the rest, offer the piṇḍa between the sacrificial post and the well.
Near <s>Gopracāra</s> are those appointed by <s>Brahmā</s>, extending up to <s>Brahmā</s>.
By merely serving them, the ancestors go toward liberation.
Having circumambulated the sacrificial post, one obtains the fruit of a <s>Vājapeya</s>.
On the fourth day, after bathing at <s>Phalgutīrtha</s> and satisfying the gods and others,
having performed śrāddha on <s>Gayāśīrṣa</s>, he should do it at <s>Rudrapada</s> and the other places.

children.text: piṇḍāndehi mukhe vyāse pañcāgnau ca padatraye
children.translated_text: Give piṇḍas at <s>Vyāsa's</s> mouth, at <s>Pañcāgni</s>, and at the three footprints.
A śrāddha performed at <s>Sūrya</s>, <s>Indu</s>, and <s>Kārttikeya</s> is likewise inexhaustible.
One should perform a śrāddha for nine deities and for twelve deities
on the Anvaṣṭakā days, at a rite for increase, at <s>Gayā</s>, and on the day of death.

children.text: atra mātuḥ pṛthak śrāddhamanyatra patinā saha
children.translated_text: Here the śrāddha for the mother is separate; elsewhere it is together with her husband.

children.text: snātvā daśāśvamedhe tu dṛṣṭvā devaṃ pitāmaham ||
children.translated_text: Having bathed at <s>Daśāśvamedha</s> and seen the god <s>Pitāmaha</s>,

children.text: rudrapādaṃ naraḥ spṛṣṭvā na cehāvartate punaḥ
children.translated_text: and having touched <s>Rudrapāda</s>, a man does not return again to this world.
The fruit that one would obtain by giving the earth filled with wealth three times,
that same fruit he obtains by performing śrāddha at <s>Gayāśiras</s>.
If at <s>Gayāśiras</s> he gives a piṇḍa the size of a śamī leaf,

children.text: pitaro yānti devatvaṃ nātra kāryā vicāraṇā
children.translated_text: the ancestors attain divine status; no doubt should be entertained about this.
On <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s> the footprint was placed by the wise <s>Mahādeva</s>.
With even a little austerity there one obtains great merit.

children.text: gayāśīrṣe tu yaḥ piṇḍānnāmnā yeṣāṃ tu nirvapet ||
children.translated_text: At <s>Gayāśiras</s>, for those in whose names one offers piṇḍas,
those who are in hell go to heaven, and those who are in heaven obtain liberation.
On the fifth day, having bathed at <s>Gayālola</s>, then beneath the vaṭa tree,
one should give piṇḍas for the ancestors, and he rescues his entire family.
Having reached the root of the vaṭa tree, even with vegetables or with hot water,
when one Brahmin is fed, O Brahmin, ten million are counted as fed.
When śrāddha has been performed at the <s>Akṣayavaṭa</s> and <s>Prapitāmaha</s> has been seen,
one obtains imperishable worlds and rescues a hundred families.

children.text: eṣṭavyā bahavaḥ puttrā yadyeko 'pi gayāṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: Many sons should be desired, if even one of them might go to <s>Gayā</s>,
or might sacrifice with a horse-sacrifice, or might release a blue bull.
A certain preta, addressing a certain merchant, said:
'In my name, perform the offering of a piṇḍa at <s>Gayāśiras</s>.
I would be freed from the condition of a preta, and it would give heaven to the giver as well.'
Having heard this, the merchant at <s>Gayāśiras</s> offered a piṇḍa to the king of pretas,
together with his younger brothers, and afterward he gave offerings to his own ancestors.
All were liberated, and <s>Viśāla</s> too, the giver of piṇḍas, became possessed of a son.
In <s>Viśālā</s> there was <s>Viśāla</s>, a prince; he said to the Brahmins:
'How may sons and the like be mine?' And the Brahmins answered <s>Viśāla</s>:
'Through the giving of piṇḍas at <s>Gayā</s>, everything will come to be for you.'
Then <s>Viśāla</s> became a giver of piṇḍas at <s>Gayāśiras</s> and became possessed of sons.
Seeing in the sky a white, a red, and a black man, he spoke:

children.text: ke yūyaṃ teṣu caivaikaḥ sitaḥ proce viśālakam
children.translated_text: 'Who are you?' And one among them, the white one, said to <s>Viśāla</s>:

children.text: ahaṃ sitaste janaka indralokaṃ gataḥ śabham ||
children.translated_text: 'I am the white one, your father, who has gone to the auspicious world of <s>Indra</s>.

children.text: mama putra pitā rakto brahmahā pāpakṛtparam
children.translated_text: My son, my father is the red one, a Brahmin-slayer and supreme sinner.
This black one is my grandfather; sages were killed by him.

children.text: avīciṃ narakaṃ prāptau muktau jātau ca piṇḍada
children.translated_text: They had reached the <s>Avīci</s> hell, but they have now been liberated, O giver of piṇḍas.
After that, all of us have been set free, and we go to the highest heaven.'

children.text: kṛtakṛtyo viśālo 'pi rājyaṃ kṛtvā divaṃ yayau
children.translated_text: <s>Viśāla</s> too, having accomplished his purpose and ruled the kingdom, went to heaven.
May those ancestors in our family whose rites of piṇḍa and water have lapsed,
and those who had no tonsure ceremony performed, and those who came forth from the womb,

children.text: yeṣāṃ dāho na kriyā ca ye 'gnidagdhāstathāpare ||
children.translated_text: those for whom there was no cremation and no rite, and likewise others who were burned by fire,

children.text: bhūmau dattena tṛpyantu tṛptā yāntu parāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: be satisfied by what is given on the ground; satisfied, may they go to the highest state.
The father, the grandfather, and likewise the great-grandfather,
the mother, the paternal grandmother, and likewise the paternal great-grandmother,
and likewise the maternal grandfather and the maternal great-grandfather,
the aged maternal great-grandfather, and likewise the maternal grandmother thereafter,
the maternal great-grandmother and the aged maternal great-grandmother too:
may this piṇḍa for these and for others become inexhaustible and present itself to them.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe gayāmāhātmyaṃ nāma caturaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighty-fourth chapter, named 'The Greatness of <s>Gayā</s>,' is completed.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Having bathed at <s>Pretaśilā</s> and the other places, and with water belonging to <s>Varuṇa</s> and nectar,
one should give the piṇḍa with these mantras, after invoking the ancestors and the more remote ancestors.

children.text: asmatkule mṛtā ye ca gatiryeṣāṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: Those who have died in our family, and for whom no path is known,
I shall invoke all of them upon the surface of darbha grass with sesame-water.

children.text: pitṛvaṃśe mṛtā ye ca mātṛvaṃśe ca ye mṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have died in the paternal line, and those who have died in the maternal line,
for the sake of their rescue, I give this piṇḍa.

children.text: mātāmahakule ye ca gatiryeṣāṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: Those in the family of the maternal grandfather for whom no path is known,
for the sake of their rescue, I give this piṇḍa.

children.text: ajātadantā ye kecidye ca garbhe prapīḍitāḥ
children.translated_text: Those, whoever they are, whose teeth had not yet appeared, and those who were afflicted in the womb,
for the sake of their rescue, I give this piṇḍa.
And whatever groups of relatives there are, bereft of name and gotra,

children.text: svagotre paragotre vā gatiryeṣāṃ na vidyate
children.translated_text: whether in one's own gotra or in another gotra, for whom no path is known,
for the sake of their rescue, I give this piṇḍa.
Those who died by hanging, and those killed by poison or weapons,

children.text: ātmopaghātino ye ca tebhyaḥ piṇḍaṃ dadāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: and those who killed themselves: to them I give a piṇḍa.
Those who died in a conflagration, and those killed by lions and tigers,
or by fanged beasts or by horned animals: for them I give a piṇḍa.
Those, whoever they are, who were burned by fire, and also others who were not burned by fire,

children.text: vidyuccaurahatā ye ca tebhyaḥ piṇḍaṃ dadāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: and those killed by lightning or thieves: to them I give a piṇḍa.

children.text: raurave cāndhatāmisre kālasūtre ca ye gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have gone to <s>Raurava</s>, to <s>Andhatāmisra</s>, and to <s>Kālasūtra</s>,
for the sake of their rescue, I give this piṇḍa.

children.text: asipatravane ghore kumbhīpāke ca ye gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who have gone to the dreadful <s>Asipatravana</s> and to <s>Kumbhīpāka</s>,
for the sake of their rescue, I give this piṇḍa.
For others who dwell in places of torment and in the world of pretas,
for the sake of their rescue, I give this piṇḍa.
And those who have gone into animal wombs, as birds, insects, or reptiles,
or who abide in the womb of trees: to them I give this <s>piṇḍa</s> offering.
Those who have been led by the commands of <s>Yama</s> into places of countless torments:
for the sake of rescuing them, I give this <s>piṇḍa</s> offering.
Those who wander through thousands of other births by their own karma,

children.text: mānuṣyaṃ durlabhaṃ yeṣāṃ tebhyaḥ piṇḍaṃ dadāmyaham ||
children.translated_text: for whom human birth is hard to obtain: to them I give this <s>piṇḍa</s> offering.
Those who are kin or not kin, and those who were kin in another birth:
may they all always attain satisfaction through the gift of <s>piṇḍas</s>.
Whatever ancestors of mine remain in the form of pretas,
may they all always attain satisfaction through the gift of <s>piṇḍas</s>.

children.text: ye me pitṛkule jātāḥ kule mātustathaiva ca
children.translated_text: Those born in my father's lineage, and likewise in my mother's lineage,
and those among teachers, fathers-in-law, and relatives, and whatever other kinsmen have died;
those in my family whose <s>piṇḍa</s> offerings have lapsed, who are without sons and wives,
those injured by the failure of rites, those blind from birth, and likewise the lame;
the deformed, those who died in the womb, and those known and unknown in my family:
may the <s>piṇḍa</s> given by me stand before them, inexhaustible.
May the gods be my witnesses, <s>Brahmā</s>, <s>Īśāna</s>, and the others.

children.text: mayā gayāṃ samāsādya pitṝṇāṃ niṣkṛtiḥ kṛtā ||
children.translated_text: Having reached <s>Gayā</s>, I have performed expiation for the ancestors.
I have come to <s>Gayā</s>, O god <s>Gadādhara</s>, for the ancestral rite.
Be my witness today to that: I am free from the three debts.

children.text: mahānadī brahmasaro 'kṣayo vaṭaḥ prabhāsam udyantamaho gayāśiraḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Mahānadī</s>, <s>Brahmasaras</s>, <s>Akṣayavaṭa</s>, <s>Prabhāsa</s>, <s>Udyanta</s>, and indeed <s>Gayāśiras</s>,
<s>Sarasvatī</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, and <s>Kadhenupṛṣṭha</s>: these places of <s>Kurukṣetra</s> are present at <s>Gayā</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe gayāmāhātmyaṃ nāma pañcāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighty-fifth chapter, named 'The Greatness of <s>Gayā</s>,' is completed.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: yeyaṃ pretaśilā khyātā gayāyāṃ sā tridhā sthitā
children.translated_text: This rock known as <s>Pretaśilā</s> at <s>Gayā</s> is situated in three forms:
at <s>Prabhāsa</s>, at <s>Pretakuṇḍa</s>, and also on the head of <s>Gayāsura</s>.
The rock, made of all the gods, was upheld by <s>Dharma</s> for prosperity.

children.text: pretatvaṃ ye gatā nṝṇāṃ mitrādyā bāndhavādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those among men who have entered the state of a preta, friends and other relatives,
because the auspicious <s>Pretaśilā</s> exists for their rescue,
therefore sages, kings, queens, and others here always
become goers to <s>Brahmaloka</s> when they perform <s>śrāddha</s> and the other rites on that rock.

children.text: gayāsurasya yanmuṇḍaṃ tasya pṛṣṭhe śilā yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Because the rock is on the back of the head of <s>Gayāsura</s>,
this mountain is therefore <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, the 'back of the head,' and it is made of all the gods.
Because at the feet of <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s> are the <s>Brahmasaras</s> and the other sources,
and because a lotus grove is among them, it is marked by that as well.
The mountain is named <s>Aravinda</s>, because it is marked by <s>Krauñca</s>'s foot.
Therefore the mountain is <s>Krauñcapāda</s>, granting <s>Brahmaloka</s> to the ancestors.
<s>Gadādhara</s> and the other primordial gods were established there at the beginning.
They are unmanifest in the form of the rock; therefore the rock is made of gods.
The rock covered the head of <s>Gayā</s> and, because of its weight, remained there.
In the course of time <s>Ādigadādhara</s> became manifest and stood there,
<s>Hari</s>, without beginning or end, together with <s>Mahārudra</s> and the other gods,
for the protection of <s>dharma</s> and for the destruction of <s>adharma</s> and the rest.
For the destruction of daityas and rākṣasas, he had formerly become <s>Matsya</s>,
<s>Kūrma</s>, <s>Varāha</s>, <s>Nṛhari</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, and the mighty <s>Rāma</s>,

children.text: yathā dāśarathī rāmaḥ kṛṣṇo buddho 'tha kalkyapi ||
children.translated_text: as <s>Rāma Dāśarathi</s>, as <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, then as <s>Buddha</s>, and also as <s>Kalki</s>.
So too, though of unmanifest form, the primordial <s>Gadādhara</s> became manifest.
Because he was first worshiped here in the beginning by the gods headed by <s>Brahmā</s>,
with water for the feet and the rest, with perfumes, flowers, and the like, therefore he is <s>Ādigadādhara</s>.

children.text: gadādharaṃ suraiḥ sārdhamādyaṃ gatvā dadāti yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever goes to the primordial <s>Gadādhara</s> together with the gods and gives

children.text: arghyaṃ pātraṃ ca pādyaṃ ca gandhapuṣpaṃ ca dhūpakam
children.translated_text: arghya, vessels, water for the feet, perfume, flowers, and incense,

children.text: dīpaṃ naivedyam utkṛṣṭaṃ mālyāni vividhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: a lamp, excellent food-offerings, and various garlands,
garments, a crown, a bell, a chowrie, and a fine viewing-offering,
ornaments and the like, <s>piṇḍas</s>, gifts of food, and so forth:
for them there are wealth, grain, life, health, and prosperity,
the welfare of offspring and descendants, knowledge, wealth, and the desired object of love.
There is a wife, residence in heaven and elsewhere, and after coming back from heaven, sovereignty.
He becomes of noble family, endowed with goodness, with enemies crushed in battle,
freed from execution and imprisonment, and at the end he obtains <s>mokṣa</s>.
Those who perform <s>śrāddha</s>, <s>piṇḍa</s> offerings, and the like go to <s>Brahmaloka</s> with their ancestors.
Those who worship <s>Jagannātha</s>, <s>Subhadrā</s>, and <s>Balabhadra</s>,
having obtained knowledge, fortune, and sons, go to <s>Puruṣottama</s>.
In front of <s>Puruṣottamarāja</s>, <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Gaṇa</s> there,
<s>piṇḍa</s> offerings and the like for the ancestors grant <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Having bowed to <s>Kapardin</s> and <s>Vighneśa</s>, one is freed from all obstacles.
Having worshiped <s>Kārtikeya</s>, one obtains <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Having worshiped the twelve <s>Ādityas</s>, one is freed from all diseases.
Having worshiped <s>Vaiśvānara</s>, one obtains supreme brilliance.
Then, having worshiped <s>Revanta</s>, one obtains unsurpassed horses.
Having worshiped <s>Indra</s>, one obtains great sovereignty; having worshiped <s>Gaurī</s>, good fortune.

children.text: vidyāṃ sarasvatīṃ prārcya lakṣmīṃ sampūjya ca śriyam
children.translated_text: Having worshiped <s>Sarasvatī</s>, one obtains knowledge; having fully worshiped <s>Lakṣmī</s>, prosperity.
And having worshiped <s>Garuḍa</s>, one is freed from hosts of obstacles.
Having worshiped <s>Kṣetrapāla</s>, one is freed from hosts of planets.
Having worshiped <s>Muṇḍapṛṣṭha</s>, one obtains every desire.
Having worshiped the <s>Nāgāṣṭaka</s>, one who has been bitten by a snake is released.
And after worshipping <s>Brahmā</s>, one would attain <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Having worshipped <s>Balabhadra</s>, one would obtain strength and health;
and having worshipped <s>Subhadrā</s>, one would attain supreme good fortune.
Having worshipped <s>Puruṣottama</s>, one obtains all desires.
And having worshipped <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, one becomes lord over men.

children.text: spṛṣṭvā natvā nārasiṃhaṃ saṃgrāme vijayī bhavet
children.translated_text: Having touched and bowed to <s>Nārasiṃha</s>, one becomes victorious in battle.
And having worshipped <s>Varāha</s>, one obtains rule over the earth.
Having touched <s>Mālā</s> and <s>Vidyādhara</s>, one obtains the station of a <s>Vidyādhara</s>.
Having worshipped <s>Ādigadādhara</s>, one obtains all desires.
Having worshipped <s>Somanātha</s>, one attains the world of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having bowed to <s>Rudreśvara</s>, one is honored in the world of <s>Rudra</s>.
A man, having bowed to <s>Rāmeśvara</s>, becomes greatly beloved by <s>Rāma</s>.
A man, having praised <s>Brahmeśvara</s>, becomes fit for <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
A man, having worshipped <s>Kāleśvara</s>, becomes a conqueror of time.
And having worshipped <s>Kedāra</s>, one is honored in the world of <s>Śiva</s>.

children.text: siddheśvaraṃ ca sampūjya siddho brahmapuraṃ vrajet
children.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Siddheśvara</s>, the perfected one goes to <s>Brahmapura</s>.
Having seen <s>Ādigadādhara</s> together with the first <s>Rudra</s>s and the others,
a man, having raised up a hundred families, leads them to <s>Brahmapura</s>.
One seeking <s>dharma</s> obtains <s>dharma</s>; one seeking wealth obtains wealth.
A desirer obtains desired pleasures; one seeking liberation obtains liberation.
One seeking kingship obtains kingship; one seeking peace obtains peace.
One seeking every goal obtains everything by worshipping <s>Ādigadādhara</s>.

children.text: putrānputrārthinī strī ca saubhāgyaṃ ca tadarthinī ||
children.translated_text: A woman who desires sons obtains sons, and one who desires good fortune obtains that good fortune.
And a woman who desires lineage indeed obtains lineage after worshipping <s>Ādigadādhara</s>.
Through <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestral rite), the giving of <s>piṇḍa</s>s, the giving of food, and the giving of water,
one attains <s>Brahmaloka</s> after worshipping <s>Ādigadādhara</s>.

children.text: pṛthivyāṃ sarvatīrthebhyo yathā śreṣṭhā gayā purī ||
children.translated_text: Just as the city of <s>Gayā</s> is best among all tīrthas on earth,
so too <s>Gadādhara</s>, whose form begins with stone, is also the best.

children.text: tasmindṛṣṭe śilā dṛṣṭā yataḥ sarvaṃ gadādharaḥ ||
children.translated_text: When he is seen, the stone has been seen, because <s>Gadādhara</s> is everything.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe gayāmāhātmyaṃ nāma ṣaḍaśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighty-sixth chapter, named The Greatness of <s>Gayā</s>, is completed.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall describe the fourteen <s>Manu</s>s and their sons, beginning with <s>Suka</s> and the others.
First was <s>Svāyambhuva Manu</s>; <s>Agnighra</s> and the others were his sons.
<s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,
and the very splendid <s>Vasiṣṭha</s> are named as the seven sages.
Those called <s>Jaya</s>, those called <s>Śācamita</s>, the <s>Śukra</s>s, and likewise the <s>Yāma</s>s
are said to be four twelvefold groups, drinkers of soma.
<s>Viśvabhuk Vāmadeva</s> was <s>Indra</s>; <s>Bāṣkali</s> indeed became his enemy.
That <s>Daitya</s> was slain by the great-souled <s>Viṣṇu</s> with his discus.
Then came <s>Svārociṣa Manu</s>; his son was <s>Maṇḍaleśvara</s>.
<s>Citraka</s>, <s>Vinata</s>, <s>Karṇānta</s>, <s>Vidyut</s>, and <s>Ravi</s>,
<s>Bṛhadguṇa</s> and <s>Nabhas</s>, possessing great strength and valor,
<s>Ūrjastambha</s>, <s>Prāṇa</s>, <s>Ṛṣabha</s>, and also <s>Niścala</s>,
