<s>Dattoli</s> and <s>Avarīvāṃs</s> are named as the seven sages.
The <s>Tuṣita</s>s are said to be twelve, and so too those who are <s>Pārāvata</s>s.
<s>Vipaścit</s> was <s>Indra</s> of the gods; his enemy was <s>Purukṛtsara</s>.
The Lord <s>Madhusūdana</s> slew him in the form of an elephant.
The sons of <s>Auttama Manu</s> were <s>Āja</s> and <s>Paraśu</s>,
<s>Vinīta</s>, <s>Suketu</s>, <s>Sumitra</s>, <s>Subala</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>,
<s>Deva</s>, <s>Devāvṛdha</s>, <s>Rudra</s>, <s>Mahotsāha</s>, and <s>Jita</s>.
<s>Rathaujā</s>, <s>Ūrdhvabāhu</s>, <s>Śaraṇa</s>, and the blameless sage
<s>Sutapas</s> and <s>Śaṅku</s>: these are named as the seven sages.
The <s>Vaśavarti</s>s, the <s>Svadhāman</s>s, the <s>Śiva</s>s, the <s>Satya</s>s, and the <s>Pratardana</s>s

children.text: pañca devagaṇāḥ proktāḥ sarve dvādaśakāstu te
children.translated_text: are declared to be five groups of gods, all of them twelvefold.
<s>Svaśānti</s> was <s>Indra</s>; his enemy was the <s>Dānava</s> named <s>Pralamba</s>.
<s>Hari Viṣṇu</s>, in the form of a fish, slew that <s>Dānava</s>.
The sons of <s>Tāmasa Manu</s> were <s>Jānujaṅgha</s> and then <s>Nirbhaya</s>,
<s>Navakhyāti</s>, <s>Naya</s>, <s>Priyabhṛtya</s>, and <s>Vivikṣipa</s>,
<s>Dṛḍheṣudhi</s>, <s>Prastalākṣa</s>, <s>Kṛbandhu</s>, and <s>Kṛta</s>.
<s>Jyotirdhāman</s>, <s>Pṛthu</s>, <s>Kāvya</s>, <s>Caitra</s>, <s>Cetāgni</s>, and <s>Hemaka</s>
are named as the seven sages; so too the <s>Surāga</s>s and the <s>Sudhiya</s>s.
The <s>Hari</s>s and the <s>Devatāmā</s>s were four groups, each numbering twenty-five.

children.text: gaṇā indraḥ śibis tasya śatrur bhīmarathāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śibi</s> was <s>Indra</s> of the hosts; his enemy is remembered as <s>Bhīmaratha</s>.
The Asura <s>Bhīmaratha</s> was slain by <s>Hari</s> in the form of a tortoise.
The son of <s>Raivata Manu</s> was <s>Mahāprāṇa</s>, and also <s>Sādhaka</s>.
<s>Vanabandhu</s>, <s>Niramitra</s>, <s>Pratyaṅga</s>, <s>Parahā</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>,
<s>Dṛḍhavrata</s> and <s>Ketuśṛṅga</s>; his sages are described.
<s>Vedaśrī</s>, <s>Vedabāhu</s>, and likewise <s>Ūrdhvabāhu</s>,
<s>Hiraṇyaroman</s>, <s>Parjanya</s>, <s>Satyanetra</s>, and <s>Svadhāman</s>,
and the <s>Abhūtarajasa</s>s, and likewise the <s>Devāśvamedhasa</s>s,
the <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>s and the <s>Amṛta</s>s were the four groups of deities.

children.text: gaṇe caturdaśa surā vibhur indraḥ pratāpavān
children.translated_text: In each group there were fourteen gods; <s>Vibhu</s> was the powerful <s>Indra</s>.
The enemy, the <s>Daitya</s> <s>Śānta</s>, was slain by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of a swan.
The sons of <s>Cākṣuṣa Manu</s> were <s>Uru</s>, <s>Puru</s>, and mighty <s>Mahābala</s>,
<s>Śatadyumna</s>, <s>Tapasvī</s>, <s>Satyabāhu</s>, and <s>Kṛti</s>,
<s>Agniṣṇu</s>, <s>Atirātra</s>, <s>Sudyumna</s>, and likewise <s>Nara</s>.
<s>Haviṣmān</s>, <s>Uttama</s>, the illustrious <s>Svadhāmā</s>, and likewise <s>Virajas</s>,
<s>Abhimāna</s>, <s>Sahiṣṇu</s>, and <s>Madhuśrī</s> are remembered as the sages.
<s>Āryās</s>, <s>Prabhūtās</s>, <s>Bhāvyās</s>, <s>Lekhās</s>, and likewise <s>Pṛthukās</s>:

children.text: aṣṭakasya gaṇāḥ pañca tathā proktā divaukasām
children.translated_text: these five hosts of the heaven-dwellers are declared for the eighth one.
The <s>Indra</s> will be <s>Manojava</s>; the enemy, <s>Mahākāla</s> and <s>Mahābhaja</s>,
was slain in horse form by <s>Hari</s>, the sustainer of the worlds.
These are the sons of <s>Vaivasvata Manu</s>, devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>:
<s>Ikṣvāku</s>, then <s>Nābhāga</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, and also <s>Śaryāti</s>,
<s>Nariṣyanta</s>, likewise <s>Pāṃsu</s>, <s>Nabha</s>, and <s>Nediṣṭha</s>,
<s>Karūṣa</s>, <s>Pṛṣadhra</s>, and <s>Sudyumna</s> are the sons of <s>Manu</s>.
<s>Atri</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, the venerable <s>Jamadagni</s>, and <s>Kaśyapa</s>,
<s>Gautama</s>, <s>Bharadvāja</s>, and then <s>Viśvāmitra</s> as the seventh,
and likewise the forty-nine <s>Maruts</s> are celebrated.
The <s>Ādityas</s>, <s>Vasus</s>, and <s>Sādhyas</s> are three hosts of twelve each;
and the eleven <s>Rudras</s> and the eight <s>Vasus</s> are proclaimed.
The two <s>Aśvins</s> are specified, and likewise the ten <s>Viśvedevās</s>.
There are just ten <s>Āṅgirasa</s> gods, and likewise nine hosts of gods.

children.text: tejasvī nāma vai śakro hiraṇyākṣo ripuḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The <s>Śakra</s> is named <s>Tejasvī</s>; <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> is remembered as the enemy.
That one named <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s> was slain by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of a boar.
I shall tell the sons of the future <s>Manu</s> known as <s>Sāvarṇi</s>.
<s>Vijaya</s>, <s>Cārvavīra</s>, <s>Nirmoha</s>, <s>Satyavāk</s>, and <s>Ṛtī</s>,
<s>Variṣṭha</s>, <s>Gariṣṭha</s>, and also <s>Vācaḥsaṃgati</s>,
<s>Aśvatthāmā</s>, <s>Kṛpa</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Gālava</s>, and then <s>Dīptimān</s>,
likewise <s>Ṛṣyaśṛṅga</s> and <s>Rāma</s> are celebrated as the seven sages.
<s>Sutapas</s>, <s>Amṛtābhas</s>, and also the <s>Mukhyas</s> are then the gods.

children.text: teṣāṃ gaṇastu devānām ekaiko viṃśakaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: Of those gods each host is remembered as consisting of twenty.
<s>Bali</s>, the son of <s>Virocana</s>, will be their <s>Indra</s>.
After giving this earth, three steps, to <s>Viṣṇu</s> when he begged for it,
he will abandon prosperity and the rank of <s>Indra</s>, and then attain perfection.
Hear the sons of the ninth, <s>Dakṣasāvarṇi</s>, born from <s>Varuṇa</s>.
<s>Dhṛtiketu</s>, <s>Dīptiketu</s>, <s>Pañcahasta</s>, <s>Nirāmaya</s>,
<s>Pṛthuśravā</s>, <s>Bṛhaddyumna</s>, <s>Ṛcīka</s>, and <s>Bṛhatguṇa</s>,
<s>Medhātithi</s>, <s>Dyuti</s>, <s>Savasa</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>,
<s>Jyotiṣmān</s>, <s>Havya</s>, and <s>Kavya</s>; the sages will be <s>Vibhu</s>, <s>Īśvara</s>,
<s>Para</s>, <s>Marīci</s>, <s>Garbha</s>, and those three called <s>Svadharman</s>.
<s>Deśaśatru</s>, <s>Kālakākṣa</s>, and <s>Padmanābha</s> will be his slayer.

children.text: bhaviṣyanti tadā devā ekaiko dvādaśo gaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: At that time these will be the gods, each host numbering twelve.
Their <s>Indra</s> will be the greatly valiant <s>Adbhuta</s>, O <s>Hara</s>.
Now hear the sons of <s>Dharma</s>'s son, the tenth <s>Manu</s>.
<s>Sukṣetra</s>, <s>Uttamaujas</s>, <s>Bhūriśreṇya</s>, and mighty <s>Vīryavān</s>,
<s>Śatānīka</s>, <s>Niramitra</s>, <s>Vṛṣasena</s>, and <s>Jayadratha</s>,
<s>Bhūridyumna</s> and <s>Suvarcas</s>; <s>Śānti</s> will be the powerful <s>Indra</s>.
<s>Ayomūrti</s>, <s>Haviṣmān</s>, <s>Sukṛti</s>, and likewise <s>Avyaya</s>,
<s>Nābhāga</s>, <s>Apratimaujas</s>, and <s>Saurabha</s> are also the sages.
At that time the host of deities, called <s>Prāṇa</s>, will number one hundred.
Their <s>Indra</s> will be named <s>Śānti</s>, of great strength.
<s>Bali</s> will be the enemy, and <s>Hari</s> will strike him down with a mace.
I shall tell you the sons of <s>Rudra</s>'s son, the eleventh <s>Manu</s>.
<s>Sarvatraga</s>, <s>Suśarman</s>, <s>Devānīka</s>, <s>Puru</s>, and <s>Guru</s>,
<s>Kṣetravarṇa</s>, <s>Dṛḍheṣu</s>, <s>Ārdraka</s>, and likewise <s>Putraka</s>,
<s>Haviṣmān</s>, <s>Haviṣya</s>, <s>Varuṇa</s>, and the two <s>Viśvavistaras</s>,
<s>Viṣṇu</s> and <s>Agnitejas</s> are celebrated as the seven sages.
The gods will be <s>Vihaṅgamas</s>, <s>Kāmagams</s>, and likewise <s>Nirmāṇarucis</s>.
Each host of theirs consists of thirty-one, and their <s>Indra</s> is <s>Vṛṣa</s>.
<s>Dhasagrīva</s> will be his enemy, and the one in the form of <s>Śrī</s> will slay him.
Hear the sons of <s>Dakṣa</s>'s son, the twelfth <s>Manu</s>.
<s>Devavān</s>, <s>Upadeva</s>, <s>Devaśreṣṭha</s>, <s>Vidūratha</s>,
<s>Mitravān</s>, <s>Mitradeva</s>, <s>Mitrabindu</s>, mighty in valor,
<s>Mitravāha</s> and <s>Pravāha</s> are the sons of <s>Dakṣaputra Manu</s>.
<s>Tapasvin</s>, <s>Sutapas</s>, <s>Tapomūrti</s>, <s>Taporati</s>,
<s>Tapodhṛti</s>, another <s>Dyuti</s>, and the seventh, <s>Tapodhana</s>,
the <s>Svadharmans</s>, <s>Sutapas</s>, <s>Haritas</s>, and likewise <s>Hohitas</s>,
and the <s>Surārayas</s>: these are the hosts, each host numbering ten.
<s>Ṛtadhāmā</s> will be the auspicious <s>Indra</s>; <s>Tāraka</s> is the enemy's name.
<s>Hari</s>, becoming a neuter being, will slay him, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
Learn from me the sons of <s>Raucya</s>, the thirteenth <s>Manu</s>.
<s>Citrasena</s>, <s>Vicitra</s>, <s>Tapodharmarata</s>, <s>Dhṛti</s>,
<s>Sunetra</s>, <s>Kṣetravṛtti</s>, <s>Sunaya</s>, <s>Dharmapa</s>, and <s>Dṛḍha</s>,
<s>Dhṛtimān</s>, <s>Avyaya</s>, and also <s>Niśārūpa</s> and <s>Nirutsuka</s>,

children.text: nirmohas tattvadarśī ca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nirmoha</s> and <s>Tattvadarśin</s> are celebrated as the seven sages.
The immortals will be the <s>Svaromans</s>, <s>Svadharmans</s>, and likewise <s>Svakarmans</s>.
There will be thirty-three divisions of the hosts of gods there.
The <s>Indra</s> will be <s>Divaspati</s>; the enemy will be the dānava named <s>Tviṣṭibha</s>.
<s>Mādhava</s> will slay him in the form of a peacock.
Hear from me the sons of <s>Bhautya</s>, the fourteenth <s>Manu</s>.

children.text: urur gabhīro dhṛṣṭaśca tarasvī grāha eva ca
children.translated_text: <s>Uru</s>, <s>Gabhīra</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, <s>Tarasvī</s>, and <s>Grāha</s>,
<s>Abhimānin</s>, <s>Pravīra</s>, <s>Jiṣṇu</s>, and likewise <s>Saṃkrandana</s>,
<s>Tejasvī</s> and <s>Durlabha</s>: these are the sons of <s>Bhautya Manu</s>.
<s>Agnīdhra</s>, <s>Agnibāhu</s>, <s>Māgadha</s>, and likewise <s>Śuci</s>,

children.text: ajito muktaśukrau ca ṛṣayaḥ sapta kīrtitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ajita</s>, and <s>Mukta</s> and <s>Śukra</s>: these are celebrated as the seven seers.
The <s>Cākṣuṣas</s>, the <s>Karmaniṣṭhas</s>, the <s>Pavitras</s>, and likewise the <s>Bhrājins</s>,
and the <s>Vacovṛddhas</s>: these five groups of gods are said to consist of seven each.
<s>Śuci</s> was <s>Indra</s>, a great daitya, the slayer of foes; <s>Hari</s> himself,
the one god, was made fourfold by <s>Viṣṇu</s> in the form of <s>Vyāsa</s>.
Thereafter the <s>Purāṇas</s> and the eighteen branches of knowledge were made:
the ancillary disciplines, the four <s>Vedas</s>, and the extended systems of <s>Mīmāṃsā</s> and <s>Nyāya</s>;
the <s>Purāṇa</s>, <s>Dharmaśāstra</s>, <s>Āyurveda</s>, and <s>Arthaśāstra</s>,
and <s>Dhanurveda</s> and <s>Gāndharva</s>: these indeed are the eighteen branches of knowledge.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe manutadvaṃśanirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighty-seventh chapter, named 'Description of the Manus and Their Lineages,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Hari</s> spoke of the <s>manvantaras</s> to <s>Brahmā</s> and the others, and to <s>Hara</s> as well;
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> told the hymn to the ancestors to <s>Krauñcuki</s>. Hear that.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Formerly <s>Ruci</s> the Prajāpati, without possessiveness and without egoism,
fearless and of immeasurable power, wandered over this earth.
Seeing that sage without a sacred fire, without a dwelling, eating once a day, outside any settled āśrama,

children.text: nimuktasaṅgaṃ taṃ dṛṣṭvā procuḥ svapitaro munim ||
children.translated_text: and free from attachment, his own ancestors addressed him.
The ancestors said:

children.text: vatsa kasmāttvayā puṇyo na kṛto dārasaṃgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: Child, why have you not undertaken the blessed acquisition of a wife?
Since it is a cause of heaven and liberation, without that bond there is constant loss.
A householder, performing the proper honoring of all the gods and also of the ancestors,
and likewise of the seers and of those in need, obtains the worlds.
By uttering <s>svāhā</s> he apportions to the gods; by uttering <s>svadhā</s>, to the ancestors;
by giving food, he also apportions to servants and the like, and to guests.

children.text: sattvaṃ daivād ṛṇād bandham imam asmadṛṇādapi
children.translated_text: O sage among men, from the debt to the gods, from this bond of debt to us,
and from the debt to living beings day by day, you have incurred an obligation.
Without producing sons, without satisfying the gods and likewise the ancestors,

children.text: akṛtvā ca kathaṃ māṇḍyaṃ svargatiṃ prāptumicchasi ||
children.translated_text: and without performing the rites, how, in your folly, do you wish to attain the path to heaven?
Child, through improper conduct there would be for you only an awakening to suffering;
after death, having left hell, there is only suffering again in another birth.
<s>Ruci</s> said:
Possession is for excessive suffering, for sin, and for a downward course;

children.text: bhavatyato mayā pūrvaṃ na kṛto dārasaṃgrahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: therefore I have not formerly undertaken the acquisition of a wife.
A means that endangers the self is undertaken after a moment's consultation;
that too does not become a cause of one's own liberation, because it involves possession.
The self that is without possession is washed clean day after day;

children.text: mama tv apaṅkadigdho 'pi vidyāmbhobhirvaraṃ hi tat ||
children.translated_text: but even if mine is smeared with mud, it is better that this be done with the waters of knowledge.
The self, marked with the mud of karma produced through many births,
should be washed by disciplined men with the waters of knowledge of reality.
The ancestors said:
It is fitting that even the self should be washed by those whose senses are restrained;
but, child, this is not the path of means on which you are proceeding.
By the five sacrifices, by austerities, and by gifts, when you drive away evil
without aiming at their fruit, your former good and bad karma is removed.

children.text: evaṃ na bandho bhavati kurvataḥ kāraṇātmakam
children.translated_text: For one who acts in this way, bondage does not arise from action that has a causal character;

children.text: na ca bandhāya tatkarma bhavaty anatisaṃnibham ||
children.translated_text: nor does that action become a cause of bondage when it is not closely attached to its fruit.

children.text: pūrvakarma kṛtaṃ bogaiḥ kṣīyate hyaniśaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Former karma is steadily exhausted by experiences,
which for human beings are made of pleasure and pain and are of the nature of merit and demerit.
Thus the self is cleansed by the wise and protected from bondage;
it is to be guarded by one's own discernment and is not burned by the mud of sin.
<s>Ruci</s> said:
Grandfathers, in the Veda ignorance is said to be ripened through the path of action;

children.text: tatkathaṃ karmaṇo mārge bhavanto yojayanti mām ||
children.translated_text: so how do you set me upon the path of action?
The ancestors said:
The statement that all this action is ignorance is false speech;

children.text: kiṃtu vidyāpariprāptau hetuḥ karma na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: rather, action is the cause for the full attainment of knowledge; there is no doubt.

children.text: vihitākaraṇānartho na sadbhiḥ kriyate tu yaḥ
children.translated_text: The misfortune arising from not performing what is prescribed is not incurred by good people;
but that other restraint which is supposed to lead to liberation instead grants a downward course.
When you think, 'I shall cleanse myself,' and regard that as best,
you too are burned by sins arising from the non-performance of what is prescribed.
Even ignorance becomes helpful to people, like poison,
when used through the method of proper observance; though fit to bind, it does not bind then.
Therefore, child, you should undertake marriage according to rule.
Otherwise your whole life from birth will be fruitless, without attaining the other-worldly good.
<s>Ruci</s> said:

children.text: vṛddho 'haṃ sāmprataṃ ko me pitaraḥ sampradāsyati
children.translated_text: I am old now, ancestors; who will give me
a wife? And for a poor man the acquisition of a wife is hard to accomplish.
The ancestors said:
Child, our fall and your own downward course

children.text: nūnaṃ bhāvi bhavitrī ca nābhinandasi no vacaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will certainly come to pass, since you do not welcome our word.
Having spoken thus, his ancestors, while he watched, O best of sages,
suddenly became invisible, like lamps struck by the wind.
The great ascetic sage <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> told <s>Krauñcuki</s>
the whole account of <s>Ruci</s>, characterized by the dialogue with the ancestors.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe karmajñānaṃ nāmāṣṭāśītitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the eighty-eighth chapter, named 'Action and Knowledge,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Asked by <s>Krauñcuki</s>, <s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> again spoke to him,
for that man was deeply agitated in mind by the words of the ancestors.
The Brahmin-seer, desiring a maiden, wandered over the earth,
but, not finding a maiden, he was inflamed by the words of the ancestors.
He fell into deep anxiety, his mind extremely distressed.

children.text: kiṃ karomi kva gacchāmi kathaṃ me dārasaṃgrahaḥ
children.translated_text: "What shall I do? Where shall I go? How can the taking of a wife
quickly come about for me, bringing prosperity to my ancestors and to myself?"
As that great-souled one was thinking thus, a thought arose in him:
"By austerity I shall propitiate this lotus-born <s>Brahmā</s>."
Then the high-minded one practiced austerity for a hundred divine years.
Remaining there for a long time in the forests, established in restraint,
he then undertook the highest discipline for the sake of worship.
Then <s>Brahmā</s>, the grandsire of the world, revealed himself
and said, "I am pleased. Let what you desire be spoken."
Then he bowed down and told <s>Brahmā</s>, the refuge of the world,
what, at the command of his ancestors, he wished to accomplish.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
"You shall become a <s>Prajāpati</s>; creatures are to be created by you.
Having created creatures, produced sons, O brahmin, and performed the rites as well,
having fulfilled your appointed office, you will then attain perfection.
Therefore do as the ancestors have told you: undertake marriage.
Keeping this desire in mind, let worship of the ancestors be performed.

children.text: ta eva tuṣṭāḥ pitaraḥ pradāsyanti tavepsitam
children.translated_text: Those very ancestors, when pleased, will grant what you desire.

children.text: patnīṃ sutāṃśca saṃtuṣṭāḥ kiṃ na dadyuḥ pitāmahāḥ ||
children.translated_text: When satisfied, what would the grandsires not give: a wife and sons?"
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
Having heard this speech of <s>Brahmā</s>, whose birth is unmanifest,
the brahmin performed <s>pitṛtarpaṇa</s> on a secluded sandbank of a river.
Then, with reverence, he praised the ancestors with these hymns,
becoming intent and concentrated, his neck bowed with devotion.
<s>Ruci</s> said:

children.text: namasye 'haṃ pitṝn bhaktyā ye vasanty adhidevatam
children.translated_text: With devotion I bow to the ancestors who dwell as presiding deities,

children.text: devairapi hi tarpyante ye śrāddheṣu svadhottaraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: who are satisfied even by the gods in <s>śrāddhas</s> with offerings rich in <s>svadhā</s>.

children.text: namasye 'haṃ pitṝn svarge ye tarpyante maharṣibhiḥ
children.translated_text: I bow to the ancestors in heaven who are satisfied by great seers
with mind-made <s>śrāddhas</s>, with devotion, by those desiring enjoyment and liberation.
I bow to the ancestors in heaven whom the siddhas satisfy
in <s>śrāddhas</s> with all divine and unsurpassed offerings.
With devotion I bow to the ancestors who are worshiped in heaven by the Guhyakas,
who maintain absorption in them and attain supreme, ultimate prosperity.

children.text: namasye 'haṃ pitṝn martyairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā
children.translated_text: I bow to the ancestors who are always worshiped by mortals on earth
in <s>śrāddhas</s> with faith, granting nourishment in the desired worlds.

children.text: namasye 'haṃ pitṝn viprairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā
children.translated_text: I bow to the ancestors who are always worshiped by brahmins on earth
for the attainment of desired and cherished aims, and who grant the Prajāpati's blessing.
I bow to those ancestors who are satisfied by forest-dwellers
with forest <s>śrāddhas</s>, by restrained eaters whose sins have been burned away by austerity.
I bow to the ancestors who, by steadfast brahmins following <s>dharma</s>,
are continually satisfied through meditations by those of controlled self.
I bow to the ancestors whom kṣatriyas satisfy with <s>śrāddhas</s>,
with all ancestral offerings according to rule, granting the fruits of both worlds.

children.text: namasye 'haṃ pitṝn vaiśyairarcyante bhuvi ye sadā
children.translated_text: I bow to the ancestors who are always worshiped on earth by vaiśyas,
ever devoted to their own duties, with flowers, incense, food, and water.
I bow to the ancestors who, in <s>śrāddha</s>, are satisfied even by śūdras with devotion,
the whole world being satisfied; they are famed by the name Sukālins.
I bow to the ancestors who, in <s>śrāddha</s>, are satisfied in Pātāla by great asuras,
eaters of nectar, always free from hypocrisy and pride.
I bow to the ancestors who are worshiped with <s>śrāddhas</s> in Rasātala,
according to rule by nāgas seeking desires, with every kind of enjoyment.
I bow to the ancestors, always satisfied by serpents with <s>śrāddhas</s>,
there itself, according to rule, endowed with mantras, enjoyments, and prosperity.

children.text: pitṝn namasye nivasanti sākṣādye devaloke 'tha mahītale vā
children.translated_text: I bow to the ancestors who dwell directly in the world of the gods or on the earth,

children.text: tathāntarikṣe ca surāripūjyāste vai pratīcchantu mayopanītam ||
children.translated_text: and also in the midspace, worshiped by the enemies of the gods; may they accept what I have offered.

children.text: pitṝn namasye paramārthabhūtā ye vai vimāne nivasantyamūrtāḥ
children.translated_text: I bow to the ancestors who are ultimate reality, who dwell bodiless in aerial cars,
whom lordly yogins worship with stainless minds as causes of release from afflictions.

children.text: pitṝn namasye divi ye ca mūrtāḥ svadhābhujaḥ kāmyaphalābhisandhau
children.translated_text: I bow to the ancestors in heaven who are embodied, eaters of <s>svadhā</s>, intent on desired fruits,
able to grant all wishes, and givers of liberation to those who have no selfish aim.

children.text: tṛpyantu te 'sminpitaraḥ samastā icchāvatāṃ ye pradiśanti kāmān
children.translated_text: May all those ancestors be satisfied in this rite, who allot desires to those who possess wishes:
godhood, the status of <s>Indra</s>, or something higher than that, elephants, horses, jewels, and great houses.

children.text: somasya ye raśmiṣu ye 'rkabimbe śukle vimāne ca sadā vasanti
children.translated_text: Those who dwell in the rays of the moon, in the orb of the sun, and always in the bright aerial car,
may those ancestors be satisfied here with food, water, perfume, and the like, and may they proceed from here to nourishment.

children.text: yeṣāṃ hute 'gnau haviṣā ca tṛptirye bhuñjate vipraśarīrasaṃsthāḥ
children.translated_text: Those whose satisfaction comes from oblations offered into fire, and those who eat while abiding in the bodies of brahmins,

children.text: ye piṇḍadānena mudaṃ prayānti tṛpyantu te 'sminpitaro 'nnatoyaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: those who rejoice through the giving of <s>piṇḍas</s>: may those ancestors be satisfied here with food and water.
Those who are pleased by rhinoceros meat, by desired liquors, by black sesame seeds, divine and delightful,

children.text: kālena śākena maharṣivaryaiḥ saṃprīṇitāste mudamatra yāntu ||
children.translated_text: and in due season by greens, those foremost great seers: may they come to joy here.

children.text: kavyānyaśeṣāṇi ca yānyabhīṣṭānyatīva teṣāṃ mama pūjitānām
children.translated_text: Whatever ancestral offerings are desired by those whom I have worshiped with deep devotion,

children.text: teṣāṃ ca sānnidhyamihāstu puṣpagandhāmbubhojyeṣu mayā kṛteṣu ||
children.translated_text: may their presence be here among the flowers, scents, water, and foods prepared by me.

children.text: dine dine ye pratigṛhṇate 'rcāṃ māsāntapūjyā bhuvi ye 'ṣṭakāsu
children.translated_text: May those ancestors of mine who receive worship day by day, and those who are worshiped at the end of the month on the <s>aṣṭakās</s>,

children.text: ye vatsarānte 'bhyudaye ca pūjyāḥ prayāntu te me pitaro 'tra tuṣṭim ||
children.translated_text: and those who are worshiped at the end of the year and at an auspicious occasion, come here to satisfaction.

children.text: pūjyā dvijānāṃ kumudendubhāso ye kṣattriyāṇāṃ jvalanārkavarṇāḥ
children.translated_text: Those worshipful ones who, for the twice-born, have the brightness of the water-lily and the moon, those who for kṣatriyas have the color of fire and the sun,

children.text: tathā viśāṃ ye kanakāvadātā nīlīprabhāḥ śūdrajanasya ye ca ||
children.translated_text: likewise those for vaiśyas who are bright like gold, and those for the śūdra people who have a dark-blue radiance,
may all of them, in this rite, through my presentation of flowers, perfume, incense, water, food, and the like,

children.text: tathāgnihomena ca yānti tṛptiṃ sadā pitṛbhyaḥ praṇato 'smi tebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and likewise through the fire oblation, attain satisfaction. I am ever bowed down to those <s>pitṛs</s>.
Those who, for the sake of complete satisfaction, partake of the well-brought ancestral offerings after the gods,

children.text: tṛptāśca ye bhūtisṛjo bhavanti tṛpyantu te 'sminpraṇato 'smi tebhyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and those who, being satisfied, become creators of prosperity, may they be satisfied in this rite. I am bowed down to them.
May they destroy rākṣasas, bhūtas, and fierce asuras, and also whatever is inauspicious for creatures.
May those primordial ones among the gods, worshiped by the lord of the immortals, be satisfied in this rite. I am bowed down to them.
The <s>Agniṣvāttas</s>, <s>Barhiṣads</s>, <s>Ājyapās</s>, and likewise the <s>Somapās</s>,
may these <s>pitṛs</s>, satisfied by me, come to satisfaction in this <s>śrāddha</s>.

children.text: agniṣvāttāḥ pitṛgaṇāḥ prācīṃ rakṣantu me diśam
children.translated_text: May the <s>Agniṣvātta</s> hosts of <s>pitṛs</s> guard my eastern direction.

children.text: tathā barhiṣadaḥ pāntu yāmyāṃ me pitaraḥ sadā
children.translated_text: Likewise may the <s>Barhiṣad</s> ancestors always protect my southern direction.
In the same way may the <s>Ājyapās</s> protect the west, and the <s>Somapās</s> the north.
From rākṣasas, bhūtas, and piśācas, and likewise from the fault of asuras,

children.text: sarvataḥ pitaro rakṣāṃ kurvantu mama nityaśaḥ ||
children.translated_text: may the ancestors always make protection for me on every side.
<s>Viśva</s>, <s>Viśvabhuj</s>, <s>Ārādhya</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Dhanya</s>, and <s>Śubhānana</s>,

children.text: bhūtido bhūtikṛd bhūtiḥ pitṝṇāṃ ye gaṇā nava ||
children.translated_text: <s>Bhūtida</s>, <s>Bhūtikṛt</s>, and <s>Bhūti</s>: these are the nine hosts of the <s>pitṛs</s>.
<s>Kalyāṇa</s>, <s>Kalyada</s>, <s>Kartṛ</s>, <s>Kalya</s>, and <s>Kalyatarāśraya</s>,
<s>Kalyatāhetu</s> and <s>Anagha</s>: these six hosts are remembered.
<s>Vara</s>, <s>Vareṇya</s>, <s>Varada</s>, <s>Tuṣṭida</s>, and likewise <s>Puṣṭida</s>,

children.text: viśvapātā tathā dhātā saptaite ca gaṇāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: as well as <s>Viśvapātṛ</s> and <s>Dhātṛ</s>: these seven hosts too are remembered.
<s>Mahān</s>, <s>Mahātmā</s>, <s>Mahita</s>, <s>Mahimāvān</s>, and <s>Mahābala</s>,
these five hosts of the <s>pitṛs</s> too are destroyers of sin.
Another is <s>Sukhada</s>, another <s>Dhanada</s>, another <s>Dharmada</s>, and another <s>Bhūtida</s>.
Thus a fourfold host of the <s>pitṛs</s> is also taught.
The thirty-one hosts of the <s>pitṛs</s>, by whom the whole world is pervaded,
may those very hosts of <s>pitṛs</s> here be pleased by what I have offered.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
As he was praising in this way, a lofty mass of radiance
suddenly appeared, spreading through the sky.
Seeing that very great radiance standing there and covering the world,

children.text: jānubhyāmavanīṃ gatvā ruciḥ stotram idaṃ jagau ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ruci</s>, having gone down to the earth on his knees, sang this hymn.
<s>Ruci</s> said:
I always bow to those worshiped, incorporeal <s>pitṛs</s> of blazing brilliance,
to those meditative ones with divine sight.
They are the leaders of <s>Indra</s> and the others, and also of <s>Dakṣa</s> and <s>Marīci</s>,
and likewise of the Seven Sages and the others; I bow to those granters of desires.
They are the leaders of the Manus and the others, and likewise of the sun and moon.
I bow to all those <s>pitṛs</s>, even those in the ocean.
Of the lunar mansions, the planets, wind, fire, and the sky,
and likewise of heaven and earth, I bow with joined hands.
To <s>Prajāpati</s>, to <s>Kaśyapa</s>, to <s>Soma</s>, and to <s>Varuṇa</s>,
and always to the lords of yoga, I bow with joined hands.
Homage to the seven hosts, and likewise to those in the seven worlds.
I bow to <s>Svāyaṃbhuva</s>, to <s>Brahmā</s>, whose sight is yoga.
I bow to the <s>Soma</s>-sustained hosts of <s>pitṛs</s>, and likewise to those who bear the form of yoga.
Likewise I bow to <s>Soma</s>, the father of the worlds.
I also bow to other <s>pitṛs</s> whose form is fire,
for this whole universe, without remainder, is made of fire and <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: ye ca tejasi ye caite somasūryāgnimūrtayaḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are in radiance, and those whose forms are <s>Soma</s>, the sun, and fire,
and who have the form of the world and likewise the form of <s>Brahman</s>,
to all those yogin <s>pitṛs</s>, with a controlled mind,
homage, homage; may there be homage to you. May the eaters of <s>svadhā</s> be gracious.
<s>Mārkaṇḍeya</s> said:
When they had thus been praised by him, O best of sages, from that radiance
those <s>pitṛs</s> came forth, illuminating the ten directions.
And the offering that had been made by him, of flowers, perfume, and anointing paste,
adorned them; then he saw them standing before him.
<s>Ruci</s>, bowing down with devotion, again with joined hands,
said to each one respectfully, "Homage to you, homage to you."
Then the pleased <s>pitṛs</s> said to that best of sages,
"Choose a boon." He, with his neck bent down, spoke to them.
<s>Ruci</s> said:
The role of creating creatures has been assigned to me by <s>Brahmā</s>.
Therefore I desire a blessed, divine wife, endowed with offspring.
The <s>pitṛs</s> said:
Here itself, at once, may an exceedingly lovely wife become yours.

children.text: tasyāṃ ca putro bhavitā bhavato munisattama ||
children.translated_text: And from her a son will be born to you, O best of sages.
Wise and lord of a <s>manvantara</s>, marked by your own name,

children.text: ruce raucya iti khyātiṃ prayāsyati jagattraye ||
children.translated_text: he will gain fame in the three worlds as <s>Raucya</s>, son of <s>Ruci</s>.
Many sons of his too, great-souled and of great strength and valor,
will become protectors of the earth.

children.text: tvaṃ ca prajāpatir bhūtvā prajāḥ sṛṣṭvā caturvidhāḥ
children.translated_text: And you, having become a <s>Prajāpati</s> and created the four kinds of creatures,
when your authority has come to an end, knowing <s>dharma</s>, will then obtain perfection.

children.text: stotreṇānena ca naro yo 'smān stoṣyati bhaktitaḥ
children.translated_text: And the man who, with devotion, will praise us with this hymn
Pleased with him, we grant enjoyments, offspring, and supreme meditation.
Therefore those who desire longevity, health, wealth, and sons, grandsons, and the like

children.text: vāñchadbhiḥ satataṃ stavyāḥ stotreṇānena vai yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: should constantly praise us with this hymn.

children.text: śrāddheṣu ya imaṃ bhaktyā tvasmatprītikaraṃ stavam
children.translated_text: Whoever, at <s>śrāddha</s> rites, with devotion, standing before the foremost twice-born while they are eating,
will recite this praise that brings delight to us,
then, through our joy at hearing the hymn, when supreme presence has been established,
that <s>śrāddha</s> will become inexhaustible through us, without doubt.
Even if the <s>śrāddha</s> is performed for one unlearned in the Veda, even if it is impaired,
or if it has been performed otherwise, with wealth obtained unjustly,
or with offerings made by persons unfit for <s>śrāddha</s>, or with damaged gifts,
or even at the wrong time or place, or lacking the proper rule,
or if it has been performed by men without faith, relying on hypocrisy,
nevertheless, by the utterance of this for our satisfaction,
wherever this happiness-bringing hymn to us is recited at a <s>śrāddha</s>,
there satisfaction lasting twelve years arises for us.
In winter it bestows satisfaction for twelve years;
in the cold season this auspicious hymn gives satisfaction for twice as many years.
In spring, during the <s>śrāddha</s> rite, it gives satisfaction for sixteen years,
and in summer also, when recited, it produces satisfaction for sixteen years.
Even when a <s>śrāddha</s> has been performed at an improper time, if it is completed by this hymn,
in the rainy season inexhaustible satisfaction arises for us, O <s>Ruci</s>.
Recited also in autumn, at the time of <s>śrāddha</s>,
this grants us, through those men, satisfaction lasting fifteen years.
And in whatever house this text remains written down at all times,
there, when a <s>śrāddha</s> is performed, our presence will occur.
Therefore, O greatly fortunate one, this should be made heard by you at a <s>śrāddha</s>,
before the brahmins while they are eating, for it nourishes us.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe rucikṛtapitṛstotraṃ nāmaikonanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the eighty-ninth chapter, named 'The Hymn to the Ancestors Composed by <s>Ruci</s>,' is complete.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
The sages beginning with <s>Svāyambhuva</s> meditate on <s>Hari</s> through ritual action,
devoted to vows, conduct, worship, meditation, praise, and muttered prayer.
He is devoid of body, senses, mind, intellect, breath, and ego,
devoid of space and also devoid of fire.
He is devoid of water and devoid of its qualities,
devoid also of earth and devoid of all beings.
He is the overseer of beings, the controller of what is bound, the lord, the all-pervading one,
whose form is the state of consciousness, the overseer of all, stainless.
Free from attachment, the great lord, worshipped by all the gods,
he is of the nature of light, not constituted by sattva, and devoid of austerity.
Ever devoid of rajas and distinct from the three guṇas,
he is devoid of every form and devoid of agency and the like.
Without latent impressions, pure, free from all faults,
free from thirst, and free from the various kinds of grief and delusion,
without old age or death, immutable, free from delusion,
without origination and also free from dissolution.
He is truth, free from all conventional conduct, partless, the supreme lord,
free from waking, dream, deep sleep, and the rest, and free from name.
He is the witness of waking and the other states, peaceful in nature, lord of the gods,
eternally present in waking and the rest, free from effect and cause.

children.text: sarvadṛṣṭaṃ tathā mūrtaṃ sūkṣmaṃ sūkṣmataraṃ param
children.translated_text: Seen by all, yet embodied, subtle, subtler still, supreme,
the awareness of knowledge, sight, and hearing, whose nature is supreme bliss.
Just as he is free from <s>Viśva</s>, so too he is devoid of <s>Taijasa</s>,
and he is also free from <s>Prājña</s>; he is the fourth state, the supreme imperishable.
Protector of all, destroyer of all, and of the nature of the self of all beings,
devoid of the qualities of intellect, foundationless, auspicious <s>Hari</s>.
He is free from modification and knowable by the <s>Vedānta</s>s,
the form of the Veda, the supreme being, beyond the senses, auspicious.

children.text: śabdena varjitaṃ caiva rasena ca vivarjitam
children.translated_text: He is devoid of sound and also devoid of taste,
a god without touch and devoid of mere visible form.
He is devoid of form and likewise devoid of smell;
beginningless <s>Brahman</s>, extending to the cranial aperture: 'I am <s>Brahman</s> alone.'
Having known this, the self-controlled man should perform meditation on the great god.

children.text: dhyānaṃ yaḥ kurute hyevaṃ sa bhaved bahma mānavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whoever meditates in this way, that human being becomes <s>Brahman</s>.

children.text: iti dhyānaṃ samākhyātam aśvirasya mayā tava
children.translated_text: Thus have I fully declared the meditation to you, O lord whose banner bears the bull.
Now I shall tell something else; say what that is, O bull-bannered one.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe haridhyānaṃ nāmaikanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the ninety-first chapter, named 'Meditation on <s>Hari</s>,' is complete.
<s>Rudra</s> said:
Tell again the meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, O bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
by merely knowing which a man becomes one who has fulfilled his purpose.
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall declare the meditation on <s>Hari</s>, which crushes the net of māyā;
that meditation is twofold, O <s>Hara</s>, by the distinction between formed and formless and the like.

children.text: amūrtaṃ rudra kathitaṃ hanta mūrtaṃ bravīmyaham
children.translated_text: The formless has been described, O <s>Rudra</s>; now, come, I shall speak of the formed.
Brilliant like ten million suns, victorious and shining on one side,
<s>Hari</s>, white like jasmine and cow's milk, is to be meditated upon by those who seek liberation,
endowed with a broad and very beautiful conch,
and with a fierce garland of flames equal to a thousand suns.
Endowed with the discus too, peaceful, holding a mace in his hand, with an auspicious face;
with a very precious crown blazing with jewels,
the god, armed, all-pervading, and likewise holding a lotus;
wearing a forest garland, bright, full-bodied, adorned with gold,
well clothed, pure in body, beautiful-eared, seated on a lotus;
golden-bodied, wearing a lovely necklace, with auspicious armlets,
furnished with bracelets and adorned with a forest garland;
marked with the Śrīvatsa and the Kaustubha, possessing eyes revered by <s>Lakṣmī</s>,
endowed with qualities beginning with minuteness, the maker of creation and dissolution;
to be meditated on by sages, to be meditated on by asuras, to be meditated on by gods, exceedingly beautiful,
abiding in the hearts of all beings, from <s>Brahmā</s> down to a fixed pillar;
eternal, imperishable, pure, the lord who grants favor to all,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, the great god, with flashing makara-earrings;
the destroyer of distress, worthy of worship, auspicious, the destroyer of the wicked,
the self of all, of every form, all-pervading, destroyer of hostile planetary influence;
furnished with lovely rings and with very bright nails,
a refuge, a maker of happiness, gentle in form, the great lord;
adorned with every ornament and anointed with fine sandal paste,
united with all the gods and bringing pleasure to all the gods;
desiring the welfare of all worlds, lord of all, source of all beings,
standing in the solar disk, standing in fire, abiding in water;
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, bearer of the world, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, to be meditated on by those who desire liberation;
The self is to be meditated on as, 'I am <s>Vāsudeva</s>,' as <s>Hari</s>, <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: dhyāyantyevaṃ ca ye viṣṇuṃ te yānti paramāṃ gatim
children.translated_text: Those who thus meditate on <s>Viṣṇu</s> go to the supreme goal.

children.text: yājñavalkyaḥ purā hyevaṃ dhyātvā viṣṇuṃ sureśvaram ||
children.translated_text: In ancient times <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, having meditated in just this way on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the gods,
attained the office of teacher of dharma and went to the supreme state.
Therefore you too, O lord of gods, O <s>Śaṅkara</s>, should contemplate <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
Whoever recites the meditation on <s>Viṣṇu</s> attains the supreme goal.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe viṣṇudhyānaṃ nāma dvinavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the ninety-second chapter, named 'Meditation on Viṣṇu,' is completed.
<s>Maheśvara</s> said:

children.text: yājñavalkyena yatpūrvaṃ dharmaṃ proktaṃ kayaṃ hare
children.translated_text: Tell me, O <s>Hari</s>, the dharma that was formerly declared by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,
tell that to me according to truth, O slayer of <s>Keśin</s>, O <s>Mādhava</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
After bowing to <s>Yājñavalkya</s>, who was staying in <s>Mithilā</s>,
the sages went and asked him in full about varṇa-dharma and the rest.

children.text: tebhyaḥ sa kathayāmāsa viṣṇuṃ dhyātvā jitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having meditated on <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he, with senses conquered, explained it to them.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
Learn the dharmas in that country where the black antelope lives,
mixed with Purāṇa, logic, Mīmāṃsā, Dharmaśāstra, and the ancillary sciences.

children.text: vedāḥ sthānāni vidyānāṃ dharmasya ca caturdaśa
children.translated_text: The Vedas, the Purāṇas, Nyāya, Mīmāṃsā, Dharmaśāstra, and the Vedāṅgas are the fourteen seats of knowledge and of dharma.
The expounders of the Dharmaśāstras are <s>Manu</s>, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Yama</s>, <s>Aṅgiras</s>,
<s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Dakṣa</s>, <s>Saṃvarta</s>, <s>Śātātapa</s>, <s>Parāśara</s>,
<s>Āpastamba</s>, <s>Uśanas</s>, <s>Vyāsa</s>, <s>Kātyāyana</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
<s>Gautama</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Likhita</s>, <s>Hārīta</s>, <s>Atri</s>, and I as well.
These, having worshiped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, became teachers of dharma.
Whatever substance is given to a worthy recipient, with faith, by a proper means according to place and time,
all that is the mark of dharma.
Sacrifice, good conduct, restraint, nonviolence, giving, and the practice of self-study,
and this is the highest dharma: vision of the self through yoga.
Four knowers of Vedic dharma, or an assembly of three learned in the three Vedas,
or even one best knower of the self, declares what one's own dharma is.
The varṇas are Brahmin, Kṣatriya, Vaiśya, and Śūdra; the first three among them are twice-born.

children.text: niṣekādyāḥ śmaśānāntās teṣāṃ vai mantrataḥ kriyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For them, the rites from impregnation up to the cremation ground are to be performed with mantras.
For a male, garbhādhāna is at the season; puṃsavana is before fetal movement,

children.text: ṣaṣṭhe 'ṣṭame vā sīmantaḥ prasave jātakarma ca ||
children.translated_text: sīmanta is in the sixth or eighth month, and jātakarman at birth.
Naming is on the eleventh day, going out in the fourth month,
and annaprāśana in the sixth month; the cūḍā rite should be performed according to family custom.
In this way the fault arisen from seed and womb comes to appeasement.

children.text: tūṣṇīm etāḥ kriyāḥ strīṇāṃ vivāhaśca samantrakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For women these rites are silent, while marriage is accompanied by mantras.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktavarṇadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma trinavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the ninety-third chapter, named 'The Explanation of Varṇa-Dharma Spoken by Yājñavalkya,' is completed.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
The upanayana of a Brahmin should be in the eighth year from conception, or in the eighth year after birth;
for kings in the eleventh year, and for Vaiśyas, according to some, in accordance with family custom.
Having initiated the pupil, preceded by the great vyāhṛtis, the teacher should
teach him the Veda and instruct him in purity and proper conduct.
By day, and at the twilights, with the sacred thread held at the ear and facing north,
he should pass urine and feces; but at night he should face south.
Having risen while holding his penis, with clods of earth taken up and with waters,
the observer of the great vow should perform purification that removes smell and smearing.
Sitting in a clean place, with his knees within, facing north,
or east, a twice-born man should always sip water with the Brahma-tīrtha.
The bases of the little finger, forefinger, and thumb, and the tip of the hand
are respectively the tīrthas of <s>Prajāpati</s>, the ancestors, <s>Brahmā</s>, and the gods.
He should sip water three times, wipe twice, and touch the bodily apertures with waters,
but with waters that are in their natural state, not with those having froth or bubbles.
For the twice-born classes, they should reach the heart, throat, and palate respectively.
A woman and also a <s>śūdra</s>, when touched even once by these, would finally become purified.
Bathing with mantras whose deity is water, sprinkling, restraint of the breath,
attendance upon the sun as well, and repeated recitation of the <s>Gāyatrī</s> with its confirmation are prescribed.
He should recite the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, together with its head, preceded by the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>,
joined with the sacred syllable before each part; this, done three times, is restraint of the breath.
Having restrained the breaths and sprinkled himself with the three verses whose deity is water,
he should sit reciting the <s>Sāvitrī</s> until the stars rise in the west.

children.text: sandhyāṃ prāk prātarevaṃ hi tiṣṭhed ā sūryadarśanāt
children.translated_text: At morning twilight he should stand in this way, facing east, until the sight of the sun.
After that he should perform the fire rite at both twilights.
Then he should greet the elders, saying, 'I am so-and-so.',
and he should attend upon the teacher, composed, for the sake of <s>svādhyāya</s> (Vedic study).
When summoned, he should study, and he should report everything to him.
He should always do what is beneficial for him by deeds of mind, speech, and body.
He should carry the staff, the antelope skin, the sacred thread, and the girdle,
and should go for alms among blameless brahmins for the support of himself.
At the beginning, middle, or end, it should be marked by the proper begging formula,
for the alms-rounds of brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas respectively.
Having performed the fire rite, he should eat, disciplined, with the teacher's permission,
preceded by the rite of sipping water, honoring the food and not reviling it.
A brahmacarin who stands firm in his vow should not eat food from one source, except in distress.
A brahmin may, if he wishes, eat at a <s>śrāddha</s>, provided he does not injure his vow.
He should avoid honey, meat, and also cooked delicacies and the like.

children.text: sa gururyaḥ kriyāḥ kṛtvā vedamasmai prayacchati ||
children.translated_text: He is the guru who, after performing the rites, imparts the Veda to him.
The one who, after initiating him, gives him this is proclaimed to be the <s>ācārya</s>.
One who teaches a single portion is an <s>upādhyāya</s>; an <s>ṛtvij</s> is said to be one who performs the sacrifice.
These are to be honored in the order just given, but the mother is weightier than all of them.
For each Veda, <s>brahmacarya</s> lasts twelve years, or five,
or, according to some, until the learning is completed; the keśānta rite is in the sixteenth year.
Up to the sixteenth, the twenty-second, and the twenty-fourth year,
is the latest time for <s>upanayana</s> for a brahmin, kṣatriya, and vaiśya respectively.
After that these men fall, being deprived of all <s>dharma</s>.
Fallen from the <s>Sāvitrī</s>, they are <s>vrātyas</s>, unless they undergo the <s>vrātyastoma</s> rite.
The first birth is when they are born from the mother; the second is the tying of the muñja girdle.
Therefore brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas are the twice-born classes.

children.text: yajñānāṃ tapasāṃ caiva śubhānāṃ caiva karmaṇām ||
children.translated_text: For sacrifices, austerities, and auspicious rites,
the Veda alone is the supreme bringer of final good for the twice-born.
With honey and milk the twice-born man satisfies the gods,
and with honey and ghee the ancestors, when he studies the ṛks every day.
Likewise the twice-born man should recite the <s>Yajus</s>, the <s>Sāman</s>, and the <s>Atharvāṅgirasa</s>.
He thereby satisfies the ancestors and the gods every day with ghee and nectar.
Dialogues, purāṇas, hymns of praise, and narrative songs,
and also histories and branches of knowledge: whoever studies these every day according to his ability
satisfies the ancestors and the gods with meat, milk, boiled rice, and the like.
When they are satisfied, they satisfy him with the auspicious fruits of every desire.

children.text: yaṃ yaṃ kratum adhīte 'sau tasyasyāpnuyāt phalam ||
children.translated_text: Whatever rite he studies, he obtains the fruit of that very rite.
The twice-born man shares in the fruit of gift of land, austerity, and <s>svādhyāya</s>.
A lifelong brahmacarin should dwell in the presence of the <s>ācārya</s>.
In his absence, he should dwell with his son, with his wife, or even with the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> fire.
By this rule, with his senses conquered, he should discipline the body.
He obtains <s>Brahmaloka</s> and is not born again here.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktavarṇadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturnavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s> called the first part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the ninety-fourth chapter named 'Explanation of the duties of the varṇas as spoken by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>'.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
Listen, sages restrained in your vows, to the <s>dharmas</s> of the householder.

children.text: gurave ca dhanaṃ dattvā snātvā ca tadanujñayā ||
children.translated_text: Having given wealth to the teacher, and having bathed with his permission,
one who has completed <s>brahmacarya</s> should marry a woman possessing auspicious marks,
not previously taken by another, lovely, not a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> relative, and younger than himself,
free from disease, having brothers, and not born from the same seer-lineage or gotra.
She should be beyond the fifth degree on the mother's side and likewise beyond the seventh on the father's side.
She should come from a great family of learned Vedic brahmins renowned for ten generations.

children.text: savarṇaḥ śrotriyo vidvānvaro doṣānvito na ca ||
children.translated_text: The bridegroom should be of the same varṇa, a <s>śrotriya</s>, learned, and not marked by faults.
As for what is said among the twice-born about taking a wife from a <s>śūdra</s>,

children.text: na tanmama mataṃ yasmāttatrāyaṃ jāyate svayam ||
children.translated_text: that is not my opinion, because in that case he himself is born there.
In the order of the varṇas, there are three, then two, then one, respectively,
as wives for brahmins, kṣatriyas, and vaiśyas; for one born a <s>śūdra</s>, there is his own woman.
The <s>Brāhma</s> marriage is when she is summoned and given, adorned according to one's means.
The son born from that marriage purifies twenty-one men on both sides.
The <s>Daiva</s> marriage is when she is given to the officiating priest standing at a sacrifice; the <s>Ārṣa</s> is by accepting a pair of cows.
The first-born son purifies fourteen, and a later-born son purifies six.

children.text: ityuktvā caratāṃ dharmaṃ saha yā dīyate 'rthine
children.translated_text: When she is given to a suitor with the words, 'Practice <s>dharma</s> together,'
that is the <s>Kāya</s> marriage; the son born from it purifies six in the lineage, together with himself.
The <s>Āsura</s> marriage is from taking wealth; the <s>Gāndharva</s> is by mutual agreement,
the <s>Rākṣasa</s> by seizure in battle, and the <s>Paiśāca</s> through deceit of a maiden.
For a brahmin the first four are approved; likewise the <s>Gāndharva</s> and <s>Rākṣasa</s>
for a king; the <s>Āsura</s> for a vaiśya; and for a śūdra the last is censured.
The hand should be grasped in the case of women of the same varṇa; for a kṣatriya woman, he should take an arrow.
A <s>vaiśya</s> woman should take up the goad; and in causing pain to one of higher birth,

children.text: pitā pitāmaho bhrātā sakulyo jananī tathā
children.translated_text: the father, the grandfather, the brother, a member of the same family, and likewise the mother,
the giver of the maiden, when the earlier one is absent, each succeeding one while in proper condition.
If he does not give her, he incurs the guilt of embryo-killing at every menstrual season.
In the absence of these givers, the maiden should make her own choice of husband.
A maiden is given only once; one who carries her off is liable to the punishment of a thief.

children.text: aduṣṭāṃ hi tyajandaṇḍyaḥ suduṣṭāṃ tu parityajet ||
children.translated_text: A man is punishable if he abandons a blameless wife, but he may abandon one who is thoroughly corrupted.
When there is no son, the brother-in-law, known to be suitable, may go to a woman desiring a son.

children.text: sapiṇḍo vā sagotro vā ghṛtābhyakta ṛtāviyāt ||
children.translated_text: Or a <s>sapiṇḍa</s> or a man of the same lineage, anointed with ghee, should approach her in her season.
He should go to her until conception occurs; otherwise he becomes fallen.
A son born by this rule becomes the son of the owner of the field.
A woman deprived of authority, stained, living only on a lump of food,
despised and sleeping on a low bed, should be made to dwell apart if she is adulterous.

children.text: somaḥ śaucaṃ dadau tāsāṃ gandharvaśca śubhāṃ giram
children.translated_text: <s>Soma</s> gave women purity, and the <s>Gandharva</s> gave them auspicious speech;

children.text: pāvakaḥ sarvamedhyatvaṃ medhyā vai yoṣito yataḥ ||
children.translated_text: fire gave them complete purity, for women are indeed pure.

children.text: vyabhicārādṛtau śuddhir garbhe tyāgaṃ karoti ca
children.translated_text: After adultery there is purity at the menstrual season; but if there is pregnancy, abandonment is prescribed.
For them, abandonment is also prescribed in the case of killing the fetus or the husband, and likewise in a great sin.
Even if she drinks liquor, is diseased, hostile, barren, destructive of wealth, or unpleasant in speech,

children.text: adhivinnā ca bhartavyā mahad eno 'nyathā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: or superseded by another wife, she is to be maintained; otherwise there would be great sin.
Where there is no opposition between husband and wife, there the three aims of life increase.

children.text: mṛte jīvati yā patyau yā nānyamupagacchati ||
children.translated_text: When her husband is dead or living, a woman who does not approach another man,
obtains fame here and rejoices with <s>Umā</s>.

children.text: śuddhāṃ tyajaṃstṛtīyāṃśaṃ dadyād ā maraṇaṃ striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: If a man abandons a pure wife, he should give a third share for the woman until death.
Women should do the word of the husband; this is the supreme <s>dharma</s> of women.
There are sixteen nights of the menstrual season for women; on the even-numbered ones he should sleep with her.

children.text: brahmacārī ca parvāṇy ādyāśtatastras tu varjayet
children.translated_text: He should remain celibate on the festival days and avoid the first four nights.

children.text: evaṃ gacchan striyaṃ kṣāmāṃ maghāṃ mūlāṃ ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: Thus, when approaching a woman, he should avoid one who is emaciated, and the lunar mansions <s>Maghā</s> and <s>Mūlā</s>.
He thereby begets a son marked with good signs and free from disease,

children.text: yathā kāmī bhavedvāpi strīṇāṃ balam anusmaran ||
children.translated_text: or as he may desire, remembering the power of women.
He should be devoted to his own wife alone, and women are to be protected in every way.
By the husband, brother, father, kinsman, mother-in-law, father-in-law, and brother-in-law,
and by relatives, women are to be honored with ornaments, clothing, and food.
Restrained in her possessions, capable, cheerful, and turned away from expenditure,
she should always pay homage at the feet of her mother-in-law and father-in-law.
Games, bodily adornment, the sight of assemblies and festivals,
laughter, and going to another's house should be avoided by a woman whose husband is away.

children.text: rakṣetkanyāṃ pitā bālye yauvane patireva tām ||
children.translated_text: The father should protect a maiden in childhood; in youth her husband alone protects her.
In old age the son protects her; otherwise her kinsmen do so.

children.text: patiṃ vinā na tiṣṭhettu divā vā yadi vā niśi ||
children.translated_text: She should not remain without her husband, whether by day or by night.
In a religious rite he should appoint the elder wife, never the younger one.
A husband should cremate a wife who has lived virtuously with the <s>agnihotra</s> fire.
He should take another wife according to rule, and also the fire, without delay.
A woman devoted to her husband goes to heaven, after obtaining fame here.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktagṛhalthadharmanirṇayo nāma pañcanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the ninety-fifth chapter, named 'The Determination of the Householder's Dharma Taught by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is complete.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
I shall declare the supreme rule concerning mixed castes and the duties of householders and the like.

children.text: viprān mūrdhāvaṣikto hi kṣatriyāyāṃ viśaḥ striyām ||
children.translated_text: A <s>mūrdhāvasikta</s> is born from a <s>brāhmaṇa</s> in a <s>kṣatriyā</s> woman; in a <s>vaiśya</s> woman,
an <s>ambaṣṭha</s> is born, and in a <s>śūdrā</s> woman a <s>niṣāda</s>, also called <s>parvata</s>.
A <s>māhiṣya</s> is born from a <s>kṣatriya</s> in a <s>vaiśya</s> woman; in a <s>śūdrā</s> woman one is called <s>mleccha</s>.
From a <s>vaiśya</s> in a <s>śūdrā</s> woman comes a <s>karaṇa</s>; this is remembered as the rule in women of lower class.
From a <s>kṣatriya</s> in a <s>brāhmaṇī</s> woman comes a <s>sūta</s>; from a <s>vaiśya</s>, likewise, a <s>vaidehaka</s>.
One born from a <s>śūdra</s> is a <s>cāṇḍāla</s>, despised by all the classes.
A <s>kṣatriyā</s> woman gives birth to a <s>māgadha</s> from a <s>vaiśya</s>, and to a <s>kṣattṛ</s> from a <s>śūdra</s>.
A <s>vaiśya</s> woman from a <s>śūdra</s> generated a son called <s>ayogava</s>.
From a <s>māhiṣya</s> in a <s>karaṇī</s> woman a <s>rathakāra</s> is born.
Those born in direct and reverse order should be known as base or good, according to their origin.
Through elevation of caste, one is to be known as twice-born in the seventh or even in the fifth generation.
When occupations are interchanged, equality of action is as before, higher or lower according to what precedes and follows.

children.text: karma smārtaṃ vivāhāgnau kurvīta pratyahaṃ gṛhī ||
children.translated_text: A householder should perform the smārta rite every day in the marriage fire.
Except at the time of gift, he should perform the śrauta rite in the consecrated fires.
Having completed care of the body and performed the prescribed purification, a twice-born man
should attend upon the morning <s>sandhyā</s>, after first cleaning his teeth.
Having offered oblations in the fire to all the gods, he should mutter mantras with concentration.
He should learn the meanings of the Vedas and the various śāstras.
For the accomplishment of welfare and security and the like, the householder should approach the Lord.
Having bathed, he should satisfy and worship the gods and the ancestors.
Then, according to his ability, he should recite the Vedas, the Purāṇas, together with the Itihāsas.
For the accomplishment of the sacrifice of muttered prayer, he should recite the knowledge concerning the self.
The offering of bali, the ancestral offering, the fire oblation, Vedic study, and honoring guests
are the great sacrifices to beings, ancestors, immortals, <s>Brahman</s>, and humans.
What is offered to the gods should be cast into the fire; he should take and set out the bali for beings.
He should place food on the ground for dogs, <s>cāṇḍālas</s>, and crows.
Food and also water should be given every day to the ancestors and to humans.
He should perform Vedic study every day and should not cook food for himself alone.
Children, women living in the household, the aged, pregnant women, the sick, and maidens,
as well as guests and servants, should be fed; the husband and wife should eat what remains.
By the rule of the <s>prāṇāgnihotra</s> he should eat the food without disparaging it.

children.text: mitaṃ vipākaṃ ca hitaṃ bhakṣyaṃ bālādipūrvakam
children.translated_text: The food should be moderate, well digested, beneficial, and fit to eat, after first feeding children and the others.
One eats after sipping water both before and after the meal.
A twice-born man should make the food fireless and nectar-like.
Food should be given to guests of the several classes, according to one's capacity and in proper order.
A guest should not be driven away, even in the evening; there is no deliberation about this.

children.text: satkṛtya bhikṣave bhikṣā dātavyā suvratāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Alms should be given respectfully to a mendicant and to one of good vows.
He should feed all who have arrived, and should give a great bull to a learned <s>śrotriya</s>.
Once each year graduates, teachers, and kings are to be honored.

children.text: priyo vivāhyaśca tathā yajñaṃ pratyṛtvijaḥ punaḥ
children.translated_text: So too a beloved person, one connected with marriage, and again the officiating priests at a sacrifice.
A traveler is called a guest; a <s>śrotriya</s> is one who has mastered the Veda.
These two are to be honored by a householder who desires the world of <s>Brahman</s>.
He should not be fond of another's cooking, except when there is a blameless invitation.
He should avoid restlessness of speech, hands, and feet, and also overeating.

children.text: śrotriyaṃ vātithiṃ tṛptam ā sīmāntād anuvrajet ||
children.translated_text: He should accompany a satisfied <s>śrotriya</s> or guest as far as the boundary.
For the rest of the day he should sit together with cultivated, beloved kinsmen.

children.text: upāsya paścimāṃ sandhyāṃ hutvāgnau bhojanaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: After attending upon the evening twilight and making an oblation in the fire, he should then eat.
He should do this together with his servants, and should reflect on his own welfare.

children.text: brāhme muhūrte cotthāya mānyo vipro dhanādibhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rising in the <s>brāhma</s> hour, he should honor a Brahmin with wealth and other gifts.
The road is to be yielded to the aged, the afflicted, and those carrying burdens.
Sacrifice, study, and giving are duties of the Vaiśya and also of the Kṣatriya.
For a Brahmin, accepting gifts is additional, as are officiating at sacrifices and teaching.
The chief duty of a Kṣatriya is the protection of the subjects.
Lending at interest, agriculture, trade, and tending cattle are remembered as the duties of the Vaiśya.
The Śūdra's duty is service to the twice-born; a twice-born man should not neglect sacrifices.
Nonviolence, truth, non-stealing, purity, restraint of the senses,
self-control, patience, straightforwardness, and giving are means of <s>dharma</s> for all.
One should practice a livelihood appropriate to oneself, one that is not crooked and not deceitful.
One who has more than three years' food is fit to drink <s>Soma</s>.

children.text: syādannaṃ vārṣikaṃ yasya kuryāt prakasaumikīṃ kriyām
children.translated_text: One whose food supply lasts a year should perform the preliminary rite connected with Soma.
Each year the Soma rite, the animal offering, and the recurring rite
as well as the first-fruits offering and the <s>cāturmāsya</s> rites should be carefully performed.
When these are impossible, a twice-born man should perform the <s>Vaiśvānara</s> offering.

children.text: hīnakalpaṃ na kurvīta sati dravye phalapradam
children.translated_text: When resources are available, he should not perform an inferior procedure, since the proper one gives fruit.
By performing a sacrifice with what has been begged from a Śūdra, one is born as a Caṇḍāla.
He should not take what has been obtained for the sake of sacrifice; otherwise he may become a kite or even a crow.
He may be one whose grain is stored in a granary or a jar, one who has three days' supply, or even one who has only tomorrow's supply.
Or he may live by gleaning grain; among these, each later way is better than the one before it.
He should not seek wealth that obstructs his own Vedic recitation, nor should he seek it from just anywhere.
When sinking from hunger, he may seek wealth from a king, a pupil, or those for whom he sacrifices.
He should avoid ostentation, mercenary motives, heretical behavior, and the conduct of a hypocrite.
He should wear white garments, keep his hair, beard, and nails low-cut, and remain pure.
He should not eat in view of his wife, nor while wearing a single garment, nor while standing.
He should never speak what is unpleasant; he should wear the sacred thread and be disciplined.
He should circumambulate the gods, carrying a staff and water-pot.
He should not urinate in a river, in shade, on ashes, in a cow-pen, in water, or on a road.
Nor should he do so facing fire, the sun, cows, <s>Soma</s>, twilight, water, women, or twice-born men.
He should not gaze at fire, the sun, a naked woman, or a woman engaged in intercourse.

children.text: na ca mūtraṃ purīṣaṃ vā svapet pratyakśirā na ca ||
children.translated_text: Nor should he look at urine or feces, and he should not sleep with his head toward the west.
He should not cast spittle, blood, feces, urine, or poisons into water.
He should not warm his feet at a fire, nor should he step over it.
He should not drink water with joined hands, nor should he wake one who is sleeping.
He should not play with dice, nor should he lie down with gamblers or with the diseased.
He should avoid improper action, smoke from a corpse, and crossing a river.
He should avoid sitting among hair, ashes, husks, charcoal, and skulls.
He should not point out a cow while she is suckling, and he should never enter by a way that is not a door.
He should not accept anything from a greedy king who acts contrary to scripture.
The commencement of Vedic study is to be performed on the Śrāvaṇī day, or under the asterism Śravaṇa,
or under Hasta when the herbs appear, or on the fifth day of Śrāvaṇa.
In the month of Pauṣa, under Rohiṇī, or on the Aṣṭakā as well,
he should perform the formal release of the Vedic metres by the water, outside, according to rule.
There is to be no Vedic study for three days when a pupil, officiating priest, teacher, or kinsman has died.
The same applies at the commencement and release of study, and when a learned man of one's own Vedic branch has died.
There is no study at twilight thunder, at a thunderbolt strike, at an earthquake, or at the fall of meteors.
After completing the Veda, for a day and a night, and after studying the <s>Āraṇyaka</s>, there is likewise no study.
There is no study on the fifteenth, fourteenth, and eighth lunar days, and during an eclipse caused by <s>Rāhu</s>.

children.text: ṛtusandhiṣu bhuktvā vā śrāddhikaṃ pratigṛhya ca ||
children.translated_text: Nor at the junctions of seasons, after eating food connected with a <s>śrāddha</s>, or after accepting such a gift.
When an interruption has been made by cattle, a frog, a mongoose, a dog, a snake, a cat, or a pig,
there is no study for a day and a night; likewise at the fall of lightning and at an upheaval.
There is no study at the cries of a dog, jackal, donkey, or owl, and at the sound of chanting, arrows, or distress.
Nor near what is impure, a corpse, a Śūdra, an outcaste, a cremation ground, or a fallen person.
Nor in an impure place, when oneself is impure, or when lightning and thunder are combined.
Nor after eating with wet hands, in water, at midnight, or in a violent wind.
Nor when the quarters are burning, when dust is raining, or amid twilight, fog, and alarms.

children.text: dhāvataḥ pūtigandhe ca śiṣṭe ca gṛhamāgate ||
children.translated_text: while one is running, when there is a foul smell, and when a learned person has come to the house,
when riding on a donkey, camel, elephant, horse, boat, tree, or mountain:
these are known as the thirty-seven temporary occasions for suspending study.
One should not step over what is prescribed by the Veda, nor a teacher, the shadow of a king, or another man's wife,
nor blood, feces, urine, spittle, or bodily scrapings.
<s>brāhmaṇas</s>, serpents, <s>kṣatriyas</s>, and one's own self should never be despised.
Leavings, feces, urine, and water used for washing the feet should be cast away at a distance.
One should follow the conduct taught in <s>śruti</s> and <s>smṛti</s>, and should not touch vulnerable spots.

children.text: na nindātāḍane kuryātsutaṃ śiṣyaṃ ca tāḍayet ||
children.translated_text: One should not engage in abuse or beating, though one may chastise a son and a pupil.
One should always practice <s>dharma</s> (right conduct), and should not do what is opposed to it.
A householder should not quarrel with his mother, father, guests, or wealthy people.
Without removing five lumps, one should not bathe in waters belonging to another.
One may bathe in rivers, springs, divine or excavated tanks, and lakes.
One should avoid another person's bed and the like, and should not eat, except in distress,
the food of a miser, a captive, a thief, or one of no known standing,
of a lute-player, an accursed man, a usurer, a courtesan, or one initiated by a group,
of a physician, a sick man, an angry man, a eunuch, or one who lives by the stage,
of cruel, fierce, fallen, outcaste, hypocritical, or leftover-eating people,
and of sellers of scripture, men ruled by women, or priests who officiate for a whole village,
of pitiless men, kings, washermen, ingrates, or those who live by slaughter,
of slanderers and liars, and likewise of sellers of Soma,
or of bards and goldsmiths; the food of such people should never be eaten.
Meat eaten without ritual purpose, and food containing hair or insects, should not be eaten.
One should avoid cooked rice that is stale, leftover, touched by a dog, or sprinkled by a fallen person,
touched by a menstruating woman, publicly decried, or insufficient,
smelled by a cow, left over by birds, or deliberately touched by the feet.
Among <s>śūdras</s>, the slave, the cowherd, the family friend, and the half-share ploughman
are people whose food may be eaten, as is the barber and the man who has offered himself.
Stale food may be eaten when it has been smeared with fat and kept for a long time.
Even without fat, preparations of wheat, barley, and milk-products may be eaten.
One should avoid the milk of camels, single-hooved animals, and women.
One should avoid the meat of carnivorous birds, of the dātyūha bird, and of parrots,
as well as cranes, single-hooved animals, haṃsas, herons, egrets, and ṭiṭṭibha birds,
and kṛsara, saṃyāva, pāyasa, apūpa, and śaṣkulī cakes made without ritual purpose,
the kurara bird, web-footed creatures, the wagtail, animals, and birds.
After a man has deliberately eaten cāṣa birds, fish, and red-footed creatures,
or has deliberately eaten dried meat, he should observe a three-day fast.
Having eaten onions, garlic, and the like, he should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> (lunar penance).

children.text: śrāddhe devānpitṝn prārcya khādanmāṃsaṃ na doṣabhāk ||
children.translated_text: At a <s>śrāddha</s> (ancestor rite), after honoring the gods and ancestors, one incurs no fault by eating meat.
That evil-doer dwells in a terrible hell for as many days as there are hairs on the animal,
namely the one who kills animals contrary to the rule.

children.text: māṃsaṃ saṃtyajya saṃprārthya kāmānyāti tato harim ||
children.translated_text: Having renounced meat and prayed, one attains the desired objects and thereafter <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktaśrāddhanirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṇṇavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the ninety-sixth chapter, named 'The Exposition of the <s>śrāddha</s> Taught by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is complete.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
I shall explain the purification of substances; listen to that, best ones.
For gold, silver, shell, conch, ropes and the like, and hides,
and for vessels and seats, purification is held to be by water.
Hot water is for the sruk and sruva ladles, and grain and the like are purified by sprinkling.
Wood, horn, and the like are purified by scraping; sacrificial vessels by wiping.
Woolen and silk articles are purified with warm water and cow urine.
Alms food and a woman's mouth are regarded as pure, while earthenware is purified by being fired again.
For food smelled by a cow, or contaminated by hair, flies, or insects,
purification is effected by throwing ashes on it; purification of the ground is by wiping and the like.
Tin, lead, and copper are purified with alkaline, sour, and water washes.
Iron and bronze are purified with ashes and water, and anything whose impurity is unknown is always pure.
Something smeared with impure matter is purified with earth and water, by removing the smell and the coating.
Water that satisfies cows, remains in its natural condition, and is held in the earth is pure,
and so is meat dropped by dogs, <s>caṇḍālas</s>, carnivores, and the like.
Sunbeams, fire, dust, shadow, a cow, a horse, the earth, and the wind,
splashes from horses and goats, and drops from sipping water are pure.

children.text: snātvā pītvā kṣute supte bhuktvā rathyāprasarpaṇe
children.translated_text: After bathing, drinking, sneezing, sleeping, eating, and walking along a road,
one who has sipped water should sip again, and also after putting on another garment.
After sneezing, spitting, sleeping, putting on a garment, or shedding tears,
in these five cases one should not sip water, but should touch the right ear.
For Agni and the other gods dwell in a <s>brāhmaṇa</s>'s right ear.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktadravyaśuddhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the ninety-seventh chapter, named 'The Exposition of the Purification of Substances Taught by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is complete.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:

children.text: atha dānavidhiṃ vakṣye tanme śṛṇuta suvratāḥ
children.translated_text: Now I shall explain the rule for gifts; listen to me, you of good vows.
<s>brāhmaṇas</s> are superior to others, and among them those devoted to ritual action are superior.

children.text: brahmavettā ca tebhyo 'pi pātraṃ vidyāt tapo'nvitāḥ
children.translated_text: One should know a knower of <s>Brahman</s>, endowed with austerity, to be a worthy recipient even beyond them.
Cows, land, grain, gold, and the like should be given, with honor, to a worthy recipient.

children.text: vidyātapobhyāṃ hīnena na tu grāhyaḥ pratigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: A gift should not be accepted by one who lacks learning and austerity.
By accepting it, he drags the giver down, and himself as well.
One should give every day to a worthy recipient, and especially on special occasions.
Even when asked, one should give according to one's ability, the gift being purified by faith.
She should have golden horns, silver hoofs, be gentle, and be furnished with cloth;
a milch cow, together with a bronze vessel and a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (honorarium), should be given.
The horn is said to be worth ten <s>suvarṇas</s>, and the hoof made of seven <s>palas</s>;
the bronze vessel for the calf is declared to weigh fifty <s>palas</s>.
With a golden pippala-leaf vessel, either a male calf or even a female calf,
her offspring too, free from disease, should be given.
The giver obtains heaven for years equal in number to the hairs on the cow;
and if she is a <s>kapilā</s> cow, she further carries his family across up to the seventh generation.

children.text: yāvadvatsasya dvau pādau mukhaṃ yonyāṃ pradṛśyate
children.translated_text: As long as the calf's two feet and face are seen at the womb,

children.text: tāvadgauḥ pṛthivī jñeyā yāvadgarbhaṃ na muñcati ||
children.translated_text: the cow is to be understood as the earth, so long as she has not released the fetus.
Having given, in whatever way, a cow, whether a milch cow or even a non-milch cow,
provided she is healthy and not exhausted, the giver is honored in heaven.
Massaging the weary, tending the sick, worshiping the gods,
washing feet, and cleaning away the leavings of twice-born men are equivalent to the gift of a cow.
Having given to a twice-born man whatever he desires, one obtains heaven;
having given land, lamps, food, garments, and ghee, one goes to prosperity.
By giving a house, grain, umbrella, garlands, trees or a vehicle, ghee, and water,
and by giving a bed and unguents, one is honored in the world of heaven.
The giver of <s>brahma</s> reaches <s>Brahmaloka</s>, hard for the gods to obtain;
this includes the meanings of the Veda, the ritual scriptures, and the Dharmaśāstras.
Even by purchasing them or by having them written, he obtains <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
Because from this root the Lord formerly created the world,
therefore a compendium of Vedic meaning should be made with every effort.
Whoever writes out and gives an <s>Itihāsa</s> or a <s>Purāṇa</s>
obtains merit equal to the gift of <s>brahma</s>, with a twofold elevation.
Materialism, false reasoning, and speech in Prakrit or barbarian languages

children.text: na śrotavyaṃ dvijenaitadadho nayati taṃ dvijam
children.translated_text: should not be heard by a twice-born man; it leads that twice-born man downward.
One who is capable, but does not accept, obtains the worlds of the giver.

children.text: kuśāḥ śākaṃ payo gandhāḥ pratyākhyeyā na vāri ca
children.translated_text: Kuśa grass, vegetables, milk, fragrances, and water should not be refused;
what has been brought without asking should be accepted, even from a person of evil deeds,
except from adulterous women, heretics, fallen persons, and enemies as well.
For the worship of gods and guests, and precisely for the satisfaction of the ancestors,
one should accept from every quarter, and also for the sake of satisfying oneself.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktadānadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
