children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the ninety-eighth chapter, named 'The Explanation of the Dharma of Gifts Spoken by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is completed.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
Now I shall state the procedure for <s>śrāddha</s>, which destroys all sins:
the new moon, the <s>aṣṭakā</s> days, occasions of increase, the dark fortnight, and the two solstitial passages;
the proper materials, the availability of Brahmins, the equinoxes, and the sun's transitions;
<s>vyatīpāta</s>, <s>gajacchāyā</s>, and eclipses of the moon and sun;
and even one's own inclination toward <s>śrāddha</s> are proclaimed as times for <s>śrāddha</s>.
One connected with the sacred fire and all the gods, a <s>śrotriya</s>, a young knower of the Veda,
one who knows the meaning of the Veda, a chanter of the Jyeṣṭhasāman, one versed in the Trimadhu and Trisuparṇa,
a sister's son, an officiating priest, a son-in-law, a sacrificer, a father-in-law, and a maternal uncle;
one versed in the Triṇāciketa, a daughter's son, a pupil, a relation, and kinsmen;
those devoted to ritual action, those devoted to austerity, maintainers of the five fires, and brahmacārins;
and those devoted to father and mother: these Brahmins are the deities of the <s>śrāddha</s>.
A sick man, one with deficient or excessive limbs, a one-eyed man, and the son of a remarried woman,

children.text: avakīrṇyāda yo ye ca ye cācāravivarjitāḥ
children.translated_text: an avakīrṇin and others, and those who are devoid of proper conduct,

children.text: avaiṣṇavāśca te sarve na śrāddhārhāḥ kadācana ||
children.translated_text: and non-Vaiṣṇavas: all these are never fit for <s>śrāddha</s>.
He should invite them on the previous day, and the twice-born men should be self-controlled.
When they have arrived in the forenoon, he should seat them on seats.
For the gods and for the ancestors he should arrange them, as far as he is able, in their proper places, in even numbers;

children.text: dvau daiva prāgudak pitrye trīṇyekaṃ cobhayoḥ pṛthak ||
children.translated_text: two for the divine rite, facing east or north, and for the ancestral rite three or one, separately for each side.
The same procedure applies for the maternal grandfathers, or else the rite may be performed as a Vaiśvadeva rite.
Having given water for washing the hands, and also kuśa grass for the seats,
he should invoke the <s>Viśvadevas</s>, with permission, by the verse beginning 'Viśvadevāsaḥ.'
Then, with barley, he should scatter the food in a vessel furnished with a <s>pavitra</s> ring.

children.text: śaṃ no devyā payaḥ kṣiptvā yavo 'sīti yavāṃstathā
children.translated_text: Having poured water with 'Śaṃ no devī,' and likewise barley with 'Yavo 'si,'

children.text: yā divyā iti mantreṇa hasteṣveva viniṣkṣipet ||
children.translated_text: he should place it directly in their hands with the mantra beginning 'Yā divyā.'
He should provide scented water, a lamp, garlands, wreaths, and lights.
Then, making the sacred thread <s>apasavya</s>, he should move counterclockwise for the ancestors.
Having given doubled kuśa grass, he should invoke the ancestors with the verse beginning 'Uśantas tvā';

children.text: āvāhya tadanujñāto japed āyan tu nas tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: after invoking them and receiving permission, he should then recite 'Āyantu naḥ.'
Sesame seeds should be used in place of barley, and he should perform the <s>arghya</s> and the rest as before.
Having given the <s>arghya</s>, he should place their mingled streams in a vessel according to rule.
Saying 'You are the seat of the ancestors,' he turns the vessel upside down below.
Taking food soaked in ghee, he asks, 'Shall I make the offering in the fire?'
When he has been told, 'Do it,' he offers in the fire as in the ancestral sacrifice.
Then, composed, he should give the remainder of the oblation in the vessels,
in such vessels as have been obtained, and especially in silver ones.
After giving the food, he performs the consecration of the vessel with 'The earth is the vessel.'
Having done this with 'This is <s>Viṣṇu</s>,' he should place the thumb of the twice-born man there.
After reciting the <s>vyāhṛtis</s>, the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, and the verses beginning 'Madhu vātā,'
he should say, 'Eat at your ease'; they too should eat, restrained in speech.
Without anger and without haste, he should give the desired food and the sacrificial fare.

children.text: ā tṛptestu pavitrāṇi japtvā pūrvajapaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: After reciting the purificatory formulas until satisfaction, and likewise the earlier muttered prayer,

children.text: annamādāya tṛptāḥ sthaḥ śeṣaṃ caivānumantrya ca ||
children.translated_text: he should take the food, ask, "Are you satisfied?", and receive permission concerning the remainder.
He should scatter that food on the ground and give water once to each.
Taking up all the food mixed with sesame, he should face south.
Near the leftovers he should offer <s>piṇḍas</s> as in the ancestral sacrifice.
He should do the same also for the maternal grandfathers, and then give water for sipping.
Then he should have the blessing of well-being pronounced and give imperishable water.
Having given a fee according to his ability, he should utter the formula of <s>svadhā</s>.
When permitted with the words, "Let it be said," he should say, "<s>Svadhā</s> to the ancestors."
When the brahmins have said, "Let there be <s>svadhā</s>," he should then sprinkle water on the ground.
Saying, "May they be pleased," and in this way giving water to the <s>Viśvedevās</s>,
he should say, "May our donors increase; may the Vedas and our lineage increase.

children.text: śraddhā ca no mā vyagamad bahu deyaṃ ca no 'stviti
children.translated_text: May faith not depart from us, and may there be much for us to give."

children.text: ity utkrotkrā priyā vācaḥ praṇipatya visarjayet ||
children.translated_text: Having uttered such pleasing words again and again, he should bow down and dismiss them.

children.text: vāje vāje iti prītyā pitṛpūrvaṃ visarjanam
children.translated_text: With affection he should perform the dismissal with the verse beginning "Vāje vāje," beginning with the ancestors.
In the vessel for the arghya into which those streams had first been poured,
he should set the ancestor-vessel upright and dismiss the brahmins.
Having followed them clockwise, he should eat what has been served to the ancestors.

children.text: brahmacārī bhavettāṃ tu rajanīṃ bhāryayā saha
children.translated_text: On that night he should remain celibate, even while together with his wife.
Having thus performed the clockwise rite, at a prosperity rite he should also worship the <s>Nāndīmukha</s> ancestors.

children.text: yajet tadadhi karkandhūmiśrāḥ piṇḍā yaivaḥ śritāḥ
children.translated_text: Then the <s>piṇḍas</s>, apparently mixed with <s>karkandhū</s> berries and prepared with barley, are prescribed.
The <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> rite is without the divine portion, with one food and one purifying grass.
It lacks invocation and the fire-offering action, and it is performed with the sacred thread turned to the right.
In the place of the imperishable-water formula, he should dismiss the brahmins with, "May it attend upon him."
He should say, "Be pleased," and they should reply, "Indeed, we are pleased by these."
He should prepare four vessels mixed with fragrance, water, and sesame.
For the arghya, he should pour the vessel for the departed one into the vessels of the ancestors.
With the two verses beginning "Ye samānāḥ," he should perform the rest as before.
This is the <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s>, an <s>ekoddiṣṭa</s> rite, and it is the same also for a woman.
For one whose <s>sapiṇḍīkaraṇa</s> takes place before a year has passed,
the twice-born man should give his food, together with a water-pot, for a year.

children.text: piṇḍāṃśca goja viprebhyo dadyādagnau jale 'pi vā ||
children.translated_text: He should give the <s>piṇḍas</s> to cows or to brahmins, or place them in fire or in water.

children.text: haviṣyānnena vai māsaṃ pāyasena tu vatsaram
children.translated_text: With sacrificial food they are satisfied for a month, but with milk-rice for a year.
With fish, deer, sheep, bird, goat, and spotted-deer meat,
and with the meats of antelope, <s>ruru</s> deer, boar, and hare, in due order,
the grandfathers are satisfied here by offerings for increasing numbers of months.
One should give on the thirteenth day in the rainy season and under the <s>Maghās</s>; there is no doubt.
Thus, beginning with the first lunar day, the giver of <s>śrāddha</s> obtains desires such as a maiden and the rest.
For those slain by weapons, the offering is made on the fourteenth day.

children.text: svargaṃ hyapatyamojaśca śauryaṃ kṣetraṃ balaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Heaven, offspring, vigor, heroism, land, and strength,

children.text: putraśraiṣṭhyaṃ sa saubhāgyaṃ samṛddhiṃ mukhyatāṃ śubham
children.translated_text: the excellence of sons, good fortune, prosperity, preeminence, and auspiciousness,
the turning of the wheel, and such things as trade as well,
freedom from disease, fame, freedom from grief, and the highest goal,

children.text: dhanaṃ vidyāṃ ca vāksiddhiṃ kupyaṃ go'jāvikaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: wealth, learning, success in speech, metal goods, cows, goats, and sheep,
horses and long life: these are obtained by one who properly offers <s>śrāddha</s>.
From <s>Kṛttikā</s> through <s>Bharaṇī</s>, he may obtain these desired objects.
The twice-born men, pleased by gifts such as garments, indeed please the man who has performed <s>śrāddha</s>.

children.text: āyuḥ prajā dhanaṃ vidyāṃ svargamokṣasukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: Longevity, offspring, wealth, learning, heaven, liberation, and happiness

children.text: prayacchati yathā rājyaṃ prītyā nityaṃ pitāmahaḥ ||
children.translated_text: the grandfather always grants with affection, just as he grants a kingdom.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktaśrāddhavidhinirūpaṇaṃ nāma navanavatitamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the ninety-ninth chapter, named "The Explanation of the Rule for Śrāddha Taught by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>," is complete.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
Understand the signs of one afflicted by <s>Vināyaka</s>.
In dreams he plunges excessively into water and sees shaven-headed men.
He is downcast, his undertakings are fruitless, and without cause he sinks in assemblies.

children.text: rājā rājyaṃ kumārī ca patiṃ putraṃ ca gurviṇī ||
children.translated_text: A king does not obtain his kingdom, a maiden her husband, nor a pregnant woman her son.
For him a ritual bath should be performed on an auspicious day, according to rule.
He is first to be rubbed and purified with a paste of white mustard mixed with ghee.
His head should then be anointed with all herbs and all fragrances.
While he sits on an auspicious seat, he should have good brahmins pronounce blessings.

children.text: mṛttikāṃ rocanāṃ gandhān gugguluṃ cāpsu niḥkṣipet
children.translated_text: One should throw clay, yellow pigment, perfumes, and guggulu into the waters,
which have been brought from a lake in four pitchers of the same color.
He should be placed on a red hide of an ox and likewise on an auspicious seat.
"The thousand-eyed, hundred-streamed one is remembered by the seers as purifying.
With it I consecrate you; may the <s>Pāvamānī</s> verses purify you.

children.text: bhagaṃ tu varuṇo rājā bhagaṃ sūryo bṛhaspatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: May King <s>Varuṇa</s> give fortune; may <s>Sūrya</s> and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> give fortune.
May <s>Indra</s>, <s>Vāyu</s>, and the Seven Seers give fortune.

children.text: yatte keśeṣu daurbhāgyaṃ sīmante yacca mūrdhani ||
children.translated_text: Whatever misfortune is in your hair, in your hair-parting, and on your head,

children.text: lalāṭe karṇayor akṣṇor āpas tadghnantu te sadā
children.translated_text: on your forehead, ears, and eyes, may the waters always destroy that for you."
When he has bathed, he should offer mustard oil with a ladle made of udumbara wood.
He should pour the oblation on the head, holding kuśa grasses with the left hand.
With <s>Mita</s> and <s>Samita</s>, and likewise with the two <s>Śālakaṭaṅkaṭas</s>,
with <s>Kuṣmāṇḍa</s> and <s>Rājaputra</s>, each ending with <s>svāhā</s>,
he should make an offering on the ground at a crossroads, spreading kuśa grasses everywhere,
both cooked and uncooked rice, and also sesame-paste rice.

children.text: puṣpaṃ citraṃ sugandhaṃ ca surāṃ ca trividhāmapi ||
children.translated_text: Flowers of various colors and fragrant ones, and also liquor of the three kinds,
radishes, pūrikās and apūpas, likewise auṇḍeraka cakes, and garlands,
curds, milk-rice, cooked food, and flour mixed with molasses and water:
having brought all these, then placing his head on the ground,
he should attend upon <s>Ambikā</s> and, with joined hands, give the arghya offering.
With dūrvā grass, mustard seeds, and flowers, and, finally, with rites connected with the birth of a son,
having performed the rite of blessing, he should pray to the virtuous <s>Ambikā</s>:

children.text: rūpaṃ dehi yaśo dehi bhagaṃ bhagavati dehi me
children.translated_text: "Give me beauty; give me fame; O blessed Goddess, give me fortune.

children.text: putrāndehi śriyaṃ dehi sarvānkāmāṃśca dehi me ||
children.translated_text: Give me sons; give me prosperity; and give me all desired things."
Afterward he should feed Brahmins, with white garments and ointments.
Having honored the planets as well, he should give a pair of garments to the guru.
Devoted to worship of the sun, he obtains auspiciousness and the fruit of the rite.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktagaṇapatikalpanirūpaṇaṃ nāma śatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the hundredth chapter, named "The Description of the Procedure for <s>Gaṇapati</s> as Taught by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
One who desires prosperity or desires pacification, or who is afflicted by planetary aspect or sorcery,

children.text: grahayajñaṃ samaṃ kuryād grahāścaite budhaiḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: should perform the planetary sacrifice in due measure; and these are remembered by the wise as the planets:
the Sun, the Moon, <s>Maṅgala</s>, <s>Budha</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s>,
<s>Śukra</s>, <s>Śanaiścara</s>, <s>Rāhu</s>, and <s>Ketu</s> are remembered as the host of planets.
From copper, crystal, red sandalwood, gold for both,
silver, iron, lead, and bronze: learn the corresponding colors.

children.text: raktaḥ śuklastathā raktaḥ pītaḥ pītaḥ sito'sitaḥ
children.translated_text: Red, white, likewise red, yellow, yellow, white, black,
black, and black are the colors in order, O sages; then the substances are as follows.
He should establish them in the colors of the planets and draw them on cloth for the sake of the oblation.
He should bathe them and perform the homa according to rule with the planetary substances.
Gold pieces should be given, as well as garments and fine flowers.
Fragrances and offerings should be given, and guggulu incense is to be offered.
There, with the mantras, sacrificial porridges should be prepared for each deity.
With the hymns beginning "ā kṛṣṇena," "imaṃ devāḥ," and "agnir mūrdhā divaḥ kakut,"
and with "udbudhyasva," he should offer oblations with these in that very order.
Then, in order, with "bṛhaspate paridīya," "sarve," and "annāt parisrutam,"

children.text: śaṃ no devī kayānaśca ketuṃ kraṇvanniti kramāt ||
children.translated_text: and with "śaṃ no devī," "kayā naḥ," and "ketuṃ kṛṇvan," he should offer.
Arka wood, palāśa, khadira, then apāmārga and pippala,

children.text: audumbaraḥ śamī dūrvā kuśāśca samidhaḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: audumbara, śamī, dūrvā grass, and kuśa grass are the fuel-sticks in order.
They are to be offered with honey and ghee, and also mixed with curds.
Rice with molasses, milk-rice, sacrificial food, and ṣāṣṭika rice cooked in milk,
curd-rice, an oblation, cakes, meat, and various foods

children.text: dadyād grahakramād etān grahebhyo bhājanaṃ tataḥ ||
children.translated_text: should be given to the planets in planetary order; then the vessel should be given to the planets.
A cow, a conch, an ox, a golden garment, and likewise a horse,

children.text: kṛṣṇā gaurāyasaṃ chāga etā vai dakṣiṇāḥ kramāt
children.translated_text: a black cow, an iron object, and a goat: these are indeed the gifts in order.

children.text: grahāḥ pūjyāḥ sadā yasmād rājyādi prāpyate phalam ||
children.translated_text: The planets should always be worshiped, since through them the fruit beginning with sovereignty is obtained.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktagrahaśāntinirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the hundred-and-first chapter, named "The Description of Planetary Pacification as Taught by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
I shall describe the forest-dweller's āśrama; let the great sages hear it.

children.text: putreṣu bhāryāṃ niḥkṣipya vanaṃ gacchetsahaiva vā ||
children.translated_text: Having entrusted his wife to his sons, he should go to the forest, or he may go together with her.
The forest-dweller should be celibate, maintaining the sacred fires and worship, and patient.
With what is produced from untilled ground he should satisfy the fires, ancestors, gods, and guests,
and also servants; wearing beard, matted hair, and body hair, self-controlled,
subdued, bathing at the three junctions of the day, and abstaining from receiving gifts,
devoted to Vedic recitation, given to meditation, and delighting in the welfare of all beings,
he should undertake the taking of provisions for a day, for a month, or for the interval between them.
In Āśvayuja he should abandon what has been cultivated and apply himself to the proper time with vows and the like.
He may eat once in a fortnight or once in a month, and he may use his teeth as his mortar.
Practicing the cāndrāyaṇa vow, he should sleep on the ground and perform his rites with fruits and the like.
In summer he should stand amid the five fires; during the rains he should sleep on bare ground.
In winter he should wear wet garments, and he should pass the day through the practice of yoga.
Toward one who pierces him with thorns and one who anoints him with sandalwood,

children.text: akruddhaḥ parituṣṭaśca samastasya ca tasya ca ||
children.translated_text: he should be without anger and content, the same toward both of them.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktavānaprasthadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the hundred-and-second chapter, named "The Description of the Forest-Dweller's Dharma as Taught by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>."
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
I shall teach the <s>dharma</s> of the mendicant; understand it, O best ones.
From the forest or from the household, having performed a sacrifice with the gift of all one's Vedic property,
and after that the prājāpatya rite, having placed the fire within himself,
beneficial to all beings, peaceful, bearing the triple staff and carrying a water-pot,
wandering through every hermitage, he should resort to a village for the sake of alms.
Uncareless, he should go about for alms in the evening, without being conspicuous.
When the village is filled with mendicants, he should seek only enough for the journey, free from greed.
Or he may become a paramahaṃsa, bearing a single staff and beginning with the restraints.
Perfected in yoga, abandoning the body, he attains immortality here.
A householder who is generous, fond of guests, and wise is released even in the śrāddha rite.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktavānaprasthasaṃnyāsadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma tryuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-third chapter, named 'The Explanation of the Dharma of Forest-Dwellers and Renunciants Spoken by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is completed.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
After the hell that has arisen from a great sin, when the sinful karma has been exhausted,

children.text: brahmahā śvā kharoṣṭraḥ syādbheko yakaḥ surāpyapi ||
children.translated_text: a killer of a Brahmin becomes a dog, a donkey, or a camel; and a drinker of liquor becomes a frog or a yaka.
A thief of gold becomes a worm or an insect; one who violates the teacher's bed becomes grass and the like.
One becomes afflicted with consumption, black-toothed, bad-nailed, and disfigured.

children.text: brahmahatyākramāt syuśca tatsarvaṃ vā śiśer bhavet
children.translated_text: These occur in the order beginning with Brahmin-killing, or all of them may occur even from infancy.
A thief of food becomes deceitful, and a stealer of speech becomes mute.
A thief of grain has an extra limb; a slanderer has a foul-smelling nose.
A taker of oil drinks oil; an informer has a foul-smelling mouth.

children.text: brahmasvaṃ kanyakāṃ krītvā vane rakṣo bhavedvṛṣaḥ
children.translated_text: After taking a Brahmin's property or buying a maiden, one becomes a demon in the forest, or a bull.
A thief of jewels is born in a low condition; a thief of leaves and vegetables becomes a peacock.
Having stolen a bunch, one becomes a musk-rat; a thief of grain becomes a mouse.

children.text: phalaṃ kapiḥ paśūnhṛtvā tvajā kākaḥ payastathā ||
children.translated_text: Having stolen fruit, one becomes a monkey; having stolen cattle, hide, or milk, one becomes a crow.

children.text: māṃsaṃ gṛdhraḥ paṭaṃ śvitrī cīrī lavaṇahārakaḥ
children.translated_text: A thief of meat becomes a vulture; a thief of cloth becomes afflicted with white leprosy; a thief of salt becomes a cīrī bird.
Having received the result according to the deed, through the passage of time they enter animal birth.
They are born lacking proper marks, poor, the lowest of men.
Then, when they have become free from impurity, they are born as disciplined men in a great family,
endowed with auspicious marks and furnished with wealth and grain.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktakarmavipākanirūpaṇaṃ nāma caturuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the first section called the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-fourth chapter, named 'The Explanation of Karmic Consequence Spoken by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is completed.
From not performing what is prescribed, and from practicing what is censured,
and also from not restraining the senses, a man comes to a fall.
Therefore <s>prāyaścitta</s> (expiation) should be performed carefully for purification;
in this way his inner self and also the world become pleased.
The world becomes pleased, and the self likewise; through expiations there is destruction of sin.
But sinners who do not perform expiation and are devoid of remorse
go to hells, to <s>Mahāraurava</s> and <s>Raurava</s>,
to <s>Tāmisra</s> and <s>Lohaśaṅku</s>, filled with foul stench,
to <s>Haṃsābha</s>, <s>Lohitoda</s>, and the path of the <s>Saṃjīvana</s> river,
to <s>Mahānilaya</s>, <s>Kākola</s>, <s>Andhatāmisra</s>, and <s>Vāpana</s>;

children.text: avīciṃ kumbhīpākaṃ ca yānti pāpā hyapuṇyataḥ
children.translated_text: through demerit sinners indeed go to <s>Avīci</s> and <s>Kumbhīpāka</s>.
The killer of a Brahmin, the drinker of liquor, the thief, one who consorts with them, and one who violates the teacher's bed: these are major sinners.
Slandering the teacher and slandering the Veda are both equivalent to killing a Brahmin.
Eating forbidden food and undertaking crooked conduct
and tasting the mouth of a menstruating woman are equivalent to drinking liquor.
The theft of horses, jewels, and the like is considered equivalent to stealing gold.
With regard to a friend's wife, maidens, women of one's own birth-line, outcaste women,
and likewise women of the same gotra, intercourse is remembered as equivalent to violating the teacher's bed.

children.text: pituḥ svasāraṃ mātuśca mātulānīṃ snuṣām api
children.translated_text: His father's sister, his mother's sister, his maternal uncle's wife, his daughter-in-law,
his mother's co-wife, his sister, and likewise the teacher's daughter,
the teacher's wife, and his own daughter: one who goes to these women is a violator of the teacher's bed.
After his penis has been cut off, death is his punishment; and the same applies to the woman if she acted willingly.
Killing a cow, becoming a vrātya, theft, and improper handling of debts,
not maintaining the sacred fires, selling forbidden goods, and marrying before an elder brother,
receiving instruction from a servant and teaching for hire,
adultery, being married while an elder brother remains unmarried, usury, and dealing in salt,
and living by censured gain from a Śūdra, Vaiśya, or degraded Kṣatriya,
atheism, violation of vows, selling meat from the spit, and the sale of cows or horses,
abandoning father, mother, or friend, and selling ponds or parks,
defiling a maiden and sacrificing for a younger brother married before his elder,
giving a maiden to that very man, deceitfulness, and violation of vows,
beginning ritual acts for one's own sake, and resorting to wine-drinking women,
abandoning Vedic recitation, the sacred fire, and a son, and also abandoning relatives,
approaching false treatises, and selling one's wife or oneself:
these have been declared subsidiary sins; now learn the expiation.
Bearing a skull as his emblem on his head, eating alms, and making his deed known,
the killer of a Brahmin, eating moderately for twelve years, obtains purification.

children.text: lomabhyaḥ svāheti ca vā lomaprabhṛti vai tanum ||
children.translated_text: Or, with the formula 'svāhā to the hairs' and so on, beginning with the hairs, he should offer his body,
up to the marrow, each part with its own mantra in proper order.
Purification may come from protecting Brahmins; after doing this, there is indeed purification.

children.text: nirātaṅkaṃ dvijaṃ gāṃ ca brāhmaṇārthe hato 'pi vā
children.translated_text: Or if, for the sake of a Brahmin, he saves a twice-born man or a cow from danger, even if he is killed, he is purified.

children.text: araṇye niyato juptvā triḥ kṛtvo vedasaṃhitām ||
children.translated_text: Restrained in the forest, after reciting the Vedic Saṃhitā three times,

children.text: sarasvatīṃ vā saṃsevyaṃ dhanaṃ pātre samarpayet
children.translated_text: or after serving <s>Sarasvatī</s>, he should give wealth to a worthy recipient.
One who has killed a Kṣatriya or a Vaiśya at a sacrifice should observe the vow of a Brahmin-killer.
So too the killer of an embryo, according to caste, and the destroyer of an Ātreyī woman,
should observe the vow; even without killing, one who has come for the purpose of killing should do so.
But in the case of a Brahmin present at a soma-pressing, he should observe the vow in double measure.
For a drinker of liquor, purification comes after drinking liquor-water, ghee, and cow urine,

children.text: agnivarṇaṃ ghṛtaṃ vāpi cīravāsā jaṭī bhavet
children.translated_text: or ghee heated to the color of fire; he should wear rags and have matted hair.
He should perform the vow of a Brahmin-killer, and afterward he is fit for initiation again.
And because of drinking semen, feces, and urine, a Brahmin woman who drinks liquor
falls from her husband's world and becomes a vulture, a sow, or a bitch.

children.text: svarṇahārī dvijo rājñe dattvā tu musalaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: A twice-born thief of gold, having given a mace to the king,
and having made public declaration of his deed, becomes pure if he is killed by him.
By giving gold equal to himself in weight, a twice-born man may attain purification.
If he should secretly sleep on a bed together with a woman,
he should cut off his penis and testicles and cast them away in the south-western quarter.
Or, one who has gone to his teacher's bed should perform the <s>prājāpatya</s> <s>kṛcchra</s> (expiatory austerity) for a year.

children.text: cāndrāyaṇaṃ vā trīn māsān abhyased vedasaṃhitām
children.translated_text: Or he should practice the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow for three months and recite a Vedic <s>saṃhitā</s>.
A killer of a cow should drink <s>pañcagavya</s> (the five products of the cow) and remain restrained for a month.
Sleeping in a cowshed, following the cows, he is purified by the gift of a cow.
Purification from lesser sins also comes through the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow.

children.text: payasā vāpi māsena parākeṇāpi vā punaḥ
children.translated_text: Or it may come in a month by living on milk, or again by the <s>parāka</s> vow.

children.text: ṛṣabhaikaṃ sahasraṃ gā dadyāt kṣatravadhe pumān ||
children.translated_text: For killing a Kṣatriya, a man should give one bull and a thousand cows.
Or he should observe the vow for killing a Brahmin for three years.
The killer of a Vaiśya should observe this for one year, or should give one hundred cows.
The killer of a Śūdra should observe this for six months, or should give ten cows.
Having killed an uncorrupted woman, he should observe the vow for killing a Śūdra.
For killing a cat, monitor lizard, mongoose, domestic animal, or frog,

children.text: pibetkṣīraṃ tryahaṃ pāpī kṛcchraṃ vāpyadhikaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: the sinner should drink milk for three days, or should perform a still greater <s>kṛcchra</s>.
For an elephant, five dark bulls are due; for a parrot, a two-year-old calf.
For donkeys, goats, and sheep a bull should be given; for a crane, a three-year-old animal.
For cutting trees, shrubs, creepers, and plants, one should recite a hundred Ṛgvedic verses.

children.text: avakīrṇo bhaved gatvā brahmacārī ca yoṣitam ||
children.translated_text: A brahmacārin who has intercourse with a woman becomes an <s>avakīrṇa</s> (one whose vow has been broken).
After offering a donkey as the sacrificial animal to <s>Nairṛta</s>, he is purified.
For eating honey or meat, a <s>kṛcchra</s> is to be performed, along with the remaining vows.
If a pupil sent out by the teacher dies, the teacher should perform three <s>kṛcchras</s>.
Having acted against his teacher, one is purified only after appeasing him.
One should approach even enemies with gifts of grain and the like, or with gestures of affection and so on.

children.text: kriyamāṇopakāre ca mṛte vipre na pātakam ||
children.translated_text: If a Brahmin dies while assistance is being rendered, there is no sin.
One who falsely accuses another of a great sin or a lesser sin
should remain for a month living on water, reciting mantras, with his senses restrained.
One who approaches his brother's wife without being appointed for it should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s> vow.
After approaching a menstruating woman, he becomes pure at the end of three nights by drinking ghee.
Living in a cowshed, remaining celibate, and observing a milk-vow for one month,
constantly engaged in reciting the <s>Gāyatrī</s>, he is released from the fault of accepting improper gifts.
A priest who sacrifices for <s>vrātyas</s>, and one who lives in such a manner, should perform three <s>kṛcchras</s>.
One who has corrupted the Veda should eat barley for a year; so too one who has abandoned those who sought refuge.
One who rides on a donkey or a camel should perform three breath-regulations.

children.text: nagnaḥ snātvā ca suptvā ca gatvā caiva divā striyam ||
children.translated_text: The same applies after bathing naked, sleeping naked, or going to a woman by day.

children.text: guruṃ tvaṃkṛtya huṃkṛtya vipraṃ nirjitya vādataḥ
children.translated_text: Having addressed his teacher as “you,” shouted “huṃ” at him, or defeated a Brahmin in debate,
after appeasing him, O sages, one should then fast for a day.
For raising a staff against a Brahmin there is a <s>kṛcchra</s>; for striking him down, an <s>atikṛcchra</s>.

children.text: deśaṃ kālaṃ vayaḥ śaktiṃ pāpaṃ cāvekṣya yatnataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having carefully considered place, time, age, strength, and the sin,

children.text: prāyaścittaṃ prakalpyaṃ syādyatra yoktā tu niṣkṛtiḥ
children.translated_text: an expiation should be prescribed wherever there is one qualified to apply the remedy.
Abortion and reviling the husband are causes of downfall for women.

children.text: eṣa grahāntike doṣaḥ tasmāttāṃ dūtaras tyajet
children.translated_text: This fault concerns the embryo; therefore one should avoid her from afar.
One whose fault is publicly known should perform a vow approved by his teacher.
But one whose fault is not publicly known should practice a secret vow.
A killer of a Brahmin, after fasting for three nights and reciting the <s>Aghamarṣaṇa</s>,

children.text: antarjale viśuddhe ca dattvā gāṃ ca payasvinīm
children.translated_text: is purified in clean water, and also after giving a milk-giving cow.
With the Ṛgvedic verse “to the hairs, svāhā,” he should live on air for a day.
Having recited in water, he should offer forty oblations of ghee.
After fasting for three nights and offering ghee with the <s>Kūṣmāṇḍī</s> verses, he becomes pure.

children.text: surāpaḥ svarṇahārī ca rudrajāpī jale sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: A drinker of liquor and a thief of gold, standing in water and reciting the <s>Rudra</s>,
and one who has gone to his teacher's bed are released by recitation of the <s>Sahasraśīrṣa</s>.
One should perform a hundred breath-regulations for the removal of all sins.
He becomes pure by drinking Soma-water accompanied by the syllable <s>oṃ</s>.
After fasting, if a twice-born man has drunk semen, feces, or urine,
the sin committed in ignorance is destroyed when the three twilight rites are performed.
For twice-born men, sin is destroyed by eleven recitations of the <s>Rudra</s>.
One devoted to Vedic study, peaceful, and intent on the five sacrifices,

children.text: na spṛśanti hā pāpāni cāśu smṛtvā hyapohitaḥ
children.translated_text: is not touched by sins; by recollection he quickly drives them away.
Having recited the <s>Gāyatrī</s> a thousand times, he is pure, except from the killing of a Brahmin.
Celibacy, compassion, patience, meditation, truthfulness, and freedom from stain,
non-injury, non-stealing, gentleness, and restraint: these are remembered as the <s>yamas</s>.
Bathing, silence, fasting, sacrifice, Vedic study, and restraint of the sexual organ,

children.text: tapo 'krodho gurorbhaktiḥ śaucaṃ ca niyamāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: austerity, absence of anger, devotion to the teacher, and purity are remembered as the <s>niyamas</s>.
<s>Pañcagavya</s> consists of cow's milk, curds, urine, dung, and ghee.

children.text: jagdhvā pare 'hny upavaset kṛcchraṃ sāntapanaṃ caret ||
children.translated_text: Having consumed it, one should fast on the following day; thus one performs the <s>sāṃtapana</s> <s>kṛcchra</s>.
Using the <s>sāṃtapana</s> substances separately for six days, together with fasting,
this <s>kṛcchra</s>, lasting seven days, is remembered as the great <s>sāṃtapana</s>.
With waters infused with leaves of parṇa, udumbara, lotus, bilva, and kuśa,
each practiced separately on each day, it is called the leaf-<s>kṛcchra</s>.
One should drink, on each successive day, heated milk, heated ghee, and heated water.
Together with a fast for one night, this is the purifying heated <s>kṛcchra</s>.
By eating once by day, by eating at night, and likewise by eating what is obtained unasked,
and by fasting, the quarter-<s>kṛcchra</s> is declared.
When done three times in whatever manner, this is called the <s>prājāpatya</s>.
This same observance becomes the <s>atikṛcchra</s> when the food is only a palmful of water.
The <s>kṛcchrātikṛcchra</s> is performed with milk for twenty-one days,
and the <s>parāka</s> is declared to consist of twelve days of fasting.
On successive days, oil-cake, rice-water, buttermilk-water, water, and barley meal,
one item each, and then a fast: this is called the gentle <s>kṛcchra</s>.
By practicing these for three nights each, one by one in sequence,
this is to be known as the <s>tulāpuruṣa</s>, lasting fifteen days.
In the bright fortnight he should take morsels increasing according to the lunar dates, each the size of a peacock's egg;
in the dark fortnight he should decrease one morsel at a time: he should perform the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.
In whatever manner, two hundred and forty morsels
he should consume within a single month; that is another <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>.

children.text: kṛtvā triṣavaṇaṃ snānaṃ piṇḍaṃ cāndrāyaṇaṃ caret
children.translated_text: Having bathed at the three daily libation-times, he should perform the morsel-based <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>;
he should recite purifying texts and consecrate the morsels with the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
For sins that have not been specifically prescribed, purification is by the <s>cāndrāyaṇa</s>;
and one who performs this for the sake of <s>dharma</s> goes to the same world as the moon.
One who performs a <s>kṛcchra</s> while desiring <s>dharma</s> obtains great prosperity.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktaprāyaścittaviveko nāma pañcottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first section called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the one-hundred-fifth chapter, named 'The Explanation of Expiation Spoken by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is completed.
<s>Yājñavalkya</s> said:
I shall explain impurity after death; listen to that, you whose vows are restrained.
One should bury a child less than two years old, and after that one should not perform the water offering.
Having accompanied him as far as the cremation ground, together with the other relatives,
the <s>Yama</s> hymn should be recited, while he is burned by those reciting it, with ordinary fire.
If he had entered upon the sacred fires, he should be cremated as an <s>āhitāgni</s>, according to the prescribed rite.
On the seventh or else the tenth day the relatives approach the waters.
Facing the direction of the ancestors, they recite, 'May this sin that has burned us go away,'
and in the same way water rites are performed for the maternal grandfather, teacher, and wives.
Discretionary water offerings are for a son, friend, sister's son, father-in-law, and officiating priest;
restrained in speech, they pour water once, using the name and lineage.
But for heretics and fallen persons they should not perform water rites,
nor for brahmacārins, outcast initiates, and women who go as they please.
Women who drink liquor and women who kill themselves are not fit recipients of impurity observances or water offerings.

children.text: tato na roditavyaṃ hi tvanityā jīvasaṃsthitiḥ ||
children.translated_text: After that one should not weep, for the condition of living beings is impermanent.
The rite should be performed according to one's ability; then one should go back home.
Having chewed neem leaves, controlled, at the doorway of the house,
then having sipped water and touched fire, water, cow dung, a cow, and white mustard seeds,
they should enter, after touching these and slowly placing a foot on a stone.
The rite beginning with entry, even after contact with the corpse,
brings purification at that very moment for those who have seen it; for others, purification comes through bathing and restraint.
They should sleep on the ground, eating food that has been bought or obtained, each separately.
The one who performs the morsel-offering should give food to the departed for three days.
Water should be set out in the open for one day, but milk in an earthen vessel;
the <s>vaitāna</s> and domestic fire rites, and the rites enjoined by <s>śruti</s>, should be performed.

children.text: ā dantajanmanaḥ sadyaḥ ā cūḍaṃ naiśikī smṛtā
children.translated_text: Until the growth of teeth there is immediate purification; until the tonsure, one night is remembered;

children.text: trirātram ā vratādeśād daśarātram ataḥ param ||
children.translated_text: until initiation into vows, three nights; after that, ten nights.
Corpse impurity is said to be either three nights or ten nights.
For one under two years old, in both cases, the birth-impurity belongs to the mother alone.
When birth and death occur within the same period, one is purified by the remaining days.

children.text: daśa dvādaśa varṇānāṃ tathā pañcadaśaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: For the social classes the periods are ten, twelve, and likewise fifteen days,
and also thirty days; thus is the impurity for death and birth.
For unmarried girls and for children, purification is in one day.
For a teacher, pupil, reciter, maternal uncle, and <s>śrotriya</s>,
for non-natural sons and for wives who have gone to another man,
and likewise for a resident and for a king, purification is completed on that same day.
For those killed by a king, a cow, or a Brahmin, and at once for those who kill themselves,
and for those killed by poison and the like, there is no impurity for the ruler of the earth.
Likewise for those engaged in a sacrificial session, vow-observers, brahmacārins, donors, and knowers of Brahman.

children.text: dāne vivāhe yajñe ca saṃgrāme deśaviplave
children.translated_text: At a gift, a marriage, and a sacrifice, and in battle or in the upheaval of a country,

children.text: āpadyapi ca kaṣṭāyāṃ sadyaḥ śaucaṃ vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: and also in a severe calamity, immediate purity is prescribed.
Time, fire, ritual action, earth, wind, the mind, knowledge, austerity, and recitation,
repentance and fasting: these are causes of purification for everyone.
For those who have done what should not be done, giving is a purifier; the current of a river also purifies.
In distress, a twice-born man may live by the occupation of a Kṣatriya, or even by that of Vaiśyas.
Fruit, soma, linen, creepers, curds, milk, ghee, water,
sesame-rice, juice, alkali, honey, lac, cooked food, and oblation,
cloth, stone, liquor, flowers, greens, earth, leather, and sandals,

children.text: eṇatvacaṃ ca kauśeyaṃ lavaṇaṃ māsameva ca ||
children.translated_text: antelope skin, silk, salt, and meat,
oil-cake, roots, and perfumes: living by a Vaiśya's occupation, he should not sell these.
Sesame may be taken for sale for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, if exchanged for an equal amount of grain.
Even a twice-born man fallen into distress should not sell salt and the like.
A Brahmin who accepts from inferior persons is not tainted, O twice-born one, just as the sun is not.
He may perform agriculture and similar work in the same way; horses likewise are not to be sold.
When, after remaining hungry for three days, he is seen to be without livelihood,

children.text: rājā dharmyāṃ prakurvīta vṛttiṃ viprādikasya ca ||
children.translated_text: the king should provide a lawful livelihood for a Brahmin and the others.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yājñavalkyoktāśaucāpadvṛttyornirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaḍuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first section called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the one-hundred-sixth chapter, named 'The Explanation of Impurity and Emergency Livelihood Spoken by <s>Yājñavalkya</s>,' is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
<s>Parāśara</s> spoke to <s>Vyāsa</s> about <s>dharma</s> beginning with the duties of varṇa and āśrama.

children.text: kalpe kalpe kṣayotpattyā kṣīyante nu prajādayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In every kalpa, through destruction and arising, are creatures and the rest indeed diminished and produced?

children.text: śrutiḥ smṛtiḥ sadācāro yaḥ kaścid vedakartṛkaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>śruti</s>, <s>smṛti</s>, good custom, and whatever is founded on the Veda,

children.text: vedāḥ smṛtā brāhmaṇādau dharmā manvādibhiḥ sadā ||
children.translated_text: the Vedas and the dharmas beginning with the brāhmaṇas are always remembered by <s>Manu</s> and the others.

children.text: dānaṃ kaliyuge dharmaḥ kartāraṃ ca kalau tyajet
children.translated_text: In the <s>Kali-yuga</s>, gift-giving is <s>dharma</s>; in Kali one should also abandon the doer.

children.text: pāpakṛtyaṃ tu tatraiva śāpaṃ phalati varṣataḥ ||
children.translated_text: There a sinful deed, and likewise a curse, bears fruit after a year.
From proper conduct one obtains everything; the six rites, day by day, are:
twilight worship, bathing, recitation, oblation, and worship of gods, guests, and the like.
A brahmin firm in good vows is extraordinary then, and ascetics too are extraordinary then.
A kṣatriya should conquer enemy armies and protect the earth.
For a vaiśya there should be trade, agriculture, and the like; for a śūdra, devotion to the twice-born.
One falls through eating what must not be eaten, through theft, and through intercourse with women who must not be approached.

children.text: kṛṣiṃ kurvandvijaḥ śrāntaṃ balīvardaṃ na vāhayet
children.translated_text: A twice-born man practicing agriculture should not drive an exhausted bull.
For half the day he should perform bathing, yoga, and the like, and should feed brahmins.

children.text: nirvapetpañca yajñāni krūre nindāṃ ca kārayet
children.translated_text: He should offer the five sacrifices and cause blame to be directed at cruelty.
He should not sell sesame or ghee; one connected with slaughter-sacrifice is tainted by sin.

children.text: rājño dattvā tu ṣaḍbhāgaṃ devatānāṃ ca viṃśatim
children.translated_text: Having given a sixth share to the king and a twentieth to the deities,
and a thirty-third to the brahmins, the cultivator is not tainted.
Cultivators, whether kṣatriyas, vaiśyas, or śūdras, are thieves if they do not give at the threshing floor.
A brahmin should be purified in three days during impurity caused by death.
A kṣatriya after ten days, vaiśyas after twelve days, and a śūdra after a month.
A brahmin becomes pure after ten days, and a kṣatriya after twelve days.
A vaiśya after fifteen days, while a śūdra is purified after a month.
Heirs who share one piṇḍa but have separate doors and dwellings,

children.text: janmanā ca vipattau ca bhavetteṣāṃ ca sūtakam
children.translated_text: for them impurity occurs both at birth and at death.

children.text: caturthe daśarātraṃ syāt ṣaṇniśāḥ puṃsi pañcame ||
children.translated_text: In the fourth degree it is ten nights; in the fifth, for a male, six nights.
In the sixth there is purity after four days, and in the seventh after three days.

children.text: deśāntare mṛte bāle sadyaḥ śuddhiryato mṛte ||
children.translated_text: When a child has died in another country, there is immediate purity, because he died away from home.

children.text: ajātadantā ye bālā ye ca garbhād viniḥsṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Children whose teeth have not yet appeared, and those who have come forth from the womb,
for them there is no fire-rite, no piṇḍa, and no water-offering.

children.text: yadi garbho vipadyata sravate vāpi yoṣitaḥ
children.translated_text: If a fetus perishes, or if a woman's miscarriage flows out,
for as many months as the fetus had remained, for that many days there is impurity.

children.text: ā nāmakaraṇāt sadya ā cūḍāntād aharniśam
children.translated_text: Until the naming, purity is immediate; until the tonsure, it lasts a day and night.

children.text: ā vratāttu trirātreṇa tadūrdhvaṃ daśabhir dinaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Until the vow-initiation it lasts three nights; beyond that, ten days.

children.text: ā caturthād bhavet stravaḥ pātaḥ pañcamaṣaṣṭhayoḥ
children.translated_text: Up to the fourth month it is a discharge; in the fifth and sixth it is a miscarriage.
Because of celibacy, the agnihotra, and the avoidance of contact, there is no impurity.
Artisans, craftsmen, physicians, female and male slaves, and servants,
one who maintains the sacred fire, a śrotriya, and a king are declared immediately pure.
The mother is purified after ten days; at childbirth the father is pure after bathing.
Through contact with the woman in childbirth there is birth impurity; after sipping water, the father is pure.
At marriages, festivals, and sacrifices, if impurity from death or birth intervenes,
it is prescribed that only what was previously resolved upon should proceed, and other things should be set aside.
Birth impurity is purified by a death; at a birth, impurity for people is like that caused by death.
For those who die while protecting cows and the like, impurity lasts only one night.
By carrying an unclaimed corpse one is purified through prāṇāyāma.
From carrying the corpse of a śūdra, one becomes impure for three nights.
For one who kills himself, takes poison, hangs himself, or is bitten by worms, there is no funeral rite.

children.text: gohataṃ kṛmidaṣṭaṃ ca spṛṣṭvā kṛcchreṇa śudhyati ||
children.translated_text: Having touched one killed by a cow or bitten by worms, one is purified by a kṛcchra penance.
A wife who abandons a blameless, unfallen husband in his youth

children.text: saptajanma bhavetstrītvaṃ vaidhavyaṃ ca punaḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: will have female birth for seven lives and widowhood again and again.

children.text: bālahatyā tvagamanād ṛtau ca strī tu sūkari
children.translated_text: For killing a child, for illicit intercourse, and for intercourse in the menstrual season, a woman becomes a sow.
Women who approach forbidden men while observing vows are fallen and excluded from drinking-water rites.

children.text: aurasaḥ kṣetrajaḥ putraḥ pitṛjau piṇḍadau pituḥ
children.translated_text: The legitimate son and the kṣetraja son, born for the father, give piṇḍas to the father.
In the case of parivedana there is a kṛcchra penance, and for the girl there is likewise a kṛcchra.
The giver should perform an atikṛcchra, and the hotṛ should perform a cāndrāyaṇa.
In the case of hunchbacks, dwarfs, impotent men, stammerers, and dullards,
and those blind from birth, deaf, or mute, there is no fault in parivedana.

children.text: naṣṭe mṛte pravrajite klībe vā patite patau ||
children.translated_text: When the husband is lost, dead, renounced, impotent, or fallen,
in these five calamities another husband is prescribed for women.
A woman who dies together with her husband dwells in heaven for as many years as there are hairs.
A man bitten by a dog or the like becomes pure through recitation of the <s>Gāyatrī</s>.
A brahmin who maintained the sacred fire but was killed by cāṇḍālas and the like should be burned with common fire.

children.text: kṣīraiḥ prakṣālya tasyāsthi svāgninā mantrato dahet
children.translated_text: After washing his bones with milk, one should burn them with his own sacred fire, accompanied by mantras.

children.text: pravāse tu mṛte bhūyaḥ kṛtvā kuśamayaṃ dahet ||
children.translated_text: But if he dies abroad, one should again make an effigy of kuśa grass and burn it.
Having spread it on a black antelope skin, with six hundred pieces of palāśa wood,

children.text: śamīṃ śiśre viniḥkṣipya araṇiṃ vṛṣaṇe kṣipet ||
children.translated_text: placing śamī wood on the penis, one should place the araṇi at the testicles.
The fuel-stick should be in the right hand, and likewise the upabhṛt ladle in the left hand.

children.text: pārśve tūlūkhalaṃ dadyātpṛṣṭhe tu musalaṃ dadet ||
children.translated_text: He should place the mortar at the side and put the pestle at the back.
Placing a stone on the chest, and rice, ghee, and sesame in the mouth,

children.text: śrotre ca prokṣaṇīṃ dadyād ājyasthālīṃ ca cakṣuṣoḥ ||
children.translated_text: he should put the sprinkling vessel at the ear and the ghee-pot at the eyes.

children.text: karṇe netre mukhe ghrāṇe hiraṇyaśakalān kṣipet
children.translated_text: He should place pieces of gold in the ears, eyes, mouth, and nose.
Through the implements of the agnihotra, there is attainment of <s>Brahmaloka</s>.
With the words "to that heavenly world, svāhā," there is one oblation of ghee.
For geese, sarasa cranes, krauñca birds, cakravāka ducks, and domestic fowl,
and for one who kills a peacock or a ram, purity comes after a day and night.
Having killed any birds at all, one is purified after a day and night.
Having killed any quadrupeds at all, he should fast for a day and night and recite.
Having killed a śūdra, one should perform a kṛcchra penance; but the killer of a vaiśya should perform an atikṛcchra.
For killing a kṣatriya, one should perform a cāndrāyaṇa; for killing a Brahmin, one should undertake the penance of twenty-two or thirty-two parts.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe parāśaroktadharmanirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the hundred-and-seventh chapter, named "The Description of Dharma as Taught by <s>Parāśara</s>."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
I shall declare the essence of policy, resting on the science of wealth and related teachings,
beneficial for kings and others, meritorious, and bestowing long life, heaven, and the like.

children.text: sadbhiḥ saṅgaṃ prakurvīta siddhikāmaḥ sadā naraḥ
children.translated_text: A person who desires success should always cultivate association with good people.
From bad people there is no benefit here in this world or in the next.
One should avoid petty conversation, and should rather seek the sight of one who is not wicked.
One should avoid conflict with a friend and affection for one who serves an enemy.
By instructing a foolish pupil, by maintaining a wicked woman,
and by association with wicked people, even a learned man sinks down.

children.text: brāhmaṇaṃ bāliśaṃ kṣatram ayoddhāraṃ viśaṃ jaḍam
children.translated_text: A foolish Brahmin, a kṣatriya who does not fight, a dull vaiśya,
and a śūdra furnished with letters: these one should avoid from afar.

children.text: kālena ripuṇā sandhiḥ kāle mitreṇa vigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: At the proper time there may be alliance with an enemy, and at the proper time conflict with a friend.
The learned man waits for the right time, relying on the cause and purpose of the task.

children.text: kālaḥ pacati bhūtāni kālaḥ saṃharate prajāḥ
children.translated_text: Time ripens beings; Time withdraws creatures.

children.text: kālaḥ supteṣu jāgarti kālo hi duratikramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Time remains awake among those who sleep, for Time is hard to pass beyond.

children.text: kāleṣu harate vīryaṃ kāle garbhe ca vartate
children.translated_text: In due times Time carries off strength, and in time it abides in the womb.

children.text: kālo janayate sṛṣṭiṃ punaḥ kālo 'pi saṃharet ||
children.translated_text: Time brings forth creation, and again Time also withdraws it.
Time, whose movement is subtle, is eternal, and here it is understood as twofold:
through its course in gross collections, and through its other, subtle course.
<s>Bṛhaspati</s> spoke this essence of policy to the lord of the gods,
by which <s>Indra</s> became all-knowing and, having slain the Daityas, attained heaven.
Royal sages and Brahmins should perform worship of gods, Brahmins, and the like.
One should sacrifice with the horse sacrifice, which destroys great sins.

children.text: uttamaiḥ saha sāṃgatyaṃ paṇḍitaiḥ saha satkathām
children.translated_text: Keeping company with the excellent, holding good conversation with the learned,
and making friendship with those who are not greedy, a man does not sink down.
Slander, another's property or affair, ridicule, another man's wife,

children.text: paraveśmani vāsaṃ ca na kurvīta kadācana ||
children.translated_text: and dwelling in another's house: these one should never do.
Even a stranger who is beneficial is kin; even kin who is harmful is a stranger.
A disease born in the body is harmful; medicine from the forest is beneficial.

children.text: sa bandhuryo hite yuktaḥ sa pitā yastu poṣakaḥ
children.translated_text: He is kin who is engaged in one's welfare; he is a father who nourishes.

children.text: tanmitraṃ yatra viśvāsaḥ sa deśo yatra jīvyate ||
children.translated_text: That is a friend in whom there is trust; that is a country where one can live.

children.text: sa bhṛtyo yo vidheyastu tadbījaṃ yatprarohati
children.translated_text: He is a servant who is obedient; that is seed which sprouts.

children.text: sā bhāryā yā priyaṃ brūte sa putro yastu jīvati ||
children.translated_text: She is a wife who speaks what is pleasant; he is a son who lives.

children.text: sa jīvati guṇā yasya dharmo yasya sa jīvati
children.translated_text: He lives who has virtues; he lives who has <s>dharma</s>.
For one who is devoid of virtue and <s>dharma</s>, his life is fruitless.

children.text: sā bhāryā yā gṛhe dakṣā sā bhāryā yā priyaṃvadā
children.translated_text: She is a wife who is skillful in the house; she is a wife who speaks pleasantly.

children.text: sā bhāryā yā patiprāṇā sā bhāryā yā pativratā ||
children.translated_text: She is a wife whose life is her husband; she is a wife who is devoted to her husband.

children.text: nityaṃ snātā sugandhā ca nityaṃ ca priyavādinī
children.translated_text: Always bathed and fragrant, and always speaking pleasantly,
eating little, speaking little, and constantly joined with auspicious acts,
constantly rich in <s>dharma</s>, and constantly dear to her husband,
constantly pleasing in speech, and constantly desirous at the proper season,
endowed with acts such as these and increasing every good fortune:

children.text: yasyedṛśī bhaved bhāryā sa devendro na mānuṣaḥ ||
children.translated_text: he whose wife is like this is <s>Devendra</s>, not a mere human being.
He whose wife has deformed eyes, is foul, and delights in quarrels,

children.text: uttarottaravādā syā sā jarā na jarā jarā ||
children.translated_text: and is one who answers back more and more: she is old age; ordinary old age is not old age.
He whose wife is attached to another and longs for another's house,

children.text: kukriyā tyaktalajjā ca sā jarā na jarā jarā ||
children.translated_text: whose conduct is bad and who has abandoned shame: she is old age; ordinary old age is not old age.
He whose wife knows virtues and follows her husband,

children.text: alpālpena tu saṃtuṣṭā sā priyā na priyā priyā ||
children.translated_text: content even with very little: she is beloved; no one else is truly beloved.
A wicked wife, a deceitful friend, and a servant who answers back,

children.text: sasarpe ca gṛhe vāso mṛtyureva na saṃśayaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and dwelling in a house with a snake: these are death itself, without doubt.
Abandon association with bad people; cultivate the company of the good.
Do merit day and night; constantly remember impermanence.

children.text: vyālīkaṇṭhapradeśā hyapi ca phaṇabhṛdbhāṣaṇā yā ca raudrī yā kṛṣṇā vyākulāgī rudhiranayanasaṃvyākulā vyāghrakalpā
children.translated_text: A woman who is dreadful, snake-necked, speaking like a hooded serpent, fierce, dark, with disordered limbs, with blood-red eyes in turmoil, and resembling a tiger,

children.text: krodhe yaivogravaktrā sphuradanalaśikhā kākajihvā karālā sevyā na strī vidagdhā parapuragamanā bhrāntacittā viraktā ||
children.translated_text: who in anger has a terrible face, with blazing fire-like flashes and a fearsome crow-like tongue: such a clever woman, going to another man's place, confused in mind and estranged, is not to be attended.

children.text: saktiḥ sutoke sukṛtaṃ kṛtaghne śatiṃ ca vahnau haime
children.translated_text: Attachment to a child, a good deed toward an ingrate, and coldness in fire or heat in snow
may perhaps arise by the force of fate; but passion for courtesans should never arise.

children.text: bhujaṅgame veśmani dṛṣṭidṛṣṭe vyādhau cikitsāvinivartite ca
children.translated_text: When a serpent has been seen face to face in the house, and when a disease has been turned back by treatment,

children.text: dehe ca bālyādivayo'nvite ca kālāvṛto 'sau labhate dhṛtiṃ kaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when the body has passed through the ages beginning with childhood, who, enveloped by Time, obtains firmness?

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bṛhaspatiproktanītisāranirūpaṇaṃ nāmāṣṭottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the hundred-and-eighth chapter, named "The Description of the Essence of Policy as Taught by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>."
<s>Sūta</s> said:
One should preserve wealth for the sake of calamity; one should preserve one's wife even by means of wealth.
One should always preserve oneself, even by means of wife and wealth.

children.text: tyajed ekaṃ kulasyārthe grāmasyārthe kulaṃ tyajet
children.translated_text: One should abandon one person for the sake of the family; for the sake of the village, one should abandon the family.
For the sake of the country one should abandon the village; for the sake of oneself one should abandon the earth.

children.text: varaṃ hi narake vāso na tu duścarite gṛhe
children.translated_text: Better indeed is dwelling in hell than in a house of bad conduct.
Sin is exhausted from hell, but one does not get free from a bad house.
A wise man moves with one foot and stands with one.

children.text: na parīkṣya paraṃ sthānaṃ pūrvamāyatanaṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: One should not abandon a former abode before examining another place.
One should leave a country of bad conduct; one should leave a dwelling beset by trouble.
One should abandon a miserly king; one should abandon a friend full of deceit.

children.text: arthena kiṃ kṛpaṇahastagatena kena jñānena kiṃ bahuśaṭhāgrahasaṃkulena
children.translated_text: What use is wealth fallen into the hand of a miser? What use is knowledge crowded with much obstinate deceit?

children.text: rūpeṇa kiṃ guṇaparākramavarjitena mitreṇa kiṃ vyasanakālaparāṅmukhena ||
children.translated_text: What use is beauty without virtue and valor? What use is a friend who turns away in a time of calamity?

children.text: adṛṣṭapūrvā bahavaḥ sahāyāḥ sarve padasthasya bhavanti mitrāḥ
children.translated_text: Many helpers, never seen before, all become friends of a man who is in office.
But for one deprived of wealth and fallen from office, even his own kinsman becomes an enemy at the wrong time.

children.text: āpatsu mitraṃ jānī yādraṇe śūraṃ rahaḥ śucim
children.translated_text: One should know a friend in misfortunes, a hero in battle, and a pure person in private.

children.text: bhāryā ca vibhave kṣīṇe durbhikṣe ca priyātithim ||
children.translated_text: One should know a wife when prosperity has dwindled, and a beloved guest in famine.

children.text: vṛkṣaṃ kṣīṇaphalaṃ tyajanti vihagāḥ śuṣkaṃ saraḥ sārasā nirdravyaṃ puruṣaṃ tyajanti gaṇikā bhraṣṭaṃ nṛpaṃ mantriṇaḥ
children.translated_text: Birds abandon a tree whose fruit is exhausted; cranes abandon a dried-up lake; courtesans abandon a man without money; ministers abandon a fallen king.

children.text: puṣpaṃ paryuṣitaṃ tyajanti madhupāḥ dagdhaṃ vanāntaṃ mṛgāḥ sarvaḥ kāryavaśājjano hi ramate kasyāsti ko vallabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Bees abandon a flower that is stale, and deer abandon a burned forest. Everyone indeed delights according to his own purpose; who is dear to whom?
A greedy man should be managed by giving wealth, and a praiseworthy man by the gesture of folded hands.
A fool should be managed by following his wishes, and a learned man by speaking the truth as it is.

children.text: sadbhāvena hi tuṣyanti devāḥ satpuruṣā dvijāḥ
children.translated_text: The gods, good men, and twice-borns are pleased by sincere disposition.
Others are pleased by food and drink, while the learned are pleased by honor and gifts.
One should deal with a superior by bowing down, and with a rogue by division.
One should deal with a low person by a small gift, and with an equal by equal displays of strength.

children.text: yasya yasya hi yo bhāvas tasya tasya hitaṃ vadan
children.translated_text: Whatever disposition each person has, by speaking what is beneficial to that person
and entering into it, an intelligent man should quickly bring him under his own control.

children.text: nadīnāṃ ca nakhīnāṃ ca śṛṅgiṇāṃ śastrapāṇinām
children.translated_text: In rivers, in those with claws, in those with horns, and in men holding weapons,

children.text: viśvāso naiva gantavyaḥ strīṣu rājakuleṣu ca ||
children.translated_text: trust should never be placed, nor in women or royal households.
Loss of wealth, mental pain, misconduct in the house,
deception, and insult: a wise man should not make these public.
Association with base and wicked people, excessive separation or over-familiarity,
affection, and residence in another's house destroy the good conduct of women.

children.text: kasya doṣaḥ kule nāsti vyādhinā ko pīḍitaḥ
children.translated_text: In whose family is there no fault? Who is not afflicted by disease?

children.text: kena na vyasanaṃ prāptaṃ śriyaḥ kasya nirantarāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Who has not met with misfortune? Whose fortunes are uninterrupted?

children.text: ko 'rthaṃ prāpya na garvito bhuvi naraḥ kasyāpadonāgatāḥ strībhiḥ kasya na khaṇḍitaṃ bhuvi manaḥ ko nāma rājñāṃ priyaḥ
children.translated_text: What man on earth, having gained wealth, has not become proud? Whose calamities have not come? Whose mind on earth has not been broken by women? Who, indeed, is dear to kings?

children.text: kaḥ kālasya na gocarāntaragataḥ ko 'rtho gato gauravaṃ ko vā durjanavāgurānipatitaḥ kṣemeṇa yātaḥ pumān ||
children.translated_text: Who has not come within the range of time? What wealth has come to dignity? What man, fallen into the snare of the wicked, has gone away safely?
That action in which there is no friend, kinsman, or relative, and in which one's own judgment is absent,
and in which, even when accomplished, the rise of a result is not seen,

children.text: vipattau ca mahadduḥkhaṃ tad budhaḥ kathamācaret ||
children.translated_text: and in misfortune there is great suffering: how could a wise man undertake it?

children.text: yasmindeśe na saṃmānaṃ na prītirna ca bāndhavāḥ
children.translated_text: That country where there is no respect, no affection, and no relatives,

children.text: na ca vidyāgamaḥ kaścittaṃ deśaṃ parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: and no acquisition of learning at all: one should completely avoid that country.

children.text: dhanasya yasya rājato bhayaṃ na cāsti caurataḥ
children.translated_text: That wealth for which there is no fear from the king and none from thieves,

children.text: mṛtaṃ ca yanna mucyate samarjayasva taddhanam ||
children.translated_text: and which is not released when one is dead: acquire that wealth.

children.text: yadarjitaṃ prāṇaharaiḥ pariśramairmṛtasya taṃ vai vibhajanti rikthinaḥ
children.translated_text: What has been gained by life-destroying exertions is divided by heirs when the man is dead.

children.text: kṛtaṃ ca yadduṣkṛtamarthalipsayā tadeva doṣopahatasya yautukam ||
children.translated_text: And whatever evil deed was done from desire for wealth, that alone is the dowry of the man struck down by fault.
For a miser, wealth accumulated and stored away, handled again and again,
like that of a mouse, is only for misery.
Naked, addicted, harsh men, with hands marked by skulls,
show here to the world this sort of fruit of not giving.

children.text: śikṣayanti ca yācante dehīti kṛpaṇā janāḥ
children.translated_text: And beggars instruct miserly people when they ask, 'Give!'
'This is the condition of not giving; may you too not become like this.'

children.text: saṃcitaṃ kratuśatairna yujyate yācitaṃ guṇavate na dīyate
children.translated_text: Wealth collected even by hundreds of sacrifices is not enjoyed; when requested, it is not given to a worthy man.
Therefore wealth guarded by a miser comes to be used in the house of thieves and kings.

children.text: na devebhyo na viprebhyo bandhubhyo naiva cātmane
children.translated_text: The wealth of a miser goes neither to the gods, nor to Brahmins, nor to relatives, nor even to himself,
but to fire, thieves, and kings.
May you never have those riches that come with extreme hardship,
with transgression of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), or by bowing down before an enemy.
The destruction of learning is lack of practice; the destruction of women is dirty clothing.
For diseases, digested food is destruction; for an enemy, destruction is expansiveness of stratagem.
Punishment is the killing of a thief; little speech is the killing of a bad friend.
A separate bed is the killing of women, and lack of invitation is the killing of a Brahmin.

children.text: durjanāḥ śilpino dāsā duṣṭāśca paṭahāḥ striyaḥ
children.translated_text: Wicked people, craftsmen, servants, bad drums, and women

children.text: tāḍitā mārdavaṃ yānti na te satkārabhājanam ||
children.translated_text: become gentle when beaten; they are not fit recipients of respectful treatment.
One should know servants when they are sent on a task, and relatives when misfortune arrives.

children.text: mitramāpadi kāle ca bhāryāṃ ca vibhavakṣaye ||
children.translated_text: One should know a friend at a time of distress, and a wife when prosperity is lost.

children.text: strīṇāṃ dviguṇa āhāraḥ prajñā caiva caturguṇā
children.translated_text: For women, food is twice as much, and intelligence is four times as much;
enterprise is six times as much, and desire is remembered as eight times as much.

children.text: na svapnena jayennidrāṃ na kāmena striyaṃ jayet
children.translated_text: One should not conquer sleep by sleeping, nor conquer a woman by desire.

children.text: na cendhanairjayedvahniṃ na madyena tṛṣāṃ jayet ||
children.translated_text: One should not conquer fire with fuel, nor conquer thirst with liquor.
With meat-rich meals, rich foods, liquors, fragrant unguents,
charming garments, and garlands, desire expands among women.
Even in celibacy, the activity of <s>Manmatha</s> is to be spoken of as having arrived:

children.text: hṛdyaṃ hi puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā yoniḥ praklidyate striyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: for when a woman sees a pleasing man, her womb becomes moist.

children.text: suveṣaṃ puruṣaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhrātaraṃ yadi vā sutam
children.translated_text: Seeing a well-dressed man, whether a brother or a son,

children.text: yoniḥ klidyati nārīṇāṃ satyaṃ satyaṃ hi śaunaka ||
children.translated_text: the womb of women becomes moist; truly, truly, O <s>Śaunaka</s>.

children.text: nadyaśca nāryaśca samasvabhāvāḥ svatantrabhāve gamanādike ca
children.translated_text: Rivers and women have the same nature, in freedom of movement and the like;

children.text: toyaiśca doṣaiśca nipātayanti nadyo hi kūlāni kulāni nāryaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with waters and with faults they bring things down: rivers bring down banks, and women bring down families.

children.text: nadī pātayate kūlaṃ nārī pātayate kulam
children.translated_text: A river makes a bank fall; a woman makes a family fall.

children.text: nārīṇāṃ ca nadīnāṃ ca svacchandā lalitā gatiḥ ||
children.translated_text: For women and for rivers the course is free-willed and graceful.
Fire is not satisfied with wood, nor the great ocean with rivers;
Death is not satisfied with all beings, nor are doe-eyed women with men.
There is no satiety with the well-bred, with desired things, and with those who speak pleasantly,

children.text: sukhānāṃ ca sutānāṃ ca jīvitasya varasya ca ||
children.translated_text: nor with pleasures, sons, life, or a fine husband.

children.text: rājā na tapto dhanasaṃcayena na sāgarastṛptimagājjalena
children.translated_text: A king is not sated by the accumulation of wealth, nor does the ocean reach satiety with water;

children.text: na paṇḍitastṛpyati bhāṣitena tṛptaṃ na cakṣurnṛpadarśanena ||
children.translated_text: a learned man is not satisfied with discourse, and the eye is not satisfied with seeing a king.
For the best of men, whose lives are earned by their own action and <s>dharma</s> (right conduct), who are always devoted to the scriptures and to their wives,
who have conquered their senses and love guests, liberation is present even at home.
Women agreeable to the mind, beautiful and well adorned,
and residence on the tops of palaces would be heaven for one of auspicious deeds.

children.text: na dānena na mānena nārjavena na savayā
children.translated_text: Not by gifts, not by honor, not by straightforwardness, not by service,

children.text: na śastreṇa na śāstreṇa sarvathā viṣamā striyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: not by weapons and not by scripture: in every way women are difficult.
Knowledge comes gradually, wealth gradually, and one should climb a mountain gradually;

children.text: śanaiḥ kāmaṃ ca dharmaṃ ca pañcaitāni śanaiḥ śanaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: desire and <s>dharma</s> too come gradually: these five are attained little by little.
Worship of the gods and the like is lasting; gifts to Brahmins are lasting;

children.text: śāśvataṃ saguṇā vidyā suhṛnmitraṃ ca śāśvatam ||
children.translated_text: knowledge joined with good qualities is lasting, and a good-hearted friend is lasting.

children.text: ye bālabhāvānna paṭhanti vidyāṃ ye yauvanasthā hy adhanātmadārāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who do not study learning in childhood, and those who in youth have neither wealth, self-possession, nor wives,

children.text: te śocanīyā iha jīvaloke manuṣyarūpeṇa mṛgāścaranti ||
children.translated_text: are pitiable here in the world of the living; in human form they wander like animals.
A servant of scripture should not set his mind on eating while studying;
a seeker of learning should go even very far away, swift as <s>Garuḍa</s>.

children.text: ye bālabhāve na paṭhanti vidyāṃ kāmāturā yauvananaṣṭavittāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who do not study learning in childhood, who are love-stricken in youth and have lost their wealth,

children.text: te vṛddhabhāve paribhūyamānāḥ saṃdahyamānāḥ śiśire yathābjam ||
children.translated_text: being despised in old age, burn as a lotus does in winter.

children.text: tarke 'pratiṣṭhā śrutayo vibhinnāḥ nāsāvṛṣiryasya mataṃ na bhinnam
children.translated_text: Reasoning has no firm foundation; the revealed texts are divided; there is no sage whose opinion is not different.

children.text: dharmasya tattvaṃ nihitaṃ guhāyāṃ mahājano yena gataḥ sa panthāḥ ||
children.translated_text: The truth of <s>dharma</s> is hidden in a cave; the path is that by which the great people have gone.
By outward forms, gestures, gait, activity, and speech,
and by changes of the eyes and face, the inward mind is recognized.

children.text: anuktamapyūhati paṇḍito janaḥ pareṅgitajñānaphalā hi buddhayaḥ
children.translated_text: A learned person infers even what has not been said, for minds bear fruit in the knowledge of another's gestures;

children.text: udīrito 'rthaḥ paśunāpi gṛhyate hayāśca nāgāśca vahanti darśitam ||
children.translated_text: a meaning that has been uttered is grasped even by an animal, and horses and elephants carry out what has been indicated.

children.text: arthādbhraṣṭastīrthayātrāṃ tu gacchetsatyādbhraṣṭo rauravaṃ vai vrajecca
children.translated_text: One fallen from wealth should go on pilgrimage; one fallen from truth surely goes to <s>Raurava</s>;

children.text: yogādbhraṣṭaḥ satyaghṛtiṃ ca gacchedrājyādbhraṣṭo mṛgayāyāṃ vrajecca ||
children.translated_text: one fallen from yoga should go to <s>satyaghṛti</s>, and one fallen from sovereignty should go to hunting.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bṛhadṛnītisāre navottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first section called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Bṛhadnītisāra</s>, the one-hundred-ninth chapter is completed.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
He who abandons fixed things and pursues unfixed things

children.text: dhruvāṇi tasya naśyanti hyadhruvaṃ naṣṭameva ca ||
children.translated_text: loses the fixed things he has, while the unfixed thing is already lost.

children.text: vāgyantrahīnasya narasya vidyā śastraṃ yathā kāpuruṣasya haste
children.translated_text: The learning of a man lacking the instrument of speech is like a weapon in the hand of a coward;

children.text: na tuṣṭimutpādayate śarīre hyandhasya dārā iva darśanīyāḥ ||
children.translated_text: it produces no satisfaction in the body, like beautiful wives for a blind man.
The power to eat when there is food, and the power of love with excellent women,
and the power to give when there is wealth: these are not the fruit of slight austerity.
The Vedas have the <s>agnihotra</s> as their fruit; good character and conduct have an auspicious fruit.
Wives have love and sons as their fruit; wealth has giving and enjoyment as its fruit.
A wise man should choose a maiden from a good family, even if she is ugly;
he should never choose one from no good family, even if she is beautiful and has shapely hips.

children.text: arthenāpi hi kiṃ tena yasyānarthe tu saṃgatiḥ
children.translated_text: What use is even that wealth whose association is with misfortune?

children.text: ko hi nāma śikhājātaṃ pannagasya maṇiṃ haret ||
children.translated_text: Who indeed would take a jewel born on the crest of a serpent?
An oblation may be taken even from a bad family, and a good saying even from a child;
gold may be taken from filth, and a jewel of a woman even from a bad family.
Nectar should be taken even from poison, and gold even from filth;
excellent learning even from a low person, and a jewel of a woman even from a bad family.

children.text: na rājñā saha mitratvaṃ na sarpo nirviṣaḥ kvacit
children.translated_text: There is no friendship with a king; a serpent is never without poison.

children.text: na kulaṃ nirmalaṃ tatra strījano yatra jāyate ||
children.translated_text: There is no stainless family there where womankind is born.
One should appoint a devoted servant to the household, and set a son to his studies;
one should set an enemy among vices, and direct a beloved person toward <s>dharma</s>.
Servants and ornaments are to be employed only in their proper places;

children.text: na hi cūḍāmaṇiḥ pāde śobhate vai kadācana ||
children.translated_text: for a crest-jewel never shines on the foot.
A crest-jewel, the ocean, fire, a bell, and an unbroken garment,
or else a ruler of the earth, whether on the head or, by mistake, on the foot: such is the thought.
Like a cluster of flowers, there are two courses for a high-minded person:

children.text: mūrdhni vā sarvalokānāṃ śīrṣataḥ patito vane ||
children.translated_text: either upon the heads of all people, or fallen from the head in the forest.
If a jewel fit to be set among ornaments of gold is bound in tin,

children.text: na ca virauti na cāpi sa śobhate bhavati yojayiturvacanīyatā ||
children.translated_text: it neither rings out nor shines; the blame belongs to the one who set it there.
Among horses, elephants, iron, wood, stone, garments,
