women, men, and waters, there is a very great difference.
Even when he has been mistreated, a man whose way is firmness cannot have all his virtues crushed.

children.text: adhaḥ khalenāpi kṛtasya vahnernādhaḥ śikhā yāti kadācideva ||
children.translated_text: For the flame of fire, even when it has been pushed downward by a base man, never goes downward.

children.text: na sadaśvaḥ kaśāghātaṃ siṃho na gajagarjitam
children.translated_text: A good horse does not endure the stroke of a whip, a lion does not endure the trumpeting of an elephant,
nor does a hero endure what is prescribed by another, or a terrifying roar.

children.text: yadi vibhavavihīnaḥ pracyuto vāśu daivānna tu khalajanasevāṃ kāṅkṣayennaiva nīcām
children.translated_text: If one has lost prosperity or has quickly fallen through fate, still one should not long for service to base people, nor for anything low.

children.text: na tṛṇamadanakārye sukṣudhārto 'tti siṃhaḥ pibati rudhiramuṣṇaṃ prāyaśaḥ kuñjarāṇām ||
children.translated_text: Even when extremely hungry, a lion does not eat grass for the sake of satisfying hunger; rather, it usually drinks the hot blood of elephants.

children.text: sakṛdduṣṭaṃ ca yo mitraṃ punaḥ saṃdhātumicchati
children.translated_text: He who wishes to make peace again with a friend once corrupted
would take hold of death itself, like a mule taking hold of pregnancy.
Wise men should not disregard the children of an enemy, even when they speak pleasantly.

children.text: tānyeva kāleṣu vipatkarāṇi viṣasya pātrāṇyapi dāruṇāni ||
children.translated_text: In time those very children become bringers of disaster, like terrible vessels of poison.
With an enemy bound by an act of assistance, one should remove an enemy,
just as one removes a thorn stuck in the foot with a thorn held in the hand.
One should never constantly brood over those intent on doing harm.
They will fall by themselves, like trees growing on a riverbank.
Misfortunes appear in the form of benefits, and benefits in the form of misfortunes.

children.text: bhavanti te vināśāya daivāyattasya vai sadā ||
children.translated_text: For one who is dependent on fate, they always come about for his destruction.

children.text: kāryakālocitā pāpā matiḥ saṃjāyate hi vai
children.translated_text: At the proper time for an action, even an evil thought arises,

children.text: sānukūle tu daive śaṃ puṃsaḥ sarvatra jāyate ||
children.translated_text: but when fate is favorable, well-being arises everywhere for a man.
In matters involving the use of wealth, and likewise in the acquisition of learning,

children.text: āhāre vyavahāre ca tyaktalajjaḥ sadā bhavet ||
children.translated_text: in eating and in dealings with others, one should always be free from shame.

children.text: dhaninaḥ śrotriyo rājā nadī vaidyastu pañcamaḥ
children.translated_text: A wealthy man, a learned Brahmin, a king, a river, and a physician as the fifth:

children.text: pañca yatra na vidyante na kuryāttatra saṃsthitim ||
children.translated_text: where these five are not found, one should not take up residence there.
Ordinary social life, fear, shame, courtesy, and a habit of giving:

children.text: pañca yatra na vidyante na tatra divasaṃ vaset ||
children.translated_text: where these five are not found, one should not live there even for a day.
A knower of proper times, a learned Brahmin, a king, a river, and a good man as the fifth:

children.text: ete yatra na vidyante tatra vāsaṃ na kārayet ||
children.translated_text: where these are not found, one should not make a dwelling there.
Knowledge, indeed, has no single fixed resting place, O <s>Śaunaka</s>.

children.text: sarvaḥ sarvaṃ na jānāti sarvajño nāsti kutracit ||
children.translated_text: Everyone does not know everything; there is no omniscient person anywhere.

children.text: na sarvavitkaścidihāsti loke nātyantamūrkho bhuvi cāpi kaścit
children.translated_text: There is no one here in the world who knows everything, nor is there anyone on earth who is utterly foolish.

children.text: jñānena nīcottamamadhyamena yo 'yaṃ vijānāti sa tena vidvān ||
children.translated_text: By the knowledge, whether low, highest, or middling, by which this man understands, by that he is learned.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bṛhadṛ nītisāre daśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part called the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, in the extensive essence of polity, is the one hundred and tenth chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: pārthivasya tu vakṣyāmi bhṛtyānāṃ caiva lakṣaṇam
children.translated_text: Now I shall describe the characteristics of a king and also of his servants.
For a protector of the earth should always examine everything properly.
Devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), he constantly protects the kingdom.
Having conquered enemy armies, he should protect the earth by <s>dharma</s>.
He should gather from flower to flower, but should not cause the root to be cut,
like a maker of garlands in a forest, not like a maker of charcoal.
Those who milk and drink the milk do not consume what has been spoiled.
Foreign kingdoms should be enjoyed by kings, but not damaged.

children.text: nodhaś chindyāttu yo dhenvāḥ kṣārārtho labhate payaḥ
children.translated_text: One seeking milk does not cut off the udder of a cow.

children.text: evaṃ rāṣṭraṃ prayogeṇa pīḍyamānaṃ na vardhate ||
children.translated_text: In the same way, a kingdom oppressed by exactions does not prosper.
Therefore, with every effort, he should protect the earth.
For the protector there will be land, fame, lifespan, renown, and strength.
Having worshiped <s>Viṣṇu</s>, righteous-minded and devoted to the welfare of cows and Brahmins,
a king who has conquered his senses is able to protect his subjects.

children.text: aiśvaryamadhruvaṃ prāpya rājā dharme matiṃ caret
children.translated_text: Having obtained unstable sovereignty, a king should set his mind on <s>dharma</s>.
Prosperity and wealth and the like, not being under one's own control, may perish in a moment.

children.text: satyaṃ manoramāḥ kāmāḥ satyaṃ ramyā vibhūtayaḥ
children.translated_text: It is true that pleasures are delightful, and true that powers and riches are charming,
but life is indeed unsteady, like the flickering movement of a woman's sidelong glance.

children.text: vyāghrīva tiṣṭhati jarā paritarjayantī rogāśca śatrava iva prabhavanti gātre
children.translated_text: Old age stands threatening all around like a tigress, and diseases arise in the body like enemies.

children.text: āyuḥ parisravati bhinnaghaṭādivāmbho loko na cātmahitamācaratīha kaścit ||
children.translated_text: Life leaks away like water from a broken pot, yet no one in this world practices what is for his own good.

children.text: niḥśaṅkaṃ kiṃ manuṣyāḥ kuruta parahitaṃ yuktamagre hitaṃ yanmodadhvaṃ kāminībhirmadanaśarahatā mandamandātidṛṣṭyā
children.translated_text: Why are you unconcerned, O people? Do good to others, what is fitting and beneficial for the future; do not become intoxicated by women wounded by the arrows of love, with their slow, sidelong glances.

children.text: mā pāpaṃ saṃkurudhvaṃ dvijahariparamāḥ saṃbhajadhvaṃ sadaiva āyur niḥśeṣameti skhalati jalaghaṭībhūtamṛtyucchalena ||
children.translated_text: Do not commit sin. Ever worship the Brahmins and <s>Hari</s> as supreme; life goes away entirely, slipping by under the guise of death as a water-clock.
He who regards other men's wives as mothers, others' wealth as clods of earth,

children.text: ātmavat sarvabhūteṣu yaḥ paśyati sa paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all beings as himself: he is a learned man.
For this purpose, O best of Brahmins, rulers desire a kingdom:
that their word may not be obstructed in all their affairs.
For this purpose kings accumulate wealth:
after protecting themselves, that wealth should go to the twice-born.
Through the sound of <s>oṃkāra</s> among Brahmins, by which the kingdom increases,

children.text: sa rājā vardhate yogādvyādhibhiśca na badhyate ||
children.translated_text: that king grows through yoga and is not bound by diseases.
Even sages who are without power accumulate wealth.
How much more then should a protector of the earth, who protects his subjects like sons?
He who has wealth has friends; he who has wealth has kinsmen.

children.text: yasyārthāḥ sa pumāṃlloke yasyārthāḥ sa ca paṇḍitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: He who has wealth is a man in the world; he who has wealth is also learned.

children.text: tyajanti mitrāṇi dhanairvihīnaṃ putrāśca dārāśca suhṛjjanāśca
children.translated_text: Friends abandon a man devoid of wealth, as do sons, wives, and dear companions

children.text: te cārthavantaṃ punarāśrayanti hyartho hi loke puruṣasya bandhuḥ ||
children.translated_text: And they again resort to a man possessed of wealth, for wealth in this world is a man's kinsman.

children.text: andhā hi rājā bhavati yastu śāstravivarjitaḥ
children.translated_text: A king who is without śāstra is indeed blind.

children.text: andhaḥ paśyati cāreṇa śāstrahīno na paśyati ||
children.translated_text: A blind man sees by means of a spy; one without śāstra does not see.
He whose sons, servants, ministers, and priests

children.text: indriyāṇi prasuptāni tasya rājyaṃ ciraṃ na hi ||
children.translated_text: have their senses asleep: his kingdom does not last long.
He by whom these three have been won, sons, servants, and kinsmen,
by him the earth bounded by the four oceans has been conquered equally with kings.
A king who transgresses what is joined with śāstra and what is joined with reason,

children.text: sahi naśyati vai rājā iha loke paratra ca ||
children.translated_text: that king indeed perishes both in this world and in the next.

children.text: manastāpaṃ na kurvīta āpadaṃ prāpya pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: A king should not make mental distress for himself when he has met with calamity.

children.text: samabuddhiḥ prasannātmā prasannātmā sukhaduḥkhe samo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: With balanced understanding and a clear mind, a clear-minded man should be the same in pleasure and pain.
Steadfast men, when they meet hardship, do not become despondent.

children.text: praviśya vadanaṃ rāhoḥ kiṃ nodati punaḥ śaśī ||
children.translated_text: Having entered the mouth of <s>Rāhu</s>, does the moon not rise again?

children.text: dhigdhik śarīrasukhalālitamānaveṣu mā khedayeddhanakṛśaṃ hi śarīrameva
children.translated_text: Fie, fie on men pampered by bodily pleasure; one should not distress the body itself when it has become thin through poverty.

children.text: saddārakā hyadhanapāṇḍusutāḥ śrutā hi duḥkhaṃ vihāya punareva sukhaṃ prapannāḥ ||
children.translated_text: For noble children, even the poor sons of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, are heard to have abandoned misery and attained happiness again.
Having looked after the science of the gandharvas, music, and groups of courtesans,
the king should protect in the world the sciences of archery and arthaśāstra.

children.text: kāraṇena vinā bhṛtye yastu kupyati pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: A king who becomes angry with servants without cause
takes hold of a poisonous madness released by a black snake.
He should restrain his gaze from fickleness, and he should restrain false speech

children.text: mānave śrotriye caiva bhṛtyavarge sadaiva hi ||
children.translated_text: among ordinary men, among Vedic Brahmins, and likewise always among the class of servants.
A king who acts playfully, proud of servants and kinsmen,
is always quickly overpowered by enemies in matters of rule.

children.text: huṅkāre bhṛkuṭīṃ naiva sadā kurvīta pārthivaḥ
children.translated_text: A king should never constantly make a frown or angry snort.

children.text: vinā doṣeṇa yo bhṛtyān rājādhamaṇa śāsti ca
children.translated_text: The base king who punishes servants without any fault
should abandon in this world playful pleasures and enjoyments, O lord of earth.
Enemies set in conflict are subdued by those given to comfort.

children.text: udyogaḥ sāhasaṃ dhairyaṃ buddhiḥ śaktiḥ parākramaḥ
children.translated_text: Enterprise, daring, courage, intelligence, power, and valor:
when a man's energy is sixfold in this way, even a god is wary of him.

children.text: udyogena kṛte kārye siddhir yasya na vidyate
children.translated_text: When success is not found in a task after effort has been made,

children.text: daivaṃ tasya pramāṇaṃ hi kartavyaṃ pauruṣaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: fate is then the authority; human effort must always be undertaken.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bṛhadṛ nītisāre ekādaśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, called the first section, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Bṛhadṛ Nītisāra</s>, the one hundred and eleventh chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
Servants should be known as of many kinds: highest, lowest, and middle.
They should be appointed according to suitability in the three kinds of tasks.

children.text: bhṛtye parīkṣaṇaṃ vakṣye yasya yasya hi yo guṇaḥ
children.translated_text: I shall explain the testing of servants, according to whatever quality each one has.
I shall declare this matter just as it has been taught.
Just as gold is tested in four ways, by rubbing, cutting, heating, and striking,

children.text: tathā caturbhirbhṛtakaṃ parīkṣayed vatena śīlena kalena karmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: so a hired servant should be tested in four ways: by conduct, character, family, and work.
One endowed with good family, character, and virtues, devoted to truth and <s>dharma</s> (righteous order),
handsome and very agreeable, is appointed superintendent of the treasury.
One who examines value and appearance should be the examiner of jewels.
One who understands strength and weakness is appointed commander of the army.
One who knows the truth of gestures and outward signs, who is strong and pleasing to look at,

children.text: apramādī pramāthī ca pratīhāraḥ sa ucyate ||
children.translated_text: careful and forceful, is called the chamberlain.
Intelligent, eloquent, wise, truthful, and self-controlled,
and conversant with all śāstras: such a good man is the scribe.
Intelligent and thoughtful, and able to observe another's mind,

children.text: krūro yathoktavādī ca eṣa dūto vidhīyate ||
children.translated_text: stern and speaking as instructed: such a one is appointed messenger.
A learned man who knows all smṛti and śāstra, and is self-controlled,
endowed with the virtues of bravery and heroism, is appointed superintendent of justice.
One whose office comes from father and grandfather, who is skilled, learned in śāstra, and truthful,
and who is pure and firm, is called the cook.
One practiced in āyurveda, pleasing to all,
and endowed with long life, character, and virtues, is appointed physician.
One who knows the truth of the Vedas and Vedāṅgas, and is devoted to recitation and oblation,
always intent on giving blessings: such is the royal priest.
A scribe, a reciter, an accountant, and a warder:
if such a one is given to laziness, the king should always remove him from duty.
Double-tongued, causing agitation, cruel, and utterly harsh:
the mouth of a wicked man and of a snake serves only for harm.
A wicked man should be avoided, even though adorned with learning.

children.text: maṇinā bhūṣitaḥ sarpaḥ kimasau na bhayaṅkaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Is a snake adorned with a jewel not frightening?

children.text: akāraṇaviṣkṛtakopadhāriṇaḥ khalādbhayaṃ kasya na nāma jāyate
children.translated_text: From a wicked man who bears anger displayed without cause, for whom indeed does fear not arise?

children.text: viṣaṃ mahāherviṣamasya durvacaḥ saduḥsahaṃ saṃnipatet sadā mukhe ||
children.translated_text: The poison of a great serpent and the harsh speech of such a man always come together in his mouth, very hard to bear.
A servant equal in wealth, equal in power, knowing vulnerable points, and resolute,

children.text: ardharājyaharaṃ bhṛtyaṃ yo hanyātsa na hanyate ||
children.translated_text: who seizes half the kingdom: one who kills such a servant is not killed.
Those who are endowed with bravery, gentle and measured in speech, self-controlled, and truly valorous,

children.text: prāgeva paścādviparītarūpā ye te tu bhṛtyā na hitā bhavanti ||
children.translated_text: but afterward become the opposite of what they were before: such servants are not beneficial.
Servants who are free from laziness, well contented, and ready to give warning,
who are equal in pleasure and pain and steadfast, are rare in the worlds.
And one who is devoid of patience and restraint, cruel-minded, and a slanderer
A pretender, a deceiver, and a rogue, one possessed by greed,

children.text: aśakto bhayabhītaśca rājñā tyaktavya eva saḥ ||
children.translated_text: and one who is incapable and terrified by fear: such a man must indeed be abandoned by the king.
Well-joined missiles and various weapons
should be brought into the fortress; then he should strike down the enemy.
For six months, or else for a year, the ruler should make a treaty;

children.text: paśyan saṃcitam ātmānaṃ punaḥ śatruṃ nipātayet ||
children.translated_text: seeing himself built up in strength, he should then strike down the enemy again.
But the man who appoints fools: for the king all three of these follow,
disgrace, loss of wealth, and falling into hell.

children.text: yat kiṃcit kurute karma śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
children.translated_text: Whatever deed a servant performs, whether auspicious or inauspicious,

children.text: tena sma vardhate rājā sūkṣmato bhṛtyakāryataḥ ||
children.translated_text: by that the king is affected, even subtly, because of the servant's work.
Therefore the lord of the earth should always appoint a wise man
to the accomplishment of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), desire, and wealth, and for the welfare of cows and Brahmins.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bṛhaspatyuktanītisāre dvādaśottarakaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the former section, in the first part called the Ācārakāṇḍa, in the Nītisāra taught by <s>Bṛhaspati</s>, this is the one-hundred-and-twelfth chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
One should appoint a man endowed with virtues and avoid one who lacks virtue;

children.text: paṇḍitasya guṇāḥ sarve mūrkhe doṣāśca kevalāḥ ||
children.translated_text: all virtues belong to the learned man, but in a fool there are only faults.
One should always sit with good people and form association with good people;

children.text: sadbhirvivādaṃ maitrīṃ ca nāsadbhiḥ kiṃcid ācaret ||
children.translated_text: one may have dispute and friendship with the good, but should do nothing at all with the bad.
With learned men, with disciplined men, with knowers of <s>dharma</s>, and with speakers of truth,

children.text: bandhastho 'pi tiṣṭhecca na tu rājye khalaiḥ saha ||
children.translated_text: one should remain even in bondage, but not in a kingdom together with villains.
Undertakings that leave something in reserve are useful in a difficult affair;
therefore one should have all undertakings carried out with something left in reserve.

children.text: madhuheva duhet sāraṃ kusumaṃ ca na ghātayet
children.translated_text: Like a gatherer of honey he should draw out the essence, but he should not injure the flower;

children.text: vatsāpekṣī duhet kṣīraṃ bhūmiṃ gāṃ caiva pārthivaḥ ||
children.translated_text: expecting the calf, O king, he should milk the milk, and likewise the earth as a cow.
Just as the six-footed bee gathers honey from flowers in due order,

children.text: tathā vittam upādāya rājā kurvīta sañcayam ||
children.translated_text: so the king, taking wealth, should make an accumulation.

children.text: valmīkaṃ madhujālaṃ ca śuklaṇkṣe tu candramāḥ
children.translated_text: An anthill, a honeycomb, the moon in the bright fortnight,

children.text: rājadravyaṃ ca bhaikṣyaṃ ca stokaṃ stokaṃ pravardhate ||
children.translated_text: royal revenue, and alms grow little by little.
Seeing the decline of what has been acquired and the accumulation of what has been given away,
one should make the day not fruitless in acts of giving, study, and ritual work.

children.text: vane 'pi doṣāḥ prabhavanti rāgiṇāṃ gṛhe 'pi pañcendriyanigrahastapaḥ
children.translated_text: Even in a forest, faults arise for those who are passionate; even in a house, restraint of the five senses is austerity.

children.text: akutsite karmaṇi yaḥ pravartate nivṛttarāgasya gṛhaṃ tapovanam ||
children.translated_text: For one who engages in blameless action and whose passion has ceased, the house is a grove of austerity.

children.text: satyena rakṣyate dharmo vidyā yogena rakṣyate
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> is protected by truth; learning is protected by disciplined practice;

children.text: mṛjayā rakṣyate pātraṃ kulaṃ śalina rakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: a vessel is protected by cleaning, and a family is protected by good conduct.

children.text: varaṃ vindhyāṭavyāṃ nivasanamabhuktasya maraṇaṃ varaṃ sarpākīrṇe śayanamatha kūpe nipatanam
children.translated_text: Better residence in the <s>Vindhya</s> forest, death without food, better a bed crowded with snakes, or falling into a well;

children.text: varaṃ bhrāntāvarte sabhayajalamadhye praviśanaṃ na tu svīye pakṣe hi dhanam aṇu dehīti kathanam ||
children.translated_text: better entering fearful water in a whirling eddy, than saying in one's own circle, 'Give me even a particle of wealth.'
When fortune is exhausted, riches decline, not through enjoyment;

children.text: pūrvārjite hi sukṛte na naśyanti kadācana ||
children.translated_text: for when merit has been acquired before, they never perish.

children.text: viprāṇāṃ bhūṣaṇaṃ vidyā pṛthivyā bhūṣaṇaṃ nṛpaḥ
children.translated_text: Learning is the adornment of Brahmins; a king is the adornment of the earth;

children.text: nabhaso bhūṣaṇaṃ candraḥ śīlaṃ sarvasya bhūṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: the moon is the adornment of the sky, and character is the adornment of everyone.

children.text: ete te candratulyāḥ kṣitipatitanayā bhīmasenārjunādyāḥ śūrāḥ satyapratijñā dinakaravapuṣaḥ keśavenopagūḍhāḥ
children.translated_text: These sons of kings, equal to the moon, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and the others, heroes true to their vows, sun-like in body, embraced by <s>Keśava</s>,

children.text: te vai duṣṭagrahasthāḥ kṛpaṇavaśagatā bhaikṣyacaryāṃ prayātāḥ ko vā kasminsamartho bhavati vidhivaśād bhrāmayet karmarekhā ||
children.translated_text: even they, placed under an evil planet and brought under wretched dependence, went to the practice of begging. Who is capable of what, when the line of karma, under fate's power, makes one wander?

children.text: brahmā yena kulālavanniyamito brahmāṇḍabhāṇḍodare viṣṇuryena daśāvatāragahane kṣipto mahāsaṅkaṭe
children.translated_text: By whom <s>Brahmā</s>, like a potter, was confined inside the vessel of the cosmic egg, and by whom <s>Viṣṇu</s> was cast into great danger in the deep tangle of the ten avatāras,

children.text: rudro yena kapālapāṇipuṭake bhikṣāṭanaṃ kāritaḥ sūryo bhrāmyati nityameva gagane tasmai namaḥ karṇaṇe ||
children.translated_text: by whom <s>Rudra</s> was made to wander for alms with a skull in his cupped hands, and by whom the sun ever roams in the sky: homage to that cause.

children.text: dātā balir yācako murārirdānaṃ mahī vipramukhasya madhye
children.translated_text: The giver was <s>Bali</s>, the beggar was <s>Murāri</s>, and the gift was the earth, in the presence of a Brahmin;

children.text: dattvā phalaṃ bandhanameva labdhaṃ namo 'stu te daiva yatheṣṭakāriṇe ||
children.translated_text: having given, the result he obtained was only bondage. Homage to you, O fate, who act as you please.
Even if one's mother should be <s>Lakṣmī</s> and one's father directly <s>Janārdana</s>,

children.text: kubuddhau pratipattiś cet tasmin daṇḍaḥ patetsadā ||
children.translated_text: if one's understanding is fixed on bad judgment, punishment always falls upon him.

children.text: yena yena yathā yadvatpurā karma suniścitam
children.translated_text: Whatever former karma was firmly determined, in whatever way and in whatever manner,
that very thing one later experiences, placed by oneself upon oneself.
Sorrow is fashioned by oneself, and happiness is fashioned by oneself;
beginning with the bed of the womb, one experiences what belongs to a previous body.

children.text: na cāntarikṣe na samudramadhye na parvatānāṃ vivarapraveśe
children.translated_text: Not in the sky, not in the middle of the sea, not by entering the clefts of mountains,

children.text: na mātṛmūrdhni pradhṛtas tathāṅke tyaktuṃ kṣamaḥ karma kṛtaṃ naro hi ||
children.translated_text: nor even when held on a mother's head or in her lap, is a man able to abandon the karma he has done.

children.text: dugastrikūṭaḥ parikhā samudro rakṣāṃsi yodhāḥ paramā ca vṛttiḥ
children.translated_text: The fortress was <s>Trikūṭa</s>, the moat was the ocean, the defenders were rākṣasas, the warriors and resources were supreme,

children.text: śāstraṃ ca vai tūśanasā pradiṣṭaṃ sa rāvaṇaḥ kālavaśādvinaṣṭaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the science was that taught by <s>Uśanas</s>; yet that <s>Rāvaṇa</s> perished under the power of time.

children.text: yasminvayasi yatkāle yaddivā yacca vā niśi
children.translated_text: At whatever age, at whatever time, on whatever day or night,

children.text: yanmuhūrte kṣaṇe vāpi tattathā na tadanyathā ||
children.translated_text: at whatever muhūrta or even moment, it is just so, and not otherwise.
They may go into the sky or enter beneath the earth;
they may hold all the directions, but what has not been given is not obtained.

children.text: purādhītā ca yā vidyā purā dattaṃ ca yaddhanam
children.translated_text: The learning studied before, the wealth given before,

children.text: purā kṛtāni karmāṇi hyagre dhāvanti dhāvataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and the deeds done before run ahead of one who runs.
Karmas are principal here, even when the lunar mansion is right and the planet is auspicious;
though her wedding moment was fixed by <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Jānakī</s> became a vessel of suffering.

children.text: sthūlajaṅgho yadā rāmaḥ śabdagāmī ca lakṣmaṇaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> is thick-shanked, and <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> is one who follows sound,
and when <s>Sītā</s> is thick-haired, those three are vessels of suffering.

children.text: na pituḥ karmaṇā putraḥ pitā vā putrakarmaṇā
children.translated_text: A son does not go by the deed of his father, nor a father by the deed of his son.

children.text: svayaṃ kṛtena gacchanti svayaṃ baddhāḥ svakarmaṇā ||
children.translated_text: They go by what they themselves have done, bound by their own <s>karma</s>.
In bodies produced by <s>karma</s>, diseases of body and mind
fall here like arrows released by strong bowmen.
Though a steadfast man seeks his aim otherwise with an intelligence filled with scripture,
previously made <s>karma</s>, like a master, arranges it otherwise.

children.text: bālo yuvā ca vṛddhaśca yaḥ karoti śubhāśubham
children.translated_text: A child, a youth, or an old man: whatever good or bad deed he does,
he experiences that in that final condition, birth after birth.
Even without seeing it, even though dwelling in a foreign land, a human being
is carried by the wind of the fall of his own <s>karma</s> to the place where its fruit is.

children.text: prāptavyamarthaṃ labhate manuṣyo devo 'pi taṃ vārayituṃ na śaktaḥ
children.translated_text: A man obtains the object that is to be obtained; not even a god is able to prevent it.

children.text: ato na śocāmi na vismayo me lalāṭalekhā na punaḥ prayāti yadasmadīyaṃ na tu tat pareṣām ||
children.translated_text: Therefore I do not grieve, nor is there amazement for me: the writing on the forehead does not return again; what is ours is not another's.

children.text: sarpaḥ kūpe gajaḥ skandhe bila ākhuśca dhāvati
children.translated_text: A serpent is in a well, an elephant on a shoulder, and a mouse runs into a hole;
but who can flee from <s>karma</s> more quickly than a man?
True knowledge does not become small; even when given away it increases,
like water standing in a well, which becomes abundant water indeed.

children.text: ye 'rthā dharmeṇa te satyā ye 'dharmeṇa gatāḥ śriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Those gains that come through <s>dharma</s> are real; riches that have come through <s>adharma</s> are not.
In the world <s>dharma</s> and wealth are great; remembering this, one should act for the sake of wealth.

children.text: annārtho yāni duḥkhāni karoti kṛpaṇo janaḥ
children.translated_text: The sufferings that a miserly man undergoes for the sake of food,

children.text: tānyeva yadi dharmārtho na bhūyaḥ kleśabhājanam ||
children.translated_text: if he underwent those same sufferings for the sake of <s>dharma</s>, he would not again become a vessel of distress.
Of all forms of purity, purity in regard to food is distinguished.

children.text: yo 'nnārthaiḥ śuciḥ śaucānna mṛdā vāriṇā śuciḥ ||
children.translated_text: One who is pure in the means of food is pure by that purity, not pure merely by clay or water.
Truth is purity; purity of mind is purity; restraint of the senses is purity.

children.text: sarvabhūte dayā śaucaṃ jalaśaucaṃ ca pañcamam ||
children.translated_text: Compassion toward all beings is purity, and purity by water is the fifth.

children.text: yasya satyaṃ ca śaucaṃ ca tasya svargo na durlabhaḥ
children.translated_text: For one who has truth and purity, heaven is not hard to obtain.
The man whose speech is truth surpasses even the horse sacrifice.
Even with a thousand clods of earth and a hundred washings with water,
a man of bad conduct, whose mind is ruined by his disposition, is not purified.

children.text: yasya hastau ca pādau ca manaścaiva susaṃyatam
children.translated_text: He whose hands and feet, and whose mind too, are well restrained,
and who has learning, austerity, and fame, obtains the fruit of a sacred bathing-place.
He is not delighted by honors, and he is not angered by insults.
When angry he should not speak harshly: this is the mark of a good man.
No one is satisfied by the timely and beneficial speech

children.text: kāle śrutvā hitaṃ vākyaṃ na kaścitparituṣyati ||
children.translated_text: of a poor man, even if he is intelligent and gentle.
By the force and power of mantras, by wisdom, or by manly effort,
mortals do not obtain what is unobtainable; what lamentation is there in that?
What was obtained by me unasked has gone away again at my sending.
It has gone to the very place from which it came; what lamentation is there in that?
At night there is always a gathering of many birds in one tree.
In the morning they go to different directions; what lamentation is there in that?
Of all those traveling in one caravan and going to the same place,
if one goes ahead quickly alone, what lamentation is there in that?
Beings have unmanifest beginnings and manifest middles, O <s>Śaunaka</s>;
their ends too are unmanifest indeed. What lamentation is there in that?
One whose time has not arrived does not die, even when pierced by a hundred arrows.

children.text: kuśāgreṇa tu saṃspṛṣṭaṃ prāptakālo na jīvati ||
children.translated_text: But one whose time has arrived does not live when merely touched by the tip of a blade of kuśa grass.
One obtains only what is to be obtained and goes only where one is to go.

children.text: prāptavyānyeva prāpnoti duḥkhāni ca sukhāni ca ||
children.translated_text: One receives only what is to be received, both sufferings and pleasures.
A person obtains this and that; what will he accomplish with babbling?

children.text: ācodyamānāni yathā puṣpāṇi ca phalāni ca
children.translated_text: Just as flowers and fruits, though not being urged on,
do not pass beyond their proper time, so too does <s>karma</s> done before.

children.text: śīlaṃ kulaṃ naiva na caiva vidyā jñānaṃ guṇā naiva na bījaśuddhiḥ
children.translated_text: Not character, not family, not learning, not knowledge, not virtues, and not purity of seed:

children.text: bhāgyāni pūrvaṃ tapasārjitāni kāle phalantyasya yathaiva vṛkṣāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fortunes formerly earned by austerity bear fruit for him in time, just like trees.

children.text: tatra mṛtyuryatra hantā tatra śrīryatra sampadaḥ
children.translated_text: Death is there where the killer is; prosperity is there where riches are.

children.text: tatra tatra svayaṃ yāti preryamāṇaḥ svakarmabhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: To each such place a person goes by himself, impelled by his own <s>karma</s>.
A deed done in the past follows its maker,
just as a calf finds its mother among thousands of cows.
So <s>karma</s> done before follows its maker.

children.text: sukṛtaṃ bhuṅkṣva cātmīyaṃ mūḍha kiṃ paritapyase ||
children.translated_text: Enjoy your own good deed, fool; why do you torment yourself?

children.text: yathā pūrvakṛtaṃ karma śubhaṃ vā yadi vāśubham
children.translated_text: As the previously done deed is, whether good or bad,
so it follows its maker in another birth.
A base man sees the mustard-seed-sized faults of others.
His own bilva-fruit-sized faults he does not see, even while seeing them.
For those joined with passion, hatred, and the rest, there is no happiness anywhere, O twice-born one.

children.text: vicārya khalu paśyāmi tatsukhaṃ yatra nirvṛtiḥ ||
children.translated_text: When I consider the matter, I see happiness where there is cessation.

children.text: yatra sneho bhayaṃ tatra sneho duḥkhasya bhājanam
children.translated_text: Where there is affection, there is fear; affection is a vessel of suffering.
Sufferings have affection as their root; when it is abandoned, there is great happiness.
The body itself is the abode of both suffering and happiness.

children.text: jīvitaṃ ca śarīraṃ ca jātyaiva saha jāyate ||
children.translated_text: Life and the body are born together with birth itself.

children.text: sarvaṃ paravaśaṃ duḥkhaṃ sarvam ātmavaśaṃ sukham
children.translated_text: Everything dependent on another is suffering; everything under one's own control is happiness.
One should know this in summary as the characteristic of happiness and suffering.
Immediately after happiness comes suffering, and immediately after suffering comes happiness.
For human beings, happiness and suffering revolve like a wheel.
What has gone has passed away; and if something is yet to be, that too is far off.

children.text: vartamānena varteta na sa śokena bādhyate ||
children.translated_text: One should conduct oneself by what is present; then one is not afflicted by grief.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bṛhadṛ nītisāre trayodaśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one-hundred-and-thirteenth chapter, the great essence of nīti, in the Ācārakāṇḍa of the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, called the first part, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Sūta</s> said:
No one is anyone's friend, and no one is anyone's enemy.
Friends, and likewise enemies, arise only from a cause.
A protection from grief, a protection from fear, a vessel of affection and trust:
by whom was this jewel, the two-syllabled word 'friend,' created?
He by whom the two syllables '<s>Hari</s>' have been uttered even once
has thereby girded himself for the journey toward liberation.

children.text: na mātari na dāreṣu na sodarye na cātmaje
children.translated_text: Neither in one's mother, nor in one's wives, nor in a brother born of the same womb, nor in one's own son
do men have such trust as they have in a friend born by nature.
If one desires lasting affection, one should avoid three faults:
gambling, the use of money, and looking at women in secret.

children.text: mātrā svasrā duhitrā vā na viviktāsano vaset
children.translated_text: One should not sit in a secluded place with one's mother, sister, or daughter,
for the powerful host of the senses drags away even a learned man.
Desire, delighting in what is contrary, is not found among things under one's own control;
as the means, killing, and punishment are, so indeed it follows along.
Even the range of the wind of the cosmic dissolution, of a horse, or of the great ocean

children.text: śakyate prasaro boddhuṃ na hyaraktasya cetasaḥ ||
children.translated_text: can be understood, but not the mind of one who is not attached.

children.text: kṣaṇo nāsti raho nāsti nāsti prārthayitā janaḥ
children.translated_text: There is no moment, there is no privacy, there is no person who solicits;
therefore, O <s>Śaunaka</s>, the chastity of women arises.

children.text: ekaḥ vai sevate nityam anyaś cetapi rocate
children.translated_text: One man may serve constantly, while another is pleasing even in her thought;
and through the nonavailability of men alone a woman becomes devoted to her husband.
The secret things that a mother, distressed by passion, does
should not be pondered by her sons, because they involve lapses from good conduct.

children.text: parādhīnā nidrā parahṛdayakṛtyānusaraṇaṃ sadā helā hāsyaṃ niyatamapi śokena rahitam
children.translated_text: Sleep dependent on another, following the business of another's heart, constant contempt and laughter, and being always free from grief:

children.text: paṇe nyastaḥ kāyo viṭajanakhurairdāritagalo bahūtkaṇṭhavṛtirjagati gaṇikrāyā bahumataḥ ||
children.translated_text: her body staked for a price, her throat torn by the nails of libertines, her livelihood full of longing; in the world the life of a courtesan is much esteemed.

children.text: agnirāpaḥ striyo mūrkhāḥ sarpā rājakulāni ca
children.translated_text: Fire, water, women, fools, snakes, and royal households:
these six, always served by others, take life at once.

children.text: kiṃ citraṃ yadi vedaśāstrakuśalo vipro bhavetpaṇḍitaḥ kiṃ citraṃ yadi daṇḍanītikuśalo rājā bhaveddhārmikaḥ
children.translated_text: What is remarkable if a Brahmin, skilled in Veda and śāstra, becomes learned? What is remarkable if a king, skilled in the science of punishment, becomes righteous?

children.text: kiṃ citraṃ yadi rūpayauvanavatī sādhvī bhavetkāminī taccitraṃ yadi nirdhano 'pi puruṣaḥ pāpaṃ na kuryāt kvacit ||
children.translated_text: What is remarkable if a lovely woman endowed with beauty and youth becomes virtuous? The wonder is if a man, though poor, never commits sin.
One should not give one's own vulnerable point to another, and one should know another's vulnerable point.
One should hide one's limbs like a tortoise and observe the state of another.
Women dwelling at the bottom of the netherworld or stationed on high ramparts,

children.text: yadi no cikurodbhedāllabhyante kaiḥ striyo na hi ||
children.translated_text: if they are not obtained through the sprouting of hair, by whom indeed are women not obtained?
A man of the same ways, knowing one's vital points, sharp, a thorn to his own people,

children.text: na tathā bādhate śatruḥ kṛtavairo bahiḥ sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: does not torment one as much as an enemy who has made hostility and stands outside.

children.text: sa paṇḍito yo hyanuñjayedvai miṣṭena bālaṃ viniyena śiṣṭam
children.translated_text: He is wise who wins over a child with sweetness and a disciplined gentleman with humility,

children.text: arthena nārīṃ tapasā hi devānsarvāṃśca lokāṃśca susaṃgraheṇa ||
children.translated_text: a woman with wealth, the gods by austerity, and all people by good conciliation.

children.text: chalena mitraṃ kaluṣeṇa dharmaṃ paropatāpena samṛddhibhāvanam
children.translated_text: Those who desire a friend by deceit, <s>dharma</s> by impurity, the growth of prosperity by harming others,

children.text: sukhena vidyāṃ puruṣeṇa nārīṃ vāñchanti vai ye na ca paṇḍitāste ||
children.translated_text: learning by comfort, and a woman merely by manhood, they indeed are not wise.
If a foolish man, desiring fruit, cuts down a fruitful tree,
his undertaking is surely fruitless, and he incurs a great fault.

children.text: sadhano hi tapasvī ca dūrato vai kṛtaśramaḥ
children.translated_text: That a wealthy man is an ascetic, that labor done from afar is real effort,
that a wine-drinking woman is chaste: O Brahmin, I do not believe these things.
One should not trust the untrustworthy; one should not even trust a friend completely.
A friend, becoming angry at some time, may reveal every secret.
Trust toward all beings and goodness toward all beings:
one should hide one's own nature; this indeed is the mark of a good man.
In whatever undertaking has been done, one follows the doer;
even while acting in every way, one should maintain courage and understanding.

children.text: vṛddhāḥ striyo navaṃ madyaṃ śuṣkaṃ māṃsaṃ trimūlakam
children.translated_text: Old women, new wine, dry meat, the three-root vegetable,

children.text: rātrau dadhi divā svapnaṃ vidvānṣaṭ parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: curds at night, and sleep by day: a wise man should avoid these six.

children.text: viṣaṃ goṣṭhī daridrasya vṛddhasya taruṇī viṣam
children.translated_text: A gathering is poison for a poor man; a young woman is poison for an old man.

children.text: viṣaṃ kuśikṣitā vidyā ajīrṇe bhojanaṃ viṣam ||
children.translated_text: Badly taught learning is poison; food during indigestion is poison.
Singing is dear to one whose voice is not clear; a high seat is dear to a low man.

children.text: priyaṃ dānaṃ daridrasya bhūnaś ca taruṇī priyā ||
children.translated_text: Giving is dear to a poor man, and a young woman is dear to a decrepit man.

children.text: atyambupānaṃ kaṭhināśanaṃ ca dhātukṣayo vegavidhāraṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Drinking too much water, eating hard food, depletion of the bodily elements, and suppression of urges,

children.text: divāśayo jāgaraṇaṃ ca rātrau ṣaḍbhirnarāṇāṃ nivasanti rogāḥ ||
children.translated_text: sleeping by day and waking at night: by these six, diseases dwell among men.

children.text: bālātapaś cāpy atimaithunaṃ ca śmaśānadhūmaḥ karatāpanaṃ ca
children.translated_text: The young sun, excessive intercourse, smoke from a cremation ground, heating the hands,
and looking at the face of a menstruating woman: these indeed diminish a long life.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ māṃsaṃ striyo vṛddhā bālārkastaruṇaṃ dadhi
children.translated_text: Dry meat, old women, the young sun, fresh curds,

children.text: prabhāte maithunaṃ nidrā sadyaḥ prāṇaharāṇi ṣaṭ ||
children.translated_text: intercourse and sleep in the morning: these six take life at once.

children.text: sadyaḥ pakvaghṛtaṃ drākṣā bālā strī kṣīrabhojanam
children.translated_text: Freshly cooked ghee, grapes, a young woman, a meal of milk,
hot water, and the shade of a tree: these six take life at once.
Well-water, the shade of a banyan tree, and the breasts of women...
In the cold season it should be warm, and in the hot season cool.
Three things quickly produce strength: youth, oil-massage, and good food.

children.text: trayo balaharāḥ sadyo hyadhvā ve maithunaṃ jvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Three things quickly take away strength: a journey, indeed, sexual intercourse, and fever.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ māṃsaṃ payo nityaṃ bhāryāmitraiḥ sahaiva tu
children.translated_text: Dry meat, milk taken constantly, and also eating together with wife and friends

children.text: na bhoktavyaṃ nṛpaiḥ sārdhaṃ viyogaṃ kurute kṣaṇāt ||
children.translated_text: should not be consumed together with kings; it causes separation in an instant.
A person wearing dirty clothes, carrying filth on his teeth, eating too much, and speaking harsh words,

children.text: sūryodaye hyastamaye 'pi śāyinaṃ vimuñcati śrīrapi cakrapāṇinam ||
children.translated_text: and one who sleeps at sunrise and also at sunset, is abandoned by <s>Śrī</s>, even if he were <s>Cakrapāṇin</s>.

children.text: nityaṃ chedas tṛṇānāṃ dharaṇivilekhanaṃ pādayoścāpamārṣṭiḥ dantānāmapyaśaucaṃ malinavasanatā rūkṣatā mūrdhajānām
children.translated_text: Constant cutting of grass, scratching the ground, rubbing the feet, uncleanness of the teeth, wearing soiled garments, and roughness of the hair,

children.text: dve saṃdhye cāpi nidrā vivasanaśayanaṃ grāsahāsātirekaḥ svāṅge pīṭhe ca vādyaṃ nidhanamupanayetkeśavasyāpi lakṣmīm ||
children.translated_text: sleep at both twilights, sleeping naked, excess in mouthfuls and laughter, and drumming on one's own body or seat bring about the destruction of the <s>Lakṣmī</s> even of <s>Keśava</s>.
A head well washed, feet well cleaned, service to a beautiful woman, eating little,
not sleeping naked, and intercourse outside the forbidden lunar days: these six bring back prosperity that has long been lost.

children.text: yasya kasya tu puṣpasya pāṇāḍarasya viśeṣataḥ
children.translated_text: Of any flower whatsoever, and especially of <s>pāṇāḍara</s>,
when it is worn on the head, misfortune is struck back.

children.text: dīpasya paścimā chāyā chāyā śayyāsanasya ca
children.translated_text: The western shadow of a lamp, the shadow of a bed or seat,
and the water-place of a washerman: <s>Lakṣmī</s> remains there.

children.text: bālātapaḥ pretadhūmaḥ strī vṛddhā taruṇaṃ dadhi
children.translated_text: Early sunlight, smoke from a corpse, an old woman, fresh curds,
and dust from a broom should not be resorted to by one who desires long life.
The dust of elephants, horses, chariots, grain,
and cows should be known as auspicious, but that of donkeys, camels, goats, and sheep as inauspicious.
The dust of cows, the dust of grain, and the dust arising from a son's body:
this dust is greatly praised and destroys great sins.
The dust of goats, the dust of donkeys, and the dust from a broom:
this dust is a great evil, producing great guilt.
The wind from a winnowing basket, water from the tips of nails, water used for washing after bathing,
water from the hair, and dust from a broom destroy merit previously acquired.
Between two Brahmins, between a Brahmin and a fire, between a husband and wife, and likewise between masters,

children.text: antareṇa na gantavyaṃ hayasya vṛṣabhasya ca ||
children.translated_text: one should not pass, nor between a horse and a bull.
In women, kings, fires, snakes, Vedic study, service to an enemy,
and the enjoyment of pleasures, what wise man deserves to place trust?
One should not trust the untrustworthy, and one should not trust the trustworthy too much.
The danger that has arisen from trust cuts one down even from the root.

children.text: vairiṇā saha saṃdhāya viśvasto yadi tiṣṭhati
children.translated_text: If a man makes peace with an enemy and then remains trusting,

children.text: sa vṛkṣāgre prasupto hi patitaḥ pratibudhyate ||
children.translated_text: he is like one asleep at the top of a tree: he wakes only after he has fallen.
One should not be excessively gentle, nor one whose actions are excessively cruel.
By gentleness one defeats the gentle, and by harshness the harsh.
One should not be excessively straight, nor likewise excessively gentle.
Straight trees are cut down there, while crooked trees remain standing.

children.text: namanti phalino vṛkṣā namanti guṇino janāḥ
children.translated_text: Trees laden with fruit bend down, and people endowed with virtues bend down.

children.text: śuṣkavṛkṣāśca mūrkhāśca bhidyante na namanti ca ||
children.translated_text: Dry trees and fools break; they do not bend.
Unasked-for sufferings come just as they go away,

children.text: mārjāra iva lumpeta tathā prārthayitāra naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: but a man who asks should seize, like a cat.
Great prosperities always move before and behind the noble man.
With the ignoble it is the opposite; act as you wish.
A counsel heard by six ears is broken; one heard by four ears is preserved.

children.text: dvikarṇasya tu mantrasya brahmāpyantaṃ na budhyate ||
children.translated_text: As for a counsel heard by two ears, even <s>Brahmā</s> does not know its end.

children.text: tayā gavā kiṃ kriyate yā na dogdhrī na garbhiṇī
children.translated_text: What is done with a cow that neither gives milk nor is pregnant?

children.text: ko 'rthaḥ putreṇa jātena yo na vidvānna dhārmikaḥ ||
children.translated_text: What use is a son who has been born but is neither learned nor righteous?
By even a single good son, endowed with knowledge and intelligence,
a family is illuminated by that lion among men, just as the sky is by the moon.
By even a single good tree, flowering and fragrant,

children.text: vanaṃ suvāsitaṃ sarvaṃ suputreṇa kulaṃ yathā ||
children.translated_text: the whole forest is perfumed, just as a family is by a good son.

children.text: eko hi guṇavānputro nirguṇena śatena kim
children.translated_text: One son who has virtue is enough; what use are a hundred without virtue?

children.text: candro hanti tamāṃsyeko na ca jyotiḥsahasrakam ||
children.translated_text: The single moon destroys darkness, not a thousand lights.
One should fondle a son for five years, and discipline him for ten years.

children.text: prāpte tu ṣoḍaśe varṣe putraṃ mitravadācaret ||
children.translated_text: But when he has reached his sixteenth year, one should behave toward one's son like a friend.
When being born he takes away the wife; while growing he takes away wealth.
When dying he takes away life. There is no enemy equal to a son.
Some are tigers with the faces of deer; some are deer with the faces of tigers.
When their true nature is not known, there is distrust at every step.
There is one fault of those who are patient; a second does not arise:
because people think a man endowed with patience is powerless.
One should assent to this very thing: enjoyments are broken in a moment.

children.text: snigdheṣu ca vidagdhasya matayo vai hyanākulāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Among affectionate people, the thoughts of a clever man are indeed unconfused.

children.text: jyeṣṭhaḥ pitṛsamo bhrātā mṛte pitari śaunaka
children.translated_text: An elder brother is equal to the father when the father has died, O <s>Śaunaka</s>.
He should be the father of all and the protector of all.
Toward all the younger ones he conducts himself with equal treatment,
just as toward sons who live with equal share and enjoyment.
The coming together of many things of little strength is formidable.
A rope bound together with grasses can bind even an elephant.

children.text: apahṛtya parasvaṃ hi yastu dānaṃ prayacchati
children.translated_text: He who gives a gift after stealing another's property:

children.text: sa dātā narakaṃ yāti yasyārthāstasya tatphalam ||
children.translated_text: that giver goes to hell; the fruit belongs to the one whose wealth it was.
Through the destruction of property belonging to the gods and through the taking of a Brahmin's property...
Families become no families at all also through transgression against a brāhmaṇa.

children.text: brahmaghne ca surāpe ca core bhagnavrate tathā
children.translated_text: For killing a brāhmaṇa, drinking liquor, theft, and likewise breaking a vow,
an expiation has been prescribed by good people; for one who is ungrateful there is no expiation.
The ancestors and gods do not partake of the offerings of a petty man who is the husband of a vṛṣalī,
nor of a man conquered by his wife, in whose house she has a paramour.
One who is ungrateful, ignoble, long in anger, and crooked:
know these four as caṇḍālas; the fifth is born so by caste.
An enemy, even small, should not be neglected with contempt, O foolish one.
Even a small fire, when unrestrainable, reduces the world to ashes.

children.text: nave vayasi yaḥ śāntaḥ sa śānta iti me matiḥ
children.translated_text: He who is calm in early youth is calm, in my opinion.

children.text: dhātuṣu kṣīyamāṇeṣu śamaḥ kasya na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: When the bodily constituents are wasting away, in whom does calm not arise?
Fortunes, O best of brāhmaṇas, are common to all, like roads.

children.text: madīyā iti matvā vai na hi harṣayuto bhavet ||
children.translated_text: Thinking, 'They are mine,' one should not become filled with delight.

children.text: cittāyattaṃ dhātuvaśyaṃ śarīraṃ citte naṣṭe dhātavo yānti nāśam
children.translated_text: The body is dependent on the mind and subject to the <s>dhātu</s>s (bodily constituents); when the mind is destroyed, the <s>dhātu</s>s go to ruin.

children.text: tasmāccittaṃ sarvadā rakṣaṇīyaṃ svasthe citte dhātavaḥ sambhavanti ||
children.translated_text: Therefore the mind should always be guarded; when the mind is healthy, the <s>dhātu</s>s are well established.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bṛhadṛ nītisāre caturdaśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first part of the eastern section, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, in the Bṛhad-nītisāra, ends the one hundred and fourteenth chapter.
<s>Sūta</s> said:

children.text: kumāryāṃ ca kumitraṃ ca kurājānaṃ kuputrakam
children.translated_text: A maiden, a bad friend, a bad king, and a bad son,

children.text: kukanyāṃ ca kudeśaṃ ca dūrataḥ parivarjayet ||
children.translated_text: a bad daughter and a bad country: one should avoid them from far away.

children.text: dharmaḥ pravrajitastapaḥ pracalitaṃ satyaṃ ca dūraṃ gataṃ pṛthvī vandhyaphalā janāḥ kapaṭino laulye sthitā brāhmaṇāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Dharma</s> has gone into exile, austerity has become unsteady, truth has gone far away; the earth bears barren fruit, people are deceitful, and brāhmaṇas are fixed in greed.

children.text: martyāḥ strīvaśagāḥ striyaśca capalā nīcā janā unnatāḥ hā kaṣṭaṃ khalu jīvitaṃ kaliyuge dhanyā janā ye mṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Mortals are subject to women, women are fickle, and low people are exalted. Alas, life in the <s>Kaliyuga</s> is painful; blessed are those people who are dead.

children.text: dhanyāste ye na paśyanti deśabhaṅgaṃ kulakṣayam
children.translated_text: Blessed are those who do not see the breaking of a country and the ruin of a family,
wives whose hearts have gone to another, and a son fixed in bad habits.
There is no satisfaction in a bad son; how could there be delight in a bad wife?

children.text: sumitre nāsti viśvāsaḥ kurājye nāsti jīvitam ||
children.translated_text: There is no trust in a good friend; there is no life in a bad kingdom.

children.text: parānnaṃ ca parasvaṃ ca paraśayyāḥ parastriyaḥ
children.translated_text: Another's food, another's wealth, another's beds, another's wives,
and dwelling in another's house would take away prosperity even from <s>Śakra</s>.
Through conversation, contact of limbs, association, and eating together,
through sitting, lying down, and riding together, sin passes among men.

children.text: striyo naśyanti rūpeṇa tapaḥ krodhena naśyati
children.translated_text: Women are ruined by beauty; austerity is ruined by anger.
Cows are ruined by roaming at the doorway, and the best of twice-born men by food from a śūdra.
Through sitting, through one shared bed, through eating, and through mixture in a dining row,
sin passes from there like water from jar to jar.
In indulgent fondling there are many faults; in chastisement there are many virtues.

children.text: tasmācchiṣyaṃ ca putraṃ ca tāḍayenna tu lālayet ||
children.translated_text: Therefore one should chastise a pupil and a son, but should not indulge them.

children.text: adhvā jarā dehavatāṃ parvatānāṃ jalaṃ jarā
children.translated_text: A journey is old age for embodied beings; water is old age for mountains.
Lack of intercourse is old age for women, and sunlight is old age for garments.
Inferior men desire strife; middling men desire alliance.

children.text: uttamā mānamicchanti māno hi mahatāṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: The best men desire honor, for honor is the wealth of the great.

children.text: māno hi mūlamarthasya māne sati dhanena kim
children.translated_text: Honor is indeed the root of wealth; when honor exists, what need is there of wealth?
For one whose honor and pride have fallen away, what use is wealth, and what use is life?
Inferior men desire wealth; middling men desire both wealth and honor.

children.text: uttamā mānamicchanti māno hi mahatāṃ dhanam ||
children.translated_text: The best men desire honor, for honor is the wealth of the great.

children.text: vane 'pi siṃhā na namanti kaṃ ca bubhukṣitā māṃsanirīkṣaṇaṃ ca
children.translated_text: Even in the forest, lions do not bow to anyone, though hungry and looking at meat.

children.text: dhanairvihīnāḥ sukuleṣu jātā na nīcakarmāṇi samārabhante ||
children.translated_text: Those born in good families, though deprived of wealth, do not undertake low actions.

children.text: nābhiṣeko na saṃskāraḥ siṃhasya kriyate vane
children.translated_text: No consecration and no rite of refinement is performed for the lion in the forest.
For one whose strength is always mighty, lordship among beasts arises by itself.

children.text: vaṇikpramādī bhṛkaśca mānī bhikṣurvilāsī hyadhanaśca kāmī
children.translated_text: A negligent merchant, an uncertain servant, a proud mendicant, a pleasure-loving poor man who is lustful,

children.text: varāṅganā cāpriyavādinī ca na te ca karmāṇi samārabhante ||
children.translated_text: and a courtesan who speaks unpleasantly: these do not undertake their proper occupations.

children.text: dātā daridraḥ kṛpaṇo 'rthayuktaḥ puttro 'vidheyaḥ kujanasya sevā
children.translated_text: A poor giver, a miser possessed of wealth, a disobedient son, service to a bad man,

children.text: paropakāreṣu narasya mṛtyuḥ prajāyate duścaritāni pañca ||
children.translated_text: and a man's death in acts of helping others: these five misfortunes arise.

children.text: kāntāviyogaḥ svajanāpamānaṃ ṛṇasya śeṣaḥ kujanasya sevā
children.translated_text: Separation from a beloved, insult by one's own people, the remainder of a debt, service to a bad man,

children.text: dāridryābhāvād vimukhāśca mitrā vināgninā pañca dahanti tīvrāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and friends turned away because of poverty: these five burn fiercely without fire.
Among thousands of anxieties, and in the midst of them, four anxieties are like the edge of a sword:

children.text: nīcāpamānaṃ kṣudhitaṃ kalatraṃ bhāryā viraktā sahajoparodhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: insult by the low, a hungry wife, an estranged wife, and obstruction by kinsmen.

children.text: vaśyaśca putre 'rthakarī ca vidyā arogitā sajjanasaṃgatiśca
children.translated_text: An obedient son, learning that produces wealth, health, association with good people,

children.text: iṣṭā ca bhāryā vaśavartinī ca duḥkhasya mūloddharaṇāni pañca ||
children.translated_text: and a beloved wife who remains obedient: these five uproot suffering from its root.
The deer, elephant, moth, bee, and fish are each slain by one of the five sense objects.

children.text: ekaḥ pramāthī sa kathaṃ na ghātyo yaḥ sevate pañcabhireva pañca ||
children.translated_text: How should one careless man not be destroyed, when he indulges in all five by means of all five senses?
Impatient, harsh, stiff, ill-clothed, and arriving uninvited:

children.text: pañca viprā na pūjyante bṛhaspatisamā api ||
children.translated_text: these five brāhmaṇas are not to be honored, even if they are equal to <s>Bṛhaspati</s>.

children.text: āyuḥ karma ca vittaṃ ca vidyā nidhanameva ca
children.translated_text: Life span, action, wealth, learning, and death itself:
these five are determined for an embodied being as it is being born.
In climbing a mountain, in water, in a cow pen, in restraining the wicked,

children.text: patitasya samutthāne śastāḥ pañca guṇāḥ smṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: and in raising up one who has fallen, five virtues are remembered as praiseworthy.
The shadow of a cloud, affection for a rogue, association with another's wife,

children.text: pañcaite hyasthirā bhāvā yauvanāni dhanāni ca ||
children.translated_text: and youth and riches: these five states are indeed unstable.
Life in the world is unstable; wealth and youth are unstable.
Sons, wives, and the like are unstable; <s>dharma</s> (righteous order), fame, and renown are stable.
A life of a hundred years is very little; night takes away half of it.
Even that remaining half is made fruitless in part by illness, grief, old age, and exertions.

children.text: āyurvarṣaśataṃ nṛṇāṃ parimitaṃ rātrau tadardhaṃ gataṃ tasyārdhasthitakiṃcidardham adhikaṃ bālyasya kāle gatam
children.translated_text: The life of men is limited to a hundred years; half of it passes in the night, and of the remaining half, a portion greater than half passes in the time of childhood.

children.text: kiṃcid bandhuviyogaduḥkhamaraṇair bhūpālasevāgataṃ śeṣaṃ vāritaraṅgagarbhacapalaṃ mānena kiṃ māninām ||
children.translated_text: Some is spent in the sorrow of separation from kin, in deaths, and in service to kings; the rest is as unsteady as something within the waves of water. What use is pride to the proud?
In the world, death, made of day and night, moves about in the form of old age.
Death devours beings as a serpent devours the wind.

children.text: gacchatastiṣṭhato vāpi jāgrataḥ svapato na cet
children.translated_text: Whether one is going or standing, awake or asleep, if one is not acting
for the welfare of all beings, one's activity is like that of a beast.
For a person whose mind is empty of reflection on harm and benefit, though much debated in the domain of scripture,
and whose thought is satisfied merely with filling the belly, what difference is there between a human beast and a beast?

children.text: śaurye tapasi dāne ca yasya na prathitaṃ yaśaḥ
children.translated_text: He whose fame has not become renowned in courage, austerity, and giving,
or in learning or the acquisition of wealth, is merely his mother's excrement.
That which is lived even for a moment by men renowned for knowledge, valor, and fame, with their honor unbroken,

children.text: tannāma jīvitamiti pravadanti tajjñāḥ kāko 'pi jīvati ciraṃ ca baliṃ ca bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: the wise call that alone life; even a crow lives long and eats offerings.

children.text: kiṃ jīvitena dhanamānavivarjitena mitreṇa kiṃ bhavati bhītisaśaṅkitena
children.translated_text: What is the use of life without wealth and honor? What is the use of a friend who is fearful and suspicious?

children.text: siṃhavrataṃ carata gacchata mā viṣādaṃ kāko 'pi jīvati ciraṃ ca baliṃ ca bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: Practice the lion's vow; go on, do not despair. Even a crow lives long and eats offerings.

children.text: yo vātmanīha na gurau na ca bhṛtyavarge dīne dayāṃ na kurute na ca mitrakārye
children.translated_text: He who in this world shows no compassion toward himself, his teacher, his class of servants, the poor, or a friend's business,

children.text: kiṃ tasya jīvitaphalena manuṣyaloke kāko 'pi jīvati ciraṃ ca baliṃ ca bhuṅkte ||
children.translated_text: what is the fruit of his life in the human world? Even a crow lives long and eats offerings.
The days of one who is empty of the <s>trivarga</s> (the three aims) come and go.
Like a blacksmith's bellows, though breathing, he does not live.
Fulfillment belongs to one whose conduct is independent, not to living under another's control.

children.text: ye parādhīnakarmāṇo jīvanto 'pi ca te mṛtāḥ ||
children.translated_text: Those whose actions are dependent on another are dead, even while alive.
Base men are easily filled; the cupped paws of a mouse are easy to fill.
A base man, unsatisfied though he is, is pleased even by a little.

children.text: abhracchāyā tṛṇādagnir no ca sevā patho jalam
children.translated_text: The shade of a cloud, fire from grass, service, water on a road,
a courtesan's love, and affection for a villain: these six are like bubbles.

children.text: vācā vihitasārthena loko na ca sukhāyate
children.translated_text: The world is not made happy by speech, even when it has a useful purpose.

children.text: jīvitaṃ mānamūlaṃ hi māne mlāne kutaḥ sukham ||
children.translated_text: Life has honor as its root; when honor has withered, where can happiness be?

children.text: abalasya balaṃ rājā bālasya ruditaṃ balam
children.translated_text: The king is the strength of the weak; crying is the strength of a child.

children.text: balaṃ mūrkhasya maunaṃ hi taskarasyānṛtaṃ balam ||
children.translated_text: Silence is the strength of a fool, and falsehood is the strength of a thief.
Just as a man gradually learns a <s>śāstra</s> (treatise),
so his intelligence develops, and knowledge becomes pleasing to him.

children.text: yathāyathā hi puruṣaḥ kalyāṇe kurute matim
children.translated_text: Just as a man gradually turns his mind toward what is good,
so he becomes attached everywhere as one beloved by good people.
A person is ruined by three things: greed, negligence, and misplaced trust.

children.text: tasmāllobho na kartavyaḥ pramādo no na viśvaset ||
children.translated_text: Therefore greed should not be practiced, negligence should not be practiced, and one should not place trust blindly.
One should fear danger only so long as the danger has not arrived.

children.text: utpanne tu bhaye tīvre sthātavyaṃ vai hyabhītavat ||
children.translated_text: But when a fierce danger has arisen, one should stand firm as if fearless.
A remainder of debt, a remainder of fire, and likewise a remainder of disease

children.text: punaḥ punaḥ pravardhante tasmāccheṣaṃ na kārayet ||
children.translated_text: grow again and again; therefore one should not leave a remainder.
One should return a favor for a favor, and violence for violence.

children.text: na tatra doṣaṃ paśyāmi duṣṭe doṣaṃ samācaret ||
children.translated_text: I see no fault there; toward the wicked one should act with wickedness.
One should avoid a friend who ruins one's business behind one's back but speaks pleasantly to one's face,
and likewise an enemy made of deceit.
By association with a bad person, even a good person is ruined.
Even clear water is made muddy by mud.

children.text: sa bhuṅkte sa dvijo bhuṅkte samaśeṣanirūpaṇam
children.translated_text: He eats, that twice-born man truly eats, after making a full and proper apportionment.
Therefore a twice-born man should be honored with every effort and care.

children.text: tadbhujyate yaddvijabhuktaśeṣaṃ sa buddhimānyo na karoti pāpam
children.translated_text: What is eaten is that which remains after a twice-born man has eaten; wise is the man who does not commit sin.

children.text: tatsauhṛdaṃ yat kriyate parokṣe dambhairvinā yaḥ kriyate sa dharmaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is friendship which is performed out of sight; that is <s>dharma</s> which is performed without pretence.

children.text: na sā sabhā yatra na santi vṛddhāḥ vṛddhā na te ye na vadanti dharmam
children.translated_text: That is not an assembly where there are no elders; they are not elders who do not speak <s>dharma</s>.

children.text: dharmaḥ sa no yatra na satyamasti naitatsatyaṃ yacchalenānuviddham ||
children.translated_text: That is not <s>dharma</s> where truth is absent; that is not truth which is pierced by deceit.
Among human beings the Brahmin is foremost, and among luminous things the sun is foremost.
Among all limbs the head is foremost, and among vows truth is supreme.

children.text: tanmaṅgalaṃ yatra manaḥ prasannaṃ tajjīvanaṃ yanna parasya sevā
children.translated_text: That is auspicious where the mind is serene; that is life which is not service to another.

children.text: tadarjitaṃ yatsvajanena bhuktaṃ tadgarjitaṃ yatsamare ripūṇām ||
children.translated_text: That is what has been acquired which has been enjoyed by one's own people; that is a roar which belongs to enemies in battle.

children.text: sā strī yā na madaṃ kuryātsa sukhī tṛṣṇayojjhitaḥ
children.translated_text: She is a wife who does not become intoxicated with pride; he is happy who has abandoned thirsting desire.

children.text: tanmitraṃ yatra viśvāsaḥ puruṣaḥ sa jitendriyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That is a friend in whom there is trust; that is a man who has conquered his senses.
There, affection joined with respect is released; where friendship has been destroyed,

children.text: tadeva kevalaṃ ślāghyaṃ yasyātmā kriyate stutau ||
children.translated_text: that alone is praiseworthy in which one's own self is made the object of praise.
One should not seek the origins of rivers, sacrificial fires, the <s>Bhārata</s>, or a vessel.

children.text: mūlānveṣo na kartavyo mūlāddoṣo na hīyate ||
children.translated_text: Fault is not removed from the root by tracing the root.
Rivers end in salt water, and sexual intercourse ends in divisions concerning women.
Slander ends in public talk, and wealth ends the threefold suffering.
Royal fortune ends with a Brahmin's curse; Brahminical brilliance ends with sin.
As recited, O lord: it ends with <s>ācamana</s> (ritual sipping), with dwelling in a cowherd hamlet, and a family's end comes through a woman.
All dwellings end in decay; all elevations end in downfall.
Unions end in separation, for life indeed ends in death.
If one wishes to come back again, one should not follow along too far;
one should turn back from the water's edge and from the foot of a green-looking tree.

children.text: anāyake na vastavyaṃ na caiva bahunāyake
children.translated_text: One should not live in a place with no leader, nor indeed in one with many leaders;
one should not live where a woman is leader; one may live where a child is leader.

children.text: pitā rakṣati kaumāre bhartā rakṣati yauvane
children.translated_text: The father protects a woman in childhood, and the husband protects her in youth;

children.text: putrastu sthavire kāle na strī svātantryamarhati ||
children.translated_text: the son protects her in old age; a woman is not deemed fit for independence.
One should abandon a barren wife in the eighth year, one whose children die in the ninth,
one who bears only daughters in the eleventh, and one who speaks unpleasantly immediately.
Because people do not seek them, from fear of the household, and for the sake of wealth,
three women who have departed from proper bounds remain with their husbands.

children.text: aśvaṃ śrāntaṃ gajaṃ mattaṃ gāvaḥ prathamasūtikāḥ
children.translated_text: A tired horse, a rutting elephant, cows that have calved for the first time,
and frogs in a waterless place: a wise man should avoid them from afar.

children.text: arthāturāṇāṃ na suhṛnna bandhuḥ kāmāturāṇāṃ na bhayaṃ na lajjā
children.translated_text: For those distressed by wealth there is no friend and no kinsman; for those distressed by desire there is no fear and no shame.

children.text: cintāturāṇāṃ na sukhaṃ na nidrā kṣudhāturāṇāṃ na balaṃ na tejaḥ ||
children.translated_text: For those distressed by worry there is no happiness and no sleep; for those distressed by hunger there is no strength and no vigor.
How can there be sleep for a poor man, or for the chief servant of another,
or for one attached to another's wife, or for one who steals another's property?

children.text: sukhaṃ svapity anṛṇavān vyādhimuktaśca yo naraḥ
children.translated_text: The man who is free of debt and free of disease sleeps happily;

children.text: sāvakāśastu vai bhuṅkte yastu dārairna saṃgataḥ ||
children.translated_text: and he who is not joined to a wife eats with leisure.
A lotus grows upward according to the measure of the water;
a servant becomes proud through his own powerful master.
For a lotus standing in its place, <s>Varuṇa</s> and <s>Bhāskara</s> are friends;
for that very lotus, when displaced from its place, they cause wetness and drying.

children.text: ye padasthasya mitrāṇi te tasya riputāṃ gatāḥ
children.translated_text: Those who are friends to a man established in his position become enemies to him when he has fallen from it;
<s>Bhānu</s> loves the lotus in water, but dries it when it is pulled up onto land.

children.text: sthānasthitāni pūjyante pūjyante ca pade sthitāḥ
children.translated_text: Things standing in their proper place are honored, and people established in rank are honored;

children.text: sthānabhraṣṭā na pūjyante keśā dantā nakhā narāḥ ||
children.translated_text: fallen from their place, hair, teeth, nails, and men are not honored.
Conduct declares one's family; speech declares one's country.
Agitation declares affection; the body declares food.

children.text: vṛthā vṛṣṭiḥ samudrasya vṛthā tṛptasya bhojanam
children.translated_text: Rain falling into the ocean is useless; food for one already satisfied is useless.

children.text: vṛthā dānaṃ samṛddhasya nīcasya sukṛtaṃ vṛthā ||
children.translated_text: A gift to one who is already prosperous is useless; a good deed done for a base man is useless.

children.text: dūrastho 'pi samīpastho yo yasya hṛdaye sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Even far away, he in whose heart someone dwells is near;
expelled even from the heart, though standing nearby, he is far away.
A fallen face, a pitiable voice, sweat on the limbs, and great fear:

children.text: maraṇe yāni cihnāni tāni cihnāni yācake ||
children.translated_text: the signs that appear at death are the same signs in a beggar.
Rather than birth as one who begs, even for one bent over, struck by worms, and driven out by wind,

children.text: śikhare vasatastasya varaṃ janma na yācitam ||
children.translated_text: living on a mountain peak is preferable.
Because, after begging, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the lord of the world, went into dwarfhood,
who is higher than he, and what gain that goes to begging does not become diminished?

children.text: mātā śatruḥ pitā vairī bālā yena na pāṭhitāḥ
children.translated_text: A mother is an enemy, and a father is hostile, if children have not been educated by them;

children.text: sabhāmadhye na śobhante haṃsamadhye bakā yathā ||
children.translated_text: they do not shine in the midst of an assembly, just as cranes do not among swans.

children.text: vidyā nāma kurūparūpam adhikaṃ vidyātiguptaṃ dhanaṃ vidyā sādhukarī janapriyakarī vidyā gurūṇāṃ guruḥ
children.translated_text: Learning is beauty surpassing beauty for the ugly; learning is a well-hidden treasure; learning produces goodness and makes one beloved among people; learning is the teacher of teachers.

children.text: vidyā bandhujanārtināśanakarī vidyā paraṃ daivataṃ vidyā rājasu pūjitā hi manujo vidyāvihīnaḥ paśuḥ ||
children.translated_text: Learning removes the distress of kinsmen; learning is the supreme deity; learning is honored among kings; a man without learning is a beast.

children.text: gṛhe cābhyantare dravyaṃ lagnaṃ caiva tu dṛśyate
children.translated_text: Property fastened inside the house is seen there,

children.text: aśeṣaṃ haraṇīyaṃ ca vidyā na hriyate paraiḥ ||
children.translated_text: and all of it can be taken away; learning is not taken away by others.
The <s>Śaunakīya Nītisāra</s> and all the vows concerning <s>Viṣṇu</s>

children.text: kathayāmāsa vai pūrvaṃ tatra śuśrāva śaṅkaraḥ
children.translated_text: were formerly taught everywhere by <s>Viṣṇu</s>; there <s>Śaṅkara</s> heard them.
<s>Vyāsa</s> heard them from <s>Śaṅkara</s>, and we ourselves heard them from <s>Vyāsa</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śaunakoktanītisārādivarṇanaṃ nāma pañcadaśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first section called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the one-hundred-fifteenth chapter, named 'Description of the <s>Nītisāra</s> and Related Teachings Spoken by <s>Śaunaka</s>.'
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: vratāni vyāsa vakṣyāmi hariryaiḥ sarvado bhavet
children.translated_text: O <s>Vyāsa</s>, I shall describe the vows by which <s>Hari</s> becomes the giver of everything.
When <s>Hari</s> is worshipped in all months, lunar mansions, lunar days, and weekdays,
with eating once, eating at night, the fruit of fasting, and so forth,
he grants wealth, grain, sons, sovereignty, victory, and the like.
On the first lunar day, <s>Vaiśvānara</s> and <s>Kubera</s>, when worshipped, grant wealth.
On <s>Puṣya</s>, <s>Brahmā</s>, worshipped on the first lunar day, and likewise <s>Śrī</s> on <s>Aśvinī</s>...
On the second lunar day, <s>Yama</s> and <s>Lakṣmī-Nārāyaṇa</s> here grant wealth.
On the third lunar day are the three gods, <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Vighneśa</s>, and <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
On the fourth is the <s>Caturvyūha</s>; on the fifth, <s>Hari</s> is worshipped.
<s>Kārttikeya</s> and <s>Ravi</s> are on the sixth; on the seventh, <s>Bhāskara</s> grants wealth.
On <s>Durgāṣṭamī</s>, on the ninth, the Mothers and then the Directions grant wealth.
On the tenth are <s>Yama</s> and <s>Candra</s>; on the eleventh one should sacrifice to the seers.
On the twelfth is <s>Hari</s>; on the thirteenth are <s>Kāma</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>.
On the fourteenth and fifteenth, <s>Brahmā</s> and the ancestors grant wealth.
On the new-moon day the weekdays beginning with that of <s>Bhāskara</s> are to be worshipped;
and the lunar mansions and yogas, when worshipped, bestow everything.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe tithyādivratavarṇanaṃ nāma ṣoḍaśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first section called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the one-hundred-sixteenth chapter, named 'Description of Vows Beginning with Lunar Days.'
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
In the bright fortnight of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, O <s>Vyāsa</s>, [there is] <s>Anaṅga-trayodaśī</s>...
He should use a tooth-stick born from jasmine and worship <s>Śiva</s> with <s>dhattūra</s> flowers.
In <s>Pauṣa</s>, after tasting honey, the <s>naivedya</s> (food offering) is to be offered with the formula, “to <s>Anaṅga</s>.”
He should also worship <s>Yogeśvara</s> with bilva leaves; the tooth-stick is from the kadamba tree.
The tooth-stick may be sandalwood and the like, and the offering is <s>kṛsarā</s> and similar foods.
In <s>Māgha</s> he should worship <s>Naṭeśvara</s> with kunda flowers and a pearl garland.

children.text: plakṣeṇa dantakāṣṭhaṃ ca naivedyaṃ pūrikā mune ||
children.translated_text: The tooth-stick is from plakṣa, and the <s>naivedya</s> is a <s>pūrikā</s>, O sage.
In <s>Phālguna</s> he should worship <s>Vīreśvara</s> with marūbaka plants.
Sugar, greens, and cakes are offered, and the tooth-cleaning stick is from the mango tree.
In <s>Caitra</s> he should worship <s>Surūpa</s>, and at night he should make him taste camphor.
The tooth-cleaning is from the aṭa tree, and as <s>naivedya</s> he should give a <s>śaṣkulī</s> cake.
In <s>Vaiśākha</s> the worship of <s>Śambhu</s> is with damanaka plants and aśoka flowers.
For <s>Mahārūpa</s>, the <s>naivedya</s> is rice with molasses and a food called <s>puṭṭabara</s>.
He should also make him use the tooth-stick and should likewise give nutmeg.
In <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> he should worship <s>Pradyumna</s> with campaka flowers and chew what is from bilva.
Likewise, with clove and in <s>Āṣāḍha</s>, the text gives an uncertain prescription connected with <s>Umā</s>.
Aguru is the tooth-stick, and he should worship him with apāmārga plants.
In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> he should offer karavīra to <s>Śambhu</s>, the trident-holder.
The observance includes fragrant consumption, offerings such as ghee, and purification with karavīra, though the wording is uncertain.
In <s>Bhādrapada</s> he should worship <s>Sadyojāta</s> with bakula flowers and cakes.
In <s>Āśvina</s>, for <s>Surādhipa</s>, there is a prescription involving fragrant food and madanaka, though the reading is uncertain.
