With campaka flowers, and with a gift of modakas, the intervening words about gold or garments are corrupt.
The tooth-stick is from khadira, and in <s>Kārttika</s> he should worship <s>Rudra</s>.
The tooth-stick is from badarī, and the line gives a further uncertain rule concerning <s>Madana</s> and food.
Giving milk and vegetables, at the end of the year he should worship <s>Śiva</s> with lotuses.
He should place <s>Rati</s> and <s>Anaṅga</s>, as stated, upon a golden maṇḍala.
With perfumes and the like he should make ten thousand oblations of sesame, rice, and other grains.
He should hold a vigil with singing and instruments, then, after worshiping at dawn, announce the rite.

children.text: dvijāya śayyāṃ pātraṃ ca chatraṃ vastramupānahau ||
children.translated_text: To a Brahmin he should give a bed, a vessel, an umbrella, a garment, and shoes.
He should give a cow and feed a Brahmin with devotion; then the man becomes one who has fulfilled his duty.
This is the complete concluding rite, and such a rite is to be contemplated in all vows.
Its fruit is prosperity, sons, health, good fortune, and heaven.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe 'naṅgatrayodaśīvrataṃ nāma saptadaśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one hundred and seventeenth chapter, named the <s>Anaṅgatrayodaśīvrata</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall describe the <s>Akhaṇḍadvādaśī</s> vow, which pacifies obstacles to complete release.
In the bright fortnight of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, subsisting on cow products and fasting,
on the twelfth lunar day he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>; for four months he should give
to a Brahmin a vessel containing five kinds of grain, and he should say this:

children.text: saptajanmani he viṣṇo yanmayā hi vrataṃ kṛtam
children.translated_text: O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, whatever vow has been performed by me over seven births,
O blessed Lord, by your grace may that be unbroken for me here.
Just as the whole world is unbroken, and you alone are <s>Puruṣottama</s>,
so may all my vows indeed be complete and unbroken.
From <s>Caitra</s> onward he should give vessels of saktu, and from <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> onward vessels mixed with ghee.
When the performer of the vow has completed the observance, he obtains a wife, sons, and heaven.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe 'khaṇḍadvādaśīvratakathanaṃ nāmāṣṭādaśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one hundred and eighteenth chapter, named the teaching of the <s>Akhaṇḍadvādaśīvrata</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall describe the <s>Agastyārghyavrata</s>, which grants enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: aprāpte bhāskare kanyāṃ sati bhāge tribhirdinaiḥ ||
children.translated_text: Three days before <s>Bhāskara</s>, the sun, reaches <s>Kanyā</s>, when the proper portion has arrived,

children.text: arghyaṃ dadyādagastyāya mūrtiṃ sampūjya vai mune
children.translated_text: one should give an <s>arghya</s> (honor offering) to <s>Agastya</s>, after duly worshiping his image, O sage.
The image should be made of kāśa flowers in a pot; at twilight he should keep vigil.
Having fasted, he should worship with curds, unbroken rice, and the like, and with fruits and flowers.
The vessel should be furnished with five colors and supplied with gold and silver.
It should contain seven kinds of grain and be smeared with curd and sandalwood.
With the mantra beginning <s>agastyaḥ khanamāna</s>, he should have the <s>arghya</s> presented.
O you who shine like khāsa flowers, born of fire and wind,
son of <s>Mitra</s> and <s>Varuṇa</s>, pot-born one, homage to you.
Śūdras, women, and others should by this same rite give up grain, fruit, and juice.
He should give the pot, together with gold and a <s>dakṣiṇā</s> (honorarium), to a twice-born man.

children.text: bhojayecca dvijānsapta varṣaṃ kṛtvā tu sarvabhāk ||
children.translated_text: He should feed seven Brahmins; after performing this for a year, he becomes possessed of all attainments.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe 'gastyārghyavrataṃ nāmaikonaviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the revered <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one hundred and nineteenth chapter, named the <s>Agastyārghyavrata</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall describe the <s>Rambhātṛtīyā</s>, which gives good fortune, prosperity, sons, and the like.
In the bright fortnight of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, having fasted on the third lunar day,
he should worship <s>Gaurī</s> with bilva leaves, then with kuśa-water in hand.
In the season beginning with kadamba he should worship the mountain's daughter, and in <s>Pauṣa</s> with marūbaka plants.
He eats camphor and the like, gives <s>kṛsarā</s>, and uses a jasmine tooth-stick.
In <s>Māgha</s> he should worship <s>Bhadrā</s> with kalhāra flowers, eat ghee, and give maṇḍaka cakes.
The tooth-stick is described uncertainly as gītīmaya; in <s>Phālguna</s> he should worship <s>Gomatī</s>.
With kunda flowers, having prepared the tooth-stick, he eats jīva and gives <s>śaṣkulī</s> cakes, though the reading is uncertain.
In <s>Caitra</s> he should worship <s>Viśālākṣī</s> with damanaka plants and give <s>kṛsarā</s>.
He eats curds; the tooth-stick is tagara, and he should worship <s>Śrīmukhī</s>.
In <s>Vaiśākha</s> he should worship with karṇikāra flowers; eating aśoka and giving vaṭa are prescribed, though the wording is terse.
In <s>Jyeṣṭha</s> he should worship <s>Nārāyaṇī</s> with hundred-petalled lotuses and give sugar-candy.
He should eat cloves; in <s>Āṣāḍha</s> he should worship <s>Mādhavī</s>.
He should eat sesame, worship with bilva leaves, and give cakes made of milk-rice.
In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> he should offer an audumbara tooth-stick and tagara flowers to <s>Śrī</s>.
With a tooth-stick of mallikā, and as a giver of milk, he should worship the supreme goddess.
In <s>Bhādrapada</s> he should worship with lotuses, giving such things as horns and jaggery.
In <s>Āśvayuja</s> he should worship the royal maiden with hibiscus flowers and cumin.
At night he should make her taste the offerings; in <s>Kārtika</s> he should worship with kṛsara.
He should worship <s>Padmajā</s> with jasmine flowers, subsisting on pañcagavya.
At the end of the year he should worship married twice-born men with rice cooked in ghee.
Having worshipped <s>Umā</s> and <s>Maheśvara</s>, he should give jaggery and the like.
With garments, umbrellas, gold, and other gifts, and keeping vigil at night,
with song and music, giving cows and other gifts in the morning, he obtains everything.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe rambhātṛtīyāvrataṃ nāma viṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one hundred twentieth chapter, named the Rambhā-tṛtīyā vow.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
The Cāturmāsya vows have been stated; one should undertake them on <s>Ekādaśī</s>,

children.text: āṣāḍhyāṃ paurṇamāsyāṃ vā sarveṇa harim arcya ca ||
children.translated_text: or on the full-moon day of <s>Āṣāḍhī</s>, after worshipping <s>Hari</s> with all means.

children.text: idaṃ vrataṃ mayā deva gṛhītaṃ puratastava
children.translated_text: O god, this vow has been undertaken by me before you;
may it attain unobstructed completion, when you are gracious, O <s>Keśava</s>.
O god, if, after undertaking this vow, I should die before it is complete,
then may it become complete for me through your grace, O <s>Janārdana</s>.
Having worshipped in this way, he should undertake the vow, worship, recitation, and the rest.

children.text: sarvāghaṃ ca kṣayaṃ yāti cikīrṣedyo harervratam ||
children.translated_text: Whoever wishes to perform <s>Hari</s>'s vow goes to the destruction of all sin.
After bathing and worshipping, he should undertake the vow, worship, recitation, and the rest.
After bathing, if he worships for the four months while taking one meal a day,

children.text: viṣṇuṃ sa yāti viṣṇor va lokaṃ malavivarjitam ||
children.translated_text: worshipping <s>Viṣṇu</s>, he goes to <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s stainless world.
Abandoning liquor, meat, and strong drink, through knowledge of the Veda and worship of <s>Hari</s>,
avoiding oil and performing kṛcchra observances, he reaches <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world and becomes devoted to <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
By a fast of one night he becomes a god dwelling in an aerial palace.
By three nights he goes to <s>Śvetadvīpa</s>; a man who eats only every sixth meal does so as well.
By the cāndrāyaṇa vow he obtains <s>Hari</s>'s abode and liberation without asking for it.
By the prājāpatya vow he obtains <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world; the performer of the parāka vow attains <s>Hari</s>.
Eating saktu, barley, and alms, or eating milk, curds, and ghee,
living on cow urine and barley, or eating pañcagavya,
eating vegetables, roots, fruits, and the like, and abstaining from juices, he becomes a sharer in <s>Viṣṇu</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe cāturmāsyavratanirūpaṇaṃ nāmakāvaśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one hundred twenty-first chapter, named the Description of the Cāturmāsya Vow.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall tell you the vow called month-long fasting, the best of all.
A forest-dweller, a renunciant, or a woman may perform the month-long fast.
Having fasted on <s>Ekādaśī</s> in the bright fortnight of <s>Āśvina</s>,
he should undertake this vow for as many as thirty days.
From today, O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, until your awakening,
may I worship you, O <s>Vāmana</s>, for exactly thirty days.
O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, between the bright twelfth days of <s>Kārtika</s> and <s>Āśvina</s>,

children.text: mriye yadyantarāle tu vratabhaṅgo na me bhavet ||
children.translated_text: if I die in the interval, may there be no breaking of my vow.
The vow-keeper, bathing at the three junctions of the day, should worship <s>Hari</s> with sandal and other offerings.
He should avoid body-anointing and the smearing of perfumes in the temple of the deity.
Then, after worshipping on <s>Dvādaśī</s>, he should provide a meal for twice-born men.
Then the performer of <s>Hari</s>'s month-long fast should perform the pāraṇa, the breaking of the fast.
If, while established in the vow, he faints in the interval, he may take milk and the like.
The vow is not destroyed by milk and the like; he obtains enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe māsopavāsavrataṃ nāma dvāviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one hundred twenty-second chapter, named the Month-long Fast Vow.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: vratāni kārtike vakṣye snātvā viṣṇuṃ prapūjayet
children.translated_text: I shall explain the vows in <s>Kārtika</s>; after bathing one should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
For a month he may eat one meal a day, eat at night, or live on unsolicited food,
or on milk, vegetables, fruits, and the like, or again by fasting.
Freed from all sins and with his desires fulfilled, he goes to <s>Hari</s>.
<s>Hari</s>'s vow is always best; next it is so in the southern course of the sun,
then in Cāturmāsya, and after that, in <s>Kārtika</s>, the Bhīṣma-pañcaka.
Thereafter one should undertake the best vow on the bright <s>Ekādaśī</s>.
Having bathed three times a day, he should worship <s>Hari</s> with barley and other offerings for the ancestors and others.
Keeping silence, he should worship with ghee and the like, and with pañcagavya and water.
After bathing him, he should anoint him with camphor and similar substances.
For five days a twice-born man should burn incense of guggulu mixed with ghee.
The food offering should be paramānna, and he should recite one hundred and eight times:
"Oṃ, homage to <s>Vāsudeva</s>." With ghee, rice, sesame, and the like,
he should make oblations with the eight-syllabled mantra ending in svāhā.

children.text: prathame 'hni hareḥ pādau yajet padmair dvitayika
children.translated_text: On the first day he should worship <s>Hari</s>'s feet with lotuses; on the second,
the region of the knees with bilva leaves, and then the navel with sandal paste.
With bilva and hibiscus he should worship the shoulders, and on the fifth day the head
with mālatī flowers; he should sleep on the ground and consume cow dung in sequence,

children.text: gomūtraṃ ca dadhi kṣīraṃ pañcame pañcagavyakam
children.translated_text: then cow urine, curds, milk, and on the fifth day pañcagavya.
On the fifteenth day he should eat at night; the vow-keeper becomes a sharer in enjoyment and liberation.
The <s>Ekādaśī</s> vow is constant; one should perform it in both fortnights.
It destroys masses of sin and hell, grants all things, and gives <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s world.

children.text: ekādaśī dvādaśī ca niśānte ca trayodaśī
children.translated_text: Where <s>Ekādaśī</s>, <s>Dvādaśī</s>, and, at the end of the night, <s>Trayodaśī</s> occur,
there <s>Ekādaśī</s> is permanent, and <s>Hari</s> is present there.
Where the tenth lunar day and <s>Ekādaśī</s> occur together, demons and the like are present there.
One should perform the <s>pāraṇa</s> (breaking of the fast) on the twelfth; in impurity from birth or death one should act accordingly.
One should fast on a fourteenth lunar day, and on a first lunar day mixed with the preceding one,
on a full-moon day and on a new-moon day when mixed with the first lunar day, O sage.
One should also fast on a second lunar day mixed with the third, and on the third itself,
and always on one joined with the fourth, one accompanied by the fourth observance,

children.text: pañcamīṃ ṣaṣṭhyasaṃyuktāṃ ṣaṣṭhyā yuktāṃ ca saptamīm ||
children.translated_text: on a fifth not joined with the sixth, and on a seventh joined with the sixth.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhīṣmapañcakādivrataṃ nāma trayoviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and twenty-third chapter, named the vow beginning with the <s>Bhīṣmapañcaka</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall declare the <s>Śivarātri</s> vow and its story, which grants all desires,

children.text: yathā ca gaurī bhūteśaṃ pṛcchati sma paraṃ vratam ||
children.translated_text: just as <s>Gaurī</s> once asked <s>Bhūteśa</s> about the supreme vow.
<s>Īśvara</s> said:
Between <s>Māgha</s> and <s>Phālguna</s>, the fourteenth lunar day that falls in the dark fortnight,
on that day <s>Rudra</s>, when worshipped with a night vigil, grants enjoyment and liberation.
<s>Hara</s> should be worshipped for one's desires, and <s>Keśava</s> on the twelfth day;
when worshipped by those who fast, he likewise carries them across from hell.
At <s>Arbuda</s> there was a sinful <s>Niṣāda</s> king named <s>Sundarasena</s>.

children.text: sa kukkuraiḥ samāyukto mṛgānhantuṃ vanaṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Accompanied by dogs, he went into the forest to kill deer.
Not obtaining deer or other game, and afflicted by hunger and thirst on the mountain,
at night he remained awake in a thicket on the bank of a pond.
There was a liṅga there; while protecting his own body, he shook himself there,
and leaves fell upon the very head of the liṅga, without his knowing it.

children.text: tena dhūlinirodhāya kṣiptaṃ nīraṃ ca liṅgake
children.translated_text: To keep down the dust he threw water upon the liṅga,
and one arrow accidentally slipped from his hand.
Going down to the ground on his knees, he touched the liṅga and picked it up.

children.text: evaṃ snānaṃ sparśanaṃ ca pūjanaṃ jāgaro 'bhavat ||
children.translated_text: Thus bathing, touching, worship, and a night vigil came about.
In the morning he returned home and ate the food given by his wife.

children.text: kāle mṛto yamabhaṭaiḥ pāśairbaddhvā tu nīyate ||
children.translated_text: When he died in due course, he was bound with nooses and led away by the servants of <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: tadā mama gaṇairyuddhe jitvā muktīkṛtaḥ sa ca
children.translated_text: Then, in battle, my <s>gaṇas</s> defeated them and freed him.
Together with his dog he became a stainless <s>gaṇa</s> standing near me.
Thus merit arises even unknowingly; when done knowingly, the merit is imperishable.

children.text: trayodaśyāṃ śivaṃ pūjya kuryātta niyamaṃ vratī ||
children.translated_text: Having worshipped <s>Śiva</s> on the thirteenth day, the vow-holder should undertake this observance.
"O god, tomorrow, on the fourteenth day, I shall keep vigil through the night.
I shall perform worship, gifts, austerity, and oblation according to my own power.
Having fasted on the fourteenth day, O <s>Śambhu</s>, on the following day
I shall eat for the sake of enjoyment and liberation; be my refuge, O <s>Bhaveśvara</s>."
At that time, having approached the guru, he should bathe the deity with <s>pañcagavya</s> and nectarean substances.

children.text: oṃ namo namaḥ śivāya gandhādyaḥ pūjayeddharam ||
children.translated_text: With "Oṃ, homage, homage to <s>Śiva</s>," he should worship <s>Hara</s> with sandal and the other offerings.
He should offer sesame, rice, paddy, and <s>cāru</s> mixed with ghee into the fire.
After making the oblation and giving the full offering, he should listen to songs and sacred stories.

children.text: ardharātre triyāme ca caturthe ca punayarjat
children.translated_text: At midnight, in the third watch, and again in the fourth, he should worship once more.

children.text: mūlamantraṃ tathā japtvā prabhāte tu kṣamāpayet ||
children.translated_text: Then, having recited the root mantra, he should ask forgiveness in the morning:
"O god, by your grace this vow has been worshipfully performed by me without obstacle.
Forgive me, O lord of the worlds, O <s>Hara</s>, ruler of the three worlds.
Whatever merit I have made today, whatever has been offered to <s>Rudra</s>,
by your grace, O god, this vow has now been completed by me.

children.text: prasanno bhava me śrīman gṛhaṃ prati ca gamyatām
children.translated_text: Be gracious to me, illustrious one, and return to your abode.
By the mere sight of you I have been purified; there is no doubt."
He should feed those fixed in meditation and give garments, umbrellas, and other gifts.
"O god of gods, O <s>Bhūteśa</s>, maker of benefit for the worlds,

children.text: yanmayā śraddhayā dattaṃ prīyatāṃ tena me prabhuḥ
children.translated_text: may the lord be pleased with what I have given with faith."
Having thus asked forgiveness, the vow-holder should perform it for twelve years.
Having obtained fame, prosperity, sons, kingdom, and the like, he goes to the city of <s>Śiva</s>.
In all twelve months here, too, one should perform the night vigil.

children.text: vratī dvādaśa saṃbhojya dīpadaḥ svargam āpnuyāt ||
children.translated_text: The vow-holder who feeds twelve people and gives lamps obtains heaven.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śivarātrivrataṃ nāma caturviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and twenty-fourth chapter, named the <s>Śivarātri</s> vow.
<s>Pitāmaha</s> said:
The universal emperor <s>Māndhātā</s> was a king who observed the <s>Ekādaśī</s> fast.

children.text: ekādaśyāṃ na bhuñjīta pakṣayor ubhayor api ||
children.translated_text: One should not eat on <s>Ekādaśī</s> in either of the two fortnights.
<s>Gāndhārī</s> observed an <s>Ekādaśī</s> mixed with the tenth lunar day;
her hundred sons were destroyed, and therefore one should avoid that day.
Where the twelfth lunar day and <s>Ekādaśī</s> occur together, <s>Hari</s> is present there.
Where the tenth lunar day and <s>Ekādaśī</s> occur together, an asura is present there.
When doubt arises because many statements contradict one another,

children.text: dvādaśī tu tadā grāhyā trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇam
children.translated_text: then the twelfth day should be accepted, and the breaking of the fast should be on the thirteenth.
Even if <s>Ekādaśī</s> lasts only a small portion, the twelfth day too should be fasted on.
<s>Ekādaśī</s>, the twelfth day, and especially the thirteenth day,
that lunar day mixed with the three is to be accepted; it is auspicious and removes all sin.
Having fasted on <s>Ekādaśī</s> itself, or else on the twelfth day, O twice-born one,

children.text: trimiśrāṃ caiva kurvīta na daśamyā yutāṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: one should observe the one mixed with the three, but never one joined with the tenth day.
Keeping vigil at night and listening to the <s>Purāṇa</s>, O king,
and worshipping <s>Gadādhara</s>, having fasted on the two <s>Ekādaśīs</s>,
<s>Rukmāṅgada</s> attained liberation, and others too through the <s>Ekādaśī</s> vow.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe ekādaśīmāhātmyaṃ nāma pañcaviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-twenty-fifth chapter, called "The Greatness of Ekādaśī."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Formerly, in the month of Māgha, in the bright fortnight, when it was joined with the solar asterism,
there was one Ekādaśī, and it was fasted by <s>Bhīma</s>.
Having performed that wondrous vow, he became free from debt to his ancestors.
It is renowned as Bhīma-dvādaśī, increasing the merit of living beings.
Even without the asterism, this observance destroys sins such as Brahmin-slaying.
It destroys great sin, as a bad king destroys a realm.

children.text: kuputtrastu kulaṃ yadvatkubhāryā ca patiṃ yathā
children.translated_text: As a bad son destroys a family, and as a bad wife destroys her husband,

children.text: adharmaṃ ca yathā dharmaḥ kumantrī ca yathā nṛpam ||
children.translated_text: as <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) destroys <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness), and as a bad minister destroys a king,

children.text: ajñānena yathā jñānaṃ śaucam āśaucakaṃ yathā
children.translated_text: as knowledge destroys ignorance, and purity destroys impurity,

children.text: aśraddhayā yathā śraddhā satyaṃ caivānṛtair yathā ||
children.translated_text: as faith destroys lack of faith, and truth indeed destroys falsehoods,
as heat strikes down snow, and the accumulation of wealth destroys misfortune,
as a gift is spoiled by an improper performer, and austerity by vanity,
as a son is spoiled by lack of training, and cows by wandering far away,
as peace is spoiled by anger, and wealth by lack of increase,
as learning is affected by knowledge, and as fruit is gained by freedom from desire,
so this auspicious Dvādaśī has been taught for the destruction of sin.
Brahmin-slaying, drinking liquor, theft, and intercourse with the wife of one's guru:
when these have arisen all at once, this Tripuṣkara-like observance destroys them.

children.text: na cāpi naimiṣaṃ kṣetraṃ kurukṣetraṃ prabhāsakam
children.translated_text: Neither the sacred field of <s>Naimiṣa</s>, nor <s>Kurukṣetra</s>, nor <s>Prabhāsa</s>,

children.text: kālindī yamunā gaṅgā na caiva na sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: nor the <s>Kālindī</s>, <s>Yamunā</s>, <s>Gaṅgā</s>, nor indeed <s>Sarasvatī</s>,
nor all sacred fords are equal to Ekādaśī.

children.text: na dānaṃ na japo homo na cānyatsukṛtaṃ kvacit ||
children.translated_text: There is no gift, no recitation, no fire-offering, and no other good deed anywhere equal to it.
On one side is the gift of the earth; on the other side is the day of <s>Hari</s>.
Greater even than that, this excellent Ekādaśī is of great merit.
On this day, having made a golden image of the god as the <s>Varāha</s> person,

children.text: ghaṭopari nave pātre kṛtvā vai tāmrabhājane ||
children.translated_text: and having placed it upon a water-pot in a new vessel, indeed in a copper dish,
filled with all seeds, O Brahmins, and covered with a white cloth,
one should carefully perform worship with gold, lamps, and the other requisites.

children.text: varāhāya namaḥ pādau kroḍākṛtaye namaḥ kaṭim
children.translated_text: One should worship the feet, saying "obeisance to <s>Varāha</s>," and the waist, saying "obeisance to him of boar form."
One should worship the navel as belonging to the deep-voiced one, and the chest as belonging to the bearer of <s>Śrīvatsa</s>.
One should worship the arms as belonging to the thousand-headed one, and the neck as belonging to the lord of all.

children.text: mukhaṃ sarvātmane pūjyaṃ lalāṭaṃ prabhavāya ca ||
children.translated_text: The face should be worshiped as belonging to the self of all, and the forehead as belonging to the source.
The hair of the discus-bearing god should be worshiped as belonging to the hundred-rayed one.

children.text: vidhinā pūjayitvā tu kṛtvā jāgaraṇaṃ niśi ||
children.translated_text: Having worshiped according to rule, one should keep vigil at night.
After hearing a Purāṇa that expounds the greatness of the god,

children.text: prātarviprāya dattvā ca yācakāya śubhāya tat ||
children.translated_text: in the morning one should give that auspicious object to a Brahmin who asks for it.
Having presented the furnishings together with the golden boar,
afterward one should break the fast, not over-sated, as one who has completed the vow.

children.text: evaṃ kṛtvā naro vidyānna bhūyastanapo bhavet
children.translated_text: A man who has done this should know that he will not again become afflicted.
By fasting on the meritorious Ekādaśī, he is freed from the three debts.
By performing all the vows and the rest, he obtains what his mind desires.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe ekādaśīmāhātmyaṃ nāma saptaviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-twenty-seventh chapter, called "The Greatness of Ekādaśī."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:

children.text: vratāni vyāsa vakṣyāmi yaistuṣṭaḥ sarvado hariḥ
children.translated_text: O <s>Vyāsa</s>, I shall explain the vows by which <s>Hari</s>, the giver of all, is pleased.

children.text: śāstrodito hi niyamo vrataṃ tacca tapo matam ||
children.translated_text: The rule enjoined by scripture is a vow, and that is regarded as austerity.
The particular observances of this vow are self-restraint and the like.
One should bathe three times each day, sleep on the ground, and have the senses conquered.
One should avoid conversation with women, Śūdras, and fallen persons.
One should offer the five purifying substances, as far as one is able.
A man possessed of merit should perform all these <s>kṛcchra</s> (austere penance) observances.
For the sake of preserving the hair, he should perform the vow in double measure.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ māṣaṃ masūraṃ ca caṇakaṃ koradūṣakam
children.translated_text: One who is fasting should avoid bell-metal, māṣa beans, lentils, chickpeas, and kodrava grain,

children.text: śākaṃ madhu parānnaṃ ca varjayed upavāsavān ||
children.translated_text: greens, honey, and food belonging to another.
Flowers, ornaments, garments, incense, perfume, and anointing,
as well as tooth-cleaning and collyrium, spoil a fast.
Having used a tooth-stick and the five products of the cow, one should perform the vow in the morning.
From drinking water repeatedly and from chewing betel,
a fast is spoiled, and also from sleeping by day and from sexual intercourse.
Forbearance, truth, compassion, giving, purity, and restraint of the senses,
worship of the gods, offerings into fire, contentment, and non-stealing:
this tenfold <s>dharma</s> (discipline) is remembered as common to all vows.
A nighttime meal is after the sight of the stars; a non-night meal is eating at night.

children.text: gomūtraṃ ca palaṃ dadyādardhāṅguṣṭhaṃ tu gomayam ||
children.translated_text: One should give one pala of cow urine and cow dung of half a thumb's measure.
One should give seven palas of milk and three palas of curds.
One should give one phala of ghee and one pala of water infused with kuśa grass.

children.text: gāyattryā caiva gandheti āpyāyasva dṛ dadhigrahaḥ
children.translated_text: With the <s>Gāyatrī</s> and the mantras beginning "gandha," "āpyāyasva," and the formula for taking curds,
and with "tejo 'si," one should perform the god's brahmakūrca vow.
The establishing of sacred fires, consecrations, sacrifices, gifts, and vows,
Vedic vows, the release of a bull, tonsure, and the investiture with the girdle,
auspicious rites and ablutions should be avoided in an intercalary month.
The lunar month is from new moon to new moon; the sāvana month consists of thirty days.
The solar month is reckoned from the sun's ingress, and the nakṣatra month by the twenty-seven asterisms.
The solar month is for marriage; for sacrifices and the like the sāvana reckoning applies.
Pairs, fires, yugas, elements, the six, sages, Vasus, and apertures...
The twelfth lunar day joined with <s>Rudra</s>, and then the full-moon day joined with the fourteenth,
and even the first lunar day and the new-moon day: the observance of these tithis has great fruit.

children.text: etadvyastaṃ mahāghoraṃ hanti puṇyaṃ purā kṛtam ||
children.translated_text: If this is inverted, it is very terrible and destroys the merit formerly performed.

children.text: prārabdhatapasā strīṇāṃ rajo hanyādvrataṃ na hi
children.translated_text: For women whose austerity has already begun, menstruation does not destroy the vow.
She should have gifts and the like done by others, but bodily acts she should do herself.
If a breach of the vow occurs from anger, negligence, or greed,

children.text: dinatrayaṃ na bhuñjīta śiraso muṇḍanaṃ bhavet ||
children.translated_text: one should not eat for three days, and there should be shaving of the head.
When the body is incapable, one should have sons and others perform the vow.
If a Brahmin observing a vow has fainted, one should make him drink water and the like.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vrataparibhāṣā nāmāṣṭāviṃśatyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and twenty-eighth chapter, named the definition of vows.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall teach the vows beginning with the first lunar day; listen, O <s>Vyāsa</s>.
One goes to the state of <s>Vaiśvānara</s>; this is remembered as the <s>Śikhi</s> vow.
On the first lunar day one should eat one meal, and at the completion give a tawny cow.
Beginning with <s>Caitra</s>, one should perform worship of <s>Brahmā</s> according to rule,
with sandal, flowers, acts of worship, gifts, garlands, and other pleasing things.
Together with oblations one should worship the god, and one obtains all desires.

children.text: kārtike ta site 'ṣṭamyāṃ puṣpahārī ca vatsaram ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Kārttika</s>, on the bright eighth, one should subsist on flowers for a year.
A man who gives flowers and the like becomes possessed of beauty in form.
In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, on the third day of the dark fortnight, one should worship <s>Śrīdhara</s> together with <s>Śrī</s>.
In the rite of the unempty bed, one should give fruit to a twice-born man.

children.text: śayyāṃ dattvā prārthayecca śrīdharāya namaḥ śriyai ||
children.translated_text: Having given a bed, one should pray, "Homage to <s>Śrīdhara</s>; homage to <s>Śrī</s>."

children.text: umāṃ śivaṃ hutāśaṃ ca tṛtīyāyāṃ ca pūjayet
children.translated_text: On the third day one should worship <s>Umā</s>, <s>Śiva</s>, and <s>Hutāśa</s>.

children.text: haviṣyam annaṃ naivedyaṃ deyaṃ damanakaṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: Cooked sacrificial food should be given as the offering, and likewise damanaka.
Beginning with <s>Caitra</s>, one obtains the fruit; this was declared to me by <s>Umā</s>.
Whoever avoids salt on the third day beginning with <s>Phālguna</s>,
at the completion should give a bed and a house furnished with implements.
Having worshipped a Brahmin couple, he should say, "May <s>Bhavānī</s> be pleased."
He dwells forever in the world of <s>Gaurī</s>; this is the supreme bringer of good fortune.

children.text: gaurī kālī umā bhadrā durgā kāntiḥ sarasvatī ||
children.translated_text: <s>Gaurī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Umā</s>, <s>Bhadrā</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Kānti</s>, and <s>Sarasvatī</s>,

children.text: maṅgalā vaiṣṇavī lakṣmīḥ śivā nārāyaṇī kramāt
children.translated_text: <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>, <s>Lakṣmī</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, and <s>Nārāyaṇī</s>, in sequence:
beginning with the third day in the month of <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, one obtains such fruits as non-separation.
On the fourth day, beginning with bright <s>Māgha</s>, fasting and devoted to the vow,

children.text: dattvā tilāṃstu viprāya svayaṃ bhuṅkte tilodakam ||
children.translated_text: having given sesame seeds to a Brahmin, he himself drinks sesame-water.
The completion is in two years, and he obtains such fruits as freedom from obstacles.
"Gaḥ svāhā" is this root mantra, joined with the praṇava.

children.text: glaiṃ glāṃ hṛdaye gāṃ gīṃ hūṃ hrīṃ hrīṃ śiraḥ śikhā
children.translated_text: "Glaiṃ, glāṃ" are for the heart; "gāṃ, gīṃ, hūṃ, hrīṃ, hrīṃ" for the head and topknot.

children.text: gūṃ varma goṃ ca gaiṃ netraṃ goṃ ca āvāhanādiṣu ||
children.translated_text: "Gūṃ" is for the armor, and "goṃ" and "gaiṃ" for the eyes; "goṃ" is also used in invocation and the rest.
"Come, for <s>Ulkā</s>; <s>Gaṇandholka</s>; <s>Puṣpolka</s>; <s>Dhūpakolkaka</s>;
for <s>Dīpolkā</s>; for <s>Maholkā</s>;" then there is the offering and dismissal.
For <s>Siddholkā</s> too the gāyatrī is stated, along with nyāsa beginning with the thumb.

children.text: oṃ mahākarṇāya vidmahe vakratuṇḍāya dhīmahi tanno dantiḥ pracodayāt ||
children.translated_text: "Oṃ, may we know the great-eared one; may we meditate on the curved-trunked one; may that tusked one impel us."
One should worship with sesame oblations, and these gaṇas too are to be worshipped.
"Svāhā to <s>Gaṇa</s> and to <s>Gaṇapati</s>, and to <s>Kūṣmāṇḍaka</s>;
to <s>Amogholkā</s>, to the one-tusked one, to him whose form is the destroyer of <s>Tripura</s>;
Oṃ, homage indeed to the dark-toothed, terrible-faced <s>Āhavepa</s>."

children.text: padmadaṃṣṭrāya svāhānte mudrā vai nartanaṃ gaṇe
children.translated_text: At the end, with "svāhā" to the lotus-fanged one; in worship of <s>Gaṇa</s> there should be mudrā and dancing,
clapping of the hands and laughter; the fruit is good fortune and the like.
Likewise, in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, on the bright fourth day, one should worship <s>Gaṇa</s>.
Within a year one obtains learning, prosperity, fame, long life, and a line of sons.
On a Monday that is the fourth day, having fasted fully, one should worship <s>Gaṇa</s>.
Reciting, sacrificing, and remembering the vidyā, one goes to heaven and to nirvāṇa.
Whoever worships on the bright fourth day with broken sweets, laḍḍukas, and modakas,
through worship of the remover of obstacles obtains all desires and good fortune.
The fourth day called <s>Damanā</s>, with damanaka offerings, grants sons and the like.
With "Āṃ, homage to <s>Gaṇapati</s>," one should worship <s>Gaṇa</s> through the fourth day.
In whatever month it may be, one should offer oblations, recite, or remember.
One obtains all desires; it is the destruction of all obstacles.
One should worship <s>Vināyaka</s>, beginning with the image, by these names.
He too obtains a good destiny, as well as the happiness of heaven and liberation.
<s>Gaṇapūjya</s>, <s>Vakratuṇḍa</s>, <s>Ekadaṃṣṭrī</s>, <s>Tryambaka</s>,
<s>Nīlagrīva</s>, <s>Lambodara</s>, <s>Vikaṭa</s>, and <s>Vighnarājaka</s>,
<s>Dhūmravarṇa</s>, <s>Bhālacandra</s>, <s>Daśamasta</s>, and <s>Vināyaka</s>,
<s>Gaṇapati</s> and <s>Hastimukha</s>: with these twelve forms one should worship <s>Gaṇa</s>.
Separately and collectively, the wise person obtains all desires.

children.text: śrāvaṇe cāśvine bhādre pañcamyāṃ kāttika śubhe ||
children.translated_text: In <s>Śrāvaṇa</s>, <s>Āśvina</s>, <s>Bhādra</s>, and auspicious <s>Kārttika</s>, on the fifth day,
<s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, <s>Kālīya</s>, and <s>Maṇibhadra</s>,
<s>Airāvata</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, and <s>Dhanañjaya</s>:
when these are bathed with ghee and the like, they bestow long life, health, and prosperity.

children.text: anantaṃ vāsukiṃ śaṅkhaṃ padmaṃ kambalameva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Vāsuki</s>, <s>Śaṅkha</s>, <s>Padma</s>, and also <s>Kambala</s>,

children.text: tathā karkoṭakaṃ nāgaṃ dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca śaṅkhakam
children.translated_text: likewise the nāga <s>Karkoṭaka</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, and <s>Śaṅkhaka</s>,

children.text: kālīyaṃ takṣakaṃ caiva piṅgalaṃ māsi māsi ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kālīya</s>, <s>Takṣaka</s>, and <s>Piṅgala</s>, month by month:
in bright <s>Bhādra</s> one should worship the eight nāgas, and he goes to liberation and heaven.

children.text: dvārasyobhayato lekhyāḥ śrāvaṇe tu site yajet ||
children.translated_text: They should be drawn on both sides of the door; in bright <s>Śrāvaṇa</s> one should worship
on the fifth day the nāgas, the great serpents beginning with <s>Ananta</s>.
Milk and ghee should be given as the food offering; it removes every poison.
The <s>Nāgas</s> should have hands granting fearlessness, and the fifth day is for rescuing one who has been bitten.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe daṣṭoddhārapañcamavritaṃ nāmaikonatriṃśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and twenty-ninth chapter, named the vow of the fifth day for rescuing the bitten.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Thus, in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, one should worship <s>Kārtikeya</s>.
All bathing, gifts, and the rest on this day are said to be imperishable.
On the seventh day he should also feed Brahmins with food and should worship the Sun.

children.text: oṃ khakholkāyāmṛtatvaṃ priyasaṅgamo bhava sadā svāhā ||
children.translated_text: "Oṃ, in the vault of heaven, may there always be immortality and union with what is dear; svāhā."
On the eighth day he should break the fast; having eaten pepper, he becomes a sharer in heaven.
On the seventh day, restrained, having bathed and worshipped the <s>Divākara</s>,
he should give fruits to Brahmins, saying, "May <s>Mārtaṇḍa</s> be pleased."
He should eat a date, a coconut, or a citron.

children.text: sarve bhavantu saphalā mama kāmāḥ samantataḥ
children.translated_text: "May all my desires everywhere become fruitful."
Having worshipped the god on the seventh day, he should then feed them with milk-rice.

children.text: viprāṃśca dakṣiṇāṃ dattvā svayaṃ cātha payaḥ pibet
children.translated_text: After giving a fee to the Brahmins, he himself should then drink milk.

children.text: bhakṣyaṃ coṣyaṃ tathā lehyaṃ odanaṃ ceti kīrtitam ||
children.translated_text: Food to be chewed, sucked, licked, and cooked rice are thus mentioned.
But one who desires wealth, sons, and the like should give up this foodless observance.
Living on air, he should conquer hunger and should perform the <s>Vijaya-saptamī</s>.
One who desires his wish should eat arka; by fasting he crosses over intoxication.
Wheat, beans, barley, sixty-day rice, a bronze vessel, stone-ground food, honey, sexual intercourse, liquor, and meat,

children.text: abhyañjanāñjanatilāṃśca vivarjayedyaḥ tasyeṣitaṃ bhavati saptasu saptamīṣu ||
children.translated_text: and oiling the body, collyrium, and sesame: for the man who avoids these on the seven seventh days, what he desires comes to pass.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe saptamīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma triṃśottaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and thirtieth chapter, named the exposition of the <s>Saptamī</s> vow.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
O <s>Brahman</s>, in the month of <s>Bhādrapada</s>, having fasted on the bright eighth day,

children.text: dūrvāṃ saurīṃ gaṇeśaṃ ca phalapuṣpaiḥ śivaṃ yajet ||
children.translated_text: one should worship <s>Dūrvā</s>, <s>Saurī</s>, <s>Gaṇeśa</s>, and <s>Śiva</s> with fruits and flowers.

children.text: phalavrīhyādibhiḥ sarvaiḥ śambhave namaḥ śivāya ca
children.translated_text: With fruits, rice, and all such things, saying, "Homage to <s>Śambhu</s> and to auspicious <s>Śiva</s>."
"You, O <s>Dūrvā</s>, are born of nectar; indeed the eighth day grants all desires."
He should eat what has not been cooked by fire; he is freed from the killing of a Brahmin.
On the dark eighth day, when it is joined with <s>Rohiṇī</s>, worship of <s>Hari</s> should be performed at midnight.

children.text: kāryā viddhāpi saptamyā hanti pāpaṃ trijanmanaḥ
children.translated_text: Even if it is pierced by the seventh day, it destroys the sin of three births.
Having fasted, he should worship with mantras, and the breaking of the fast should be at the end of the lunar day.

children.text: yogāya yogapataye yogeśvarāya yogasambhavāya govindāya namonamaḥ
children.translated_text: "Repeated homage to <s>Govinda</s>, to Yoga, to the lord of Yoga, to the master of Yoga, to the source of Yoga."
"Repeated homage to <s>Govinda</s>, to Sacrifice, to the lord of Sacrifice, to the master of Sacrifice."
"Repeated homage to <s>Govinda</s>, to the All, to the lord of the All, to the master of the All."

children.text: sarvāya sarveśvarāya sarvetāya sarvasambhavāya govindāya namonamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: "Repeated homage to <s>Govinda</s>, to the One who is all, to the lord of all, to the one whose self is all, to the source of all."
He should worship the god on a prepared altar, and also <s>Rohiṇī</s> together with the Moon.
Taking water in a conch, along with flowers, fruits, and sandal paste,
and going down to the ground on his knees, he should present an arghya to the Moon.
"Born from the ocean of milk, arisen from the eye of <s>Atri</s>,
accept my arghya, O lord of the moon, together with <s>Rohiṇī</s>."

children.text: śriyai ca vasudevāya nandāya ca balāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Then he should give an arghya furnished with fruit to <s>Śrī</s>, to <s>Vasudeva</s>, to <s>Nanda</s>, and to <s>Bala</s>,
and then to <s>Yaśodā</s>.
He should recite <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Vāmana</s>, <s>Śauri</s>, <s>Vaikuṇṭha</s>, <s>Puruṣottama</s>,
<s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Hṛṣīkeśa</s>, <s>Mādhava</s>, and <s>Madhusūdana</s>,
<s>Varāha</s>, <s>Puṇḍarīkākṣa</s>, <s>Nṛsiṃha</s>, and <s>Daityasūdana</s>,
<s>Dāmodara</s>, <s>Padmanābha</s>, <s>Keśava</s>, and <s>Gāruḍadhvaja</s>,
<s>Govinda</s>, <s>Acyuta</s>, the god <s>Ananta</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>,
<s>Adhokṣaja</s>, the seed of the world, the cause of creation, continuance, and end,
beginningless and endless <s>Viṣṇu</s>, lord of the three worlds, <s>Trivikrama</s>,
<s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, four-armed, bearer of conch, discus, and mace,
wearing yellow garments, divine, adorned with a forest garland,
marked with the <s>Śrīvatsa</s>, abode of the world, lord of <s>Śrī</s>, bearer of <s>Śrī</s>, <s>Hari</s>,
the god whom the goddess <s>Devakī</s> bore from <s>Vasudeva</s>.

children.text: bhaumasya brahmaṇo guptyai tasmai brahmātmane namaḥ
children.translated_text: To him, whose self is brahman, for the protection of earthly and brahmanical order, homage.
Having recited these names, he should again pray for a path onward:
"Rescue me, O lord of the gods, O <s>Hari</s>, from the ocean of saṃsāra.
Rescue me, O lord, destroyer of all sins, from the ocean of pain and grief.
O son of <s>Devakī</s>, lord of <s>Śrī</s>, O <s>Hari</s>, rescue me from the ocean of saṃsāra.
O <s>Viṣṇu</s>, you rescue the ill-conducted who remember you again and again.
I am that one, O god, exceedingly ill-conducted; rescue me from the ocean of grief.
O lotus-eyed one, I am sunk in the great ocean of ignorance.

children.text: trāhi māṃ devadeveśa tvāmṛte 'nyo na rakṣitā
children.translated_text: Rescue me, O lord of the gods; apart from you there is no protector.
Homage again and again to <s>Vāsudeva</s>, for his own birth, for the welfare of cows and Brahmins,
and to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, to <s>Govinda</s>, for the welfare of the world.
May there be peace and may there be auspiciousness; may one obtain wealth, renown, and kingship."

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe kṛṣṇāṣṭamīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāmaikatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and thirty-first chapter, named the exposition of the <s>Kṛṣṇāṣṭamī</s> vow.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Eating only at night until the eighth day, and at the end of the year giving a cow,
one goes to the station of <s>Purandara</s>; this is called the <s>Sadgati</s> vow.
On the bright eighth day in the month of <s>Pauṣa</s>, the words "Great <s>Rudra</s>" are indeed proper.
"For my pleasure, O goddess, what has been done has the fruit of a hundred thousand."
When the eighth lunar day falls on a Wednesday in either of the two fortnights,
then on that day this vow is to be performed, and its excellent story is to be told.
Those who keep the observance on that day will not have their prosperity broken.
Taking eight handfuls of rice, with two finger-breadths set aside,
a person who desires liberation should, with true devotion and faith, prepare the food.

children.text: āmraṃ patrapuṭe kṛtvā yo bhuṅkte kuśaveṣṭite ||
children.translated_text: Whoever eats it with mango placed in a leaf-packet wrapped in <s>kuśa</s> grass,
together with <s>kalambikā</s> and sour relish, obtains the desired fruit from it.
Having worshipped <s>Budha</s> with the five offerings at a body of water,
he should give, according to his ability, a water-pot with rice as the priestly fee.
The seed-mantra is “buṃ budhāya,” ending with “svāhā”; the lotus and the rest are used.
He should visualize the dark one holding arrow and bow, with the limbs on the petals and in the center.
The meritorious story of <s>Budhāṣṭamī</s> should certainly be heard by the wise.
In the city called <s>Pāṭaliputra</s> there was an excellent twice-born man named <s>Vīra</s>.

children.text: rambhā bhāryā tasya cāsītkauśikaḥ putra uttamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His wife was <s>Rambhā</s>, and his excellent son was <s>Kauśika</s>.
He had a daughter named <s>Vijayā</s>, and there was a bull that served as a forest-guard.

children.text: gṛhītvā kauśikastaṃ ca grīṣme gaṅgāṃ gato 'ramat ||
children.translated_text: Taking that bull, <s>Kauśika</s> went to the <s>Gaṅgā</s> in summer and played there.
While he was absorbed in play with cowherds, the bull was forcibly carried off by thieves.

children.text: gaṅgātaḥ sa ca utthāya vanaṃ babhrāma duḥkhitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Rising from the <s>Gaṅgā</s>, he wandered through the forest in distress.

children.text: jalārthaṃ vijayā cāgādbhrātrā sārdhaṃ ca sāpyagāt
children.translated_text: <s>Vijayā</s> had come for water, and she too went along with her brother.
Thirsty and seeking lotus-fibers, he then came to a lake.
There he saw the worship and other rites of divine women, and he was astonished.

children.text: sa tā gatvā yayāce 'nnaṃ sānujo 'haṃ bubhukṣitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Going to them, he begged for food: “I am hungry, together with my younger sibling.”
The women said, “We will give you food for performing the vow; perform the vow.”
For the sake of a wife and for the sake of wealth, the two worshipped <s>Budha</s>.
Taking two leaf-packets of food, they ate what had been given.
When the women had gone, the two saw the wealth-giving result and the means of livelihood.
Then, receiving what the thieves had given back, he reached home at dusk.

children.text: vīraṃ ca duḥkhitaṃ natvā rātrau supto yathāsukham ||
children.translated_text: Having bowed to the sorrowing <s>Vīra</s>, he slept comfortably through the night.

children.text: kanyāṃ ca yuvatīṃ dṛṣṭvā kasmai deyā sutā mayā
children.translated_text: Seeing his daughter grown into a young woman, he thought, “To whom shall my daughter be given?”
In sorrow he said, “To <s>Yama</s>”; through proper conduct, the vow bore its true fruit.

children.text: svargaṃ gatau ca pitarau vrataṃ rājyāya kauśikaḥ
children.translated_text: The parents went to heaven, and <s>Kauśika</s> performed the vow for the sake of kingship.
He obtained the great kingdom of <s>Ayodhyā</s> after giving his sister to <s>Yama</s>.

children.text: yamo 'pi vijayāmāha gṛhasthā bhava me pure
children.translated_text: <s>Yama</s> also said to <s>Vijayā</s>, “Dwell as mistress of my household in my city.”

children.text: nodghāṭayāny atra gate yame sā na tathākarot
children.translated_text: “Do not open this when I have gone away”; but when <s>Yama</s> had gone, she did not act accordingly.
She saw her own mother standing in torment from a noose.
Then, shaken, and knowing from <s>Kauśika</s> of the vow that grants liberation,

children.text: cakre ca sā tato muktā mātā tasmāccaredvratam ||
children.translated_text: she performed it, and then her mother was freed; therefore one should practice the vow.
By the power of the merit of the vow, she went to heaven and dwelt happily there.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe budhāṣṭamīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma dvātriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and thirty-second chapter, named the explanation of the <s>Budhāṣṭamī</s> vow.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Those who drink eight buds of the <s>aśoka</s> tree under <s>Punarvasu</s>,

children.text: caitre māsi sitāṣṭamyāṃ na te śokamavāpnuyuḥ ||
children.translated_text: on the bright eighth lunar day in the month of <s>Caitra</s>, do not come to grief.
“O <s>Aśoka</s>, beloved of <s>Hara</s>, born in the spring month, remover of what is desired,
I drink you while afflicted by sorrow; always make me free from sorrow.”
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
The bright eighth lunar day in <s>Āśvayuja</s>, when joined with <s>Uttarāṣāḍhā</s>,
is called <s>Mahānavamī</s>; bathing, gifts, and the like on it are imperishable.

children.text: navamī kevalā cāpi durgāṃ caiva tu pūjayet
children.translated_text: On the ninth lunar day alone as well, one should worship <s>Durgā</s>.
This is a great vow of great merit, practiced by <s>Śaṅkara</s> and others.
Beginning with the sixth day, with such practices as eating only what has not been begged, and for a king’s victory over enemies,
one should always feed a maiden, accompanied by recitation and fire-offering.

children.text: durge durge rakṣiṇi svāhā mantro 'yaṃ pūjanādiṣu
children.translated_text: “O <s>Durgā</s>, O <s>Durgā</s>, protector, svāhā”: this is the mantra in worship and the other rites.
With long vowels and the other measures, the nine goddesses have formulas ending in “namaḥ.”
With six words, and with “namaḥ,” “svāhā,” “vaṣaṭ,” and the rest, one performs the heart and other placements.
Having assigned them from the thumb through the little finger, one should worship <s>Śivā</s>.
On the eighth day, nine wooden shrines should be made, or even just one.

children.text: tasmindevī prakartavyā haimī vā rājatāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: In that shrine the goddess should be fashioned, either of gold or of silver.

children.text: śūle khaḍge pustake vā paṭe vā maṇḍale yajet
children.translated_text: One may worship her on a trident, on a sword, in a book, on a cloth, or in a <s>maṇḍala</s>.

children.text: kapālaṃ kheṭakaṃ ghaṇṭāṃ darpaṇaṃ tarjanīṃ dhanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: She bears a skull, shield, bell, mirror, threatening finger, and bow,
as well as a banner, a <s>ḍamaru</s> drum, and a noose in her left hands;

children.text: śaktiṃ ca mudgaraṃ śūlaṃ vajraṃ khaḍgaṃ tathāṅkuśam ||
children.translated_text: and a spear, club, trident, thunderbolt, sword, and likewise a goad,
an arrow, discus, and spike: thus <s>Durgā</s> is furnished with weapons.
The remaining forms are to have sixteen hands, apart from the collyrium and the <s>ḍamaru</s>.
<s>Rudracaṇḍā</s>, <s>Pracaṇḍā</s>, <s>Caṇḍogrā</s>, and <s>Caṇḍanāyikā</s>,
<s>Caṇḍā</s>, <s>Caṇḍavatī</s>, <s>Caṇḍarūpā</s>, and <s>Aticaṇḍikā</s> are named.
The ninth is <s>Ugracaṇḍā</s>, placed in the middle, with the radiance of fire.

children.text: rocanā tvaruṇā kṛṣṇā nīlaṃ dhūmrā ca śukrakā ||
children.translated_text: The colors are yellow, reddish, black, blue, smoky, and white.

children.text: pātā ca pāṇḍurā proktā ālīḍhaṃ haritaṃ tathā
children.translated_text: Pale and whitish are also taught, and the <s>ālīḍha</s> stance is green.
Her buffalo is described with sword-tip, disheveled hair, grasping hand, and clenched fist.

children.text: japtvā daśākṣarīṃ vidyāṃ nāsau kenāpi badhyate
children.translated_text: Having recited the ten-syllable spell, he is not bound by anyone.

children.text: pañcadaśāṅgulaṃ khaḍgaṃ triśūlaṃ ca tato yajet
children.translated_text: Then he should worship a sword fifteen finger-breadths long and a trident.
Or he may worship in a <s>liṅga</s>, in sandals, or even in water.
He should guard the elaborate worship and fast on the eighth lunar day.

children.text: pañcābdaṃ mahiṣaṃ bastaṃ rātriśeṣe ca ghātayet ||
children.translated_text: At the end of the night he should sacrifice a five-year-old buffalo or a goat.
According to rule, saying “<s>Kālī</s>, <s>Kālī</s>,” he should use the blood and other substances arising from it.
In the southwest he should place <s>Pūtanā</s>, and in the northwest <s>Pāparākṣasī</s>.
He should give the offering to <s>Carakī</s> in the northeast, and <s>Vidārikā</s> in the southeast.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe mahānavamīvrataṃ nāma trayastriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-thirty-third chapter, called "The Mahānavamī Vow."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Now the <s>Mahākauśika</s> mantra, which has great fruit, is taught here.
Oṃ, obeisance to <s>Mahākauśika</s>.

children.text: oṃ hūṃ hūṃ prasphura lala lala kulva kulva culva culva khalla khalla mulva mulva gulva gulva tulva pulla pulla dhalva dhulva dhuma dhuma dhama dhama māraya māraya dhaka dhaka vajñāpaya jñāpaya vidāraya vidāraya kampa kampa kampaya kampaya pūraya pūraya āveśayāveśaya oṃ hrīṃ oṃ hrīṃ haṃ vaṃ vaṃ huṃ taṭa taṭa mada mada hrīṃ oṃ hūṃ nairṛtāyā namaḥ nirṛtaye dātavyam
children.translated_text: Oṃ hūṃ hūṃ, blaze forth; lala lala, kulva kulva, culva culva, khalla khalla, mulva mulva, gulva gulva, tulva; pulla pulla, dhalva dhulva, dhuma dhuma, dhama dhama; kill, kill; strike, strike; make known, make known; split, split; shake, shake, cause to shake; fill, fill; enter, enter. Oṃ hrīṃ, oṃ hrīṃ, haṃ vaṃ vaṃ huṃ, taṭa taṭa, mada mada, hrīṃ, oṃ hūṃ. Obeisance to <s>Nairṛta</s>; it should be given to <s>Nirṛti</s>.
With the <s>Mahākauśika</s> mantra one should offer a bali (food offering) that has been consecrated by mantra.

children.text: tasyāgrato nṛpaḥ snāyācchatraṃ kṛtvā ca paiṣṭikam
children.translated_text: In front of it the king should bathe, having made an umbrella out of flour-paste,
and, after striking it with a sword, he should give it to <s>Skanda</s> and <s>Viśākha</s>.

children.text: mātṝṇāṃ caiva devīnāṃ pūjā kāryā tathā niśi
children.translated_text: At night worship should also be performed for the Mothers and the goddesses:

children.text: brahmāṇī caiva māheśī kaumārī vaiṣṇavī tathā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Brahmāṇī</s>, <s>Māheśī</s>, <s>Kaumārī</s>, and likewise <s>Vaiṣṇavī</s>,

children.text: vārāhī caiva māhendrī cāmuṇḍā caṇḍikā tathā
children.translated_text: <s>Vārāhī</s>, <s>Māhendrī</s>, <s>Cāmuṇḍā</s>, and also <s>Caṇḍikā</s>,
<s>Jayantī</s>, <s>Maṅgalā</s>, <s>Kālī</s>, <s>Bhadrakālī</s>, and <s>Kapālinī</s>:

children.text: durgā kṣamā śivā dhātrī svāhā svadhā namo 'stu te
children.translated_text: "<s>Durgā</s>, <s>Kṣamā</s>, <s>Śivā</s>, <s>Dhātrī</s>, <s>Svāhā</s>, <s>Svadhā</s>, obeisance to you."
One should bathe the goddess with milk and the other substances, and likewise maidens and women.
Then one should honor twice-born men and even heterodox ascetics by giving food.
With banners, leaf-decorations, flags, and the like, and with cloths during chariot processions,
this worship on Mahānavamī bestows victory, sovereignty, and the like.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe mahānavamyāṃ mahākauśikamantrakṛtyādivivaraṇaṃ nāma catustriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-thirty-fourth chapter, called "The Explanation of the Mahākauśika Mantra Rite and Other Matters on Mahānavamī."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
On the bright ninth day of Āśvina one should worship with a single meal as the observance.

children.text: devīṃ vipraṃllakṣam ekaṃ japedvīraṃ vratī naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man who undertakes the vow should worship the goddess and a Brahmin, and recite the heroic mantra one hundred thousand times.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
On the bright ninth day in Caitra one should worship the goddess with damanaka plants.
He obtains long life, health, and good fortune, and is unconquered by enemies.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
On the tenth day one should eat a single meal; at the end of the year one should give ten cows,
and, after giving golden images of the quarters, one becomes lord of the cosmic egg.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
On the eleventh day worship of the sages should be performed; it is beneficial in every way.
At the end one becomes wealthy and possessed of sons, and is honored in the world of the sages.
<s>Marīci</s>, <s>Atri</s>, the two <s>Aṅgirases</s>, <s>Pulastya</s>, <s>Pulaha</s>, and <s>Kratu</s>,
and <s>Pracetas</s>, <s>Vasiṣṭha</s>, <s>Bhṛgu</s>, and <s>Nārada</s>:
from the beginning of Caitra one should perform worship with garlands produced from damanaka plants.
The eighth day called <s>Aśokā</s> is taught, and likewise the ninth called <s>Vīrā</s>;
also the tenth day of the quarters called <s>Damanā</s>, and likewise the ninth and eleventh days.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe ṛṣyekādaśīvrataṃ nāma pañcatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-thirty-fifth chapter, called "The Ṛṣyekādaśī Vow."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall explain <s>Śravaṇadvādaśī</s>, which bestows enjoyment and liberation.

children.text: ekādaśī dvādaśī ca śravaṇena ca saṃyutā ||
children.translated_text: When Ekādaśī and Dvādaśī are joined with Śravaṇa,

children.text: vijayā sā tithiḥ proktā haripūjādi cākṣayam
children.translated_text: that lunar day is called <s>Vijayā</s>; worship of <s>Hari</s> and the rest on it is imperishable.
By eating once, by eating at night, likewise by eating what is received unasked,
by fasting, or by living on alms, one does not fail to be an observer of Dvādaśī.

children.text: kāṃsyaṃ māṃsaṃ tathā kṣaudraṃ lobhaṃ vitathabhāṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: A man should avoid bell-metal vessels, meat, honey, greed, and false speech,
as well as exercise, sexual intercourse, sleeping by day, and collyrium,
and food ground on a stone and lentils on Dvādaśī.
In the month of Bhādrapada, the bright Dvādaśī joined with Śravaṇa
should be known as <s>Mahatī Dvādaśī</s>; fasting on it bears great fruit.
Bathing at the confluence of rivers, when it is joined with Wednesday, bears great fruit.

children.text: kuṃbhe saratne sajale yajetsvarṇaṃ tu vāmanam ||
children.translated_text: On a water-filled jar set with jewels one should worship a golden <s>Vāmana</s>,
covered with a pair of white garments and furnished with an umbrella and a pair of sandals.
Saying "oṃ namo vāsudevāya," one should then worship the head.

children.text: śrīdharāya mukhaṃ tadvatkaṇṭhaṃ kṛṣṇāya vai namaḥ
children.translated_text: In the same way one should worship the face for <s>Śrīdhara</s> and the neck, saying "obeisance to <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>."
Saying "obeisance to <s>Śrīpati</s>," one should worship the chest, and the arms for the bearer of all weapons.
The wise man should worship the belly, saying "obeisance to the all-pervading one," and the abdomen for <s>Keśava</s>.
He should worship the generative organ for the lord of the three worlds, and the shanks, saying "obeisance to the bearer of all."
He should worship the feet, saying "obeisance to the self of all," and offer as naivedya (food offering) milk-rice with ghee.
He should give water-pots and sweet cakes, and should cause a night vigil to be kept.
Having bathed, sipped water, and worshiped, he should speak with a handful of flowers:
"Obeisance, obeisance to you, <s>Govinda</s>, O <s>Budha</s>, called <s>Śravaṇa</s>.
Having destroyed the mass of sins, become the giver of every happiness."
May the lord of the gods be pleased; one should give the pitchers to Brahmins.
Whoever performs this on the bank of a river obtains all desires.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śravaṇadvādaśīvratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma ṣaṭtriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-thirty-sixth chapter, called "The Description of the Śravaṇadvādaśī Vow."
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
On the thirteenth day <s>Kāmadeva</s> should be worshiped with damanaka plants and the like,
together with <s>Rati</s> and <s>Prīti</s>, and with <s>Aśoka</s>, adorned with jewels.
Likewise, on the fourteenth and eighth days of both the bright and dark fortnights,
Whoever for a full year does not eat becomes a participant in liberation through the worship of <s>Śiva</s>.
Having fasted for three nights, on the <s>Kārttikī</s> day he should give an auspicious dwelling.
He obtains the world of <s>Sūrya</s>; this auspicious vow is the <s>dhāma-vrata</s> (vow of the sacred abode).

children.text: amāvasyāṃ pitṝṇāṃ ca dattaṃ jalādi tad akṣayam
children.translated_text: On the new-moon day, water and the like given to the Pitṛs is imperishable.
One who practices eating only at night, worshiping the days by the names of the weekdays, becomes a possessor of every good.

children.text: dvādaśarkṣāṇi viprarṣe pratimāsaṃ tu yāni vai
children.translated_text: The twelve lunar asterisms, O Brahmin sage, which occur in each month,
in those a man should properly worship <s>Acyuta</s>, using that name at the end.
He should worship <s>Keśava</s> in <s>Mārgaśīrṣa</s>, and so on, in the sequence beginning with <s>Kṛttikā</s>.
For four months there should be ghee-offerings in the fire, and he should present <s>kṛsara</s> (rice-and-pulse food).
From <s>Āṣāḍha</s> onward he should present milk-rice, and with that same food he should feed Brahmins.
He should observe the night-meal vow with baths in water mixed with the five products of the cow and with food-offerings.
Before the dismissal, the whole substance is called <s>naivedya</s> (food-offering).
When <s>Jagannātha</s> has been dismissed, it at once becomes <s>nirmālya</s> (the deity's remnant).
The chief knowers of the <s>Pāñcarātra</s> themselves eat the <s>naivedya</s>.
In this way, at the end of the year, he should worship with special care.

children.text: namonamaste 'cyuta saṃkṣayo 'stu pāpasya vṛddhiṃ samupaitu puṇyam
children.translated_text: Again and again obeisance to you, <s>Acyuta</s>; let my sin come to an end, and let merit increase.

children.text: aiśvaryavittādi sadākṣayaṃ me tathāstu me santatirakṣayaiva ||
children.translated_text: May my sovereignty, wealth, and the rest be ever imperishable, and may my line of descendants likewise be imperishable.

children.text: yathācyuta tvaṃ parataḥ parasmātsa brahmabhūtaḥ parataḥ parasmāt
children.translated_text: As you, O <s>Acyuta</s>, are beyond the one beyond, being the state of <s>Brahman</s>, beyond the one beyond,

children.text: tathācyutaṃ me kuru vāñchitaṃ sadā mayā kṛtaṃ pāpaharāprameya ||
children.translated_text: so, O <s>Acyuta</s>, immeasurable remover of sins committed by me, always make my desired object imperishable.
O <s>Acyuta</s>, <s>Ananta</s>, <s>Govinda</s>, be gracious; whatever is desired,
make that imperishable for me, O immeasurable self, O supreme person.
A man who performs this for seven years obtains long life, prosperity, and good destinies.
Having fasted for a year on <s>Ekādaśī</s>, and also on <s>Aṣṭamī</s> and <s>Caturdaśī</s>,

children.text: saptamīṃ pūjayedviṣṇuṃ durgāṃ śambhuṃ raviṃ kramāt
children.translated_text: and on <s>Saptamī</s>, he should worship <s>Viṣṇu</s>, <s>Durgā</s>, <s>Śambhu</s>, and <s>Ravi</s>, respectively.
Pure, he obtains their worlds and all desired objects.
By taking a single meal, by eating only at night, and likewise by living on unsolicited alms,
by fasting, and by vegetables and the like, people worship all the deities.
On all lunar days everyone may obtain both enjoyment and liberation.
On <s>Pratipad</s>, <s>Dhanada</s> and <s>Agni</s> are worshiped, as are <s>Nāsatya</s> and <s>Dasra</s>.
On the second lunar day are <s>Śrī</s> and <s>Yama</s>; on the fifth are <s>Pārvatī</s> together with <s>Śrī</s>.
On the sixth are the <s>Nāgas</s>; on the seventh, <s>Kārttikeya</s>; and <s>Bhāskara</s> is the giver of wealth.
On <s>Durgāṣṭamī</s> are <s>Durgā</s> and the Mothers; then on the ninth is <s>Takṣaka</s>.
On the tenth is <s>Indra</s>; on the eleventh, <s>Dhanada</s>; and on the twelfth, the lords of sages.
On the twelfth also is <s>Hari</s>; on the thirteenth is <s>Kāma</s>; and on the fourteenth, <s>Maheśvara</s>.
On the fifteenth are <s>Brahmā</s> and the other Pitṛs.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe tithivāranakṣatrādivratanirūpaṇaṃ nāma saptatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section called the first part, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one-hundred-thirty-seventh chapter, named 'The Explanation of Vows Relating to Tithis, Weekdays, Lunar Asterisms, and the Like.'
<s>Hari</s> said:
I shall proclaim the dynasties of kings and the accounts of those dynasties.
From the lotus of <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel came <s>Brahmā</s>; and <s>Dakṣa</s> came from his thumb.
Then came <s>Vivasvān</s>, born of <s>Aditi</s>; and then the son of <s>Vivasvat</s>,
<s>Manu</s>: <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, <s>Śaryāti</s>, <s>Nṛga</s>, <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>, and <s>Pṛṣadhraka</s> were his sons.

children.text: nariṣyantaśca nābhāgo diṣṭaḥ śaśaka eva ca
children.translated_text: Also <s>Nariṣyanta</s>, <s>Nābhāga</s>, <s>Diṣṭa</s>, and <s>Śaśaka</s> were his sons.
<s>Manu</s> had a daughter, <s>Ilā</s>; <s>Sudyumna</s> became his son.

children.text: ilāyāṃ tu budhājjāto rājā rudra purūravāḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Ilā</s>, through <s>Budha</s>, was born king <s>Purūravas</s>, O <s>Rudra</s>.
From <s>Sudyumna</s> there were three sons: <s>Utkala</s>, <s>Vinata</s>, and <s>Gaya</s>.
<s>Pṛṣadhra</s>, the son of <s>Manu</s>, became a Śūdra because of cow-slaughter.
From <s>Karūṣa</s> were born Kṣatriyas, famed as the <s>Kārūṣas</s>.
<s>Nābhāga</s>, the son of <s>Diṣṭa</s>, entered the condition of a Vaiśya.
From him came the son <s>Bhalandana</s>; from <s>Bhalandana</s> came <s>Vatsaprīti</s>.
Then came <s>Pāṃśu</s>; from him <s>Khanitra</s> became king, and after him came <s>Kṣupa</s>.
From <s>Kṣupa</s> came the son <s>Viṃśa</s>; from <s>Viṃśa</s> was born <s>Viviṃśaka</s>.
From <s>Viviṃśa</s> came <s>Khanīnetra</s>; <s>Vibhūti</s> is remembered as his son.
From <s>Vibhūti</s> came <s>Karandhama</s>; from him also was born <s>Avikṣit</s>.
<s>Marutta</s> was born from <s>Avikṣit</s>; after him <s>Nariṣyanta</s> is remembered.
From <s>Nariṣyanta</s> was born <s>Tamas</s>; then came <s>Rājavardhana</s>.
From <s>Rājavardhana</s> came <s>Sudhṛti</s>; <s>Nara</s> was the son of <s>Sudhṛti</s>.
From <s>Nara</s> came the son <s>Kevala</s>; and from <s>Kevala</s> came <s>Dhundhumān</s>.
From <s>Dhundhumat</s> came <s>Vegavān</s>; <s>Budha</s> was the son of <s>Vegavat</s>.
From <s>Budha</s> was born <s>Tṛṇabindu</s>, and also the maiden <s>Ailavilā</s>.
<s>Alambuṣā</s> bore <s>Viśāla</s> from <s>Tṛṇabindu</s>.
From <s>Viśāla</s> came <s>Hemacandra</s>; from <s>Hemacandra</s> came <s>Candraka</s>.
From <s>Candra</s> came <s>Dhūmrāśva</s>, and from <s>Dhūmrāśva</s> came <s>Sṛñjaya</s>.
From <s>Sañjaya</s> came <s>Sahadeva</s>; <s>Kṛśāśva</s> was his son.
From <s>Kṛśāśva</s> came <s>Somadatta</s>; after him came <s>Janamejaya</s>.
His son was <s>Sumanti</s>; these are the <s>Vaiśālaka</s> kings.

children.text: śaryātestu sukanyābhūt sā bhāryā cyavanasya tu
children.translated_text: <s>Śaryāti</s> had <s>Sukanyā</s>; she was the wife of <s>Cyavana</s>.
<s>Ananta</s> was named as a descendant of <s>Śaryāti</s>; from <s>Ananta</s> came <s>Revata</s>.
<s>Raivata</s> was the descendant of <s>Revata</s>; from <s>Raivata</s> came the daughter <s>Revatī</s>.

children.text: dhṛṣṭasya dhārṣṭarkaṃ kṣetraṃ vaiṣṇavaṃ tad babhūva ha ||
children.translated_text: The <s>Dhārṣṭārka</s> domain of <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s> became Vaiṣṇava.
<s>Neṣṭha</s> was the son of <s>Nābhāga</s>; <s>Ambarīṣa</s> too was his son.
From <s>Ambarīṣa</s> came <s>Virūpa</s>; from <s>Virūpa</s> came <s>Pṛṣadaśva</s>.
<s>Rathīnara</s> was his son, devoted to <s>Vāsudeva</s>.
<s>Ikṣvāku</s> had three sons: <s>Vikukṣi</s>, <s>Nimi</s>, and <s>Daṇḍaka</s>.
<s>Vikukṣi</s>, born of <s>Ikṣvāku</s>, was <s>Śaśāda</s> because he ate a hare.
From <s>Śaśāda</s> came a son, <s>Purañjaya</s>, who became known as <s>Kakutstha</s>.

children.text: anenās tu kakutsthācca pṛthuḥ putras tv anenasaḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Kakutstha</s> came <s>Anenas</s>; <s>Pṛthu</s> was the son of <s>Anenas</s>.
<s>Viśvarāta</s> was the son of <s>Pṛthu</s>, and <s>Ārdra</s> was born from <s>Viśvarāta</s>.
From <s>Ārdra</s> came <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, and from <s>Yuvanāśva</s> came <s>Śāvasta</s>.
<s>Bṛhadaśva</s> came from <s>Śāvasta</s>, and his son was <s>Kuvalāśvaka</s>.

children.text: dhundhumāro hi vikhyāto dṛḍhāśvaś ca tato 'bhavat
children.translated_text: He is famed as <s>Dhundhumāra</s>; after him came <s>Dṛḍhāśva</s>.
From <s>Dṛḍhāśva</s> came <s>Candrāśva</s>, <s>Kapilāśva</s>, and <s>Haryaśva</s>.
From <s>Haryaśva</s> came <s>Nikumbha</s>, and from <s>Nikumbha</s> came <s>Hitāśva</s>.
From <s>Hitāśva</s> came <s>Pūjāśva</s>, and his son was <s>Yuvanāśvaka</s>.
From <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, by <s>Bindumatī</s>, <s>Māndhātṛ</s> was then born.
<s>Mucukunda</s>, <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and <s>Purukutsa</s> were his three sons.
There were also fifty daughters; they became the wives of the sage <s>Saubhari</s>.
From <s>Ambarīṣa</s> came <s>Yuvanāśva</s>, and from <s>Yuvanāśva</s> came <s>Harita</s>.
From <s>Purukutsa</s>, in <s>Narmadā</s>, a son <s>Trasadasyu</s> was born.
After him <s>Anaraṇya</s> was born, and from <s>Anaraṇya</s> also came <s>Haryaśva</s>.
His son was <s>Vasumanas</s>; <s>Tridhanvan</s> was his son.
<s>Trayyāruṇa</s> was his son, and his son was <s>Satyarata</s>.
He is known as <s>Triśaṅku</s>; after him came <s>Hariścandra</s>.
From <s>Hariścandra</s> came <s>Rohitāśva</s>, and from <s>Rohitāśva</s> came <s>Harita</s>.
<s>Harita</s>'s son was <s>Cañcu</s>, and <s>Cañcu</s>'s son was <s>Vijaya</s>.
From <s>Vijaya</s> <s>Ruruka</s> was born, and from <s>Ruruka</s> came a son, <s>Vṛka</s>.
From <s>Vṛka</s> came the king <s>Bāhu</s>, and <s>Sagara</s> is remembered as the son of <s>Bāhu</s>.
O <s>Hara</s>, from <s>Sagara</s>, in <s>Sumatī</s>, came sixty thousand sons.
In <s>Keśinī</s> there was only one, named <s>Asamañjasa</s>.
His learned son was <s>Aṃśumān</s>, and his son was <s>Dilīpa</s>.
From <s>Dilīpa</s> came <s>Bhagīratha</s>, who brought <s>Gaṅgā</s> down to the earth.
<s>Śruta</s> was the son of <s>Bhagīratha</s>, and from <s>Śruta</s> came <s>Nābhāga</s>, it is said.
From <s>Nābhāga</s> came <s>Ambarīṣa</s>, and from <s>Ambarīṣa</s> came <s>Sindhudvīpa</s>.
<s>Ayutāyu</s> was the son of <s>Sindhudvīpa</s>, and <s>Ṛtuparṇa</s> was his son.
From <s>Ṛtuparṇa</s> came <s>Sarvakāma</s>, and <s>Sudāsa</s> was his son.

children.text: sudāsasya ca saudāso nāmnā mitrasahaḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Sudāsa</s> was <s>Saudāsa</s>, remembered by the name <s>Mitrasaha</s>.
He was also called <s>Kalmāṣapāda</s>; in <s>Damayantī</s> his son was born.
A son named <s>Aśvaka</s> was born; from <s>Aśvaka</s> came <s>Mūlaka</s>.

children.text: tato daśaratho rājā tasya cailavilaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then came King <s>Daśaratha</s>, and his son was <s>Ailavila</s>.
His son was <s>Viśvasaha</s>, and <s>Khaṭvāṅga</s> was his son.
From <s>Khaṭvāṅga</s> came <s>Dīrghabāhu</s>, and from <s>Dīrghabāhu</s> came a son, <s>Aja</s>.
His son was <s>Daśaratha</s>, and four are remembered as his sons:
<s>Rāma</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, <s>Śatrughna</s>, and <s>Bharata</s>, all very mighty.
From <s>Rāma</s> were born <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>; from <s>Bharata</s>, <s>Tārkṣa</s> and <s>Puṣkara</s>.
<s>Citrāṅgada</s> and <s>Candraketu</s> were born from <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
<s>Subāhu</s> and <s>Śūrasena</s> were born from <s>Śatrughna</s>.

children.text: kuśasya cātithiḥ putro niṣadho hyatitheḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Atithi</s> was the son of <s>Kuśa</s>, and <s>Niṣadha</s> was the son of <s>Atithi</s>.

children.text: niṣadhasya nalaḥ putro nalasya ca nabhāḥ smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Nala</s> was the son of <s>Niṣadha</s>, and <s>Nabhas</s> is remembered as <s>Nala</s>'s son.
From <s>Nabhas</s> came <s>Puṇḍarīka</s>, and <s>Kṣemadhanvan</s> was his son.
His son was <s>Devānīka</s>, and from <s>Devānīka</s> came <s>Ahīnaka</s>.
From <s>Ahīnaka</s> came <s>Ruru</s>, and <s>Pāriyātra</s> was the son of <s>Ruru</s>.
From <s>Pāriyātra</s> came <s>Dala</s>; <s>Chala</s> is remembered as <s>Dala</s>'s son.
From <s>Chala</s> came <s>Uktha</s>, then from <s>Uktha</s> came <s>Vajranābha</s>, and after him <s>Gaṇa</s>.
<s>Uṣitāśva</s> was born from <s>Gaṇa</s>, and after him came <s>Viśvasaha</s>.
<s>Hiraṇyanābha</s> was his son, and his son is remembered as <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
From <s>Puṣpa</s> came <s>Dhruvasaṃdhi</s>, and from <s>Dhruvasaṃdhi</s> came <s>Sudarśana</s>.
From <s>Sudarśana</s> came <s>Agnivarṇa</s>, and from <s>Agnivarṇa</s> came <s>Padmavarṇa</s>.
From <s>Padmavarṇa</s> came <s>Śīghra</s>, and from <s>Śīghra</s> a son, <s>Maru</s>, was born.
<s>Prasuśruta</s> was the son of <s>Maru</s>, and his son was <s>Udāvasu</s>.
From <s>Udāvasu</s> came <s>Nandivardhana</s>, and from <s>Nandivardhana</s> came <s>Suketu</s>.
From <s>Suketu</s> came <s>Devarāta</s>, and after him a son, <s>Bṛhaduktha</s>.
From <s>Bṛhaduktha</s> came <s>Mahāvīrya</s>, and <s>Sudhṛti</s> was his son.
From <s>Sudhṛti</s> came <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, and from <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s> came <s>Haryaśva</s>.
From <s>Haryaśva</s> was born <s>Maru</s>, and from <s>Maru</s> came <s>Pratīndhaka</s>.
From <s>Pratīndhaka</s> came <s>Kṛtiratha</s>, and <s>Devamīḍha</s> was his son.
From <s>Devamīḍha</s> came <s>Vibudha</s>, and from <s>Vibudha</s> came <s>Mahādhṛti</s>.
From <s>Mahādhṛti</s> came <s>Kīrtirāta</s>, and <s>Mahāroman</s> was his son.
From <s>Mahāroman</s> came <s>Svarṇaroman</s>, and <s>Hrasvaroman</s> was his son.
<s>Sīradhvaja</s> came from <s>Hrasvaroman</s>, and <s>Sītā</s> was his daughter.
His brother was <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>; from <s>Sīradhvaja</s> came <s>Bhānumān</s>.
From <s>Bhānumat</s> came <s>Śatadyumna</s>, and from <s>Śatadyumna</s> <s>Śuci</s> is remembered.
A son of <s>Śuci</s> was named <s>Ūrja</s>, and <s>Sanadvāja</s> was his son.
From <s>Sanadvāja</s> was born <s>Kuli</s>, and <s>Anañjana</s> was the son of <s>Kuli</s>.
From <s>Anañjana</s> came <s>Kulajit</s>, and his son was <s>Adhinemika</s>.
<s>Śrutāyu</s> was his son, and <s>Supārśva</s> was his son.
From <s>Supārśva</s> was born <s>Sṛṃjaya</s>, and <s>Kṣemāri</s> is remembered as coming from <s>Sṛñjaya</s>.
From <s>Kṣemāri</s> came <s>Anenas</s>, and his son is remembered as <s>Rāmaratha</s>.
From <s>Rāmaratha</s> came <s>Satyaratha</s>, and from him <s>Upaguru</s> is remembered.
From <s>Upaguru</s> came <s>Upagupta</s>, and from <s>Upagupta</s> came <s>Svāgata</s>.
From <s>Svāgata</s> <s>Svanara</s> was born, and <s>Suvarcas</s> was his son.
From <s>Suvarcas</s> came <s>Supārśva</s>, and from <s>Supārśva</s> came <s>Suśruta</s>.
From <s>Suśruta</s> was born <s>Jaya</s>, and from <s>Jaya</s> came <s>Vijaya</s>.

children.text: vijayasya ṛtaḥ putraḥ ṛtasya sunayaḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Vijaya</s> was <s>Ṛta</s>; the son of <s>Ṛta</s> was <s>Sunaya</s>.
From <s>Sunaya</s> came <s>Vītahavya</s>, and from <s>Vītahavya</s> <s>Dhṛti</s> is remembered.
<s>Bahulāśva</s> was the son of <s>Dhṛti</s>, and from <s>Bahulāśva</s> <s>Kṛti</s> is remembered.
In the two branches of <s>Janaka</s>'s lineage, the resort to yoga has been stated.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sūryavaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāmāṣṭatriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the former section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, ends the one hundred and thirty-eighth chapter, named the description of the solar dynasty.
<s>Hari</s> said:

children.text: sūryasya kathito vaṃśaḥ somavaṃśaṃ śṛṇuṣva me
children.translated_text: The lineage of <s>Sūrya</s> has been told; now hear from me the lunar lineage.
<s>Brahmā</s> was the son of <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>; from <s>Brahmā</s> arose <s>Atri</s>.

children.text: atreḥ somastasya bhāryā tārā suraguroḥ priyā
children.translated_text: From <s>Atri</s> came <s>Soma</s>; his wife was <s>Tārā</s>, beloved of the guru of the gods.
From <s>Soma</s>, <s>Tārā</s> bore <s>Budha</s>; <s>Purūravā</s> was the son of <s>Budha</s>.
Then from <s>Budha</s>'s son, through <s>Urvaśī</s>, there were six sons, known by name:
<s>Viśvāvasu</s>, <s>Śatāyus</s>, <s>Āyus</s>, <s>Dhomāna</s>, and <s>Amāvasu</s>.
From <s>Amāvasu</s> came one named <s>Bhīma</s>, and <s>Kāñcana</s> was the son of <s>Bhīma</s>.
From <s>Kāñcana</s> came <s>Suhotra</s>, and from <s>Suhotra</s> came <s>Jahnu</s>.
From <s>Jahnu</s> came <s>Sumantu</s>, and from <s>Sumantu</s> came <s>Apajāpaka</s>.
<s>Balākāśva</s> was his son, and from <s>Balākāśva</s> <s>Kuśa</s> is remembered.
From <s>Kuśa</s> came <s>Kuśāśva</s>, <s>Kuśanābha</s>, <s>Amūrtaraya</s>, and <s>Vasu</s>.
