From <s>Kuśāśva</s> was born <s>Gādhi</s>, and <s>Viśvāmitra</s> was his son.

children.text: kanyā satyavatī dattā ṛcīkāya dvijāya sā
children.translated_text: The maiden <s>Satyavatī</s> was given to the brahmin <s>Ṛcīka</s>.
From <s>Ṛcīka</s> came <s>Jamadagni</s>, and <s>Rāma</s> was his son.
From <s>Viśvāmitra</s> came sons such as <s>Devarāta</s> and <s>Madhucchandas</s>.
From <s>Āyus</s> came <s>Nahuṣa</s>; from him came <s>Anenā</s>, <s>Raji</s>, and <s>Rambha</s>.
There was also <s>Kṣatravṛddha</s>; from <s>Kṣatravṛddha</s> was born the king <s>Suhotra</s>.
<s>Kāśya</s>, <s>Kāśa</s>, and <s>Gṛtsamada</s> were the three born from <s>Suhotra</s>.
From <s>Gṛtsamada</s> came <s>Śaunaka</s>, and likewise from <s>Kāśya</s> came <s>Dīrghatamas</s>.
From him came the physician <s>Dhanvantari</s>, and <s>Ketumān</s> was his son.
<s>Bhīmaratha</s> came from <s>Ketumān</s>, and <s>Divodāsa</s> was his son.
From <s>Divodāsa</s> came <s>Pratardana</s>, who is renowned here as <s>Śatrujit</s>.
His son was <s>Ṛtadhvaja</s>, and from <s>Ṛtadhvaja</s> came <s>Alarka</s>.

children.text: alarkāt sannatir jajñe sunītaḥ sannateḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From <s>Alarka</s> was born <s>Sannati</s>, and <s>Sunīta</s> was the son of <s>Sannati</s>.
<s>Satyaketu</s> was the son of <s>Sunīta</s>, and <s>Vibhu</s> was the son of <s>Satyaketu</s>.
The son of <s>Vibhu</s> was <s>Suvibhu</s>, and from <s>Suvibhu</s> came <s>Sukumāraka</s>.
From <s>Sukumāra</s> came <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>, and <s>Vītihotra</s> was his son.
From <s>Vītihotra</s> came <s>Bharga</s>, and <s>Bhargabhūmi</s> was his son.
These kings of <s>Kāśi</s> were great-souled Vaiṣṇavas.
The five hundred sons of <s>Raji</s> were slain by <s>Śakra</s>.
From <s>Kṣattravṛddha</s> came <s>Pratikṣatra</s>, and <s>Saṃjaya</s> was his son.
<s>Vijaya</s> was the son of <s>Saṃjaya</s>, and <s>Kṛta</s> was the son of <s>Vijaya</s>.
From <s>Kṛta</s> came <s>Vṛṣadhana</s>, and <s>Sahadeva</s> was his son.
From <s>Sahadeva</s> came <s>Adīna</s>, and from <s>Adīna</s> came <s>Jayatsena</s>.
From <s>Jayatsena</s> came <s>Saṃkṛti</s>, and from <s>Saṃkṛti</s> came <s>Kṣattradharman</s>.
<s>Yati</s>, <s>Yayāti</s>, <s>Saṃyāti</s>, <s>Āyāti</s>, and <s>Vikṛti</s>, in order,
are famed as the sons of <s>Nahuṣa</s>; and as for king <s>Yayāti</s>,

children.text: yaduṃ ca turvasuṃ caiva devayānī vyajāyata ||
children.translated_text: <s>Devayānī</s> gave birth to <s>Yadu</s> and <s>Turvasu</s>.

children.text: druhyuṃ cānuṃ ca pūruṃ ca śarmiṣṭhā vārṣapārvaṇī
children.translated_text: <s>Śarmiṣṭhā</s>, daughter of <s>Vṛṣaparvan</s>, bore <s>Druhyu</s>, <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Pūru</s>.
<s>Sahasrajit</s>, <s>Kroṣṭu</s>, <s>Manā</s>, and <s>Raghu</s> were the sons of <s>Yadu</s>.
From <s>Sahasrajit</s> came <s>Śatajit</s>, and from him came <s>Haya</s> and <s>Haihaya</s>.
<s>Anaraṇya</s> was the son of <s>Haya</s>, and <s>Dharma</s> came from <s>Haihaya</s>.
From <s>Dharma</s> came <s>Dharmanetra</s>, and from <s>Dharmanetra</s> came <s>Kunti</s>.
From <s>Kunti</s> was born <s>Sāhañji</s>, and <s>Mahiṣmān</s> was his son.
<s>Bhadraśreṇya</s> was his son, and <s>Durdama</s> was the son of <s>Bhadraśreṇya</s>.
From <s>Durdama</s> came <s>Dhanaka</s>, and also <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> and <s>Jānaki</s>.
<s>Kṛtāgni</s>, <s>Kṛtakarman</s>, and the very mighty <s>Kṛtaujas</s> were also born.
From <s>Kṛtavīrya</s> came <s>Arjuna</s>, and from <s>Arjuna</s> came <s>Śūrasenaka</s>.

children.text: jayadhvajo madhuḥ śūro vṛṣaṇaḥ pañca savratāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Jayadhvaja</s>, <s>Madhu</s>, <s>Śūra</s>, and <s>Vṛṣaṇa</s> were five, observing the same vows.
From <s>Jayadhvaja</s> came <s>Tālajaṅgha</s>, and from <s>Tālajaṅgha</s> came <s>Bharata</s>.
<s>Madhu</s> was the son of <s>Vṛṣaṇa</s>; from <s>Madhu</s> came the lineage of <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> and the others.
From <s>Kroṣṭu</s> was born a son, <s>Āhi</s>, of that great-souled one.

children.text: āher uśaṅkuḥ saṃjajñe tasya citrarathaḥ sataḥ
children.translated_text: From <s>Āhi</s> was born <s>Uśaṅku</s>, and from him, the good <s>Citraratha</s>.
From <s>Citraratha</s> came <s>Śaśabindu</s>; he had a hundred thousand wives.
He also had a million sons, with excellent ones such as <s>Pṛthukīrti</s>.
<s>Pṛthukīrti</s>, <s>Pṛthujaya</s>, <s>Pṛthudāna</s>, and <s>Pṛthuśravas</s> were among them.
From <s>Pṛthuśravas</s> came <s>Tamas</s>, and from <s>Tamas</s> came <s>Uśanas</s>.
His son was named <s>Śitagu</s>; after him came <s>Śrīrukmakavaca</s>.
<s>Rukma</s>, <s>Pṛthurukma</s>, <s>Jyāmagha</s>, <s>Pālita</s>, and <s>Hari</s>
were these sons of <s>Śrīrukmakavaca</s>; likewise, from <s>Jyāmagha</s> came <s>Vidarbha</s>.
Through his wife <s>Śaibyā</s>; from <s>Vidarbha</s> came <s>Kratha</s> and <s>Kauśika</s>.
From <s>Romapāda</s> came <s>Romapāda</s>, from <s>Romapāda</s> came <s>Babhru</s>, and from <s>Babhru</s> came <s>Dhṛti</s>.

children.text: kauśikasya ṛciḥ putraḥ tataścaidyo nṛpaḥ kila
children.translated_text: The son of <s>Kauśika</s> was <s>Ṛci</s>; from him indeed came the king <s>Caidya</s>.
<s>Kunti</s> is said to have been his son, and <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> is remembered as the son of <s>Kunti</s>.
From <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> came the son <s>Nivṛti</s>, and from <s>Nivṛti</s> came <s>Daśārha</s>.
The son of <s>Daśārha</s> was <s>Vyoman</s>, and <s>Jīmūta</s> was his son.
From <s>Jīmūta</s> was born <s>Vikṛti</s>; after him came <s>Bhīmaratha</s>.
Then <s>Madhuratha</s> was born; <s>Śakuni</s> was his son.
<s>Karambhi</s> was the son of <s>Śakuni</s>; his son is remembered as <s>Devavān</s>.
From <s>Devanata</s> came <s>Devakṣatra</s>, and from <s>Devakṣatra</s> <s>Madhu</s> is remembered.
<s>Kuruvaṃśa</s> was the son of <s>Madhu</s>, and <s>Anu</s> came from <s>Kuruvaṃśa</s>.
<s>Puruhotra</s> was the son of <s>Anu</s>, and <s>Aṃśu</s> came from <s>Puruhotra</s>.
<s>Sattvaśruta</s> was the son of <s>Aṃśu</s>; then, O king, came <s>Sāttvata</s>.
From <s>Sāttvata</s> were born sons: <s>Bhajin</s>, <s>Bhajamāna</s>, and <s>Andhaka</s>.
<s>Mahābhoja</s>, the two <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> and <s>Divya</s>, and another, <s>Devāvṛdha</s>, came into being.
<s>Nimi</s>, <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, <s>Bhajamāna</s>, <s>Adayuta</s>, and also <s>Ajit</s> were born.
<s>Śatajic</s>, <s>Sahasrājit</s>, <s>Babhru</s>, <s>Deva</s>, and <s>Bṛhaspati</s> were born.
From <s>Mahābhoja</s> came <s>Bhoja</s>; and from that <s>Vṛṣṇi</s> came <s>Sumitraka</s>.
From him came one named <s>Svadhājit</s>, and likewise <s>Anamitra</s> and <s>Śinī</s>.
From <s>Anamitra</s> came <s>Nighna</s>; from <s>Nighna</s> came <s>Śatrājit</s>.
<s>Prasena</s> also was renowned; and from <s>Anamitra</s> came <s>Śibi</s> as well.
The son of <s>Śibi</s> was <s>Satyaka</s>, and from <s>Satyaka</s> came <s>Sātyaki</s>.
The son of <s>Sātyaki</s> was <s>Sañjaya</s>, and <s>Kuli</s> was his son.
The son of <s>Kuli</s> was <s>Yugandhara</s>; these are proclaimed as the <s>Śaibeya</s> line.
In the lineage of <s>Anamitra</s>, the sons were <s>Vṛṣṇi</s>, <s>Śvaphalka</s>, and <s>Citraka</s>.
And from <s>Śvaphalka</s>, through <s>Gāndinī</s>, came <s>Akrūra</s>, a devotee of <s>Viṣṇu</s>.
From <s>Akrūra</s> came <s>Upamadgu</s>, <s>Ratha</s>, and then the son <s>Devadyota</s>.
<s>Devavān</s> and <s>Upadeva</s> are remembered as the sons of <s>Akrūra</s>.
<s>Pṛthu</s> and <s>Vipṛthu</s> were of <s>Citra</s>; <s>Śuci</s> is remembered as of <s>Andhaka</s>.
<s>Kukura</s> was of <s>Bhajamāna</s>, and likewise <s>Kambalabarhiṣa</s>.
From <s>Kukura</s> was born <s>Dhṛṣṭa</s>; from him came <s>Kāpotaromaka</s>.
His son was <s>Vilomā</s>, and <s>Tumburu</s> was the son of <s>Viloman</s>.
From him was born <s>Dundubhi</s>; from him <s>Punarvasu</s> is remembered.
His children were <s>Āhuka</s> and <s>Āhukī</s>, a daughter; and of <s>Āhuka</s> there were also
<s>Devaka</s> and <s>Ugrasena</s>. From <s>Devaka</s> came <s>Devakī</s>.
<s>Vṛkadevī</s>, <s>Upadevī</s>, <s>Sahadevī</s>, and <s>Surakṣitā</s>,

children.text: śrīdevī śāntidevī ca vasudeva uvāha tāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Śrīdevī</s> and <s>Śāntidevī</s>: <s>Vasudeva</s> married them.
<s>Devavān</s> and <s>Upadeva</s> are remembered as the two sons of <s>Sahadevā</s>.
From <s>Ugrasena</s> came <s>Kaṃsa</s>, <s>Sunāman</s>, <s>Vaṭa</s>, and others.
From <s>Bhajamāna</s> came <s>Vidūratha</s>, and from <s>Vidūratha</s> came <s>Śūra</s>.
Then of the son of <s>Vidūratha</s>, and also of <s>Śūra</s>, <s>Śamī</s> was the son.
From <s>Śamin</s> came <s>Pratikṣatra</s>, and <s>Svayambhoja</s> was his son.
From <s>Svayambhoja</s> came <s>Hṛdika</s>, and <s>Kṛtavarmā</s> was his son.
<s>Deva</s> and <s>Śatadhanu</s> also came from <s>Śūra</s>, son of <s>Devamīḍhuṣa</s>.
Ten sons, beginning with <s>Vasudeva</s>, were born from <s>Māriṣā</s>.

children.text: pṛthā ca śrutadevī ca śrutakīrtiḥ śrutaśravāḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Pṛthā</s>, <s>Śrutadevī</s>, <s>Śrutakīrti</s>, <s>Śrutaśravas</s>,
and <s>Rājādhidevī</s> were born from <s>Śūra</s>. He gave his daughter <s>Pṛthā</s> to <s>Kunti</s>.
Given to <s>Kuntin</s>, she became the wife of <s>Pāṇḍu</s>; in her, by <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Anila</s>, and <s>Indra</s>,
were born <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Bhīma</s>, and <s>Pārtha</s>; <s>Nakula</s> and <s>Sahadeva</s>
were born in <s>Mādrī</s> by the <s>Nāsatya</s> and <s>Dasra</s>; and formerly <s>Karṇa</s> was born in <s>Kuntī</s>.
In <s>Śrutadevī</s>, <s>Dantavakra</s>, hard to subdue in battle, was born.
In <s>Śrutakīrti</s>, by the <s>Kaikaya</s> king, five sons beginning with <s>Saṃtardana</s> were born.
In <s>Rājādhidevī</s> were born <s>Vinda</s> and also <s>Anuvinda</s>.
<s>Śrutaśravas</s>, by <s>Damaghoṣa</s>, gave birth to <s>Śiśupāla</s>.
<s>Pauravī</s>, <s>Rohiṇī</s>, and <s>Madirā</s> were wives of <s>Ānakadundubhi</s>.
<s>Devakī</s>, foremost among them, was auspicious; in <s>Rohiṇī</s> was born <s>Balabhadra</s>.
From <s>Balabhadra</s>, in <s>Revatī</s>, were born sons beginning with <s>Sāraṇa</s>, and also <s>Śaṭha</s>.

children.text: niśaṭhaścolmuko jāto devakyāṃ ṣaṭ ca jajñire ||
children.translated_text: <s>Niśaṭha</s> and <s>Ulmuka</s> were born; and in <s>Devakī</s> six were born:
<s>Kīrtimān</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, <s>Udārya</s>, <s>Bhadrasenaka</s>,
<s>Ṛjudāsa</s>, and <s>Bhadradeva</s>; <s>Kaṃsa</s> himself killed them.
The seventh was <s>Saṃkarṣaṇa</s>, and the eighth was <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> himself.
<s>Hari</s> had sixteen thousand women as wives.
<s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, <s>Lakṣmaṇā</s>, and <s>Cāruhāsinī</s>,

children.text: śreṣṭhā jāmbavatī cāṣṭau jajñire tāḥ sutānbahūn ||
children.translated_text: the chief ones, along with <s>Jāmbavatī</s>, were eight; they bore many sons.
<s>Pradyumna</s>, <s>Cārudeṣṇa</s>, and the foremost <s>Sāmba</s> were among them.
From <s>Pradyumna</s>, in <s>Kakudminī</s>, was born the mighty <s>Aniruddha</s>.
From <s>Aniruddha</s>, in <s>Subhadrā</s>, was born a king named <s>Vajra</s>.
<s>Pratibāhu</s> was the son of <s>Vajra</s>, and <s>Cāru</s> was his son.
In the lineage of <s>Turvasu</s>, there was <s>Vahni</s>; <s>Bharga</s> was the son of <s>Vahni</s>.
From <s>Bharga</s> came the son <s>Bhānu</s>; the son of <s>Bhānu</s> was <s>Karandhama</s>.
From <s>Karandhama</s> came <s>Marut</s>. Now hear from me the lineage of <s>Druhyu</s>.
The son of <s>Druhyu</s> was <s>Setu</s>, and <s>Āraddha</s> was his son.
Of <s>Āraddha</s> himself came <s>Gāndhāra</s>; from <s>Gāndhāra</s> came <s>Gharma</s>.
<s>Ghṛta</s> was the son of <s>Gharma</s>, and <s>Durgama</s> came from <s>Ghṛta</s>.
<s>Pracetā</s> came from <s>Durgama</s>. Now listen to me to the lineage of <s>Anu</s>.
The son of <s>Anu</s> was <s>Sabhānara</s>; from him came <s>Kālañjaya</s>.
From <s>Kālañjaya</s> came <s>Sṛñjaya</s>, and from <s>Sṛñjaya</s> came <s>Puruñjaya</s>.
<s>Janamejaya</s> was his son, and <s>Mahāśāla</s> was his son.
From <s>Mahāśāla</s> came <s>Mahāmanas</s>; <s>Uśīnara</s> is remembered here.
From <s>Uśīnara</s> was born <s>Śibi</s>; <s>Vṛṣadarbha</s> was the son of <s>Śibi</s>.
From <s>Mahāmanas</s> came <s>Titikṣu</s>, whose son was <s>Ruṣadratha</s>.
From <s>Ruṣadratha</s> was born <s>Hema</s>; from <s>Hema</s> came <s>Sutapas</s>.
From <s>Sutapas</s> was born <s>Bali</s>; the <s>Aṅga</s>, <s>Vaṅga</s>, and <s>Kaliṅga</s> peoples,
as well as the <s>Andha</s>, <s>Pauṇḍra</s>, and <s>Bāleya</s> peoples, and likewise <s>Anapāna</s> and <s>Aṅgata</s>, came from him.
From <s>Anapāna</s> came <s>Diviratha</s>; then there was <s>Dharmaratha</s>.
From <s>Dharmaratha</s> came <s>Romapāda</s>, and <s>Caturaṅga</s> was his son.
<s>Pṛthulākṣa</s> was his son; <s>Campa</s> was born from <s>Pṛthulākṣa</s>.
And <s>Haryaṅga</s> was the son of <s>Campa</s>; <s>Bhadraratha</s> was his son.
<s>Bṛhatkarman</s> was his son, and after him came <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s>.
<s>Bṛhanmanas</s> was the son of <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s>, and his son was <s>Jayadratha</s>.
<s>Vijaya</s> was the son of <s>Jayadratha</s>; <s>Dhṛti</s> was the son of <s>Vijaya</s>.
<s>Dhṛtavrata</s> was the son of <s>Dhṛti</s>; from <s>Dhṛtavrata</s> came <s>Satyadharma</s>.
His son was <s>Adhiratha</s>, and <s>Karṇa</s> was his son.
<s>Vṛṣasena</s> was the son of <s>Karṇa</s>. Now hear from me the descendants of <s>Puru</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe candravaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāmaikonacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one hundred thirty-ninth chapter, named "Description of the Lunar Dynasty," in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s> of the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s> in the blessed <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
<s>Janamejaya</s> was born from <s>Puru</s>, and <s>Namasyu</s> from <s>Janamejaya</s>.
His son was <s>Abhayada</s>; from <s>Abhayada</s> came <s>Sudyu</s>.
<s>Bahugati</s> was the son of <s>Sudyu</s>, and <s>Saṃjāti</s> was his son.
<s>Vatsajāti</s> came from <s>Saṃjāti</s>, and <s>Raudrāśva</s> was his son.
<s>Ṛteyu</s>, <s>Sthaṇḍileyu</s>, <s>Kakṣeyu</s>, and <s>Kṛteyuka</s>,
<s>Jaleyu</s> and <s>Saṃtateyu</s> were the excellent sons of <s>Raudrāśva</s>.
From <s>Ṛteyu</s> came <s>Ratināra</s>, and his son was <s>Pratiratha</s>.

children.text: tasya medhātithiḥ putras tatputraś cainilaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: His son was <s>Medhātithi</s>, and his son is remembered as <s>Ainila</s>.
From <s>Ainila</s> came <s>Duṣyanta</s>, and <s>Bharata</s> was his son.
He was born from <s>Śakuntalā</s>; from <s>Bharata</s> came <s>Vitatha</s>.
<s>Manyu</s> was the son of <s>Vitatha</s>, and <s>Nara</s> is remembered as the son of <s>Manyu</s>.

children.text: narasya saṃkṛtiḥ putro gargo vai saṃkṛteḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Saṃkṛti</s> was the son of <s>Nara</s>, and <s>Garga</s> was indeed the son of <s>Saṃkṛti</s>.

children.text: gargād amanyuḥ putro vai śiniḥ putro vyajāyata
children.translated_text: From <s>Garga</s> was born a son, <s>Amanyu</s>; and <s>Śini</s> was born as a son.
From mighty <s>Manyu</s> was born a son, <s>Urukṣaya</s>.
From <s>Urukṣaya</s> came <s>Trayyāruṇi</s>; and from <s>Vyūhakṣatra</s>, born in <s>Manyu</s>'s line,
came <s>Suhotra</s>; his sons were <s>Hastin</s>, <s>Ajamīḍha</s>, and <s>Dvimīḍha</s>.
From <s>Hastin</s> came <s>Purumīḍha</s>, and <s>Kaṇva</s> came from <s>Ajamīḍha</s>.
From <s>Kaṇva</s> was born <s>Medhātithi</s>, from whom the <s>Kāṇvāyana</s> brahmins descend.
From <s>Ajamīḍha</s> came <s>Bṛhadiṣu</s>, and his son was <s>Bṛhaddhanu</s>.
<s>Bṛhatkarman</s> was his son, and his son was <s>Jayadratha</s>.
From <s>Jayadratha</s> came <s>Viśvajit</s>, and <s>Senajit</s> was his son.
<s>Rucirāśva</s> came from <s>Senajit</s>, and <s>Pṛthusena</s> was his son.
<s>Pāra</s> was the son of <s>Pṛthusena</s>, and from <s>Pāra</s> came King <s>Dvīpa</s>.

children.text: nṛpasya sṛmaraḥ putraḥ sukṛtiśca pṛthoḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: <s>Sṛmara</s> was the king's son, and <s>Sukṛti</s> was the son of <s>Pṛthu</s>.
<s>Vibhrāja</s> was the son of <s>Sukṛti</s>, and from <s>Vibhrāja</s> came <s>Aśvaha</s>.
From him, through <s>Kṛtyā</s>, came <s>Brahmadatta</s>, and <s>Viṣvaksena</s> was his son.
<s>Yavīnara</s> was the son of <s>Dvimīḍha</s>, and from <s>Yavīnara</s> came <s>Dhṛtimat</s>.
From <s>Dhṛtimat</s> came <s>Satyadhṛti</s>; <s>Dṛḍhanemi</s> was his son.
From <s>Dṛḍhanemi</s> came <s>Supārśva</s>, and from <s>Supārśva</s> likewise came <s>Sannati</s>.
<s>Kṛta</s> was the son of <s>Sannati</s>; from <s>Kṛta</s> came <s>Ugrāyudha</s>.
From <s>Ugrāyudha</s> came <s>Kṣemya</s>, and <s>Sudhīra</s> was his son.
From <s>Sudhīra</s> came <s>Purañjaya</s>; his son was <s>Vidūratha</s>.
From <s>Ajamīḍha</s>, by <s>Nalinī</s>, there was a king named <s>Nīla</s>.
From <s>Nīla</s> came a son, <s>Śānti</s>, and <s>Suśānti</s> was his son.
From <s>Suśānti</s> was born <s>Puru</s>, and <s>Arka</s> was his son.
And <s>Haryaśva</s> was the son of <s>Arka</s>; from <s>Haryaśva</s> came <s>Mukula</s>.
<s>Yavīnara</s>, <s>Bṛhadbhānu</s>, <s>Kampilla</s>, and <s>Sṛñjaya</s> likewise
were the <s>Pāñcālas</s> born from <s>Mukula</s>; <s>Śaradvān</s> was a great <s>Vaiṣṇava</s>.
His second was <s>Divodāsa</s>; from <s>Śaradvat</s>, through <s>Ahalyā</s>,
<s>Śatānanda</s> was born as a son, and <s>Satyadhṛti</s> was born from that righteous one.
<s>Kṛpa</s> and <s>Kṛpī</s> came from <s>Satyadhṛti</s>, when his seed was spilled on account of <s>Urvaśī</s>.
<s>Kṛpī</s> became the wife of <s>Droṇa</s> and gave birth to the excellent <s>Aśvatthāman</s>.
From <s>Divodāsa</s> came <s>Mitrayu</s>, and from <s>Mitrayu</s> came <s>Cyavana</s>.
<s>Sudāsa</s> was born from <s>Cyavana</s>, and <s>Saudāsa</s> was his son.
<s>Sahadeva</s> was his son, and from <s>Sahadeva</s> came <s>Somaka</s>.
<s>Jantu</s> was born from <s>Somaka</s>, and another great one was <s>Pṛṣata</s>.
From <s>Pṛṣata</s> was born <s>Drupada</s>, and after him came <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>.
From <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> came <s>Dhṛṣṭaketu</s>; <s>Ṛkṣa</s> arose from <s>Ajamīḍha</s>.
From <s>Ṛkṣa</s> was born <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s>, and from <s>Saṃvaraṇa</s> came <s>Kuru</s>.
<s>Sudhanu</s>, <s>Pīkṣi</s>, and <s>Jahnu</s> were the sons of <s>Kuru</s>.
From <s>Sudhanu</s> came <s>Suhotra</s>, and from <s>Suhotra</s> came <s>Cyavana</s>.
From <s>Cyavana</s> was born <s>Kṛtaka</s>, and likewise <s>Uparicara Vasu</s>.
<s>Bṛhadratha</s>, <s>Pratyagra</s>, and <s>Satyā</s> and the others were the sons of <s>Vasu</s>.
From <s>Bṛhadratha</s> came <s>Kuśāgra</s>, and from <s>Kuśāgra</s> came <s>Ṛṣabha</s>.
From <s>Ṛṣabha</s> came <s>Puṣpavat</s>; from him King <s>Satyahita</s> was born.
From <s>Satyahita</s> came <s>Sudhanvan</s>, and <s>Jahnu</s> came from <s>Sudhanvan</s>.
From <s>Bṛhadratha</s> came <s>Jarāsandha</s>, and <s>Sahadeva</s> was his son.
From <s>Sahadeva</s> came <s>Somāpi</s>, and <s>Śrutavat</s> was the son of <s>Somāpi</s>.
<s>Bhīmasena</s>, <s>Ugrasena</s>, <s>Śrutasena</s>, and <s>Aparājita</s>,
and another <s>Janamejaya</s> came; from <s>Jahnu</s> came <s>Suratha</s>.
From <s>Suratha</s> came <s>Vidūratha</s>, and from <s>Vidūratha</s> came <s>Sārvabhauma</s>.
From <s>Sārvabhauma</s> came <s>Jayasena</s>, and <s>Āvadhīta</s> was his son.
<s>Ayutāyus</s> was his son, and <s>Akrodhana</s> was his son.
Of <s>Akrodhana</s> there was <s>Atithi</s>, and <s>Ṛkṣa</s> was the son of <s>Atithi</s>.
From <s>Ṛkṣa</s> came <s>Bhīmasena</s>, and from <s>Bhīmasena</s> came <s>Dilīpa</s>.
From <s>Dilīpa</s> came <s>Pratīpa</s>, and from <s>Pratīpa</s> came <s>Devāpi</s>.
<s>Devāpi</s>, <s>Śantanu</s>, and <s>Bāhlīka</s>: these three brothers were kings.
From <s>Bāhlīka</s> came <s>Somadatta</s>; from him came <s>Bhūri</s> and then <s>Bhūriśravas</s>.

children.text: śalaśca śantanor bhīṣmo gaṅgāyāṃ dhārmiko mahān
children.translated_text: And <s>Śala</s>; from <s>Śantanu</s>, through <s>Gaṅgā</s>, came the great righteous <s>Bhīṣma</s>.
From <s>Śantanu</s>, through <s>Satyavatī</s>, came <s>Citrāṅgada</s> and <s>Vicitravīrya</s>.
The wives of <s>Vicitravīrya</s> were <s>Ambikā</s> and <s>Ambālikā</s>; in those two

children.text: dhṛtarāṣṭraṃ ca pāṇḍuṃ ca taddāsyāṃ viduraṃ tathā ||
children.translated_text: were born <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> and <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, and also <s>Vidura</s> in their maidservant.
<s>Vyāsa</s> begot them. <s>Gāndhārī</s>, from <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>,
bore a hundred sons, beginning with <s>Duryodhana</s>; from <s>Pāṇḍu</s> five sons were born.
<s>Prativindhya</s>, <s>Śrutasoma</s>, and <s>Śrutakīrti</s>, likewise from <s>Arjuna</s>,

children.text: śatānīkaḥ śrutakarmā draupadyāṃ pañca vai kramāt ||
children.translated_text: <s>Śatānīka</s> and <s>Śrutakarman</s>: these five were born in order from <s>Draupadī</s>.

children.text: yaudheyī ca hiḍimbā ca kauśī caiva subhadrikā
children.translated_text: <s>Yaudheyī</s>, <s>Hiḍimbā</s>, <s>Kauśī</s>, and <s>Subhadrikā</s>,

children.text: vijayā vai reṇumatī pañcabhyastu sutāḥ kramāt ||
children.translated_text: and <s>Vijayā</s> and <s>Reṇumatī</s>: from the five, sons were born in order.
<s>Devaka</s>, <s>Ghaṭotkaca</s>, <s>Abhimanyu</s>, and <s>Sarvaga</s>,
<s>Suhotra</s> and <s>Niramitra</s>; <s>Parīkṣit</s> was the son of <s>Abhimanyu</s>.
After him came <s>Janamejaya</s>; now hear of the kings who are to come.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe candravaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma catvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one-hundred-fortieth chapter, called "Description of the Lunar Dynasty," in the first section, the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s> of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Hari</s> said:
Then came <s>Śatānīka</s>, <s>Aśvamedhadatta</s>, and also <s>Adhisomaka</s>.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, <s>Aniruddha</s>, and <s>Uṣṇa</s> came, and after them King <s>Citraratha</s>.
<s>Śucidratha</s>, <s>Vṛṣṇimant</s>, <s>Suṣeṇa</s>, and <s>Sunīthaka</s>,
<s>Nṛcakṣus</s>, <s>Mukhābāṇa</s>, <s>Medhāvin</s>, and <s>Nṛpañjaya</s>,
<s>Pāriplava</s> and <s>Munaya</s>, <s>Medhāvin</s> and <s>Nṛpañjaya</s>,
<s>Bṛhadratha</s>, <s>Hari</s>, <s>Tigma</s>, <s>Śatānīka</s>, and <s>Sudānaka</s>,
<s>Udāna</s>, <s>Ahninara</s>, <s>Daṇḍapāṇi</s>, and <s>Nimittaka</s>,

children.text: kṣemakaśca tataḥ śūdraḥ pitā pūrvastataḥ sutaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and then <s>Kṣemaka</s>; thereafter there will be <s>Śūdra</s>. First the father, then the son.
The kings born in the <s>Ikṣvāku</s> lineage, beginning with <s>Bṛhadbala</s>, are now recounted.
From <s>Bṛhadbala</s> came <s>Urukṣaya</s>, and after him <s>Vatsavyūha</s>.
From <s>Vatsavyūha</s> came <s>Sūrya</s>, and <s>Sahadeva</s> was his son.
Then came <s>Bṛhadaśva</s>, <s>Bhānuratha</s>, <s>Pratīcya</s>, and <s>Pratītaka</s>.
<s>Manudeva</s>, <s>Sunakṣatra</s>, <s>Kinnara</s>, and <s>Antarikṣaka</s>,
<s>Suparṇa</s>, <s>Kṛtajit</s>, and the righteous <s>Bṛhadbhrāja</s>,

children.text: kṛtañjayo dhanañjayaḥ saṃjayaḥ śākya eva ca ||
children.translated_text: <s>Kṛtañjaya</s>, <s>Dhanañjaya</s>, <s>Saṃjaya</s>, and <s>Śākya</s>,
<s>Śuddhodana</s>, <s>Bāhula</s>, <s>Senajit</s>, and <s>Kṣudraka</s>,
<s>Sumitra</s> and <s>Kuḍava</s>; after this, hear of the <s>Māgadha</s> kings from <s>Sumitra</s>.
<s>Jarāsandha</s>, <s>Sahadeva</s>, <s>Somāpi</s>, and <s>Śrutaśravas</s>,
<s>Ayutāyus</s>, <s>Niramitra</s>, <s>Sukṣatra</s>, and <s>Bahukarmaka</s>,
<s>Śrutaṃjaya</s>, <s>Senajit</s>, <s>Bhūri</s>, and <s>Śuci</s>,
<s>Kṣemya</s>, <s>Suvrata</s>, <s>Dharma</s>, <s>Śmaśrula</s>, and <s>Dṛḍhasenaka</s>,
<s>Sumati</s>, <s>Subala</s>, <s>Nīta</s>, <s>Satyajit</s>, and <s>Viśvajit</s>,
and <s>Iṣuṃjaya</s>: these are remembered as the <s>Bārhadratha</s> kings.
After them, irreligious <s>Śūdra</s> kings will arise.
For the blessed, imperishable <s>Nārāyaṇa</s> himself is the maker of heaven and the rest.
There is occasional dissolution, elemental dissolution, and also final dissolution.

children.text: yāti bhūḥ pralayaṃ cāpsu hyāpastejasi pāvakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The earth dissolves into water, and water into fiery heat.
Fire dissolves into wind, wind into space, and space into the principle of egoity.

children.text: ahaṃ buddhau matir jove jīvo 'vyakte tadātmani ||
children.translated_text: Egoity dissolves into intellect, thought into the living soul; the living soul dissolves into the unmanifest, and that into the self.
The self is the supreme lord, <s>Viṣṇu</s>, the one <s>Nārāyaṇa</s>, <s>Nara</s>.
All that is other than the imperishable supreme, the world beginning with heaven, is indeed perishable.
Kings and the rest have gone to destruction; therefore one should avoid sin.

children.text: dharmaṃ kuryātsthiraṃ yena pāpaṃ hitvā hariṃ vrajet ||
children.translated_text: One should practice firm <s>dharma</s> (normative order), by which, abandoning sin, one reaches <s>Hari</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhaviṣyarājavaṃśadṛ nāmaikacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one-hundred-forty-first chapter, called "Description of the Future Royal Dynasties," in the first section, the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s> of the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
The lord <s>Hari</s>, having descended, protected the worlds and the rest,
for the destruction of the <s>dharma</s> (way of life) of the demons and for the preservation of Vedic <s>dharma</s> and the rest.
The unborn one takes avatāras (descents) in forms beginning with <s>Matsya</s>.
Having become <s>Matsya</s>, he slew the demon <s>Hayagrīva</s>, the thorn of the sacrifice.
<s>Keśava</s> brought back the Vedas and protected <s>Manu</s> and the others.

children.text: mandaraṃ dhārayāmāsa kūrmo bhūtvā hitāya ca ||
children.translated_text: Having become <s>Kūrma</s>, he supported <s>Mandara</s> for the welfare of all.
At the churning of the milk ocean, the divine physician <s>Dhanvantari</s> arose.
He emerged carrying a full pitcher of amṛta (nectar).
He then taught the eightfold <s>Āyurveda</s> to <s>Suśruta</s>.
<s>Hari</s>, in female form, made the gods drink the amṛta (nectar).
Then, descended as <s>Varāha</s>, he slew <s>Hiraṇyākṣa</s>.
He supported the earth and protected the gods.
Then <s>Narasiṃha</s> descended against the enemy <s>Hiraṇyakaśipu</s>.
He destroyed the demons and protected Vedic <s>dharma</s> and the rest.
Then the lord of the world became <s>Paraśurāma</s>, son of <s>Jamadagni</s>.
<s>Hari</s> made the earth devoid of kṣatriyas twenty-one times.
He slew <s>Kārtavīrya</s> in battle and gave the earth to <s>Kaśyapa</s>.
After performing a sacrifice, the mighty-armed one remained on Mount <s>Mahendra</s>.
Then <s>Rāma</s>, who was to be <s>Viṣṇu</s>, appeared in fourfold form as the crusher of wicked pride.
<s>Rāma</s> was born as the son of <s>Daśaratha</s>, and <s>Bharata</s> was his younger brother.
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s>, and <s>Jānakī</s>, <s>Rāma</s>'s wife,
and <s>Rāma</s>, for the sake of his father's truth and acting for the good of his mothers,
came to <s>Śṛṅgavera</s>, <s>Citrakūṭa</s>, and the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
Having cut off <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s>'s nose, and then <s>Khara</s> and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s>
having slain the night-roaming demon, the abductor of <s>Sītā</s>,
namely <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, and his younger brother <s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> in the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>,
having installed him in the kingdom of the rākṣasas, with <s>Sugrīva</s>, <s>Hanumān</s>, and the others,
he mounted the <s>Puṣpaka</s> together with <s>Sītā</s>, who was devoted to her husband.
With obedient <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> he went to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, his own city.
He ruled the kingdom and protected the gods and other beings, as well as his subjects.
He preserved <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and performed sacrifices such as the horse sacrifice.
That earth rejoiced at ease under King <s>Rāma</s> himself.

children.text: rāvaṇasya gṛhe sītā sthitā bheje na rāvaṇam
children.translated_text: Though <s>Sītā</s> had stayed in <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s house, she did not consort with <s>Rāvaṇa</s>.

children.text: karmaṇā manasā vācā sā gatā rāghavaṃ sadā ||
children.translated_text: In deed, mind, and speech she always went only to <s>Rāghava</s>.

children.text: pativratā tu sā sītā hyanasūyā yathaiva tu
children.translated_text: That <s>Sītā</s> was a <s>pativratā</s> (devoted wife), just like <s>Anasūyā</s>.
Hear the greatness of a <s>pativratā</s>; I shall tell it to you.
Long ago in <s>Pratiṣṭhāna</s> there was a leprous brahmin named <s>Kauśika</s>.

children.text: taṃ tathā vyādhitaṃ bhāryā patiṃ devamivārcayat ||
children.translated_text: His wife worshiped him, her diseased husband, just like a god.
Even when rebuked, she regarded that husband as a deity.
Commanded by her husband, she brought him to a courtesan, taking along a large payment.
On the road, impaled on a stake though innocent, on suspicion of theft,
was <s>Māṇḍavya</s>, overcome by extreme pain; then in the darkness that twice-born man,
<s>Kauśika</s>, mounted on his wife's shoulder, shook him.
Angered by the touch of his foot, <s>Māṇḍavya</s> said to him:
'At sunrise there shall be death for the man by whose foot I was shaken.'
Hearing that, his wife said, 'The sun will not rise.'
Then, because there was no sunrise, it was continually night.
For the span of many years this continued; then the gods became afraid.
They went to <s>Brahmā</s> for refuge, and the lotus-born one said to them:
'Ascetic power is calmed only by ascetic power; this power of hers is indeed such.
Because of the greatness of a <s>pativratā</s>, the day-maker does not rise.
And from its failure to rise there is harm to mortals and also to you.
Therefore propitiate the ascetic <s>Anasūyā</s>, wife of <s>Atri</s> and a <s>pativratā</s>,
with the desire that the sun should rise.'

children.text: taiḥ sā prasāditā gatvā hyanasūyā pativratā
children.translated_text: Propitiated by them, that <s>pativratā</s> <s>Anasūyā</s> went,
caused the sun to rise, and revived that husband.
Yet <s>Sītā</s> is said to have been greater than the <s>pativratā</s> <s>Anasūyā</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe daśāvatāradṛ nāma dvicatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one-hundred-and-forty-second chapter, called 'The Ten Avatāras.'
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
Now I shall tell the <s>Rāmāyaṇa</s>, whose hearing destroys sin.
From the lotus in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel came <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>Marīci</s> was his son.
From <s>Marīci</s> came <s>Kaśyapa</s>, from him <s>Ravi</s>, and from him <s>Manu</s> is remembered.
<s>Ikṣvāku</s> was the son of <s>Manu</s>; in his lineage King <s>Raghu</s> is remembered.
From <s>Raghu</s> <s>Aja</s> was then born, and from him mighty King <s>Daśaratha</s>.
He had four sons, very strong and valiant.
<s>Rāma</s> was born from <s>Kausalyā</s>; <s>Bharata</s> was the son of <s>Kaikeyī</s>.
The two sons <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Śatrughna</s> were born from <s>Sumitrā</s>.
<s>Rāma</s>, devoted to his father and mother, obtained from <s>Viśvāmitra</s>

children.text: astragrāmaṃ tato yakṣīṃ tāṭakāṃ prajaghāna ha ||
children.translated_text: the whole collection of weapons; then he slew the yakṣī <s>Tāṭakā</s>.
At <s>Viśvāmitra</s>'s sacrifice, the mighty one slew <s>Subāhu</s>.
Going to <s>Janaka</s>'s sacrifice, he then married <s>Jānakī</s>.

children.text: ūrmilāṃ lakṣmaṇo vīro bharato māṇḍavīṃ sutām
children.translated_text: The heroic <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> married <s>Ūrmilā</s>; <s>Bharata</s> married the daughter <s>Māṇḍavī</s>.
<s>Śatrughna</s> married <s>Kīrtimatī</s>; both were daughters of <s>Kuśadhvaja</s>.
Having gone with their father and the others to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, <s>Rāma</s> and the others stayed there.
<s>Śatrughna</s> and <s>Bharata</s> went to <s>Yudhājit</s>, their maternal uncle.
When they had gone, that excellent king set out to give the kingdom
to <s>Rāma</s>, his son; then <s>Kaikeyī</s> made a request.
She desired that <s>Rāma</s> should dwell in the forest for fourteen years.

children.text: rāmaḥ pitṛhitārthaṃ ca lakṣmaṇena ca sītayā ||
children.translated_text: For the sake of his father's welfare, <s>Rāma</s>, together with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and <s>Sītā</s>,
abandoned the kingdom like a blade of grass and went to <s>Śṛṅgaverapura</s>.

children.text: rathaṃ tyaktvā prayāgaṃ ca citrakūṭagiriṃ gataḥ ||
children.translated_text: Leaving the chariot behind, he went to <s>Prayāga</s> and to <s>Citrakūṭa</s> mountain.

children.text: rāmasya tu viyogena rājā svargaṃ samāśritaḥ
children.translated_text: Because of separation from <s>Rāma</s>, the king went to heaven.
After performing his funeral rites, <s>Bharata</s> came and, strong as he was, said to <s>Rāma</s>:

children.text: ayodhyāṃ tu samāgatya rājyaṃ kuru mahāmate
children.translated_text: 'Come back to <s>Ayodhyā</s> and rule the kingdom, great-minded one.'

children.text: sa naicchatpāduke dattvā rājyāya bharatāya tu ||
children.translated_text: He did not wish to do so; giving his sandals to <s>Bharata</s> for the kingdom,
he dismissed <s>Bharata</s>, and <s>Bharata</s> governed <s>Rāma</s>'s kingdom.
Staying in <s>Nandigrāma</s>, devoted and observant of his vow, he did not enter <s>Ayodhyā</s>.
<s>Rāma</s> too came from <s>Citrakūṭa</s> to <s>Atri</s>'s hermitage.
After bowing to <s>Sutīkṣṇa</s> and <s>Agastya</s>, he came to the <s>Daṇḍaka</s> forest.
There a rākṣasī named <s>Śūrpaṇakhā</s> came to devour him.
Having cut off her ears and nose, <s>Rāma</s> then drove her away.
Incited by her, <s>Khara</s> came, and <s>Dūṣaṇa</s> and <s>Triśiras</s> likewise,
with an army of fourteen thousand rākṣasas.
<s>Rāma</s>, for his part, sent them with arrows to the city of <s>Yama</s>.
Incited by the rākṣasī, <s>Rāvaṇa</s> came for the abduction.
First he made <s>Mārīca</s> take the form of a deer; then, bearing a triple staff,

children.text: sītayā prerito rāmo mārīcaṃ nijaghāna ha ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s>, urged by <s>Sītā</s>, slew <s>Mārīca</s>.

children.text: mriyamāṇaḥ sa ca prāha hā sīte lakṣmaṇeti ca
children.translated_text: As he was dying, he cried out, "Alas, <s>Sītā</s>! <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>!"
Then <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>, addressed by <s>Sītā</s>, went; and <s>Rāma</s> no longer saw him.

children.text: uvāca rākṣasī māyā nūnaṃ sītā hṛteti saḥ
children.translated_text: He said, "This is surely a rākṣasa illusion; <s>Sītā</s> has been carried off."
Then <s>Rāvaṇa</s>, finding his opportunity, took <s>Jānakī</s> onto his lap,

children.text: jaṭāyuṣaṃ vinirbhidya yayau laṅkāṃ tato balī
children.translated_text: and, having pierced <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, the mighty one went to <s>Laṅkā</s>.
There he kept her guarded in the shade of an aśoka tree.

children.text: āgatya rāmaḥ śūnyāṃ ca parṇaśālāṃ dadarśa ha
children.translated_text: When <s>Rāma</s> came back, he saw that the leaf-hut was empty.
After grieving for <s>Jānakī</s>, the lord began to search for her.

children.text: jaṭāyuṣaṃ ca saṃskṛtya tadukto dakṣiṇāṃ diśam
children.translated_text: He performed the funeral rites for <s>Jaṭāyus</s>, and, directed by him, went toward the southern quarter.

children.text: gatvā sakhyaṃ tataścakre sugrīveṇa ca rāghavaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Then <s>Rāghava</s> made an alliance with <s>Sugrīva</s>.
With an arrow of unbent joints he pierced seven palm trees,
and, having slain <s>Vālin</s>, the lord of the monkeys in <s>Kiṣkindhā</s>,
<s>Rāma</s> made <s>Sugrīva</s> king while he himself remained on <s>Ṛśyamūka</s>.
<s>Sugrīva</s> sent forth monkeys, great as mountains,
eagerly to search for <s>Sītā</s> in the quarters beginning with the east.
Those who had gone to the western, northern, and eastern quarters returned.

children.text: dakṣiṇāṃ tu diśaṃ ye ca mārgayanto 'tha jānakīm
children.translated_text: But those who were searching for <s>Jānakī</s> in the southern quarter
through forests, mountains, islands, and riverbanks,
did not see <s>Jānakī</s> and resolved upon death.
From the words of <s>Sampāti</s>, <s>Hanūmān</s>, the foremost monkey, learned the truth.
He leapt across the ocean, the abode of sea-creatures, one hundred yojanas wide,
and there he saw <s>Jānakī</s> staying in the aśoka grove.
She was being threatened by rākṣasī women and by the rākṣasa <s>Rāvaṇa</s>,

children.text: bhava bhāryeti vadatā cintayantīṃ ca rāghavam ||
children.translated_text: who said, "Become my wife," while she kept thinking of <s>Rāghava</s>.
The monkey gave her the ring and spoke words of welfare to <s>Sītā</s>:

children.text: rāmasya tasya dūto 'haṃ śokaṃ mā kuru maithili ||
children.translated_text: "I am the messenger of that <s>Rāma</s>; do not grieve, <s>Maithilī</s>.

children.text: svābhijñānaṃ ca me dehi yena rāmaḥ smariṣyati
children.translated_text: Give me a token of recognition by which <s>Rāma</s> will remember you."
Hearing this, <s>Sītā</s> gave the jewel from her braid to <s>Hanūmat</s>.

children.text: yathā rāmo nayecchīghraṃ tathā vācyaṃ tvayā kape
children.translated_text: "Speak to him, monkey, in such a way that <s>Rāma</s> will bring me away quickly."

children.text: tathetyuktvā tu hanumānvanaṃ divyaṃ babhañja ha ||
children.translated_text: Saying "So be it," <s>Hanūmān</s> then broke apart the splendid grove.
After killing <s>Akṣa</s> and other rākṣasas, he himself submitted to capture.
Bound by all the arrows of <s>Indrajit</s>, he saw <s>Rāvaṇa</s> and said:
"I am <s>Hanūmān</s>, the messenger of <s>Rāma</s>; give <s>Maithilī</s> to <s>Rāma</s>."
Hearing this, the enraged one set his tail on fire.
The monkey, his tail blazing, burned <s>Laṅkā</s>, mighty as he was.

children.text: dagdhvā laṅkāṃ samāyāto rāmapārśvaṃ sa vānaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: Having burned <s>Laṅkā</s>, that monkey returned to <s>Rāma</s>'s side.
After eating fruit in the honey-grove, he announced, "<s>Sītā</s> has been seen."

children.text: veṇīratnaṃ ca rāmāya rāmo laṅkāpurīṃ yayau ||
children.translated_text: He gave the braid-jewel to <s>Rāma</s>, and <s>Rāma</s> set out for the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
He went with <s>Sugrīva</s>, with <s>Hanūmān</s>, with <s>Aṅgada</s>, and with <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s>.
<s>Vibhīṣaṇa</s> also came to <s>Rāghava</s> for refuge.
<s>Rāma</s> consecrated that younger brother of <s>Rāvaṇa</s> for the sovereignty of <s>Laṅkā</s>.

children.text: rāmo nalena setuṃ ca kṛtvābdhau cottatāra tam ||
children.translated_text: <s>Rāma</s> had a bridge built across the ocean by <s>Nala</s> and crossed over it.
Standing on <s>Suvelā</s>, he saw the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
Then those heroic monkeys, <s>Nīla</s>, <s>Aṅgada</s>, <s>Nala</s>, and the others,
the heroic <s>Dhūmra</s> and <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, with <s>Jāmbavat</s> at their head,
and those headed by <s>Mainda</s> and <s>Dvivida</s>, broke into the city of <s>Laṅkā</s>.
With <s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> and the monkeys, <s>Rāma</s> slew all the great-bodied rākṣasas,
dark like masses of collyrium-black clouds.
He slew <s>Vidyujjihva</s>, <s>Dhūmrākṣa</s>, <s>Devāntaka</s> and <s>Narāntaka</s>,
<s>Mahodara</s>, <s>Mahāpārśva</s>, and the very mighty <s>Atikāya</s>,

children.text: kumbhaṃ nikumbhaṃ mattaṃ ca makarākṣaṃ hyakampanam
children.translated_text: <s>Kumbha</s>, <s>Nikumbha</s>, <s>Matta</s>, <s>Makarākṣa</s>, and <s>Akampana</s>,
heroic <s>Prahasta</s>, <s>Unmatta</s>, and the mighty <s>Kumbhakarṇa</s>.
<s>Lakṣmaṇa</s> cut down <s>Rāvaṇi</s>, while the mighty <s>Rāghava</s>, with weapons and the rest,
cut off <s>Rāvaṇa</s>'s circles of arms and felled him.

children.text: sītāṃ śuddhāṃ gṛhītvātha vimāne puṣpake sthitaḥ
children.translated_text: Then, taking back <s>Sītā</s>, now purified, he mounted the aerial car <s>Puṣpaka</s>.
Together with the monkeys he returned to <s>Ayodhyā</s>, the excellent city.
There he ruled the kingdom, protecting his subjects as though they were his sons.
After performing ten horse sacrifices, <s>Rāghava</s> duly made
the offering of piṇḍas at <s>Gayāśiras</s> and gave gifts.

children.text: putrau kuśalavau dṛṣṭvā tau ca rājye 'bhyaṣecayat ||
children.translated_text: Seeing his two sons <s>Kuśa</s> and <s>Lava</s>, he consecrated them in the kingdom.
<s>Rāma</s> ruled for eleven thousand years.
<s>Śatrughna</s> slew <s>Lavaṇa</s>, and then <s>Bharata</s> slew <s>Śailūṣa</s>.
After bowing to sages beginning with <s>Agastya</s> and hearing of the origin of the rākṣasas,
he went to heaven together with the people of <s>Ayodhyā</s>, having fulfilled his purpose.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe rāmāyaṇavarṇanaṃ nāma tricatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one hundred forty-third chapter, named "The Description of the Rāmāyaṇa," in the first section called the Pūrvakhaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, of the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall proclaim the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>, the supreme greatness of <s>Kṛṣṇa</s>.
From <s>Vasudeva</s>, in <s>Devakī</s>, <s>Vāsudeva</s>, <s>Bala</s>, was born.
For the protection of <s>dharma</s> (righteous order) and the destruction of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness),
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s> firmly sucked the breasts of <s>Pūtanā</s> and brought her to destruction.
The cart was overturned, and the two arjuna trees were broken.
The serpent <s>Kāliya</s> was subdued, and <s>Dhenuka</s> was struck down.
The mountain <s>Govardhana</s> was held up, and he was honored by <s>Indra</s>.
<s>Hari</s> accomplished the removal of the earth's burden and made his vow.
For the protection of <s>Arjuna</s> and the others, enemies beginning with <s>Ariṣṭa</s> were struck down.
The demon <s>Keśī</s> was killed, and the cowherds and the others were satisfied.
<s>Cāṇūra</s>, <s>Muṣṭika</s> the wrestler, and <s>Kaṃsa</s> were thrown down from the platform.
<s>Rukmiṇī</s>, <s>Satyabhāmā</s>, and the others were indeed the eight chief wives of <s>Hari</s>.
There were also sixteen thousand other women of that great-souled one.
Their sons, grandsons, and so on numbered by the hundreds and by the thousands.

children.text: rukmiṇyāṃ caiva pradyumno nyavadhīcchambaraṃ ca yaḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>Rukmiṇī</s> was born <s>Pradyumna</s>, who killed <s>Śambara</s>.
His son was <s>Aniruddha</s>, the husband of <s>Uṣā</s>, daughter of <s>Bāṇa</s>.
There a great battle took place between <s>Hari</s> and <s>Śaṅkara</s>.
The thousand arms of <s>Bāṇa</s> were cut off, and only two arms remained.

children.text: narako nihato yena pārijātaṃ jahāra yaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Naraka</s> was slain by him, and he seized the <s>Pārijāta</s> tree.
<s>Śiśupāla</s> too was killed, and <s>Dvivida</s> the monkey was slain by <s>Bala</s>.

children.text: aniruddhādabhūdvajraḥ sa ca rājā gate harau
children.translated_text: From <s>Aniruddha</s> came <s>Vajra</s>; he became king when <s>Hari</s> had departed.

children.text: saṃdīpaniṃ guruṃ cakre saputraṃ ca cakāra saḥ
children.translated_text: He made <s>Sāṃdīpani</s> his guru and restored him together with his son.
He placed <s>Ugrasena</s> in <s>Mathurā</s> and protected the gods.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe harivaṃśavarṇanaṃ nāma catuścātvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the earlier section, in the first part called the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the one hundred forty-fourth chapter, named the Description of the <s>Harivaṃśa</s>.
<s>Brahmā</s> said:
I shall proclaim the <s>Bhārata</s>, the removal of the burden of the earth.
<s>Kṛṣṇa</s>, fighting on account of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> and the others, brought it about.
From the lotus in <s>Viṣṇu</s>'s navel came <s>Brahmā</s>; <s>Atri</s> was the son of <s>Brahmā</s>.
From <s>Atri</s> came <s>Soma</s>, from him <s>Budha</s>, and from him, in <s>Ilā</s>, <s>Purūravas</s>.
His son was <s>Āyus</s>; in that lineage were <s>Yayāti</s>, <s>Bharata</s>, and <s>Kuru</s>.
In his lineage was <s>Śantanu</s>; <s>Bhīṣma</s> was the son of <s>Śantanu</s> by <s>Gaṅgā</s>.
<s>Bhīṣma</s> was endowed with every virtue and had mastered the <s>Brahmavaivarta</s>.

children.text: śantanoḥ satyavatyāṃ ca dvau putrau saṃbabhūvatuḥ
children.translated_text: And to <s>Śantanu</s>, in <s>Satyavatī</s>, two sons were born.
The <s>Gandharva</s> <s>Citrāṅgada</s> killed the son named <s>Citrāṅgada</s>.
The other was <s>Vicitravīrya</s>, husband of the daughters of the king of <s>Kāśī</s>.
When <s>Vicitravīrya</s> had gone to heaven, offspring arose in his field through <s>Vyāsa</s>.
<s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> was the son of <s>Ambikā</s>, and <s>Pāṇḍu</s> was the son of <s>Ambālikā</s>.
<s>Vidura</s> was born from a servant woman; from <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s>, in <s>Gāndhārī</s>,
there were a hundred mighty sons, with <s>Duryodhana</s> as the foremost.

children.text: pāṇḍoḥ kuntyāṃ ca mādryāṃ ca pañca putrāḥ prajajñire ||
children.translated_text: And to <s>Pāṇḍu</s>, in <s>Kuntī</s> and <s>Mādrī</s>, five sons were born.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, <s>Bhīmasena</s>, <s>Arjuna</s>, and likewise <s>Nakula</s>,
and <s>Sahadeva</s>: these five had great strength and valor.
Through the working of fate, enmity arose between the <s>Kurus</s> and the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>.
The <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> were greatly harassed by the rash <s>Duryodhana</s>.
Though the heroes were burned in the lac house, they escaped by their own stainless wisdom.
Then, at <s>Ekacakrā</s>, in the dwelling of a brahmin,
those great-souled ones entered, after killing the rākṣasa <s>Baka</s>.
Then in the region of <s>Pañcāla</s> they learned of <s>Draupadī</s>'s svayaṃvara.
Knowing that she was to be won by valor, the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s> married her.
With the consent of <s>Droṇa</s> and <s>Bhīṣma</s>, <s>Dhṛtarāṣṭra</s> summoned them.
Then they received half the kingdom in the excellent city of <s>Indraprastha</s>.
Then, having built the assembly hall, the disciplined men performed the <s>rājasūya</s> sacrifice.
<s>Arjuna</s> went to <s>Dvāravatī</s> and obtained beloved <s>Subhadrā</s>,
the sister of <s>Vāsudeva</s>, with the consent of the foe of <s>Mura</s>.

children.text: nandighoṣaṃ rathaṃ divyam agner dhanur anuttamam
children.translated_text: He received the divine chariot <s>Nandighoṣa</s> and, from <s>Agni</s>, the unsurpassed bow,

children.text: gāṇḍīvaṃ nāma taddivyaṃ triṣu lokeṣu viśrutam
children.translated_text: that divine bow named <s>Gāṇḍīva</s>, famous throughout the three worlds,
as well as inexhaustible arrows and impenetrable armor.

children.text: sa tena dhanuṣā vīraḥ pāṇḍavo jātavedasam
children.translated_text: With that bow the heroic <s>Pāṇḍava</s>, for <s>Jātavedas</s>,
mighty <s>Bībhatsu</s>, with <s>Kṛṣṇa</s> as his companion, satisfied him.
Having conquered kings in the conquest of the quarters and taken jewels, he gave them
joyfully to his great elder brother <s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s>, who knew sound policy.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> too, righteous-souled and surrounded by his brothers,
was defeated by sinful <s>Duryodhana</s> through a deceptive game of dice,
while he stood by the counsel of <s>Karṇa</s>, <s>Duḥśāsana</s>, and <s>Śakuni</s>.
Then for twelve years they practiced great austerity in the forest.
With <s>Dhaumya</s> and with <s>Draupadī</s> as the sixth, they were surrounded by hosts of sages.
They went to the city of <s>Virāṭa</s> and lived there in hidden forms.
For one year those very wise men protected him at the seizure of the cattle.
Then, having gone to their own kingdom, the honored heroes petitioned
King <s>Duryodhana</s> for five villages in place of half the kingdom.
When they did not obtain them, the powerful men made war at <s>Kurukṣetra</s>,
surrounded by seven splendid <s>akṣauhiṇīs</s>.
<s>Duryodhana</s> and the others were arrayed with eleven.
The battle was confused and like a war between gods and asuras.
<s>Bhīṣma</s> was first the commander in <s>Duryodhana</s>'s army.

children.text: pāṇḍavānāṃ śikhaṇḍī ca tayoryuddhaṃ babhūva ha
children.translated_text: And <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> was on the side of the <s>Pāṇḍavas</s>; a battle took place between them.
It was weapon against weapon, very terrible, for ten nights, arrow against arrow.
Covered with hundreds of arrows from <s>Śikhaṇḍin</s> and <s>Arjuna</s>, <s>Bhīṣma</s>
awaited the northern course of the sun, meditating on the god <s>Gadādhara</s>.
Having spoken many kinds of <s>dharma</s> and satisfied many ancestors,

children.text: ānande tu pade līno vimale muktakilbiṣe ||
children.translated_text: he merged into the blissful, stainless state, free from sin.

children.text: tato droṇo yayau yoddhuṃ dhṛṣṭadyumnena vīryavān
children.translated_text: Then mighty <s>Droṇa</s> went to fight with <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s>.
That battle lasted five days and was exceedingly dreadful.

children.text: yatra te pṛthivīpālā hatāḥ pārthena saṃgare
children.translated_text: There those kings of the earth were slain by <s>Pārtha</s> in battle.
Having entered an ocean of grief, <s>Droṇa</s> too reached heaven.
Then <s>Karṇa</s> went to fight with the great-souled <s>Arjuna</s>.
After fighting a great battle for two days in the ocean of <s>Pārtha</s>'s weapons,

children.text: nimagnaḥ sūryalokaṃ tu tataḥ prāpa sa vīryavān ||
children.translated_text: the valiant one, sunk there, then reached the world of the sun.

children.text: tataḥ śalyo yayau yoddhuṃ dharmarājena dhīmatā
children.translated_text: Then <s>Śalya</s> went to fight with wise <s>Dharmarāja</s>.
In half a day <s>Śalya</s> was killed by arrows resembling blazing fire.
Then the valiant <s>Duryodhana</s>, swiftly taking up his mace,
rushed against <s>Bhīma</s>, like <s>Yama</s> the ender at the end of time.
Then he was struck down with a mace by heroic <s>Bhīma</s>.

children.text: aśvatthāmā gato drauṇiḥ suptasainyaṃ tato niśi ||
children.translated_text: After that <s>Aśvatthāman</s>, <s>Drauṇi</s>, went by night to the sleeping army.
Remembering the killing of his father, he slew them by the strength of his arms.
Then the valiant one killed <s>Dhṛṣṭadyumna</s> and the sons of <s>Draupadī</s>.
While <s>Draupadī</s> was weeping, <s>Arjuna</s>, having conquered <s>Aśvatthāman</s>
with the <s>aiṣika</s> weapon, took the excellent jewel from his head.
<s>Yudhiṣṭhira</s> comforted the women, who were overwhelmed with grief;
then, after bathing, he satisfied the gods, the fathers, and the grandfathers.
After being reassured by <s>Bhīṣma</s>, he ruled the great kingdom,
and duly worshiped <s>Viṣṇu</s> with an <s>aśvamedha</s> furnished with gifts.
Having installed <s>Parīkṣit</s> in the kingdom, and having heard of the destruction of the <s>Yādavas</s>

children.text: śrutvā tu mausale rājā japtvā nāmasahasrakam ||
children.translated_text: in the <s>Mausala</s> episode, the king recited the thousand names.
Then he went to the heaven of <s>Viṣṇu</s>, together with his brothers beginning with <s>Bhīma</s>.
<s>Vāsudeva</s> again became <s>Buddha</s> for the bewilderment of the enemies of the gods.
And <s>Viṣṇu</s> will again become <s>Kalki</s> in the village of <s>Śambhala</s>.
Mounted on a horse, he will then reduce all the worlds to ashes.
For the protection of the gods and the others, and for the removal of <s>adharma</s> (unrighteousness),

children.text: duṣṭānāṃ ca vadhārthāya hyavatāraṃ karoti ca ||
children.translated_text: and also for the purpose of killing the wicked, he takes an avatāra.
Thus <s>Dhanvantari</s> was born in the lineage at the churning of the Milk Ocean,
and he spoke <s>āyurveda</s> for the life of the gods and the others.
He taught it to the great-souled <s>Suśruta</s>, the son of <s>Viśvāmitra</s>.
A man who has heard the <s>Bhāratas</s> and the avatāras goes to heaven.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe bhāratādivarṇanaṃ nāma pañcacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one-hundred-and-forty-fifth chapter, called 'The Description of the <s>Bhārata</s> and the Other Accounts.'
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
O <s>Suśruta</s>, I shall explain truly the cause of all diseases,
as it was formerly declared by the excellent sages beginning with <s>Ātreya</s>.

children.text: rogaḥ pāpmā jvaro vyādhirvikāro duṣṭa āmayaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Roga</s>, <s>pāpman</s>, fever, illness, disorder, corruption, and <s>āmaya</s>,
as well as consumption, terror, malady, and affliction, are synonymous words.
<s>Nidāna</s> (cause), preliminary forms, manifest forms, <s>upaśaya</s> (relieving regimen),

children.text: saṃprāptiś ceti vijñānaṃ rogāṇāṃ pañcadhā smṛtam ||
children.translated_text: and <s>saṃprāpti</s> (pathogenesis): the knowledge of diseases is remembered as fivefold.
By the synonyms occasion, cause, seat, condition, arising, and reason,
they speak of <s>nidāna</s>; through it the preliminary form is recognized.
A disease that is about to arise, not yet established in a particular <s>doṣa</s>,
has an indistinct sign because of its slightness; this is so in the case of each disease.
That very thing, when it has become manifest, is called its form.
Configuration, indication, sign, mark, and shape are its terms.
The use of medicines, foods, and modes of living that are contrary to the cause and the disease,
or that act in a contrary way, and that bring comfort,

children.text: vidyādupaśayaṃ vyādheḥ sa hi sātmyamiti smṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: one should know as the <s>upaśaya</s> of a disease; that is remembered as what is suitable.
The opposite is <s>anupaśaya</s>, called what is unsuitable for the disease.
In accordance with the corrupted <s>doṣa</s>, and according as it spreads through the body,
the formation of the disease is called its <s>saṃprāpti</s>.
It is divided according to distinctions of number, variation, predominance, strength, and time,

children.text: sā bhidyate yathātraiva vakṣyante 'ṣṭau jvarā iti ||
children.translated_text: as here, for example, when it will be said that there are eight fevers.
Among combined <s>doṣas</s>, variation is the reckoning of their respective portions.
One should indicate the predominance of a disease by independence and dependence.
Strength and weakness are specified by the completeness or partialness of the causes and the rest.
The time of a disease is determined, according to the impurity, by night, day, half-day, and portions after eating.
Thus the meaning of <s>nidāna</s> has been stated; it will be taught in detail.
For all diseases, the cause is the provoked impurities.
Their provocation is said to come from the varied practice of what is unwholesome.
The unwholesome conjunction of the three has previously been declared to be threefold.
<s>Samīraṇa</s> (vāta) is aggravated by excessive use of bitter, hot, astringent, sour, and dry things,
by running, forcing out urges, keeping awake at night, and speaking too loudly,
by strenuous activity, fear, grief, anxiety, exercise, and sexual intercourse,
and in summer, at the end of the day and night, and after meals.
<s>Pitta</s> is aggravated by pungent, sour, sharp, hot, acrid, anger-producing, and burning things,
and in autumn, at midday, at midnight, and at times of burning heat.
<s>Śleṣman</s> is aggravated by sweet, sour, salty, oily, heavy, clogging, and cold things,
by sitting, sleep, pleasure, indigestion, day-sleep, and other nourishing factors,
by the non-application of vomiting and the like, and also when eaten food is undigested,

children.text: pūrvāhne pūrvarātre ca śleṣmā vakṣyāmi saṅkarān ||
children.translated_text: in the forenoon and in the first part of the night; I shall explain the mixed conditions.
Through the mixing of all of them there is <s>sannipāta</s>, the combined disorder.
Again, it arises from eating mixed, undigested, irregular, incompatible, and similar foods,
from spoiled wine and water, dried vegetables, and raw roots,
from oil-cake and from putrid, dried, lean, or otherwise bad meats,
from those various things that produce the three <s>doṣas</s>, and from changes in food,
from corrupted bodily constituents, from prior vāta, and from possession and disturbance by hostile beings,
from corrupted raw food, from excessively phlegmatic seizures, and from affliction of the birth asterism,
from many kinds of improper application and from the practice of sinful acts,
and, for women, from irregularity in childbirth and likewise from improper treatment.
For each disease, the angered <s>doṣas</s> (humoral faults), following the particular mode of the disease,
quickly enter the channels of rasa and disturb the body.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe sarvaroganidānaṃ nāma ṣaṭcatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus ends the one hundred forty-sixth chapter, named "The Cause of All Diseases," in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s> of the first section called the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall explain the cause of fever, for the understanding of all fevers.
<s>Jvara</s> (fever) is the lord of diseases, evil, the king of death, the eater, the ender,
born from the upper eye of <s>Rudra</s>, who in anger destroyed <s>Dakṣa</s>'s sacrifice.
Its heat is filled with delusion; heat is its nature, and it is born from transgression.
Cruel and known by many different names, it exists in many kinds of beings.
Among elephants it is called <s>Pākala</s>, among horses <s>Abhitāpa</s>, and among dogs <s>Alarka</s>.

children.text: indramado jaladeṣv apsu nīlikā jyotiroṣadhīṣu bhūmyāmūṣaro nāma ||
children.translated_text: Among clouds it is <s>Indramada</s>; in waters, <s>Nīlikā</s>; in luminaries and plants, another form; and on earth it is called <s>Ūṣara</s>.
Nausea, vomiting, cough, stiffness, coldness in the skin and the like,
and eruptions arising on the limbs occur in fever produced by <s>kapha</s> (phlegmatic humor).
For all of them, onset or increase occurs at the proper time according to each one's nature.
There is lack of relief from the measures stated under the cause, and relief comes from the opposite treatment.
Loss of appetite, indigestion, stiffness, and also sluggishness,
burning in the heart, impaired digestion, drowsiness, and sluggishness as well,
distress in the bladder and bowels, and non-movement of the <s>doṣas</s>,
flowing saliva, nausea, loss of hunger, and a tasteless mouth,
clear and warm heaviness of the limbs and abundant urination:

children.text: na vijīrṇaṃ na ca mlānirjvarasyāmasya lakṣaṇam ||
children.translated_text: when there is no digestion and no lassitude, this is the sign of raw, immature fever.
Emaciation from hunger, lightness of the limbs, and mildness of the fever,
with movement of the <s>doṣas</s> after eight days: these are the signs of a fever free from rawness.
In a mixed condition, a fever born from combination should be known by the signs proper to each.
Headache, fainting, vomiting, burning of the body, dryness of the throat and mouth, loss of appetite, and splitting pain in the joints,
sleeplessness, agitation, horripilation, yawning, and excessive speech arise from <s>vāta</s> together with <s>pitta</s>.
Loss of heat, loss of appetite, pain in the joints and head, spitting, difficult breathing, cough, and discoloration,
chill, torpor, darkness before the eyes, dizziness, and drowsiness are the signs of fever produced by <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Irregularity of cold, stiffness, sweat, and burning, thirst, cough, and the activity of <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: mohas tandrā liptatiktāsyatā ca jñeyaṃ rūpaṃ śleṣmapittajvarasya ||
children.translated_text: delusion, drowsiness, a coated tongue, and bitterness in the mouth: this should be known as the form of <s>kapha</s>-<s>pitta</s> fever.
A fever produced by all the <s>doṣas</s> has all the symptoms, and in it burning occurs again and again.
There is great sleep after a rise of heat, and wakefulness by day and night.

children.text: sadā vā naiva vā nidrā mahāsvedo hi naiva vā
children.translated_text: There may always be sleep, or none at all; there may be profuse sweating, or none at all.
Singing, dancing, laughter, and the like occur, and natural behavior no longer proceeds.
The eyes are tearful, turbid, red, sunken, and with disordered eyelashes.
There is pain and dizziness in the calves, flanks, head, joints, and bones.

children.text: sasvanau sarujau karṇau mahāśītau hi naiva vā
children.translated_text: The ears are noisy and painful, and there may be great cold, or none at all.
The tongue is burnt and rough, and there is heaviness and distress in the limbs and joints.
There is spitting of blood and <s>pitta</s>, tossing of the head, and extreme thirst.
One sees dark-red patches and circular marks in the internal passages.
There is pain in the heart, mixture with fecal matter, and evacuation either in small amount or excessive amount.
There is unctuousness of the mouth, loss of strength, sinking of the voice, and delirious speech.
The <s>doṣas</s> remain long in maturation, drowsiness persists, and there is constant gurgling in the throat.
One should call that condition <s>sannipāta</s> and <s>abhinyāsa</s>, in which the vital vigor is destroyed.
When the throat is obstructed by <s>vāyu</s> (wind), the <s>pitta</s> within is severely compressed.
Because it spreads and because there is an opening, it takes an outward path.
Because of that, in fever arising from <s>sannipāta</s>, the eyes become yellow like turmeric.
When the <s>doṣas</s> are greatly increased and the digestive fire is lost, with all symptoms fully present,
<s>sannipāta</s> fever is incurable; otherwise it is difficult to cure.
Apart from fever arising from <s>sannipāta</s>, where <s>pitta</s> stands separately,

children.text: tvaci koṣṭhe ca vā dāhaṃ vidadhāti puro 'nu vā ||
children.translated_text: it produces burning in the skin or in the abdomen, either before or after.
In the same way, in <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, there is cold; burning and the other symptoms are hard to overcome in them.
When cold comes first there, because of <s>pitta</s>, the <s>kapha</s> becomes liquefied and dried up.

children.text: pitte śānte 'tha vai mūrchā madastṛṣṇā ca jāyate
children.translated_text: When <s>pitta</s> is calmed, fainting, intoxication, and thirst then arise.
When burning and the rest come first, then in due order drowsiness, sluggishness, and vomiting occur at the end.
An adventitious fever is of four kinds, from injury, attachment or possession, curse, and sorcery.
Fever born from injury is accompanied by sweating in four ways, with burning and the other symptoms.
In that condition, usually because of exertion, <s>pavana</s> (wind) corrupts the blood
and produces fever with pain, grief, discoloration, and soreness.
It may arise from seizure by spirits, drugs, poison, anger, fear, grief, or desire.
In this condition, seizure through attachment or possession is marked by sudden weeping by day.
When caused by the smell of drugs, there is fainting, headache, vomiting, and wasting.
From poison come fainting and diarrhea, with dark discoloration, burning, and dizziness.
From anger come trembling, headache, and delirious speech; from fear and grief, similar symptoms arise.
From desire come dizziness, loss of appetite, burning, shame, sleeplessness, and loss of understanding and firmness.
In seizure and the like there are forms of <s>sannipāta</s>; at their beginning there are forms of wind.
Through aggravation, even in aggravation, there are forms of <s>pitta</s>; but the two fevers born from curse and sorcery
are terrible <s>sannipāta</s> fevers and are considered the most unbearable.
A person afflicted by sorcerous rites and mantras is tormented and burns.
First the mind is affected, then the body, and then there are blisters and directional bewilderments.
For one seized by burning and fainting, the fever increases every day.

children.text: iti jvaro 'ṣṭadhā dṛṣṭaḥ samāsād dvividhastu saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus fever is seen in eight forms; in summary, however, it is twofold:
bodily and mental, gentle and sharp, and having its seat within or without.
It is natural, altered, curable or incurable, with <s>āma</s> (undigested morbid matter) or without <s>āma</s>.

children.text: pūrvaṃ śarire śarīre tāpo manasi mānase
children.translated_text: First, in the body there is bodily heat, and in the mind there is mental heat;
because the winds act as carriers of conjunction, coldness arises when it is joined with <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: dāhaḥ pittayute miśraṃ miśre 'ntaḥ saṃśraye punaḥ
children.translated_text: When joined with <s>pitta</s> there is burning; when mixed there is a mixed condition; again, when it is lodged internally,
in fever the disorders become greater: internal agitation and retention of the wastes.

children.text: bahireva bahirvege tāpo 'pi ca sa sādhitaḥ
children.translated_text: But when the impulse is only outward, the heat too is external, and that is treatable.
In the rainy season, autumn, and spring it is natural, respectively, through <s>vāta</s> and the other doṣas.
Another fever is altered and hard to cure; the natural one is usually from <s>vāta</s>.
In the rains, corrupted <s>māruta</s> produces fever accompanied by <s>pitta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: kuryācca pittaṃ śaradi tasya cānucaraḥ kaphaḥ
children.translated_text: In autumn <s>pitta</s> produces it, and <s>kapha</s> is its attendant.
Because of that natural constitution and because it is a time of release, there is no danger there from fasting.
In spring <s>kapha</s> produces it, and <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> may follow that too.
In strong persons, when the doṣas are slight and there are no complications, fever is curable.
When derangement is known in every respect, it has previously been declared incurable.
Sharpness of the complications of fever, weak digestive fire, excessive urination,
no evacuation, no digestion of food, no hunger, and the appearance of <s>āma-jvara</s> (fever with undigested morbidity),
a stronger onset of fever, thirst, delirious speech, labored breathing, and dizziness,
evacuation of stool and nausea are the signs of a fever that is being digested.
When it is becoming digested and no contrary sign appears, one should fast for seven nights.
Fever is said to be fivefold according to the strength and weakness of the doṣa, time, and force.
For the most part it is taught as arising more often from <s>sannipāta</s> (combined disturbance of the doṣas).
It is continuous, constant, occurring on alternate days, tertian, and quartan.
The doṣas pervade the channels carrying the tissues, urine, and feces;
heating the whole body, and increased by factors of similar corruption,
when strong and heavy, they reside especially in <s>rasa</s> (nutritive fluid) without distinction.
Having no opposing force, they continuously produce an extremely unbearable fever.
Then the heat of fever quickly wastes the doṣa, or else the tissues.
In every form, according to the cleansing or uncleanness of <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues, the process proceeds in order.
Through <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>, after seven, ten, or twelve days,

children.text: prāyo 'nuyāti maryādāṃ mokṣāya ca vadhāya ca
children.translated_text: it usually reaches its limit, either for release or for death.
This is the opinion of <s>Agniveśa</s>; but in the tradition of <s>Hārīta</s>,

children.text: dviguṇā saptamī yā ca navamyekādaśī tathā
children.translated_text: the doubled seventh day, and likewise the ninth and the eleventh,

children.text: eṣā tridoṣamaryādā mokṣāya ca vadhāya ca ||
children.translated_text: these are the limits for a three-doṣa fever, either for release or for death.
According to cleansing or uncleanness, fever may continue here even for a long time.
In the emaciated, in those afflicted with disease, and in those who practice improper diet and the like,
even a small doṣa, gaining strength from any one cause beginning with corruption,
because it is opposed and irregular, accompanied by increase and decrease,
and because it has interruptions, produces irregular fever, sharing in irregular wasting and growth.

children.text: doṣaḥ pravartate teṣāṃ sve kāle jvarayanbalī ||
children.translated_text: For them the doṣa becomes active in its own time and, being strong, causes fever.
Then it subsides again according to the strength or weakness of the opposing force.
A fever whose doṣa has been diminished becomes subtle and dissolves into <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues.
Because it is dissolved there, it bears signs such as emaciation, discoloration, and dullness.
Because the openings of the <s>rasa</s>-carrying channels are near and deranged,

children.text: āśu sarvasya vapuṣo vyāptidoṣo na jāyate
children.translated_text: a doṣa spread through the whole body does not arise quickly.
For that reason the fever is continuous and constant; the opposite arises from the opposite condition.
Irregular fever has an irregular onset and is associated with the time of night.

children.text: doṣo raktāśrayaḥ prāyaḥ karoti saṃtataṃ jvaram ||
children.translated_text: A doṣa lodged mostly in the blood produces continuous fever.
At the junction of day and night it occurs once, when it has the alternate-day basis.
In that case the flesh-carrying channel is involved; in tertian fever, the fat-carrying channel is involved.
A gripping form comes from <s>pitta</s> and <s>vāta</s> in the head, and from <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> in the sacral region;
when the back is included, it comes from <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>, and it is remembered as having an interval of one day.
Quartan fever is situated by the doṣas in either fat, marrow, or bone.
Another kind, located in the marrow itself, indeed displays its distinctive effect.
It is twofold: from <s>kapha</s> through the thighs and shanks, and first through the head from <s>vāta</s>.
Having entered bone and marrow, it is the inverse of quartan fever.

children.text: tridhā tryahaṃ jvarayati dinamekaṃ tu muñcati
children.translated_text: In three ways it causes fever for three days and releases the patient for one day.
According to the strength and weakness of doṣas born from other activities and causes,
when they are digested and no contrary sign appears, one should fast for seven nights.
Fever may arise from the mind in the same way, and also from karma, at one time or another.
Because it moves in deep tissues, because it arises from <s>sannipāta</s>,
and because the doṣas are equally elevated, quartan fever is difficult to treat.
Among these subtle fevers, because they are subtle and very remote,
and because a small doṣa travels slowly for a long time through the pathways of blood and the rest,
it does not enter the body completely, and therefore produces heat and the like.

children.text: kramo yatnena vicchinnaḥ satāpo lakṣyate jvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: When the course has been interrupted with effort, fever is recognized as accompanied by heat.
Irregular fever has an irregular onset and follows the time of night.
In each later type, as appropriate, its movement is slower and its strength weaker.
In time, in corresponding ways, it reaches <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues accordingly.
The angered doṣa causes fever after a long, and still longer, interval.

children.text: bhūmau sthitaṃ jalaiḥ siktaṃ kālaṃ naiva pratīkṣate
children.translated_text: A seed placed in the ground and sprinkled with water does not wait for its season
in order to sprout; so too is the seed of doṣa.

children.text: vegaṃ kṛtvā viṣaṃ yadvadāśaye nayate balam
children.translated_text: Just as poison, after producing an impulse, carries strength to its seat,
and, having gained strength, flares up again, so too is the poison of time and doṣa.
Thus irregular fevers proceed, including the constant and the other kinds.
Nauseous agitation, heaviness, dejection, breaking pain in the limbs, and yawning,
loss of taste, vomiting, labored breathing: these occur in every fever that has gone into <s>rasa</s>.
Spitting of blood, thirst, dry heat, and the arising of eruptions occur.
When it has taken refuge in the blood, there are burning, redness, dizziness, intoxication, and delirious speech;
thirst, exhaustion, affected feces, internal burning, dizziness, and darkness.
When it is situated in the flesh there is foul odor and tossing of the limbs; when it is situated in the fat,
there are sweating, excessive thirst, vomiting, foul odor, or intolerance.
When it has gone into the bone there are delirious speech, exhaustion, lack of taste, and splitting pain in the bones.
There is activity of the <s>doṣas</s>, arousal, difficult breathing, convulsion of the limbs, and moaning.

children.text: antardāho bahiḥ śaityaṃ śvāso hikkā hi majjage
children.translated_text: When it has gone into the marrow there are internal burning, external coldness, difficult breathing, and hiccup;
seeing darkness, cutting pain in the vital spots, and stiffness of the penis.
When semen is discharged, death occurs if it has taken refuge in the semen.
Each later condition is harder to cure than the preceding one; the other five are the reverse.
As if smearing the limbs with <s>śleṣman</s> and with heaviness,
a mild fever with delirious speech and coldness is called <s>pralepaka</s>.
When there is a constant mild fever, dry in character, and coldness departs only with difficulty,
with stiff limbs and a predominance of <s>śleṣman</s>, it is called <s>aṅgabalāsaka</s>.
It has the appearance of the color of split turmeric and passes urine with a coating like that.

children.text: sa vai hāridrako nāma jvarabhedo 'ntakaḥ smṛtaḥ ||
children.translated_text: That variety of fever is called <s>hāridraka</s>, and it is remembered as deadly.
When <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s> are equal in a person whose <s>pitta</s> is deficient,

children.text: tīkṣṇo 'thavā divā mando jāyate rātrijo jvaraḥ ||
children.translated_text: a fever arises at night, either sharp or mild by day.
When strength has been taken away by the sun and the body has been dried out by exertion,
fever from <s>vāta</s> regularly occurs in the early part of the night.
When <s>vāta</s> is lodged in its own place in the stomach and <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s> are situated below,

children.text: tadardhaṃ śītalaṃ dehe hyardhaṃ coṣṇaṃ prajāyate ||
children.translated_text: then one half of the body becomes cold and the other half hot.

children.text: kāye pittaṃ yadā nyastaṃ śleṣmā cānte vyavasthitaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>pitta</s> is placed in the trunk and <s>śleṣman</s> is settled at the extremities,
there is heat in the body because of that, and coldness in the hands and feet.
That which rests in the chyle and blood is curable; so too that which has gone to the flesh and fat,
but that which has gone to the bone and marrow is difficult, its brightness destroyed in each corresponding limb.
Unconscious and afflicted by the force of fever, he looks about as if angry.

children.text: sadoṣam uṣṇaṃ ca sadā śakṛnmuñcati vegavat ||
children.translated_text: He constantly passes hot, morbid feces with force.
Lightness of the body, absence of weariness, confusion, and heat, proper digestion, clearness in the mouth, excellence of the senses, and freedom from pain,

children.text: svedaḥ kṣuvaḥ prakṛtiyogimano 'nnalipsā kaṇḍūśca mūrdhni vigatajvaralakṣaṇāni ||
children.translated_text: sweat, sneezing, the mind's return to its natural condition, desire for food, and itching on the head are signs that fever has departed.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe jvaranidānādikaṃ nāma saptacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one-hundred-and-forty-seventh chapter, called 'The Diagnosis and Related Matters of Fever.'
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
Now therefore I shall explain the cause of <s>raktapitta</s>.
By very hot, bitter, pungent, sour, salty, and other burning substances,
by <s>kodrava</s>, <s>uddālaka</s>, and the other things previously mentioned when used excessively,

children.text: kupitaṃ paittikaiḥ pittaṃ dravaṃ raktaṃ ca mūrchati ||
children.translated_text: <s>pitta</s>, aggravated by pitta-producing factors, and liquid blood become disordered.
Through those factors they come to have mutually similar forms and spread through the body.
Because of the corruption of <s>pitta</s> and blood, from their conjunction and even from biting,
when smell and color follow blood, it is designated by the name of blood.
It arises from the seats of blood, from the spleen and from the liver.
Heaviness of the head, lack of taste, desire for cold, a smoky sensation, sourness,

children.text: charditaś chardibaibhatsyaṃ kāsaḥ śvāso bhramaḥ klamaḥ ||
children.translated_text: vomiting, disgust at vomiting, cough, difficult breathing, dizziness, and fatigue occur.

children.text: lohito na hito matsyagandhāsyātvaṃ ca vijvare
children.translated_text: There is redness, what is not wholesome, and the mouth smells like fish when fever is absent.
There is red, yellow, and green coloration in the eyes and other parts.
There is failure to distinguish the colors blue, red, and yellow.
In dreams there is a condition resembling madness when this disease is about to arise.
When aggravated, it proceeds upward through the nose, eyes, ears, and mouth, and downward through the penis, vagina, and anus;
also through the hair follicles, or through all of these together.
The upward form is curable, because it begins with <s>kapha</s>; it is cured by purgation.
For <s>pitta</s>, purgation is indeed the best medicine, even where many medicines are available.

children.text: anubandhī kapho yatra tatra tasyāpi śuddhikṛt
children.translated_text: Where <s>kapha</s> accompanies it, a cleansing procedure for that too should be performed.

children.text: kaṣāyāḥ svādavo yasya viśuddhau śleṣmalā hitāḥ ||
children.translated_text: After purification, astringent and sweet remedies that promote <s>śleṣman</s> are beneficial.
Or remedies that are pungent, bitter, and astringent, and that by nature move <s>kapha</s>, are beneficial.
The downward form is manageable but does not grant long life; it is to be cured by induced vomiting.
For <s>pitta</s>, emesis is a lesser medicine, but it is not no medicine.
For a person whose strength remains and whose <s>pitta</s> has been calmed,
astringent treatment is beneficial for him, and only sweet substances.
When it is mixed with <s>kapha</s> and <s>māruta</s>, and turns back upward, it is incurable.
It is unbearable because it moves counter to the proper direction, and because medicine is ineffective at the incurable stage.

children.text: na hi saṃśodhanaṃ kiṃcidasya ca pratilominaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is no purificatory treatment at all for this disease when it is moving contrary to the proper direction.
In <s>raktapitta</s>, cleansing and counter-directional treatment are prescribed.
In just this way, both pacification and purification are desired here.

children.text: saṃsṛṣṭeṣu hi doṣeṣu sarvathā chardanaṃ hitam
children.translated_text: For when the <s>doṣas</s> are mixed, vomiting is beneficial in every way.

children.text: tatra doṣo 'tra gamanaṃ śivāstra iva lakṣyate ||
children.translated_text: There the movement of the <s>doṣa</s> is observed here as if it were a weapon of <s>Śiva</s>.
Complications and morbid alteration are established in them from their effects.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe raktapittanidānaṃ nāmāṣṭacatvāriṃśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
