children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one-hundred-and-forty-eighth chapter, called 'The Diagnosis of <s>Raktapitta</s>.'
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:

children.text: āśukārī yataḥ kāsaḥ sa evātaḥ pravakṣyate
children.translated_text: Since cough acts quickly, therefore it will now be explained.
Five coughs are remembered: those caused by <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>śleṣman</s>, injury, and wasting.
All of them, if neglected, lead to wasting, and each later one is stronger than the preceding.
The signs of their impending occurrence are itching in the throat and loss of taste.
There is dryness of the ears, mouth, and throat; in this case the wind is directed downward.

children.text: ūrdhvaṃ pravṛttaḥ prāpyoras tasminkaṇṭhe ca saṃsṛjan ||
children.translated_text: Having moved upward and reached the chest, and then combining in that throat,
it fills the vessels and channels, and then throws the limbs upward.
As if tossing the eyes about, with a distressed voice and pressing on the flanks,
it proceeds with a bent mouth, making a sound like cracked bronze.
It causes pain in the heart, flanks, chest, and head, stupor, agitation, and loss of voice,
and a dry cough, with a noise of great force and pain.
With horripilation, after expelling dry phlegm with difficulty, he becomes reduced.
From <s>pitta</s> come yellowness of the eyes, bitterness of the mouth, fever, and dizziness;
vomiting of <s>pitta</s> and blood, thirst, hoarseness, a smoky sensation, and intoxication;
and, during the repeated force of coughing, the seeing of lights, as it were.
From <s>kapha</s>, there is little pain in the head, while the heart is numb and heavy;
there is coating in the throat, stupor-born oppression, coryza, vomiting, and lack of appetite;
horripilation, and the discharge of thick, unctuous phlegm.
When such violent actions as fighting and the like are undertaken beyond one's strength,
the powerful <s>vāyu</s>, lodged in an injury and accompanied by <s>pitta</s>,

children.text: kupitaḥ kurute kāsaṃ kaphaṃ tena saśoṇitam
children.translated_text: becomes provoked and produces cough; through it the phlegm is mixed with blood.

children.text: pītaṃ śyāvaṃ ca śuṣkaṃ ca grathitaṃ kupitaṃ bahu ||
children.translated_text: He spits out much yellow, dark, dry, clotted, and irritated sputum,
with the throat in pain and the chest as if split apart,
as though pierced by sharp needles, and full of stabbing pain.
There is painfulness to the touch, piercing pain, pressure, and distressing heat;
he has splitting pain in the joints, fever, dyspnea, thirst, hoarseness, and trembling.
Cooing like a dove, he then has pain in the flanks,
vomiting caused by <s>kapha</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>, and his digestion, strength, and complexion decline.
In one who is wasted away there is urine mixed with blood, dyspnea, and stiffness of the back and waist.
The provoked <s>doṣas</s>, chiefly affecting the anal region and moving swiftly as <s>rājayakṣman</s> (consumption),
produce cough in the seats of wasting disease; then he spits phlegm
that resembles foul pus, is putrid, and is mixed with green and red.

children.text: supyate tudyata iva hṛdayaṃ pacatīva ca
children.translated_text: The heart becomes numb, as if being pierced, and seems to be cooking within.
There is sudden desire for heat and cold, eating much, and loss of strength.
The face becomes oily and clear, and the eyes have a lustrous appearance.
Then all the forms of wasting disease become manifest in him.
Thus this is cough born of wasting, a destroyer of the bodies of the emaciated.

children.text: yāpyau vā balināṃ tadvatkṣatajo 'pi navau tu tau ||
children.translated_text: For strong persons it may be only manageable; likewise the cough born of injury. But if those two are recent,
they may even be cured according to one's capacity; in cases beginning with the curable, the treatment is distinct.

children.text: miśrā yāpyāśca ye sarve jarasaḥ sthavirasya ca ||
children.translated_text: Mixed cases are manageable, as are all those arising from old age in an aged person.
Diseases such as cough, dyspnea, wasting, vomiting, and weakness of voice
arise because of neglect; therefore one should overcome them quickly.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe kāsanidānaṃ nāmaikonapañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one-hundred-and-forty-ninth chapter, called 'The Diagnosis of Cough.'
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
Now, therefore, I shall explain the cause of the disease called dyspnea.
Dyspnea arises from the increase of cough, or from earlier aggravations of the <s>doṣas</s>,
and also from <s>āmātisāra</s> (diarrhea with undigested matter), vomiting, poison, <s>pāṇḍu</s> (anemia or pallor), and fever;
from dust, smoke, wind, injury to vital points, and cold water.
There are five types: <s>kṣudraka</s>, <s>tamaka</s>, <s>chinna</s>, <s>mahān</s>, and, fifth, <s>ūrdhva</s>.
The wind whose movement is obstructed by <s>kapha</s>, stationed throughout the body,
vitiates the corrupted channels that carry breath, water, and food.
Located in the chest, it produces dyspnea arising from the stomach.
Its prodromal signs are pain in the heart and flanks, reversal of the vital breath,
distension, and splitting pain in the temples; there, when driven by exertion and overeating,

children.text: preritaḥ prerayankṣudraṃ svayaṃ sa samalaṃ marut
children.translated_text: that impure wind itself drives on the minor form.
Moving contrary to the normal course into the vessels of the head, the wind stirs up <s>kapha</s>.
Seizing the head, neck, chest, and flanks, and pressing upon them,
it causes cough, rattling, stupor, lack of appetite, and severe coryza,
as well as intense attacks of dyspnea that torment the vital breath.
He grows faint from its force; after expectoration he is comfortable for a moment.
Lying down, he breathes with difficulty; seated, he obtains relief.
His eyes are raised upward, he sweats on the forehead, and he is greatly afflicted.
His mouth is dry; he breathes again and again, desires warmth, and trembles.
It is aggravated by clouds, rain, cold, east winds, and phlegm-producing things.

children.text: sa yāpyastamakaḥ sādhyo narasya balino bhavet
children.translated_text: This <s>tamaka</s> type is manageable, but in a strong person it may be curable.
When it is accompanied by fever and fainting, and is not pacified by cold measures, that first condition is grave.
Afflicted by cough, difficult breathing, and the pain of a torn and cut vital part,
with sweating, fainting, distension, burning in the bladder, and troubled awareness,
with downward gaze, whitened eyes, and one sticky, blood-red eye,
dry-mouthed, delirious, wretched, without luster, and unconscious,
the miserable man breathes with a great, heavy sound, groaning.
Heaving upward, enraged, he is like a maddened bull without cease.
His knowledge and discrimination are lost; his eyes and face wander.
He rolls his eyes about, his urine and feces are obstructed, and his speech is broken.
His throat is dry, and again and again there is severe pain in the ears, temples, and head.
He who makes a long upward exhalation and does not draw it back downward,
whose mouth and ears are covered by phlegm and who is afflicted by the enraged <s>gandhavaha</s> wind,
looks upward, bewildered, casting his eyes all around.
As his vital parts are being split, he laments, with speech obstructed.
These conditions, when indistinct, may be cured; when fully manifest, they are certainly fatal.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe śvāsanidānā nāma pañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, called the first part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the one hundred fiftieth chapter, named Diagnosis of <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall also explain the diagnosis of hiccup disease, O <s>Suśruta</s>; listen to it.
Its single cause is connected with <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea); its prodromal form, number, and basis in bodily constitution are to be stated.

children.text: hikkā bhakṣyodbhavā kṣudrā yamalā mahatīti ca
children.translated_text: Hiccup is of these kinds: food-born, minor, paired, great,
and deep. In this matter, the wind, when things are used hastily and improperly,
being oppressed by foods and drinks that are dry, sharp, rough, and uncongenial,
produces hiccup in the breath, low in sound and following upon hunger.

children.text: samaṃ sandhyānnapānena yā prayāti ca sānnajā
children.translated_text: The hiccup that ceases together with food and drink at the proper time is the one born from food.
From exertion, the angered wind sets in motion the minor hiccup.
It spreads from the root of the clavicles and throat, and its impulse is slight.
It increases through exertion and becomes mild immediately after eating.
The hiccup that starts after some time with paired impulses,
and increases in the mouth as digestion proceeds, and at the time of digestion,

children.text: kampayantī śiro grīvāṃ yamalāṃ tāṃ vinirdiśet
children.translated_text: shaking the head and neck, should be identified as the paired hiccup.
Marked by delirious speech, vomiting, diarrhea, disturbed eyes, and yawning,

children.text: yamalā veginī hikkā pariṇāmavatī ca sā
children.translated_text: the paired hiccup is forceful and bound up with the process of digestion.
For a person whose brows and two temples are sunken, whose hearing is disturbed and whose eyes are impaired,

children.text: stambhayantī tanuṃ vācaṃ smṛtiṃ saṃjñāṃ ca muñcatī
children.translated_text: stiffening the body and speech, and releasing memory and consciousness,
piercing along its course and striking the vital spots,
with bending backward of the back, the great hiccup sets in.
It has great pain, a great sound, a great force, and great strength.
It arises from the lower bowel or from the navel, in the manner described before.
Having that form, it causes great yawning and stretching of the limbs.
But the deep hiccup, arising from a deep-seated cause, should be regarded as very hard to cure.

children.text: ādye dve varjayedanye sarvaliṅgāṃ ca veginīm
children.translated_text: One should treat the first two; the others, and a violent hiccup with all symptoms, should be abandoned.
For anyone whose undigested matter has accumulated, for an old man, or for one addicted to intercourse,
for one whose body is wasted by diseases and who is emaciated through interruption of food,

children.text: sarve 'pi rogā nāśāya na tvevaṃ śīghrakāriṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: all diseases may lead to destruction, but none acts so quickly

children.text: hikkāśvāsau yathā tau hi mṛtyukāle kṛtālayau ||
children.translated_text: as hiccup and <s>śvāsa</s> (dyspnea), for those two have taken up their abode at the time of death.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe hikkānidānā nāmaikapañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, called the first part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, the one hundred fifty-first chapter, named Diagnosis of Hiccup, is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
Now then I shall proclaim the diagnosis of the disease <s>yakṣman</s>.
It is accompanied by many diseases and preceded by many diseases.
It is called <s>rājayakṣmā</s>, <s>kṣaya</s> (wasting), <s>śoṣa</s> (drying up), and the king of diseases.
Because in ancient times this was the disease of the king of the lunar mansions and of the twice-born,

children.text: yacca rājā ca yakṣmā ca rājayakṣmā tato mataḥ
children.translated_text: and because it is both royal and a <s>yakṣman</s>, therefore it is considered <s>rājayakṣmā</s>.
Because it brings about wasting of the body and its remedies, and because it arises from depletion, it is <s>kṣaya</s>.
Because it dries up <s>rasa</s> and the other tissues it is <s>śoṣa</s>; it is the king of diseases as a king is among men.
Rash exertion, suppression of urges, depletion of semen, vital vigor, and unctuousness,
and abandonment of the proper regimen for food and drink: these are its four causes.
By these, <s>anila</s> (wind) is stirred up and drives <s>pitta</s> fruitlessly everywhere.
Entering the joints of the body and pressing upon the channels,
blocking the mouths of the ducts, or else opening them too much,
it produces distress in the heart, in the middle, upward, downward, and across.
The signs of its future arising are severe catarrh and fever,
salivation, sweetness in the mouth, and weakness of both digestive fire and body,
craving for food and drink, and seeing what is clean as unclean.
Flies, grass, hair, and the like usually fall into one's food and drink.
There are nausea, vomiting, loss of taste, and loss of strength even when one has bathed.
There is excessive whiteness of the hands, thighs, chest, feet, face, belly, and eyes,
pricking pain in the arms and a disgusting appearance of the tongue and body.
There is fondness for women, liquor, and meat, disgust, and covering of the head.
There is growth of nails, hair, and bones, and in dreams there may be defeat.
One may dream of falling through lizards, snakes, monkeys, wild beasts, and birds,
or of climbing upon heaps of hair, bones, chaff, ashes, and the like.
One sees empty villages and regions, and water drying up.
One sees lights in the sky, forest fires, and trees blazing.
Chronic rhinitis, dyspnea, cough, pain in the voice and head, and loss of appetite occur.
There are upward breathing, drying up, and, when it is situated in the bowel, downward vomiting.

children.text: sthite pārśve ca rugbodhe sandhisthe bhavati jvaraḥ
children.translated_text: When it is situated in the side there is pain and awakening there; when it is situated in the joints there is fever.
These eleven forms arise in <s>rājayakṣmā</s>.
One should know their complications: pains that destroy the throat,
yawning, aching of the limbs, expectoration, weakness of digestion, and foulness of the mouth.
In that condition, from <s>vāta</s> there are pains of the head and side, with aching of the limbs,
obstruction of the throat and failure of the voice; from <s>pitta</s>, in the feet, shoulders, and hands,
there are burning, diarrhea, vomiting of blood, foul smell of the mouth, fever, and intoxication.
From <s>kapha</s> there are loss of taste, vomiting, cough, and heaviness of the upper body,
salivation, chronic rhinitis, dyspnea, alteration of the voice, and weak digestive fire.
Through the <s>doṣas</s>, because the digestive fire is weak, and because swelling, coating, and <s>kapha</s> are predominant,
when the mouths of the channels are blocked and the bodily tissues are diminished,
burning arises in the seat of the mind, and other complications also occur.
Food is cooked only in the bowel, mixed with sour juices.
For the most part, in one whose bodily parts are subject to wasting, food does not nourish the limbs.

children.text: raso hyasya na raktāya māṃsāya kurute tu tat
children.translated_text: For its <s>rasa</s> does not become blood, nor does it become flesh.
Being supported on every side, it continues merely as a wasting condition.
When the signs are few and the disease is not too far wasted, one should avoid the wasting of the six bodily factors in disease;
one should treat it then, but otherwise, in all cases, it should be avoided.
Because of separate and combined <s>doṣas</s>, and because all fat is wasted away,
there is alteration of his voice: the voice is emaciated, dry, and unsteady.
From <s>anila</s> (wind) the throat becomes parrot-colored, with relief from unctuous and hot treatment;
from <s>pitta</s> there is burning in the palate and throat, and constant dryness arises.
As if smearing the throat with phlegm, the mouth makes a gurgling sound;

children.text: svayaṃ viruddhaiḥ sarvaistu sarvāliṅgaiḥ kṣayo bhavet ||
children.translated_text: when all are mutually opposed, wasting arises with all symptoms.
It seems to smoke, and the phlegmatic sign rises up very strongly.

children.text: kṛcchrasādhyāḥ kṣayāścātra sarvair alpaṃ ca varjayet ||
children.translated_text: Here the wasting diseases are difficult to cure; when all signs are present, even a slight case should be rejected.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe yakṣmanidānā nāma dvipañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the earlier part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and fifty-second chapter, named 'Diagnosis of Yakṣman,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
Now, <s>Suśruta</s>, I shall teach you the diagnosis of loss of appetite.
Loss of appetite arises from the <s>doṣas</s> lodged in the tongue and heart.
The fifth type arises from a combined disorder and from distress of the mind.
In the cases of <s>vāta</s> and the others, the mouth is respectively astringent, bitter, and sweet.
In grief, anger, and the like, everything is without taste, just as the mind is.
Because of the corrupted causes of vomiting, separately, by all of them, and by others, there is a fifth type.
The <s>udāna</s> wind, taking up the aggravated <s>doṣas</s>, throws out everything that is fit to be joined together.
Quickly distress arises for him, and salivation and distaste appear in order.
The navel and back quickly hurt, and he throws up food with pain in the side.
Then he vomits broken, scanty, slightly astringent, foamy matter.
With noisy belching, painfully and with repeated difficulty, it comes forth forcefully.
From <s>vāta</s>, it is accompanied by cough, dryness of the mouth, and oppression of the voice.
From <s>pitta</s>, it is like alkaline water, smoky, greenish-yellow,
mixed with blood, sour, pungent, and bitter, with thirst, fainting, burning, and suppuration.
From <s>kapha</s>, it is unctuous, thick, yellow; from phlegm it is like honey,
sweet, salty, abundant, persistent, and causing horripilation.
It has swelling of the mouth, sweetness, drowsiness, nausea, and cough.
When it is furnished with all the signs, it is wholly to be abandoned.
And when everything is hateful to him through sight, hearing, and the other senses,
in the disease produced by worms and by corrupted food, made angry by <s>vāta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>,
colic, trembling, and nausea occur, especially in the worm-born type.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe 'rocakanidānā nāma tripañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the earlier part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and fifty-third chapter, named 'Diagnosis of Loss of Appetite,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
Now, <s>Suśruta</s>, I shall teach you the diagnosis of heart disease and the like.
The conditions situated in the heart are remembered as five, including the signs of worm-born heart disease.
Through <s>vāta</s>, there is extreme emptiness; it is as if the heart is being eaten, and he cries aloud.

children.text: bhidyate śuṣyate stabdhaṃ hṛdayaṃ śūnyatā bhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The heart is split, dried up, and stiff; there is emptiness and dizziness.
Sudden dejection, grief, fear, and intolerance of sound occur,
with trembling, delusion from shaking, obstruction of breath, and little sleep.
From <s>pitta</s> there is thirst, fatigue, burning, sweat, and a sequence involving sour phlegm;
there is vomiting of sour <s>pitta</s>, a smoke-like sensation, and fever.
Through <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), the heart is stiff and heavy, as if it contained a stone,
with cough, weakness of the bones, spitting, sleepiness, laziness, loss of appetite, and fever.

children.text: hṛdroge hi tribhir doṣaiḥ kṛmibhiḥ śyāvanetratā
children.translated_text: In heart disease caused by the three <s>doṣas</s> there are all signs; when caused by worms there is darkening of the eyes,
entry into darkness, nausea, swelling, itching, and a flow of phlegm.
Here the heart is constantly torn apart as if by a saw.
One should treat this terrible illness quickly, for it kills quickly.
Thirst arises from <s>vāta</s>, from <s>pitta</s>, from <s>kapha</s>, from <s>sannipāta</s>, from loss of strength,
and a sixth from an associated disorder; <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> are the cause.
In all these cases, their aggravation, by thoroughly drying up the bodily elements,
causes whirling of the whole body, trembling, heat, burning in the heart, and delusion.
The channels that carry water at the root of the tongue, the throat, the soft palate, and the palate
are dried up, and thirsts arise; their general symptoms are these:
dryness of the mouth, lack of satisfaction from water, aversion to food, and loss of voice;
because of roughness of the throat, lips, and palate, there is fatigue when the tongue is put out.
There is delirious speech, derangement of consciousness, and an illness accompanied by much belching.
From <s>māruta</s> (wind) come emaciation, dejection, splitting pain in the temples, and dizziness of the head.
There is loss of smell, bad taste in the mouth, and loss of hearing, sleep, and strength.
There is increase of cold, sourness, and foam; from <s>pitta</s> come fainting and bitterness of the mouth.
The eyes are constantly red; there is dryness, burning, and excessive smoky sensation.
When <s>kapha</s>, aggravated from the fluid essence, and <s>māruta</s> enter the water-carrying channels,
then the channel, together with <s>kapha</s>, is dried up like mud.
Thereupon the throat feels as if pierced by awns; there is sleepiness and sweetness of the mouth,
distension, heaviness of the head, torpor, vomiting, and loss of appetite,

children.text: ālasyam avipākaṃ ca yaḥ sa syātsarvalakṣaṇaḥ ||
children.translated_text: with laziness and indigestion; one who has all the symptoms is such a case.
From the arising of rawness and from obstruction of the blood there is a condition of <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Thirst arises in one who, overcome by heat, suddenly resorts to cold water.

children.text: uṣṇādūrdhvaṃ gataḥ koṣṭhaṃ kuryādvai pittajaiva sā
children.translated_text: When heat has gone upward into the abdomen, it produces thirst; that one is indeed <s>pitta</s>-born.
And the thirst that arises from excessive drinking, with a sharp initial stage, is born from the cooking of unctuous matter.
From eating unctuous, pungent, sour, and salty food, thirst is <s>kapha</s>-born.
The wasting type is marked by the symptoms stated for thirst caused by depletion of fluid essence.
That severe thirst which arises from wasting, confusion, fever, and other complications of long illness

children.text: yā tṛṣṇā jāyate tīvrā sopasargātmikā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: is remembered as being of the nature of a complication.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe āmlapittanidānā nāma catuḥpañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section called the Pūrva-khaṇḍa, in the Ācārakāṇḍa, the one hundred fifty-fourth chapter, called the diagnosis of <s>āmlapitta</s>, is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall explain the diagnosis of <s>madātyaya</s> and the other disorders, as taught by the sages.
Alcohol is sharp, sour, dry, subtle, sourly penetrating, quick-acting, and light;
it is expansive and clear; because of this it is opposite to fat and vital essence.
Its sharp and other qualities, said to be so, are disturbers of the mind;
when they proceed with the force of poison, they may arise so as to end life.
By its sharp and other qualities, alcohol, when the qualities of <s>ojas</s> are weak,
agitates consciousness with its ten qualities and renders it inactive.
In the first stage of intoxication, and also in the second, when one is situated in the field of heedless pleasure,
a deluded man, overcome by bad judgment, becomes attached to it, thinking, 'This is happiness.'
Having reached the junction of the middle and highest stages, intoxication sits like a king on a throne;
then, like an unchecked serpent, there is nothing that he would not do.
This is the ground for unspeakable acts; this is the abode of bad conduct.
This alone is the supreme revealer of the many paths leading to hard ruin.

children.text: niśceṣṭaḥ san avāk śete tṛtīye 'tra made sthitaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Motionless and speechless, he lies there when he has entered the third stage of intoxication;
that sinful man has reached a state more sinful even than death.
He does not know <s>dharma</s> and <s>adharma</s>, pleasure and pain, honor and misfortune, benefit and harm;
afflicted by grief and delusion, and joined with wasting, confusion, and the like,
he falls downward into madness, dizziness, fainting, and epileptic seizure.
Strong people, those who have eaten, and great eaters do not become excessively intoxicated.
The disease called <s>madātyaya</s> may arise from <s>vāta</s>, from <s>pitta</s>, from <s>kapha</s>, or from all of them together.
Their general signs are stupefaction and pain in the heart.
There are splitting distress, violent thirst, mildness, exhaustion, fever, and lack of appetite;
obstruction in front, darkness of vision, cough, difficult breathing, and wakefulness;
excessive sweating, abdominal distension, swelling, and derangement of the mind.
He is overcome as if by a dream, and, when addressed, he does not speak.

children.text: pittāddāhajvaraḥ svedo moho nityaṃ ca vibhramaḥ ||
children.translated_text: From <s>pitta</s> there are burning, fever, sweating, delusion, and constant confusion.
From <s>kapha</s> there are vomiting, nausea, sleepiness, and heaviness of the abdomen.

children.text: sarvaje sarvaliṅgatvaṃ jñātvā madyaṃ pibettu yaḥ ||
children.translated_text: In the type born from all doṣas, all the signs occur; knowing this, a person who drinks alcohol
may suddenly find the pleasant drink becoming another condition, destructive and drying.
Through <s>māruta</s> it becomes especially severe and hard to endure for him.
In the destructive form there is spitting of phlegm, dryness of the throat, and excessive sleepiness;
there is intolerance of sound, disturbance of the mind, and indeed vāta-pain in the limbs.
There are disorders of the heart and throat, bewilderment, difficult breathing, thirst, vomiting, and fever.
But one who, self-controlled and acting deliberately, turns away from alcoholic drinks

children.text: vikāraiḥ kliśyate jātu na sa śarīramānasaḥ
children.translated_text: is never afflicted by disorders of body and mind.
From passion, delusion, and unsuitable food and drink there are said to be three diseases,
arising from obstruction of the channels that carry fat, blood, and bodily moisture:
<s>mada</s> (intoxication), <s>mūrchā</s> (fainting), and <s>apasaṃnyāsa</s> (complete collapse), each stronger than the preceding.
Here intoxication may be caused by all the doṣas, and also by blood, alcohol, or poisons.
Because its powers are manifold, the person loses his normal appearance, becomes unstable, and his dress is disordered.
In intoxication born of <s>vāta</s>, the body becomes rough, dark, and reddish.
Through <s>pitta</s> he is angry, red-yellow in appearance, and fond of quarrel.
From <s>kapha</s> he has incoherent speech as in sleep and is absorbed in brooding.
When the condition arises from all doṣas together, there is obstruction of blood and corruption of the limbs.
In the first derangement there is the character of <s>pitta</s>, and here one no longer knows one's own command.
There are trembling, excessive sleep, and fatigue greater than that caused by all the others.
One should recognize <s>vāta</s> and the others, in blood and the other seats, from the predominance of their symptoms.
In vāta-type fainting, seeing red, blue, or black, he enters into darkness.
He wakes quickly; there are pain in the heart, trembling, and dizziness.
Cough and a dusky-red complexion occur in fainting whose nature is <s>māruta</s>.

children.text: pittena raktaṃ pītaṃ vā nabhaḥ paśyanviśettamaḥ
children.translated_text: Through <s>pitta</s>, seeing the sky as red or yellow, he enters darkness.
He wakes with sweat, oppressed by burning and thirst.
He appears as though split, yellow and blue in color, with eyes confused by red and blue.
Through <s>kapha</s>, he sees the sky as cloud-like and enters darkness.
From that darkness he wakes only after a long time, with the heart and chest full of salivation.
His limbs are heavy and inert, bound up by oppressive heaviness.
With all forms present through the three doṣas, there is another condition resembling epilepsy;
it quickly throws the person down motionless, but without hideous convulsive movements.
When the doṣas have spent their force in the bodies of living beings during intoxication and fainting,
they subside by themselves, or else through withdrawal and medicines.
Exceedingly powerful disturbances seize the activity of speech, body, and mind;
when they fall together with <s>saṃnyāsa</s> (collapse), they rest on the danger of striking at life.
Because of this, men become like pieces of wood, resembling the dead.

children.text: mriyeta śīghraṃ śīghraṃ ceccikitsā na prayujyate ||
children.translated_text: A person dies very quickly if treatment is not applied at once.
As in a flood of water in a fathomless ocean full of grasping creatures,
one should quickly bring back a man who is sinking in <s>saṃnyāsa</s>.
Through impulses produced here and there by intoxication, pride, anger, and satisfaction,

children.text: yuktāyuktaṃ ca samaṃ yuktiṃ yuṅkte na madyena ||
children.translated_text: a person made drunk by alcohol no longer applies judgment evenly to what is proper and improper.
Strength, time, place, the person, constitution, tolerance, and age
should be distinguished; one then drinks in a way suited to the body, and only then drinks nectar.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe madātyayādinidānaṃ nāma pañcapañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the earlier part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and fifty-fifth chapter, named 'Diagnosis of intoxication and related conditions,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:

children.text: athārśasāṃ nidānaṃ ca vyākhyāsyāmi ca suśruta
children.translated_text: Now, <s>Suśruta</s>, I shall also explain the diagnosis of <s>arśas</s> (piles).

children.text: sarvadā prāṇināṃ māṃse kīlakāḥ prabhavanti ye ||
children.translated_text: Those fleshy pegs which always arise in the flesh of living beings
are therefore called <s>arśas</s>, because they obstruct the anal passage.
The <s>doṣas</s>, having vitiated the skin, flesh, and fat, assume various forms
and produce fleshy sprouts at the opening of the <s>apāna</s> channel; these are called <s>arśas</s>.
In brief, the division is twofold: congenital and arising later in life.
The dry, wet, and other varieties lodge according to the places of the anus.
It measures four and a half finger-breadths; there are three folds there, each situated at one and a half finger-breadths.
Of these, the first is called <s>Pravāhiṇī</s>; in the middle of the intestine is <s>Visarjinī</s>.
The outer one is <s>Saṃvaraṇī</s>, at the beginning of the anus, one finger-breadth outside.
At a further measure of half a finger-breadth are the hairs, and beyond that is the next region.
There the cause of congenital piles is affliction of the seed from the beginning.
The production of the seed of piles comes from misconduct of the mother and father,
from the anger of deities, and otherwise from the combined aggravation of the <s>doṣas</s>.
All diseases arising from the family line are thus declared incurable.
The congenital ones in particular are rough and hard to look at,
turned inward, pale, and accompanied by terrible complications.
They should be assessed separately according to individual <s>doṣa</s>, combination, and accumulation.
Those due to <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> are dry, while those due to <s>pitta</s> are wet.
The causes of aggravation of the <s>doṣas</s> are as stated before in the preceding discussion.
When the digestive fire is weak and stool is excessively accumulated, and also from sexual intercourse,
from drinking, jolting, and irregular, hard, or scanty eating,
from chafing and fissuring caused by an enema-tube and similar instruments,
from contact with very cold water and from continual excessive straining,
from suppressing the urges for urine and feces, or from forcing them out,
from disgust, diarrhea, and <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, that too being a complication,

children.text: karṣaṇād viṣamādeś ca ceṣṭābhyo yoṣitāṃ punaḥ
children.translated_text: from emaciation and from irregular activities, and, again, in women,
from the miscarriage of an unripe fetus and from the pressure of a growing fetus,
by such and other causes the <s>apāna</s> wind, aggravated in the fecal matter,
in the anal folds, moist, round, shining, and full in form,
produces piles. Before that, the preliminary symptom is weakness of digestion;
constipation, sinking pain in the bones, twisting of the calves, and dizziness;
dense swelling arising in the eyes; the stool may be broken, or there may be retention;
the <s>māruta</s> (wind), obstructed in front, generally moves below the navel;
mixed with blood and cutting all around, it painfully contracts as he breathes.
There is rumbling of the intestines, distension, and an abundance of acrid belching;
abundant urine, little feces, lack of appetite, and a smoky condition of the abdomen;
pain in the head, back, and chest, lassitude, and disordered stool;
craving for objects of the senses, and anger because treatment is distressing;
anxiety, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease, swelling, and conditions involving pallor, abdominal tumors, and enlargement of the belly.
These same symptoms increase when the piles have arisen and remain untreated.
For, being turned back by the obstruction of the lower passage caused by them,
the wind agitates the other winds that move through all the senses and the body.
Likewise, drying up urine, feces, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and wind,
it steals away the digestive fire; then those afflicted with piles generally become

children.text: kṛśo bhṛśaṃ hatotsāho dīnaḥ kṣāmo 'tha niṣprabhaḥ ||
children.translated_text: emaciated, greatly lacking vigor, miserable, wasted, and lusterless,
without substance and with their complexion gone, like a tree burned by insects.
They are afflicted by difficult and severe fluid discharges and by pains in vital spots such as are described for consumption,
as well as by cough, thirst, bad taste in the mouth, dyspnea, and nasal catarrh,
fatigue, breaking pain in the limbs, vomiting, sneezing, swelling, and fever,
impotence, deafness, stupor, and the torment of urinary gravel.
Wasted, with broken voice, brooding, repeatedly spitting, and lacking appetite,
he has pain in all the joints, bones, heart, navel, anus, and groins.
Through the anus there flows <s>pitta</s> resembling the belly of a heron,
very dry, with a pearl-like tip, and alternately digested and undigested.
He passes pale-yellow, turmeric-tinged, and slimy matter.
The anal sprouts in which much wind predominates are dry and attended with tingling;
they are plump, coal-red, rigid, uneven, and rough in form,
mutually dissimilar, crooked, sharp, and with split mouths,
resembling pods, dates, jujube fruits, or cotton fruits.
Some look like <s>kadamba</s> flowers, and some resemble mustard seeds.
They bring excessive pain in the head, sides, shoulders, shanks, thighs, groins, and other parts.
They cause sneezing, belching, constipation, oppression of the heart, and loss of appetite,
and bring cough, dyspnea, irregular digestion, ringing in the ears, and dizziness.
Afflicted by them, he passes a knotted, scanty discharge, noisy and accompanied by straining,
painful, followed by foam and mucus, and obstructed.
He becomes dark-skinned, with feces and urine bound, and with darkened eyes and face.
For him there may also arise <s>gulma</s> (abdominal tumor), splenic enlargement, abdominal disease, and <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>.
Those in which <s>pitta</s> predominates have bluish mouths and an appearance that is red, yellow, or black.
They have thin tips, ooze, smell foul, and are slender, soft, and lax.
They resemble a parrot's tongue, a piece of liver, or the mouth of a leech.
They cause burning, feverish distress, sweating, thirst, fainting, loss of appetite, and delusion.
They are hot, and the stool is liquid, bluish, hot, yellow, red, and undigested.
They are barley-shaped in the middle, and the skin, nails, and the like become greenish-yellow and turmeric-colored.
Those in which <s>śleṣman</s> predominates have large roots, are dense, only mildly painful, and white.
They are swollen, increased, unctuous, rigid, round, heavy, and firm;
slimy, motionless, smooth, rich in itching, and pleasant to the touch.
They have the appearance of karīra fruit and jackfruit seeds, and resemble the teats of a cow.
They cause cutting pains in the groins, anus, bladder, and navel,
with cough, dyspnea, nausea, salivation, loss of appetite, and catarrh.
They bring great difficulty, dullness of the head, coldness, and caustic effects,
and they cause impotence, weakness of the digestive fire, vomiting, diarrhea, and other disorders.
They are accompanied by discharges of stool and blood, abounding in fat-like and phlegmatic matter,
yet they do not flow out and do not burst; their surface and the like are pale and unctuous.
From mixed signs, from conjunction, and from accumulation, there are all the symptoms.
When blood is predominant, the pegs in the anus are marked by a yellowish form;
they are like shoots of the banyan and resemble guñjā berries and coral.
These, being extremely vitiated and hot, and afflicted by tight obstruction of stool,
suddenly discharge blood; and because that blood flows excessively,
he is tormented by sufferings arising from loss of blood.
His color, strength, and energy are diminished, his vitality is struck down, and his senses are clouded.
By mung beans, kodo millet, citron, karīra, chickpeas, and the like,
which are dry and constipating, powerful <s>vāyu</s> becomes aggravated in the place of the feces.
It blocks the downward-carrying channels and dries up what is below;
it produces a terrible obstruction of stool, flatus, and urine.
Because of that, severe pain arises in the abdomen, back, heart, and sides.
There is distension in the belly, obstruction of feces, nausea, and cutting pain,
and especially severe colic in the bladder, with swelling like a lump.
Because the wind moves upward, vomiting, loss of appetite, and fevers then arise,
as well as heart disease, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, retention of urine, and dysentery.
Deafness, severe headache, dyspnea, pain in the head, cough, and catarrh occur,
along with mental disorder, thirst, breathlessness, bilious abdominal masses, abdominal disease, and the like.

children.text: ete ca vātajā rogā jāyante bhṛśadāruṇāḥ
children.translated_text: These <s>vāta</s>-born diseases arise, exceedingly terrible.
This is the supreme complication of <s>durnāma</s> (piles), death, and <s>udāvarta</s> (upward movement of wind).
In those whose abdomen is overpowered by <s>vāta</s>, it arises even without those piles.

children.text: sahajāni tu doṣāṇi yāni cābhyantare valau ||
children.translated_text: But the congenital defects, and those situated inside in the fold,
are incurable; they are only palliated according to digestive fire, strength, and the like.
Those produced by pairs of <s>doṣas</s>, and those lodged in the second fold,
are said to be difficult to cure, as are those that have lasted a full year.
But those born in the external fold and predominated by a single <s>doṣa</s>,
and piles that have not arisen long before, are easy to cure.
Those at the penis and other places, and those arising at the navel, will be described each according to its own nature.
The forms of <s>gaṇḍūpada</s> are slimy and soft.
<s>Vyāna</s>, taking up phlegm, makes piles outside the skin.
They know that skin tag to be stable, rough, and peg-like.
From <s>vāta</s> there is pricking pain and roughness; from <s>pitta</s>, blackness of its mouth.
From <s>śleṣman</s> come its unctuousness, knottedness, and similarity of color.
A wise person should quickly make an effort to pacify piles,
for they quickly, once hardened into disease, produce an abdomen with the anus obstructed.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe 'rśonidānā nāma ṣaṭpañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> <s>Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the earlier part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and fifty-sixth chapter, named 'Diagnosis of Piles,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall tell the diagnosis of diarrhea and <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder, O <s>Suśruta</s>.
Through the <s>doṣas</s>, separately and collectively, and from fear and from grief, it is sixfold.
That <s>atīsāra</s> (diarrhea) arises especially from drinking too much water,
from dried food, fat, unctuous substances, sesame paste, and sprouted grains,
from wine, dry food, excessive quantities and the like, from unsuitable tastes, excessive unctuousness, and deranged regimen,
and from worms and incompatibility. Aggravated wind, arising from such causes,
dislodges the downward wind and thereby destroys the digestive fire.
Acting upon food and feces in the bowel, it produces such conditions as fluidity of stool.
The sign of diarrhea that is about to arise is then established:
cutting pain in the heart, anus, and abdomen, sweating of the limbs, retention of feces,
distension and indigestion. In that condition, when caused by <s>vāta</s> and without fever,
one passes stool in small amounts again and again, accompanied by noise and pain.

children.text: rūkṣaṃ saphenamacchaṃ ca gṛhītaṃ va muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: It is dry, foamy, clear, and passed repeatedly in a held-back manner.
Likewise it has a burnt-looking appearance, is slimy, and cuts as it passes.
The anus is dry and prolapsed; the patient has horripilation and sighs deeply.
When caused by <s>pitta</s>, what is passed is yellow, dark yellow, turmeric-colored, or like green grass,
mixed with blood and extremely foul-smelling; the patient has thirst, fainting, sweat, and burning.
There is pain in the anus, heat, and suppurative distress. When caused by <s>śleṣman</s>, it is thick,
slimy, accompanied by a following discharge there, scanty, and attended by straining.
There is horripilation, distress, and heaviness in the bladder, anus, and abdomen;
even after evacuation there is a sense of incomplete discharge. The type involving all has all the symptoms.

children.text: bhayena kṣubhite citte śāyite drāvayet sakṛt ||
children.translated_text: When the mind is disturbed by fear, wind liquefies the feces,
and then quickly drives out stool that is warm, liquid, and floating.
In the combined <s>vāta</s>-<s>pitta</s> type the signs are mixed; the same is said for diarrhea from grief.
In brief, <s>atīsāra</s> is twofold: with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter) and without <s>āma</s>.
The stool with <s>āma</s>, born of deranged fluid essence and blood, sinks in water because of heaviness.
The feces are foul-smelling, with gurgling, obstruction, pain, and salivation.
The <s>nirāma</s> type is the opposite; in some phlegmatic cases it does not sink.
Among cases of diarrhea, if one is not very diligent, <s>grahaṇī</s> disease
may arise for him, when the digestive fire is extinguished by extremely accumulated effects.
That by which one repeatedly passes stool, whether with <s>āma</s> or without <s>āma</s>, digested or undigested,
is <s>atīsāra</s>; from excessive flowing, it is by nature quick in its action.

children.text: sāmaṃ śīrṇam ajīrṇena jīrṇe pakvaṃ tu naiva ca ||
children.translated_text: When mixed with <s>āma</s> (undigested matter), it is broken down by indigestion; when digestion has taken place it is cooked, but otherwise not.
A long-standing disorder of the <s>grahaṇī</s> causes accumulations and bouts of evacuation.

children.text: akasmād vārasur vedham akasmāt sandhinī muhuḥ
children.translated_text: There may suddenly be piercing pain, and again and again sudden contraction in the joints.
It arises in four forms, from the separate <s>doṣas</s> and from their combined aggravation.
Its preliminary signs are weakness of the limbs, delay, scant movement of wind,
salivation, bad taste in the mouth, loss of appetite, thirst, fatigue, and dizziness.
There is binding of the abdomen, vomiting, and even a ringing sound in the ears.
The common signs are emaciation, vomiting, difficult breathing, fever,
fainting, stiffness and pain of the head, and swelling of the hands and feet.
From wind there are drowsiness, dryness of the palate, dimness of sight, and ringing in the ears.
There is pain in the sides, thighs, groin, and neck, and sharp <s>viṣūcikā</s> (griping colic).
In the afflicted parts all pains increase, and hunger and thirst are not relieved.

children.text: jīrṇe jīryati cādhmānaṃ bhukte svāsthyaṃ samaśnute
children.translated_text: When food is digested there is still distension; after eating he for a time feels well.
From <s>vāta</s>, there is fear of heart disease, abdominal tumor, piles, enlargement of the spleen, and pallor.
After a long time, with pain, he repeatedly passes stool that is liquid, dryish, thin, noisy, and foamy.
Again and again he discharges feces, with distress of the anus, upward breath, and cough.
With <s>pitta</s>, he passes liquid that is yellow, yellow-blue, or yellowish in appearance.
He is afflicted by fetid sour belching, burning in the heart and throat, loss of appetite, and thirst.
With <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), digestion is painful, and there is nausea of the mind, vomiting, and aversion to food.
There are burning in the mouth, spitting, cough, nausea, and nasal catarrh.
He feels that the heart is stiff, and that the abdomen is motionless and heavy.
The belching is foul and sweet; there is prostration accompanied by horripilation.
The stool proceeds mixed and clinging with phlegm, heavy, and accompanied by sourness.
Even in one who is not emaciated there is weakness; when all <s>doṣas</s> are involved, all the signs appear.
Those three impurities, beginning with thirst, that were taught in the division of the body,
are also causes of this <s>grahaṇī</s> disorder when they are equally present.
Disorders of <s>vāta</s>, urinary stone, skin disease, urinary disease, abdominal disease, and fistula,
together with piles and <s>grahaṇī</s>, are the eight great diseases, very hard to overcome.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe 'tisāranidānaṃ nāma saptapañcāśaduttaraśatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and fifty-seventh chapter, named 'Diagnosis of Diarrhea,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
Now then, listen, <s>Suśruta</s>, to the diagnosis of urinary obstruction.
The bladder, the head of the bladder, the penis, the waist, the testicles, and the anus
are said to have one connected channel, resting in the cavity of the rectal bone.
Although the bladder faces downward, through the mouths of the urine-bearing vessels
it is continually filled from the sides by smooth, flowing streams.
Entering by those very vessels, the <s>doṣas</s> produce twenty disorders.
Urinary obstruction, <s>prameha</s> (urinary disease), and dysuria take hold of this vital place.
In the <s>vāta</s>-born form, with pain in the bladder, groin, and penis, he passes urine little by little, again and again.
The urinary acts are difficult; in the <s>pitta</s> form the urine is yellow and always accompanied by burning pain.
Or it may be bloody; the <s>kapha</s>-born form has heaviness and swelling of the bladder and penis.

children.text: sapicchaṃ saniruddhaṃ ca sarvaiḥ sarvātmakaṃ malaiḥ
children.translated_text: It is slimy and obstructed; when all the impurities are involved, it has the nature of all of them.
When <s>vāyu</s>, turning back the mouth of the bladder and drying it up,

children.text: mūtraṃ sapittaṃ sakaphaṃ saśukraṃ vā tadā kramāt
children.translated_text: acts on urine mixed respectively with <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, or semen,
then a terrible stone arises; the <s>pitta</s>-stone is like the yellow pigment from a cow.
All stones have <s>śleṣman</s> as their support. Now its preliminary signs are these:
distension of the bladder and intense pain all around the region near it,
retention of urine in the bladder, difficult urination, fever, and loss of appetite.
The common mark is pain in the navel, the perineal raphe, and the head of the bladder.
The urine is spread out in its course when there is obstruction of the passage.
Having been checked and held back, he urinates with relief, clear and like a <s>gomedaka</s> gem.
When it is disturbed, it becomes mixed with blood, and pain occurs along the fleshy passage.
There, afflicted by the incursion of <s>vāta</s>, the sufferer grinds his teeth and trembles.
He grasps the penis and the navel, and presses them with excessive distress.
He passes feces with wind and urinates frequently, drop by drop.
His stone is dark and rough, and appears studded as if with thorns.
Through <s>pitta</s>, the bladder burns, hot as though it were being cooked.
The stone has the form of a <s>bhallātaka</s> seed, and is red, yellow, or pale.
Through <s>śleṣman</s>, the bladder feels as if it is being pricked; it is cold and heavy.

children.text: aśmarī mahatī ślakṣṇā madhuvarṇātha vā sitā
children.translated_text: The stone is large and smooth, honey-colored or else white.

children.text: etā bhavanti bālānāṃ teṣāmeva ca bhūyasām ||
children.translated_text: These occur in children, and especially among them in greater number.
Because the bodily receptacle and the growth are small, grasping and removing them is easy.
But a seminal stone becomes large and arises from retention of semen.
When semen is displaced or not discharged, <s>anila</s> (wind), between the testicles,
dries it up by compressing it; that semen becomes a semen-stone.
It causes bladder pain and difficult urination; it is white and produces swelling.
When it has just arisen, it comes away dry and dissolves.
When pressed, with fever and cough in this condition, the stone becomes like gravel.

children.text: asau vā vāyunā bhinnā sā tvasmin anulomage ||
children.translated_text: Or, broken apart by <s>vāyu</s>, when the wind moves in its proper downward direction,
it goes out together with the urine; when the movement is reversed, it suppurates.
When one holds back urine, <s>marut</s> (wind), angered at the mouth of the bladder, causes
retention of urine, pain, itching, and sometimes severe disorder.
Covering the bladder and drawing it upward, it makes the inner region swollen and distended.
There it produces pain, burning, throbbing, and twisting sensations.

children.text: binduśaśca pravarteta mūtraṃ bastau tu pīḍite ||
children.translated_text: When the bladder is pressed, urine proceeds drop by drop.
There is also obstruction of the stream; this is remembered as <s>vātabasti</s>.
It is hard to overcome; the second form is still harder when <s>anila</s> (wind) is strong.
The <s>vāyu</s> (wind) that has taken refuge in the interval between the fecal passage and the bladder
forms a dense knot shaped like an <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>, immovable and raised up.
This is called <s>vātāṣṭhīlā</s>; by its nature it obstructs the passage of feces, urine, and wind.
When <s>anila</s> (wind), becoming disordered and coiled up in the bladder, is intensely painful,
it obstructs the urine and moves about, with rigidity, twisting pain, and heaviness.
Then one passes urine only little by little, or again and again at intervals.
This is precisely called <s>vātakuṇḍalikā</s>. But when urine has been retained for a time

children.text: na nireti niruddhaṃ vā mūtrātītaṃ tadalparuk ||
children.translated_text: and does not come out, or is stopped, that is <s>mūtrātīta</s>, with little pain.
When, because of suppression, urine is checked and turned back by <s>vāta</s>,
then the urine fills the abdomen below the navel.
It causes severe pain, distension, weakness, and retention of feces.
That urine, because of a defect in the abdominal opening or because of <s>anila</s> (wind),

children.text: ākṣiptamalpamūtrasya vastau nābhau ca vā male
children.translated_text: is driven in a person who passes little urine, and after staying in the bladder, at the navel, or in the fecal matter,
it should flow slowly afterward, either with pain or without pain.
That interrupted discharge of urine is better in those whose penis is heavy.
When thirst occurs suddenly at the inner mouth of the bladder, firm and slight,
and there is a knot with pain like a urinary stone, that is called <s>mūtragranthi</s>.
When, after a man has passed urine and gone to a woman, semen is raised up by <s>vāyu</s>,
displaced from its place, it comes forth before or after he urinates.
Resembling water mixed with ash, that is called <s>mūtraśukra</s>.
When, in a dry and weak person, feces are carried upward by <s>vāta</s>,
and move along the urinary channel, then the urine is mixed with feces.
A drop of urine having the same smell occurs; that obstruction should be designated as such.
Through <s>pitta</s>, exertion, sharp, sour food, distension, and the like,
and through aggravated <s>vāyu</s>, when urine remains in the bladder and causes burning,

children.text: mūtraṃ vartayate pūrvaṃ saraktaṃ raktameva vā ||
children.translated_text: it first turns the urine blood-tinged, or else entirely blood.

children.text: uṣṇaṃ punaḥ punaḥ kṛcchrāduṣṇavātaṃ vadanti tam
children.translated_text: It is hot again and again, and passed with difficulty; this they call <s>uṣṇavāta</s>.
In one who is dry and whose body is exhausted, <s>pitta</s> and <s>māruta</s> lodged in the bladder
produce <s>mūtrakṣaya</s>, a wasting of urine, with pain and burning; it is known by that name.

children.text: pittaṃ kapho dvāvapi vā saṃhanyete 'nilena cet ||
children.translated_text: If <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, or both together are compacted by <s>anila</s>,

children.text: kṛcchrānmūtraṃ tadā pītaṃ raktaṃ śvetaṃ ghanaṃ sṛjet
children.translated_text: then with difficulty one emits urine that is yellow, red, white, and thick.
It is accompanied by burning and may have the color of powdered yellow pigment or conch shell.

children.text: śuṣkaṃ samastavarṇaṃ vā mūtrasādaṃ vadanti tam
children.translated_text: Whether dry or of all colors, they call that <s>mūtrasāda</s>.
Thus the diseases produced in connection with the passage of urine have been explained in detail.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe mūtrāghātamūtrākṛcchanidānaṃ nāmāṣṭapañcāśaduttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the first section of the earlier part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and fifty-eighth chapter, named 'Diagnosis of <s>mūtrāghāta</s> and <s>mūtrakṛcchra</s>,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:

children.text: pramehāṇāṃ nidānaṃ te vakṣye 'haṃ śṛṇu suśruta
children.translated_text: I shall tell you the diagnosis of the <s>pramehas</s>; listen, <s>Suśruta</s>.
There are twenty <s>pramehas</s>: among them, ten arise from <s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), six from <s>pitta</s>,
and four from <s>anila</s> (wind); they carry fat, urine, and <s>kapha</s>.
The man with <s>hāridrameha</s> passes excrement that is pungent and resembles turmeric.
In <s>māñjiṣṭhameha</s> it is foul-smelling and like water colored with madder.
In <s>raktameha</s> it is foul-smelling, hot, salty, and blood-colored, or blood itself.
The man with <s>vasāmeha</s> repeatedly urinates fluid mixed with fat or resembling fat.
The man with <s>majjameha</s> repeatedly passes urine like marrow or mixed with marrow.
Like an intoxicated elephant, constantly and without control of the urge,
the man with <s>hastimeha</s> passes urine that is slimy and obstructed.

children.text: madhumehī madhusamaṃ jāyate sa kila dvidhā
children.translated_text: The man with <s>madhumeha</s> has urine like honey; that condition is indeed of two kinds.
When <s>vāyu</s> is enraged through wasting of the bodily elements, or when its path is obstructed by the <s>doṣas</s>,
then, being obstructed, it displays the marks of the <s>doṣas</s> without an obvious cause.
In a moment he is depleted, in a moment filled; the disease assumes a state difficult to cure.
Every case, when neglected over time, indeed comes to the state of <s>madhumeha</s>.

children.text: madhuraṃ yacca meheṣu prāyo madhviva mehati ||
children.translated_text: And whatever among the <s>mehas</s> is sweet, usually passed like honey,
all those are called <s>madhumeha</s>, because of the sweetness of the body.
Indigestion, loss of taste, vomiting, sleepiness, cough, and catarrh
arise as complications of the <s>mehas</s> born from <s>kapha</s>.
Piercing pain in the bladder and penis, tearing pain in the scrotum, fever,
burning, thirst, sour belching, fainting, and looseness of stool occur in those born from <s>pitta</s>.
For those born from <s>vāta</s>, there are upward movement of wind, trembling, seizure of the heart, and restlessness,

children.text: śūlam unnidratā śoṣaḥ śvāsaḥ kāsaṃ ca jāyate
children.translated_text: and there arise colic, sleeplessness, wasting, dyspnea, and cough.
<s>Śarāvikā</s>, <s>kacchapikā</s>, <s>jvālinī</s>, <s>vinatā</s>, and <s>alajī</s>,
<s>masūrikā</s>, <s>sarṣapikā</s>, <s>putriṇī</s>, and <s>vidārikā</s>,
and <s>vidradhi</s>: these are the ten eruptions caused by neglected <s>prameha</s>.
There, their arising is generally from food being bound together with <s>kapha</s>.
Food that is sweet, sour, salty, unctuous, heavy, slimy, and cold,
new grain, liquor, soup, meat, sugarcane products, molasses, and milk-products,
and also sitting in one place, lying down, and abstaining from movement:
<s>kapha</s>, corrupted by these because of <s>prameha</s>, takes refuge in the bladder.
After corrupting bodily moisture, sweat, fat, grease, and flesh in the body,
and then, when <s>kapha</s> and the rest are greatly depleted, <s>pitta</s> and blood, taking refuge in the urine,
carry the bodily element to the bladder; and when that is depleted, <s>māruta</s> does so as well.
Therefore the <s>mehas</s> born from it are known by whether they are curable, incurable, and so on.
When the <s>doṣas</s> are equal, the case is equally produced; nevertheless, because of predominance,
their general sign is abundant and turbid urine.
Although there are distinctions in the <s>doṣas</s> and in the things corrupted, because of the particular combinations of these,
the distinction among the <s>mehas</s> is conceived according to differences in the color of the urine and the like.
Clear, very white, cold, odorless, and resembling water,
With <s>udakameha</s> he urinates something slightly turbid and slimy,
and in <s>ikṣumeha</s> it is exceedingly sweet, like sugarcane juice.
In <s>sāndrameha</s>, what has been passed becomes thick when it has stood for a while; he urinates thick urine.
A <s>surāmehin</s> has urine like liquor, clear above and dense below.
With hairs standing on end, in <s>piṣṭameha</s> he passes copious white urine, as if mixed with flour.
A <s>śukramehin</s> passes urine that resembles semen or is mixed with semen.
A <s>sikatāmehin</s> urinates impurities shaped like grains of sand.
A <s>śītamehin</s> very frequently passes urine that is sweet and extremely cold.

children.text: śanaiḥ śanaiḥ śanairmehī mandaṃ mandaṃ pramehati
children.translated_text: A <s>śanairmehin</s> urinates very slowly, little by little.
In <s>lālāmeha</s>, the urine is slimy and furnished with saliva-like threads.
By smell, color, taste, and touch, in <s>kṣārameha</s> it is alkaline, like alkaline water.
In <s>nīlameha</s> it is bluish; a <s>kālamehin</s> passes urine like ink.
In the joints and vital points, and in fleshy bodily sites,
there arise eruptions raised at the edges, depressed in the middle, without moisture, and attended by severe pain.
An eruption shaped like a saucer is called <s>śarāvikā</s>.
One that burns and is shaped like a tortoise should be known by the wise as <s>kacchapikā</s>.

children.text: mahatī piḍikā nīlā vinatā nāma sā smṛtā
children.translated_text: A large blue eruption is remembered as <s>vinatā</s>.
<s>Jvālinī</s>, painful and distressing, burns the skin as it rises up.

children.text: raktā sitā sphoṭacitā dāruṇā tvalajī bhavet
children.translated_text: <s>Alajī</s> is red or white, covered with blisters, and terrible.
One shaped like a lentil should be recognized as <s>masūrikā</s>.
An eruption comparable in form to a mustard seed, with suppuration and great pain in the tongue,

children.text: putriṇī mahatī cālpā susūkṣmā piḍikā smṛtā ||
children.translated_text: is remembered as <s>putriṇī</s>, whether large, small, or very minute.
One round like a <s>vidārī</s> tuber and hard is <s>vidārikā</s>.
When furnished with the marks of an abscess, it should be known as <s>vidradhikā</s>.

children.text: putriṇī ca vidārī ca duḥsahā bahumedasaḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Putriṇī</s> and <s>vidārī</s> are unbearable in persons with abundant fat,
while the others, dominated by <s>pitta</s>, arise immediately in persons with little fat.
Those eruptions occur according to the respective excess of the <s>doṣas</s>.
They arise even without <s>prameha</s> in persons whose fat is vitiated.

children.text: tāvacca nopalakṣyante yāvad varṇaṃ ca varjitam
children.translated_text: They are not recognized as such so long as the normal coloration has not been abandoned.
If one urinates fluid that is turmeric-yellow or blood-colored and lacks the prodromal signs of <s>meha</s>,

children.text: yo mūtrayeta tan mehaṃ raktapittaṃ tu tadviduḥ
children.translated_text: the experts know that condition as <s>raktapitta</s>, not that <s>meha</s>.
Sweating, bodily odor, looseness in the limbs, attachment to the pleasures of bed, seat, and sleep,
burning in the heart, eyes, tongue, and ears, heaviness and severity, and growth of the hair and nails,
liking for cold things, dryness of the throat and palate, sweetness in the mouth, and burning of the hands and feet:

children.text: bhaviṣyato mehagaṇasya rūpaṃ mūtre 'pi dhāvanti pipīlikāśca ||
children.translated_text: these are the signs of a future group of <s>mehas</s>; ants also run over the urine.

children.text: tṛṣṇā pramehe madhuraṃ prapicchaṃ madhvāmaye syād vividho vikāraḥ
children.translated_text: In <s>prameha</s> there is thirst; in <s>madhvāmaya</s> the urine is sweet and very slimy, and many kinds of disorder may occur.
From overfilling it is produced by <s>kapha</s>, or, when the <s>doṣas</s> are depleted, it is of the nature of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: sampūrṇarūpāḥ kaphapittamehāḥ krameṇa ye vai ratisambhavāśca
children.translated_text: <s>Kapha</s>- and <s>pitta</s>-born <s>mehas</s> may have full signs, as may those that arise successively and those born from sexual indulgence.

children.text: sakrāmate pittakṛtāstu yāpyāḥ sādhyo 'sti meho yadi nāsti diṣṭam ||
children.translated_text: Those produced by <s>pitta</s> are manageable; <s>meha</s> is curable if adverse fate is not present.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe pramehanidānaṃ nāmaikonaṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> <s>Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the earlier part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and fifty-ninth chapter, named 'Diagnosis of <s>Prameha</s>,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall explain the diagnosis of <s>vidradhi</s> and <s>gulma</s>; listen, O <s>Suśruta</s>.
From eating stale, excessively hot, dry, rough, and burning foods,
from crooked lying and improper movements, and from various factors that vitiate the blood,
there arises a swelling lodged in corrupted skin, flesh, fat, bone, marrow, and the abdomen.
When that swelling is external or internal and has great colic and severe pain,

children.text: vṛttaḥ syādāyato yo vā smṛto rogaḥ sa vidradhiḥ ||
children.translated_text: whether round or elongated, that disease is remembered as <s>vidradhi</s>.
It is caused by the <s>doṣas</s>, separately or combined, and also by blood and injury.
In various parts of the body it becomes dreadful, knotted, and not yet discharging.
The internal form is dreadful, deep, and increases a <s>gulma</s>-like mass,
and it discharges like an anthill; weakness of digestive fire also arises.
Its sites are the navel, bladder, liver, spleen, <s>kloma</s>, heart, belly, and groin.
When the heart is affected there is trembling, and in each site there is extremely intense pain.
The <s>vāta</s>-born type is dark or reddish, with a raised head and suppuration, and is irregular in form;
it has loss of consciousness, dizziness, distension, oozing, creeping pain, and sound.
From <s>pitta</s> it is red, coppery, or black, and has thirst, delusion, fever, and burning.
From <s>kapha</s> it arises and ripens slowly, is pale, and is accompanied by itching.
Distress, chill, stiffness, yawning, anorexia, and heaviness occur,
and it is slow to arise, with indigestion; when mixed, it is produced by all the <s>doṣas</s> together.
By its force one should here distinguish the signs of the external and internal varieties.
The external blood-born type is dark, covered with black blisters, and has intense burning, pain, and fever;
it bears the marks of <s>pitta</s> together with blood, and the internal form is stated especially for women.
Blood arising from blows by weapons and the like is also a cause of the disease.

children.text: kṣatottho vāyunā kṣiptaḥ sa raktaḥ pittamīrayan
children.translated_text: A wound-born form, driven by <s>vāyu</s>, takes up blood and impels <s>pitta</s>.
It produces a <s>vidradhi</s> with the signs of <s>pitta</s> and blood, attended by many complications.
The division of its complications is remembered according to the difference of its site.

children.text: nābhau hi dhmātaṃ cedbastau mūtrakṛcchraṃ ca jāyate ||
children.translated_text: When it is in the navel there is distension; in the bladder, painful urination arises.
There is obstruction of inhalation and exhalation, and in the spleen extreme thirst above all.
In the <s>kloma</s> there is obstruction of the throat, and in the heart pain throughout the body.
There are stupor, asthmatic oppression, cough, and pounding of the heart.
In the region between the belly and flanks, and in the belly itself, there is production of the <s>doṣas</s>.
So too, if it is in the thigh-joint, groin, waist, or back,
there is pain in the flanks; in the anus there is obstruction of wind.
Their unripe, ripe, and over-cooked states should be described as in the case of swellings.
Some, when suppurated, run out upward from the navel and mouth; others run out from the anus.
One should recognize an abscess arising in the anus, breast, or navel when there is an elevated <s>vidradhi</s> from the moistening of the <s>doṣas</s>.
The condition born from the combined <s>doṣas</s> causes a distortion of its own seat, the <s>svādhiṣṭhāna</s> region.
When a suppurated swelling is situated at the navel or bladder and has burst, whether inwardly or outwardly,
there is internal suppuration of one that has grown, while the wasted person is afflicted by complications.
There, too, a <s>vidradhi</s> (abscess) may arise in sinful men and sinful women,

children.text: mṛte tu garbhage caiva sambhavecchvayathur ghanaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and when the fetus has died in the womb, a dense swelling may occur.
Pain in a well-formed breast, or the signs of an external <s>vidradhi</s>, may be present.

children.text: nārīṇāṃ sūkṣmaraktatvāt kanyāyāṃ tu na jāyate ||
children.translated_text: Because women have subtle blood vessels, it does not arise in a maiden.
When <s>vāyu</s>, angered or having its course obstructed, acts at the root of the penis,
and reaches from the testicles and groins into the excessive channels of the scrotum,
it presses upon the vessels and produces enlargement in the two scrotal sacs.

children.text: doṣo medaḥsu tatrāste savṛddhiḥ saptadhā gadaḥ ||
children.translated_text: The <s>doṣa</s> remains there in the fat; with enlargement, the disease is of seven kinds.

children.text: mūtraṃ tayor apyanilād bāhye vābhyantare tathā
children.translated_text: Urine also, through <s>anila</s>, enters into them, either externally or internally.
When filled with <s>vāta</s>, it is rough to the touch, dry, and, from <s>vāta</s>, produces burning pain.
From <s>pitta</s> it resembles a ripe udumbara fruit, with burning, heat, and suppuration.
From <s>kapha</s> it is intense, heavy, unctuous, itchy, hard, and only slightly painful.
From blood, the lump is black, covered with eruptions, and has the marks of enlargement.
Enlargement from fat is like that from <s>kapha</s>; it is soft and resembles a palm fruit.
In a person accustomed to holding back urine, the urinary type arises there as the urine proceeds into them.
It is not deficient, is full and held fast; moving gently, it becomes disturbed.
There is difficulty in urination, and below there is a ring-like swelling of the scrotal sacs.
Through foods that aggravate <s>vāta</s> and through immersion in cold water,
and also through holding back feces and urine and through irregular movements of the limbs,
when the vital force has been agitated in bodies that are depleted within,
the wind, having become deranged, carries the blood downward.
Then, lodged at that very joint, it produces a swelling resembling a knot.
If it is neglected, it grows like a <s>gulma</s>, with distension, pain, and many diseases.

children.text: supīḍito 'ntaḥ svanavān prayāti pradhmāpayanneti punaśca mūrdhni ||
children.translated_text: When strongly pressed inside, making a sound, it goes forth; inflating again, it moves upward to the head.
This blood-enlargement is incurable and has the form of a <s>vāta</s>-enlargement.
It has dry, black, reddish veins, like a window covered with wool.
<s>Vāta</s>, in eight forms, joined with the separate <s>doṣas</s> and accumulated,
and, in women, with disorder of the menstrual fluid, produces the eighth kind.
A strong man, exhausted by fever, fainting, diarrhea, and procedures such as vomiting,
and also afflicted by cold and hunger, falls into this state.
He who drinks foods and drinks, and practices fasting, swimming, and the like,
while afflicted and impelled by conditions marked by deficient awareness,
or who, without first using unction and sweating, resorts to drying treatment,

children.text: śuddho vā śuddhihānirvā bhajeta spandanāni vā ||
children.translated_text: or who has been purified, or in whom purification has failed, or who engages in strain,
in him the wastes, dominated by <s>vāta</s>, either separately or together,
or all of them joined with blood, follow the bodily channels because of <s>vāta</s>.
Obstructing the upward and downward passages, <s>vāyu</s> produces colic pain.
It is perceptible to touch, arising as <s>gulma</s>, hot, and knot-like in form.
Through emaciation, obstruction by <s>kapha</s> and feces, or blockage of the passage,
<s>vāyu</s>, having made its seat in the abdomen, becomes hard because of dryness.
It is independent when corrupted in its own seat, and dependent when in another's seat.
Then <s>śleṣman</s>, like a compact lump, becomes mixed with the waste matter.
This is called <s>gulma</s>, having its seat in the bladder, navel, heart, or sides.
In one born from <s>vāta</s>, there are headache, fever, spleen disorder, and rumbling of the intestines.

children.text: vedhaḥ sūcyeva viḍbhraṃśaḥ kṛcchre mūtraṃ pravartate
children.translated_text: There is piercing as if with a needle, displacement of feces, and urine proceeds with difficulty.

children.text: gātre mukhe pade śothaḥ hyagnimāndyaṃ tathaiva ca ||
children.translated_text: Swelling occurs in the limbs, face, and feet, and there is also weakness of the digestive fire.
Dryness and blackness of the skin and other parts occur; because <s>anila</s> is mobile,
its shape is not fixed, and it produces various pains.
The <s>gulma</s> throbs and is driven about, as if pervaded by ants.
From <s>pitta</s> there are burning, sour belching, fainting, looseness of stool, sweating, thirst, and fever.
A yellow color appears over all the limbs, and swelling is seen from the <s>gulma</s>.
<s>Śleṣman</s> diminishes and flares up, and seems to burn its own seat.
From <s>kapha</s> there are torpor, loss of appetite, lassitude, and fever in the head.
There are catarrh, laziness, nausea, and whiteness or blackness of the skin and other parts.
The <s>gulma</s> is deep, hard, and heavy, like a child in the womb.
Remaining in their own places and not running forth, they are therefore fatal here.
For the most part, those <s>gulmas</s> that arise from two <s>doṣas</s> are produced through mixed conjunctions.
The one born from all <s>doṣas</s> has intense pain and burning, suppurates quickly, and is dense and raised.
That is incurable; but <s>raktagulma</s>, the blood <s>gulma</s>, arises only in a woman.

children.text: ṛtau yā caiva śūlārtā yati vā yonirogiṇī ||
children.translated_text: It occurs in one who is afflicted with pain at her season, or in a woman suffering from disease of the womb or vagina.
Or if a woman indulges in things that increase <s>anila</s>, her <s>samīraṇa</s> becomes angered.
It obstructs the menstrual blood regularly established in the womb each month.
It dries it up in the womb and makes the sign appear there.
There are nausea, pregnancy-longing, appearance of milk in the breasts, and acting according to desire.
Gradually, through conjunction with <s>vāyu</s>, <s>pitta</s> accumulates in the female organs.
It produces an accumulation of her blood, giving rise to the <s>gulma</s> symptoms described for <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
In the uterus especially, and in the seat of blood, there are pains.
There is vaginal discharge, foul odor, and again flowing and pain.
Sometimes the <s>gulma</s> is like a pregnancy; all these arise from sexual intercourse.

children.text: pākaṃ cireṇa bhajate naidhate vidradhiḥ punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: It undergoes suppuration after a long time, and then the <s>vidradhi</s> grows again.
That abscess, resting in corrupted blood, ripens exceedingly quickly.
Therefore, because it burns and suppurates quickly, it is called <s>vidradhi</s>.
When it has an internal seat in a <s>gulma</s>, there is burning in the bladder and pain in the spleen.
There is loss of digestive fire, complexion, and strength, or abnormal activation of the urges.
In the opposite case, when it is in the outer belly and limbs, the pain is not very great.
There is discoloration, or else cough, and a more pronounced outward swelling.
A very great swelling in the abdomen, with rumbling and extremely severe pain,
caused by obstruction of <s>vāta</s> upward and downward, is called <s>ānāha</s>.
A hard, stone-like, knotty mass, raised up like a stone, is <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>.
When it is joined with all the signs and has that same shape, it is <s>pratyaṣṭhīlā</s>.
In the same way, even wind arising from the colon, because it is lodged with intense pain,
has as signs abundant belching, constipation, inability to be satisfied, and rumbling of the intestines.

children.text: ācopam ādhmānam apaktiśaktiḥ āsannagulmasya bhavecca cihnam ||
children.translated_text: Rumbling, distension, and weakness of digestion should be signs of an approaching <s>gulma</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vidradhigulmanidānaṃ nāma ṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixtieth chapter, named 'Diagnosis of <s>vidradhi</s> and <s>gulma</s>,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:

children.text: udarāṇāṃ nidānaṃ ca vakṣye suśruta tacchṛṇu
children.translated_text: I shall explain the causes of the abdominal diseases; listen to that, <s>Suśruta</s>.
All diseases arise when the digestive fire is weak, but abdominal diseases do so especially.
Other disorders of indigestion also arise from an accumulation of waste products.
Having obstructed the upward and downward winds, and made their courses disturbed and irregular,
they corrupt <s>prāṇa</s> and <s>apāna</s> and cause those diseases to lodge in the flesh and joints.
After inflating the belly, they produce <s>udara</s>; and, by division, it is of eight kinds.
They arise from the individual <s>doṣas</s>, from all of them combined, and from conditions involving the spleen, obstruction or injury, and water.
Those afflicted by them have dry palates and lips, and swelling in the feet, hands, and abdomen.
Their activity, strength, and appetite are lost, and their bellies are made distended.
Men become corpse-like; these are the signs of its impending development.
Loss of hunger and lack of taste occur, and all food is digested with burning.

children.text: jīrṇānnaṃ yo na jānāti so 'pathyaṃ sevate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: The man who does not know when his eaten food has been digested resorts to unwholesome things.
The strength of the body wastes away; he breathes only slightly and is inactive.
The mind turns away from its objects, and grief, wasting, and the like also arise.
There is constant pain in the region of the bladder and joints, even from light and scanty meals.
Old age, indigestion, and loss of strength occur in a man suffering from abdominal disease.
Lassitude, drowsiness, languor, discharge of waste, and weakness of digestive fire occur independently.
Burning, swelling, and distension occur in the bowels when the condition is produced by water.

children.text: sarvatra toye maraṇaṃ śocanaṃ tatra niṣphalam
children.translated_text: When water is everywhere, death follows; lamentation there is useless.
The belly gurgles with networks of veins like latticed windows.
After the region of the navel and bowels has become obstructed, the urge arises and then disappears.
In the type caused by <s>māruta</s>, there are pains in the heart, waist, navel, anus, and groin.
Wind comes out with sound, and urine is passed only in small amount.
A man does not have excessive craving, and his mouth has an unpleasant taste.
In that <s>vātodara</s> there is swelling in the hands, feet, face, and belly.
There is pain in the belly, flanks, abdomen, waist, and back, and splitting pain in the joints.
There are dry cough, aching of the limbs, heaviness below, and retention of stool.
The skin and other parts are dusky-red, and the taste in the mouth is impaired.
The abdomen has pricking and splitting pain and is spread over with blue-black veins.
When distended, it makes a strange sound in the abdomen.
