Here <s>vāyu</s>, with pain and noise, moves in every possible way.
In <s>pittodara</s> there are fever, fainting, burning, and a pungent taste in the mouth.
There are dizziness, diarrhea, yellowness of the skin and other parts, and the abdomen is greenish.
The veins and other parts are yellow and coppery; with sweat and heat, the body burns.
It seems to smoke, is soft to the touch, ripens quickly, and is painful.
In the <s>śleṣmodara</s> types there are collapse, sweat, swelling, and heaviness.
There are sleep, distress, loss of taste, dyspnea, cough, and whiteness of the skin and other parts.
The abdomen is dark, unctuous, and covered with white and black veins.
When the fluid has greatly increased, it is hard, cold to the touch, heavy, and fixed.
When all three <s>doṣas</s> are provoked by various corrupting wastes,
and the accumulated wastes are vitiated in every way and mixed with blood,
then, reaching the abdominal cavity and becoming transformed, they produce a condition accompanied by wasting, fainting, and dizziness.
They produce <s>udara</s> with the signs of all three <s>doṣas</s>, quickly ripening and very severe.
And that condition increases greatly when exposed to cold and wind.
It also increases from overeating, from agitation, and from activities such as riding and drinking.
It increases through improper drinks and the like, and through depletion caused by vomiting or disease.
The spleen, situated on the left side, becomes displaced from its place and enlarges.
Growing from blood or from chyle and the other bodily elements, it gives rise to pain.
It is like an <s>aṣṭhīlā</s>, very hard, raised up like the back of a tortoise.
Increasing gradually, it produces expansion in the belly.
It is accompanied by dyspnea, cough, thirst, bad taste in the mouth, distension, and fever,
as well as pallor, fainting, vomiting, burning of the skin, and delusion.
It is reddish, variegated in color, and marked with blue and yellow discoloration.
With upward movement of wind, obstruction, stupor, thirst, and deep fever,
with heaviness, loss of taste, hardness, impediment, dizziness, and displacement,
the liver too, displaced from the right side, produces a condition like that of the spleen.

children.text: pakve bhūte yakṛti ca sadā baddhamalo gude
children.translated_text: When the liver has become suppurated, and feces are always obstructed in the rectum,
one may be afflicted by piles, by upward-moving wind, or by other disorders.
Enraged <s>anila</s> causes feces, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> to be bound up.
Because of that, <s>apāna</s>, obstructed in the abdomen, produces fever and pain.
It causes cough, dyspnea, weakness of the thighs, headache, and pain in the navel and flanks.
There is contact with impurity, loss of taste, vomiting, and fecal wind in the abdomen.
The abdomen is covered with a network of firm, blue and red vessels,
and above the navel it usually takes on the shape of a cow's tail.
Likewise, when the abdomen has been pierced by bones and other foreign bodies,
the liver and the rest are digested, and through those openings they flow outside.
Undigested matter itself burns in the rectum; then the fluid of the feces comes little by little.
It may have an altered smell, and is slimy, yellow, and red.
Then the remainder, filling the belly, begins a terrible condition.
It grows below the navel and quickly assumes the nature of water.

children.text: udrikte doṣarūpe ca vyāpte ca śvāsatṛḍbhramaiḥ
children.translated_text: When the form of the <s>doṣas</s> is aggravated and has spread, with dyspnea, thirst, and dizziness,
they call this <s>chidrodara</s>, 'perforated abdomen'; others call it <s>parisrāvin</s>, 'the oozing one.'
In a person who, after beginning the drinking of oil and the like, suddenly follows an unwholesome regimen,
or in one of weak digestive fire from drinking too much water, or one who is wasted and very emaciated,
<s>anila</s> and <s>kapha</s>, obstructed from their own paths and stupefied by water,
increase that very water, drop by drop, merely from that quantity.
From its aggravation there is an abdominal disorder accompanied by thirst, oozing from the rectum, and pain,
with cough, dyspnea, and loss of taste, and spread over with vessels of many colors.
Because it is filled with water and soft to the touch, it trembles and quivers when shaken,
and the firm, unctuous <s>bakodara</s> arises, enveloping the channels.
When all of these are neglected, the bodily constituents are displaced from their proper places.
Being cooked and liquefied, they would liquefy even the joints and the mouths of the channels.
And when sweat is obstructed, the fluids within become stupefied.
Filling that very abdomen, they produce the abdominal disease.

children.text: gurūdaraṃ sthitaṃ vṛttam āhataṃ ca na śabdakṛt
children.translated_text: The abdomen is heavy, fixed, round, and when struck it makes no sound.

children.text: hīnabalaṃ tathā ghoraṃ nāḍyāṃ spṛṣṭaṃ ca sapati ||
children.translated_text: It is accompanied by loss of strength and is dreadful; when touched at the channels it throbs.
The disappearance of the veins in the abdomen is said to be a general sign.
From <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, the spleen, and their combined disorder comes <s>dakodara</s>.
After a fortnight, water has formed, attended by obstruction and complications.
Every abdominal disease present from birth is generally regarded as the most difficult to cure.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe ekaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixty-first chapter is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:

children.text: pāṇḍuśothanidānaṃ ca śṛṇu suśruta vacmi te
children.translated_text: Listen, <s>Suśruta</s>; I shall tell you the diagnosis of <s>pāṇḍu</s> and swelling.
The wastes, predominantly <s>pitta</s>, become aggravated by the provoking factors already described.
If, there, they are repeatedly driven and impelled by powerful <s>anila</s>,
then, reaching the ten channels, they spread through the whole body.
Corrupting the skin, blood, phlegm, and flesh, and taking refuge in the nutritive fluid,
they produce various colors in the skin and flesh, especially in the skin.

children.text: svayaṃ haridrā hāridraṃ pāṇḍutvaṃ teṣu cādhikam
children.translated_text: Among these, yellowness like turmeric and pallor become especially prominent by themselves.

children.text: yāto 'yaṃ prahated ugraḥ sa rogastena gauravam ||
children.translated_text: When this severe condition has arisen after striking the tissues, that disease is therefore accompanied by heaviness.
There is slackness of touch in the tissues, an undigested condition, and loss of qualities.
Then, with little blood, fat, and bone, the person becomes without essence and has slackened senses.
His limbs seem to be falling apart, and his heart is fluid and weak.
There is pain in the eye-sockets and face, and there is stiffness there with salivation.
He has little thirst, hates cold, has diminished desire, and his digestive fire is impaired.
He has weak power, fever, dyspnea, earache, and dizziness.
It is fivefold: from the separate <s>doṣas</s>, from all of them together, and from eating earth.
Its preliminary signs are palpitation of the heart and dryness of the skin.
There are loss of taste, yellow urine, absence of sweat, and scanty urination.
In that condition, because of fat together with <s>anila</s>, there is intense pain and moistness of the limbs.
There are black eyes and black veins, nails, feces, urine, and eyes.
There is swelling, bad taste in the nose and mouth, drying of the stool, and fainting pain in the side.
In the <s>pitta</s> type, he resembles greenish bile; in the vessels and elsewhere there is fever and darkness.
There are thirst, dryness, fainting, foul smell, desire for cold, and pungency of the mouth.
There are breaking of stool, sourness, and burning; from <s>kapha</s> there is wetness about the heart.
There are drowsiness, a salty taste in the mouth, horripilation, and loss of voice.
Cough and vomiting occur; when there is accumulation, its signs are lost and it is exceedingly hard to bear.
When <s>kapha</s> is overpowered by <s>anila</s> and <s>pitta</s>, it is pungent or sweet.
After corrupting fat and the other tissues, through dryness there is discharge of blood.
It causes diminution of the channels, obstructing them as before.
When wasting has arisen in <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>, from the navel, feet, mouth, and urinary passage
one passes stool like worms, broken, mixed with blood, and accompanied by <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: yaḥ pittarogī seveta pittalaṃ tasya kāmalam
children.translated_text: If a patient with a <s>pitta</s> disease follows a <s>pitta</s>-increasing regimen, he develops <s>kāmala</s>.
The <s>pitta</s>, rising from the bowel into the branches, burns and draws away the blood and flesh.
The urine and eyes are turmeric-yellow, and the face and feces likewise are red.
He has burning, impaired digestion, and thirst; he resembles a frog and his senses are weak.
Swelling accompanied by <s>pitta</s> may occur in one enveloped by <s>pāṇḍuroga</s>.
Through neglect, the swellings and other conditions become difficult and become <s>kumbhakāmala</s>.
When <s>pāṇḍuroga</s> occurs with green and dark <s>pitta</s>,
in <s>vāta-pitta</s> there are dizziness, thirst, excitement toward women, and mild fever.
There may also be drowsiness and loss of digestive fire; they call that <s>halīmaka</s>.
Excessive lassitude is also the earlier complication in those cases.

children.text: śothaḥ pradhānaḥ kathitaḥ sa evāto nigadyate
children.translated_text: Swelling has been declared the principal condition; therefore it is now explained.
Corrupted <s>vāyu</s>, together with <s>pitta</s>, blood, and <s>kapha</s>, carries the corrupted substances outward into the vessels.
Its movement blocked by them, it makes a swelling lodged in the skin and flesh.
Since it is an elevation, compact and accumulated, they therefore call it <s>śotha</s>.
But because of all the particular causes and differences of form, it is of nine kinds.
It arises from all the various <s>doṣas</s> separately, and also from trauma and from poison.
That very condition, when carried through the whole body, becomes a generalized bodily swelling.
They know it as threefold by its specific forms: broad, raised at the tip, and knotted.
The general cause of swellings is, in particular, the class of <s>doṣas</s>.
The disease quickly arises in one weakened by exertion, fasting, and the like.
When one excessively consumes heavy and extremely cold things,
salt, alkali, pungent and sour foods, vegetables, water, sleep, and vigil,
suppression of the urges, dried meat, indigestion, fatigue, and sexual intercourse,
or when food is digested while travelling on a road or even in a jolting vehicle,
dyspnea, cough, diarrhea, piles, abdominal disease, uterine flux, and fevers,
obstruction of stool, lassitude, vomiting, hiccup, pallor, and <s>visarpa</s>,
cause upper swelling above, lower swelling in the bladder region, and middle swelling when lodged in the middle.
When it has gone through all the limbs it is all-pervading; according to its seat it may move outward or inward.
Its prodromal signs are sneezing, tension in the vessels, and heaviness of the limbs.
From <s>vāta</s>, the swelling is mobile, dry, rough-haired, reddish, or dark.
There are pains and swellings in the temples, bladder, and bowels, splitting pain, and numbness.
When <s>vāta</s> is manifest, there is exhaustion; the swelling quickly rises on the pressed body.
Yet, being relieved by unctuous rubbing, it subsides; it is small at night and large by day.
On skin smeared as if with mustard, there is a tingling sensation in that swelling.
The swelling born from <s>pitta</s> has a yellow, red, or dark appearance and causes wasting.

children.text: śīghraṃ nāsau vā praśamen madhye prāgdahate tanum ||
children.translated_text: It does not quickly come to relief; it burns the body first and in the middle.
It is accompanied by thirst, burning, fever, sweat, dizziness, moisture, intoxication, and confusion.
There is craving, looseness of stool, a smell, softness, and inability to bear touch.
Itchy, with pale hair and skin, hard, cold, and heavy,
unctuous, smooth, stable, painful, and causing sleepiness, vomiting, and weakness of digestion: this is from <s>kapha</s>.
By trauma, and by cuts, punctures, wounds, and the like from weapons and other things,
by snow and wind, by curds and wind, and by contact with <s>bhallātaka</s> and <s>kapikacchu</s>,
and by dry juices through contact, a swelling arises, accompanied by <s>visarpa</s>.
It is very hot, reddish in appearance, and generally has the characteristics of <s>pitta</s>.
The poison-born swelling arises from the crawling over or urinating of poisonous creatures,
and from blows by fangs, teeth, and nails, even of creatures that are not poisonous.
It arises from contact with matter tainted by feces, urine, semen, or impure substances,
from the wind or touch of poisonous trees, and from the application or sprinkling of compound poison.
It is soft, mobile, pendulous, swift, and productive of burning and pain.
A new swelling without complications is curable; the incurable kind has been explained before.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe pāṇḍuśothanidānaṃ nāma dviṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixty-second chapter named 'Diagnosis of Pallor and Swelling' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall tell you the diagnosis of <s>visarpa</s> and the rest, <s>Suśruta</s>; listen to it.
<s>Visarpa</s> may arise from injury and from corrupted <s>doṣas</s>, like swelling.

children.text: adhiṣṭhānaṃ ca taṃ prāhurbāhyaṃ tatra bhayācchramāt
children.translated_text: They state its seat as external there, arising from fear and exertion.
In successive order each is harder to cure; there the <s>doṣa</s> is in each case according to its own nature.
The <s>doṣas</s>, provoked by provoking factors, especially by burning substances,

children.text: dehe śīghraṃ viśantīha te 'ntare hi sthitā bahiḥ ||
children.translated_text: swiftly enter the body here; though situated within, they move outward.
Because of affliction by thirst, suppression of urges, and irregular activation,
and because the strength of digestion is quickly lost, <s>visarpa</s> spreads externally.
There, from <s>vāta</s>, that <s>visarpa</s> has pain like a <s>vāta</s> fever.
It has swelling, throbbing, pricking, splitting pain, fatigue, distress, and horripilation.
From <s>pitta</s> it moves quickly, has the signs of a <s>pitta</s> fever, and is very red.
From <s>kapha</s> it is itchy and unctuous, with pain like that of a <s>kapha</s> fever.
Those arising from the combined <s>doṣas</s> are furnished with all the signs.
They increase with the signs of their own <s>doṣas</s>, and, when neglected, with all kinds of blisters.
They too discharge sweat while bearing the marks of wounds.
From <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, it is accompanied by fever, vomiting, fainting, diarrhea, thirst, and dizziness.
It is joined with splitting of nodules, weakness of digestion, darkness before the eyes, and loss of appetite.
It makes every limb appear as if strewn with glowing coals.

children.text: yaṃyaṃ deśaṃ visarpaśca visarpati bhavet sa saḥ ||
children.translated_text: Whatever region <s>visarpa</s> spreads to, that region becomes just so affected.

children.text: śāntāṅgārāsito nīlo rakto vāśu ca cīyate
children.translated_text: It is black like cooled coals, blue, or red, and it quickly accumulates.

children.text: agnidagdha iva sphoṭaiḥ śīghragatvāddrutaṃ sa ca ||
children.translated_text: Like one burnt by fire, it is covered with blisters; because it moves swiftly, it advances rapidly.
A <s>visarpa</s> that follows the vital spots occurs when <s>vāta</s> has become very strong.
It pains the body, takes away consciousness and sleep, and sets dyspnea in motion.

children.text: hikkāṃ ca sa gato 'vasthāmīdṛśīṃ labhate naraḥ
children.translated_text: It also causes hiccup; a man who has reached such a condition
is sometimes seized by pain in the vital spots while trying to move on the ground, bed, seat, and the like.
Then, tormented, he is bewildered in mind and body.
Hard to awaken, he falls into sleep; this is called <s>agni-visarpa</s>.

children.text: kaphena ruddhaḥ pavano bhittvā taṃ bahudhā kapham
children.translated_text: <s>Vāta</s>, obstructed by <s>kapha</s>, breaks up that <s>kapha</s> in many ways,
or it vitiates the blood of one whose blood is increased, lodged in the skin, vessels, sinews, and flesh.
Having vitiated it, it produces a long-continuing form that is thick and rough in nature.
It makes a garland of nodules, reddened, with severe pain and fever.
It is accompanied by dyspnea, cough, diarrhea, dryness of the mouth, hiccup, vomiting, and dizziness,
with delusion, discoloration, fainting, breaking pain in the limbs, and weakness of digestion.
This is <s>granthi-visarpa</s>, arising from the aggravation of <s>kapha</s> and <s>māruta</s>.
From <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> there are fever, stiffness, sleep, torpor, and headache.
There are lassitude and agitation of the limbs, delirium, loss of appetite, and dizziness.
There are fainting, loss of digestive fire, splitting pain in the bones, thirst, and heaviness of the senses.

children.text: āmopaveśanaṃ lepaḥ srotasāṃ sa ca sarpati ||
children.translated_text: There is passage of undigested matter, coating of the channels, and it creeps through them.
Generally seizing the stomach, it occupies one region and is not very painful.
It is strewn with eruptions, exceedingly yellow, red, and pale;
unctuous, black, dark-blue in appearance, dirty, swollen, and heavy;
deep in suppuration; generally touched by heat, it becomes moist and bursts open.
When ripe, its flesh is split apart as if decayed, and its groups of sinews and vessels are clearly visible;
when it pervades the whole body, with all its signs, and attacks the entire skin,
and smells like a corpse, the authorities call that <s>visarpa</s> the one named <s>kardama</s>.
When, from an external cause, angered by a wound, <s>māruta</s> impels <s>pitta</s> mixed with blood,
it produces <s>visarpa</s> covered with blisters like horse gram.
It is rich in swelling, fever, pain, and burning, and is dusky red.
The three arising from the separate <s>doṣas</s> are curable, as are the paired forms when free of complications.
Those produced from all <s>doṣas</s> together, and all those that have overrun the vital spots, are incurable,
as are those whose sinews, vessels, and flesh have decayed, that are moist, and that smell like a corpse.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vīsarpanidānaṃ nāma triṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Gāruḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixty-third chapter named 'The Diagnosis of <s>Visarpa</s>' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
By improper diet and behavior, especially by incompatible ones,
and by sinful acts that are practiced, such as reviling and killing good people, fighting, and theft,

children.text: pāpmabhiḥ karmabhiḥ sadyaḥ prāktanaiḥ preritā malāḥ
children.translated_text: the humors, driven at once by present and former evil deeds,
enter the vessels and, joined with them, corrupt the skin, fat, blood, and flesh.
Having dried them up, they then move outward from there,

children.text: tvacaḥ kurvanti vaivarṇyaṃ śiṣṭāḥ kuṣṭham uśanti tam ||
children.translated_text: and cause discoloration of the skin; the learned call that <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
When such a condition is neglected over time, it enters the whole body and its cavities;
having reached all the tissues, outside and inside, and having moistened them all, it carries on
sweat, moisture, contractions, and subtle, terrible worms,
and it attacks the hair, skin, sinews, and arteries in due order.
It makes the exterior as if covered with ash; this is called external <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
<s>Kuṣṭhas</s> are sevenfold according to the <s>doṣas</s>, arising separately, in pairs, and in combination.
Although in all of them the three <s>doṣas</s> are present, the designation is made from the predominating one.
By <s>vāta</s> there is the <s>kāpāla</s> type of <s>kuṣṭha</s>; by <s>pitta</s>, <s>audumbara</s>; by <s>kapha</s>,
the type called <s>maṇḍala</s>, and <s>vicarcī</s>; <s>ṛṣyajihvā</s> is born from <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Carma</s>, <s>ekakuṣṭha</s>, <s>kiṭima</s>, <s>sidhmā</s>, <s>alasa</s>, and <s>vipādikā</s>
are born from <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>; from <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s> come <s>dadru</s> and <s>śatāruṣī</s>,
<s>puṇḍarīka</s> with blisters, <s>pāmā</s>, and <s>carmadala</s> likewise.
Among them, the first triad, <s>dadru</s>, and <s>kākaṇa</s>,
together with <s>puṇḍarīka</s> and <s>ṛṣyajihvā</s>, are the seven great <s>kuṣṭhas</s>.
Excessive smoothness, roughness to the touch, sweating, absence of sweat, and discoloration,
burning, itching, numbness in the skin, piercing pain, small raised patches, and darkness,
excessive pain in wounds, rapid onset and long persistence,
dryness even in healed lesions, excessive irritation from a slight cause,
horripilation, and blackening of the blood are the earliest signs of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
That which is black and red like a potsherd, dry, harsh, and thin,
spread out in an extended form and covered with corrupted hairs,
is the <s>kāpāla</s> type of <s>kuṣṭha</s>, remembered as irregular and full of piercing pain.
A <s>kuṣṭha</s> resembling the fruit of the fig tree is called <s>audumbara</s>.
It is round, said to be marked by many lesions, and excessive in burning and pain.
It is uncovered, not fissuring, and worm-like; such is <s>audumbara</s>.

children.text: sthiraṃ satyānaṃ guru snigdhaṃ śvetaraktaṃ malānvitam ||
children.translated_text: Firm, thick, heavy, unctuous, white and red, and joined with impurity,
with lesions attached to one another, swollen, with much itching, oozing, and worms,
and joined with a smooth yellowish appearance, is called <s>maṇḍala</s>.
<s>Vicarcikā</s> is dusky, with itching eruptions and moisture.

children.text: paruṣaṃ tatra raktāntam antaḥ śyāmaṃ samunnatam ||
children.translated_text: Rough there, red at the edges, dark within, and raised,
it is described as shaped like a deer's tongue; <s>ṛṣyajihvā</s> has many worms.
The <s>kuṣṭha</s> called <s>carma</s> has the rough touch of elephant hide.
Again, <s>kiṭima</s> is without sweat and resembles fish scales.
It is dry, fire-colored, hard to touch, itchy, rough, and black.

children.text: antā rūkṣaṃ bahiḥ snigdhamantarghṛṣṭaṃ rajaḥ kiret
children.translated_text: Dry at the margins and unctuous outside, when rubbed within it scatters dust.
Thin, unctuous, clear, without sweat, smooth to the touch, and like a flower,
it is generally on the upper body and marked by leanness, covered with pale patches full of itching.
With red fissures on the hands and feet it produces <s>vipādikā</s>.
With severe pain and intense itching, covered with reddish eruptions,
extending long like <s>dūrvā</s> grass and having the hue of the flax flower,
swollen and circular, <s>dadru</s> is said to be itchy.
With a thick root, burning pain, bleeding, and many sores,
with burning, moisture, and pain, it is generally born everywhere.
A pale patch smeared with blood and accompanied by itching, burning, and pain,
raised and covered with red marks like lotus leaves with drops of water,
that is <s>puṇḍarīka</s>, covered with white and reddish blisters.
<s>Pāmā</s> consists of blisters and eruptions, accompanied by itching, moisture, and pain.
They are minute, dusky red, and dry, generally on the buttocks, hands, and elbows.
With blisters, intolerant of touch, with itching, blood, and excessive burning,
red and splitting, <s>carmadala</s> occurs; <s>kākaṇa</s> has intense burning and pain.

children.text: pūrvaraktaṃ ca kṛṣṇaṃ ca kākaṇaṃ triphalopamam
children.translated_text: <s>Kākaṇa</s> is first red and then black, resembling the three myrobalans.
It occurs with all the black marks according to its own causes.
By the marks and treatments prescribed for distinguishing the <s>doṣas</s>, one should diagnose it.
One should abandon as incurable a <s>kuṣṭha</s> that follows its own <s>doṣa</s> and has passed into all the <s>doṣas</s>.
And whatever is stated among <s>kuṣṭhas</s> as having taken refuge in bone, marrow, and semen,
That which is in the fat is difficult to cure; that which has gone into the sinews, bones, and flesh is only manageable.

children.text: akṛcchraṃ kaphavātotthaṃ tvaggataṃ tvamalaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: That which arises from <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and is situated in the skin and is not foul, is easy to cure.

children.text: tatra tvaci sthite kuṣṭhe kāye vaivarṇyarūkṣatā ||
children.translated_text: When <s>kuṣṭha</s> is lodged in the skin, there are discoloration and roughness of the body.
In the blood and flesh there are sweating, heat, and swellings; further,
blisters occur on the hands and feet, and distress is especially severe in the joints.
Through the repeated combination of the <s>doṣa</s>, when it is in the fat there is splitting.
There is little consciousness, and there is wasting of marrow, bone, eyes, urges, and voice.
When there is a wound, there are worms; when it is in the semen, it afflicts one's wife and offspring.
All the preceding signs occur according to their own order, in animals such as deer and the rest.
<s>Śvitra</s>, also called <s>kilāsa</s>, arising from the same source as <s>kuṣṭha</s>, is dreadful.
It is described as non-discharging and as having its basis in the three <s>dhātus</s>.
From <s>vāta</s> it is dry and reddish; from <s>pitta</s> it is copper-colored, like a lotus petal.
It has burning and destroys the hair; from <s>kapha</s> it is white, dense, and heavy.
It should be recognized, with itching, as occurring successively in the blood, flesh, and fat.
By its color each of these two conditions is just such; it becomes harder to cure in each later stage.
If it is new, not mutually joined together, and has much hair that is not white,
and is not produced by burning with fire, that <s>śvitra</s> is curable; otherwise it is to be rejected.
Even if it has arisen very recently on the private parts, palms, soles, or lips,
one who desires success should especially reject <s>kilāsa</s> there.
Diseases generally spread through contact, eating together, intercourse, and similar practices,
and also through sharing one bed or seat, and through garments, garlands, and unguents.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe kuṣṭharoganidānaṃ nāma catuḥṣaṣṭyuttaraśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixty-fourth chapter named 'Diagnosis of <s>Kuṣṭha</s> Disease' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
Worms are declared to be of two kinds, by the distinction of external and internal.
By the distinction of being born from external filth, <s>kapha</s>, blood, and feces, they are fourfold.
By name they are of twenty kinds. Among them the external ones, born from filth,
are the size, shape, and color of sesame seeds, and dwell in hair and clothing.
They have many feet and are minute; by name they are lice and nits.
They are of two kinds and produce skin pustules, itching, and swellings.
Those born within, arising from <s>śleṣman</s>, and those arising externally, are sole causes of <s>kuṣṭha</s>.
Through sweet foods, molasses, milk, curds, fish, and fresh rice,
they are born from <s>kapha</s> in the stomach and, when increased, crawl everywhere.
Some resemble broad <s>bradhna</s> worms, and some are like earthworms.
Some have the form of sprouting grain, and others are thin, long, or minute.
They are white and coppery in appearance; by name they are sevenfold.
They are called <s>antrādā</s>, <s>udarāveṣṭā</s>, <s>hṛdayādā</s>, and <s>mahāgudā</s>,
and <s>cyurava</s>, <s>darbhakusuma</s>, and <s>sugandha</s>; and they produce
nausea, watering of the mouth, indigestion, and loss of taste,
fainting, vomiting, fever, abdominal distention, emaciation, sneezing, and catarrh.
The creatures born from blood are situated in the blood-carrying vessels and are minute.
They are footless, round, and copper-colored; because of their minuteness some are invisible.
They are <s>keśādā</s>, <s>romavidhvaṃsā</s>, <s>romadvīpā</s>, and <s>udumbarā</s>.
These six act only like <s>kuṣṭha</s>, together with <s>saurasa</s> and <s>mātara</s>.
Those arising from feces are born in the colon, and then they move about.
When increased, they become turned toward the stomach.
Then they make the odor of belching, breath, and feces follow along from the mouth.
They are broad, round, thin, or thick, and dark, yellow, white, or black.
Those worms have five names: <s>kakeruka</s>, <s>makeruka</s>,
<s>sausurādā</s>, the one called <s>saśūla</s>, and <s>lelihā</s>; indeed they generate
diarrhea, colic, obstruction of stool, emaciation, roughness, and pallor,
horripilation, depression of digestive fire, and itching of the anus, when they take a wrong path.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe kriminidānaṃ nāma pañcaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixty-fifth chapter named 'Diagnosis of Worms' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall tell you the diagnosis of <s>vāta</s> disease, <s>Suśruta</s>; listen to it.
In every way, the very telling of harmful matters is a cause of obstruction.
The unseen, corrupted wind affects the body in no particularized way.
It is the universal maker, the universal self, the universal form, <s>Prajāpati</s>.
It is creator, establisher, all-pervading <s>Viṣṇu</s>, destroyer, death, and end-maker.
Thus this has been stated; therefore one should always strive with effort.
When its knowledge of <s>doṣa</s> has been stated, together with its natural and pathological activity,
and after determining the divisions of the <s>doṣas</s> in brief and in detail,
each fivefold, its powerful pathological operation here
is now set forth by division, with cause and with symptoms.
<s>Vāyu</s>, angered by causes that produce wasting of the tissues, is not excessively indulged.
In the four channels and spaces it fills those very places more and more.
From those places filled with <s>doṣas</s>, after covering the opening there,
when your <s>vāyu</s> has once become angered, it causes colic, distention, and rumbling of the intestines.
It causes obstruction of stool, loss of voice, and stiffness of the sight, back, and waist.
Again in the body it produces other difficult complications.
Vomiting, dyspnea, cough, and cholera-like illness arise from the stomach,
as well as itching, obstruction, heat, and other diseases above the navel.
It causes impairment of the senses, such as hearing, and blistering and roughness in the skin.
It creates severe pains, dyspnea, poisoning-like illness, and discoloration.
It creates obstruction at the end of the intestine, loss of appetite, emaciation, and dizziness,
a lump lodged in flesh and fat, and harsh roughness in the skin and other parts.
The body is heavy and is struck with extreme pain, as if beaten with a staff and fist.
When it is situated in the bone, one should observe intense pain in the thigh-bone joints.
When it is situated in the marrow, there is instability in the bones and sleeplessness when the pains arise;
and, in the case of semen, there is rapid emission into the lap, or some abnormality.
When it is situated in the fetus and in the semen, there is distension and emptiness in the head;
there, when the enraged <s>vāta</s> (wind-humor) remains in that place, it causes swelling and difficulty.
When <s>anila</s> (wind) has gone into the joints, it produces a touch like a water-filled skin and wasting;
when it has taken refuge in the whole body, it causes piercing, splitting, throbbing, and breaking pain.
It causes stiffness, convulsion, sleepiness, breaking of the joints, and trembling.

children.text: yadā tu dhamanīḥ sarvāḥ kruddho 'bhyeti muhurmuhuḥ
children.translated_text: But when the enraged one repeatedly enters all the channels,
then it throws the body about; this disease is known as <s>ākṣepaṇa</s> (convulsion).
When <s>vāyu</s> (wind), obstructed downward, again goes upward,

children.text: tadāvaṣṭabhya hṛdayaṃ śiraḥ śaṅkhau ca pīḍayet ||
children.translated_text: then, seizing the heart, it torments the head and the temples.

children.text: sa kṣipetparito gātraṃ hanuṃ vā cāsya nāmayet
children.translated_text: It throws the limbs about on every side, or bends the jaw of the mouth;
breathing is difficult for him, and he closes both eyes.
He coos like a dove, helpless; this is <s>apatantraka</s>.

children.text: sa eva vāmanāsāyāṃ yuktastu marutā hṛdi ||
children.translated_text: The same, when joined with wind in the heart and in the left nostril,

children.text: prāpnoti ca muhuḥ svāsthyaṃ muhur asvāsthyavān bhavet
children.translated_text: obtains health again and again, and again and again becomes unwell.
When it has arisen from injury, it is considered most difficult to cure.
When <s>vāyu</s>, its body cut off, then produces stiffness with sweating in him,

children.text: vyāpnoti sakalaṃ dehaṃ yatra cāyāmyate punaḥ ||
children.translated_text: and pervades the whole body, where it is again stretched out,
and when, having entered the internal tissues, it causes obstruction of urges and of the eyes,
it produces yawning, weakness, immobility of the teeth, and loss of effort.
There is external pain in the two sides, and seizure of the jaw, back, and head.
There is outward stretching of the body, from the back toward the heart and head.

children.text: uraścotkṣipyate tatra skandho vā nāmyate tadā
children.translated_text: There the chest is raised upward, or the shoulder is then bent down.
There is discoloration in the teeth and mouth, and absence of sweat from the limbs.
They call this external stretching and lockjaw in a patient afflicted by <s>vāta</s>.
After reaching feces, urine, and blood, the <s>doṣas</s> (faults), together with wind,

children.text: āyacchanti tanor doṣāḥ sarvam ā pādamastakam
children.translated_text: stretch the body from foot to head.
In one who remains merely pale, the stretching of the wound is greatly increased.
When there is an impulse in the limbs, relief occurs; in all cases this is due to convulsion.
From scraping the tongue, from eating hot food, or from excessive pride,
the wind, aggravated and situated at the root of the jaw, stiffens the jaw
and makes the mouth either held open or held closed.
Because of that there is <s>hanustambha</s> (lockjaw), with difficult chewing and speaking.
When <s>anila</s> stiffens the speech-bearing vessels, it paralyzes the tongue.
This is <s>jihvāstambha</s> (paralysis of the tongue); because of it one lacks power over food, drink, and speech.
From carrying a load on the head, from excessive laughter and talking,
from an uneven pillow, and from chewing hard things,
<s>vāyu</s> is increased by these wind-provoking causes and takes an upward course.
It makes the face crooked, along with loud laughter and distortion of the gaze.
Then it makes his power of speech weak and his eyes rigid.
Loosening of the teeth, failure of the voice, loss of hearing, and seizure of the sight occur;
there also arise ignorance of smells, destruction of memory, fear, and difficult breathing.
There is spitting, piercing pain in the sides, and closing of one eye;
there are severe pains above the collarbone, or there may be paralysis of half the body.
Some call this <s>ardita</s> (facial paralysis), while others call it a disease of one limb.
And, having taken refuge in the blood, it may affect the vessels; the vessels supporting the head
produce a dry, painful, black <s>śirograha</s> (seizure of the head), which is incurable.
And when <s>vāyu</s>, together with the sinews, has seized the body,
it disables one or the other side; this is called <s>pakṣāghāta</s> (hemiplegia).
Half of the whole body becomes unable to act and without sensation.
Some understand it as a disease of one limb, while others as pain in the armpit region.
When <s>anila</s> has taken refuge in the whole body, there is obstruction of all the limbs and stiffness.
A side afflicted by pure <s>vāta</s> is considered very difficult to cure.
It is difficult when mixed with another <s>doṣa</s>, when greatly increased, or when caused by wasting.
When its course is blocked by undigested matter, and it is joined with <s>kapha</s>, it stiffens the limbs.
Indeed, every case of <s>daṇḍāpatānaka</s> is incurable.
When <s>vāyu</s>, arisen from the root of the shoulder and lodged there, contracts the vessels,
it produces a disorder of the arm that removes outward flowing movement.
The tendon on the back of the arm, which extends toward the palm and fingers,
destroys the function of the arms; that is also called <s>viṣūcī</s>.

children.text: vāyuḥ kaṭyāśritaḥ sakthnaḥ kaṇḍarām ākṣiped yadā
children.translated_text: When <s>vāyu</s>, lodged in the hip, convulses the tendon of the thigh,
then the creature becomes lame; from the loss of both thighs' function he becomes crippled.
He trembles when beginning to walk and goes as though limping.
One should know this as <s>kalāyakhañja</s>, with the bindings of the joints loosened.
By the use of cold, hot, liquid, dry, heavy, and unctuous things,
and in states of digested or undigested food, as well as by exertion, agitation, unctuousness, and staying awake,
<s>śleṣman</s> (phlegm), accumulated excessively at the proper time, is split apart;
overpowering the other <s>doṣa</s>, it enters the body.
Filling the bones of the thighs within, it is then obstructed by <s>śleṣman</s>;
there the bone, through that and through cold wind, bathes the thigh.
With darkened limbs, stiffness of the limbs, drowsiness, fainting, loss of appetite, and fever,
they call this <s>ūrustambha</s> (thigh-stiffness); others call it external <s>vāta</s>.
A swelling from <s>vāta</s> and blood arises in the middle of the knee, with great pain.
The condition called <s>kroṣṭukaśīrṣa</s> should be understood as being like the gross <s>kroṣṭukaśīrṣa</s>.
When it arises because a painful foot has been set down unevenly, or because of fatigue,
and <s>vāta</s> seizes the ankle, they call it <s>vātakaṇṭaka</s>.
When <s>māruta</s> afflicts the heel, the counter-toes, the navel, or the neck,
and constricts them with painful throwing motions, they call that <s>gṛdhrasī</s>.

children.text: hṛṣyete caraṇau yasya bhavetāṃ cāpi suptakau
children.translated_text: When a person's feet tingle and also become numb,
that should be known as <s>pādaharṣa</s>, produced by the provocation of <s>kapha</s> and <s>māruta</s>.
<s>Anila</s>, joined with <s>pitta</s> and blood, produces burning in the feet;
especially when one walks about, that should be designated <s>pādadāha</s>, burning of the feet.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vātavyādhinidānaṃ nāma ṣaṭṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixty-sixth chapter, named 'Diagnosis of Vāta Disorders,' is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall tell you the diagnosis of <s>vātarakta</s>, <s>Suśruta</s>; listen to it.
Through incompatible food, eating again before the previous meal is digested, anger, daytime sleep, and wakefulness at night,
for the most part among delicate people who follow improper diet and conduct,
and also among the corpulent and those living in comfort, <s>vātaśoṇita</s> becomes aggravated.
When, through injury from fire and from impurity, the blood of men has been vitiated,
<s>vāyu</s>, increased by wind-provoking and cold things, becomes enraged and moves on a wrong path.
Obstructed by blood of that same kind, it first vitiates that very blood.

children.text: tathā vāto gude pīḍāṃ balāsaṃ vātaśoṇitam ||
children.translated_text: In that way <s>vāta</s> brings pain in the anus, <s>balāsa</s>, and <s>vātaśoṇita</s>.
Having caused obstruction, it first generates the disease; afterward it runs everywhere.
Especially after emesis and the like, prolapse or pendulousness is its sign.
When it is about to arise, it is like <s>kuṣṭha</s>, and is also known by the name <s>sāmbuda</s>.
In the knees, shanks, thighs, waist, shoulders, hands, feet, limbs, and joints,
itching, throbbing, pricking, splitting pain, heaviness, and numbness
arise again and again, subside, and repeatedly appear once more.
Taking its root in the feet, and sometimes also in the hands,

children.text: ākhoriva bilaṃ kruddhaḥ kṛtsnaṃ dehaṃ vidhāvati ||
children.translated_text: when enraged it runs through the whole body like a mouse through its burrow.
At first it arises, established in the skin and flesh, with its own preceding signs;
then, after some time, it becomes deep and attacks all the bodily constituents.
In a fixed place such as the waist and the rest, the skin becomes coppery, dark, or red.
There is nodular swelling and suppuration, and that <s>vāyu</s> enters the bones and marrow.
Moving swiftly within, it acts as though cutting and grinding them apart.

children.text: karoti khañjaṃ paṅguṃ vā śarīraṃ sarvataścaran ||
children.translated_text: Ranging through the whole body, it makes the body lame or crippled.
Where <s>vāta</s> predominates, there is excessive pain, throbbing, and breaking sensation,
dryness of the swelling, blackness, dusky color, and alternations of increase and decrease,
contraction of the vessels, fingers, and joints, seizure of the limbs, and extreme pain,
dislike of cold, lack of relief, stiffness, trembling, and numbness.
When blood predominates, there is swelling, excessive pain, pricking, coppery color, and tingling.
It does not become even through oily or dry applications, and is accompanied by itching and moistness.

children.text: pitte vidāhaḥ saṃmohaḥ svādo mūrchā madastṛṣā
children.translated_text: When <s>pitta</s> predominates, there are burning, confusion, altered taste, fainting, intoxication, and thirst,
intolerance of touch, intense pain, wasting, suppuration, and very great heat.
When <s>kapha</s> predominates, there are rigidity, heaviness, numbness, unctuousness, and coldness;

children.text: kaṇḍūrmandā ca rugdvandvaṃ sarvaliṅgaṃ ca saṃkarāt ||
children.translated_text: the itching is mild, the pain is twofold, and from combination there is the full set of signs.

children.text: ekadoṣaṃ ca saṃsādhyaṃ yāpyaṃ caiva dvidoṣajam
children.translated_text: A case arising from one <s>doṣa</s> is curable; one arising from two <s>doṣas</s> is manageable only by maintenance.
One arising from all three <s>doṣas</s>, and the very dreadful <s>raktapitta</s>, should quickly be abandoned.
Blood in the limb quickly destroys; <s>māruta</s>, lodged in the branches and joints,
and mutually obstructing them, takes away the life-breaths by means of pains.
When, among the fivefold <s>vāyu</s>, <s>prāṇa</s> is provoked by dryness, fickleness, fasting,
overeating, injury, and the excitation and movement of urges,
it brings about injury to the eyes and the other organs.
Rhinitis, burning, thirst, cough, dyspnea, and the like also arise.
It may produce obstruction of the throat, displacement of excreta, vomiting, loss of appetite, and rhinitis,
and also goiter and similar diseases; this is the vāyu that has its seat above the clavicles and in the head.
<s>Vyāna</s>, vitiated by excessive walking, bathing, sport, and exertion in sense-objects,
and by incompatibles, dry things, fear, joy, grief, and the like,
causes loss of virility, energy, and strength, grief, agitation of mind, and fevers,
pricking pains of every kind, horripilation, and excessive sleep or numbness.
It causes <s>kuṣṭha</s>, <s>visarpa</s>, and other conditions, and weakness of the whole body.
<s>Samāna</s>, vitiated by irregular digestion, indigestion, cold and mixed foods,
and by untimely sleep, wakefulness, and the like, produces
colic, abdominal tumors, <s>grahaṇī</s> disorders, and other diseases lodged in the liver and stomach.
<s>Apāna</s>, through dry and heavy food, suppression of urges, and excessive riding or carrying,
and through excessive use of vehicles, drinking, rising up, and walking about,
when provoked, produces all diseases that have their seat in the large intestine,
and many conditions such as disorders of urine and semen, piles, and prolapse of the rectum.
When <s>sāma</s> vāta has spread through the whole body, it is marked by drowsiness, rigidity, and heaviness,
by unctuousness at the time of awakening, coldness, swelling, and loss of digestive fire.
By the disappearance of itching, dryness, and excess, and by relief through the appropriate treatment,
one should know that it is freed from <s>āma</s>; the opposite of drowsiness and the rest is its sign.
They describe the obstruction of <s>vāyu</s> by <s>vāta</s> as having many varieties.
When it is covered by the signs of <s>pitta</s>, there are burning, thirst, pain, dizziness, and darkness,
aggravation by pungent, hot, sour, and salty things, and a desire for cooling substances.
When covered by <s>kapha</s>, there is coldness, heaviness, pain, impairment of digestive fire, and increased desire for pungent things, ghee, and milk.
There is also a desire for fasting, exertion, dry substances, and hot substances when <s>vāta</s> is covered by <s>kapha</s>.
When covered by <s>kapha</s>, there may be aching of the limbs, nausea, heaviness, and loss of appetite.
When covered by blood, there is burning pain, arising intensely in the skin and flesh,
with reddened swelling, and circular patches appear.
A swelling caused by flesh is hard, and there are nausea and eruptions as well;

children.text: harṣaḥ pipīlikānāṃ ca saṃcāra iva jāyate
children.translated_text: horripilation arises, and it is as if ants were moving about.

children.text: calalagrano mṛduḥ śītaḥ śotho gātreṣu rocakaḥ ||
children.translated_text: There is a mobile lump; the swelling in the limbs is soft and cold, and there may be relish for food.

children.text: āḍhyavāta iva jñeyaḥ sa kṛcchro medasāvṛtaḥ
children.translated_text: When it is covered by fat, it should be known as like <s>āḍhyavāta</s>; it is difficult to treat.
When it is covered by the skin, touch is obscured, and it is hot and cold.
But when it is covered by marrow, there is irregular yawning and twisting,

children.text: śūlaṃ ca paḍyimānaśca pāṇibhyāṃ labhate sukham
children.translated_text: pain, and a sinking sensation; he obtains comfort from rubbing with the hands.

children.text: śukrāvṛte tu śothe vai cātivego na vidyate ||
children.translated_text: When it is covered by semen, swelling indeed occurs, but no excessive urge is found.

children.text: bhukte kukṣau rujā jīrṇe nikṛttir bhavati dhruvam
children.translated_text: After eating there is pain in the belly; when digestion is complete, cutting pain certainly occurs.
When it is covered by urine in the bladder, there is non-passage of urine and distension.
When it is covered in the channels, there is obstruction, and then it cuts around its own place.

children.text: patatyāśu jvarākrānto mūrchāṃ ca labhate naraḥ ||
children.translated_text: A man quickly falls, seized by fever, and also falls into fainting.
When pressed once by another, corrupted semen is emitted only after a long time.
When <s>vāyu</s> is covered by all the bodily elements, there is pain in the pelvis, groin, and back.
And when <s>māruta</s> is reversed, the heart is oppressed.

children.text: bhramo mūrchā rujā dāhaḥ pittena prāṇa āvṛte ||
children.translated_text: When <s>prāṇa</s> is covered by <s>pitta</s>, there are dizziness, fainting, pain, and burning.

children.text: rujā tandrā svarabhraṃśo dāho vyāne tu sarvaśaḥ
children.translated_text: When <s>vyāna</s> is covered by it, there are pain, torpor, loss of voice, and burning everywhere.
There is impairment of the course of movement and activity of the limbs, heat, and pain along with it.
When <s>samāna</s> is affected, there is injury to bodily heat, cessation of sweating, and severe thirst.
When <s>apāna</s> is affected, there is burning; in the stool there is a yellow color.
There is increase of menstrual discharge, heating, and also distension and difficult urination.
When <s>prāṇa</s> is covered by <s>śleṣman</s>, there is noise and obstruction of the channels,
spitting, sweating, and restriction of inhalation and exhalation.
When <s>udāna</s> is covered, there is heaviness of the body, loss of appetite, and obstruction of speech and voice.
There is loss of strength and complexion; when <s>apāna</s> is covered, there is constriction of the joints and bones.
There is heaviness in all the limbs, and great stoutness has come on.
When <s>samāna</s> is covered, there is ignorance of proper activity, absence of sweat, and weak digestive fire.

children.text: apāne sakalaṃ mūtraṃ śakṛtaḥ syāt pravartanam ||
children.translated_text: When <s>apāna</s> is covered, there is the complete discharge of urine and feces.
Thus they know the disease <s>vātarakta</s> to be of twenty-two kinds.
<s>Prāṇa</s> and the others, too, mutually overrun one another in due order.

children.text: sarve 'pi viṃśatividhaṃ vidyād āvaraṇaṃ ca yat
children.translated_text: One should know all obstruction of this sort also as twentyfold.
Nausea, obstruction of breathing, catarrh, and stiffness of the head,
heart disease and dryness of the mouth occur when <s>apāna</s> is covered by <s>prāṇa</s>.
When <s>prāṇa</s> is covered by <s>udāna</s>, there is indeed loss of strength.
The physician should distinguish every kind of obstruction by careful examination,
considering the seats of the forms of <s>vāta</s> and the increase and decrease of their functions.
There is the mutual obstruction by <s>pitta</s> of the five, beginning with <s>prāṇa</s>,
and the residence of <s>pitta</s> and the others in them, with mixed conditions produced by those mixed factors.
Likewise, with mixed <s>pitta</s> and the other <s>doṣas</s>, the mixed conditions also become manyfold.
He should attentively recognize them from the arising of the symptoms proper to each.
Slowly and repeatedly he should test even firm indications by therapeutic relief.
In particular, <s>prāṇa</s> is called life, and <s>udāna</s> is called strength.
From the affliction of those two there is loss of both lifespan and strength.
The obstructed winds, whether unknown or known, when displaced from their proper seats,
may become difficult to cure even with effort, or may be accompanied by complications.
Abscess, spleen disease, heart disease, abdominal tumors, weakness of digestive fire, and the like
become the complications of those obstructed winds when they are neglected.
O <s>Suśruta</s>, the diagnosis taught by <s>Ātreya</s> has been stated by me
for the discernment of all diseases and for the increase of human life.
Having thus understood diseases and the rest, one should then undertake treatment.
<s>Triphalā</s>, joined with honey, ghee, and jaggery, destroys all diseases.
Or <s>Triphalā</s> with the three pungents crushes all diseases.
Or it may be joined with <s>śatāvarī</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>agni</s>, and <s>viḍaṅga</s>.
<s>Śatāvarī</s>, <s>guḍūcī</s>, <s>agni</s>, <s>śuṇṭhī</s>, <s>mūṣalikā</s>, <s>balā</s>,
<s>punarnavā</s>, <s>bṛhatī</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, and leaves of <s>nimba</s>,
<s>bhṛṅgarāja</s>, <s>āmalaka</s>, and <s>vāsaka</s>: with their juice,

children.text: bhāvitā triphalā saptavāram ekam athāpi vā ||
children.translated_text: <s>Triphalā</s> may be steeped seven times, or even once.
With the substances mentioned before, according to availability, it may be made as powder or as a sweet bolus,
as a pill, ghee, oil, or decoction; it removes wasting disease.

children.text: palaṃ palārdhakaṃ vāpi karṣaṃ karṣārdhameva vā ||
children.translated_text: The dose is one <s>pala</s>, or half a <s>pala</s>, one <s>karṣa</s>, or half a <s>karṣa</s>.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vātaraktani saptaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the glorious <s>Garuḍa</s> Mahāpurāṇa, in the earlier section called the first part, in the chapter on conduct, the one hundred and sixty-seventh chapter on <s>vātarakta</s> is completed.
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
I shall tell the proven essence of formulations that removes all diseases,
O <s>Suśruta</s>; listen briefly, for the sake of the life of living beings.
From eating foods that are astringent, pungent, bitter, sour, and dry,
from anxiety, sexual intercourse, exercise, fear, grief, and keeping awake,
from loud speech, excessive burdens, excessive activity, and emaciation,
<s>vāyu</s> becomes aggravated in the rainy season, when food is digested, and at the end of the day.
From hot, sour, salty, alkaline, pungent, and undigested food,
from exposure to sharp sun and fire, and from resorting to liquor and anger,
when food is taken at a burning time, at midday, and after the rainy season,
<s>pitta</s> becomes aggravated in embodied beings in summer and also at midnight.
From excessive eating of sweet, sour, salty, unctuous, heavy, and cold foods,
and from the use of new grain, slimy foods, and the meat of marshy animals,
through lack of exercise, day-sleep, and the comforts of bed and seat,

children.text: kaphapradoṣo bhukte ca vasante ca prakupyati ||
children.translated_text: derangement of <s>kapha</s> occurs after eating and becomes aggravated in spring.
Roughness of the body, contraction, stiffness, obstruction, and the like,
as well as numbness, horripilation, rigidity, and drying up,
blackish discoloration, loosening of the limbs, weakness, and increase of fatigue occur.
With those signs of <s>vāyu</s>, one should call the disease <s>vātātmaka</s>, of the nature of <s>vāta</s>.
Burning, heat, sweating of the feet, moistening, aggravation, discoloration, and fatigue,
pungent and sour corpse-like foul odor, sweat, fainting, excessive thirst, and dizziness,
yellow and green coloration: by signs connected with these, a person is marked by <s>pitta</s>.
In the body, oiliness, sweetness, slowness of action, binding,
inertia, satiety, compactness, swelling, whiteness, and heaviness,
itching and a tendency to sleep: this is the symptom-complex arising from <s>kapha</s>.
From a combination of causes and signs, one should know a disease to be caused by two <s>doṣas</s>.
One produced by all the causes and possessing the signs of all three is <s>sānnipātika</s>.
The body of embodied beings is said to be the support of <s>doṣas</s>, tissues, and wastes.
Their equilibrium is health; the opposite is their diminution or increase.
Fat, blood, flesh, adipose tissue, bone, marrow, and semen are the bodily tissues.
<s>Vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s> are the <s>doṣas</s>; feces, urine, and the rest are remembered as wastes.

children.text: vāyuḥ śīto laghuḥ sūkṣmaḥ svaranāśī sthiro balī
children.translated_text: <s>Vāyu</s> is cold, light, subtle, destructive of the voice, firm, and strong.
<s>Pitta</s> is sour, pungent, and hot, and, in indigestion, a cause of disease.
<s>Śleṣman</s> is sweet, salty, unctuous, heavy, and very slimy.
<s>Vāyu</s> has its seat in the anus and pelvis; <s>pitta</s> is situated in the large intestine.
The seat of <s>kapha</s> is the stomach, or else the throat, head, and joints.
Pungent, bitter, and astringent tastes aggravate <s>samīraṇa</s>, the wind.
Pungent, sour, and salty tastes aggravate <s>pitta</s>; sweet, hot, and salty tastes aggravate <s>kapha</s>.
Those very same things, used in reverse, serve for the pacification of these <s>doṣas</s>.
For the sick they bring relief, and for those in a normal state they are causes of well-being.
The sweet taste should be known as beneficial to the eyes and as increasing the <s>rasa-dhātu</s>.
The sour taste, in addition, is pleasing to the mind and heart, and also kindles and digests.
The bitter taste kindles appetite, removes fever and thirst, and cleanses and dries.
The astringent taste is <s>pittala</s>, scraping, arresting, absorbent, and drying.
Substance is the supreme support of taste, potency, and digestive transformation.
It remains through taste, cooking, and later states, and is the swift support of all material things.
Potency is held to be cold or hot, or else salty; alternatively, it is simply power.
The digestive transformation of tastes is twofold, and also pungent alone.
The excellence of the physician, medicine, patient, and attendant
constitutes the four limbs of treatment; when they are the opposite, treatment does not succeed.
Having understood region, season, age, digestive fire, balance, constitution, medicine,
body, mind, strength, and disease, one should undertake the therapeutic action.
A marshy region has abundant water and mountains, and it tends to aggravate <s>kapha</s> and <s>māruta</s>.
The dry-land region has different kinds of branches and is especially associated with diseases of blood and <s>pitta</s>.
A region furnished with mixed characteristics is remembered as ordinary or intermediate.
One is a child up to sixteen; the middle period extends to seventy, and after that one is called old.
<s>Kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>anila</s> are generally said to predominate in that order.
In feeble old age, treatments with alkali, cautery, and the knife are to be avoided.
For a thin person, nourishing treatment should be done; for a corpulent body, reducing treatment.
For one of medium build, preservation is proper; three distinctions of body are accepted.
Strength is to be carefully understood from steadiness, exercise, and contentment.
A man who is not disturbed, who has great energy, and who is very bold is strong.
If drinking, food, and the like, though contrary to one's constitution,
are adapted for one's own comfort and happiness, that is called equilibrium.
From foods that increase <s>śleṣman</s> in a pregnant woman, a person of <s>śleṣman</s>-constitution is born.
Likewise, from windy and bilious foods come <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> constitutions; from wholesome food comes one of balanced tissues.
A person who is thin, dry, has little hair, is unsteady in mind,
fond of much speech, and like this even in dreams is a person of <s>vāta-prakṛti</s>.
One prematurely grey, fair, sweating, irascible, and intelligent,
and who sees blazing things even in dreams, is said to have <s>pitta-prakṛti</s>.
One with steady mind, a subtle voice, clear complexion, and oily hair,
and who sees water, rocks, and the world in dreams, is a person of <s>śleṣman-prakṛti</s>.
A person connected with two or three <s>doṣas</s> is to be known from mixed signs.
Even when another <s>doṣa</s> is present, the constitution is remembered according to the one that is stronger.
Dull, sharp, irregular, and even: these are the four kinds
of gastric fire, from predominance of <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, <s>anila</s>, and from their balance.
For even fire, maintenance should be done; for irregular fire, restraint of <s>vāta</s>.
For sharp fire, counteraction of <s>pitta</s>; for dull fire, purification of <s>śleṣman</s>.
Indigestion is the origin of all diseases and the destruction of digestive fire.
It is fourfold, with the signs of raw, sour, rasa-type, and obstructed indigestion.
From raw indigestion arise <s>viṣūcikā</s>, pain in the heart, lassitude, and the like.
In that case one should cause vomiting with <s>vacā</s>, salt, and water.
Absence of semen, dizziness, fainting, and thirst arise from sour indigestion.
When it is uncooked, cold-water drinking and exposure to wind are to be used there.
Breaking pain in the limbs, heaviness of the head, disorders from faulty food, and other diseases arise.

children.text: tasminsvāpo divā kāryo laṅghanaṃ ca vivarjanam ||
children.translated_text: In that condition, sleep by day should be done, while fasting and exertion are to be avoided.
Colic and abdominal tumor point to obstruction in the places of feces and urine.
There fomentation should be prescribed, and salt water should be drunk.
Raw, sour, and obstructed indigestion are respectively caused by <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>anila</s>.
The wise person should anoint the belly with asafoetida, <s>tryūṣaṇa</s>, and rock salt.
One should practice sleep by day, which destroys every kind of indigestion.
A mass of diseases arises from unwholesome food; therefore one should abandon unwholesome food.

children.text: uṣṇāmbu vānupānaṃ ca mākṣikaiḥ pācanaṃ bhavet
children.translated_text: Hot water as an after-drink, or digestives mixed with honey, will promote digestion.
Milk is generally incompatible with <s>karīra</s>, curds, and fish.

children.text: bilvaḥ śoṇā ca gambhārī pāṭalā gaṇikārikā
children.translated_text: <s>Bilva</s>, <s>śoṇā</s>, <s>gambhārī</s>, <s>pāṭalā</s>, and <s>gaṇikārikā</s>
are this great <s>pañcamūla</s>, kindling digestion and destroying <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Śālaparṇī</s>, <s>pṛśniparṇī</s>, the two <s>bṛhatī</s> plants, and <s>gokṣura</s>:
this is the lesser group of five roots, removing <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s> and promoting virility.
The two groups together are <s>daśamūla</s> (the ten roots), removing fever caused by the combined <s>doṣas</s>.

children.text: kāse śvāse ca tandrāyāṃ pārśvaśūle ca śasyate ||
children.translated_text: It is recommended for cough, difficult breathing, drowsiness, and pain in the side.
With these, medicated oils, ghee preparations, and poultices can overcome the disorder called <s>alaka</s>.
For a decoction the water should be four times as much; when it has been reduced to a quarter, it is again reckoned fourfold.

children.text: snehaṃ ca tatsamaṃ kṣīraṃ kalkaśca snehapādakaḥ
children.translated_text: The fat should be equal to that, the milk the same as it, and the paste a quarter of the fat.
With the drugs properly prepared, the cooking is the same for use in an enema and for drinking.
For massage one should prepare a strong cooking, and for nasal treatment a mild cooking as well.
One should consider whether the body and senses are firm, and what constitution is established in a person.
Knowing that state as health, one should treat him as a person with remaining life.
One who grasps objects through the senses in a reversed or abnormal way is marked by death.
So too is one who hates his physician, friend, and teacher, or who becomes hostile to those dear to him.
If a person's ankles, knees, forehead, jaw, and cheeks
have fallen or shifted from their places, he soon gives up his life-breaths.
If the left eye is sunken, the tongue dark, and the nose deformed,

children.text: kṛṣṇau sthānacyutau coṣṭhau kṛṣṇāsyaṃ yasya taṃ tyajet ||
children.translated_text: and if both lips are black and displaced and the mouth is black, one should abandon him.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe vaidyakaśāstraparibhāṣā nāmāṣṭaṣaṣṭyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the venerable <s>Garuḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the first section of the eastern part, in the conduct section, ends the one hundred sixty-eighth chapter, called 'Terminology of the Medical Science.'
<s>Dhanvantari</s> said:
For the sake of discerning what is wholesome and unwholesome, I shall explain the rule concerning accompanying drinks and foods.
Red <s>śāli</s> rice destroys the three <s>doṣas</s> and prevents thirst and excess fat.
<s>Mahāśāli</s> is supremely virility-promoting; <s>kalama</s> removes <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
The white <s>ṣaṣṭika</s> rice is generally cold, heavy, and destructive of the three <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Śyāmāka</s> is drying, rough, productive of <s>vāta</s>, and removing <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Priyaṅgu</s>, <s>nīvāra</s>, and <s>koradūṣa</s> are declared to be the same.
Barley, whether used repeatedly or once cooled, removes <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Wheat is virility-promoting, cold, heavy, sweet, and destructive of <s>vāta</s>.
Green gram conquers <s>kapha</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and blood disorders; it is astringent, sweet, and light.
<s>Māṣa</s> has great strengthening power, promotes virility, removes <s>pitta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, and is heavy.
<s>Rājamāṣa</s> is not virility-promoting; it destroys <s>śleṣman</s> and <s>pitta</s> and removes pains from <s>anila</s>.
Horse gram removes difficult breathing and hiccup, and dispels <s>kapha</s>, abdominal masses, and <s>anila</s>.
<s>Makuṣṭhaka</s> aggravates bleeding disorders and fever; it is cold and constipating.
Chickpea is remembered as producing <s>vāta</s> and as destroying virility, blood disorders, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s>.
Lentil is sweet, cold, constipating, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Kalāya</s> has all the same qualities, but is extremely productive of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: āgkī kaphapittaghnī śukralā ca tathā smṛtā
children.translated_text: The plant read as <s>āgkī</s> removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s> and is also remembered as semen-promoting.
Flax should be known as productive of <s>pitta</s>; white mustard conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Sesame is alkaline, sweet, unctuous, strengthening, hot, and productive of <s>pitta</s>.
Various kinds of cultivated grains are strength-destroying, rough, and cold.
<s>Citraka</s>, <s>iṅgudī</s>, <s>nālīkā</s>, <s>pippalī</s>, honey, and <s>śigru</s>,
together with <s>cavyā</s>, <s>caraṇa</s>, <s>nirguṇḍī</s>, <s>tarkārī</s>, and <s>kāśamardaka</s>,
and along with <s>bilva</s>, remove <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, kill worms, are light, and kindle digestion.
<s>Varṣābhū</s> and <s>arka</s> remove <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s> and destroy the <s>doṣas</s>.
Castor is bitter in taste; <s>kākamācī</s> removes the three <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Cāṅgerī</s> removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>; mustard gives rise to all the <s>doṣas</s>.
Safflower is just the same, and <s>rājikā</s> produces <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
The item read as <s>nāḍīca</s> removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>; <s>cuñcu</s> is sweet and cooling.
Lotus leaf removes the <s>doṣas</s>, while <s>tripuṭa</s> is especially productive of <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Vāstuka</s> is alkaline, removes all <s>doṣas</s>, and is an excellent appetizer.
<s>Taṇḍulīya</s> removes poison; the same is said of <s>pālaṅkī</s> and the other such greens.
Raw radish produces <s>doṣas</s>; when boiled, it removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
When cooked it is regarded as edible, beneficial to the throat, and removing all <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Karkoṭaka</s>, eggplant, <s>paṭola</s>, and bitter gourd
remove skin disease, urinary disorder, fever, difficult breathing, cough, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
Pumpkin removes all <s>doṣas</s>, is pleasing to the heart, and cleanses the bladder.
<s>Kaliṅga</s> and bottle gourd destroy <s>pitta</s> and produce <s>vāta</s>.
Cucumber and <s>urvāruka</s> increase <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s>, but check <s>pitta</s>.
<s>Vṛkṣāmla</s> removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>; citron diminishes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Pomegranate removes <s>vāta</s> and is constipating; the fruit of the orange is heavy.
The rind and citron are digestive stimulants and diminish <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
The item read as <s>māṣa</s> removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>; its skin is unctuous, hot, and dispels <s>anila</s>.
Juicy āmalaka is virility-promoting, sweet, pleasing to the heart, and sour in effect.
Harītakī, like nectar, is auspicious and restores relish after eating.
<s>Akṣa</s> is laxative and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>; likewise it conquers the three <s>doṣas</s>.
The sour tamarind fruit removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>śleṣman</s> and is laxative.
<s>Lakuca</s> is doṣa-producing; sweet <s>bakula</s> conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
<s>Bījapūraka</s> removes abdominal masses, <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, difficult breathing, and cough.

children.text: kapitthaṃ grāhi doṣaghnaṃ pakvaṃ guru viṣāpaham
children.translated_text: Ripe wood apple is constipating, removes <s>doṣas</s>, is heavy, and removes poison.
When young it produces <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>; when not fully ripe it increases <s>pitta</s>.
Ripe mango produces <s>vāta</s> and grants flesh, semen, complexion, and strength.
The rose-apple fruit removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>kapha</s>, and <s>pitta</s>; it is constipating and obstructive.
<s>Tinduka</s> removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>; jujube removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Bilva is obstructive and productive of <s>vāta</s>; <s>priyāla</s> dispels wind.
The fruit of <s>rājādana</s>, plantain, jackfruit, and coconut products
are said to produce semen and flesh, and to be sweet, unctuous, and heavy.
Grapes, madhūka, dates, and saffron conquer <s>vātarakta</s>.
Ripe <s>māgadhī</s> is sweet and is excellent for removing difficult breathing and <s>pitta</s>.
Fresh ginger is appetizing, aphrodisiac, kindles digestion, and removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
Dry ginger, black pepper, and long pepper are regarded as conquerors of <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
One should know black pepper to be non-aphrodisiac; so it is accepted in medical science.
Asafoetida destroys abdominal tumors, colic, and constipation, and dispels <s>vāta</s> and <s>kapha</s>.
<s>Yavānī</s>, coriander, and <s>ajājī</s> are supreme removers of <s>vāta</s> and phlegm.
Rock salt is beneficial for the eyes, aphrodisiac, and remembered as pacifying the three <s>doṣas</s>.
<s>Sauvarcala</s> salt breaks constipation, is hot, and destroys pain in the heart or chest.
<s>Viḍaṅga</s> is hot, pain-relieving, sharp, and a destroyer of <s>vāta</s>.

children.text: romakaṃ vātalaṃ svādu rocanaṃ kledanaṃ guru
children.translated_text: <s>Romaka</s> salt increases <s>vāta</s>; it is sweet, appetizing, moistening, and heavy.
<s>Yavakṣāra</s> destroys disorders of the heart, jaundice, and throat disease, and kindles the digestive fire.
<s>Sarjikṣāra</s> is burning, digestive, sharp, and penetrating.
Rainwater from the sky destroys the <s>doṣas</s>, is light, good for the heart, and removes poison.

children.text: nādeyaṃ vātalaṃ rūkṣaṃ sārasaṃ madura laghu
children.translated_text: River water increases <s>vāta</s> and is dry; lake water is sweet and light.
Certain water removes <s>vāta</s> and phlegm, while pond water is remembered as increasing <s>vāta</s>.
Water from a cascade is tasty, kindles digestion, is dry, destroys <s>kapha</s>, and is light.
Well water kindles digestion and tends toward <s>pitta</s>; spring water arising from the ground removes <s>pitta</s>.
Water that has been enjoyed by the sun's rays by day and by the moon's rays at night
is free from all <s>doṣas</s> and equal to rainwater from the sky.
Hot water removes fever, dyspnea, fat, <s>vāta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
Boiled water, when cooled, removes the three <s>doṣas</s>; but when kept overnight it becomes faulty.
Cow's milk removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>; it is unctuous, heavy, and rejuvenating.
Buffalo milk is heavier and more unctuous than cow's milk, and it destroys the digestive fire.
Goat's milk cures bloody diarrhea and removes cough, dyspnea, and <s>kapha</s>.
It is good for the eyes and life-giving for women, and it protects in cases of blood-pitta.
Curd is supremely <s>vāta</s>-removing and aphrodisiac, but it produces <s>pitta</s> and phlegm.
The whey produced from churning is <s>doṣa</s>-removing, and <s>mastu</s> clears the channels.
Freshly extracted butter removes disorders of the <s>grahaṇī</s>, piles, facial paralysis, and pain.
But transformations such as <s>kilāṭa</s> and the like are heavy and causes of skin disease.
Buttermilk is said by the earlier sages to be supreme in removing <s>grahaṇī</s> disorders, swelling, piles, jaundice, diarrhea, and abdominal tumors,
and to pacify the three <s>doṣas</s>.
Ghee is aphrodisiac and sweet, and removes <s>vāta</s>, <s>pitta</s>, and <s>kapha</s>.
Cow ghee is good for intelligence and the eyes, and through preparation it conquers the three <s>doṣas</s>.
Medicated ghee cures epilepsy, disease, insanity, and fainting.
The ghee of goats and other animals should be understood according to the good qualities of their milk.
Urine removes <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>, and removes all worms and poisons.
It removes pallor, abdominal disease, skin disease, piles, swelling, abdominal tumors, and urinary disorders.
Sesame oil, born from sesame, removes <s>vāta</s> and phlegm, gives strength, and is astringent.
Mustard oil destroys worms and pallor, and removes <s>kapha</s>, fat, and <s>vāta</s>.
Linseed oil is bad for the eyes, removes <s>pitta</s>, and destroys <s>vāta</s>.
Oil from <s>akṣa</s> destroys <s>kapha</s> and <s>pitta</s>, benefits the hair, and nourishes the skin and ears.
Honey is declared to destroy the three <s>doṣas</s>, and is also said to increase <s>vāta</s>.
It destroys hiccup, dyspnea, worms, vomiting, urinary disorder, thirst, and poison.
Products of sugarcane remove blood-pitta; they strengthen, are aphrodisiac, and produce <s>kapha</s>.

children.text: phāṇitaṃ pittalaṃ tavriṃ surā matsyaṇḍikā laghuḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Phāṇita</s> is <s>pitta</s>-producing and heavy; <s>matsyaṇḍikā</s> sugar is light.
Sugar candy is aphrodisiac, unctuous, sweet, and conquers blood-pitta and <s>vāta</s>.
Jaggery removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>, is dry, removes <s>vāta</s>, and produces <s>kapha</s>.
When old, it is <s>pitta</s>-destroying, supremely wholesome, and clarifies the blood.
Coarse sugar is said to remove blood-pitta, be aphrodisiac, and possess unctuousness.
Alcohol produces every kind of <s>pitta</s>, and because of its sourness conquers <s>kapha</s> and <s>vāta</s>.
The varieties of <s>sauvīra</s> are sharp and produce blood-pitta.
<s>Maṇḍa</s> made from roasted rice is digestive, kindles digestion, and is wholesome.
<s>Peyā</s> normalizes <s>vāta</s>, is light, and cleanses the bladder.
Prepared with buttermilk, pomegranate, the three pungents, jaggery, honey, and long pepper,
this well-made <s>peyā</s> is useful for cough, dyspnea, and dysentery.
Milk-rice produces <s>kapha</s> and gives strength; <s>kṛśarā</s> destroys <s>vāta</s>.
When well washed, strained, unctuous, pleasantly warm, light, and appetizing,
and cooked with bulbs, roots, and fruits, it is nourishing and heavy.
A well-prepared soup, taken slightly warm, is light.
Boiled and squeezed greens are wholesome when prepared with ghee, oil, and the like.
Soup with pomegranate and emblic myrobalan kindles the digestive fire and removes <s>vāta</s> and <s>pitta</s>.
Made with emblic myrobalan, it destroys dyspnea, cough, rhinitis, and <s>kapha</s>.
Soup of barley, jujube, and horse gram is good for the throat and removes <s>vāta</s>.
That made from mung beans and emblic myrobalan is absorbent and destroys phlegm and <s>pitta</s>.
Curd with jaggery removes <s>vāta</s>; roasted grain flour is dry and <s>vāta</s>-producing.
A ghee-filled preparation kindles the digestive fire; <s>śaṣkulī</s> is aphrodisiac and heavy.

children.text: bṛṃhaṇāḥ sāmiṣā bhakṣyapiṣṭa kā gukhaḥ smṛtāḥ
children.translated_text: Meat-filled foods and foods made from dough are remembered as nourishing and heavy.
Those cooked in oil harm the eyesight, and those steamed with water are hard to digest.

children.text: atyuṣṇā maṇḍakāḥ pathyāḥ śītalā gukho matāḥ
children.translated_text: <s>Maṇḍakas</s>, when very hot, are wholesome; when cold, they are considered heavy.
Water used as an after-drink removes fatigue, thirst, and the like.
By food, drink, and the like, one should carefully protect oneself so as to be free from disease.
Poison is not hot, has the color of a peacock's neck, and causes discoloration.
Its smell, touch, and tastes are intense, and mental distress arises for the eater.
When it is smelled, disease of the eyes arises, and it is incurable even for the best physicians.
Trembling, yawning, and the like arise; these are the signs of poison.

children.text: iti śrīgāruḍe mahāpurāṇe pūrvakhaṇḍe prathamāṃśākhye ācārakāṇḍe anupānādividhikathanaṃ nāmaikonasaptatyadhikaśatatamo 'dhyāyaḥ ||
children.translated_text: Thus, in the blessed <s>Gāruḍa Mahāpurāṇa</s>, in the <s>Pūrvakhaṇḍa</s>, in the first part, in the <s>Ācārakāṇḍa</s>, ends the one-hundred-and-sixty-ninth chapter, called "The Explanation of the Rules for After-Drinks and the Like."
